"I can never keep their stupid names straight."
"I believe the only one out on task right now is Swordfish."
"I'm never going to remember that."
"See? That's a part of your problem. If you don't send them their own name, they won't be able to validate your identity. And it should be on your digital receipt."
"Tch. Whatever, I'll get back to you when THAT doesn't work either."
You could use some peace and quiet - this is a Rebel sector after all.

name: AUTO_ITEM_NAMED_BOT
text: An Auto notices that you've ventured out from the beacon and approaches your ship. Its engines are fully charged. "Your digital courier has arrived! You were 28 minutes late to receive your supplies - this courier was about to depart. Now that you are here, please verify your identity by stating the name of the courier assigned to deliver your package!"

event.text: "Detecting hostility! Returning to sender." The ship makes haste and leaves immediately. As it had implied earlier, its jump engines were already charged. There's nothing more that can be done here.
"Identity confirmed. Sending supplies. We hope you have a wonderful day!"
"Incorrect response. Returning to supply depot. If this is an error, please contact your service provider."

name: AUTO_SUPPORT
text: Luckily, the Auto-Support at this beacon is not designed for combat. If you were to convince it that you were a Rebel ship, maybe it will give you supplies.

choice.text: Simply transmit your fake ID and hope for the best.
(Hacking) Reprogram the ship to distribute to Federation ships as well.

event.text: It appears that your injected code works. "Identification authorized. Dispensing supplies."

choice.text: (Hacking Weapon) Disrupt the ship's AI so that it will distribute to your ship.

event.text: Your weapon is able to jam the enemy ship's ability to tell friend from foe. It glitches momentarily, then relents. "Identifi-fi-fication authorized-ized. Dispensing su-supplies."

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Reprogram the ship to distribute to Federation ships as well.

event.text: It appears that your Engi's modifications work. "Identification authorized. Dispensing supplies."

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Reprogram the ship to distribute to Federation ships as well.

event.text: It appears that your Engineer's modifications work. "Identification authorized. Dispensing supplies."
It's not likely you can trick an AI vessel. You let it continue on its way.

name: ENGINEER_BUY_DRONES
text: A Rebel Engineer hails you. "I know this is a bit unconventional, but we are in need of drone-parts. We'll pay you in any other resource you want."

event.text: You prepare to attack the engineers.
You're good with what you have.

name: AUTO_BIRDLY_BOT
text: As you arrive at the next beacon, the communications console lights up like a Christmas tree. Every single channel is broadcasting the exact same message originating from a nearby arboreal planet. The contents of the call is a whimsical song about birds that you recognize as originating from human history, at max volume and double the usual BPM. After receiving the hail, a small Auto-ship begins flying towards your location from the planet's biosphere. "QUERY: Bird?"

event.text:
"SCANNING. Error. SCANNING. Error. Major sensor driver malfunction. Utilizing audio verification."
	The Auto-ship begins to play a pleasant bird tune through your speakers, and Wealsey responds in kind, singing its beautiful song. Your ship transmits the audio back to the Auto-ship.
	"Audio mismatch. Bird species incorrect. Conclusion: bird lovers detected. Dispensing aid to bird-lovers."

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Offer to diagnose and fix the malfunction.
(Engi Crew) Offer to diagnose and fix the malfunction.

event.text: "MISSION PARAMETERS: Find the Kestrel---[DATA CORRUPTION]. 99% of mission information lost. Data restoration, extrapolation using local communications broadcast indicates a 1.2% probability that original mission parameters included the logging, protection and tracking of Kestrel species. This planet: only nearby planet containing Kestrel species. Additional, subsequent systems failures resulted in malfunction in onboard sensor drivers. Flock: lost. Request assistance."

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Offer to diagnose and fix the malfunction.
(Engi Crew) Offer to diagnose and fix the malfunction.
(Sensors) Take some time gathering some sensor readings for the Auto-ship.

event.text: You spend some time taking readings all across the surface. It takes a long time, but eventually the Auto-ship is satisfied that it has found what it is looking for. It dispenses a modest amount of scrap and returns to the biosphere of the planet.

choice.text: (Upg. Sensors) Gather some sensor readings for the Auto-ship.

event.text: Your detailed sensor suite already scanned the entire planet. You transmit your sensor information to the Auto-ship, and are rewarded with a modest amount of scrap.

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Gather some readings for the Auto-ship.

event.text: Your detailed scanner suite already scanned the entire planet. You transmit your information to the Auto-ship, and are rewarded with a modest amount of scrap.

choice.text: Apologize and say you can't help.

event.text: "Ornithophobe detected. Violence is justified." The Auto-ship immediately powers weapons.
You decide not to dignify the query with a response. The Auto-ship immediately loses interest and returns to the biosphere of the planet.

name: AUTO_BIRDLY_BOT_GOODBYE
text: With nothing more to do, you disengage from the Auto-ship. It immediately loses interest and returns to the biosphere of the planet.

name: BIRDLY_BOT_FIX
text: "Offer accepted. Deploying memory core." Your crew examines the Auto-ship's memory core. Almost all of the memory is corrupted, and it's hard to tell what this ship used to be from data analysis alone. Your crew purges the unsalvageable data from the system, fixes the hardware issues and uploads the latest Federation standard drivers into all of its systems. Once the ship comes back online, it immediately whirs to life with more vigor than it had before. "Scanning. All kestrel specimens found and accounted for. Federation ship: has done great service in environmental conservation. Deploying gratitude." The ship dispenses a modest amount of supplies before departing.

name: AUTO_ZOLTAN_FACILITY
text: In the distance appears to just be an ordinary planet, though the vast complex built on the surface interests you. Further scans reveal a morbid truth - a primarily automated Auto-ship factory running entirely on Zoltan slave power has been constructed on the surface!

event.text: You fly closer to the surface and are immediately met by a large Auto-Battleship, but it's not attacking yet. "This is Dr. Peron Anderson. Your vessel has been spotted coming concerningly close to the facility. We suggest either stating your business or getting lost."
The scientist sighs, then ends the call. Weapons spring out of the Auto-ship's hull, and it's time for a brawl.
"You... want one of our power sources? Well, I guess we don't need THIS many of them, and the scrap is handy... alright, you've got a deal."
You'd have to be insane to tangle with such a massive structure that's undoubtedly of high value to the Rebels.
You move in to intercept the automated vessel.
You have no interest in the ship.

name: AUTO_FOREST
text: This beacon has been set up close to a lush forest planet. As you navigate closer to the surface, you can just barely make out a Rebel supply platform. It's likely staffed by a few Engineers, but nothing you can't manage.

choice.text: (Adv. Hacking) Disrupt any potential defenses the platform may have.

event.text: Your sophisticated hacking system easily breaches whatever firewalls the platform may have had in place. Now defenseless against your assault, they quickly surrender.

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Disrupt any potential defenses the platform may have.

event.text: You attack the platform, making sure to disrupt any signals to their defenses. Once the engineers staffing the platform realize that their defenses aren't working properly, they promptly surrender.
There's likely a defense system lying in wait for you. You abandon the platform.

name: AUTO_ENGINEERS_SAVE
text: A ship full of Rebel engineers is under fire from a pirate vessel. They hail you, and request that you save them.

event.text: You move in to intercept the pirate vessel.

choice.text: We aren't going to help any damn Rebels.

event.text: You leave the two ships to continue fighting.

name: AUTO_ENGINEERS_SAVE_WIN
text: The engineer ship is in poor condition. "I... I didn't expect you to actually help. I have no ship left, no crew... nothing. I suppose it will do me no harm to work aboard yours."

name: AUTO_PIRATE_CHOICE
text: At this beacon you discover a pirate and Auto-ship fighting each other. Neither notices you.

event.text: You move in to intercept the automated vessel.
You move in to intercept the pirate ship.
You leave the two ships to continue fighting.

name: AUTO_PIRATE_CHOICE_AUTO_WIN
text: "We weren't expecting support from a Federation ship. To be fair, I was looking forward to scrapping that ship. Despite this, I may be a pirate, but I am still a man who doesn't like keeping a debt. So here, take this garbage."

name: AUTO_PIRATE_CHOICE_PIRATE_WIN
text: "Logic error: Federation ship provided aid in combat. Conflicting internal code... requires reboot." The Auto-ship turns offline. You take this chance to scrap it.

name: AUTO_MINER
text: Inside the asteroid field at this beacon is a mining platform and an Automated Salvager ship. The Salvager does not notice you as it mines away at the asteroids.

choice.text: Attack the ship to get to the platform.

event.text: You prepare to engage the Auto-ship.
Fighting a mining ship in its natural habitat of an asteroid field doesn't sound like a good idea.

name: AUTO_MINER_PLATFORM
text: The automated platform holds many fuel cells freshly mined from the asteroid field. You take all that you can.

name: AUTO_BOMB_MANUFACTURE
text: An Automated ship is patrolling what appears to be a ammunition manufacturing plant. You can't access the factory while the ship is in the way.

event.text: You prepare to engage the Auto-ship.
You aren't interested in raiding the factory.

name: AUTO_BOMB_MANUFACTURE_FACTORY
text: Now that the patrol ship has been taken out, the automated factory has begun to sound an alarm. A robotic voice counts down a timer until the factory explodes. You only have time to grab one thing if you want to escape unharmed.

event.text: You grab as much ammunition as you can carry and fly away before the factory can explode.
You grab the nearest ballistic weapon and fly away before the factory can explode.

choice.text: Grab all that you can, even if it means taking some damage.

event.text: You grab the nearest ballistic weapon and as much ammunition as you can carry. Luckily you escape before the explosion can do critical damage to the hull, but several chunks of debris collide with it regardless, inflicting some damage.

name: REBEL_AUTO_SPY
text: This beacon hosts an automated ship, but not of the usual variety. It's a Surveyor, a class deployed by the Rebels to scout out sectors autonomously. If you can capture its black box, you should be able to access the data.

event.text: Luckily Auto-ship black boxes can survive most damage from combat. Destroy the ship and the data is yours.
The Rebel's data is intriguing, but you have decided against messing with the Surveyor.

name: REBEL_AUTO_SPY_ESCAPING
text: "This Automated ship has taken damage in combat. It will now proceed to escape. Do not cause further damage to this ship." Now that the Surveyor has seen you, if it can get away it'll report your location to the fleet!

name: REBEL_AUTO_SPY_GOTAWAY
text: The Surveyor jumps away, and will no doubt report your location to the fleet next.

name: REBEL_AUTO_SPY_WIN
text: You scrap the remains of the Auto-Surveyor, and bring aboard its black box. You have two options, either transmit false data to the Rebels to delay them, or download it to get a sector map.

event.text: This should delay them for a while, or at least until they realize it's a hoax.
The Surveyor appears to have collected highly detailed data on the sector. This should help considerably.

name: DISTRESS_AUTO_REPAIRS
text: An automated ship emitting this distress beacon signal is looping a message in a calming female voice. "This automated vessel has received critical hull damage. It has been programmed to give a reward to anyone who repairs it."

event.text: A long bent arm comes out of the Auto-ship and collects the scrap. You watch in fascination as it patches itself back together.
The damaged ship is in horrible condition, but it still manages to raise its weapons and defend itself.
You'd have to be an absolute idiot to invest time into repairing an enemy Auto-ship.

name: DESTROYED_AUTO_DAMAGED
text: Barely anything remains that can be scrapped from the Auto-ship.

name: DISTRESS_AUTO_TRASH
text: The only thing present at this beacon is a small system, barely more than a planet. Even from a distance, you can tell it's devoid of life - most likely stripped clean for the production of Auto-ships and their facilities. Surprisingly, your ship can pick up a faint distress signal originating from the surface. Given that it's closer to a ball of rock than anything that could support life, it's possible that it's just a faulty transponder from some half-finished Auto. It could still be worth checking out, though.

event.text: Even if the planet looks completely inhospitable, you can't just leave a distress signal. You pilot your ship down into the atmosphere and head towards the surface.

The surface of the planet is cluttered with trash everywhere you look. As you approach the signal, the chaotic spread seems to become more ordered. By the time you're right on top of it, the sprawl of garbage has been replaced with spires of compacted garbage.

The source of the signal becomes apparent soon after. A maintenance drone trundles by, carrying another block of trash. You begin to wonder how long it's been here for, but then it notices you and begins to wave wildly. It can't speak, but it seems... excited? Finding a place to land among all the clutter is a challenge, but the drone rushes towards you as soon as you do.

choice.text: (Orchid Children) Give the drone some plant matter.

event.text: The drone cradles the plants gently, then looks at you and makes a "stay here" motion. You watch as it carefully stores the children within itself before zooming away into the spires. A few minutes later, it reappears carrying a block of scrap larger than itself! You have to help it carry its bounty aboard the ship, but you can't find it in you to complain - this is a lot of scrap.
You find it unlikely that there's anything to be found down there - these are Rebel-controlled shipyards after all, and no human could survive down there. You prepare to jump away.

name: DISTRESS_AUTO_MILITIA_CHAIN
text: The moment you arrive, you begin detecting weapon discharge signatures. A Rebel Engineer is being chased by a Militia vessel, itself being chased by an Auto-ship. Both the Militia ship and the Rebel Engineer are broadcasting distress signals.

choice.text: Chase down the Engineer to let the Militia focus on the Auto.

event.text: As you corner the Engineer, the Militia ship sends you a message. "Thank goodness you're here. Try to capture them alive if you can!"

choice.text: Attack the Auto to give the Militia some breathing room.

event.text: The Auto-ship breaks off its attack to respond to your threat.

tooltip.text: The Rebel is escaping!

event.text: All the ships involved keep taking damage, but the fight eventually leaves your periphery.

name: DISTRESS_AUTO_MILITIA_CHAIN_GOTAWAY_DURING_FIGHT
text: The Engineer jumps away from the Militia before they manage to disable their vessel. The Militia captain yells "Get back here!" over the open channel, and jumps after them. It seems your fight has become a one on one engagement.

name: DISTRESS_AUTO_MILITIA_CHAIN_GOTAWAY
text: The Militia captain sighs. "Dammit. We almost had them. All this time chasing them into their territory for nothing, and our defenses are still compromised. We're sitting ducks for whenever the Rebels attack next." Annoyed, they jump away.

name: AUTO_GHOST_WANTWRECK
text: You arrive in orbit above a barren planet. The only noteworthy feature on its surface is a large Vagabond camp, a rarity in a sector so hostile to Ghosts. You wonder whether or not to contact them until you receive a message from them. "Salutations, mysterious 'not a Rebel'. Though we are currently satiated with our ample bounty of discarded vessels, we find ourselves constantly pondering over a matter most elusive and difficult. But first, have you perchance, heard of the scarlet-clad demons sometimes wielded by the Rebellion?"

event.text: "Wonderful! Then we shall gloss over the protracted explanations I was so begrudgingly prepared to dole out. As you can see behind us, we are well acquainted with the internals of various more unremarkable ships. But having recently caught eye of a scarlet demon, we were struck by insatiable curiosity about what might lie within. But alas, to no avail, as it was more than a fair-handed fight for us. I daresay, we were lucky to escape with our very mortality intact! But perhaps your arsenal might be more of a match for it?"
The Vagabonds send you the coordinates of the ship they want you to defeat, and wish you good luck.

"Very well, we shall share with you all the wisdom we can bring to bear. As you should invariably bear knowledge of, the Rebellion makes extensive application of, uh, how does your vernacular refer to them again? "Auto-ships?" But among such devilspawn, there are some adorned with scarlet hues, and branded with some unknowable white insignia. We happened upon one the other day, inquisitive as to what its interiors may bear compared to its less distinguished brethren. It was regrettably too much for our capabilities - though you appear capable of reducing it to naught but a crimson wreck. Would this proposal be of intrigue to you?"
The Vagabonds send you the coordinates of the ship they want you to defeat, and wish you good luck.
The Vagabonds cut comms, but not before sending you one final message. "You are a person of most dreary and uninteresting character! May you never besmirch us with your presence again!"

name: AUTO_GHOST_WANTWRECK_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Vagabond camp has asked you to destroy a powerful Auto-ship here.

text: You find the Auto-ship the Vagabonds wanted you to hunt down soon after arriving at this beacon. It doesn't seem to have spotted you yet, but you won't have long until it does see you.

event.text: The Auto-ship detects your hostile intentions, and moves to retaliate in turn.

name: AUTO_GHOST_WANTWRECK_QUEST_WIN
text: You've destroyed the Auto-ship as the Vagabonds requested. You pick up a few loose pieces of wreckage scattered around, but what now?

choice.text: Wait for the Vagabonds to arrive.

event.text: A wrecked ship jumps in not long after you've finished destroying the Auto-ship. The Vagabonds inside move to inspect the wreckage carefully. "Hmm, the innards of this machination are most fascinating. The construction is most exquisite, and even the wiring would seem to be done with a remarkable care for the finer details." They then proceed to discard the ship's internal computer, before taking full control of the ship.

"Your accomplishment here was one we could not hope to match. Please, accept our wholehearted gratitude for your fine deed here today." One of the Vagabonds, so impressed by your performance, wishes to join your crew.
You opt to try and salvage as much as possible before the Vagabonds arrive. You find a functioning Sentry weapon in the remaining wreckage.

name: ENCOUNTER_AUTO_HACKER
text: Your arrival is greeted by numerous computer alerts. The nearby automated Rebel Hacker has used a local satellite in conjunction with its Hacking to deploy a virus to disrupt your Shields System. Hopefully it won't cause further problems before you can destroy it.

event.text: Your hacking system automatically counters the digital assault and you move in to fight the ship.
Your Anti-Virus automatically counters the digital assault and you move in to fight the ship.

name: ENCOUNTER_AUTO_SUN
text: You arrive at the beacon to find yourself dangerously close to a star. An automated Rebel ship, impervious to the heat, moves in to engage.

name: ENCOUNTER_AUTO_ASTEROID
text: You arrive in an asteroid belt to discover that a Rebel automated-scout has been stationed here. Prepare for a fight!

name: ENCOUNTER_ENGINEER_SALVAGE
text: An engineer ship at this beacon is busy repairing a broken Auto-ship. As soon as they see you, they abandon the wreck and attack.

name: ENCOUNTER_ENGINEER_SALVAGE_WIN
text: You scrap what remains of the automated wreck.

name: ENCOUNTER_AUTO_ELITE
text: A Rebel Auto-ship advances towards you with clear intent, and while hostile Auto-ships are (unfortunately) a normal occurrence for you, this one is no usual sight. Its elegant and pristine figure suggests this is one of the more refined automatons produced in the heart of Wentworth Innovations. Battle stations!

name: AUTO_ENGINEER_MISTAKE
text: A damaged Engineer vessel orbits this beacon. It appears to still be functional, and a single hull repair drone is patching up some of the damage.

event.text: "Ugh, you aren't here to kill us, are you?" You shake your head. "Oh, good. In that case, maybe you could help us. We had an issue with a cognitive prototype we were working on. After the Free Roamer incident, the Rebellion banned all attempts at creating fully sentient ship AI. We uh... we broke that rule, and it was a terrible mistake. Now the Auto-ship has escaped. You don't suppose you could track it down and destroy it? We can't let command know about this slip-up..."
These guys make an easy target. You arm the weapons.
The Engineer makes no attempt to hail you in return. Just in case, you put a little distance between your ships.

name: AUTO_ENGINEER_MISTAKE_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of the rogue Rebel cognitive.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: You've arrived at the co-ordinates given by the Engineers, but instead you've found a crashed starliner converted into a massive city bustling with pirates. A prime place to find a rogue AI, but not an easy one to search through.

event.text: Fortunately, the pirates don't really seem to care that you're a Federation officer. Living so close to Rebel space, it's probably a nice change of pace if anything. Asking around about a rogue cognitive however turns up confusing results. Most people have no idea what a cognitive is, and most redirect you to speak with the king of the city.

You step into a massive, cobbled together tower of spliced cargo containers and the hulls of former Rebel ships. In the center sits a throne, on which rests a rotund man with a black paper hat staring down upon you. He isn't particularly imposing, save for the buzzsaw that apparently has replaced his left hand. "I see yee have found me in my d-d-dominion. Welcome, matey!"

The man 'stands' up, revealing he in-fact has no feet, but rather a set of treads. He rolls towards you, and it becomes clear this is no man at all, but rather a ramshackle Doctor Drone. "Arg, I be Cap'ain A5540L3, at your service. How might I help you, lad?" The drone sticks out his left hand to shake yours before he remembers his situation, and so quickly stuffs it behind his back and reaches out his right instead, which is instead a much less imposing but still concerning blaster arm from a Battle Drone.
This mission isn't worth stirring up an entire city of pirates. You pull away from the city.

name: A55_HANDSHAKE
text: You carefully grab his arm cannon and shake it up and down a few times. "Arg, mighty grip you've got there, lad! Now, surely there's a reason the Federation's come prodding around here."

name: A55_FIGHT
text: It doesn't take a genius to realize this is the cognitive in question, and you waste no further time explaining the situation to him. "Hmmm. Sounds grave, matey. You surely understand I'm not just gonna r-r-roll out of here with you."

choice.text: Then we have a standoff, don't we?

event.text: "Arg, it would appear so." A55 does his best to clap, then whistles. Seconds later, a massive Auto-Dreadnaught comes whirling by through a hole in the ceiling of the massive throne room. "Last chance lad, I don't wanna cause no bloodshed t-t-today."

Curiously, A55's massive vessel makes no attempt to fight you until you get into your cruiser, though it easily could have blown your crew away during the run. You have no time to contemplate this further, it's time to fight!
You turn and walk out of the room. A55 watches you leave in mild amusement and confusion.

name: A55_DEFEAT
text: Suddenly, the Dreadnaught shuts offline, falling to the ground. In the distance approaches the engineers from earlier, here to collect their AI. You don't have time to hail them before you receive another hail from A55. "Please matey, don't hand me over. They'll tear me apart and turn me offline! That's no proper fate for a pirate, arg!"

event.text: You grab the medic drone, carting him over to the Engineers. "He's integrated himself into a new chassis? Incredible! It's a shame we'll have to destroy it, but at least this drone will look cool as a trophy. Don't speak of this to anyone."

choice.text: Lie to the Engineers, tell them the Auto-ship is A55.

event.text: A55 hides while you inform the engineers about the Auto-ship, which they briefly scan. The engineer frowns, "Huh, I can see traces of his programming here, but it looks like the core migrated to a new chassis. This must have been a distraction, we'll have to keep searching. Here's your pay or something. Don't speak of this to anyone."

"Thank you, matey. Arg, though you did choose to try and murder me a few minutes ago, your heart is clearly in the right place lad. I suspect my time here as king might be short lived, those Engineers will come around again. But as I prepare to leave, take this."

"Thank you, matey. Arg, though you did choose to try and murder me a few minutes ago, your heart is clearly in the right place lad. I suspect my time here as king might be short lived, those Engineers will come around again. I think I shall come with you, in hopes I might live to see a future without Rebels. Let me send you over some scans o' me ship - not the one you destroyed, but one I plundered from the Rebel databanks back in the day."

name: AUTO_POWERCORE
text: It appears a large generator has been sculpted onto the face of a nearby snow planet. It's quite a spectacle, but something is wrong...

event.text: A battalion of pirate ships flies away, chased off by a distant Rebel ship. A warning plays over the intercom. "It is recommended that all personnel evacuate Power Grid 800 immediately. Catastrophic reactor failure is imminent. Estimated 3 minutes remaining until collapse."

choice.text: There's time left, swing by and try to salvage some supplies.

event.text: As you move in to salvage, you're stopped by a large Engineer vessel. "Damn pirates! We told you to get the hell out of here!" Though the ship moves in to chase you off, you can't help but notice that reactor countdown is still going, and you figure the Engineers must know as well.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_ESCAPE
text: Suddenly, the Engineer ship jumps away so abruptly, they must have used an MV drive, leaving you alone with the power core. You receive another warning from the core. "Warning: Reactor instability has reached 99%. Destruction is imminent. Evacuate immediately. Estimated 3 seconds remaining until collapse."

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Get the hell out of there.
(Adv. Engines) Get the hell out of there.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_DEFEAT
text: You've defeated the Engineer ship, but that victory won't last for long. You receive another warning from the core. "Warning: Reactor instability has reached 99%. Destruction is imminent. Evacuate immediately. Estimated 3 seconds remaining until collapse."

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Get the hell out of there.
(Adv. Engines) Get the hell out of there.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_ALMOSTBOOM
text: The Engineer ship has taken critical damage. Before you can get in a finishing shot you're interupted by another alarm. "Warning: Reactor instability has reached 97%. Evacuate the premises immediately. Estimated 1 minute remaining until collapse."

choice.text: Urge the Engineers to stop fighting.

event.text: "You think we can just leave? It's a better fate to blow the hell up than face Vance's wrath! I'd rather die fighting the Federation and become a martyr than-" The engineers are cut off by another warning. "Warning: Reactor instability has reached critical levels. Destruction imminent, evacuation mandatory. Time remaining: undetermined. Repeat: reactor-" The message continues to loop, and it seems like it's a good warning. Surely, there's something you can do to stop the explosion?

choice.text: Send in your crew to fix the reactor, and quickly!

event.text: You pull closer to the power core, and drop off your crew. They hurry inside to the control panel, which is sparking. There's 3 buttons, but their labels are barely legible. Pressing one of them might save the day, but you have no idea which.
Your crew flips open the protective casing and smashes the button as fast as they can. Now you can only hope it worked...
Your crew flips open the protective casing and smashes the button as fast as they can. Now you can only hope it worked...
Your crew flips open the protective casing and smashes the button as fast as they can. Now you can only hope it worked...

You rapidly flip through the manual, and sure enough under the section for "Rebel Automated Power Core Explosion Prevention Protocols" it clearly states to press the red button. You relay this to the crew, who flips open the protective casing and smashes the button as fast as they can.

Your engineer searches deep through their memories and remembers a staff training day where they explained the importance of each button. Recalling the red button was the correct solution, you relay this to the crew who flips open the protective casing and smashes the button as fast as they can.

You power up the engines and fly as far away as you can, and watch from a distance as the mothership is consumed by a massive explosion that rips through the planet's surface leaving a crater so large you can see it all the way from the other side of the system. You pull a little closer and scrap the wreckage on the outer rim, though the center is leaking heavy radiation and is not safe to journey towards.

choice.text: Keep fighting to the bitter end.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_BIGBOOM
text: An ear splitting explosion reverbs throughout the ship as a deadly inferno consumes the power core. Your ship is caught in the explosion, and takes heavy damage. You fly away as quickly as possible, your engines burning up as you go.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_BIGBOOM_ESCAPE
text: You speed away from the power core as fast as you possible can. You escape the initial explosion, but much of the debris still collides with your ship, causing damage to the hull.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_BIGBOOM_ESCAPE_GOOD
text: Your advanced engines are easily able to get you out in time. You watch the explosion from a safe distance.

name: AUTO_POWERCORE_SAVE
text: A loud beep emanates from the console. "Emergency Reactor Meltdown Prevention button pressed. Stopping countdown to imminent explosion. Reactor stabilized." By some incredible miracle, it appears you've stopped the explosion.

event.text: The Engineers are amazed. "I-I didn't even know that button was a thing! You've saved all of us... but why? Why put your life on the line just to save a Rebel facility?"

"Perhaps we are fighting for the wrong side here... Regardless, we must leave this facility at once. Vance won't be happy we let that pirate raid almost destroy the reactor and I doubt he'd let us live through it. I'll come with you, and bring everything that I can with me."

tooltip.text: The reactor will detonate in this much time. Nothing can stop this, so make sure to jump away or end the fight before it reaches 0!

name: CLAN_FAUNA_START
text: A Clansman ship is in orbit around a world that is largely arboreal. Upon your arrival, they send you a hail. "The planet below hasss the mossst dangerousss arboreal creature in the galaxy. With itsss innate psssychic powersss, it isss asss formidable in battle asss it isss at sssubverting your mind. Mossst ssspeciesss won't cut it. It can't even be ssstunned. Our Ssslugsss can help, but are not ssstrong enough on their own."

choice.text: Ask them why they don't just use their ship mounted weapons.

event.text: "Do you have no underssstanding of what it meansss to hunt the beassst? If we ussse ssship grade weaponsss, we have not accomplissshed anything. Plusss, it tendsss to leave a sssmouldering crater inssstead of a presssentable trophy. And it'd be nice not to dessstroy the foressst in the processs."
Looks like the hunters are about to become the hunted. They seem caught off guard, but quickly recover.
You apologize and decide not to get involved.

name: CLAN_FAUNA_OFFER_TO_HELP
text: "You have ssssome way to help ussss in the hunt?"

choice.text: (A55) "Let me show ye how it be done!" [-1|]

event.text: A55 skillfully subdues the creature as the Clansmen do their best to help. "Arr, this bounty put up a good fight, but it were no match for me!" The Clansmen are beyond impressed with the drone's mechanically perfect precision and surprising cunning.

choice.text: (Special Boarding Drone) Send a powerful drone to help assist the Slugs. [-1|]
(Boarding Drone Offense) Send a drone to help assist the Slugs [-1|].
(Boarding Drone Support) Send a weak drone to help assist the Slugs. [-1|]
(Chaotic Holodrone) Tell them you have a fantastic idea. [-1|]

event.text: The Chaotic Holodrone produces a crew member. Unfortunately for the Clansmen, they immediately side with the beast, and the duo effortlessly slaughter the hunting party. Your new loyal crew member returns to your ship, satisfied by a job well done, eagerly telling everyone else about their best friend.

choice.text: (The One Who Rhymes) "Everyone should stand aside. Let me be your horror guide!"

event.text: "Oh the years, how long it's been? That I should see the Fox again. How he hungers, how he yearns, oh how much his stomach churns. For dreams and flesh alike, he needs. His weakness is two mouths to feed. Now let's feed him all he craves, and end the lives of all these knaves." The One Who Rhymes places the beast directly onto the Clansman's ship. The panic and terror of the huntsmen is quickly silenced as the beast devours every single one of them. The One Who Rhymes provides you with the bounty of their ship.

"Now he's fed and now he's free. The galaxy is his to see. He'll spy a snack, he'll meet a meal, he'll make the useful people kneel. There is so much for him to know, think of all the places he'll go!"

choice.text: (Siren Crew) Your Siren may prove useful.

event.text: "Never persssonally encountered this lovely creature, but I got a hunch I know jussst the thing to sssstop it." Irwin gives out commands to all of the Clansmen. Under his flawless leadership, the beast is sedated and captured with no casualties at all. The Clansmen are in awe at witnessing the skill of a legend.

choice.text: (Vortigon) Vortigon seems eager to face the challenge.
(Telepathic Alkali) "How interesting. I'll provide medical support if you let me study thhhe beast."
(Turzil) Turzil supports an all-out offensive strike.
(Separatist Crew) You offer your Engi Separatist.
(Defender Crew) You offer your Engi Defender.
(Osmian Crew) Your Osmian can lend support.
(Technician Crew) Your Technician can lend support.

event.text: Looks like the hunters are about to become the hunted. They seem caught off guard, but quickly recover.

choice.text: Never mind, we have nothing suitable.

event.text: You apologize and decide not to get involved.

name: CLAN_FAUNA_IMPRESSIVE_SUCCESS
text: "That wasss glorioussss. We owe thisss sssuccesssful hunt to you, Renegade. They will sssurely sssing sssongsss of thisss great hunt." The Clansmen heap rewards upon you.

name: CLAN_FAUNA_MODEST_SUCCESS
text: "That wasss a definite ssssuccesss. To challenge the beasssst issss to flirt with death. Here isss your reward for your part." The Clansmen gift you some scrap.

name: CLAN_FAUNA_PYRRHIC_SUCCESS
text: "What a disssassster. We may have won, but that could have gone much better. Ssstill, your help, marginal asss it wasss, wasss meaningful." The Clansmen toss an obligatory reward.

name: CLAN_FAUNA_FAILURE
text: "What a disssassster. You were abssssolutely no help whatsssoever. Get out of our ssssight asss we mourn our dead."

name: CLAN_FAUNA_CATASTROPHIC_FAILURE
text: "WHAT ISSSS WRONG WITH YOU? ARE YOU THE DUMBESSSST RENEGADE IN THE ENTIRE MULTIVERSSSE?"

name: CLAN_TOURISTS
text: Some Crystals tend be xenophobic and hostile, but others can be very friendly and hospitable. Crystals such as these are often found in tourist locations.

choice.text: These Crystals make easy targets. Attack!

event.text: You arm the weapons and engage the crystalline tourists.

choice.text: (Guild Crew) Offer them a list of destinations.

event.text: "Oh, you're one of them! I greatly appreciate your offer, but there's no need. We already bought a map earlier, we can give you a copy if you'd like!"

choice.text: (Upg. Weapons) Give me everything you have or die.

event.text: "By the crypt! No need to be so hostile! We'll give you anything you want!" The Crystals send over some supplies.

"Oh, hello friend! I assume there's some lovely souvenir you're dying to buy, but are short on cash, and I'm happy to help!" The Crystals send over some scrap, and you don't bother mentioning you're a military vessel.
You leave the tourists be and fly away.

name: CLAN_CRISIS
text: A Guild ship is drifting nearby. It still has power, but all non-critical systems are online.

event.text: The ship responds and shows a Clansman frantically clawing at his feelers. "How did I get here? Why isss thisss what my life hasss become? A ssshadow of a perssson, a violent killer..."

choice.text: Put this man out of his misery.

event.text: You arm your weapons and attack the Clansman. It looks as though they aren't even trying to fight back.

choice.text: This guy is a sorry wretch. Leave him.

event.text: For all you know, this could be a trap. You ignore the Clansman.

name: CLAN_SPICES
text: Though the Guild normally stays to nebulas like the Slugs, it appears a trading outpost has been set up in this clearing to attract better business. That appears to have worked well... because a jet black and very powerful Slug ship is holding the lodge hostage and demanding the Clansmen hand over their 'exotic spices.' Probably drugs, if you had to guess.

event.text: You arm the weapons and attack the strange Slug ship.

choice.text: Help the black Slug ship out and take the drugs yourself.

event.text: To do this you'll have to kill the Clansmen without destroying their station. Be careful!
The origin of this new Slug vessel will have to go unknown. It's too risky to get involved when there's more important things at hand.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_CLAN_SHARPSHOOTER
text: The clearing isn't the only point of interest at this beacon. On the surface of a nearby planet, you find a shooting gallery that appears to have attracted an unusually large gathering of foreign vessels. Unfortunately, entry doesn't appear to be free, and you'll have to cough up some scrap to get inside.

event.text: You hand over the entry fee, and are soon ushered inside.
You hand over the now reduced entry fee, and are soon ushered inside.
As much as you'd like to spend time here, you really don't have as much as you'd like until the Rebel fleet arrives. You prepare to set off.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_SHARPSHOOTER_INTERIOR
text: Upon arriving in the main shooting gallery, a Slug clerk offers you a complimentary gift of high quality FTL fuel. You suspect this strange present is part of what enticed so many ships here, as few people seem to be engaging with the various intended attractions. The shooting gallery itself is divided into several themed stages, with the Orchid and Crystal tours catching your eye. Strangely, it seems that the first attempt at each one is free, with subsequent attempts requiring a fee.

choice.text: Try out the Orchid themed "Guardians of Rt'lak Et" stage.

event.text: This particular attraction appears to involve shooting at wooden targets depicting Vampweeds attempting to invade the Orchid Grand Gardens. The depicted scenario seems absurdly unrealistic, and no doubt playing to a multitude of unfortunate caricatures, but that shouldn't pose much of an issue with your attempts to succeed here.

choice.text: (Soldier Crew) Your Soldier's firearm training should give them an edge in this game.
(Praetor Crew) Your Praetor's unique firearm should give them an edge in this game.
(Haynes) Haynes' unique firearm should help out in this game.
(Irwin) Irwin's unique firearm should help out in this game.
(Jerry) Jerry has a really, really big gun. What more needs to be said?
Try out the Crystal themed "Ycathine's Wonders" stage.

event.text: This particular attraction features crystalline sculptures based on no known creature. Upon looking at the associated small text, you find that the crystalline creatures are supposed to be the monstrous denizens of the seemingly mythical crypt of the former Crystalline emperor Ycathine. Seems a waste to expend such beautiful sculpting technique on throwaway nonexistent cryptids at a tourist trap, but Slugs are known to be quite excessive about such things.

choice.text: (Soldier Crew) Your Soldier's firearm training should give them an edge in this game.
(Praetor Crew) Your Praetor's unique firearm should give them an edge in this game.
(Haynes) Haynes' unique firearm should help out in this game.
(Irwin) Irwin's unique firearm should help out in this game.
(Jerry) Jerry has a really, really big gun. What more needs to be said?
Try talking to the other disinterested people here.

name: CLAN_SHARPSHOOTER_KERNEL_CREW
text: With a mixture of expertise and a capable firearm, your crew member manages to hit every target on their first attempt. A Slug Clansman approaches you from behind. "Good going there. Not many people manage that firssst attempt. In fact, it'sss how we make mossst of our profitsss. Anywaysss, here'sss your prize. Jussst don't asssk how we got it, can't have the Praetorian asssking too many quessstionsss here."

name: CLAN_SHARPSHOOTER_KERNEL_JERRY
text: As soon as Jerry finishes walking up to the stand, he takes fire at the targets with frightening accuracy. Somehow, not a single shot misses a target. As you remark on how relieved you are to not be facing him as an enemy, a Slug Clansman approaches you from behind. "Good going there. Not many people manage that firssst attempt. In fact, it'sss how we make mossst of our profitsss. Anywaysss, here'sss your prize. Jussst don't asssk how we got it, can't have the Praetorian asssking too many quessstionsss here."

name: CLAN_SHARPSHOOTER_CRYSTAL_JERRY
text: As soon as Jerry finishes walking up to the stand, he takes fire at the targets with frightening accuracy. Somehow, not a single shot misses a target. As you remark on how relieved you are to not be facing him as an enemy, a Slug Clansman approaches you from behind. "Good going there. Not many people manage that firssst attempt. Jussst don't asssk how we got it, you have no idea how ssstiff the Cryssstalline people can be about thessse thingsss."

name: NEBULA_CLAN_JAMMER_SALESMAN
text: A small lodge is present here. "Looking to ssssspice up your hunt? Let me tell you thissss, there'ssss no better way to sssstalk your prey than to use a jammer to weaken them. Come take a look!"

choice.text: Purchase a jammer of vital ship operations.

event.text: You decline the lodge's offer. There's still time to do something at this beacon.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_RODEO
text: As you explore the nearby system you find a large gathering of foreign ships, mostly belonging to the Guild. It looks friendly enough, so you land nearby and take closer look, and see what appears to be a rodeo!

event.text: You're greeted by a Ranger with an oversized hat, who explains the basics. "We've rounded up quite a handful of Equinoidsss, and we're going to hold a grand sssspace rodeo! You can enter one of your crew if you want, for a sssmall entrance fee of 25 ssscrap. Whatever participant lastsss the longessst winsss the prize, a weapon we definitely didn't sssteal! It's one big-assss beam, if that enticesss you!"

You hand over some scrap to the Clansman, who reassures you by saying "Don't worry about your crew either, we ain't rookiesss here! We've got a whole medical team on ssstandbye in cassse thingssss go sssouth!"

choice.text: Send out a random crew member.

event.text: Your crew steps up to the competitors' chamber amongst some other aliens. Some Clansmen finish up preparing, and then usher in the first few contestants...

choice.text: Wish your crew luck and wait for the results.
(Soldier Crew) Your Soldier has some training in mounted combat. Send him.

event.text: Your crew steps up to the competitors' chamber amongst some other aliens. Some Clansmen finish up preparing, and then usher in the first few contestants...

choice.text: Wish your crew luck and wait for the results.
(Jerry) Jerry really really wants to ride the horse! Send him.

event.text: Jerry steps up to the competitors' chamber amongst some other aliens. Some Clansmen finish up preparing, and then usher in the first few contestants...

choice.text: Wish your crew luck and wait for the results.
(Lizard Crew) Your Lizard has ridden Equinoids before. Send him.

event.text: Your crew steps up to the competitors' chamber amongst some other aliens. Some Clansmen finish up preparing, and then usher in the first few contestants...

choice.text: Wish your crew luck and wait for the results.
You don't have any eligible riders with you. And don't even think about putting the drones on the horse...

event.text: "No one really knowsss where they came from firssst, but through the medium of sssspace travel they've been introduced to hundredsss of planetsss around the galaxy. They're pretty passsive asss long asss you're kind to them."

choice.text: Buy one of their younger, untamed Equinoids.
Interesting, but no reason to stick around.
Our mission is too important to waste time entering a contest.

event.text: Apparently, you aren't interested in the prospect of riding alien horses. You're pretty boring, all in all.

name: CLAN_RODEO_JERRY
text: As soon as Jerry mounts the wild beast, the Equinoid is immediately calmed, standing passively while Jerry gently strokes its mane. There's an outroar from the crowd calling you a cheater, but after a quick drug test to verify you didn't subdue the horse, you're declared the winner and the prize is brought out!

event.text: As you prepare to leave the rodeo, you see an Equinoid running towards you dragging the Ranger by its lead. "Woah, woah! Ssstop!" The Clansmen brings the Equinoid to a halt, but only because the horse has stopped right before Jerry. "Thisss one broke out of containment and chasssed you all the way out here. Guesss ssshe really likesss your friend. Might asss well keep her, we got plenty more."

name: NEBULA_CLAN_PLUSHIES
text: It seems you've found another lodge established within the nebula. Oddly enough, it seems to have been repurposed as a... tourist location?

event.text: A Clansman Ranger is leaning against a wall, talking to a small gathering of Zoltan officials, who leave shortly after you enter. "Pffft, imagine being sssuch a ssstick in the mud. Those Zoltans came here to assssk if I have a PERMIT to run thissss ssstore! Whossse sssector do they think thissss isss anywaysss? Didn't even buy anything..."
"Ah, I'm glad you asssked! Plussshiess! Of varioussss exotic creaturessss I've ssseen acrosss the galaxy. Come on, take a look! You'd probably be the firsssst persssson to buy one anywaysss..."
"That there'ss a G.A.Sss! That'ssss sshort for 'Giant Alien Ssspider.' No idea what the sssciencey term isss, that'sss jusst what everyone callsss them."
"Oh, well thanksss for your busssinesss! That'sss probably my firssst profit in... well ever. Guessss ssetting up ssshop in a nebula wasssn't a good idea."

"Y-you want all of them? Well I'll be... You either REALLY like my plussshiesss, or you're one hell of a philanthropissst. I'll tell you what, sssince my busssinesss here ain't going too well, I think I'll ssstick with you for a while!"
"Well, goodbye then. Thanksss for making my day, traveler!"
"Ah, oh well. Thanksss for atleassst entertaining the idea..."
"That there'ss an Equinoid! They got 6 legsss, and they ain't technically a horssse. Heard there'sss even a couple of them ssscattered around thisss ssector! Not that I'm sssuprissed."
"Oh, well thanksss for your busssinesss! That'sss probably my firssst profit in... well ever. Guessss ssetting up ssshop in a nebula wasssn't a good idea."

"Y-you want all of them? Well I'll be... You either REALLY like my plussshiesss, or you're one hell of a philanthropissst. I'll tell you what, sssince my busssinesss here ain't going too well, I think I'll ssstick with you for a while!"
"Well, goodbye then. Thanksss for making my day, traveler!"
"Ah, oh well. Thanksss for atleassst entertaining the idea..."
"That there'ss a... well I don't actually know the name. They're jusssst lizard thingsss I guessss."
"Oh, well thanksss for your busssinesss! That'sss probably my firssst profit in... well ever. Guessss ssetting up ssshop in a nebula wasssn't a good idea."

Once again, your murderous tendencies have taken the spotlight, and you are now attacking more people.
You have better things to do than visiting random tourist traps.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_SHELL_MECHANIC
text: A Shell Mechanic resides here. They contact you the moment you arrive. "Are you here to oppose thhhhe Guild? Or are you here to support thhhhem?"

event.text: "Thhhhen you shall die withhhh thhhe rest of thhhe occupiers!"

name: CLAN_MECHANIC_BELIEF
text: "Ahhhh, so you are an ally, thhhhen. Would you like us to patch up your ship? Or are you more in need of supplies?"

event.text: "Good choice, it is what we pride ourselves on."
"We can spare a few. Make good use of thhhhem."
"We can spare a few. Make good use of thhhhem."
"If you need scrap thhhhat badly, we can give you some of our reserves. Don't waste it."
"Thhhhen good luck out thhhhere."

name: NEBULA_CLAN_SHELLANGRY
text: A civilian Shell ship has found themselves deep in Guild space, but they don't seem scared of the ravenous hunters out there looking for blood. Instead, they look furious to see you here. "Oh great, now thhhhe Federation is getting involved with thhhe Guild? Why don't you get a conscience and stop killing innocent people you scum!"

choice.text: How dare you call us scum!

event.text: You try not to think about how you're proving the Shell's point and prepare to defend yourself... through violent murder.

Your Shell reasons with the others, explaining you're only going through this sector to get to Node 17 on your mission. Luckily, the Shells are reasonable and apologize, and offer some fuel and scrap to aid you.

Your Monk reasons with the Shells, explaining you're only going through this sector to get to Node 17 on your mission, and that immediately accusing foreigners of having blood on their hands is an irrational behavior. Luckily, the Shells are reasonable and apologize, and offer some fuel and scrap to aid you.
You shut down the Shell ship's oxygen, frightening them into submission. "Ok, I'm sorry we called you scum! We surrender!"

name: NEBULA_CLAN_SHELL_RADIANT
text: You almost immediately receive a brief message from a nearby Shell Radiant vessel. "Might want to hurry away, Renegade. Thhhe Geniocracy has dispatched military forces to thhhis sector and thhhings might get messy soon."

choice.text: What's the Geniocracy doing in Guild space?

event.text: You aren't sure if you expected a response, but fortunately a friendly Radiant appears on the screen, who's more than willing to talk. "Thhhe EHG has been hunting our species for far too long. We didn't want to risk an all out war with thhhe Kleptocracy, but it's time we finally take a stand. We will drive thhhhe Guild out of thhhis sector and force the Kleptocracy to regulate thhheir activity, or die trying. And I don't plan on dying."

choice.text: Defend the Guild and attack the Radiants!

event.text: You aren't quite sure how to justify your actions, but you're sure you can think of something convincing later. For now, time to fight!

choice.text: Offer your assistance to the Shells.

event.text: "You want to help? Well I suppose it doesn't hurt. We could use some supplies if you have any."
"Thhhhank you Federation. Well since we have plenty of missiles now, I guess we don't need thhhis drone."
"Thhhhank you Federation. Well since we have plenty of drone parts now, I guess we don't need thhhis weapon."
"I have a feeling you aren't part of thhhhe Geniocracy... buuuuuut we Shells must stick togethhhher. Maybe thhhhis will help?"
"Thhhank you Federation. And may you have good luck with your mission as well."

choice.text: Abide by their warning and leave.

event.text: You now have some time on your hands.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_SUZERAIN
text: The nearby system holds a Suzerain muttering to himself as they fly through the nebula. They don't seem to care much about your presence here.

event.text: "No bother me! Guild stealing all of kills. What happen to time when Hive most feared, and claimed all prey? Space now Clan territory, disgusting!"

"Haha, stupid Federation captain thinking all nebula sector once nebula sector! Haven't ever heard of Coalition Cealaforming tech? Guild, trading with Coalition, buying many many cealaformer to make this sector!"

choice.text: Yeah, I think I've fought one of those before.

event.text: "Having you? Then you do good service to all galaxy! Slug thinking they can make everything nebula? Well they wrong! Federation got them, apparently! Hahah! This service cannot go unpaid!"
"Of course not having met one! Secret Coalition tech, not for Federation knowing! Wait, oh I make an oopsie. Cannot let anyone know I told you this!"

choice.text: Why? Is the Guild not part of the Kleptocracy, which is part of the Coalition?

event.text: "Well, yes. But Guild conversion of sector not Kleptocracy doing. And Coalition much like Federation, have own hangar, budget, soldier. They not just giving Cealaformer away to hunter."

choice.text: If the Guild wasn't supposed to use Cealaformer tech here, why did the Coalition sell it to them?

event.text: "Probably because Slug doing dirty behind other member back! Or... I not knowing. All I know is this not once nebula sector, and now Guild stealing all precious prey here!"

choice.text: Is this sector home to some exotic species?

event.text: "Yes and no. Most, Guild bring here themselves. Look, asking too many question! I said not bother me, and you bothering me!"
"Yes yes, whatever. Now leave!"
"GAH! YOU SO ANNOYING! DIE!"

choice.text: But aren't the Mantis and Slugs allied? Through the Coalition, that is?

event.text: "No no, tiny Federation brain fail to understand. See, Coalition is much like Federation. Engi, Zoltan, Orchid, Human, except with better race, like Mantis... and other ones."
"Gah! You not understanding. Yes, we ally. But Coalition border not work like Federation border. All race keep to own territory, and share Coalition territory."

choice.text: Wouldn't that mean the EHG is only hunting in Slug territory?

event.text: "Are deaf? You miss entire point! EHG should only hunting in Slug space. This NOT Slug space! This sector claimed after Slug Expansion Wars end. Filthy Slugs never follow treaties!"

choice.text: Why don't the other members of the Coalition step in?

event.text: "Rockman not caring, Leech too busy. Hive afraid of more conflict, hit very hard during Expansion Wars. It seeming like I only one who caring..."

choice.text: Why not take matters into your own hands?

event.text: "And do what? I one Mantis. Slug, many many Slug. You thinking I can kill entire Kleptocracy by self? You stupid man! Your brain size of Algerian Berry! Haha! That very small, if not knowing. I saying you dumb. Now leave alone."

"At least Federation biding by border laws, even if always argue with each other. Coalition is too weak, doom to fail. Perhaps it time to seek alternative before I caught in crossfires of civil dispute..."

"HAHAHAHAH! You very funny! And also dumb. I not joining Federation in million year! You no space for Mantis, too busy letting Free Mantis ruin your land. Now, you have wasted enough of time. Get gone."

choice.text: (Hive Mantis Crew) Convince him to join you.

event.text: "Federation having Mantis? I here thinking only Free Mantis welcome. Federation might be in bad spot, but not bad as Coalition! I take offer, captain."

choice.text: Why not go solo? Surely as a Suzerain you could be a famous bounty hunter in no time.

event.text: "Oooh! Federation making the good idea now! Yes, claws sharp, claws kill! I be rich in time not at all! You are genius, even if still smelly and stupid. For your most intelligent idea accepting this, I not needing it soon enough!"

choice.text: What treaty? Who did this land belong to first?

event.text: "After Slug Expansion Wars Coalition form and make pact, none take land from other race. Each race has own expansion law, Slugs let keep all of nebula. This sector within Hive limits, yet Slug take it first!"

choice.text: Why not take matters into your own hands?

event.text: "And do what? I one Mantis. Slug, many many Slug. You thinking I can kill entire Kleptocracy by self? You stupid man! Your brain size of Algerian Berry! Haha! That very small, if not knowing. I saying you dumb. Now leave alone."

choice.text: Couldn't you just ask for permission to hunt here? The EHG seems fairly friendly to tourists and outsiders.

event.text: "Oh! For once, Federation have good idea. Why not thinking that, instead of killing Slug... You make good point. I pay you for having smart brain and helping me."

choice.text: But don't you all hate each other?

event.text: "Yes, of course! Slug greedy, Rockman slow, dumb. Leech smelly, reminding me of old corpse as I wishing they were. Mantis not standing these, but Hive say alliance good for keeping Slug out of Mantis territory."

choice.text: Wouldn't an alliance mean more Slugs are in Mantis Territory?

event.text: "If it were dumb Federation, yes! But we smarter, alliance not grant permit for other race in other territory. Coalition territory shared, all others independent. Vital for Coalition survival. Making sense to you?"
"Good. Now stop talking me, very boring and tiresome."
"Gah, very annoying. Ask too many question, not understand anything! Federation captain miniscule intelligence, I will kill!"

choice.text: I see. This definitely answers my question.

event.text: "Good. Now stop talking me, very boring and tiresome."

choice.text: I feel you man. Slugs suck.

event.text: "Yes yes, we agree on this. Glad see other rational thinking man in space, even if smelly Fed! We Slug hater must band together, and fight off smelly Slug." The Suzerain is so pleased with you agreeing with him he even offers to patch up some of your hull damage.

choice.text: This guy is in a bad mood, don't bother him.

event.text: You don't know why the Hive has one of its most feared warriors so far out in Slug space, but it's probably not good.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_TAX
text: You've only just barely entered the beacon when a Clansman ship flies past, tailed by several large Clairvoyant vessels. You know the EHG is still a part of the Kleptocracy, so you can't imagine why they might be sending the enforcers out here.

event.text: You pursue the Slugs through the nebula, where you find the Clansmen have hunkered up in a cave, and won't come out. The Clairvoyants appear to be at a loss.

"You ssssee, normally the Kleptocracy doessssn't get involved in EHG affairsss, but their membersss are ssstill citizensss of our nation, and they have taxesss to pay. Assss you can tell, the men who've locked themssselvesss in that cave owe... quite a lot."
"Ohhh, uh, about 17 million. In Kleptocracy Oseroes. If I wasss to transsslate that into ssscrap, which ssseems to be the currency around here, it comesss to around... 260 million."

choice.text: Use some missiles to blow the Clansmen out of the cave.

event.text: You lay the bombs all around the cave then wait for them to explode. The impact sends the cave crumbling in and forcing the Clansmen out, where they're arrested.

choice.text: Fight the Clairvoyants to aid the Clansmen.

event.text: You're known to be one to commit many crimes yourself in your travels. Though yours are normally warcrimes and this is a case of tax evasion, that doesn't mean you can't help a fellow criminal out. In the name of the Federation, of course.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Try to reason with the Clansmen.

event.text: Your Slug goes up to the awning of the cave, where he speaks with the Clansmen. Playing off of their better reason, he convinces them that dying trapped in a cave is a far worse fate than going to prison, even if it's a Slug one. This works, and the Clansmen surrender.

"Oh! Uh, sssir! I didn't sssee you there, my king. Er, ex-king. I don't... you don't really have authority over thisss sssir, but I'm a Clairvoyant, and I think you did great thingsss for our nation, even if you weren't the bessst leader at timesss. If you're willing to ssstand up for thessse men though, I won't quessstion it." The Slug clears their debts, then flies away.

choice.text: What a funky and unpredictable situation. Anyways, I'm bored; time to move on.

event.text: You now have some time on your hands.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_TAX_SAVECLAN
text: You approach the Clansmen, who whisper "Are they gone?" Once you assure them the Clairvoyants are gone, they exit the cave and thank you. "Haha! Tax evasssion worksss out flawlesssly once again. Uh... I guessss I ssshould reward you. How about a reactor upgrade?"

name: NEBULA_CLAN_TAX_SAVEKLEPT
text: "Ah, well that handlessss that. Thank you, Federation. Didn't know you had interessst in helping with Kleptocracy affairsss. Perhapsss a bit of scrap will help compenssate for your help in ressolving thisss isssue."

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_CLAN_GHOST
text: You aren't sure from where, but you're receiving a hail from a Guild Ranger. "Up for a bit of work? Ssssome Ghossstsss sssstole my ssship! I intend to get it back, through any methodsss I can, and you look like a damn well efficient one."

event.text: "Good, good! Jusssst pleassse don't dessstroy it!"
You aren't some chump change mercenary. You have standards! You mute the Slug.

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_CLAN_DUSK
text: A distress signal appears to be coming from a Clansman ship being pursued by a Duskbringer. You are promptly hailed: "Pleasssse help! We made a terrible missstake, trying to ssstudy how Dussskbringer explosssion tech workss on live captivesss... now they're mad and want usss dead. I'm not sssuprissed to be honessst but pleassse ssstill help?"

event.text: You arm the weapons and engage the Duskbringer vessel.
You arm the weapons and engage the Clansman vessel.
You mute the Clansmen and continue on with your unhelpful existence.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_CLAN_STORM
text: This beacon is impaired by a passing ion storm. A Guild ship reveals itself, with obvious hostile intentions. It's unsurprising to say the least: these conditions only further encourage their tendencies to prey upon targets, as if they were encircling a beast caught in a bear trap.

name: NEBULA_CLAN_PHEROMONES
text: You've seen a lot of things in your travels, but you don't think you've ever seen the wastes of half a Mantis fleet lying before a Guild megastructure. A massive mechanic arm appears to be collecting the wrecks one by one and moving them towards a small docking bay.

event.text: You pilot towards the structure and enter through a hangar door, where you're greeted by a Clansman. "Oh god, you aren't here to ssshut usss down, are you?"

"Oh thank god. Wait, ssso why are you here? Have you come to watch my operation? Thisss here isss a pheromone extraction plant. The pheromone bussinesss isss booming, and we want to get a firm grip on it before thossse Free Mantiss bastardsss monopolize the whole thing."
"Pleasssure doing bussinessss with you! Jusssst don't tell the Federation. Or the Hive. Actually, jusssst don't tell anyone pleassse."

choice.text: Where did all the Mantis come from?

event.text: "Oh well uh... we bought them from the Ghosssstsss. Yeah, that sssoundsss... believable."

choice.text: Then where did the Ghosts get this many Mantis ships from?

event.text: "Thhhheeeee... Mantissss ssstore?"

choice.text: I didn't know that was a thing.

event.text: "Oh no yeah, it'sss definitely real! I can give you the coordinatesss, if you'd like!"
"Oh pissss off Federation! You can't judge me!" The Clansman scurries away and sounds the alarm. Looks like we have to fight!
"Uhhhh, ok..." The Clansman quickly draws out a pen and scribbles down some barely legible numbers, hands them to you, then scurries off.

choice.text: Sounds cool, but we don't have any reason to stick around.

event.text: If you don't want to risk ending up like these Mantis, you probably shouldn't get any closer.

name: CLAN_PHEROMONES_DEMAND
text: "Alright, you've killed my men, now what? Are you going to ssshut down my facility? Arressst me? Make me do an embarrassssing dance?"

event.text: You don't technically have the authority to do this, but that's never stopped you before. You pretend you know what you're doing and seize all that you can carry, then order them to close down the building. You know they probably won't, but in the end you got what you wanted.

You don't actually have handcuffs on you, and you aren't really sure what you're doing. Fortunately the Clansman doesn't seem to know Federation law very well either, so when you tell him it's standard for Federation criminals to do service aboard the ship holding the arrest, he doesn't question it.
Sorrowfully, the Clansman does a waltz, but eventually breaks down into a sobbing heap. You take pity on the poor creature and only steal some of his scrap instead of all of it.

choice.text: (Zoltan Crew) Carry out this arrest in an official manner.

event.text: Your Zoltan breaks out a pair of handcuffs from somewhere and cuffs the Clansmen one by one. They order the facility shut down, citing various codes if you hadn't known better would have assumed were made up, then ushers the Clansmen aboard your ship and confiscated several crates of supplies. When you ask what happens next, your Zoltan shrugs and figures you might as well make use of all this.

name: NEBULA_QUEST_CLAN_PHEROMONES_STORE

unvisitedTooltip.text: Overly suspicious coordinates provided by a Ranger.

text: Even though it's more than likely that Clansman was lying, you still take a trip to the coordinates he specified. Fascinatingly, you see a junkyard of Mantis ships with a Ghost-populated Mantis ship guarding it.

choice.text: Excuse me, is this the Mantis store?

event.text: It takes a few silent moments until your translator can work out the quirks of Ghost dialect - "Yes, and welcome. We sell used Mantis ships. Our stock is greatly diminished after a large shipment was ordered by the members of a renowned Guild, but there's surely a pleasant model still available for your needs."

This is probably the most scrap you've ever spent on one item before, but hopefully it's worth it. The Ghosts bring over a Mantis ship, which you find still contains the corpses of the previous crew, and their weapons as well!
While you don't have much use for the ship itself, you might as well scrap all that you can. You start with the weapons...
You pull another weapon off of the hull.
You pull another weapon off of the hull.
You pull another weapon off of the hull.
You pull another weapon off of the hull.
You arm the weapons and attack the Ghost ship.

choice.text: Well, there's not much reason to stick around.

event.text: This is too much, even for you. Some things just aren't meant to be known, seen, or interacted with. This is one of those you reckon, and steer course as far away as possible.

name: NEBULA_QUEST_CLAN_PHEROMONES_STORE_CHOICE
text: The Ghosts are gone, but the shipyard still appears to have many Ghosts wandering about. Do you risk salvaging some supplies before you go?

event.text: You scrounge around in the Mantis ships and grab some more supplies, but an angry team of Ghosts climbs aboard to avenge their fallen friends!

choice.text: Don't take the risk and leave.

name: BOUGHT_THE_GHOST_SHIP
text: Though you've taken everything you need from the ship for now, you figure there's no harm in sending the wreck back to the Federation hangar... because why not?

name: PONY_WORLD
text: It seems you've stumbled across a lush planet teeming with all kinds of exotic life. Judging from the impossibly well kept grasslands and the breathtaking rock sculptures, it seems this must be one of the EHG's best maintained hunting grounds. These locations are reserved for only the wealthiest of customers, not just Clansmen, and are stocked with lifeforms bred offworld. The planet seems to be entirely untouched by infrastructure, though scans show a single abnormality. A ship is on the surface.

event.text: You fly your ship near the crashed ship, noticing that it's a Guild vessel. It's incredibly old however and shows signs of rusting. Several brightly colored equinoids graze nearby, and you watch them peacefully roam when a voice speaks to you. "Do not disturb the equinoids, friend. They are tortured souls, the Guild is not kind."

You spin around but see no one. You lay your eyes on a hazy grey cloud that seems to engulf the area in front of you but are uncertain what it is. "Do not be afraid. We are nothing but an ancient voice. We are the Story Teller, and we have been an overseer of these lands for many years. Would you like to hear a story?"

You take a seat next to the grazing ponies, and one wanders over and plants its muzzle on your shoulder. The clouds move around you in seemingly patternless motions as he begins his story. "Once, many years ago, there was a boy who would come here with his uncle. His father was gone, and his mother dead. His uncle was a proud man, but the boy was meek. These trips were unusual and not an easy liberty, but his uncle wanted so desperately to earn the boy's affection."

"At first they came and simply watched the wildlife, but they never got too close. His uncle forbade it. One day, his uncle brought a gun. He showed the boy how to use it, and shot a bird from the sky. But all the boy did was cry. His uncle did not understand, and every day this would repeat itself. The pair would come, an animal would die, the boy would cry. The boy wielded the gun several times, and he fired it with deadly accuracy, but never once would he hit an animal. Instead, he would shoot cans and stones."

"One day, his uncle simply gave up. He stayed in his ship and let the boy free. He hoped he would learn to grow cold once he saw the equinoids did not share the same love for him as he did for them. But the boy would eagerly spend every day feeding the equinoids in bliss. The equinoids treated them as one of their own foals. The boy and the equinoids had more in common than the boy's own uncle. Bastardized and left without a home, forced into a new purpose by a master who did not understand their true nature."

"Every day the boy would beg his uncle to travel here, and every day his uncle's jealousy grew. How could the boy love a mindless alien more than his own flesh and blood? One day, the equinoids roamed further than they had before, and the boy followed. Soon, he even left the sight of his uncle, who in a panic realized he had lost track of the precious child and rushed after him. The boy wandered aimlessly but never afraid until he found a wreck. Mossy and rusted the ship lay in a state of disrepair, piloted by a lost Engi."

"The Engi was wounded, having been shot down by a Clansman who had seen through the disguise of his stolen craft. The Engi, too, had befriended the equinoids, and the equinoids thought it was time the boy meet the Engi. Good friends the two became, and for hours they talked of nothing in particular. The Engi had seen many things in his travels but understood little, while the boy had been so sheltered yet understood everything he had seen. The boy taught the Engi many things, and the Engi amused the boy with many stories."

"As night fell, the boy grew tired and bid the Engi goodnight. He walked away, guided once again by the equinoids. The boy never returned. We do not know what happened to him. We miss his voice. The equinoids make good company, but they do not understand our stories..."

choice.text: I assume you are the Engi in the story?

event.text: "Yes. But we are that Engi no more. We have been separated from the Harmony for so long we can hardly remember what it was like. We are nothing but guardians of this place. Many ships come and go. We do not mind them, as long as they do not disturb the equinoids..."

choice.text: No, but we'll stay for a while.

event.text: "Good. It is rare someone takes the time to admire the beauty of foreign lands like these. Visitors come often, but they merely come and go in a hurry. We do not mind them, as long as they do not disturb the equinoids..."

choice.text: We don't have time for stories. We have to go.

event.text: "A shame. No one has time these days... Well, we shall not leave this place. Carry on traveler. If you ever change your mind, you know where we'll be..."
The EHG probably won't like you poking around their special hunting areas. Best not to risk it.

name: PONY_WORLD_HUNTERS
text: As if right on cue, a new vessel arrives. A dark black hull suggests this is some special, highly important Slug vessel. They don't seem to mind you and land nearby, drawing out their hunting gear and making pleasant small talk. That is, until the Story Teller wanders over to them, and politely asks that they move their vessel somewhere else so as to not disturb the equinoids. The Slugs break into laughter and immediately begin to aim their guns mockingly at the ponies.

event.text: As expected, the Slugs don't take kindly to you interupting them. "Why'sss a Federation ssship here anywayssss? Thissss isss Guild territory! Looksss like you jussst became our next hunt!"

choice.text: Seems trouble is brewing. Best we leave.

name: PONY_WORLD_WIN
text: The Slug vessel has been destroyed. Unfortunately the wreckage damages the landscape, but none of the animals are hit. While you are scrapping the wreckage you notice several Slugs are still on the ground tormenting the equinoids.

event.text: Before you can do anything, the grey cloud suddenly grows larger and conceals the Slugs in a curtain of grey. You hear a blood curdling scream and suddenly the cloud dissipates, leaving nothing but a puddle of lacerated flesh and blood. "We warned them not to disturb the equinoids... Some people simply do not listen..."

You watch as the Story Teller floats back to their ship, where it waits for you. "It is unusual that you chose to assist us. It is true you found this place because of our vessel, correct? Then take it. We have no need for it any more."
"Goodbye, friend. We will make sure your story does not go untold..."

choice.text: (Jerry) "I think I'm the boy in your story..."

event.text: The Story Teller drifts over to Jerry, and slowly begins to condense into the form of a crimson Engi. "Our friend. It has been so long since we have seen you... How have the stars aligned to grant us this reunion? We can still see the innocence in your eyes. We apologize for our ramblings. How we wish we could join you, but we cannot. What we can offer is a gift. We wish you the best of journeys, Jerry, and your friends. Now this story can finally have a happy ending..."

choice.text: Offer to take the Story Teller with you.

event.text: "We're afraid we must never leave this place. A good guardian would never leave behind that which they protect. You have no need for us regardless. We are not fighters. Do not worry, we will make sure your story does not go untold..."

name: SYLVAN_SALT_QUEST_INTRO_CHAOS
text: You step aboard the lodge, feeling almost as if you're meant to expect someone here. Yet, no one steps forward. You wander around until you catch an intriguing conversation between a Clansman and a pirate concerning an individual called the "Saltman". You sit down at the table adjacent to them and lean in closer to hear what they're saying.

event.text: Suddenly, you hear a loud and obnoxious voice ringing in your ear, that causes you to fall out of your chair. You look up and see the gnome has mysteriously appeared on the table and is now yelling at you. Annoyed at your strange behavior, the station owners ask you to leave. You apologize and blame it on the gnome, which only confuses them more. After some arguing back and forth whether the gnome is real or not, you head back to the ship and find a mysterious set of coordinates pinned to your dashboard with a note. "Please find him for me. -S"

name: SYLVAN_SALT_QUEST_INTRO_NOPE
text: You step aboard the lodge, feeling almost as if you're meant to expect someone here. Yet, no one steps forward. You wander around until you catch an intriguing conversation between a Clansman and a pirate concerning an individual called the "Saltman". name: COALITION_FED_RECON
text: The beacon seems to be little more than a planet with a small industrialized settlement.

event.text: After a short pause, a Federation stealth ship decloaks nearby and hails you. "Ah, an ally! We've been performing reconnaissance here. Let me explain."
As you prepare to attack them, the Federation ship seems to fumble for their weapons. They weren't expecting your aggression.

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Something is off. Do a deep scan of the region.

event.text: Your sensors detect a cloaked Federation ship. It's trying to avoid detection from the planet below - and seemingly you as well.
The ship decloaks, their response is curt. "What do you want? You're going to jeopardize our mission."
"Is that so? Fine. We'll explain."
"Damn it! I knew they couldn't be trusted!" You hear them say, as they rush to their battlestations.
As soon as you force them to decloak, they approach you at an attack vector. "We know how you operate, Renegade! You catch us off guard!"
There's nothing more to do here, except perhaps some activity on your ship.

name: RECON_EXPLAIN_MISSION
text: "This planet is a production facility for high-end Coalition equipment. Best case scenario, we sabotage it without them becoming the wiser.
