choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Force the Alpha to split.

event.text: After being struck by your weapon, the Alpha begins to shake more violently, and suddenly erupts into a fine mist, slowly reforming into two separate Ghosts. The twins look at each other and begin to scream, but are subdued by the confused medical staff. "What in the great nebula has occurred? This is not how the process is intended to go about! I-I truly am uncertain of what to consider of this situation. These ones are not... uh... we would rather not have them in the field of battle. Have them instead."

You catch various odd phrases among the Shell's speech like "plasma membrane" and "rapid sub-division of the quantum something something". Does it mean anything? You're inclined to say no. Later, your Shell does indeed tell you that they made up everything they said, but it seems to register with the Alpha who finally agrees to go through with the process. The medical team pays you for your help.
Voluntarily putting yourself closer to the firing range of an elite Dynasty vessel doesn't sound like the best idea right now.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_TRINKETS
text: "The demons linger about... come aboard, it's safe from them here. I have many wonders aboard, maybe you'd like one?" A softly speaking Ghost waves for you to come aboard.

event.text: You step aboard the ship, surprised to find it's full of oxygen. Around the walls are hanging various small trinkets. "These are my prized creations. Would you care for one? Only 10 scrap..."

choice.text: Buy a totem of war [+8% weapon fire rate].
Buy an emblem of speed [+20% crew movement speed, +20% FTL recharge rate].
Buy an ingot of fortitude [+20% shield charge speed, +10% system sabotage resistance].

event.text: You have better things to do than looking at 'wonders' right now.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_TRINKETS_WAR
text: "Heheh... just don't ask how it works." You head back to the ship, uncertain what to do with the object. You finally decide to place it on your dashboard and hope it works.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_TRINKETS_SPEED
text: "Heheh... just don't ask how it works." You head back to the ship, uncertain what to do with the object. You finally decide to place it on your dashboard and hope it works.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_TRINKETS_SHIELD
text: "Heheh... just don't ask how it works." You head back to the ship, uncertain what to do with the object. You finally decide to place it on your dashboard and hope it works.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_INTERROGATION
text: Looks like something important is going on nearby. You pull closer and see a group of Dynasty vessels parked around a disabled Auto-ship, shouting at it with their weapons charged.

event.text: "We have captured the demon! Hark, yet it speaks not. Speak foul beast, speak! By the command of the Prime Reaper, we demand ye speak!"
The Ghost's 'head' swivels to face you. "Huh? What garble do you speak?"

choice.text: It's not alive. It's just a machine.
(Engineer Crew) Interface with the Auto and "make it speak".

event.text: Your engineer remotely access the Auto-ship and powers it online. Fortunately, its vocal module is still active. "OooOooOoOoh! You have captured me. You are now cursed! If you do not give the Federation all of your scrap, your children will be stillborn and your crops will be plagued. OooOoOoOoooOh!" The Ghosts suddenly go into panic, scrambling for a weapon, until they realize you're a Federation ship. Desperate not to be cursed, they give you all of their scrap.

choice.text: (Upg. Hacking) Interface with the Auto and "make it speak".

event.text: You stealthily deploy your hacking module onto the Auto-ship and power it up. Fortunately, its vocal module is still active. "OooOooOoOoh! You have captured me. You are now cursed! If you do not give the Federation all of your scrap, your children will be stillborn and your crops will be plagued. OooOoOoOoooOh!" The Ghosts suddenly go into panic, scrambling for a weapon, until they realize you're a Federation ship. Desperate not to be cursed, they give you all of their scrap.
These Ghosts don't seem to realize the Auto-ships can't speak. At least, not unless programmed to. Sentient Auto-ships? That's silly...
This looks pretty serious, and it's probably safest to not intervene.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_UNIQUE_HACKERBID
text: You weren't really prepared to encounter a Slug Hacker vessel out here, but it looks like they're having some sort of auction with a few pirates and even a Reaper vessel!

event.text: The Hacker pauses his counting to introduce you. "Why, I have invented a pieccce of tech unlike any you've ssseen. Capable of fully disssabling autopilotsss running only off of nonessssential backup power, or ssshut it off entirely for only 2 reactor barsss! These Dynasssty folkssss ssseem to really want it. If you're gonna bid, you'll have to enter at leasssst, oh, 30 ssscrap."
"Then let the bidding begin!"

The Slug begins to call off numbers, and eventually the Dynasty raises the price.
							Current Price: 30 scrap.

Still pretty low. The Phantoms raise almost immediately.
									Current Price: 35 scrap.
The sounds of numbers being rapidly listed off quickly fades as you distance yourself from the auction.

name: DYNASTY_UNIQUE_HACKERBID_65
text: At last, the Ghosts give up, and none of the other pirates bother to move. Looks like you've won! The Hackers declare you the winner. "Well then, pay up for your prize!"

event.text: The Slugs are furious, and immediately engage! Looks like you aren't getting that augment...

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_SMUGGLER
text: A black smuggler ship comes drifting out of the nebula a few minutes after you jump in. "Good, just who we've been hoping to see. A ship with guns better than ours! I'd be surprised if you haven't caught wind of these Ghosts yet. Dynasty, more like DyNASTY! Am I right? Right? Yeah ok. Anyways, we're carrying a shipment full of 'unethically obtained' armaments or however you fancy people say it. Dynasty won't cooperate and just let us through. There's a security checkpoint nearby. Take it out or 'convince' them to let us pass and we've got a spicy new weapon for you. Deal?"

event.text: You approach the station, and are surprised to find they hail you first! "Be on the watch, trouble is stirring in the nebulas. A pirate with dangerous cargo has been spotted, but their location remains unknown. If you have any information on their whereabouts, do not hesitate to share it."
The most reliable way to help the smugglers is simply to blow these Ghosts up. Hopefully should be easy enough.
"For what is this generous donation? Hark? To turn a back to the security of this beacon for the next 5 hours? Well, I do suppose this is a deal we can arrange."
You hail the smugglers, letting them know it's safe. "A bribe? How boring, I was looking for some damn fireworks! But, I'm a man of my word. Sometimes. Right now I am. But not always. Here you go."

choice.text: Sell them the location of the smugglers.

event.text: You doubt the Smugglers are going to give you a weapon after this, but it was effortless scrap, and who can complain about that?

choice.text: (Savior of the Dynasty) Could you do us a favor?

event.text: "Oh the gods bestow upon me an honor like I never knew! An embarrassment, I am, for not having recognized the savior of our lands! Yes, yes, we will do anything!" You kindly ask them to allow your smuggler 'friends' through, and they oblige without hesitation.
You hail the smugglers, letting them know it's safe. "Hah, what was that? I was looking for some damn fireworks! But, I'm a man of my word. Sometimes. Right now I am. But not always. Here you go."
You don't make deals with pirates, but you'll gladly fight them instead!

choice.text: We aren't going to work for some smugglers.

event.text: You somewhat rudely decline the smugglers' offer and fly away.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_AUTOQUEST
text: Almost immediately, you receive a hail from what appears to be an Auto-station lingering nearby. "Hello. This is a prerecorded message for all nearby non-Dynasty vessels. The nearby settlement of Ghosts has proven problematic for the Rebellion. Recapture it, and this platform is authorized to reward you with a drone."

event.text: It feels weird working for the Rebellion, but you can't think of anything more satisfyingly ironic than using their own weapon against them. Assuming you succeed, of course. As you approach the colony, one of their vessels rises to face you.
It means you won't get the weapon, but it's much easier just to kill this Auto-station than to go fight a Dynasty colony. Plus, it means not working for the Rebellion!

choice.text: Let them sort out the problem on their own.

event.text: Neither the Rebels' nor the Dynasty's problems matter to you.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_ZOLTAUTO
text: You notice the shadow of a ship slipping through the nebulas behind you, and begin to fear it might be following you, until it comes bursting out of the clouds, revealing itself to be a Dynasty vessel. Their weapons are off however, and their comms are open for communication.

event.text: "We have identified you as a Multiverse Renegade vessel. Does this statement hold true? If so, we suspect you are not opposed to matters of mercenary work. A ship of automated nature but Zoltan origins has been spotted dangerously close to a loyal Dynasty colony. While these do not pose the same threat as a Rebel vessel, it could create hysteria of immense proportions amongst our citizens. Could you disable it?"

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_DESERTERS
text: From the depths of the clouds approaches a Dynasty ship, their captain speaking in a soft whisper of static. "Please aid us... we are no longer of the mind to take part in the Reaper's war. I desire an outing. May I desert to your ship?" Before you can even consider responding, you notice a quick blur of motion in the distance. Looks like the deserters are being followed.

choice.text: Allow the Ghost onto the crew.
Tough luck, but we aren't getting involved.

event.text: You cut comms and distance yourself from the Dynasty ships.

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_LOST
text:
You notice an unusual amount of static over your radio. You play with it a bit until suddenly your translator switches on and begins to spit out dialogue from a Dynasty ship concealed nearby. "We are but hopelessly disoriented, you brainless bobolyne!"
		
	"Oh close thine mouth, you worthless bespawler. We have no brains, we are but gas! This senseless debauchery of the insults will present us no solution."

event.text: "Oh, Reaper's sweet travesty, you are Federation! We shall take no 'help' from you, fiend!" This wasn't the reaction you expected, but if you can force them into surrendering perhaps they'll finally be willing to take your help?
"Oh, but speak not further! For it seems a fellow is offering us their most charitable aid. Many thanks, good friend. We shan't let this favor go forgotten."
It's better to let the Ghosts bicker between themselves than to let a Dynasty ship harass you.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_DYNASTY_OCCUPIED
text: While it can be hard to tell the differences between nebulas, something is definitely off here. Several bright lights through the clouds guide you to a massive Dynasty mining colony, built in loosely-joined structures around a fleet of ancient and dilapidated ships. You expect to see heavy traffic, or at least signs of activity, but the colony is mostly dormant. Even stranger, a fleet of Duskbringer ships have surrounded the colony as well. What could be happening here?

event.text: You land on the only landing pad that seems to be unguarded in the entire colony. As you make the uncomfortable waddle through the depressurized hallways in your burdensome space suits, you notice several very well armed and suited Duskbringer patrols moving back and forth, and the occasional Phantom lingering about only to duck into an alley or building when any soldiers go past.

Making sure not to be spotted, you duck between alleyways and follow the patrols. Eventually you find the commander's office, which clearly once belonged to a proud Phantom instead. "Renegades, in my colony? Hm, more likely than I thought. Didn't think anyone else was stupid enough to come to this forsaken place full of gasbags. Do you know how many times I've been called a 'breather' here? What kind of insult even is that? Sure, we have to wear these big ugly suits just so we can breathe, but at least our biology isn't comprised of hot air!"
					
					The Duskbringer smirks and leans back in her chair. "But I'm getting carried away. I assume you're peaceful, since you aren't shooting yet. So, if you're up for it... I have an offer. We took this colony a few weeks back in hopes of securing part of the Dynasty's Aether supply. It's gone wonderfully, except these damn Phantoms started teaming up. Now, the Dynasty's sending Vagabond hitmen to screw with us, hoping we'll leave before long. I sure as hell ain't losing to a species as inferior as this. Hmph. The Dynasty had its prime some eons ago, but now it's time for a new glorious empire. One run by Zoltans, but to make that happen first we need the kind of weapons this Aether will go towards making. Intel suggests a hidden fleet is waiting for a good chance to strike. Take out their leader and I'll compensate you."

You aren't sure how it'd reflect on the Federation to be assisting the Duskbringers like this, but the Dynasty is no ally of the Federation either. If the 'compensation' will help you in your mission, then so be it.

You duck into one of the alleyways and try checking the insides of several buildings. Eventually you find what seems to be a hideout constructed inside an abandoned warehouse. "Who comes to this zone of control? Be you Duskbringer? Or perhaps a fellow countryman or Vagabond? State thine name and business in these parts!" You let the Phantom know you're a Renegade, seeing no reason to lie. "Hark, a Renegade? I should be disgusted to share space with such an undignified entity... but thou might be most useful to this good cause. The Zoltan menace has assumed control over this land, and seized the most important assets of Aether! Unless thou should wish for such equipment to fall into the hands of your enemy, it is my wisest suggestion thou chart a course to enact sweet justice. Thine choice is yours, but time is ever ticking."
If what the Phantoms say is true, and you have no reason to assume it isn't, then you can't let the Duskbringers seize a large supply of Aether! Get ready for battle!

choice.text: Report the Phantoms to the occupational forces.

event.text: Though assuming you're hostile at first, once you manage to speak to the Duskbringers they seem reasonably pleased, if not a bit cold towards you. "Good, so the Renegades wisened up and learned not to mess with the superior force. Smart one you are. The damn Dynasty started cooperating with the Vagabond clans just to spite us. Seems the only thing this dysfunctional species can agree on is they don't want anyone else to have their fair share of Aether. For your trouble and cleaner state of mind, I think we can work up some kind of reward."
For whatever reason there might be for Duskbringers to be in Dynasty space, you don't want to get involved in any way.

name: DYNASTY_OCCUPIED_GHOSTS
text: During the disarray caused by the fight, it seems a combined force of Dynasty and Vagabond vessels have broken through the Duskbringer defenses and sent them packing. Back in the colony, the surviving Ghosts are celebrating. "Thou inflict your blows most elegantly, Renegade. I can see now why the Federation would seek your employment. You may be confused, yes, as to why the likes of Spectral and Vagabond have joined here, but for all the struggles in our species, at least any sane and rational being can come to the mind that suicide bombing neofascists are not worthy of wielding the sacred technology of the Forefathers. Please, accept one of our finest soldiers. They will serve you masterfully."

name: DYNASTY_OCCUPIED_DUSK
text: With the leader of the Dynasty fleet taken out, the rest of the forces are scattered and disorganized, allowing the Duskbringers to pick them off easily. "Excellent work Renegade. Never though I'd be complimenting my enemy for their combat, but you've got skills. I can't lie, I'm impressed. If you ever decide you're tired of this Federation bullshit, and want to make the Multiverse a better place afterall, then give the Duskbringers a call, alright? We aren't stupid, we can cooperate with inferior beings when they're loyal. Now, your compensation."

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_DYNASTY_MONSTER
text: Your computer is suddenly flooded with alerts from nearby Dynasty security platforms. You listen to the static as your translator struggles to pick out something discernable from pure noise. "Avast! Turn thine's spirits away from this place and take content in safety not to be found here."

event.text: You assume they'll simply ignore you, but to your surprise a Phantom appears on the other end. "Oh? Have the maniacal hands of the lingering demon not yet snatched you away from this plane? Then consider yourself lucky, and take this chance to flee. You would be no coward to do such a thing..."
"A most horrible demon! It haunts these grounds, it ravages our colonies and it displaces our supplies! Oh flee, oh flee, for it shall strike you too if you stay!"

choice.text: We shall help! Fight the horrible demon.

event.text: You pilot further into the nebula, preparing yourself mentally for whatever monstrous ship lies ahead. At last, you lay eyes on it... and it's not really what you expected.
Sounds like there's something bad going on here - it's only safe to turn tail and run.

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_DYNASTY_ENGINEER
text: You follow the signal of the distress call to what looks to be... an abandoned Engineer vessel? The crew are nowhere to be found, but there's signs of a struggle, and the air is thick with the putrid scent of Ghosts.

choice.text: Try and track down the Engineers.

event.text: Exploring the nearby system leads you to a Dynasty station with several ships docked. Inside, several Ghosts are jeering as one of the engineers is escorted towards a guillotine device with a shimmering electrified blade. They spot you and give you a pleading glance, silently begging you to help them.
You draw your blaster and shoot the guard escorting the engineer, followed by the execution machine itself. You run out of the room followed by the wounded engineer as angry Ghosts rush towards you!

choice.text: Stay safe and hang back to scrap their ship.

event.text: With no one to stop you, you pull apart the hull of the engineer vessel and bring it back aboard.

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_DYNASTY_GRANDFATHER
text: You barely have a moment to investigate the source of the distress call before it comes to you. A vagabond vessel approaches, carrying a Phantom alpha. "Hail to me! I am Aneidio, grandfather to Dessius! Though time has been most cruel, I look to you for respite from the constant heckling that I am plagued with."

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Check the thoughts of the Ghost.

event.text: "It issss obvioussss he isss not really the grandfather of thisss sssupposssed Dessssiusss. Neverthelessss, he ssseemss to TRULY believe it himssself. Hilariousssly sssad."

choice.text: Tell the Alpha you believe him.
Try to explain to him that he can't be.

event.text: "You question me? I am in outrage!" The Ghost suddenly attacks!

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Check the thoughts of the Ghost.

event.text: "It is obvious he is not really the grandfathhher of thhhis supposed Dessius. Neverthhheless, he seems to TRULY believe it hhhimself. Hhhilariously sad."

choice.text: Tell the Alpha you believe him.
Try to explain to him that he can't be.

event.text: "You question me? I am in outrage!" The Ghost suddenly attacks!

choice.text: If you're his grandfather, then how are you not still in charge?

event.text: "You question me? I am in outrage!" The Ghost suddenly attacks!
"Hahahah! Then I bet you are not even that of the real Dessius! Do not lie to me!" The ship suddenly attacks!

name: DYNASTY_GRANDFATHER_BELIEVE
text: "Hah! I hardly believe it. If you are telling the truth, then I demand you solve for me one problem which ails me. My most critical skeptic, a Reaper captain named Tykaneous, resides nearby in this system. See to it he perishes, and I will join your crew. You should be honored to even be presented such a chance."

event.text: "You're working with the old prune? That ass-wad has never ceased to annoy me. Didn't know the Federation employs ass-wad sympathizers, breather!"
"Hmph. Then out of my sight, breather!"

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_DYNASTY_ELITE
text: The Reapers are the Dynasty's finest vessels. You've heard the Phantoms are hard to please, which says a lot for these hand picked elites to be put in charge of the Dynasty's highest matters. Apparently, you classify as one such thing!

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is a location of a Dynasty forward outpost.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

event.text: If the Dynasty is watching this sector, chances are they've already collected a ton of data... and data in any form is valuable to you!
Newton knows for what reason the Dynasty has been establishing these locations around the galaxy, but getting involved is a less than good idea.

choice.text: (Dessius) Request access to the data held in the outpost.

event.text: If the Dynasty is watching this sector, chances are they've already collected a ton of data. Luckily, you do happen to have a powerful ally at your side, who can grant you access to said data. Smooth talk aside, you are granted supplies and an advantage against the Rebel fleet.

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is a location of a Dynasty forward outpost.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

event.text: If the Dynasty is watching this sector, chances are they've already collected a ton of data... and data in any form is valuable to you!
Newton knows for what reason the Dynasty has been establishing these locations around the galaxy, but getting involved is a less than good idea.

choice.text: (Dessius) Request access to the data held in the outpost.

event.text: If the Dynasty is watching this sector, chances are they've already collected a ton of data. Luckily, you do happen to have a powerful ally at your side, who can grant you access to said data. Smooth talk aside, you are granted supplies and an advantage against the Rebel fleet.

name: DYNASTY_OUTPOST_DEFEAT
text: The outpost has fallen. This definitely won't please the Dynasty, but what are they going to do about it?

event.text: Looks like one of the station's terminals survived, a black box of sorts. In it contains heavily detailed map data for this sector, and predictions of the Rebel fleet progress. This will help greatly!

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_SPECIALRUIN

unvisitedTooltip.text: This beacon contains ancient ruins.

text: You've heard that the Dynasty's territory is littered with ruins from days past. But the wrecks in the distance... well, those don't look like Dynasty ships to you.

event.text: A massive Dynasty ship lurches towards you. "Wastes of days past are not those which require the temperament of modern day's impacts. What shift in the cosmic balance has led to your sudden appearance to this location? Do thou seek to stir a ruckus? Or just make the days of mine less enjoyable for the foreseeable future? Should I even continue to persist in this reality after?"

The Phantom sighs. "Your barbaric vernacular singes my tongue, but yes, I shall put an attempt to communicate in a way your primitive ape brain might understand. This beacon is the last of the great Obelisk wastes in this sector that require cleansing. This task was left up to Salvaging Operation DN-03. All objects or artifacts collected here are to be brought back for processing. We request that you leave, and warn you that our vessels are armed for combat as well as they are prepared for collection of ancient rubbish."

choice.text: Fight them to access the ruins!

event.text: "Ooh, you are a foul creature! How the anger and thoughts of violence twist your face into an unpleasant swirl of unconditional hatred. Erasing you shall do all but yourself a favor."

The Phantom lets out the loudest scream you've ever heard. "EEEK! DO MY EYES DECEIVE ME? THE OBELISK HAVE RETURNED?! Oh by the Reaper's name shall I fight to make certain your disease of a species may never return in forces of such volume ever again!"

name: DYNASTY_SPECIALRUIN_REWARD
text: "Ruination! It comes! Oh how the foul blackness consumes my sight. I weaken, and I fade. Exit, stage right..." The Dynasty vessel has fallen, and you scrap the wreck.

event.text: With the Dynasty out of the way, you pull apart the ancient wreckage, and find a unique weapon unlike any you've seen!

You catch Dessius giving you a disapproving look, but you figure he'll get over it eventually. If he really cared, he would have stepped in beforehand. You pull apart the ancient wreckage, and find a unique weapon unlike any you've seen!

name: DYNASTY_SPECIALRUIN_LOG
text: As you start to leave, you notice a strange, still illuminated augment installed in the ship's cargo bay. Scans reveal the device can tap into Multiverse Drives from across other realities!

name: NEBULA_DYNASTY_DREADNAUGHT
text: This beacon provides quite the break from the bland purple clouds elsewhere in this sector. In the distance is also what looks to be the Dynasty Capitol, and the Prime Reaper's palace. You're surprised the Ghosts have so little protection for this important structure...

event.text: As you approach, it suddenly becomes apparent something is deathly awry. Blaring sirens fill the air as distant blots of color scurry about on the surface. Distant laser fire can be heard as the shadow of a massive black object moves closer to the distant palace, trailed by the ruins of what was once the Dynasty's finest fleet.

Looks like it's an Auto-ship... and far larger than usual. As soon as you enter its scanning range, it speaks. "It is advisable you leave. I do not aim to kill you. Not today. My batteries are better spent testing out my chassis on some easy targets. Leave, and I will kill you another day instead. That is my promise." Oddly well spoken for a robot...

choice.text: Let's teach this hunk of metal some manners.

event.text: "Unadvisable decision. Your failure will be my pleasure. You are aware the odds are massively against you? Regardless... you will die here."

choice.text: Abide this peculiar warning and leave.

event.text: "A wise decision. If only my superiors could listen to me in such a manner."

choice.text: This is as good a time as any to leave.

event.text: This isn't a good place for a Federation ship to be. You owe nothing to the Dynasty - you aren't going to waste valuable time saving them from whatever latest monstrosity the Rebellion has cooked up.

name: DYNASTY_DREADNAUGHT_VICTORY
text: You land on the planet's surface, briefly considering salvaging some of the Dynasty wrecks before a massive Dynasty cruiser flies by and lands next to yours. Out of it steps several Alphas and a pink Ghost wearing armor and wielding a massive sword. If you had to take a guess, this would be the Prime Reaper, the ancestral leader of the Dynasty.

event.text: The Reaper begins to speak, but you can't understand a word he says. You realize you left your translator back on the ship, but before you can run and get it the Reaper waves you back and presses a button on his armor. "The demon's heart is perished! Who art thou, and for what reasonings have you come to bless us with this?"

"Mysterious! Intriguing. Most intriguing. Are you always this cryptic? I hope so! I am Dessius, son of Adotious, 16th Prime Reaper of the Spectral Dynasty. You have saved our people, no name. I am inclined to like you because of that. Long after the terror of the Obelisks have we feared another invasion might bring our climactic end, and today the demon almost got his wish. Until you arrived, that is!"

"The Obelisks. One of 5 ancient empires that ruled the galaxy so long ago your kind have no memories of their rule. I cannot blame your ignorance, those foul cuboids were but their own cause of destruction. A god complex does no good, especially not if you wield tech capable of ripping holes through space time. But enough of them. They're dead, much unlike us today! At last, we see the end of the foul demons. Their kind shall plague us no more!"

choice.text: The Rebel AI is kept on the Flagship, not that Dreadnaught.

event.text: "You are to say... that was not the demon's heart? Then we shall continue to teeter on the brink of imminent doom unless this monster can be brought to ultimate peace! But, my not-present ears detect the faintest slivers of hope in your breath. You say, you know the location of the heart? The true source of our sufferings? Then I must go in attendance. In our wake shall remain not one demon's twitching conniver that we have not sent to the gallows!"

name: DYNASTY_DREADNAUGHT_REWARD
text: "Oh, but before we depart, I find it imperative that we prepare for the travels ahead. It is clear to me now the Federation is no longer a threat. I shall deliver but my finest war vessels to their lands so that they too may vanquish the Rebel threat that terrorizes us all! As for you my friend, let us see what not we can help you with."

name: CRYSTAL_FOREIGNER_MAP
text: You notice another foreigner nearby, a ship of scout classification. They hail you and make a brief offer to sell you the map data they have been collecting from this sector.

choice.text: We can't verify the quality of their maps. Decline.

event.text: You decline the scout's offer and carry on.

name: CRYSTAL_CACHE_MV
text: Odd radar pings from a huge, orbiting asteroid here reveal a Crystalline cache of some kind. A deep crater has been sealed over with a thick layer of crystal to keep whatever's inside safe - it'd take some serious firepower to break though.

choice.text: Attempt to break through with the weapons you have.

event.text: Your powerful weapon dislodges and shatters a massive shard of crystal, leaving enough space to send an away team to climb down and take a look.

choice.text: This was a fantastic display of firepower, but who is going to investigate in there?

event.text: You ignore the cache and do something onboard the ship.

choice.text: (Crystal Crew) Have your Crystal crew recalibrate your weapons.

event.text: Your Crystalline crew-member is able to adjust the detonation frequency of your weapons to resonate with this type of crystal, and the barrier gives little resistance.
You ignore the cache and do something onboard the ship.

name: CRYSTAL_SCRAP_EXCITED_MV
text: You receive a signal from a private relay on a nearby inhabited planet. "Oh goodness, an Alien vessel! I was wondering how long until I would see one now that we've left the homeworlds! Please, I am a collector of many artifacts, I'm sure what is scrap to you is priceless to me."

event.text: "My word! Is this... a 25th century Rockman thrust stabilizer?! What do you want for it? Wait, I have a better proposal. I long to see the galaxy. I propose I come with you. What do you say?"
"I shan't even gather my belongings - only permit me to leave my family a message." The Crystalline being joins your crew.
Scrap is priceless no matter where you are in the galaxy. You hold onto your goods and prepare to jump.

name: CRYSTAL_HUMAN_TESTS_MV
text: You arrive near what appears to be a Crystalline research facility. A scientist quickly messages you, "Ah! Some more aliens. Please, I've heard so much about all the different races in this galaxy and I am really curious about your physiology! Would you let us run a few simple tests?"

choice.text: Allow them to run tests on a crewmember.
The scientists will have to look elsewhere for test subjects.

event.text: "I see. That is a shame. Perhaps the next vessel we meet will be able to contribute to the advancement of science."

"Ah! My dear evolutionary cousin! This is truly wonderful! We have countless historical records of your kind but we lack information on the past few hundreds of years. We can learn so much from these scans, we must get to analyzing them as soon as possible! Please, take this."

"Is that... ? Impossible... The lost sister species to Crystal and Rock kind! This is truly wonderful! We have so little records of the Salty Ones. We have a lot to learn from these scans, we must get to analyzing them as soon as possible! Please, take this."
"Oh... you're one of us. I'm afraid you must not have understood. I asked for an alien volunteer. I have no need for one of my own." They cut comms.

choice.text: (Backup DNA Bank) Send your crew's data.

event.text: "What is this? Full genetic and personal profiles stored digitally? I did not think this possible... This will help our research immeasurably. Please, take this in exchange for your help."

name: CRYSTAL_CHATTY_MV
text: A small civilian vessel messages you, "Wow! You're one of the Federation, aren't you! Are you busy? Can I ask you a question?"

event.text: "What do you eat? What is your culture like? How long do your people live?"
"I see. Oh well. Maybe the next alien I meet will be nicer..." You prepare to jump.
"I see... I guess you're busy."

choice.text: (Crystal Crew) Have your crew speak to them.

event.text: "Wow, you're one of us! I didn't know we already made an alliance with the Federation. I guess I won't bother you, but here, have some of our extra supplies!"

name: CRYSTAL_MONTY
text: As you arrive at this beacon, you are stopped by a Crystalline vessel. "Stop! Who would cross the beacon of death must answer me these questions three, ere the other side he see."

choice.text: Ask me the questions. I am not afraid.

event.text: "What... is your name?"
"What... is your quest?"

choice.text: We don't have time for this, attack!

event.text: You ignore the Crystal's questions and attack!

name: CRYSTAL_MONTY_CORRECT
text: "Right. Off you go!" The Crystals wave you past. As you leave, you find the wreckage of several ships who failed the test before you. You feel a little guilty about it, but you don't waste the opportunity and scrap the ships.

name: CRYSTAL_MONTY_INCORRECT
text: "Hee hee, wrong!" The Crystal fires a large shard from one of their weapons straight into the ships hull, and moves in to attack.

name: CRYSTAL_MONTY_UNKNOWN
text: "Oh well!" The Crystals move in to attack.

name: CRYSTAL_AUTO_SURVEYOR
text: An Auto-Surveyor vessel is patrolling the nearby area, likely sent by the Rebels to scout out the new Crystal territory.

choice.text: Attack the ship, if we can get its black box we can download the data!

event.text: You prepare to engage the automated vessel.
You successfully download the data without alerting the ship.

choice.text: (Hacking Weapon) Jam its sensors and download its data.

event.text: You successfully download the data while the ship tries to get its sensors back online.
The ship poses no interest to you.

name: CRYSTAL_TORTURE
text: This beacon welcomes you with a gruesome and unnerving sight. A Crystalline station has several different creatures embedded in its hull, slowly suffocating or crushed under the weight of the crystalline plating.

event.text: "Ah, so you wish to join the likes of these pitiful creatures? Let it be so!"
The station doesn't attempt to contact you as your FTL charges.
While scrapping the station, you notice that the crew encased in the ship are still barely alive... but they won't for long.
The Medbay heals their wounds, but it cannot bring them back from the dead. Many of the ex-prisoners do not make it, but one lucky soul was able to be revived.

choice.text: There's too little we can do to help.

name: CRYSTAL_REBEL_CRYSTAL_MV
text: Crystal shards fly past the screen as soon as you arrive. Checking the scanners, it looks like a Crystalline ship is engaged with a Rebel!

event.text: You message the Crystalline ship your intentions and move in to intercept the Rebel ship.

You move in to intercept the Crystalline ship. As soon as the Rebel scans your ship it takes the opportunity to jump. You have the sneaking suspicion they will inform the fleet of your position, but that's the least of your current concerns.
With the two ships engaged in combat, you sneak by unnoticed.

name: CRYSTAL_REBEL_CRYSTAL2_MV
text: You're greeted by an unwelcome sight - a Rebel advance ship is laying down fire on a Crystalline vessel in the distance.

event.text: Before you can engage, the Crystalline ship scores a direct hit and obliterates the Rebel ship! They hail: "You, you are like these other aliens! You brought them here!" With that they turn their cannons on you!
It's best to take advantage of the rare occasions when the Rebels aren't shooting at you. You prepare to jump.

name: CRYSTAL_MANTIS_CRYSTAL_MV
text: You discover a number of civilian ships fleeing the area. Shots are fired and you find the assailant; a Mantis ship is attacking one of the smaller ships!

event.text: You activate your impulse engines and fly between the Mantis and their prey, weapons charging. You appear to have their full attention.
You try to keep a low profile and quickly prepare to jump.

name: CRYSTAL_PIRATE_CRYSTAL_MV
text: A pirate ship jumps in right after you arrive at the beacon. It almost charges a small Crystalline transport ship, weapons armed.

event.text: You chase down the pirate before it has a chance to engage the civilian ship. When it detects the real threat, it turns to face you.
You assume the Crystalline ship can handle itself. You have enough of your own problems.

name: CRYSTAL_FED_MV
text: There appears to be a fight going on nearby. A Crystalline border guard is chasing a small Federation ship!

event.text: It doesn't look like the Fed ship can stand much more pressure. You fly in and intercept the Crystalline ship.
With the Federation ship distracting the guard, you are free to continue on your mission.

name: CRYSTAL_FED_DESERTER_MV
text: For a moment you assume it's a glitch, but no... you've found a rare Elite Federation military ship! They hail you and, after some probing, reveal that they deserted the Federation fleet and decided to hide among the Crystals, figuring there would be few other Federation ships here to find them.

event.text: You send over some supplies to help them on their way and in return they upload their flight plan to your computer, allowing you to map the sector! "The Federation fleet's still standing - get there while you can!"
Deserters cannot be tolerated. You open fire on the cowards - though it doesn't please you to do so. The Federation needs every soldier it can get.
You send them a friendly warning regarding the armada of Rebel ships pursuing you, and then get underway lest they catch you up.

name: CRYSTAL_REQUEST_MV
text: The moment you arrive you notice a Crystalline ship in the vicinity keeping its distance. They message you, "The 'Rebels' that are trying to hunt YOU down are creating havoc everywhere they go. Bah, we came here to escape this crap..."

event.text: "To minimize their impact on our people, we would like you to give them your flight path out of our sector. We would like to remain civil and are willing to pay you in 'scrap' for the increased danger it poses."
It was never your intention to lead the Rebels here, and frankly you could do with the scrap. The Crystalline ship immediately jumps off to inform the Rebels, leaving you with a fleet to outrun!

choice.text: Accept the scrap but give them false flight plans.
(Crystal Crew) Try to convince them of the importance of your mission.
(Sentinel Crew) Try to convince them of the importance of your mission.
(Ruwen) Convince them of the importance of your mission.

event.text: "Oh my. I didn't realize you were currently visiting this sector. Yes, I think we can make this work." The Crystals agree to give the Rebels falsified flight plans and give you a plentiful helping of scrap.

choice.text: (Decoy Buoys) Accept the scrap but give them falsified flight plans.

event.text: Your decoy buoys allows you to create very convincing flight plans. They accept it as true and give you the scrap. The deception may not be the most honorable tactic, but staying ahead of the fleet is your highest priority.
You apologize for the trouble you've brought them, but explain that you have no choice. They seem to understand, and break the comm link to set about preparing defenses.

name: CRYSTAL_HELP_DIG_MV
text: A large Crystalline ship is floating in space here. They hail: "Aliens?! How curious. We request your aid. We have men buried on a nearby planet and we must dig them out."

event.text: You do as you're asked and send a crewmember down to the planet to assist. They discover a massive Crystal excavation operation and it quickly becomes clear this is a task that will take days, not hours.

You're committed to both saving the Federation and upholding the principles it worked to maintain. Your crewmember will remain and make good on the promise - you still have a galaxy to save. They give you some supplies for your trouble.

The Crystalline captain contacts you urgently: "What is the meaning of this?! Had you no wish to aid us you might simply have declined, but THIS... is an insult!" He turns his massive ship on yours and you prepare to fight for your life.

You've made a commitment, and that still means something. You wait one jump cycle and then inquire with the Crystalline captain about the status of the operation. "We respect your strength. The operation will take one more cycle."

You're committed to both saving the Federation and upholding the principles it worked to maintain. Your crewmember will remain and make good on the promise - you still have a galaxy to save. They give you some supplies for your trouble.

The Crystalline captain contacts you urgently: "What is the meaning of this?! Had you no wish to aid us you might simply have declined, but THIS... is an insult!" He turns his massive ship on yours and you prepare to fight for your life.

Another cycle passes while the Rebel fleet draws ever nearer. You contact the captain again. "Alien Captain, your knowledge of our customs has most impressed us. Your crewmember is on their way back to you now, along with a token of our respect."

choice.text: (Temporal Manipulator) Use your system to try and increase the speed of the dig.

event.text: Having decided that waiting further would cause too many problems, you opt to use your Temporal Manipulator to speed up the excavation process. It's subtle, but your crewmember manages to finish up before the next cycle. The Crystals they were working with offer a reward for their hard work.

choice.text: (Adv. Temporal) Use your system to increase the speed of the dig.

event.text: You're not entirely sure how well this will work out, but you decide to use your exotic system to speed up the excavation process. Initially the Crystals involved are perplexed and a little worried at what seems to be happening, but they soon realize roughly what's going on and decide to take full advantage of it. The operation proceeds smoothly and the Crystals reward you handsomely for it.

choice.text: You have no crew to spare.

event.text: "We understand. You rely on machines for so much. Yours is a soft and weak species - we would hardly even have noticed your presence. Fly well."

name: DISTRESS_CRYSTAL_SICK_FIRE
text: There is a Crystal clinic at this beacon. Smoke is emerging from it, and the station is all gummed up with crystal lockdown. A medic hails you. "Help! We're trying to deal with a fire, but we can't move! One of our patients had a bad reaction to their Ryapel... We can't move as long as their lockdown is uncontrollable!" The fire doesn't seem to be too intense - if you act fast you can put it out before any more harm is done.

event.text: Your crew teleports onto the station and begins to put out the fire. The fire hasn't spread far, so your crew is easily able to save the spooked patients. "Whew. That was a close one. Thank you for saving the clinic. Unfortunately, the patient in question will still be difficult to treat in their current condition..."

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay) Offer to treat the lock-down prone patient.

event.text: Your crew is able to phase past the crystals and enter the clinic. The fire hasn't spread far, so your crew is easily able to save the spooked patients. "Whew. That was a close one. Thank you for saving the clinic. Unfortunately, the patient in question will still be difficult to treat in their current condition..."

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay + Teleporter) Offer to treat the lock-down prone patient.
(Jerry) Break down the crystal barrier and put out the fire.

event.text: Jerry blasts his way into the clinic like an action hero, blasting down the doors with his massive gun. The fire hasn't spread far, so your crew is easily able to save the spooked patients and put out the fire. "Whew. That was a close one. Thank you for saving the clinic. Unfortunately, the patient in question will still be difficult to treat in their current condition..."

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay) Offer to treat the lock-down prone patient.
(Paladin Crew) Break down the crystal barrier and put out the fire.

event.text: Your Paladin is able to break past the crystals and enter the clinic. The fire hasn't spread far, so your crew is easily able to save the spooked patients and put out the fire. "Whew. That was a close one. Thank you for saving the clinic. Unfortunately, the patient in question will still be difficult to treat in their current condition..."

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay) Offer to treat the lock-down prone patient.
(Recon Drone) Use your Recon Drone to break in and evacuate the clinic.

event.text: Your drone smashes the doors down with great efficiency and evacuates the sickly Crystals. The fire hasn't spread far, so the clinic staff are easily able put it out as the evacuation transpires. "Whew. That was a close one. Thank you for saving the clinic. Unfortunately, the patient in question will still be difficult to treat in their current condition..."

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay) Offer to treat the lock-down prone patient.
Your extinguisher system can't properly interface with the clinic in its locked-down state.
Break down the crystal barrier and put out the fire.

event.text: The clinic's fire starts to get out of control - a lot of patients are likely dying. You do your best to ignore this grim reality.

name: CRYSTAL_SICK_TREATMENT
text: Having moved the Crystal to your own ship, you're able to treat their condition. As the clinicians tell you, the patient had a bad reaction to their medicine. You're able to treat their symptoms and return them to the clinic. Before they leave, they offer you a piece of crystal technology for helping them.

name: DISTRESS_CRYSTAL_VAGABOND_CONFLICT
text: You arrive at a scene of one Crystal ship fleeing from another. The pursuer is broadcasting on an open channel. "This is your final warning, pests! The Empire does not tolerate reappropriation of derelict ships!" The other ship desperately sends you a communique - a Ghost requests your help. "I beseech thee! Grant us thy aid!"

event.text: "Outsiders! You dare interrupt law enforcement within our borders? You will die for your insolence!" The Crystal switches its target to you instead of the Vagabond!
"Alas! Our fortune worsens!" The Vagabond is cornered between your ships! You seem to be in a better position to attack.

"Attention, belligerents! The Empress of the Crystals will agree to a peaceable compromise, with conditions. First and foremost: Vagabond ship, are the bodies of the Crystals who died still onboard?"

"...we have swept their remains into a corner." The Vagabond captain admits, sheepishly.

"Fine. We demand their remains, which will be enshrined within the Scintillating Mausoleum. Second condition: You must provide payment and a gift in exchange for the vessel. Once this is done, our patrol will escort you to the exit of our sector, and you may not return, under penalty of death."

The Vagabonds take a moment to discuss it, before agreeing to the terms.

"My empress! You are generous and wise. Will this be the new policy moving forwards?"
						
						Dianesh shakes her head. "I'll adjust our foreign policy when I am done traveling the galaxy. For now, continue operating as you have." The Crystals offer their queen a small tribute.

choice.text: (Dessius) Convince the Vagabonds to turn over the ship.

event.text: Dessius belts a command to his people. "Thou art vastly too proud! Grant our rivals that which they lay sovereignty over. Surely thine lives measure greater worth than to expire here!" At this suggestion the Vagabonds give up the ship to the Crystals. As they leave their ship, one insists that they be allowed on yours!
"Federation, you have impressed us with your diplomatic acumen. No shots had to be fired due to your involvement. We offer a tribute in thanks for your assistance."
You decide not to interfere in the Empire's jurisdiction.

name: DISTRESS_REFUGEE_CRYSTAL
text: You have encountered a refugee ship drifting in space. It looks as if it was fleeing the Rebel advance and ran out of fuel. Its distress beacon is active, but you're not sure anyone is on board.

event.text: You're wary of the refugees but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: QUEST_CRYSTAL_REBEL_ATTACK_ORCHID
text: As you arrive, you spot a Rebel pursuing a Gathering vessel. However, once the Rebel notices you, it breaks off to attack you instead!

name: CRYSTAL_ORCHID_SAVED
text: "You have done us a great service! Unfortunately, that Rebel attack killed the Crystal scout that was escorting us through the sector. We have a very important sociology conference to get to... do you think you could help us make it there?"

event.text: "Thank you kindly. I hope we can make it in time."
"We'll find another way, then. Hopefully a friendly Crystal will help us."

name: CRYSTAL_ORCHID_ESCORT_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Crystal sociology conference is happening here.

text: The Orchid vessel jumps in after you, pleased to have arrived at their conference. "Ah, we were wondering when you would arrive. The Empire has been very curious about the sociological insights of the Ctl'Yae. Thank you for guiding them here. You can stay for the conference if you'd like." As fun as it sounds, there is a mission to be done. However, they do allow you and your crew to sample some of the complimentary buffet. The Orchids also give you a gift.

name: CRYSTALHOME_ZOLTENVOY
text: It appears a brave Zoltan ship has pushed deep into Crystalline space, but their hull has received critical damage, with several massive breaches in the hull.

event.text: You board the ship, but it's already too late. A dying Zoltan in the corner manages to cough out some final words to you. "The Crystals- they were here... take this to them... You know what to do with it." The Zoltan slides over a package containing a large Zoltan-made bomb, and a letter noting some coordinates, then dissipates into nothing.
It's probably too late anyways, and not worth the effort. You ignore the Zoltan ship.

name: CRYSTALHOME_ZOLTENVOY_DELIVERY

unvisitedTooltip.text: Coordinates of a Sentinel outpost given by a dying Peacekeeper.

text: You've arrived at the destination given to you by the Zoltan. A Sentinel vessel is guarding an outpost where a military operation appears to be run.

choice.text: Give them the bomb - the Zoltans must have been delivering this.
Detonate the bomb - the Zoltans must have wanted revenge for being attacked.

event.text: You don't know what the Zoltan wanted, but better not to get involved. You break down the bomb into some ammunition.

name: ENCOUNTER_CRYSTAL_STATION
text: A Crystal station nearby notices your ship. "We do not welcome outsiders here! Get out, now!" It appears they're willing to back their threats up with their weapons.

name: CRYSTAL_CONVOY
text: A large convoy of lumbering civilian ships appears to be passing through this region. You show no hostile intentions, but they are taking no chances, immediately sending their escort to attack!

name: CRYSTAL_HUNTER
text: Crystal shards fly past your ship as soon as you jump. You scan to find the assailant and discover a Crystalline ship carrying a number of humans in its cargo bay. It must be hunting the alien ships!

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_CRYSTAL_MIRROR
text: The planet in the distance is rather bland, save for a few lakes and rivers. Curiously enough, that hasn't stopped a Crystal ship from docking next to a pond.

event.text: You find the captain of the Crystal ship kneeling besides one of the aforementioned ponds, staring deeply into it. When you ask him about his fascination, he replies: "Hello, Captain. Do take a look into the pond and tell me, isn't that the most beautiful creature you have ever seen in your life?" Expecting to see a water creature of some sort, you bend over and look, but all you can see is the reflection of the Crystal captain.

choice.text: (Nights) Nights is eager to answer that question.

event.text:
Still heavily drunk, Nights stumbles over to the pond, takes one look at the "creature", and erupts into manic laughter. "HAHAHAHAHA! You call that beautiful?? Ssssee, that ssslimy bassstard Sssslocknog, well he looksss ten times better than thisss, and my eyesss sssour jussst from glancing at him! Your sssense of beauty isss sssoo bad it makesss me wanna-"
						
Nights doesn't get to finish as he vomits straight into the pond, throwing up from all his excessive drinking. Horrified from both his words and the now disfigured "creature", the Crystal collapses on the spot.

choice.text: Call in the captain's crew so they can check on him.

event.text: Upon arriving at the scene, his crew conclude that their captain died immediately after fainting from the emotional damage. While the crew "mourn" their captain's death and return a little too excitedly to their ship, their second-in-command discreetly transfers some goods to you for helping them get off this planet.

Just before you head back to your ship, an Orchid Praetor taps you on your back. It seems they just appeared out of nowhere and have no recollection of their past, but they seem to be willing to work for you if it means they won't be stuck behind on this planet.
Who cares about sightseeing? We have better things to do.

name: ENCOUNTER_CRYSTAL_ELITE
text: Crystal Sentinels are the protectors of the Crystal sectors, and are much stronger than their civilian brothers. By entering into their new Homeworlds with a military-tier cruiser, the Crystal people have deemed you a threat worthy of the retribution of a Sentinel vessel!

name: CRYSTAL_SANCTUARY
text: You've discovered a massive Crystalline society, well furnished and protected. In the center is a small village surrounding a massive contraption... it looks like a gateway of some sort?

event.text: The contraption seems to resemble a much larger version of the Waystone, the device that the Crystalline people used to seal off their old homeworlds. As you approach, a massive Crystalline cruiser approaches, its weapons aiming straight at you!

A ceremoniously painted purple Crystal stands before you, far taller than those in the background. "I am Empress Dianesh Kryel. You... are a foreigner, and foreigners are unwelcome. The Federation has given us its aid, and for that we are grateful. But we are no longer in need of the Federation, and you need nothing of us. We shall negotiate terms."

"The terms on which you leave this place. Your presence here is not sanctioned. I know people like you. Ambassador Ruwen has told me the stories. You are barbarians, murderers. Renegades like you were the ones who first stole our home from us. And I refuse to allow such things to transpire again. I will satisfy whatever vain desires you might have to ensure you leave and never return. My people do not want you here."

Dianesh gestures for a small transport ship to approach and deliver a specialized Crystal weapon. "We have met your demands, now you will abide by ours and leave." You figure it's best not to press further and follow their instructions.

Dianesh gestures for a small transport ship to approach. It delivers a Crystalline prisoner, who eagerly joins your crew as long as it brings an end to their sentence. "We have met your demands, now you will abide by ours and leave." You figure it's best not to press further and follow their instructions.

Dianesh gestures for a support ship to come by and give a full repair. "We have met your demands, now you will abide by ours and leave." You figure it's best not to press further and follow their instructions.

choice.text: We did not come here to harm you. We are not as bad as you say.

event.text: "Oh but you see, only by making such claims do you prove your intentions. Were you of true heart, you would have already left. But you persist. Persistence is a threat. And my people do not take kindly to threats." You try to protest further but Dianesh will not listen. She waves and her cruiser moves forth to strike you down. This doesn't have to necessarily end in bloodshed, but the Crystals aren't going to listen easily.
Diving so deep into a Crystalline city is generally not a good idea. You distance yourself from the planet.

name: CRYSTAL_BOSS_DEFEAT
text: You have defeated the cruiser, and with it have killed the Crystalline empress. Though this can only spell bad news for the future, you content yourself with salvaging the remains of the ship.

event.text: This will no doubt only hurt the Crystalline people's views on foreigners, but it's too late to change it now. Perhaps, in a future reality, there might be a better way to resolve this...

name: CRYSTAL_BOSS_SURRENDER
text: The Crystal cruiser, and the crew on board, are on their last breath. The ship's engines flare as it rocks back and forth, barely able to keep up with you any longer.

event.text: You power down your weapons. A little while later, the Crystals do the same. Dianesh appears onscreen, breathing heavily with a long crack down her once smooth face. "So... so you have chosen mercy. I must say, I did not expect this..."
There will be no mercy for the Crystals, not today.

name: CRYSTAL_BOSS_MERCY
text: You land your ship nearby the city, guided by Dianesh. The large Crystalline being steps out of her battered cruiser and comes to face you.

event.text: "It seems I might have been misguided in my assumptions. You have... my most sincere apologies for this aggression. I am an honorable woman, and I have disgraced myself by attacking you. I will not have this be. With Ruwen away, there is no one but myself to offer their services to you. Maybe when this is through, we can see if there is a place for my people among the Federation..."

name: FEDERATION_SUPPLY
text: You discover a fully militarized Federation station here, though it appears they are selling supplies to passing Federation allied ships.

event.text: No one is safe from you, not even allied Federation stations.
You aren't interested in the station. You ignore them.

name: FED_SUPPLY_STATION_KILL
text: Your unnecessary, unprovoked, barbaric attack on an allied Federation Station has been successful, if you could call killing them as success. You scrap what remains.

name: FEDERATION_FREECREW
text: A damaged Federation ship hails you. "Good, a friendly face for once. Our ship has taken catastrophic damage and there's no chance of repairing it. I don't suppose you'd be willing to allow me aboard? I'm a shield technician and I'm sure my skills could be of service to you."

choice.text: We don't need any more crew, sorry.

event.text: "Oh... ok. Hopefully I'll be able to keep the shields under control so they don't implode before another ship arrives to help..."

name: FEDERATION_RANT
text: Your arrival at this beacon is met with an unusual sight; an unarmed Illesctrian ship far from Zoltan territory. They contact you, and from their tone, the monk speaking to you does not seem particularly happy about something. "Renegade, this multiversal conflict is one of an endless cycle, one that you seem to be at the core of. But are you really fighting to try and end it, or just to perpetuate it further for your own gains?" Though Zoltans do not have faces, you nevertheless feel like they are staring intently at you, waiting to judge you for your answer.

choice.text: The Multiverse is full of conflict. Some fights must be finished to bring lasting peace.

event.text: The stare from the Zoltan monk softens slightly. "A wise answer. It is good to know that there is more to you Renegades than meets the eye. May your journey for peace bring good fortunes."

choice.text: The Multiverse is full of conflict. Some fights must be finished to bring lasting peace.

event.text: Despite your answer, the Zoltan still glares coldly at you. "A wise answer, is what I would have said if I was blind to your infamy. Your lies betray your true interests. Do not expect your deception to go without consequences!" Suddenly, as if in response to this, a Peacekeeper ship jumps in to confront you.

choice.text: We're just in it for the scrap and murder.

event.text: The Zoltan sighs. "It is because of people like you that this galaxy is stuck in perpetual turmoil! Though perhaps I might be able to communicate better using the barbaric language of your weaponry." They eject an unusual Bomb weapon from their ship towards yours. "May this inspire a change in your heart. Get out of my sight." They promptly jump away afterwards, leaving you to inspect their unexpected "gift" for you.
The Zoltan on the other end sighs deeply, before cutting comms and jumping away.

"Are you treating this like some idle matter? The decisions you make across your journey will each have consequences deep and long lasting! At least have the conviction in whatever they are, even if they are not necessarily as righteous as they should be." It seems your response has deeply angered them, and they intend to keep rambling on for a while longer.

choice.text: Let them continue, even if it takes a long time.

event.text: The Zoltan monk continues to rant on for a while longer. The meaning of their words soon vanishes from your mind, and eventually you lose track of how long has passed here. Just as you almost fall asleep from it, the monk asks you a simple question. "So, do you understand what I mean by this?"

"Ah, good to hear. Perhaps I misjudged you from the outset. Very well. I shall join your endeavors, to learn even more of your cause and your ways." Fortunately, they don't really seem to notice that you didn't pay any attention to what they said earlier.
"Seriously..." They almost begin another round of lecturing, but pass out from exhaustion just before they start again. You take this opportunity to leave them behind at this beacon.

"Ah, good to hear. Perhaps I misjudged you from the outset. Very well. I shall join your endeavors, to learn even more of your cause and your ways." Fortunately, they don't really seem to notice that you didn't pay any attention to what they said earlier.

You power up your weapons, intent on making them stop their ramblings. The Monks send out a distress signal, and soon enough a Zoltan ship answers it. The Monks jump away just before the fighting starts.

name: FEDERATION_AMMO
text: A Federation station is sending out a request for ammunition, in return for scrap. Their high demand is likely due to the increasing number of Rebel blockades. They might be able to spare some blueprints if you are generous.

choice.text: Offer 5 missiles for whatever scrap they have.
Offer 10 missiles for a patch-up and some extra fuel.
Offer 20 missiles out of the goodness of your heart.

event.text: "Wow, are you serious? Thank you, your kindness will not be forgotten! I'll make sure the Federation fleet understands what you've done for them."

choice.text: We don't have anything to sell.

event.text: You ignore the station.

name: FEDERATION_ITEM_DEBATE
text: An Engi ship, an Orchid ship, a Crystal ship and a Zoltan ship surround a debris field of multiple rebel ships. There was a large battle, but they were victorious.

choice.text: Ask if they need help salvaging the wreckage.

event.text:
At your prompting, the Orchid ship invites your ship to join their group communication. As soon as you do, the Crystal talks first.

"Hello, Renegade. There is a problem: The other ships are claiming that our crystal arsenal didn't sway the tide of our battle in our favor!" 

The Orchid speaks up. "I'm sorry you had to get pulled into this Renegade. I do want to point out that our kernels penetrated the enemy shields and knocked out their engines. It's thanks to us that you had the accuracy you did."

The Zoltan snorts. "Baffling argument. Ludicrous, even. You may have scratched their paint job, but our Lucerne beam did the lion's share of the work. We did the most hull damage, therefore we were the most consequential ship in that fight. We don't even HAVE to aim."

The Engi ship chirps in. "Zoltan's assertion = illogical. Beams = inconsequential if (fire support == false). Engi combat drones >> all other contributions."

choice.text: The Engi is right. Drones probably had the biggest impact.

event.text: The Engi captain interjects. "Confirmed. Renegade has authenticated Engi logic. Therefore: Engi allocation of resources = most efficient." The other three captains sigh and nod. "Renegade: Delivering gratuity."

choice.text: The Zoltan is right. Beams ended the fight much quicker.

event.text: The Zoltan smirks. "It is plain to see. The Renegade's countless battles have exposed them to the truth. Therefore, I will distribute the spoils as I see fit. Any objections?" The other three captains are silent. "Wonderful. Oh, and here is a gift of appreciation, Renegade."

choice.text: The Orchid is right. Knocking out systems is vital to surviving fights.

event.text: The Orchid gesticulates in delight. "The Renegade is wise! With that in mind, you all can surely agree we get first dibs?" The Zoltan and Crystal mutter in annoyance, while the Engi simply nods. "Fantastic. Renegade, please accept a token of our thanks."

choice.text: The Crystal is right. Crystal weapons are a good balance between shield penetration and sustainability.

event.text: The Crystal proudly interjects. "As expected. Our weapons are superior, as is our decision making. We will be deciding who gets what." The others look annoyed but protest no longer. "Renegade, we will let you have this. You clearly know how to use it."

choice.text: (Drone, Crystal, Kernel, Beam) Behold, my loadout makes use of all of these!

event.text:
The others look on in wonder. 

The Zoltan staggers backwards and clutches his chest. "Incredible. Our weapons are that synergistic?" 

Orchid nods, pleased, "Of course! We are stronger together than we are apart. It makes sense!" 

The Engi cocks its head to the side. "Compatibility = high. Renegade experience = greatest among us." 

The Crystal nods. "I concur. Renegade, you may take the largest share, and we will evenly distribute the rest."

choice.text: Demand that they give you a portion of the scrap for your important mission.
(Upg. Cloaking) Attempt to steal some scrap when they are not looking.

event.text: With your cloaking device active, you carefully maneuver around the ship and try to get closer... but you don't have much time. You need a little extra reach to collect anything meaningful.

choice.text: No good. You don't have anything that can reach.

event.text: You carefully get out of there before you are noticed.
You now have some time to do something on the ship.

name: FED_ARGEONN_CONTACT
text: A small Federation ship is skulking far from the beacon. They seem to be waiting for someone.

event.text: The Federation ship responds. "You're here for... business, aren't you?"
"Thought so. Let me tell them that the coast is clear." A moment later, an Argeonn ship approaches.

choice.text: Threaten to report the Federation ship for being in cahoots with smugglers.

event.text: The Federation captain quickly flies away. The smuggler angrily yells after the Federation captain: "Damn you! You were supposed to protect us!"
"I must have you confused for someone else. Go on your way."
You now have some time to do something on the ship.
No Rebels will be allowed to live so long as you can help it.
You have no interest in fighting the Rebel ship.

name: FEDERATION_BROKEN_DRONE
text: A Federation automated supply drone nearby is on the fritz, sparking and occasionally sending garbled, meaningless messages. It must have received serious damage.

event.text: Your Engi is no stranger to working on Auto-ships and drones, and easily identifies the problem. Once the Auto-ship is fixed, it distributes supplies and patches up your hull.

Your Engineer tries to explain that they're only used to working on Rebel Auto-ships, but you convince them to try anyways. They manage to get the drone working long enough to repair some hull before something goes wrong and the ship turns hostile!
Your repair drone quickly patches up the Auto-ship. Once fixed, it distributes supplies and patches up your hull.

choice.text: (Lanius Crew) Have your Lanius salvage the drone.

event.text: Your Lanius is able to salvage the drone with little difficulty, knowing exactly what to disassemble to prevent triggering its defenses.
You aren't interested by the malfunctioning automaton.

name: FEDERATION_DRONE_TEST
text: A Federation research station is orbiting a nearby planet. You notice an unusually colored Federation auto-ship fly up from the planet and dock at the station, next to a few other similar vessels.

event.text: Your call is answered by an Engi wearing a lab coat. "Renegade, your arrival at Federation automated shipyard 78-A has been noted. We have a proposal for you. Our proposal: your assistance in testing novel auto-ship designs. Multiple testing applications are valid. Successful testing will be rewarded, and compensatory repairs will be supplied as well." They offer you multiple tests you can run on their auto-ships.

choice.text: Pick the "Drone Systems Targeting Analysis Test."

event.text: The Engi explains the test to you, and shows you the auto-ship you'll be running the test with. "Test requirements: allow automated ship to fire on your ship for duration of test. Damage to auto-ship hull = failure. System and ion damage are tolerable. Is this acceptable?"
The Engi powers up the auto-ship. It detaches from the station to face you.

choice.text: Pick the "Drone Hull Endurance Analysis Test."

event.text: The Engi explains the test to you, and shows you the auto-ship you'll be running the test with. "Test requirements: destroy automated ship. AI programming has already been saved elsewhere on this station, so destruction != a setback. Escape attempts will be registered as a test failure. Is this acceptable?"
The Engi powers up the auto-ship. It detaches from the station to face you.
Though the auto-ships are somewhat intriguing, you don't feel inclined to investigate further.

name: FED_DRONE_TEST_SUPERFAIL
text: "Test result = catastrophic failure. New recommendation to Renegade ship: piss off."

name: FED_DRONE_TEST_FAIL
text: "Test result = failure. As a result, consider all rewards and compensatory repairs to be annulled. Future recommendation: listen to provided instructions."

name: FED_DRONE_NODAMAGE_SUCCESS
text: The drone depowers after the testing session concludes. The Engi hails you. "Test results : Data successfully processed. Your performance = satisfactory. Reward will be provided momentarily." The station repairs your hull and rewards you as thanks for your contributions.

name: FED_DRONE_COMBAT_SUCCESS
text: The Engi hails you not long after the auto-ship explodes. "Test results : Data successfully processed. Your performance = satisfactory. Reward will be provided momentarily." The station repairs your hull and rewards you as thanks for your contributions.

name: FEDERATION_HANGAR_RAID
text: A large Federation hangar has been built on the nearby planet. Any Federation ship is allowed to dock.

event.text: You transmit your ID and not long after are allowed to enter. A repair team moves in to refuel your ship and make some repairs.

As you exit the hangar a blaring siren fills the air. A Rebel squadron is approaching! The planetary defense cannons are overwhelmed and most of the Rebel ships are able to get past. An Elite ship locks onto you and attacks!
It's tempting, but you can't waste any time.

name: FEDERATION_SHIPCLASS
text: A nearby Federation ship is sending in a hail request.

event.text: A middle-aged human appears on your screen. "Greetings, Renegade cruis- erm, uh, vessel?"

"Well, even though cruiser would nowadays be the de-facto term to refer to a ship such as yours... my fascination in history just can't stomach the fact that naval terms have been dumbed down over the years. A cruiser required much more manpower than that to properly operate! Do you fancy an alternative or more accurate name for your type of ship?"

choice.text: Just say spaceship instead of complicating everything.

event.text: "...Heh. Sure, you can't go wrong, I'll give you that - but it gets old and tiring pretty fast. I'll... go find someone else and gather their idea on the matter."
It's rude, but unless it's an emergency, you can't afford to waste time right now.

name: FEDERATION_SHIPCLASS_ARGUE
text: "W-what? That's hardly a fitting term to use for your ship either! Is there no one else these days that bothers studying our past, wanting to correct that clear matter of misconception?"

choice.text: There's no need to be petty over that.

event.text: "PETTY?! I did not become a history aficionado just so I could be made fun of by a washed-up Renegade like you! How dare you mock me like that? I'll put you in your place!"

choice.text: Leave, before this guy comes up with an irrational excuse to open fire on you.

name: FEDERATION_ENCOUNTER_ELITE_STEALTH
text: The Federation ship patrolling this beacon is no ordinary vessel. Its distinct shape marks it as part of the Federation's latest stealth fleet, created to help keep up with the never ending arms race with the Rebellion. Fortunately, they don't seem to object to your presence, but they aren't particularly welcoming either.

event.text: For some reason, you decide to open fire on an especially well-armed allied ship. They hardly hesitate to return the favor. Hopefully this will be worth it.

choice.text: Given your sketchy reputation, it's probably best to avoid making unnecessary requests from your allies.

event.text: "...Yes? We are currently not under any orders to provide aid to passing vessels. We can provide you with some additional fuel, but not much else."
Unsatisfied at their pitiful offer, you've decided to do whatever it takes to get more.
"...Yes? We are currently not under any orders to provide aid to passing vessels. Though given your contributions, we could probably make an exception for you. Just don't spend too long deciding."
Their patrol route soons takes them away from your ship, leaving you mostly alone here.

name: DISTRESS_FEDERATION_KNIGHTS_AND_KNAVES
text: At this beacon, you find three Federation ships: a corvette, a fighter and a light cruiser. You can tell that there is a lot of comm chatter between them, suggesting that something serious is happening. As you arrive, the light cruiser's captain invites you into the open communication channel.

event.text:
"Renegade, I'm glad you are here," says the light cruiser captain, "We've got a major situation on our hands. A Federation Captain went turncoat - or was a spy - and replaced his crew with Rebels! The trouble is, I'm not sure which it is, and we have no way of escorting both of them."

The captain of the fighter chips in. "Are we seriously leaving this up to a Renegade? How do we know they're not just interested in our scrap?"

"You would say that, Rebel!" The captain of the corvette says. "They're still Federation where it counts."

The fighter captain crosses her arms. "We're Federation through and through. I'm confident that we can prove it. Can you say the same?"

The captain of the light cruiser holds up his hand. "Settle down, and stop posturing. Renegade, do you have any ideas?"

Tully glances at the security feeds. As the three captains realize the admiral is in their midst, their reactions are revealing. The corvette's captain seems to look surprised, before putting on a poker face, while the other two look on in admiration. The light cruiser's captain holds his hands open. "Admiral! I didn't realize you were here!"

"Thank you both for your service. I need to talk to this defector." Tully's eyes meet the captain of the corvette. "So, why did you do it?"

"I..." The captain begins to crack. "While I was... in the academy, the Rebels took my planet. And, they gave me a choice."

"I understand. Still, you made an oath. We have three ships, and you have one. Do right by your men and surrender. They will be taken as POWs and treated fairly."

The captain nods, and surrenders.

"Oho, a mystery. I believe I'm in my element here." Haynes gestures with his pipe as he studies the feed of each ship. "Hmm, intriguing. I can't help but notice that on the fighter, there is a Federation-issue gun lying in the corner of the cockpit. Quite curious, considering you might expect a discarded weapon if there was a scuffle."

The captain of the fighter looks panicked. "I can explain!"

Haynes shakes his head. "In addition, your pilot is wearing his uniform incorrectly. Can you explain that?"

"I-I must have told him to correct it a thousand times! But I swear, he's as loyal to the Federation as he can be."

"You're right- because you're NOT the impostor."

The fighter captain's face turns from panic to confusion, then relief. "W-what do you mean?"

"Your ship bears dirt, dust, clutter and residence. The other ship is suspiciously clean, spotless and with no character. I suspect we could uncover more."

The corvette captain has a poker face. "We have nothing to hide. We clean our ship properly."

"Then, since you have nothing to hide, I'd be glad to see a video of the last time you cleaned. Surely it was within the last 24 hours? And, I'm sure there's no blood residuals either, hm?"

After a staredown, with three other ships aiming their weapons at them, the corvette finally stands down.

choice.text: (Jerry) Politely ask the impostor's crew to surrender.

event.text:
"Hey guys, it's me, Jerry." Jerry waves. The corvette's pilot looks surprised and waves at him.

"Guys! Get in here, it's Jerry!" The other Rebels start to filter into the room.

The captain looks alarmed. "What are you doing?"

"Dude, we can't lie to Jerry, man, come on."

Jerry smiles. "Would you guys mind giving the Federation their ship back?"

The captain seems unhappy at the situation, but his crew don't seem to want to harm Jerry.

choice.text: (Soldier Crew) Demand that both ships transmit data only Federation enlisted personnel would know.

event.text: Your soldier barks out a command to have every soldier salute and announce their serial number, platoon, graduating class, and drill sergeant. The fighter's crew immediately transmit a video of each crewmen saluting and proudly providing what they're ordered to. Some of them even throw an anecdote of their training along with it.
