event.text: "Greetingsss, mossst disssgussssting and rotund one. We've been looking for sssuch a fine ssspecimen for a century. You are truly the ugliessst being in the galaxy and dessserve to be embalmed and shown in a mussseum. I can only wonder what your mother looksss like."

choice.text: We won't suffer such insults! Attack!

event.text: Infuriated by this sudden and uncalled for barrage of insults, you open fire. "Haha! Not only are you fat, but you're sssstupid too!" The Slug captain sends a distress message to the nearby Orchid planet claiming to be attacked by pirates. To your surprise, the Orchids on the nearby planet activate their security systems and lock onto your ship! Damn Slugs.

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Block any distress signals the Slug might make, and attack!

event.text: You fire at the Slug ship and they immediately respond with evasive maneuvers. The Slug captain sends a distress message to the nearby Orchid planet claiming to be attacked by pirates, but it fails to go through. Their initial plan failed, the Slugs have no choice but to fight you on their own.

Nights knocks you away from the console and grabs the mic. "Awww, that'ssss adorable. I ssssee where thissss sssscheme issss going from a mile away - you're professssional victimssss! Too fragile and inssssecure to fight your own battlessss, sssso you hide behind a bunch of flowerssss. You're the mosssst ssssad and pathetic losssserssss I could even imagine. And as long assss we're making assssumptionssss about each other'ssss motherssss, I'm going to guessss by that misssserable look on your ugly mug that you've never actually made yourssss proud."

After hanging up, Nights immediately gets into a shuttle and boards the enemy ship, which has been dead silent the whole time. When he comes back, the shuttle is carrying a large amount of scrap. He chuckles as he dumps it in the cargo hold.

Your Slug turns to the others, dons a pair of shades, and simply states "Couldn't be worssse than your mother after I annihilated her in bed lasssst night." Shocked and outraged, the Slug captain has no idea how to respond. Eventually, in utter humiliation, he concedes and offers surrender.

choice.text: (Tony Sr.) Tony asks to speak with them.

event.text: Tony snaps a picture of the lead Slug, then begins groveling and crying in front of the camera. You and the Slugs are speechless as you watch Tony wail, until his phone buzzes and he immediately snaps back to his usual self. "Thanks for giving my assistants time to look you up. I'd insult your mother, but it'd feel mean, knowing how decrepit her apartment complex on your homeworld is. It'd be a shame if someone made her problems worse by buying the place and having it bulldozed. So why don't you cut your losses and thank me for the warning?" The Slugs toss some scrap your way and jump away, leaving you to worry about what information your crewmate might have against you.

choice.text: Close communications and leave the system.

event.text: You ignore the Slugs, knowing this is most probably a trick.

name: ORCHID_FIELD_NORMAL
text: A vast beautiful field of flowers lays on the nearby planet. A stunning view of flowers scattered across miles and miles.

choice.text: Pick some flowers, maybe you can sell them.

event.text: As you and your crew begin to cheerfully pluck some flowers from the sunny field, an Orchid ship descends from the sky, their crew in tears. "Monsters! You slaughter our children!"
While still utterly mortified, the Orchids at least are willing to let you leave. They insist you give back all of the flowers you picked and then demand you leave at once.

choice.text: Double down and take the corpses back with you.

event.text: As you lug the gigantic pile of flowers back with you, the sobbing Orchids turn furious. "You bastards! You will pay for this!"

choice.text: Pick some flowers, maybe you can sell them.

event.text: As you move to pick some flowers, Mayeb blocks your path. She looks more pissed off than you have ever seen her.

choice.text: Pick some flowers, maybe you can sell them.
Pick some flowers, maybe you can sell them.
(Orchid Crew) Your Orchid waves their vines frantically, warning you not to do it.

event.text: Your Orchid informs you the field is filled with young Orchid children who have not yet developed mobility. You realise you were nearly about to commit genocide and decide against it.

A strange insidious thought takes over your mind, and acting purely on instinct you raise the weapons and fire them at the field, to the shock and horror of the Orchids observing you. However, rather than decimating the field, the flowers are suddenly transformed into fully grown Orchids. Immediately, the onset of a mid-life crisis drives the field into madness before they are promptly turned back into wailing and barely developed baby flowers, their minds forever turned to mush by a sudden rush of memories and experiences of their adult selves that have yet to even be. Uncertain of what even just happened (and terrified you'll do the same to them), the field's owners simply demand you leave.

A strange insidious thought takes over your mind, and acting purely on instinct you raise the weapons and fire them at the field, to the shock and horror of the Orchids observing you. However, rather than decimating the field, the flowers are suddenly transformed into fully grown Orchids. Though a part of you expects this sudden transformation to be temporary, they remain in their adult forms. Unfortunately, there isn't quite enough room in the field for all of the newly grown Orchids, and you are forced to accept a large number of them on your ship.

Though it's not fertilizer in the traditional sense, the nanobots stimulate the growth of the flowers. The Orchid Caretakers of the field seem to take notice of this and thank you for your generosity, though they advise you not to provide "unsolicited growth stimulation" to other people's children in the future.

Your crew erupts into a fit of maniac laughter as the field is set ablaze. The Orchid Caretakers watching over the field are absolutely horrified, and a Praetor swoops in to stop your act of genocide!

choice.text: You can't seem to get ahold of your Lost Sun.
We have better things to do.

event.text: You ignore the flowers and carry on with your mission.

name: ORCHID_FIELD_SECURE
text: As you approach the nearby planet which seems to contain a large field of flowers, you're stopped by an incredibly well armed station. "Stop right there! I don't care who you are or what your reason for being here is. This is a high security zone under protection by the Praetorian. You must leave."

event.text: The Floral sighs. "We've heard news from other realities that some sicko Renegades have been making a habit of going into our fields and massacring our children. It's become an epidemic, and the Gathering has authorized maximum force in protecting our children now. The SPS has been established to ensure no one else can commit these heinous crimes again."

choice.text: Fight the station to access the planet.

event.text: "Are you KIDDING me? Kader, sound the alarms! We've got another one on our hands!"
If Renegades have really been doing stuff like this, you don't want to be anything like them. You decide to leave.
You don't want to mess with whatever is going on here. You decide to leave as soon as possible.

name: ORCHID_FIELD_SECURE_WIN
text: With the station out of the way you descend to the planet below. The Orchid Caretakers running the place are terrified at the sight of you, pleading you to spare the children.

event.text: Despite your crew's reservations, you order them to pick the flowers anyways. The Caretakers try to pull you away but to no avail as you gun down anyone who gets in your way. Satisfied with your maniacal efforts, you return to the ship with piles of corpses in tow. The word Renegade will surely become a vile insult to anyone here who witnessed this event.
As you move to pick some flowers, Mayeb blocks your path. She looks more pissed off than you have ever seen her.

choice.text: We've done enough, let's just go.

event.text: While at least you didn't go all of the way, it's hard to pretend this won't continue to negatively reinforce the bad reputation of Renegades across the Multiverse.

name: IVAR_PROTECTING_THE_KIDS
text: You feel something small hit the back of your head. You turn around and find Ivar staring at you, a bottle of wine in one vine and his spear at the ready in the other. He takes a massive swig of his drink and then wipes his mouth. "You know, I consider myself a well-humored fellow. I take things in stride. I laugh at dark jokes, I let mean comments slide off, I let people ridicule and look down on me with reasonably thick skin. I mean hey, I'm in politics, aren't I?" He laughs humorlessly. "But this is crossing the line. I'm going to have to ask you to step away from the children. If you dare touch them, we're going to have a problem." Ivar takes another drink. His teeth clench menacingly as he addresses you again. "Got it?"

event.text: Ivar relaxes. "Don't make me get serious again, Captain. I hate being serious."

choice.text: Continue trying to pluck the flowers.

event.text: You feel a sharp pain as Ivar's spear strikes true. You double over in pain onto the floor, blood seeping out from your uniform. "I tried to warn you, captain. Don't worry, I hear the Gathering's prisons have an excellent track record of patching up wounds."
You realize that, in a daze, you may have imagined what just happened. Ivar is still right in front of you, waiting for your response to his implicit ultimatum. Will you really go through with it?
Ivar relaxes. "Don't make me get serious again, Captain. I hate being serious."

You feel a sharp pain as Ivar's spear strikes true. You double over in pain onto the floor, blood seeping out from your uniform. "I tried to warn you, captain. Don't worry, I hear the Gathering's prisons have an excellent track record of patching up wounds."

choice.text: Continue trying to pluck the flowers.

event.text: "Yeah, I don't think so." Ivar pins you up against the wall with his spear and orders your own crew to take you to the brig. To your surprise the crew actually obeys, grabbing you and dragging you away. As you demand an explanation for their mutiny, Ivar turns around and smiles. "Silly Renegade. Did you forget that I'm a politician? I'm on a first name basis with the rest of the crew. I wanted to be friends with you too, but I'm afraid I don't associate with child-murderers."
You realize that, in a daze, you may have imagined what just happened. Ivar is still right in front of you, waiting for your response to his implicit ultimatum. Will you really go through with it?
Ivar relaxes. "Don't make me get serious again, Captain. I hate being serious."

"Yeah, I don't think so." Ivar pins you up against the wall with his spear and orders your own crew to take you to the brig. To your surprise the crew actually obeys, grabbing you and dragging you away. As you demand an explanation for their mutiny, Ivar turns around and smiles. "Silly Renegade. Did you forget that I'm a politician? I'm on a first name basis with the rest of the crew. I wanted to be friends with you too, but I'm afraid I don't associate with child-murderers."

name: TY_EREL_PROTECTING_THE_KIDS
text: A strong vine wraps around your arm. You're being held still by Ty E'Rel. Although his expression is as neutral as ever, he seems more menacing than usual. "Captain, I will not allow you to harm these children."

event.text: Ty E'Rel nods. You lurch away from him as he loosens his grip. You can still feel him staring daggers at you as you order your ship away from the planet.

choice.text: Struggle free and continue trying to pluck the flowers.

event.text:
You feel his vines begin to constrict around your neck. No matter how hard you fight, you can't break free. You begin to drift away from consciousness.

In what feels like a moment later, you awaken with a headache. The ship is no longer anywhere near the planet. You've lost quite a bit of time, and you won't be able to stay here much longer. Ty E'Rel is keeping his distance for now, but things are likely to be tense from here on out.

choice.text: Order your crew to help you.

event.text: You try to get your crew to intervene on your behalf, but they seem unwilling. Ty E'Rel shakes his head. "I've had a discussion with them already. The rest of the crew will no longer follow your orders unless you agree to leave the children alone." Eventually, your crew pilots the ship away from the fields while Ty E'Rel holds you down. Once you're clear, he lets go, but you can tell the crew no longer respects you as they once might have - if they ever did.

choice.text: Try to get a word in.
Wait for her to calm down.
Nod to try and appease her.

event.text: "Fine. I've made my point. Now what do you have to say for yourself?"

choice.text: I've heard you out, but I'm still going to do it.

event.text: Mayeb puts her vines on her hips. "I don't think so! There's more that I have to say, and you're going to listen to me until you learn your lesson."
Mayeb folds her vines. "Say it more clearly. What are you apologizing for?"

choice.text: I'm sorry for thoughtlessly endangering the lives of children.

event.text: "Good. Now let's get the hell out of here."

name: ORCHID_THEFT
text: A distressed band of Florals hails you. Though it appears most live a mute lifestyle, one Orchid is able to communicate vocally. "Please help! An Auto-ship has come and stolen our children! Please rescue them!"

event.text: You track down the Auto-ship, and it appears it has not yet left the system. It loops a single message, "GIVE ME THE PLANT", and attacks you!

You give the corpses over to the Auto-ship, which it scans then accepts. "Plant has been given. Thank you for your contributions to the Rebel Xeno-Identification Project. Accept this monetary compensation for your offering."
You apologize and mute the Orchids.

name: ORCHID_SACRIFICE
text: A small fleet of Lost Sun ships orbit a small uninhabited planet. You intercept communication between two of the ships and hear them mention something about an execution.

event.text: You pilot closer to the planet's surface. In the center of a large tent is a massive bonfire with an Orchid Praetor tied up! A large brutish Rockman stands waving his hands and speaking loudly to a cheering crowd of fellow Lost Suns. "The Gathering has made it clear where they stand on the side of liberty! They claim to be allies of the Federation and purveyors of peace, yet they continue to forge good-mannered relations with the Elders in the face of their own tyranny! Today we make an example of how the Lost Suns treat such indignation!"

You send in a team of crew to rush in and cut down the Orchid before the Lost Suns can drop them into the fire. You rush back to the ship with a horde of angry Rocks and an attack ship in hot pursuit.

choice.text: (Floral Crew) Demand the prisoners are freed.

event.text: "Haha! The pitiful plant creature wishes to fight for its kin! You work aboard a Federation mercenary vessel, yet you defend the actions of people who have done everything but defend your virtues! Get out of here at once!" You don't have time to free the Praetor or protest, because a Lost Sun vessel is dispatched to chase you away!

Your Commando speaks with the other Lost Suns, eventually coming to an understanding that perhaps massacring the Federation's allies isn't a good idea. The Lost Suns untie the Orchid Praetor, who thanks you and offers to work aboard your ship.
"M'am! I- I am s-so so so sorry. I uhh, uh, I was just doing my duty for the glory of the Lost Suns! Please, don't discharge me. I will free the Orchid immediately."
"What... what are these. You have given me corpses? Of children? What... what is wrong with you. We're here to make an example of injustice, not of child slaughter. Get the hell out of here!"
There really is no worse time to go making enemies with the Lost Suns than now. You pull away from the planet.
If the Lost Suns are performing some sort of sacrifice here, you want no part in it.

name: ORCHID_ELITEDUEL
text: You're surprised to find not one but two elite ships squaring off at this beacon! A Lanius Welder and an Orchid Praetor have entered a duel, and you find yourself caught in the middle of it!

event.text: You intercept the Lanius ship and prepare for combat.
You intercept the Orchid ship and prepare for combat.

choice.text: Fly the hell away from here!

event.text: You power up the engines and fly far away from the two ships.

name: GARDEN_DUEL_LANIUS_DEFEAT
text: You've defeated the Lanius elites, and now the bounty of their ship is yours.

event.text: The Orchid silently nods to you in thanks, and gives you a Kernel weapon from their ship as payment.

name: GARDEN_DUEL_ORCHID_DEFEAT
text: You've defeated the Orchid elites, and now the bounty of their ship is yours.

event.text: "Are debt, paying." The Lanius send over some random materials.

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_NOTPIRATES
text: A damaged Orchid panics when you jump in. "So you pirates have returned to destroy us? We will not go peacefully like last time!"

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_WEEDS
text: An Orchid ship frantically hails you. "Federation, help! Our station has become overrun with massive man-eating weeds!"

choice.text: Send a team to assist! Massive man-eating weeds are no laughing matter.
It appears you lack bodies to throw at the bloodthirsty plants.

event.text: Plants and fire are a combination that don't mix well. The Orchid personnel evacuate, and your Goul sets the station ablaze. Once the weeds are gone for certain, the station is vented and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your creative problem solving.

Plants and fire are a combination that don't mix well. The Orchid personnel evacuate, and your Lost Sun sets the station ablaze. Once the weeds are gone for certain, the station is vented and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your creative problem solving.

Your crew suits up and board the station, firing on the weeds and quickly taking them down. Once they are gone for certain, the station is vented, and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your ruthless but efficient problem solving.

Your crewmember arms up and board the station, easily coming up with a plan. Using a combination of their senses and specialised hunting gear, the abominations are felled in a decisive strike, and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your ruthless but efficient problem solving.

Irwin boards the station, easily coming up with a plan. Using his knowledge of past battles against equally twisted creatures, the abominations are swiftly dealt with, and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your ruthless but efficient problem solving.

Plants and fire are a combination that don't mix well. The Orchid personnel evacuate, and you set the station ablaze. Once the weeds are gone for certain, the station is vented and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your creative problem solving.

There's no reason why your weapon wouldn't be effective against these deadly weeds. The Orchid personnel evacuate, and you fire upon the station. Once the weeds are gone for certain, the station is vented and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your creative problem solving.

The murderbots will rid the station of anything living. The Orchid personnel evacuate, and you flood the station with the deadly nanobots. Once the weeds are gone for certain, the nanobots are called back and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your creative problem solving.

The Shell's toxic gas can kill nearly any organic matter quickly. The Orchid personnel evacuate, and you flood the station with the deadly gas. Once the weeds are gone for certain, the station is vented and the Orchids give you a brand new Kernel weapon for your creative problem solving.

choice.text: (Shell Guardian Crew) Have your Shell Guardian handle the weeds.

event.text: Your Shell has little fear of the deadly weeds, having such a hard exterior. Once the weeds are rid of, the Orchid personnel reward you with a new Kernel weapon for handling the situation so quickly.

choice.text: (Boarding Drone) Send your drone to handle the weeds.

event.text: You pull up alongside the station and release the drone through the airlock. Within a short time the majority of the creatures are dead, with only a little collateral damage. The Orchid personnel express their most sincere gratitude and offer you a Kernel weapon.
You can't risk fighting deadly aliens on every station you find. You prepare to jump.

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_JUNGLE
text: The distress signal is originating from a stunningly beautiful forest planet with a developed Orchid outpost not too far away. You don't see any ships in need of distress.

event.text: You scope out the area around the outpost. It doesn't take long to find the true origins of the distress beacon, a damaged distress beacon laying a few miles from two ships, one Orchid, and the other Rebel.

It appears the Rebels have taken the Orchid ship, which was trying to return to the outpost, hostage. The Orchid ship's relay systems have been damaged beyond repair and the Rebels have lined up the Orchids firing squad style. "Alright, we got the last of the plant things. We gonna shoot 'em now, or take them back to the stronghold and make a big display out of it?"
You arm the weapons and charge the Rebel ship. The officers scatter back to their ship to defend themselves.

choice.text: (Upg. Weapons) Fire a shot straight into the Rebel ship.

event.text: One shot straight into their engines is all it takes to cripple the Rebel ship. Now helpless, the Rebels surrender and scatter into the forest, leaving their ship to you.

choice.text: (Mind Control) Turn the Rebels against each other.

event.text: The Rebel commander whips around and blasts one of the other soldiers in the chest. Confused, the rest of the Rebels enter a firefight with each other, until every single last of of them has managed to kill each other, leaving no one to guard their ship.

choice.text: (Mind Affecting Weapon) Turn the Rebels against each other.

event.text: Chaos erupts as each of the Rebels hit by your weapon draws their weapons and begin a violent free for all. The bloodbath continues until every single last of of them has managed to kill each other, leaving no one to guard their ship.
You can't risk your primary mission to save a couple Orchids. You feel guilty, but you know you had no part in this crime anyways.
Whoever they were, they probably got help already. There's no need to stick around.

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_ROCK_CRASH
text: On the nearby planet is the crash-site of a Rock vessel, heavily damaged, but their distress beacon still functioning.

event.text: You have no interest in helping the Rockmen.

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_EMPTY_SHIP
text: A distress signal is coming from an Orchid ship, drifting far away from common interstellar routes. You try to communicate but there is no answer.

choice.text: There's no one to send to board that ship.
(Adv. Sensors) Fetch the ship's security logs first.

event.text: You have no need to communicate with the ship.

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_COLONY_FIRE
text: A distress signal is coming from the surface of a planet near the beacon. A wildfire is spreading towards a small Orchid colony which lacks the resources to extinguish it or evacuate in time.

choice.text: Help to evacuate as many civilians as you can.

event.text: The ecosystem on the Orchid planet is so vulnerable to fire that even your whole crew isn't enough to save the Orchid colony in time. You succeeded in helping more hardy individuals but most of the Orchid seeds and babies are lost to the fire.

choice.text: This incident is no concern to us.

event.text: There's nothing you can do. Your crew is upset but you prepare to jump.

choice.text: (Fire Suppression) Use the augmentation to save the colony.

event.text: The Fire Suppression system is deployed in the colony from your ship, and helps tremendously in holding back wildfires in key points while all the living Orchids evacuate. One of the Orchids is so impressed by your performance that they ask to join your crew.

choice.text: (Mantis Pheromones) Use the augmentation to speed up the evacuation.

event.text: Affected by pheromones, your crew and the Orchid civilians move a lot faster, leaving no one behind. After the colony is evacuated, one of the Orchids is so impressed by your performance that they ask to join your crew.

choice.text: (Crystal Crew) Block wildfire spreading to buy some time.

event.text: Your crewmember erects giant crystalline walls in mere seconds, and within minutes a defense barrier is in place to restrict the fire. The flames are slowed down and all of the colony manages to escape to safety. One of the Orchids is so impressed by your performance that they ask to join your crew.

choice.text: (Lockdown Bomb) Block wildfire spreading to win some time.

event.text: The bomb is used to erect giant crystalline walls in mere seconds. The flames are slowed down and all of the colony manages to escape to safety. One of the Orchids is so impressed by your performance that they ask to join your crew.

choice.text: (Drone Reactor Booster) Deploy superior drones to help. [-2|]

event.text: The onboard drones are reprogrammed and used for help. They carry seeds, babies, and valuables, put out fires and save the day in the end. One of the Orchids is so impressed by your performance that they ask to join your crew.

name: ORCHID_ZOLTAN_QUEST_START
text: An unarmed Zoltan ship greets you. "Our vessel is on a diplomatic mission to the Orchid worlds. We would like to hire you to go ahead of us and offer a small gift to one of the nearby Orchid colonies to herald our arrival."

event.text: The Zoltans deliver a box containing a gift to Orchids. The package contains a replica of a Zoltan spaceship of an unusual shape, which vibrates rapidly, radiating light and heat. It's made from high quality metals and very pleasant to look at.
After you've received the gift, the Zoltans transfer over the coords for your destination.

You inspect the device and quickly discover that it's actually a Duskbringer-made bomb in disguise! This was a trap! The bomb seems to have been set to deploy a message revealing it to be a Rebel ploy. This must have been some complex coordinated effort between the Duskbringers and Rebels to sabotage your mission.
As soon as the unarmed ship realizes you haven't fallen for their trap, a Duskbringer escort reveals itself and attacks!

choice.text: (Duskbringer Crew) Your Duskbringer recognizes something strange with the device...

event.text: Your Duskbringer inspects the device and quickly discovers that it's actually a bomb in disguise! This was a trap! The bomb seems to have been set to deploy a message revealing it to be a Rebel ploy. This must have been some complex coordinated effort between the Duskbringers and Rebels to sabotage your mission.
As soon as the unarmed ship realizes you haven't fallen for their trap, a Duskbringer escort reveals itself and attacks!
You don't have time for diplomatic missions.

name: ORCHID_ZOLTAN_QUEST_FINISH

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Zoltan asked you to deliver a gift to a Gathering settlement.

text: You arrive at the co-ordinates to find the Orchid settlement. They welcome you in.

event.text: You don't mention the sculpture to the Orchids. You shake 'tendrils' with them and leave. This sculpture will likely sell for a bit of scrap.

You lamely toss the dead children at the feet of the Orchids. They stare unblinking at you for a few moments, then begin to scream. You run back to the ship followed by one of their strongest vessels.

name: ORCHID_PIRATE_FRIENDLY_ASB
text: A pirate ship worn out by many battles moves in your direction from behind an Orchid planet. An ASB system seems to have been installed on the nearby planet, and if you sent out a distress signal you might be able to take advantage of it!

event.text: You send a distress signal, and the Gathering military force stationed at the planet responds immediately and targets the pirate with an Anti-Ship Battery.

You send a distress signal. The Gathering military force stationed at the planet responds after a short delay - by targeting both you and the pirate with an Anti-Ship Battery. Unfortunately for you, they are not oblivious to your crimes.

name: ORCHID_CAPTURED_REBEL
text: You are surprised to hear the crew of an Orchid ship talk in human language: "Surrender. All nearby worlds are controlled by Rebellion forces. Resistance is futile." From the uneasy movements of the ship, it seems the Rebels have recently taken control of this ship and still aren't used to piloting it. Nevertheless, they lock onto you and attack!

name: ORCHID_SUZERAIN_VETERAN
text: A Mantis Suzerain, his carapace laden with scars from his ancient past, glares at you through the monitor. "The Federation-Mantis war never ended. I refuse to recognize the treaties... still to this day I, last bastion of glorious decade, continue our work. I will eradicating every last scumling in this galaxy. The flowers are weak. But you... surely you are even weaker."

name: CARETAKER_PRAETOR_ARGUMENT
text: By the time you reach the beacon, a Praetor seems to have already responded to the distress call. Its origin was a small, brown shuttle - they seem to be discussing something.

event.text:
"...and maybe this Federation ship can help me. Renegade! It's good timing that you have come. The Praetorian are committing a grievous wrong, one that only the Caretakers of Rt'lak Et are trying to fix!"

The Praetor grumbles. "I am not saying I support what's being done. But the Praetors are preoccupied. With the recent campaign against our border, we cannot afford the infighting. We don't have the resources."

The Caretaker leans in. "The Gathering is forcibly relocating many natives of Rt'lak Et, which will no doubt inflict considerable harm. You need to help us make our case to the Gathering, stand up for those who cannot stand for themselves. None of the other Florals are willing to help."

The Caretaker lets out a sigh. "The Kadahellian Schism began after the Theocracy uplifted us. This allowed us - the Ctl'Yae - to explore until we found Rt'lak Et, our greatest gardenworld. Nowhere else in the known galaxy does such a lush and perfect environment exist for advanced plant life. While we have many garden worlds, Rt'lak Et is special. Our people grow and manufacture our best ships and weapons there. But our government has decided to lower themselves to relocating many species which cannot survive in weaker climates offworld in the name of stepping up weapon production. The long term ecological ramifications could be severe."

event.name: CARETAKER_CHAT
event.text: The Praetor shakes her head. "The Duskbringers believe they can weaken the Federation by burning down our Gardenworlds. For the most part, they had been unsuccessful, as we diverted the majority of our forces to hold the line. Truth be told, for as long as our production gardens are under threat, the Gathering is likely to push for heavier militarization. Unfortunately, one of their number managed to make it into our territory anyway. We can't divert any more ships away from the front lines, which means our ability to chase them is limited. The best we can do is defend our core worlds and hope they don't do much damage."

The Praetor clenches her foliage. "Our listening post at Kat'ar Lek went dark. We had a Praetor stationed there, and they haven't been responding. We don't have the resources to send another right now, and they can destroy most other Floral vessels. If you can take them out, they lose their one foothold in our territory, which we believe will force them to back off. And if this happens, I can certainly convince my government to offer you a ship for your fleet."

The Caretaker adds. "If you want to help us, the first relocation transport is on its way to its destination. I can transmit coordinates so that we can intercept them. Either we can talk some sense into them... or, we might have to get a little aggressive."
"That is a relief. If you can get the invaders off our back, this will ease tensions. And, I give you my word that I will stop any further harm from occurring. We will be waiting."
"Excellent! I was beginning to lose hope. I will follow behind. If we can sort this out, I will offer what I can." The Caretaker indicates the heading of the offending ship into your map.
"Wow, really? That's... unexpected." The Praetor blinks. "Here are the coordinates of the outpost."
"I worry you are stretching yourself thin." The Caretaker shakes his head. "Here's the location of the transport. Much obliged."

choice.text: We don't have time to help either.

event.text: Both Orchids make annoyed noises. "Why did you get involved if you weren't going to help?" "What a waste of time."
The Orchids can probably work this out between each other.

name: GARDEN_INVASION_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Praetor has tasked you with tracking down a powerful ship.

text: You arrive to find a heavily damaged listening post, as well as a few destroyed and derelict Floral ships. The Duskbringer captain sends a message to taunt you. "The Federation must be desperate to send you after us. We will burn these horrid worlds for the glory of our righteous cause!"

name: ORCHID_INVASION_WIN
text: The formidable New Order ship falls, leaving you victorious. The Duskbringers let out a final cry as their bodies explode into nothingness. Their ship provides a healthy amount of resources.

event.text: You quickly look over all the ships for any survivors, but all you can find are corpses. You collect what you can from the wreckages.

name: ORCHID_INVASION_LIFE_SCAN
text: You're able to detect a surviving life form on a derelict ship - a dying Praetor scarred badly from an explosion. They won't last long.

event.text: You rush the Praetor to your medical facilities just in time to heal their wounds. As they recover enough stamina to talk, they sit up on the bed.

choice.text: Discuss the situation with the Praetor.
(Upg. Clone Bay) Register the Praetor into the clone bay.

event.text: You rush the Praetor to your clone bay just in time. They expire just as the system scans their biological patterns. After a brief moment, the Praetor exits the clone bay in confusion before realizing what just happened.

choice.text: Discuss the situation with the Praetor.

event.text: You send in your medical crew, who patches the dying Praetor up on the spot, successfully saving their life. Your medical crew returns alongside the Praetor.

choice.text: Discuss the situation with the Praetor.

event.text: You send in your medical drone. The drone patches up the Praetor on the spot, successfully saving their life. You send the Praetor a shuttle to make their way to your ship.

choice.text: Discuss the situation with the Praetor.

event.text: Your medical bomb explodes, filling the room with healing nanites, which quickly reverses the damage from the explosion. You send the Praetor a shuttle to make their way to your ship.

choice.text: Discuss the situation with the Praetor.

event.text: The Praetor appears in your teleporter room, completely free of harm. They stand up, confused at what has happened. After a few moments of confusion, they turn to you.

choice.text: Discuss the situation with the Praetor.
Nothing can be done to save this Orchid.

event.text: Unfortunately, you can only watch helplessly as the Orchid passes. You collect what you can from the wreckages.

choice.text: Use the listening station to contact the Orchids.

name: ORCHID_INVASION_PRAETOR_SAVED
text: "I'm... alive. Thank you, kind Renegade. Bastards took us by surprise. If you don't mind, there's something I want to do. This won't take long." The Praetor takes a shuttle to the listening station and patches it up. It whirrs to life and begins a long-ranged broadcast of the derelict New Order ship. After doing this, the Praetor relaxes. "Anyhow, let me thank you for saving my life. I can offer you the cache lying hidden at this post."

choice.text: The Praetors from the front lines are hailing you.

event.text: "Well done, Renegade! You even rescued one of our soldiers, and for that we are forever grateful. It looks like the Duskbringers won't hold on for much longer. Hopefully this will ease some of the tensions within the gardens. Good luck."

choice.text: Ask the Praetor you rescued if they will accompany you.

event.text: The Praetor returns to your ship. "I owe you my life, Captain."

name: ORCHID_INVASION_CONTACT_PRAETORS
text: You use the long-ranged communication relays connected to the station to inform the Praetors of your success. "Fantastic work. With luck, they will realize what has happened. Now that their foothold is gone, they will either back off, or make a mistake that we can capitalize upon. As promised, we will send a ship to your hangar."

name: ORCHID_RELOCATION_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Caretaker wants you to help the plants that are being relocated here.

text: As you arrive, you immediately notice a massive Orchid freighter. As you look closer, there is a massive greenhouse taking up most of it - this freighter must be able to carry an entire city's worth of Orchids! Despite its large size, there is only a single Orchid Fighter escorting it. They don't seem to consider you a threat and continue to move along. The Caretaker shuttle that originally tasked you with the request jumps in not long after you do.

event.text: The escort responds as the transport stands by. "Greetings, friend of the Federation. What troubles you?"

choice.text: (Ty E'Rel) Inform them that they must turn their ship around.

event.text:
"Ambassador Ty E'Rel?? You came all the way out here for this?"

"I wouldn't stop you if this wasn't important. We must return to Rt'lak Et with these creatures. We can explain more when we arrive."

"A-are you sure? This freighter is extremely expensive to move and maintain... wouldn't it be better if we waited here if there's any uncertainty?"

Ty E'Rel snorts. "That's a stupid question."

Ivar pounds the console. "Oy! What are you doin' over there?"

"Is that Premier Ivar?"

"You're making a mistake over there! Here I am over in the Confederacy trying to make things a little more joyful, and what do I find on my latest visit to the Gathering? You, making the same mistake we made when you left us! Now turn around, I have some people to give a piece of my mind!"

"But... Mr. Vampweed Premier, this ship is incredibly costly to move and maintain! We can't just-"
               
"I will help with whatever extra costs are incurred. Just do what I say!" Cowed, the ships begin to turn around.

choice.text: (Positive Orchid Reputation) Convince them to turn back.

event.text: You make a passionate case on behalf of the plants that they are transporting. "Well... you're held in good regard in these parts... But, this freighter is extremely costly to move and maintain. Are you sure you can convince the leadership to change their mind?" You give them your assurance that you'll do your best. They seem to accept this and turn their ships around.

You make a passionate case on behalf of the plants that they are transporting. The escort interrupts. "Sorry, but we have our orders. If you've been listening to those Caretakers, especially Mayeb, please just forget about it. We know what we're doing."

choice.text: Tell them you won't leave them alone until they change their mind.

event.text: "Stand down, Renegade. No need to escalate this. I'm going to ask you to leave."
"I didn't want to have to do this, but you leave me no choice!" The Orchid ship warms its weapons.
You stand down. The ships eventually jump away without contacting you again.
"Was that really the best you could do...?" The Caretaker sighs. "I suppose it was too much to ask that you show a little more backstem."
You apologize. The Orchid responds cheerfully. "No problem. Glad you understand."
"Was that really the best you could do...?" The Caretaker sighs. "I suppose it was too much to ask that you show a little more backstem."
The escort is caught offguard by your sudden attack. "You madman! Why are you attacking a garden convoy?"

name: ORCHID_RELOCATION_CONTACT_SHUTTLE
text: "Well, you managed to hold up your end of the bargain. I don't think I can do this alone... would you accompany us to Rt'lak Et? If you do, I will devote myself to your cause." The Caretaker gives the reward as promised.

choice.text: Accept the Caretaker and the coordinates.

event.text: "You won't regret this, Renegade. I will serve you faithfully. Now let's hurry to Rt'lak Et!"
"I appreciate what you've done for us anyway. Good luck, Renegade."

name: ORCHID_NONSAPIENT_RESCUE
text: With the escort vanquished, the helpless freighter immediately hails you. You respond as your crew begin to salvage the escort. "We surrender! Please, we will set a course back home. Just let us live!"

name: GARDEN_WORLD_CRUISER_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of Rt'lak Et.

text: You draw closer to Rt'lak Et, the greatest of the Orchid Gardenworlds. The alien infrastructure of the planet showcases the most breathtaking, impressive biotechnology available anywhere in the galaxy. The Caretaker sends you the precise latitude and longitude that concerns your mission. As you approach, it's clear there's a standoff: a small contingent of Caretakers are standing against a massive Orchid Elite ship. Nearby, there is also an Orchid station overseeing the conflict.

choice.text: Get closer and tune into the communications between the Orchid factions.

event.text:
"We've had enough of your alarmism, Mayeb. That parasite must be eroding your mind."
               
"It's not alarmism! If you keep removing so many species from the planet, not only is it immoral, but it could do long-term harm to the ecosystem. And don't you dare call P'Erpah a 'parasite'. She is my sister."
       
"Your sister? And yet, you are the only one who can 'hear' her. Perhaps we should send you off for 'treatment'."
       
"If you're done personally attacking us, maybe you could respond to the points I'm making."

The Praetor ship turns to yours. "These are internal affairs of the Ctl'Yae. The Federation must not interfere."

	A new voice comes over the comm, from the station. "Calm yourself, Praetor Bralmeb. I am Counsellor Pael, mediating this dispute. Although, the decision's been finalized. We are simply trying to convince Mayeb that she needs to stand down."

choice.text: Try to convince them to listen to Mayeb.

event.text:
You begin to make your case, but as you do, you are interrupted by the arrival of the freighter that you intercepted.
						   
	Bralmeb is astonished. "What?? You've returned so soon?? What's the meaning of this?" He mutes, and you're greeted with a few moments of radio silence as the freighter privately fills in the Praetors.
					   
	Mayeb, meanwhile, takes the opportunity to contact you. "Renegade, I appreciate your help in this matter, but I urge you to try and defuse the situation. I don't know if it's still possible, but do what you can."

The Praetor hails you, looking absolutely furious. "You meddlesome Renegade. You think that you can simply dictate the policy of whomever you come across? I don't care how powerful you think you are, or who you claim to represent. The Gathering will no longer sit on the galactic sidelines and be told what to do!" The Praetor ship arms its weapons. This will likely be a difficult fight.
You stay back and marvel at the planet from afar.

name: ORCHID_GARDENWORLD_SURRENDER
text: The Orchid cruiser is on the brink of defeat. Although their resolve doesn't waver, you could try one last attempt at diplomacy.

choice.text: Try to end the fight diplomatically.

event.text: You hail them, and the ship momentarily stops fighting you. Praetor Bralmeb seems frazzled, but still angry. "What, do you want me to grovel for my life? You want me to roll over and accept your way of doing things?"

choice.text: (Ivar) Tell them who they just fired upon.

event.text:
"Hey! Roothead! You just fired upon the premier of the Vampweeds! Do you realize what that means?"

Bralmeb seems uncomfortable. "Well... I..."

"So you're lucky that the attractive powerhouses over here love making peace as much as I do! Listen, this doesn't HAVE to be an interstellar incident. Just calm down, take your lumps and listen to this lovely Caretaker without judgement, okay?"

Bralmeb is still miffed, but for the moment he seems pacified.

Ty E'Rel takes a stern posture. "You have committed an unprovoked attack on a vessel carrying the primary diplomatic envoy between the Oro'Bache and the Ctl'Yae. As stated in the Kadahellian'ek Treaty, this is a grade 1 offense and is considered treason."

Bralmeb seems uncomfortable. "Unprovoked...? You..."

"I would like to remind you how 'provocation' is defined within the Accords. Or have you not read them? They were written before you sprouted. I should know, though, I was the third person to sign."

Bralmeb stutters, and falls silent. He disengages his weapons systems.

choice.text: (Tully) Get to the root of the problem.

event.text:
"This is Admiral Tully of the Federation fleet. Stand down, I repeat, stand down."

Bralmeb responds immediately. "Tully...? Why are you involving yourself in our affairs?"

"You said that you were stepping up military production because you feel that you are not properly represented on the galactic stage. Is that true?" Bralmeb nods. Tully continues. "Your people are often hesitant to ask for planets in other systems or military aid. Why then, are you resorting to such drastic measures in your own space?"
               
"...it is not our way. We do not like to be seen as dependent. We want to be self sufficient and provide for others."
               
"The Federation is meant to be a collaborative effort. We encourage you to ask for more - after all, your people are often generous."
               
Bralmeb pauses, and backs down without another word.

choice.text: You attacked us before we could talk. At least let us get a word in.

event.text: "Fine, but it will not change anything. Make your case."
"Hmph! I'm no scientist. I am a soldier, and if we want to be relevant, we have to bolster our forces. You criticize me for being ignorant. In my opinion, it's you who is ignorant!"

choice.text: Ask him if he has any scientists backing up his position.

event.text: Bralmeb grumbles. "If you won't listen to my viewpoint, then this conversation is over." Bralmeb stares at you for a moment. "I've gotten word that you helped out my colleagues. For that reason, I see no need to continue this fight. But my people need this, and I will not let them down." Just like that, he cuts comms again.

choice.text: Ask him if he has any scientists backing up his position.

event.text: "I've had enough of this! You won't listen to reason!" Just like that, he cuts comms again. Looks like it's back to fighting.

choice.text: Remind him that you serve your own military.

event.text: "I suppose that you are. Tell me, why would you decline to make the Federation stronger when you're currently on the run from a fleet of Rebel ships? Where's the logic in that?"

choice.text: We're not compromising who we are by doing what we're doing.

event.text: "Hmph, I thought we were getting somewhere." Bralmeb shakes his head. "If you're going to question my integrity, then this conversation is over." Bralmeb stares at you for a moment. "I've gotten word that you helped out my colleagues. For that reason, I see no need to continue this fight. But my people need this, and I will not let them down." Just like that, he cuts comms again.

choice.text: We're not compromising who we are by doing what we're doing.

event.text: "Hmph, I thought we were getting somewhere. You're just as foolish as the rest of them." Just like that, he cuts comms again. Looks like it's back to fighting.

choice.text: If you want to be stronger for the Federation, why not ask them for new worlds to use, or other ways to help?

event.text: "Our representatives do not like to make a lot of requests. It is not our way. Yes, it would be... better if we could get more out of this alliance, but this is all we can do."

choice.text: Then isn't your quarrel with your representatives, not the Caretakers?

event.text: Bralmeb falls silent. "...Very well. Maybe I am fighting the wrong people. I will back down. But if I can make no headway with our advocates, then do not fault me for pressing for this again."

choice.text: Tell him that he is being too aggressive, and to calm down before we engage in discourse.

event.text: "Too aggressive? How dare you! I don't have to listen to this." Just like that, he cuts comms again. Looks like it's back to fighting.

name: ORCHID_GARDENWORLD_MAYEB_WIN
text: Counsellor Pael and Mayeb adjudicate for a moment. Mayeb looks pleased. Pael clears his throat and addresses you. "Very well, as we re-settle the life from the freighter we will carefully review the data from the Caretakers. Perhaps we were... overzealous in our desire to bolster our military strength. And... as for you, Captain, we would like to sincerely apologize if your ship was damaged. Please accept a reimbursement from the Gathering for your trouble."

event.text: Mayeb smiles at you. "You have done so much for the Caretakers of Rt'lak Et. We were able to grow a special Caretaker cruiser for long ranged ecological missions... maybe it will prove useful to you. And... you've gone above and beyond on my behalf so... I would like to join your crew, if you're willing. I'm the Grand Gardener, but with the situation resolved peacefully, I think my peers can handle things without me. What do you say?"

name: ORCHID_GARDENWORLD_UNEASY_RESOLUTION
text: Counsellor Pael looks uneasy. "For better or for worse, it looks like we'll have to resettle for the immediate future. We'll have to address these problems over the course of the next few weeks. Months, even. Whatever happens, I appreciate your restraint. We hope this scrap will aid you on your trek to Node 17."

event.text: Mayeb smiles. "Thank you for taking our side. These next few months are going to be busy, but you've given us more than enough of a headstart. All I have to offer right now is one of our finest weapons, freshly grown. May it serve you well."

name: ORCHID_GARDENWORLD_DEFEAT
text: You have vanquished the Orchid Cruiser. However, the other Orchid defenses in the area probably wouldn't take too kindly to you scrapping their ship. You have no choice but to leave it adrift.

event.text:
Counsellor Pael sighs. "You've put us in a difficult situation here, Renegade. The freighter is not designed to be in operation for as long as it has, so we will have no choice but to reverse the decision for now. Please go, you've troubled us enough."

Mayeb nods. "It's too bad you were not able to spare them, captain. I appreciate your assistance, but the way this was resolved, I'm going to have to keep fighting for my cause. I wish I could offer more."

name: GATHERING_LOW_TRAFFIC
text: This area of the Gathering seems to normally be a low-traffic region. Despite this, an Orchid distress call is coming from this area.

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_PIRATE_TRAP
text: The transmitter is adrift, unconnected to any ship. A pirate blocks your path. "You're not one of these leafy weenies, but you'll do!" Looks like this was a trap!

name: DISTRESS_ORCHID_AMBASSADOR
text: A badly damaged cruiser of Orchid design is sending out a distress call. A Coalition Predator follows close behind, firing upon it.

event.text: You're greeted by a visibly withered Orchid. Both of his heritages are identifiable, having notable traits from both the Florals and the Vampweeds. Despite the state of his ship, he hasn't lost his veneer of professionalism. "Salutations. My name is Ty E'Rel." He gestures to the attacking ship. "Any assistance you could offer would be greatly appreciated." However, the moment you contact the Orchids, you attract the attention of the Coalition Predator.

choice.text: Demand that the Coalition ship stop firing.

event.text: You decide not to get involved - the Coalition ship remains focused on the unusual Orchid cruiser.

name: TY_EREL_RESCUE_GATHERING
text: The Coalition Predator is vanquished. The Ambassadorial Cruiser approaches yours as you scrap the Predator's remains.

event.text: The elderly plant appears on your viewscreen. He looks completely unruffled despite the recent attempt on his life. "Your arrival is timely. My compliments to your punctuality. My ship isn't in the best condition, but I would be more than happy to let you take it back to the Federation."

surrender.text: "Stop! State your demands, and we will end this!"

choice.text: Convince them to turn their ships around and return to Rt'lak Et.

event.name: RELOCATION_SURRENDER
event.text: "You... you're really passionate about this, aren't you? We'll do as you ask. If you can convince the rulership to change their minds, maybe it will be for the best." The escort sighs. "I'm probably going to get demoted for this..."

name: SHELL_VAMPWEED_HEALTH
text: A Vampweed ship hails you. "Excuse me! We got completely lost when trying to follow that guard's instructions. Those Shells can be so hard to understand, you know? Do you know the way to a Shell health center? Nebulas are an absolute nightmare to navigate."

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Give them your scanner readings.

event.text: "That's exactly what we need. I think we can find our way from here. Oh, you probably want some kind of reward now, don't you? Fine, here you go."

choice.text: (Shell Scientist) Offer to help them out.

event.text: The Shell Scientist offers to help. The Vampweed replies: "You see, my brother was mutated from some experiments performed by some Shell Scientists. There's been some side effects. Mental fog, chronic pain... Among other things. We have Shell Scientists in the Confederacy, but we don't have the research that they do. Unless your ship has some advanced lab equipment, I don't think there's much you can do, apart from telling me where to go."

choice.text: We do have an advanced lab, actually.

event.text: "Is that so? Well, I guess we'll do business with you instead, then." The Shell Scientist takes a look at the Cultivator up close. After a bit of work, the Shell writes a few prescriptions that might deal with some of the symptoms.
"Not bad, we were able to get our problem dealt with without even bothering with the nebula. Well, I think a tip is in order."

choice.text: Your Shell can give them directions.

event.text: "I think we can find our way from here. Oh, you probably want some kind of reward now don't you? Fine, here you go."

"You see, my brother was mutated from some experiments performed by some Shell Scientists. There's been some side effects. Mental fog, chronic pain... Among other things. We have Scientists in the Confederacy, but we don't have the research that they do. Unless your ship has some advanced lab equipment, I don't think there's much you can do, apart from telling me where to go."

choice.text: Alkali already knows how to help.

event.text: "Nobody's more experienced withhh Cultivators thhhhan I am. Bring him here." The Vampweeds are surprised, but travel over to your ship anyway. Alkali is quickly able to diagnose and treat the issue. "Here's thhhhe treatment. Don't deviate from it for 2 monthhhs. If thhhhe problems persist afterwards, come back for anothhhher checkup." Alkali discharges the patient and hands them their bill.
"Not bad, we were able to get our problem dealt with without even bothering with the nebula. Well, I think a tip is in order."
Once they detect your hostile intent, they respond in kind.
You apologize and recommend they ask somebody local to the region.

name: SHELL_CLAN_CHOICE
text: A Shell and a Slug Clansmen ship have entered a dogfight at this beacon. It seems the only way to get past is to fight one of them.

event.text: You attack the Shell ship head on, prompting the Guild ship to break away. Apparently, their dedication to the hunt does not go so far as to putting themselves in debt of a Federation ship, and so they jump away to leave you alone with the Shells.
You attack the Slug Clansmen head on. The Shells don't seem to want to stick around to see the outcome, and jump away.

name: ENCOUNTER_SHELL
text: Shells usually like to take refuge in the nebulas, but it seems one has wandered too far into a clearing. They seem to think you must be hunting them, because they immediately attack!

name: NEBULA_SHELL_CULTIVATOR_LAB
text: Next to this beacon is a small information terminal, providing directions to a laboratory in the nearest system - apparently they're in need of Vampweed volunteers.

event.text: You set a course for the lab. As you draw close, a laboratory admin contacts you. "Welcome, Renegade. We here at thhhhe Oro'Bache Genome Research Institute would like your permission to study and improve your crew. Do you have any Vampweed volunteers?"

"Splendid. Sign thhhhis waiver and let us run some tests, and see if thhhe procedure works." Your Vampweed enters the lab. After a short medical examination, the lab technician asks you if you have their medical records.

choice.text: (Medbay) Give the lab tech your medbay records.

event.text: Your crew is given specialized medicine based on their medical history. The Shell scientists hook your Vampweed up to a medical pod. After your crew is sealed inside, the pod begins to whir and hum...

Alkali tells the lab assistant to stand aside and hooks your Vampweed into a medical pod, already having sufficient knowledge to anticipate the medical needs of your crew. After your crew is sealed inside, the pod begins to whir and hum...
"I suppose we'll have to do withhhhout." The Shell scientists hook your Vampweed up to a medical pod. After your crew is sealed inside, the pod begins to whir and hum...

choice.text: Your Cultivator has a history with Shells - their medical history is already on file.

event.text:
"Premier Ivar? To what do we owe thhhhe pleasure?"
					
					Ivar chuckles. "I was just passing through. It's been a while since I've visited a lab. Last time I was here, Alkali showed me around."
					
					The scientist beams. "His presence is missed around here. Well, I dare not subject you to any tests - I'd hate to endanger thhhhe most respected alien in all of thhhhe Geniocracy. If you'd like, I can ask somebody from thhhhhe institute if thhhey would join your cause."

"Ah, thhhhe esteemed Ambassador E'Rel! Have you been well?"
					
					Ty E'Rel nods. "The relationship between the Oro'bache and the Ctl'Yae remains steady, though it's not a trivial endeavor. Did your lab have any other questions about the Gathering I can answer?"
					
					"Not at thhhhis time. Your responses and volunteers have been most helpful. We'd love to repay you. If you'd like, I can ask somebody from thhhhe institute if thhhey would join your cause."
"Ah, pity. Well, if you find any volunteers in thhhe future, be sure to direct thhhem our way."
You focus on warming up your engines instead of investigating.

name: CULTIVATOR_POD_SUCCESS
text: Your crew stumbles out of the pod looking quite different. They're bigger, stronger and capable of dispersing spores. "Congratulations, your Vampweed has been upgraded! We hope to see you again."

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_SHELL_FISHING
text: Your sensors pick up nothing in this part of the nebula, though the clouds here are a little less thick. You're about to prepare to jump away when you notice something tumbling towards you! You brace for something bad, but when it's finally near enough to make out, you realize it's... a weapon? It bounces off your hull with a faint clang and begins spiraling away.

event.text: You chase after the weapon. You're able to barely detect it disappear behind a cloud, and moments later you're able to scoop up what you think is a Beam weapon. It seems too easy, but you're not going to turn down a free weapon.

Before you can jump away, another ship appears nearby! They don't seem hostile however, and they hail you moments later. "Hello. We're running an experiment on how likely thhhhe average ship is to trust random objects in space, especially with thhhhe isolation thhhhe surrounding nebula provides." The Shell running this "experiment" rambles on about things you don't really understand, but you get the feeling they don't think very highly of you for grabbing the weapon. "Anyways, we'll pay you for your time. Just give us our weapon back so we can lau- I mean, test othhher ships."

The Shells send you some basic resources. When you crack open the supply crate they've sent, there's a note on top - something about a word on the ceiling? They must be crazy, because when you look there's nothing there.

choice.text: If they're dead, they won't need it anymore. Attack!

event.text: The Shell turns to someone offscreen. "Thhhhat's new. Allona, mark down thhhhat subject 33 is remarkably unintelligent-" The comm cuts and the Shells begin to fight back!

choice.text: That's way too suspicious. Leave it.

event.text: Space is huge. There's literally no way this weapon is just a stroke of luck. You let the thing disappear into the clouds and begin to charge your jump.

Before you're able to leave, another ship appears nearby! They don't seem hostile however, and they hail you moments later. "Finally! Someone who's not an idiot! You wouldn't believe how many morons see a weapon fly at thhhem and thhhhink 'Wow, thhhhat's not weird at all!'" The Shells, who explain they're running some kind of experiment, transfer you some resources for your time and even more for "not being an idiot".

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_SHELL_FOSSILS
text: Nearby drifts a Shell biologist, close to a large unpopulated planet. You receive a hail from the ship. "Long ago, we thhhink thhhis planet might have been habitable! Even more so, it could even hold thhhe fossils to thhe missing link between thhhe Shell and Slug races! Isn't thhhat cool?"

event.text: "Oh, it is so amazing to meet someone else who finds thhhhis interesting! Oohh, ohh, I know! I have a job for you, if you're interested. There's a couple fossil samples on thhhat planet that I want to collect, but thhhe atmosphere is too thhin for us to survive long. Do you thhhhink you could go get thhhem for us? Retrieving thhhem shouldn't be hard, thhhhere should be an abandoned dig site nearby."

You pilot down to the surface of the planet, where you spot a Smuggler ship collecting the fossils for themselves. "Hey, I wonder how much we could sell these funky rocks on the market fo- ah crap, it's a Fed! Run!"
"Thhhat's ok. Thhhanks for listening to my rambling anyways!"
You don't have time to take a biology lesson.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_TOXINTEST
text: Nearby appears to be a Shell science laboratory. They hail you: "Oh, good a visitor! We haven't seen many people recently, which is rathhhher unfortunate. With so many new... Rebels coming by, we've noticed you outsiders react rathhher strangely to our toxins. We would like to test thhhe effects on any aliens you might have... we understand thhhe risk and will pay accordingly."

choice.text: The scientists will have to look elsewhere for test subjects.

event.text: "We uh... appreciate thhhe gesture, but we really don't need to test on our own species..."

choice.text: (Anaerobic Crew) Send over your Anaerobic crew.

event.text: "How interesting! While thhhe toxin certainly still has an effect, smaller doses don't seem to cause as much harm. I wish I could test larger concentrations, but thhhat would be almost certainly fatal. Regardless, thhhank you for your help!"
"It is okay, I'm sure a Federation ship such as yours has more important thhhings to do anyways."

name: NEBULA_SHELL_SUZERAIN
text: Perhaps the last ship you expected to see in these nebulas were a Suzerain. Even less so, one who hails you almost immediately after jumping in.

event.text: "Captain, captain. These Shells, they very interesting, yes? I looking to capture one and use it for personal claw sharpener, but keep sawing in half!" The Mantis chuckles. "Do happen have Shell I can use?"

choice.text: Apologize, decline, and get the hell out of here.
Apologize, decline, and get the hell out of here.

event.text: "Tsk tsk, I know you having Shell on there! I cannot just let you get away with my prize!"
You power up the weapons and engage the Suzerains.

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Give the Suzerain your Shell crew.

event.text: You pass over your Shell to the Suzerain.

removeCrew.text: Though your Shell will likely be dead soon, it's probably best you don't clone them after this.

event.text: "Ah, thanking you! This one doing well, yes! Here is pay. Take warrior, not enough room for him now."

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Give the Suzerain your Shell Scientist.

event.text: You pass over your Shell to the Suzerain.

removeCrew.text: Though your Shell will likely be dead soon, it's probably best you don't clone them after this.

event.text: "Ah, thanking you! This one doing well, yes! Here is pay. Take warrior, not enough room for him now."

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Give the Suzerain your Shell Mechanic.

event.text: You pass over your Shell to the Suzerain.

removeCrew.text: Though your Shell will likely be dead soon, it's probably best you don't clone them after this.

event.text: "Ah, thanking you! This one doing well, yes! Here is pay. Take warrior, not enough room for him now."

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Give the Suzerain your Shell Guardian.

event.text: You pass over your Shell to the Suzerain.

removeCrew.text: Though your Shell will likely be dead soon, it's probably best you don't clone them after this.

event.text: "Ah, thanking you! This one doing well, yes! Here is pay. Take warrior, not enough room for him now."

choice.text: (Radiant Crew) Give the Suzerain your Radiant crew and let them be poisoned.

event.text: You send over your Radiant to the Suzerain. Not realizing it's a trap, they offer you a large reward.

Not long after, you notice radio silence from the Suzerain ship. You receive a hail from your Radiant, who you come pick up again. You take a brief glance into the ship and see all of the Mantis twitching on the ground, their brains having been reduced to mush.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_COALITION_RECRUITER
text: You notice a familiar shade of blue in this nebula. You quickly hide after realizing it's the Coalition! You catch radio chatter between them and a Shell ship, trying to recruit the Shells to their side.

choice.text: Interject and try to recruit the Shells yourself!

event.text: "Wha-" You cut off the Coalition and interrupt the conversation, preaching about the Federation. The irate Coalition captain continues his monologue, but the Shells don't seem to know who to listen to.

choice.text: Try to sway over the Shells with promises of a friendly alliance.

event.text: You make promises of a long-lasting alliance, open borders, and of course free cookies. The offer, especially the last part, seems to win over the Shells, much to the displeasure of the Coalition ship. Seeing that they've failed their mission, they decide to attack your ship!

choice.text: Try to sway over the Shells with promises of safety.

event.text: You promise safety to the Shells, but they could care less. Already confident in their defense, they opt to listen to the Coalition ship instead, who turns out to be very convincing. Now that they've won over the Shells, the ship attacks you next!

choice.text: Try to sway over the Shells with threats.

event.text: You threaten the Shells, but it does little more then agitate them. They opt to listen to the Coalition ship instead, who turns out to be very convincing. Now that they've won over the Shells, the ship attacks you next!

The Shells seem to believe the word of their friend. Confident in the Federation, one of them even offer to join your crew, much to the displeasure of the Coalition ship. Seeing that they've failed their mission, they decide to attack your ship!

choice.text: Step in and attack the Coalition ship.

event.text: You slip out of your hiding spot and attack the Coalition vessel. The Shell ship quickly jumps away.
If the Shells want to join the Coalition, so be it. Hopefully, they realize what a mess they're getting into though...

name: NEBULA_SHELL_CLAN_LODGE
text: It appears the Exotic Hunters Guild has established a hunting lodge near this beacon. Quite a bold move doing it within Shell space, but the Clansmen were never known for respecting territorial boundaries.

event.text: You'll be doing everyone a favor by getting rid of these guys. You ready the weapons and move in for the kill.
The lodge, seeing one of their members aboard your ship, agrees and transfers over some supplies.
It won't be long until one of the Shells notices this place and puts a stop to their operation. You have more important things to do than bother it.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_HIDING
text: You notice a Shell vessel, heavily damaged but still partially operational drifting nearby. Suddenly, the computer registered an unwanted teleporter signal!

event.text: A Shell materializes on the ship, and quickly rolls away into a far corner. Not long after, a Slug Clansman comes out from the nebula, firing a shot into the Shell ship, destroying it. It's not hard to piece two and two together here.

choice.text: Hand over the Shell to the Clansmen.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_ZOLTAN_TOXIN
text: You're hailed by a Zoltan science vessel. "You are a Federation vessel, correct? We request that you do us a service - for pay of course - by hunting down and capturing a Shell vessel. We wish to reverse engineer their toxins to develop a non-fatal paralysing chemical for peaceful conflict resolution."

event.text: "It is imperative that you do not destroy the vessel so that we may harvest the gas." The Zoltans direct you to a nearby Shell ship.
"Do not think that we will forget your unwillingness to help your allies." The Zoltans say no more.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_ADBUCTION
text: You spot a civilian ship nearby under attack by a Shell Abductor!

event.text: You're surprised to see the Shells actually respond to your hails. "Hello. Thhhis might look bad, but we promise not to harm thhhhese civilians. We only want to run a couple tests on thhhhhem, nothing more. It's for science!"

choice.text: Demand they leave the civilians alone.
Explain the situation to the civilians.

event.text: You don't give the Shells any chances and attack immediately.
You aren't sure why the Shells are attacking, but it's best not for you to get involved.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_NEUROTOXINLAB
text: Through the clouds of this nebula you spot a Rebel science station. It's strange to see one of these in Shell space, but surely there's a good reason.

event.text: Strangely, no Rebel ships interrupt you as you approach. Even stranger, the station appears to be empty of all life-signs except for one.

Surely, only one Rebel could cause no harm to you. You send over your crew. Inside, they find a large laboratory scattered with the corpses of scientists, though none have any visible wounds. The room smells faintly strange.

Your crew continue through the station, searching for the life-sign you had detected earlier. They find an unshaven, dishevelled engineer rocking back and forth, drooling and hugging a large cube. Your crew manage to calm him down long enough for him to explain the situation. It appears the engineers aboard were tasked with researching the neurotoxin released by the Shells and weaponize it, when one of their Auto-ships turned hostile. Using the toxin, it killed off all of the other scientists. The engineer warns you that now that you've boarded the station, the AI must know you're here too!
Your crew, followed by the psychotic engineer, hurry back to the ship. As they do, a large Auto-ship detaches from the station and chases you!

choice.text: This is strange. Pull out your crew.

event.text: You call the crew back to the ship, just in case.
You put some distance between yourself and the Rebel station, for good measure.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_MERCENARY
text: You aren't alone at this beacon. Nearby is a Syndicate vessel, all of its systems online but the ship remaining mostly inactive.

choice.text: Hail the mercenaries and see why they're here.

event.text: "Oh errr. We were hired by some Clansmen to capture one of these Shell ships, but that's a lot harder a task than we were prepared for. Now, we're kinda just waiting here until a Shell ship comes by and randomly dies. However long that'll take..."

choice.text: Help them out, seek out a Shell ship and capture them.

event.text: You fly past the mercenaries and deeper into the nebula until you encounter a Shell ship.
You decide not to give the pirates any chances and attack immediately.
Mercenaries in Central Shell space can't bode well. You ignore the ship.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_IMMUNITY
text: You receive a hail from a nearby Shell vessel pursuing what appears to be a Slug Clansman slipping away into the nebula.

event.text: "Thhhe Federation helps people, right? We need help! Thhhose Clansmen have stolen samples of thhhe Shell toxins. If thhey can bring it back to thhheir lab, thhhey might be able to develop an antidote! If thhhat happens, thhhhey'll be able to board our ships without any issues."

choice.text: Agree to hunt down the Clansmen.

event.text: "Perfect! If you can recover thhhe samples thhat would be wonderful, but if thhhat is beyond your capabilities don't worry. All we need is thhhem dead."
You don't know what's happening here, but you aren't interested in getting involved. You ignore the Shell, and eventually they give up and continue to chase down the Slugs.

name: NEBULA_SHELL_HIDDEN_COLONY
text: You catch the rear of a Shell ship slip away into the nebula. If you're quick, you might be able to catch up to them.

event.text: As you follow the ship through the nebula, you're shocked to find a massive Shell colony between several connected stations.
You hail the Shells within the colony. They wait for what you will say.
You decide the best course of action here is to attack these peaceful aliens for no good reason.
There is some talk amongst the Shells, but it seems they all agree trading with you will bring no harm.

choice.text: Demand they hand over some supplies.

event.text: You don't know what's happening here, but whatever that lone Shell ship is doing is of no concern to your mission.

name: SHELL_HIDDEN_COLONY_SURRENDER
text: "Please, stop! We will give you anythhhing, please just spare thhhe rest of us!"

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_SHELL_CHOICE
text: You spot a Shell ship approaching a small Slug transport. You aren't sure what the Slugs did to deserve this, but they appear to be in trouble.

event.text: Almost immediately after moving to help the Slugs they jump away, sending one last message to your ship's computer. "Psych!" The Shell ship is confused but assumes you have something to do with it and attacks!
You ignore the Slug ship and move past.

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_SHELL_SUFFOCATING
text: A nearby Shell ship appears to be the source of the distress beacon. Their life support has broken, and they're suffocating rapidly!

choice.text: Board and try to save the Shells!

event.text: You dock with the Shell ship, but it seems they aren't happy to see you. They mistake you for pirates and attack, though they won't last long without oxygen...

choice.text: (Upg. Oxygen) Dock and refill their O2.

event.text: You dock with the Shell ship and slowly refill their oxygen. It appears it's just enough to keep their levels stable long enough for the last survivor to escape. Without any crew or ship left, they offer to join yours.

choice.text: (Orchid Crew) Send over the Orchid to refill their oxygen.

event.text: You dock with the Shell ship and slowly refill their oxygen. It appears your Orchid is just enough to keep their levels stable long enough for the last survivor to escape. Without any crew or ship left, they offer to join yours.
Unfortunately, docking with their ship is likely too hazardous, considering Shell ships contain neurotoxin gasses. It's best for you to not get involved.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SHELL_CIVILIAN
text: Shell civilians aren't usually ones for direct combat... but with the bulk of the Military District on strike, a few have felt the need to take it into their own hands to protect the sector. Apparently, you're a threat, because the nearby Shell ship attacks!

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SHELL_MANAGEMENT
text: A Shell management vessel is performing construction on a nearby security checkpoint. Your sudden appearance has concerned them, and without any other ships to protect the checkpoint, they jump the gun and attack!

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SHELL_STORM
text: It appears a Shell ship is waiting inside this Ion storm. For what reasons they find you hostile you aren't sure, but it appears you can't get out of this fight so easily.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SHELL_SLUG
text: Usually, standard Slug ships like to avoid Shell sectors, not wanting to start a feud with their cousin species. However, one outlier ship appears to have crossed paths with you, and now it seems they're looking to fight!

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SHELL_AUTO
text: The Rebels aren't big fans of the Shells, but they're usually too afraid of their toxins to attack them in person. Instead, they prefer to send Auto-ships to do their dirty work. Unfortunately, one of these Auto-ships recognizes you and attacks!

name: NEBULA_SHELL_SMUGGLER
text: It appears a Smuggler ship is trying to sneak their way through this nebula! They notice you watching them and attack, not wanting you to rat out their location!

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SHELL_ELITE
text: The Shell Radiants are the protectors of Shell space. Their highly toxic composition works well at deterring enemy crew. Unfortunately, it seems one of these ships has found you in the nebula, and thinks you're a threat!

name: NEBULA_SHELL_UNIQUE_LAB
text: You receive a hail from a Federation vessel hiding in the nebula. "Oh, good, you must be the backup we called for! We were transporting troops to Node 17 when we were forced to detour through this sector. We thought we would be fine until a Shell Abductor came from nowhere and abducted our crew! We suspect they're being held at this beacon in a nearby laboratory, but we don't have enough firepower to rescue them on our own."

choice.text: Agree to help and inspect the station.

event.text: The station is unlike any other station you've ever seen, massive and painted in the colors of an Elite. This must be an important location.

choice.text: Hail them and negotiate peacefully. No need to murder these scientists.

event.text: "Oh, a Federation vessel. Welcome to thhhis beacon! What can I do for you?" You explain the situation, and the Shell seems to contemplate for a moment. "Oh, I see. My apologies, it has always been Shell custom to study creatures who enter our space. We bring no harm to thhhem of course, we simply bring thhhem aboard, run a quick few painless tests, and send thhhem on our way. We meant no harm! Do not worry, I'll have thhhem all released immediately. We want no trouble."
