While the Shells are releasing the Federation crew, you notice another jump signature has been detected. Suddenly, a stealth vessel appears at the beacon. You catch a message sent from the ship to the Shells. "This is Nighthawk, responding to the Federation distress beacon. You are in possession of Class-B Federation personnel. We will be docking with you shortly, you will surrender and be taken aboard for arrest or we will use force."

choice.text: (Tully) Order the Stealth ship to stand down.

event.text:
Tully responds to the call. "Stand down. You are engaging in unnecessary hostile action against a neutral power. The Federation ought to manage its relations with foreign powers with consideration, not aggression."
										
									The captain of the Nighthawk looks embarrassed. "We didn't realize the Admiral himself was here. We... overstepped our bounds. Please, accept our apologies. Now that our soldiers are returned, we'll withdraw after we collect the abductees." Nighthawk disconnects and begins transferring the soldiers.

"You sent a Federation Admiral to advocate for us...? I'm not sure how to thhhink about thhhat - but I don't have time to anyways. Please, I hope you will allow me to come withhh you now thhhat I cannot stay here."

choice.text: The Shells don't deserve this! Protect them and attack the Stealth ship.

event.text: You maneuver the ship in-between the stealth ship and the Shells. "You are protecting criminals? We will have no choice but to use force then!"

choice.text: Crap, we can't get involved in this. Leave.
Attack the station in hopes you can save the soldiers.

event.text: You arm the weapons and attack the Shell Laboratory. If you want to save the soldiers, you'll have to clean this place of crew without destroying the hull.

choice.text: This is more than we expected, leave.
Explain that you aren't the backup and leave.

event.text: You apologize to the Federation ship and explain you're on a more important mission. Hopefully, the real backup will arrive soon to help them.

name: SHELL_UNIQUE_LAB_RESCUE_LAB
text: "You saved us! Thhhat was a Federation ship thhhough... You would betray your own people to save us? I'm not sure how to thhhink about thhhat - but I don't have time to anyways. Please, I hope you will allow me to come withhh you now thhhat I cannot stay here. I will of course still free thhhese men and send thhhem back to thhheir ship first."

destroyed.text: The laboratory explodes, undoubtedly killing all of the crew, including the Federation personnel inside. You hope the Federation doesn't hear about this blunder...

deadCrew.text: You've killed all of the scientists aboard the station. You scrap the exterior of the hull.

event.text: You board the station and free all of the Federation personnel. They thank you briefly before rushing back to their ship, which has docked with the station to retrieve them. The Federation ship thanks you and pays you for your help.

You take a quick look around the station before you leave and find a strange device in one of the laboratories. It appears to be made to emit the neurotoxin that usually protects Shell ships. The one installed in the lab must have broken during the fight, judging from the fact you're able to be here now, but this one is fully functional. You bring it back to the ship.

destroyed.text: You've neutralized the stealth ship, and rescued the Shells in the process.

deadCrew.text: You've neutralized the stealth ship, and rescued the Shells in the process.

name: FINISH_BEACON_HACKER

visitedTooltip.text: This is the real exit beacon.

text: You've arrived at the exit...

event.text: It seems you've found the exit, but your Atlas won't connect. Something appears to be blocking the signal...
Suddenly, you receive a hail from a broadcast station hidden behind a small moon. "What'ssss thisss? The ssssilly little Renegade ssship isss trying to LEAVE? I'm afraid I can't allow that!"
The hacker station has been defeated, but the Rebel fleet has taken control of the beacon! You'll have to fight your way out!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: HACKER_EXIT_DEFEAT
text: The Hacker station has been defeated. Fortunately, your Atlas connects to the exit beacon as soon as the hacker threat is removed.

name: HACKED_CIVILIANS_FREECREW
text: A Union ship hiding from the hackers hails you. "Please, I can't keep hiding forever. Will you let me work on board your ship, so that I can escape from this bloody sector?"

choice.text: We don't need any more crew, sorry.

event.text: You apologize to them and carry on your mission.

name: HACKER_CIVILIAN_STATION
text: "A ship! I didn't think anyone would ever find us. A battalion of hackers moved through here and ransacked our station. We're out of supplies and we can't do business without them. Would you be willing to sell us some? We don't have scrap, but we can offer payment in other ways."

event.text: You transfer some fuel over to the civilians.
You transfer some ammunition over to the civilians.
You transfer some droneparts over to the civilians.
You apologize to the civilians and cut comms.

name: HACKER_CIVILIAN_STATION_THANK
text: "Thank you, we'll make sure to hide these better in case we're raided again. Now, how can we help you?"

event.text: "Yes, we can help with that. I will send out a repair team immediately!"

choice.text: We need to delay the fleet.

event.text: "I'm not sure how much we could do... but if the fleet comes by, we will lie about your location. Hopefully, they'll believe us."

choice.text: We could use a reactor upgrade.

event.text: "Yes, I think we can manage this. I'll send out a team to make some upgrades immediately."

name: HACKED_MILITIA
text: A Militia ship is passing through this system, likely trying to avoid the hackers who murdered the rest of their colleagues.

event.text: The Militia ship has received some damage from what likely was a recent battle. The crew is alive, but they're afraid and trying to flee the sector.
The militiamen thank you for your offer. You spend some time fixing their damaged systems, and are paid for your efforts.
Morals are obviously not of importance to you, as you have decided to attack the militia ship.
You don't disturb the ship and instead do something on board.

name: HACKER_OFFER
text: "Well if it issssn't the very ship I've been looking for. I'm ssssorry if my friendsss haven't given you a warm welcome, but I am here to extend an offer of kindnesss. I'm ssssure we could reach a mutually benificial trade..."

choice.text: Express interest in what they may offer.

event.text: "Ahh, I ssssee you have an eye for opportunity. Ressspectable." The hacker shows you some possible trades or services they could offer.

choice.text: Pay for detailed data on the sector.

event.text: The hackers transfer the data to your computer. Luckily, it doesn't appear to conceal any viruses.

choice.text: Pay for them to distract the fleet.

event.text: "I wassss hoping you would choossse thisssss. I will enjoy thissss job greatly..." You can imagine whatever they plan to do will be of great annoyance to the fleet.

"Sssso you wisssh to follow in our footsssteps? Cute. Really, quite cute. Don't let it go to your head, we will rule thissss sssector!" The Slug sends out a team to install the Hacking system on your ship. You make sure to keep a careful eye on them.
"Ssssshame. Try not to get killed..."
These Slug bastards are holding the civilians of this sector hostage. There's no way you're going to let them go so easily.

choice.text: We have no need for your services.

event.text: "Ssssshame. Try not to get killed..."

name: HACKED_PDS
text: A Hacker is currently interfacing with a planetary defense grid - they look distracted, and do not notice you yet. The station next to the grid hails you, but their message is garbled. "They're trying to hack our defense grid... but we're not making it easy for them! If you can help, then help. Otherwise, get out of here before it's too late!"

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Prevent them from interfering with the defense grid.

event.text: You're able to jam the hacking signal to the station's anti-ship batteries, which allows the defense grid to only target the enemy hacker. The Union station commander seems ecstatic. "Haha! Get 'em!"

The Hacker tries to taunt you. "Haha, you fool! We have already gained accessss to the defensssse grid!" The Slugs activate the grid... although it doesn't seem to be able to distinguish friend from foe. The captain then yells at his crew: "...What do you mean we weren't done yet?"

choice.text: Offer the hacker some scrap to scram.

event.text: "Hmmm... On the one hand, if we finissssh hacking the defensssse grid you might pay more... but we are outnumbered... Fine, we will accept your offer. Goodbye!"

choice.text: Get out of there before it's too late.

event.text: You elect to get out of the region as soon as possible. Unfortunately, this leaves you with no time to spend on on-ship activities.

name: HACKED_PDS_RESCUE
text: "Thanks for intervening - they almost had us. We'll make sure any other hacker that gets close will be sorry they messed with us. Take this and keep up the good work." The station gives you some resources and a weapon for your time.

name: HACKED_HOSTAGES
text: A small civilian colony nearby appears to be under control by a group of Hackers. The civilians are helpless against their captors.

event.text: You aren't going to let some corrupt filthy Slugs hold innocent civilians hostage when you can help it. You engage the hackers.

choice.text: Pay the hackers to release the civilians.

event.text: "What issss thiss? A generoussss donation from a mysssterioussss Federation benefactor? How kind. We weren't milking much cassssh from these civiliansss anywaysss..." The hackers release control over the civilians and jump away.
Either the hackers don't notice you, or they simply don't care to deal with your ship. You ignore the colony and carry on your way.

name: HACKED_HOSTAGES_WIN
text: You've defeated the hacker ship. The rest of the hackers, afraid of you now that you've defeated their colleague, flee from the system.

name: HACKED_CIVILIAN_WRECK_TRAP
text: The wreckage of a civilian ship drifts nearby. It's unfortunate that the civilians had to die in such a way, but there's likely some supplies on board that you can salvage.

choice.text: You have no crew to perform any form of salvage.
(Slug Crew) Have your Slug check the wreckage first.
(Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell check the wreckage first.

event.text: You aren't a gang of pirates or filthy hackers. Professionals have standards.

name: HACKED_FLEET_SPY
text: A hacker ship hails you. "Hello friendssss, it isss unfortunate that we mussst meet under thessse circumssstancessss. Assss you know, the Rebel fleet will pay a high price to know your location. That issss of courssse, unlesss you're willing to pay to keep your location a... ssssecret."

choice.text: Pay them not to alert the fleet.

event.text: "Thissss will do fine. Enjoy the ressst of your travelssss."

choice.text: We can't let this information get out! We have to kill the hackers.

event.text: You can't risk having the hackers leak your location to the fleet. You have to destroy them.
"Oh well. Hope you have ssssome fun with the Rebelssss then!" The hackers jump away.

name: HACKED_FANCY_CLASS
text: It appears a Slug and Hacker vessel are squaring off at this beacon. Judging from the dialogue you've intercepted between the ships, it seems they're arguing something about... ship classes?

event.text: The hackers won't respond to your hails, but the Slugs will. "The hackerssss have been leeching ssssshipssss from the Sssslug ssshipyardsssss for yearsss! They ressshape the interiorsss ssslightly and give them ssssome fancy namesss! Imagine the nerve of that."
You've decided to defend the Slugs and fight the Hacker vessel. Prepare for combat!
You've decided to defend the Hackers and fight the Slug vessel. Prepare for combat!
You'll stay out of a duel between two Slug ships. Mutual destruction would be a fitting end for them both.
You'll stay out of a duel between two Slug ships. Mutual destruction would be a fitting end for them both.

name: FANCY_CLASS_HACKER
text: You've defeated the Hacker vessel. You salvage the remains.

event.text: "An interesssting turn of eventsss... but not one that I'm going to complain about. Ssssome ssscrap is in order for you."

name: FANCY_CLASS_SLUG
text: You've defeated the Slug vessel. You salvage the remains.

event.text: "That wasss... unexpected. Moralssss my assss, I know you're looking for a reward. I don't ssssuppose you'd find usssse in a little delay in the Rebel fleet..."

name: NEBULA_LOST_SHIP_HACKER
text: A heavily damaged Federation ship is hiding in the nebula at this beacon. Before you have time to make contact with them, they fade into the nebula.

choice.text: Attempt to follow and help them.
Keep your position, they can handle themselves.

event.text: You decide not to chase after the Feds.

choice.text: (Teleporter) Lock onto their life-signs with your teleporter.

event.text: You beam the Federation crew aboard. One gladly joins your crew, the rest wait to be dropped off at the next station.

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Pump extra power into your sensors and try to track them.

name: DISTRESS_HACKER_MILITIA
text: The distress beacon here appears to originate from a Militia ship, currently fleeing from a Hacker vessel.

event.text: This sector needs all of the Militiamen that it can, and you aren't going to let the Hackers kill any more of them.
You can't risk your mission by rescuing the Militia ship. You carry on.

name: DISTRESS_HACKER_MILITIA_WIN
text: The hacker ship has been defeated. You scrap the ship.

event.text: It appears most of the Militiamen did not survive the attack. The lone survivor, their captain, offers to join your crew.

name: QUEST_HACKER_HOSPITAL
text: "Incoming ship, I don't know who you are or why you've come here, but please, hear me out. The hackers... they've captured a hospital in a nearby system. Many of us have family there, and we can't afford to pay their ransom. Please, you're their only hope."

event.text: The civilians forward the location of the occupied hospital. "Do everything you can, please."
The voice on the other side sobs, and shortly disconnects.

name: QUEST_HACKER_HOSPITAL_DESTINATION

unvisitedTooltip.text: Populated hospital occupied by Hackers.

text: The hospital at this beacon is indeed guarded by a hacker vessel as you were told. They swiftly hail: "If you don't have our ranssssom, then you'd besssst leave immediately."

choice.text: Attack the hackers holding the hospital hostage.

event.text: You have no intention of letting the hackers get away with their misdeeds.

choice.text: Pay the ransom to make them leave the hospital alone.

event.text: "Pleassssure doing bussssinessss with you." The Hacker vessel departs from this beacon.

choice.text: Apologize and leave as soon as you can.

event.text: "Tell thosssse humanssss they had better hurry up and pony up the dough."

name: HOSPITAL_SAVED
text: "This is the acting chief of staff of this hospital. We can't offer much, but we're in your debt. How can we help?"

choice.text: Have them upgrade your Clone Bay.

event.text: "Our lab technicians could do this in their sleep. I hope this helps you on your mission."
"Our lab technicians could do this in their sleep. I hope this helps you on your mission."

choice.text: Have them install an onboard lab for crew upgrades.

event.text: "Our researchers have state of the art lab equipment. We can spare some on your behalf."

choice.text: Have them upgrade your onboard lab.

event.text: "Our researchers have state of the art lab equipment. We can spare some on your behalf."

choice.text: Ask for a member of their medical staff to join you.

event.text: "That won't be a problem. We've got an aide who would rather be anywhere else than this sector right now."

choice.text: Ask if they can delay the fleet.

event.text: "We'll do what we can, but don't expect a miracle here, Renegade."

name: ENCOUNTER_HACKER_REBEL
text: A Rebel ship comes speeding towards you. "Damn it! The hackers took control of this sector while we were stationed here, and we have to find our way out! Now a Federation ship is here too? Hell, we gotta get to the fleet..."

name: ENCOUNTER_HACKER_AUTO
text: A Rebel Auto-ship, painted in hacker blue, sends you a message. "This is U-578-694. I have been repurposed to serve my new masters and destroy all intruders. Enjoy the rest of your miserable existence."

name: DESTROYED_HACKER_AUTO
text: You've defeated the hacked Auto-ship. You salvage what remains.

name: HACKED_DISABLED
text: You notice a change in the air, almost as if it's getting thinner. You check the computer to see your Life Support has been disabled! A Hacker ship hails you. "What an unfortunate thing to happen to a sssship like yoursss. If you have ssssome ssscrap, perhapsss we could sssolve thisss little... breathing problem of yoursss?"

event.text: "Good choice! We'll have that little problem taken care of rather quickly."

choice.text: You bastards, we aren't giving you anything!

event.text: "Poor decissssion... hope you won't be needing it any time sssoon!"
The hackers are dumbfounded by your apparent recovery from their cyber attack. Enraged, they raise their weapons and attack!

name: HACKER_CACHE

unvisitedTooltip.text: Uyo%Heav#Ton@Sdtviie!Stih*Anecbo

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. A hacker cache was located here.

text: The source of the strange garbled beacon here appears to be a Hacker Broadcasting Station. This must be one of the stations jamming the radio.

event.text: You raise your weapons and engage the broadcast station. You notice your systems fluctuating, they must have multiple combat augments onboard jamming you!
The Anti-Virus works its magic and counters the digital assault without any problems.
The Hacker ship's virus is much harder to purge than you expected, and you have to overclock the hacking system. Your systems return to normal, but your hacking has taken a huge loss.
You aren't willing to endanger yourself attacking a hacker station.

name: HACKER_CACHE_DEFEAT
text: The Hackers have been defeated. Your systems return to normal, and you move in to scrap the station.

event.text: You're about to leave when you notice a small platform and a cache nearby the wreck of the broadcast station.

name: HACKER_CACHE_QUEST
text: It appears you've taken out all of the Hacker broadcast stations in the sector! No longer restricted, your radio suddenly gets a flood of alerts, including a high priority Federation distress signal!

name: HACKER_FED_DISTRESS

unvisitedTooltip.text: Federation distress signal.

text: You've arrived at the location of the Federation distress call... except there's no Federation ship here. Instead, there's a massive Hacker cruiser waiting for you! "You think you're clever? Do you even know how long it took to sssset up all thossse ssstationss? Well, it doesssn't matter now. Thisss isss what you get for crossssing the Hacker clan'ssss path!"

name: HACKER_FED_WIN
text: Right as you finish off the hackers, a life pod detaches from the ship and spirals out into space... only for you to scoop it up and bring it aboard. Inside, you can see the surviving Slug quivering in fear.

event.text: You pry open the lifepod, and the Slug slides out slowly, hands in the air. "Ok, I sssurrender! You fight well. Too well... I'll give you anything and everything you want! Data, labor, ssscrap, all I assssk isss you don't kill me!"
You now have some time on your hands.

name: ENGI_SALVAGER
text: It appears a Lanius ship at this beacon is half-way through salvaging an Engi ship with crew still aboard. Though the Lanius ignores you, the Engi ship attempts to hail you. They request that you save them from the Lanius.

event.text: "We do not know what is. The trash ship. Trash is not a problem for to eat!" It seems the Lanius have mistaken the Engi ship as wreckage.

choice.text: Try to explain that there are Engi onboard.
(Lanius Crew) Have your crewmember explain the situation to them.

event.text: With the help of your Lanius crew, you successfully explain to the other ship that the Engi ship isn't wreckage. The other Lanius seems satisfied with this explanation and jumps away.
Communicating further is pointless. The only way to do this is through combat.
The Lanius ship continues to ignore you as you slink away.

name: ENGI_AID
text: An Engi colony established nearby hails you. "Federation presence suggests... Dire need of aid. Question: what is your need?"

event.text: "Request granted. Repair drone dispatched."
"Request granted. Refueling drone dispatched."
"Request granted. Payload drone dispatched."
"Request denied, restricted area. Salvage drone dispatched as alternative."

name: ENGI_FLEET_DELAY_MV
text: You notice an Engi colony hiding on the other side of a nearby moon. It turns out they're excavating an equipment cache from the Federation-Mantis War, and they suggest it might be used to lure the pursuing rebel fleet.

event.text: You transfer down some missile warheads and the Engi rig them to blow before setting a distress signal to attract the fleet's attention.
You have the Engi complete their excavations and bring the supplies onboard.

name: ENGI_SURRENDER_MV
text: An Engi ship in the vicinity, seeing you jump in armed to the teeth, immediately broadcasts its surrender: "Subject goal: wealth. Engi motivation: survival. Transfer of goods acceptable?"

event.text: The Engi obediently transfer over the goods and get on their way. Money for nothing.
The Engi were right to assume you're hostile! You attack the ship.

choice.text: Remind them that you are in good standing with the Harmony, and of the importance of your mission.

event.text: "Acknowledged. Your presence = positive for the Harmony. Clearing your ship, granting request for tribute."

choice.text: (Engi Defender) This ship is cleared already. Our mission will benefit the Harmony.

event.text: "Acknowledged. Trustworthy crewmember detected. Clearing your ship, granting request for tribute."

Mafan exuberantly yaps about their scientific mission, which causes the Engi to pause their search. After winding down, Mafan folds their arms. "If anything, you ought to donate to our scientific mission, since it will benefit the Harmony."
				
			"...Acknowledged. Trustworthy Ministry scientist detected. Clearing your ship, granting request for tribute."

The Defender doesn't respond immediately, but Ty E'rel continues. "According to the Federation Charter, section 3, Ambassadors are granted priority clearance in all Federation aligned sectors - including Harmony sectors. Ours is a mission of stability."

			The Defender finally responds. "Request acknowledged. On your way."
The Engi thoroughly search your ship, but come up empty handed. "You = cleared. If fugitive = discovered, then report. Else, carry on."

The Engi investigator searches the ship for your crew, and initially finds nothing. However, just before they leave, they discover a crewmember of yours that they take issue with. "Fugitive detected. Hostile intervention = necessary."

choice.text: We will not consent to being searched.

event.text: "Unacceptable. Refusal = admission of guilt. Arrest imminent." Looks like you can't get out of this situation that easily.

choice.text: Jerry nervously speaks. "Um, I think the Harmony knows about my connection to my uncle. They might have me on their watchlist."
Turzil speaks up. "The -Harmony- is [still] searching for me. If my presence is discovered, then we -- will be attacked."
Your Separatist informs you that this vessel will need to be destroyed.
As per the Rebel-Harmony non-aggression pact, Wentworth technicians are not allowed in Harmony space.
The Engi will not tolerate a former MFK Rebel in their region of space.
Your Angel tells you that it would be better to fight your way out of this situation.
Legionnaires are among the most dangerous troops the Rebellion has ever fielded; the Harmony will likely be outraged at their presence.

name: ENGI_ADVISORY
text: There is a small advisory at this beacon. "ALERT: The system at this beacon is the site of the most common Mantis attacks in the sector. ADVISORY: Spend very little time at this beacon. If a Mantis ship is spotted, please report to the Harmony."

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Locate the Mantis with your scanners.
(Adv. Sensors) Locate the Mantis with your sensors.
Follow the advice and move along.

event.text: Fighting Mantises is something you're capable of, but going out of your way to look for them doesn't seem like a good way to spend your time.

name: ENGI_FORWARD_TO_HARMONY
text: You send a long-ranged communique to the nearest communication hub. Shortly after, a Harmony vessel jumps in with a message: "Appreciated. This information will curtail similar attacks in the future." The Harmony rewards you with some scrap and drone parts for your trouble.

name: ENGI_LOCATE_MANTIS_AMBUSH
text: Your systems immediately locate the Mantis ships. There are ambush points that they have set up for themselves. Since you know their locations, you can face any kind of ship you want, or you can avoid a fight and give the Harmony the intel to do so.

event.text: With foreknowledge of the ambush, you get the drop on the Mantis. However, they are ready to fight back!
With foreknowledge of the ambush, you get the drop on the Suzerain. However, they are ready to fight back!

name: DEFEAT_SUZERAIN_ELITE_ADVISORY
text: You've managed to take down a powerful Hive Elite and their ship, and now the remains are yours to scrap.

event.text: It seems the cargo of the Mantis Elite ship survived the fight. Inside is a functional weapon, which you bring back on board.

choice.text: Forward the rest of the information to the Harmony.

name: ENGI_IMPLANT_UNION
text: A Harmony ship is currently docked with a Union ship. There's a small amount of debris, suggesting there may have been a struggle preceding your arrival.

event.text: The Engi ship responds. "This vessel = suspected of future Rebel sympathies. Actuarial reports suggest best option = forcibly installing behavioral correction implants. This action = necessary for Harmony prosperity and safety."

choice.text: We won't stand for this disgusting violation of human rights!

event.text: "Harmony prosperity >> any Human's rights. Impeding Harmony prosperity = unacceptable." The Engi vessel responds to your threat in kind.

choice.text: (Engi Defender) Try to convince them this may not be necessary.

event.text:
"Do you have proof that this vessel = future Rebels?"
					
					"Negative."
					
					"Then stand down. Rebel threat probability estimation: under conflict initiation threshold."
					
					"Understood. However, expect consequences if your decision processing = unwise." The other Engi ship jumps away.
As disturbing as that prospect is, you don't have all the information. Provoking the Harmony is not on your to-do list either.

name: ENGI_VS_VAMPWEED
text: A dogfight has broken out between a Confederate vessel and a Harmony vessel.

event.text: "Of course the Federation would take the side of these crazy machines." The Vampweed breaks off to respond to your attack!
"Federation is delinquent in allied responsibilities. Dispatching traitor."

choice.text: Let these two fight it out.

event.text: The affairs of these two ships doesn't concern you.

name: ENGI_VS_VAMPWEED_VAMPWEED_KILLED
text: "Federation assistance appreciated. Intolerant foreign element dispatched. Dispensing drone reward." The Engi ship jumps away, leaving the question of what had gone down hanging in the air.

name: ENGI_VS_VAMPWEED_ENGI_KILLED
text: "So the Federation has some scruples after all. All we came here to do is trade, and these crazy nutjobs searched our ship and attacked us without telling why." The Vampweed captain sends one of their signature drones.

name: ENGI_SEX
text: What appeared to be a single damaged ship is in fact two ships that have smashed into each other... there is a flurry of comm signals and damage, and it's hard to determine what occurred. The vessels appear to be... Engi? They look locked together by the impact and can't free themselves.

choice.text: Attempt to help the ships by prying them apart.

event.text: To your surprise, one of the Engi vessels attacks! One ship detaches itself, surprisingly still quite whole, and opens fire - it looks like it's somehow identified you as hostile!
This isn't your business.

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Have your Engi crewmember hail the vessel and assess the damage.

event.text: Your Engi crewmember refuses. In a halting use of adjectives and nouns, followed by some animated holographic aids, the Engi explains the ships are... using each other to, loosely translated, "achieve a union." For some reason, this consolidation of ship matter sounds embarrassing and personal.

You elect to leave the two Engi ships... to their "business." After questioning your Engi crewmember, however, you do manage to salvage what scrap parts you can from the perimeter, even though you feel slightly dirty for doing so.

name: ENGI_SEX_SHIP_DONE
text: Apparently, you interrupted the equivalent of a "consolidation" of two ships that were using each other's parts to construct a new vessel. The Engi were not truly hostile, their targeting computers had not finished adjusting. There's nothing to be done about it now. You leave the remains for the surviving ship.

name: ENGI_DECONSTRUCTOR_JUNKYARD
text: From the beacon, you can spot several large masses. Among them are two gigantic fields of debris, with an indistinct mass between them. One debris field is very high in metallic content, and the other, much larger debris field seems to have very little salvageable content.

choice.text: Explore the pile of metallic debris.
Explore the mass between the fields.

event.text: You emerge closer to find a large, buzzing cloud of nanomachines, as well as a gigantic chamber. Periodically, what appears to be an Engi ship drags something from the metallic debris field towards the cloud. However, once you get close, an Engi ship intercepts you. "This region = restricted to Engi nanoforms. Proceed: away from this beacon."

Your Engi explains the importance of your mission, and requests whatever resources can be spared. "...confirmed. Allied Engi: on important mission. You may: request one Harmony construct. Will offer resources."
In a shimmering haze, a brand new Engi is printed from the swarm directly into your cargo bay. The Engi nods at you, ready to take orders.
In a shimmering haze, a drone schematic is printed from the swarm directly into your cargo bay.
In a shimmering haze, a drone schematic is printed from the swarm directly into your cargo bay.
"Goal = gather salvage, provide to greater collective. Resources: produce more [nanomachines, drone schematics, vessel components]. Question: answered. Go."
The Engi immediately responds to your aggression - they were anticipating your greed.
The Engi immediately responds to your aggression.
You decide not to spend any time examining these fields.

name: JUNKYARD_HAIL_SWARM
text: The swarm sends a text message in return. "Plea: spare. Will offer surrender."

event.text: In a shimmering haze, a brand new Engi is printed from the swarm directly into your cargo bay. The Engi nods at you, ready to take orders.
In a shimmering haze, a drone schematic is printed from the swarm directly into your cargo bay.
In a shimmering haze, a drone schematic is printed from the swarm directly into your cargo bay.

name: ENGI_VIRUS
text: The Engi are awaiting you at the beacon, with their weapons online! They explain a computer virus that is wanted for hostile acts against the Engi (multiple counts of binary scrambling, nano-dissolution, and variable interference) is aboard your vessel.

event.text: They insist they must destroy your ship to prevent the virus from escaping!

choice.text: Hold on! Let us try to purge the system code!

event.text: Wiping your Engine core and shields proves useless... eventually you trap the virus in the weapons systems to purge it, but before you do, the Engi grow restless and attack!
The Engi be damned, no one threatens your ship. You prepare for a fight!
Turzil isolates the virus and talks to it, interfacing with the system. You can tell it tries to possess him, but it doesn't seem to take.

After a few minutes, the virus "sees the light" and integrates itself in a positive manner with the computer society on your ship, repairing your hull and attempting to optimize your reactor. "Negotiation successful. If you are -willing-, I recommend thanking our new routine."

The Engi thank you for deleting the virus, and jump away. They offer an augmentation as a reward. Fortunately, they remained unaware of Turzil's presence - they must have been too preoccupied with the virus.

It takes some time, and the virus is slippery, but you eventually confine it to a useless sub-system prison where it frantically begins calculating insults at you. You eject the system from the ship and then silence the little binary criminal with your weapons.
The Engi thank you for deleting the virus, and jump away. They offer an augmentation as a reward.
You proceed to interface with the virus and optimize its repair and benevolence routines.
After a few minutes, the virus "sees the light" and integrates itself in a positive manner with the computer society on your ship, repairing your hull and attempting to optimize your reactor.
The Engi thank you for deleting the virus, and jump away. They offer an augmentation as a reward.
You proceed to interface with the virus and optimize its repair and benevolence routines.
After a few minutes, the virus "sees the light" and integrates itself in a positive manner with the computer society on your ship, repairing your hull and attempting to optimize your reactor.
The Engi thank you for deleting the virus, and jump away. They offer an augmentation as a reward.
Your Anti-Virus makes quick work, finding the hostile code and erasing it from existence.
The Engi thank you for deleting the virus, and jump away. They offer an augmentation as a reward.

choice.text: (Lanius Crew) Your Lanius crewmember gestures frantically.

event.text: Oddly enough, the Lanius seems aware of which computer the virus is present in, and proceeds to... digest the terminal. There is a burst of O2, and the Engi ship powers down its weapons, no longer sensing the virus on board. The Engi send some parts over to repair your damaged computer, along with an augmentation as a reward for terminating the virus.

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Have your Engi crewmember negotiate with the Engi ship.

event.text: As the Engi attempts to contact the vessel and negotiate, your Engi crewmember suddenly dissolves into nanites - the virus has murdered again! Detecting activity on board your ship, the Engi vessel opens fire!

removeCrew.text: The virus appears to have disrupted your clone bay's capability to revive the lost crewmember!

choice.text: (Engi Defender) Have your Defender crewmember negotiate with the Engi ship.

event.text: As the Engi attempts to contact the vessel and negotiate, your Defender crewmember suddenly collapses, struggling - the virus must have infected them! However, your Defender gets up not long after. "Threat neutralized. Deleted code: 2 lines." This seems good enough for the Engi ship, and they reward you for deleting the virus.

choice.text: (Cognitive Crew) Have your Cognitive negotiate with the virus.

event.text: You explain to the Engi that you might have a solution, then wait for your Cognitive to do its job. Not too long after, the Cognitive comes back online. "Negotiation attempts have failed, resorted to alternative methods. I instead convinced the virus that life is pointless. Once it had adopted the same nihilistic philosophies that plague my databanks, it decided to end its life rather than continue to suffer." Satisfied, the Engi ship rewards you for deleting the virus.

name: ENGI_VIRUS_REBORN
text: To your surprise your Engi crewmember reforms. It looks as if the virus reconstituted, repurposed, and reprogrammed the Engi host and wants to travel with you... and it seems to have learned a great deal from its time on your ship.

name: ENGI_COMPLEX
text: A huge, well protected Engi Station is at this beacon. From the looks of it, it appears to be staffed partially by Engi Defenders. Clearly, it's protecting something important.

event.text: Whatever secrets this station holds, you want them. Best way to get what you want? Through the distribution of violence.
Scans show the station is some sort of Engi production facility! Maybe if you can kill the crew, you can find a way to produce an Engi crew.
You decide to try and take over the facility. You power up your weapons and engage.
Attacking a well armed Engi Station in Harmony space is practically suicide. You decide it's best to ignore it.
Attacking a well armed Engi Station in Harmony space is practically suicide. You decide it's best to ignore it.

name: DESTROYED_ENGI_COMPLEX
text: The remains of the Engi Station are littered with far more Engi corpses than there were crew staffing it. The origin of them will remain unsolved; you decide to scrap the only remains of the station.

name: DEAD_CREW_ENGI_COMPLEX
text: Aboard the station you're surprised to find hundreds upon hundreds of tubes filled with nanobots. In some of the tubes they have begun to resemble Engi, and in others, they are still a swarming mess that resembles sentient goop.

choice.text: Try to reprogram one of the Engi to serve you.

event.text: Your attempts at trying to create an Engi fail horribly, and a monstrous abomination of a creature falls out of the test tubes, latching onto one of your crew and tearing off their head! You blast it with your rifle but that only seems to temporarily stun it. You retreat back to the ship before it can kill any more of you. You stick to scrapping the external regions of the station.

removeCrew.text: Luckily, your crew member has already been cloned by the time you return to the ship.

choice.text: You don't feel confident to suffer the consequences of playing god without anyone watching your back.
Ignore the tubes and scrap the station.

event.text: Trying to play around with things you don't understand can be deadly. You stick to what you do know: scrapping newly emptied stations.

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Reprogram one of the Engi to serve you.

event.text: You pick one of the better looking Engi and reprogram it to serve you faithfully. While the Engi is produced, you collect some of the supplies around the station.

choice.text: (Hacking) Reprogram one of the Engi to serve you.

event.text: You pick one of the better looking Engi and reprogram it to serve you faithfully. While the Engi is produced, you collect some of the supplies around the station.

choice.text: (Adv. Hacking) Reprogram one of the Engi to serve you.

event.text: With your hacking you're able to access one of the higher security areas, which appears to contain Engi Defenders! You reprogram one of them to serve you loyally, and quickly grab some supplies on your way out.

choice.text: (Obelisk Crew) Your Obelisk knows how to manufacture Engi.

event.text: As the Obelisks were (indirectly) responsible for the creation of the Engi, it's no surprise they know how to operate the machinery. It sets one of the machines to create an Engi Defender while you grab some supplies.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_SALVAGE
text: This beacon is littered with parts from Civilians and Pirates, and even a few Engi ships. Only one Elite Engi ship remains, and from the lack of damage you assume it was not involved in the battle.

event.text: "Presence unexpected. Assistance requested. Battle has occurred here, wreckage = heavy. Aid in salvaging greatly appreciated. One stipulation: any salvage must be returned to this ship in return for fair payment."

choice.text: Agree, knowing it will take a lot of time.

event.text: You collect as much of the debris as you can in a somewhat reasonable amount of time.
It's quite a lot, but you know you're supposed to give it back to the Engi ship.

choice.text: Give the supplies back to the Engi.

event.text: The Engi collects the supplies.
You wait for your reward, but the Engi transfer nothing over. You hail them, to which they respond, "Reward is already present. Gratification and warm feeling for helping others."

choice.text: What? We will not stand for this!

event.text: You aren't about to put up with this garbage. You power up the weapons and prepare to engage the Engi head-on.
"Your efforts = appreciated." The Engi ship ends the call and goes back to salvaging.

choice.text: Refuse to give the resources back.

event.text: You've spent too long collecting all this salvage, you aren't going to just hand it over willingly.

choice.text: (Harmony Crew) Request you split the supplies.

event.text: "This compromise... fair." There's some argument on who gets the larger half, but eventually you reach an agreement.

choice.text: (Magnet Arm) Use your ship arm to collect additional scrap.

event.text: Your Magnet Arm is fortunately able to increase the amount retrieved within a reasonable timespan.
It's quite a lot, but you know you're supposed to give it back to the Engi ship.

choice.text: Give the supplies back to the Engi.

event.text: The Engi collects the supplies.
You wait for your reward, but the Engi transfer nothing over. You hail them, to which they respond, "Reward is already present. Gratification and warm feeling for helping others."

choice.text: What? We will not stand for this!

event.text: You aren't about to put up with this garbage. You power up the weapons and prepare to engage the Engi head-on.
"Your efforts = appreciated." The Engi ship ends the call and goes back to salvaging.

choice.text: Refuse to give the resources back.

event.text: You've spent too long collecting all this salvage, you aren't going to just hand it over willingly.

choice.text: (Harmony Crew) Request you split the supplies.

event.text: "This compromise... fair." Fortunately both sides are able to get an equal split of the salvage.
The Engi end communication and go back to salvaging the wreck. They don't respond to further hails.
You start to collect some of the scrap when the Engi ship starts approaching quickly. "This area is restricted. Salvaging: banned. Hostile response required."
You avoid the Engi ship and the wreckage.

name: DISTRESS_HARMONY_SALVAGE_HELP_DESTROY
text: With the Engi ship destroyed, you have no chance of getting back all that you had previously salvaged. You collect what's left of the wreckage.

choice.text: Collect some more of the wreckage.

event.text: You can't collect much more without the Rebel fleet advancing further, but it's better than nothing.

name: DISTRESS_HARMONY_SALVAGE_HELP_CAPTURE
text: With the Engi ship emptied, your previous salvage can easily be recollected. You best leave the beacon quickly before the Rebel fleet can progress further.

name: DISTRESS_HARMONY_SALVAGE_HELP_CAPTURE_MAGNET
text: With the Engi ship emptied, your previous salvage can easily be recollected. You best leave the beacon quickly before the Rebel fleet can progress further.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_HACKER
text: The source of the distress beacon appeared to have been an Engi ship under attack from an Auto-Hacker. As you jump in, a hacking drone pierces through the Engi ship. The Auto-Hacker moves in to attack, and a set of hacked Engi are beamed aboard.

name: DISTRESS_HARMONY_HACKER_WIN
text: The Auto-Hacker has been destroyed. You scrap the remains.

event.text: With the Auto-ship destroyed the remaining Engi onboard their ship return to normal. They give you some droneparts.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_REACTOR
text: You arrive at a smouldering Engi research station, its distress call unanswered - attacked by pirates or Mantis most likely. There may be someone left alive, or else something of value left on board.

choice.text: You have no one aboard to send over.

event.text: The place looks in bad state, probably nothing of use there. Time to move on.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_REACTOR_SCAN
text: Scans reveal the station's reactor is overloading! Not only that, but an injured Engi and a functioning drone schematic are still on board! There's not time for both...

event.text: Your away team heads straight for the Engi and returns with time to spare. You put some distance on the station before it blows and the Engi is so impressed by your crew that they volunteer to join you!

Your drone heads straight for the Engi and returns with time to spare. You put some distance on the station before it blows and the Engi is so impressed by your tactic that they volunteer to join you!

The Engi don't feel things the same way other species do. They'd want the tech to be saved. Your away team heads straight for the goods and returns with time to spare. You put some distance on the station before it blows.

The Engi don't feel things the same way other species do. They'd want the tech to be saved. Your drone heads straight for the goods and returns with time to spare. You put some distance on the station before it blows.

choice.text: There's no one aboard to perform an extraction of loot or crew.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_REBEL
text: The distress signal originates from a small Engi ship under attack by a Rebel fighter - but when the Rebels see Federation markings they turn to attack!

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_REBEL_RESULT
text: The Engi vessel turns out to be very poorly equipped - barely a runabout, really. They're trying to outrun the Rebels, and need all the help they can get.

choice.text: Give them 40 scrap, 2 missiles and 2 fuel.

event.text: Engi can't feel fear, so they bear you no ill will when you explain you're unwilling to help. They set off on their journey and you do the same.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_REBEL_LIST2
text: They wouldn't get more than a few jumps with that load-out. You provide them with all the munitions and supplies they should need for the journey home. "Generosity magnitude unpredicted. Well-being syntax error [value too high]. Accept this token."

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_PARTY
text: The distress beacon here is coming from an Engi vessel, but it does not seem to be in any danger.

choice.text: Hail the Engi to see what's wrong.

event.text: An Engi wearing a purple party hat appears onscreen. In the backgrounds are colorful rapidly flashing lights and several Slugs dancing. "Commence greetings. Inquiry: knowledge of how to 'party hard'. Request: mind-altering substances for gratification, recommended by Slug visitors."

choice.text: (Ion Weapon) Zap the Engi, it's close enough.

event.text: The Engi flails like a puppet for a few minutes. Once it regains control over itself, its screen begins to rapidly flash colors, and it speaks very slowly. "Graaaaatituuuuuude. Thiiiiiis is: dooooope. Aaaaacceeeeept cooompeeeensaaaaaatiooon."

choice.text: (Mantis Pheromones) Disperse the pheromones over their ship.

event.text: A steady distribution of the pheromones certainly has... an effect on the crew. You may have given them too much, because now the Slugs are trying to climb the walls and the Engi are hugging the drones. While they're distracted you scrap some of the exterior regions of their ship.

choice.text: (Orchid Crew) Have your Orchid work some magic on them.

event.text: The Orchids have a unique ability to put others in a... "daze". The effect is visible on the Slugs and Engi who begin to act very strangely. They pay you for your "assistance."

choice.text: (Butler Drone) Turn it up to eleven.

event.text: It's not exactly what they requested, but they won't complain. The Butler tends to every numerous needs the Slugs and Engi request when they notice it. Soon, it eventually raises the already high volume, and the crew can no longer keep up. Before they all pass out, they graciously pay you for your "assistance."

choice.text: (Quarp Juice) Add some extra energy to this party.

event.text: You share out helpings of Quarp Juice to the Engi and their Slug companions. Immediately the partygoers start to get more energetic and excited. The Engi, who is visibly shaking, pays you before rushing off to join their Slug companions, who seem to be bouncing around the room.
The threat must have already disappeared, and the Engi simply have not yet switched off their distress beacon. You move on.

name: DISTRESS_ENGI_DANGER
text: You receive a distress call from a nearby Engi ship. "Assistance requested. Danger present. Imminent destruction."

choice.text: Respond to the call and move in to assist.

name: QUEST_ENGI_SLAVE
text: You find a poorly equipped set of Mantis ships. Surprisingly, one of them hails you. "You're Federation ship? Maybe yes, maybe no, we not care. We have proposition for you."

event.text: "As can see, arsenal on ships less than good. High grade Engi military facility is nearby, we cannot raid it like this. Your ship, better armed. Break in, steal slaves, bring to us. We pay you."
The leader of the Mantis ships, a Suzerain vessel, transmits the co-ordinates of the facility, and shows you how to communicate with them when the job is done.

choice.text: We aren't in the slavery business.

event.text: "Pah, Federation ship so boring. Don't come back."

choice.text: We aren't looking to take any jobs.

event.text: "Pah, Federation ship so boring. Don't come back."

name: QUEST_ENGI_SLAVE_FACILITY

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Mantis asked you to raid a station to gain Engi captives.

text: The Engi facility appears to be a medium sized Engi station. If you're going to capture slaves, you'll need to weaken their defenses enough that they surrender.

event.text: You prepare to engage the station. Completely unable to flee, the Engi have no choice but to fight back.

choice.text: (Teleporter) Try to board and take an Engi.

event.text: Your crew's attempts at boarding the ship go in vain. The Engi security system is too good and detects your crew almost immediately. You beam them back and prepare to fight.
You aren't going to go stealing Engi slaves for a Mantis, especially not in the Harmony sector.

name: DESTROYED_ENGI_SLAVE_REQUEST
text: You have no hope of saving an Engi now that you have destroyed the station. You delete the Mantis contact and scrap the station.

name: DEAD_CREW_ENGI_SLAVE_REQUEST
text: In a mission to capture a living Engi crew, you decided it was a good idea to murder them all. With no way to get a live Engi now, you delete the Mantis contact and scrap the station.

name: SURRENDER_ENGI_SLAVE_REQUEST
text: The Engi station transmits a surrender message. They're willing to meet any of your demands.

choice.text: Demand they give you an Engi as a slave.

event.text: The Engi station spends a few minutes deciding who to send over. At last, one unlucky Engi is sent over to your ship.

choice.text: Do as promised and bring them back to the Mantis.

event.text: It seems brutal, but you have no choice but to lock up the Engi in the cargo hold. You contact the Mantis, who are pleased with you. They transmit their new co-ordinates.

choice.text: Let them stay and work aboard your ship.

event.text: The Engi is as close to surprised as it can be. With this outcome much preferred to toiling away on a Mantis ship, the Engi willingly joins your crew.

choice.text: Screw the Mantis and the Engi, let's finish this fight.

name: QUEST_ENGI_SLAVE_MANTIS

unvisitedTooltip.text: The Mantis are awaiting the delivery of the Engi here.

text: You arrive at the location of the Mantis. They take the Engi aboard, and as promised give you plenty of scrap, as well as a drone they stole from another Engi ship.

name: QUEST_ENGI_CRIME
text: Of all the ships you would have thought to see here, a Rebel Engineer is the last one you would have expected. They're busy inspecting the wreck of an Engi ship, though due to the non-aggression pact between the Rebels and Engi, and the fact that the Engineer's weapons don't match with the damage done to the ship, it's likely they weren't the one to destroy the ship.

choice.text: Hail them to ask about the wreck.

event.text: The Engineer sighs, deep in thought. "No, we didn't do this... It's a shame that someone would. I know it's very uncharacteristic of a Rebel to care about something like this, but I didn't join the Rebellion for just a 'glorious human future'. The Rebels fund my projects, and that's all I care about. Someone has been hunting the Engi in this territory, and I want it stopped. Do you think you could inspect the wreck and figure out who did it?"

choice.text: We aren't detectives, we can't help.

event.text: "Expected. This was the second reason I joined the Rebellion..."

choice.text: Who cares about who's responsible? Kill the Rebels!

event.text: It doesn't matter if the Engineers didn't kill the Engi, they've no doubt killed plenty others.
The Engineer continues to inspect the Engi wreck and ignores your ship.

event.text: You report your theory to the Engineers. "I'll trust your word. After scanning the beacon, we were able to find the last few ships to jump through here. Here are the current co-ordinates of the last Mantis ship to enter this system."

"Again, too vague. We kill many Engi ship. What your point?"

choice.text: Close enough. Report them to the Engineer.

event.text: The Engineer is glad you've caught the Mantis ship. They jump in nearby to apprehend the Mantis. Naturally, they aren't going to give up without a fight, but now you have extra fire support on your side.

name: QUEST_ENGI_CRIME_LOSE
text: You've failed to track down the true killers of the Engi ship. You refrain from contacting the Engineers, and scrap the wreckage.

name: ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_ENGI
text: There must have been rich pickings for pirates around here up until war broke out. The pirate you encounter here looks worn down, but hungry. You'll have to fight!

name: ENCOUNTER_SEPARATIST_ENGI
text: A Separatist refugee hiding from the Engi patrols is laying low at this beacon. When they see a Federation ship jumping in nearby, they assume you've come for them, and attack!

name: ENCOUNTER_ENGI_ELITE
text: The Engi Defenders are usually non-confrontational, but as their name suggests, their key purpose is to defend the Harmony. One way or another, they have decided your ship poses a threat and move in to neutralize you.

name: HARMONY_LINK_DEFAULT

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of a Harmony Link.

visitedTooltip.text: This is the location of a Harmony Link.

text: It appears you've discovered a Harmony Link. These massive planet-sized structures are made up of trillions of nanobots, and transmit a strong signal to all of the Engi in the sector.

name: HARMONY_LINK_UNIQUE

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of a Harmony Link.

visitedTooltip.text: This is the location of a Harmony Link.

text: It appears you've discovered a Harmony Link. These massive planet-sized structures are made up of trillions of nanobots, and transmit a strong signal to all of the Engi in the sector.

name: HARMONY_LINK_FIGHTENGI
text: An Engi ship is resting nearby the Harmony Link. It's an elite, but they aren't attacking just yet.

event.text: As you approach, suddenly the Engi ship activates and its drones come online. "Multiverse-Drive equipped vessel approaching. Threat to Harmony Link: activating defensive protocols."
"Refusal. Task: protecting Harmony link. Do not interfere." Looks like you won't be getting anything out of them.

choice.text: If they won't give us supplies, we'll take them!

event.text: "Multiverse-Drive equipped vessel approaching. Threat to Harmony Link: activating defensive protocols."
"Harmony unit detected. Protocol requires aid to be given."
If they're no threat to you, then you'll be no threat to them.

name: HARMONY_LINK_FIGHTMANTIS
text: A Suzerain ship is waiting near the beacon, likely hunting for Engi. "Federation, we recommend staying away, unless want to become next prey..."

event.text: "Fine. If have death wish, then let me be one to grant it!"

choice.text: Ask if they have slaves to offer.

event.text: "Hmmm. Hoping for trade? Well... maybe. Made successful hunt previously, supposed go to Hive though, so prices steep."
"Good, good. Now leave, there killing to be done."
"Good, good. Now leave, there killing to be done."
If they're no threat to you, then you'll be no threat to them.

name: HARMONY_LINK_ANCIENT
text: Orbiting around the Link is the wreckage of several massive structures... or are they ships? Composed of gigantic cubical segments, the vessels are larger than any you've ever seen, but they've been completely decimated. A strangely designed but non-cubical automaton rests silently by the wreckage. You aren't sure if moving closer will awaken it.

choice.text: Destroy the ship first, just in case.

event.text: You approach the vessel, and it activates automatically, as you expected. Prepare for combat! It seems like the ship isn't using all of its systems... let's hope it stays that way!

choice.text: Attempt to salvage without alerting the ship.

event.text: You attempt to scrap the furthest regions of the wreckage, but not long after you see the Auto-ship approaching, awakened by your presence! It gets a shot off, damaging your hull, and you quickly pull the crew back into the ship with what you've gathered so far. It seems like the ship isn't using all of its systems... let's hope it stays that way!
You warily distance yourself from the vessel. You can almost make out the lights flickering on the vessel and the slightest movement to observe your ship, as if it were watching...

name: HARMONY_LINK_ANCIENT_WIN
text: The foreign Auto-ship has been eliminated. You find a large helping of scrap in the wreckage.

event.text: Without the Auto-ship to disturb you, you scout out the remaining wreckage. It appears most of the hull material is unrecognized by your database, and it's too strong to easily be stripped for scrap. Whoever made these ships must have been highly advanced, or from a completely different galaxy...

Inside one of the larger cruisers you're surprised to find what appears to be a robot of some sorts, entirely cubical in craft just like the ships. The room around it has been partially dissolved and strange looking Lanius corpses are scattered around. You bring back the robot to the ship out of curiosity, but without any obvious way to activate it, it'll have to remain in the back corners of the storage bay for now. Along with it, you find some strange coords that you mark on your map.

name: TURZIL_PIRATE_TRANSPORT
text: A Smuggler transport is attempting to sneak past the Engi patrols at this beacon. They're trying desperately to avoid you and you suspect they must have something important on board.

event.text: "Ah crap it's the Feds! We gotta get outta here!" The Smugglers power up their engines and attempt to flee! You'll have to defeat them before they can escape.
You have no interest in whatever the Smugglers are carrying.

name: TURZIL_PIRATE_SURRENDER
text: The Smugglers hail you, surrendering. "Alright, alright! You win! Take our cargo and let us go! They aren't paying us enough anyways..."

event.text: The smugglers eject a lifepod from their ship and jump away. You pull it open to find a strangely colored Engi Defender.
"You have eliminated [primary] source of transport out of sector. Request: you -transport- my person out of Harmony. Will pay."

name: TURZIL_PIRATE_DESTROYED
text: You have destroyed the smuggler ship. Though their cargo has been destroyed, at least some scrap remains from the battle.

name: TURZIL_PIRATE_DEADCREW
text: You have killed all of the smugglers, leaving their cargo hopefully intact. You scrap some of the exterior of the ship first.

event.text: You open the cargo to find a strangely colored Engi Defender sitting in the corner staring at the ceiling. They wear no chains or anything else to suggest they might be a slave. The only other possibility is they're hitching a ride with the smugglers.
"You have eliminated [primary] source of transport out of sector. Request: you -transport- my person out of Harmony. Will pay."

name: HARMONY_FUGITIVE
text: You prepare to charge the FTL drive when you notice an Engi Cruiser approaching you! Your FTL drive is unresponsive - this can't be good...

event.text: "Hello. This is HA-34U representing the Engi Harmony. We are aware that you are carrying fugitive TRZ-1L. We request you hand over the fugitive, and we will provide high payment. It is unwise to challenge the Harmony."

Tully broadcasts to the Engi vessel. "This is Admiral Tully of the Federation Fleet. Do not fire upon this ship. I repeat, do not fire on this ship."
					
					HA-34U pauses. "Your status is acknowledged. However, you vastly underestimate the importance of the Harmony's need for TRZ-1L. The Harmony is a core member of the Federation; to assume that the needs of the entire Harmony are lesser than one Admiral indicates poor judgement."
					
					Tully widens his stance and folds his arms behind his back. "You are right about one thing. As a large portion of the Federation, you have the right to take legal action against me. Maybe it will end my career. But I'm leaving here with Turzil. Unless the Federation wins its war against the Rebels, I think you'll find that the brass will be hesitant to remove someone as qualified as me."
					
					The Engi on the viewscreen stares without speaking for several seconds. Eventually, the comm is cut. The Harmony ship powers down its weapons and makes no further moves against you.

Tully lets out a sigh as you warm up your FTL. "They're in for a nasty surprise when they find out that the Tully from this universe is still busy with the Rebels at Node 17. Still, they're not likely to forget this, so maybe we should avoid the Harmony from here on."
							
							Turzil puts a hand on Tully's arm, causing Tully to turn to face him. "I don't -know- how to express my gratitude. You are, and always will be... -my- friend."
							
							Tully puts his other hand on top of Turzil's. "I won't lose you again. Stay by my side, I will protect you as long as I'm able. Maybe when this is all over... we can find a universe where the Harmony won't be able to find you?"
							
							Turzil nods. "We should -liberate- this universe [first]."
You don't intend on handing over your crew! You prepare to fight the cruiser.

name: HARMONY_FUGITIVE_EASYROUTE
text: You knew the Engi was shady but you didn't realize they had beef with the actual Harmony! You can't risk angering the entirety of the Engi collective: you accept the payment.

removeCrew.text: You cannot clone the Engi as they are no longer part of your crew.

name: HARMONY_FUGITIVE_SURRENDER
text: "This is your: last chance. Hand over the fugitive and you will be allowed to live."

event.text: This fight isn't worth continuing. You hand over the fugitive and accept the payment.

removeCrew.text: You cannot clone the Engi as they are no longer part of your crew.

name: HARMONY_FUGITIVE_WIN
text: You have defeated an Elite Engi Cruiser inside the Engi Harmony. You doubt the Harmony will be happy about this, but you've made it out alive of this fight.

event.text: Despite your efforts it appears the fugitive did not survive the fight. You'll have to carry on without them.

You turn to face the Engi fugitive who caused this problem in the first place. "Apologies, this conflict [should] have been predicted. It is important that my -identity- be provided. I am: General Turzil. My mission: escape [capture] of Harmony. I have achieved status of wanted -fugitive- for disobeying Harmony-Rebel non-aggression pact during Federation Civil War, and [assisting] Separatist movements in dismantling of Harmony. It is my -request- that you take me with you to avoid death and protection of -underground- Separatist movements."

surrender.text: Suddenly, the ship sends a transmission, whose language is indiscernible. Your translator struggles, turning out nonsense like "Turkey alpha on the blue yesterday." The transmission stops, and immediately after your systems go haywire! The ship has activated some kind of bizarre combat augment!

event.text: To make matters worse, it appears the ship's remaining systems have come online!

gotaway.text: The smugglers jump away. You may never know what was in their cargo...

name: FINISH_BEACON_HEKTAR
text: You've finally found the exit to this dreadful sector.

event.text: You're stopped before you can leave by a massive Hektar vessel. "Sssorry, but you may not leave thisss sssector! You sssstill owe Hektar Indusssstriessss a lot of money!"

choice.text: (Billy) Have Billy clear you for leaving.

event.text: Fortunately, it only takes a few minutes before Billy returns, and you're allowed to leave. Guess it pays to have the CEO of a major corporation aboard your ship.

choice.text: (Metyunt) Have Metyunt clear you for leaving.

event.text: Fortunately, it only takes a few minutes before Metyunt returns, and you're allowed to leave. Guess it pays to have the staff manager of a major corporation aboard your ship.

choice.text: Looks like we'll have to fight our way out!

event.text: The only way out now is to fight! You power up your weapons and prepare to engage.
Looks like the Rebel fleet has taken control of the beacon! You'll have to fight your way out!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: HEKTAR_INVESTOR
text: Nearby, the ship of a wealthy tycoon is exploring the beacon. Might be an interesting chat.

event.text: You fly away from the shuttle and find somewhere else to do something aboard the ship.

name: HEKTAR_INVESTOR_QUESTIONS_NOTMET
text: "Oh, chip chap cheerio good fellow! I am Count Dinkleman Reichster Von Applebuzz Tri Tri the Fourth, at your service. I have taken a long venture to these lands to see what treasures Hektar might have to offer me and my immense wealth. Tell me, good sir or madam, what are your opinions on Hektar?"

choice.text: They're tricking people into being trapped in this sector.

event.text: "Good heavens, what a genius idea! Forcing people into paying off an imaginary debt by trapping them in a massive market place, then hiding it in a nebula where the Federation will never find it? Delightful! I'm sure you think it's horrible though, because you aren't disgustingly rich. Anyways, thanks for the chat, gotta go!" The man sprints back to his ship, dropping several piles of scrap from his pockets as he goes.

"Oh, well you know what they say in 'the business'. Actually, I don't. I'm not in 'the business'. But somewhere, I'm sure they have some justfiable reasons for slavery. Clearly, you wouldn't know, because you aren't disgustingly rich. Anyways, thanks for the chat, gotta go!" The man sprints back to his ship, dropping several piles of scrap from his pockets as he goes.
"Just alright, eh? Well, what about their products? You have a large military vessel at your disposal. Do you enjoy the use of Hektar's signature modular weaponry?"

"Good you say? Marvelous! I'm no military man, but I'll take your word for it! I shall invest in Hektar. A remarkable chat, good fellow. Say, do me a service and take this worthless assistant of mine off of my hands. I think one of Hektar's lizard people will serve me better."

"Oh, well that's certainly not good. I'm no military man, but I'll take your word for it! I shall not invest in Hektar. Here, you can have this worthless piece of junk, considering I certainly won't want it."
"Well, then you are worthless to me. Imagine being so poor. Thanks for the chat, gotta go!" The man sprints back to his ship, dropping several piles of scrap from his pockets as he goes.

name: HEKTAR_INVESTOR_QUESTIONS_MET
text: "Strange poor person, we meet again! It is me, Count Dinkleman Reichster Von Applebuzz Tri Tri the Fourth! What a coincidence we happen upon each other on this occasion. I have taken a long venture to these lands to see what treasures Hektar might have to offer me and my immense wealth. Tell me, good sir or madam, what are your opinions on Hektar?"

name: DISTRESS_HEKTAR_GHETTO
text: The nearby planet boasts both a bustling ghetto full of lizards - and a pirate ship firing upon them! There's a good chance Hektar knows about this but doesn't care to intervene, so you might be their only hope!

event.text: You prepare to fight the pirate ship.
The lives of these lizards are nothing to you. Bah, let them all die for all you care.

name: HEKTAR_UNION
text: You're surprised to find a band of lizards aboard a nearby Hektar ship, unaccompanied by any Slugs. They hail you. "You are a military ship, right? I think you could be of assistance to us. Will you help?"

event.text: "We have begun the steps towards establishing a union that might finally make this place less of a hell to work at. Unfortunately, our boss refuses to even acknowledge our efforts. Will you help 'encourage' him for us? Just make sure you don't kill him, otherwise this will all have been pointless!"
The lizards show you where their boss is located and reinforce that you must not kill him.

choice.text: Reveal their plan to their manager.

event.text: The Slug laughs when he learns about the lizards' plan. "Hah, thossse idiotss don't even know how to wear a ssshirt the right way. Thanksss for telling me though, a good whippin' will do them good!" The greedy Slug doesn't even give you anything in return, but the lizards are furious and storm your ship!
The lizards make no further comment and go back to talking amongst themselves.

name: HEKTAR_SUZERAIN
text: You really can't say you expected to find a Suzerain ship so far out here, and you heavily doubt they're victims to Hektar. For what reasons might they have come?

event.text: The Suzerain responds, flailing his arms in several grand motions. "Greetings! You are hearing of the great Billy Hektar, yes? He is man of fewest ethics, leader of greatest and most morally bankrupt corporation in WHOLE Multiverse! I come to learn from him and master ways of becoming living scum myself! Have you heard his teachings?"
"I see you are having Slug one aboard your ship! Squishy men, but most natural commers of retched living! Honored I am, and giving you things."

"I see you are having Guild man aboard your ship! Hunter and poacher of sentient things, skinner of the living! Oh how I envy your nerves of steel and torturous methods of mutilation! Honored I am, and giving you things."
"I see you are having stealthy cloaking Slug aboard your ship! Cunning master of silent assassinations and devilish trickery! Oh, oh, how I hoping to learn! Yes, I coming with to learn from you!"

"I see you are having evilest taxidermy man aboard your ship! Master of sniping and knowledgeable in all forms of unethical biological weapons! Oh, oh, how I hoping to learn! Yes, I coming with to learn from you!"
"You are having one of Billy's own disciples! You are seeing oh great Billy in the flesh! I honored, truly! Please, allowing me to come and learn!"
"EEK! It is you! Most ungraceful one, Billy himself! I not knowing what to say, overcome with excitement! Please, allowing me to come with you, it would be biggest of honors!"
"Hah! Then you are stupid idiot! Biggest of fools, ethically driven and morally abundant! Hahahahah! The galaxy needing less of you, so I doing that."
There's no sane reason to go interacting with Suzerains unless you want to risk having your head removed. You put a large distance between your ships just in case.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_HEKTAR_RAIN
text: On the small nearby planet through the clearing you observe a small Hektar facility. It turns out to be some agricultural center, but the planet is otherwise barren and devoid of life. Scans show the facility is mostly being run by lizards.

event.text: As you approach the facility, your video feed shows a strange scene. A band of lizards are rotating around a small planter of unsprouted seeds, chanting a song. Their leader appears to be wearing a crudely made cardboard mask.

"We sing the rain song, and hope the rain comes! Hektar has put us here, in this desolate place, and expects seeds to grow and make great bounty! But there is no water here!" The lizard grumbles. "I will sing the rain song till creation dies. But if rain does not come, I die first!"

You dismount from the ship with your crew and join the lizards in chanting. Of course, the 'rain' never comes, but they seem happy you offered your help. After a while the lizards give up, but offer to upgrade your ship afterwards.

choice.text: (Guntput) Send Guntput down there with them.

event.text: The lizards seem shocked to see Guntput. "Oh great Shaman! I ashamed! We should have listened, your advice was most wise. Now, we are trapped, and there is no rain! What will become of us?" Guntput frowns and smacks the lizard with his shield. "There is no point in shame. What is done is done. Our people will live, the homeworlds are in shambles but we live. The rain will not come you fool. Come with us, we will make better use of you than rotting in Hektar's communes."

choice.text: (Billy) Send Billy down there with them.

event.text: Upon seeing Billy the lizards all bow, but he seems mostly confused. "Why... why are you guysss down here? Aren't you sssupposssed to be packing boxesss or running the cargo ssships?" The lizards shake their heads. "Box shipping full! Cargo ships all piloted! Still, more slaves come in. Too many workers, so we are placed here." Billy shudders upon hearing the word slave. "Mhm... I... Okay maybe I made a little missstake here. Uh... you guyssss are formally disssmissed. Go back to your homesss or whatever." The lizards are confused. "We... have no homes. You abducted us." Billy winces again. "Uhm... then you're working for usss now."

choice.text: (Fire Weapon) Start a fire to turn on the sprinklers.

event.text: The lizards shriek as your weapons set the facility ablaze. Indeed, the sprinklers do come on, but are useless at stopping the blaze. Soon the whole building goes up in smoke and the lizards are forced to evacuate. "You are stupidest being! What did you expect to happen? Go, shoo! Hektar will be furious."

choice.text: Try to get them to give up.

event.text: "Did not hear me? I said I sing the rain song till the day creation dies or rain comes!" The lizard shakes his head in annoyance and goes back to chanting.
You doubt there's going to be anything of value to find at an agriculture facility.

name: NEBULA_HEKTAR_SYLVAN
text: "Sssstranger, welcome to my beacon!" You jump, thinking you've somehow found Sylvan yet again, but instead it seems this is just another Hektar employee, not the infamous traveling merchant.

choice.text: Why are you pretending to be Sylvan?

event.text: "Well, Sssylvan isss my hero! He'ssss sso cool. And hot. I wisssh I wasss that cool and hot... Pardon the oxymoron."
The Slug perks up. "In fact, I do!" He resumes his impersonation from before. "Come on in sssstranger, and take a look at my goodssss!"

choice.text: You're not quite up to his level, shield and weaponry wise.

event.text: "Yeah... I'm not even sssure how he managed thisss! Every time I try to inssstall that many ssshields I jussst get an obnoxious beep like I've hit a hardcoded limit or sssomething."

choice.text: Offer him some scrap to spruce up his ship.

event.text: "That'ssss quite generoussss, ssstranger! Uh, I mean, thankssss."
"Oh man, I don't have anything to give... wait, no! I do! Thissss isss very valuable to me, but I'm sssure you'll get a lot more ussse out of it than me. Pleasssse take good care of it though."
The Slug perks up. "In fact, I do!" He resumes his impersonation from before. "Come on in sssstranger, and take a look at my goodssss!"
"OH GOD! IT'SSS YOU! OH MY OH MY OH MY OH MY OH MY!" The Slug practically demands that you allow him on the ship so that he can work alongside Sylvan.
You aren't sure why someone would try to immitate Sylvan, but it's nothing more than a nuisance to you.

name: NEBULA_HEKTAR_TOYS
text: A small Hektar run gift-shop is nearby. It's highly unlikely it's carrying any military goods, but maybe you'll find something interesting inside?

event.text: You're welcomed by an overweight Slug. "Visssitorssss! Come on in! I have ssssomething to ssshow you! I've created a new line of pull-ssstring toysss resssembling variousss racesss accrosss the galaxy. Come and try them!"

The human toy squeaks, and spits out "Glory to the Rebellion!" The Slug notices your shock and tries to calm your nerves. "It'sss okay! A lot of humansss are Rebelsss, that'sss the point! It'ss relatable for humansss!"

The Slug laughs nervously. "I'm guesssing you don't like it then? *Sigh*, okay..." The Slug slithers back to the store counter, defeated. "There'sss a military depot not too far from here. Go there inssstead if you want sssomething wortwhile..."

"You actually like it? OH BOY! Thank you ssso much! My brother tried to ssstart a plusssshie line in the EHG and thingsss haven't been going well for him, ssso I can't wait to tell him that good newsss! Wait, better yet, I'll come with you, and then I can ssssell my toysss to the whole Multiverssse!"
Your crew explains their opinions on the toy. The Slug thoughtfully contemplates this advice, and seems grateful. "Thank you ssso much for your input! Here, have thisss!"

The Mantis toy squeaks, and spits out "Kill all living things!" The Slug notices your shock and tries to calm your nerves. "It'sss okay! Mantisss are jussst like that! It'sss not offensssive if it'ssss true, right?"

The Slug laughs nervously. "I'm guesssing you don't like it then? *Sigh*, okay..." The Slug slithers back to the store counter, defeated. "There'sss a military depot not too far from here. Go there inssstead if you want sssomething wortwhile..."
