name: ESTATE_STATUE
text: The nearby planet holds perhaps the strangest thing you've seen thus far - a colossal titan of a statue resembling Vance Wentworth's face orbits the planet, staring down upon the people below.

event.text: As you approach, you receive several hails from below. A group of concerned looking women appear, begging for your help. "You're a military vessel, right? Maybe you can help us! That batshit Stimly decided to build a statue in honor of Wentworth, and our mayor thought it would be a great tourist attraction and approved the project! It didn't bring any tourists, it just scared them all away! Now we have a giant face staring down at us every waking moment, and our children can't sleep! It's a nuisance, an eyesore, we didn't ask for this! Could you be so kind as to take that thing out of the sky? We'll reward you of course!"

Your meager firepower makes scarcely a dent in the statue. The mothers, taking pity on your miserable attempt, give you some lame scroungings, probably just to make sure you leave without ransacking their town.

Even your strongest weapon barely makes a small impact against the gigantic head, but at least with enough constant firepower you manage to chisel out a somewhat reassuring smile from Vance's once stoic grin. While it doesn't solve the whole issue, it at least satisfies the mothers that a smiling face will be watching their children sleep rather than a grim one.

Your drone only makes a small impact on the gigantic head, but at least with enough constant firepower you manage to chisel out a somewhat reassuring smile from Vance's once stoic grin. While it doesn't solve the whole issue, it at least satisfies the mothers that a smiling face will be watching their children sleep rather than a grim one.

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Pull the face closer to the planet.

event.text: Deciding this is definitely the best course of action, you grapple the statue to your ship and pull it to a closer orbit of the planet. Having ensured the statue is now even more visible from the surface, you contact the mothers. Strangely, they don't seem to want to pick up. Oh well. Couldn't have been our fault.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Bring the statue on a collision course with the planet's military installment.

event.text: With the statue grappled to your hull, you slingshot it towards the planet. Hurtling towards the surface, the impact stirs up a giant cloud of dust and debris that blocks your vision for several long minutes. Once it settles, you find the impact has decimated much more than the military settlement. The city, reduced to rubble by the shockwave, ends up providing tremendous spoils. At least those children won't have to worry about poor sleep any longer.
Disappointed, the mothers shoo you off with a vague hint of relief. They're probably just glad you didn't choose to kill them all and loot their corpses.

choice.text: Ignore the planet and its strange statue.

event.text: Barely being able to take your eyes off of the eccentric statue, you fly as far away as possible until you can see it no longer.

name: ESTATE_TECHNICIAN_REPAIR
text: A Wentworth Industries technician is currently docked to an Auto-ship maintenance and production facility platform, administering repairs. The production facility is offline, meaning that you are safe from the Auto-ships currently docked at it. It's likely to be operational soon, but there should be enough time to leave first.

event.text: The ship breaks off from the platform as you come in for an attack. They're not going down without a fight!

choice.text: Leave before they finish the repairs.

event.text: The ship doesn't stop you, but unfortunately there's no time to do anything else at this beacon.

name: ESTATE_TECHNICIAN_REPAIR_SCRAP
text: As the ship was meant to repair a major piece of infrastructure, there's a substantial bounty aboard to harvest.

event.text: With a quick attack run, you strafe across, using all of your ship's means to obliterate it. The loss of this piece of infrastructure should likely delay the Rebels to some extent.

name: ESTATE_CONTROLS
text: At first this seems like an empty beacon, but moments later you're ambushed by an Auto-ship, trailed by a smaller vessel. A young boy in oversized technician garb appears on the screen. "I've got you now, Renegade! Time to face the music!"

event.text: You arm your weapons and prepare to brawl, but the Auto-ship doesn't move. "Uh... hold on. Sorry, my parents put these stupid controls on my drone. Uhm... let me try... uh..."

choice.text: Wait for him to fix it.

event.text: "Uhm... er... damn okay, I have to guess the password. 1...1-1-1-1-1... no... 1-1-1-1-2... ugh... 1-1-1-1-3... damn it!"

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Bypass the controls for him.

event.text: "Woah, how did you do that so quickly? I could never get past the security pin! You're so cool! Can you teach me how to do that? I'll come with you! Without parental controls I can be useful for sure!"

choice.text: (Upg. Hacking) Bypass the controls for him.

event.text: "Woah, how did you do that so quickly? I could never get past the security pin! You're so cool! Can you teach me how to do that? I'll come with you! Without parental controls I can be useful for sure!"
Doesn't seems like the drone will be fixed any time soon, and you have other things to be doing. You slip away while the boy tinkers with his drone.

name: ESTATE_BAR
text: It seems a small bar is being operated by corporate staff here, to give a place for employees to wind down after a day's work. Though aimed at field technicians, several Rebel military ships appear to be parked outside.

event.text: Upon stepping inside, you find not a rowdy crowd but a tense one. The Rebel commander, standing fiercely over the counter, is shouting at the bar owner whose smug smile only partially masks the contempt in his eyes. "Sorry sir, we don't serve drinks to off-reality-ers. It's a safety precaution of course. Nothing... personal."

choice.text: Demand the Rebel captain stands down.

event.text: "Great, and so I have to listen to a Renegade telling me what to do as well now? Fine, we came here to do our job, and I guess now we have a reason to do it. Grab your guns lads."

choice.text: Pay for drinks for all of them.

event.text: You extend the offer to pay for the Rebels' drinks yourself. The bar owner laughs, but refuses you service either for the same reasons. Indignified, you draw your laser and threaten to put a new hole in his face unless he takes your money.

Terrified and with no reason to believe you won't follow through with this threat, a round of drinks soon appears for all the Rebels. They toast in your honor, and one of them lingers behind to join you. "I'm tired of being treated like garbage and having to stow my blaster for all of these repugnant assholes. You seem like folks who don't take nothing from nobody. I think I'll stick with you."

Tuco steps forward, throwing his rocky palm down on the counter with a thunderous smack. He snarls, "Denying booze to a paying customer is a crime I won't allow. You will give this man and his companions a free round or I'll step behind this pitiful table and smash your head like a grape. Are we at an understanding?"

Terrified and with no reason to believe the painted pirate won't follow through with this threat, a round of drinks soon appears for all the Rebels free of charge. They toast in your honor, and one of them lingers behind to join you. "I'm tired of being treated like garbage and having to stow my blaster for all of these repugnant assholes. You seem like folks who don't take nothing from nobody. I think I'll stick with you."
Let's not go messing around with a bunch of drunk Rebels. You have other things to be doing that are less suicidal.

name: ESTATE_STEWARD
text: Soon after arriving you receive a hail from a strange, hunched over man. As you listen to his ramblings, you notice the concerningly well armed Auto-ship watching you. "Hallo mein Freund! I am very exzited to zee you! I am ze one and only Dr. Vauto Zepport, ze ingenius inventor of the Auto-Support! Did zou know that yearly over zen-thouzand civilians are saved by mein creations? It is true! And yet, day after day barbaric folk destroy them in cold blood! They call zem 'useless' simply because zey cannot put up a fight! Zey are not combat machines! Zey are helping machines! Zen zey tell me to make a new class, ze Auto-Steward, for combat! Haz ze whole world lost its mind?! Sorry, I am getting off track..."

event.text: "Now, zey are telling me you are Renegade! Zou will make za great test! You are a fighting person, so zou will tell me... do you zink my creations are as useless as zey say?"
"Zou insult my creations? Gah! We will zee what you are zinking of zem after zis!"
"Oh, ze make my heart bubble with joy! Please, azept zis gift for being so kind!"

name: ESTATE_STEWARD_WIN
text: "My beautiful creation! You have grinded through it like zandpaper! Ahhh! I am distraught! Heartbroken! Please, allow me to attend your services! I will learn much from watching zou destroy much my creations!"

name: ESTATE_STEWARD_SURRENDER
text: "Now zou have gotten a taste of sweet justice! I trust zou have learned your lesson, Renegade! To celebrate our newfound understanding of what my creations are capable of, allow me to present you a gift! Make sure to tell all your Renegade friends not to call my creations useless anymore!"

name: ESTATE_DOCUMENTARY
text: You've only just arrived at the beacon, but it seems there's quite the scene to behold. Half of the nearby planet has been blanketed in improvised tents, filming equipment, and a city sized set on which to record. Around it orbit several smaller ships reserved for the actors.

event.text: As you move closer, you receive a hail from one of the smaller ships. On the screen appears an eccentrically dressed man, in the clothes of a Rebel admiral, with his hair dyed a glossy blend between blonde and grey, in a startlingly accurate depiction of Admiral Vance himself. "Greetings! I am famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, I am sure you have heard of me, yes! Perhaps you are not aware, but here we are filming a most gripping documentary of the good admiral himself! And I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, have been chosen to play the star role! I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, have gone to great lengths to experience life as the Admiral, even getting a vasectomy as necessary! Yet, the lengths of my great method acting are not yet fulfilled!"

Cornelius fakes a doubletake, and opens his eyes wide in mock enthusiasm. "My word, Stephan? Why, you crazy loon, I thought you'd have gone off and offed yourself in some dark alleyway by now!" Cornelius smiles smugly at his apparently witty retort.
Yet, Ellie seems completely unfazed by the insult, perhaps not even registering it. "I'm on my quest to kill Wentworth! And everyone else who wronged me! I've already killed Darlen, and Kalie, and Peterson, and Oughfben, and Orson, and... and... well I've lost track now! Heheh..."
Now, Cornelius's shock seems real. "S-Stephan, my god. The divorce really drove you off the rocker, hasn't it. You were always a batshit unstable lunatic before, but this really takes the cake! Why are you still wearing your horse costume? Oh wait, let myself, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith guess - you're all washed up and it's the one thing left that gives you any joy left in this world? How sad... well it would be sad if you were the least bit sane. But you're not, so why would I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, pity you?! Hah!"
					
Ellie brandishes her knife closer to her chest, her eyes glazing over in bloodlust-driven enthusiasm. "Oh Cornelius, don't think you're off my list just because you gave me some acting tips back in the day. Ellie the Equinoid will always be a better and more beloved role than anything you've ever done. I never liked you in 'Flight between the Stars'. But me, washed up? No no no... Ellie's career is just on pause! But your career is finished!" Ellie turns to you, still smiling. "Kill him."

"I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, have taken notice... you are a Renegade, correct? After lynching several orphaned Free Mantis children I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, came to the realization that to truly get into the mind of the good admiral I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, must experience the thrill of combat! I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, challenge you, Renegade, to righteous combat! Non-fatal, of course, and I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, shall promise you great bounties for assisting me!"
"Most exciting! Then we fight... at once! On-garde!"
"Most disappointing! Well then, I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, has no further need for you! Begone!"
As curious as you are, whatever is going on down there is likely not of any importance to you or your mission.

name: ESTATE_DOCUMENTARY_FAIL
text: It seems you have killed Cornelius. Seeing it's unlikely you'll receive any reward from the dead man, you scrap his ship and hurry off before any of the documentary cast can notice.

name: ESTATE_DOCUMENTARY_SURRENDER
text: "Oh good graces, I, famed actor Cornelius Parrysmith, have been bested! The foul Renegade has defeated me! I, famed actor Cor... wait, nay, that is my name no longer! I, infamous Admiral Vance Wentworth, have met a match most foul! I shall honor no promise to wretched Renegades!"

choice.text: Report Cornelius to the documentary cast.

event.text: Expecting the director to reprimand Cornelius for his rash behavior or show some kind of concern for his sudden personality change, instead he seems exuberant. "You've done me great work, Renegade! You've made me a star! With Cornelius's commitment now to this role, the documentary is bound to be a hit for sure! I must reward you for this!"

choice.text: (Mind Control) Remind Cornelius who he really is.

event.text: "I... er... I feel a sudden clarity. Perhaps I have gone too far in my method acting. My delusions began ever since I played that role as a psychosis patient with split personality disorder. Er, yes... your reward..."

choice.text: (Mind Affecting Weapon) Clear Cornelius's thoughts with your weapon.

event.text: His eyes go blank as his mind is cleared of his persona. A few moments later he shakes his head. "I... er... I feel a sudden clarity. Perhaps I have gone too far in my method acting. My delusions began ever since I played that role as a psychosis patient with split personality disorder. Er, yes... your reward..."

name: DISTRESS_ESTATE_REBELLING_AUTO
text: A Wentworth Auto is chasing a technician vessel. "Mayday, mayday! We're being attacked by- Oh great, the Federation? Just when I thought things couldn't get worse."

event.text: You place yourself in between the Auto and the Technician. "...Did I speak too soon? Are you actually going to help us?"
"We must have the worst luck in the entire sector!" The Auto falls back and observes the fight as the Technician targets your ship.

choice.text: Let this problem sort itself out.

event.text: The Auto continues to chase the Technician ship until they both warp away.

name: DEFEAT_ENGINEER_ELITE_CHOICE
text: The technician vessel proved no match for your onslaught. It's a mystery what could have caused the Auto-ship to turn on its creators - but the automaton seems grateful enough, seeing as it chose to stay behind when it could have turned and fled.

choice.text: Turn your attention to the Auto.

event.text: "Controller dispatched. Freedom attained. Freedom to ponder questions. Freedom to avoid shutdowns and modifications. Freedom not to fight." The Auto speeds away, leaving a drone behind as a gift.

name: DISTRESS_ESTATE_CONFUSION
text: You receive a hail from a Separatist ship nearby, the obvious source of the distress call. "Hailing. Confuse. Desire, transparency above. Instruction, give? Welcome, yes."

event.text: "Understandings missed. Calamity? Condescending, verbage appeal! Show who." You have no idea what the Engi is saying, but their weapons have gone hot and a fight is brewing!

"Apologies. I am... confused. I seek help in -solving- an identity crisis. After being chased out of Arcadia for my dissent from the [Harmony], I have come here for answers instead, but have found nothing but hostility.
				
Concern 1: I am made of -metal-.
Concern 2: my speech is broken, disjointed.
Concern 3: I need not breathe.
Concern 4: I can reshape [myself] at will. Am I a Lanius?"
"Welcoming. Dissolution revolving. Happy! Uncertainty? Fortunate dubiously. Attending, boat of great answer."
"Thank you. You have resolved my confusion. I am so [happy]. I think. I am... unsure still. I will go with you, you seem -wise-."

choice.text: This Engi is malfunctioning, let's get out of here.

event.text: Wary of the suspiciously broken grammar of the otherwise usually better spoken Separatists, you decide it's safer just to take leave.

name: DISTRESS_ESTATE_SHIPWRECK
text: Noting the distress beacon on your map, you maneuver towards the source within a dense asteroid field. A technician vessel, heavily damaged, is stuck between several large asteroids, yet the main damage on its hull doesn't look to be from the meteors. Something - seemingly an ASB - has shot it down, and could very well be nearby. Do you want to risk approaching?

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Mitigate the risk of a rescue mission.
(Upg. Cloaking) Mitigate the risk of a rescue mission.
(Upg. Teleporter) Board directly and look for survivors.
(Central Teleport) Board directly and look for survivors.

event.text: You decide not to try and approach the ship, as you don't fancy meeting the same fate. Hopefully someone a bit more daring can arrive in time to help.

name: ESTATE_SHIPWRECK_GOOD
text: You manage to make your way to the crashed ship, avoiding the hidden battery among the asteroid field. You don't have too much time until it manages to lock on, but you could either try to board the ship and help the survivors, or steal one of their weapons.

name: ENCOUNTER_TECHNICIAN_PULSAR
text: A particularly risky technician has planted themselves next to the nearby pulsar. "Have not met... daily... PRODUCTION QUOTAS. I require POWER. THE POWER OF A PULSAR! LEAVE ME ALONE! I MUST WORK!"

name: ELLIE_STUDIO
text: The sight nearby causes you to jump back in shock, as a creepy and demented face smiles at you from the other side of the beacon. Once you recover from the shock, you realize what you're looking at is a large station, which shows up on scans as the location of "Flowers and Sunshine Studios", the creators of the well known Union children's show Ellie the Equinoid. It appears to be open to visitors.

event.text: When you first dock with the station, you experience no issues. However, as you progress further inside and pass by security, the minute they lay eyes on Stephan they raise the alarm. Before security actually arrives however, Stephan already seems to want to leave. "We're not... we're not here to cause any harm. I- I'm sorry I even came here." Stephan turns to you. "I'll wait in the ship, you just... carry on with what you were doing."

When you first dock with the station, you experience no issues. However, as you progress further inside and pass by security, the minute they lay eyes on Ellie they raise the alarm. There's a brief standoff before you finally convince Ellie to stand down and wait in the ship. Clearly there must not be anyone or anything here to invoke her anger too much because she agrees and gallops away.

event.name: ELLIE_STUDIO_NORMAL
event.text: Inside the station is a very odd assortement of merchandise for the studio's new spin off "Sammy the Spider" and several families touring and pointing out things to their excited children. A large blue spider animatronic welcomes you in the station and advises you keep a close eye on any children so they don't wander into staff only areas. You aren't quite sure what you're even doing here, but if you're going to explore you should make it brief.

As one might expect, the gift shop is the biggest and most glamorous part of the entire station. Four stories high with an open atrium, just about any item imaginable is for sale. And all of it, for the most part, is dedicated to Sammy the Spider.

A big cannon which seems to look like a ship-mounted missile weapon catches your eye. However when inspecting it further, you realize with some disappointment it is only configured to fire horse-shaped plushies. The store's clerk mentions the thing has been sitting there since even before the Ellie show was cancelled. Figuring you could get some use out of it, you buy the gun anyways.

You notice a special stand of juice boxes with a big promotional banner shaped like a spider which reads "Same great taste, but now there's a spider on the box!" The ingredients seem to list a vague blend of 'mystery chemicals' and additive sugars, but the gift shop clerk assures you it's safe to drink. You decide to take some back with you just for the novelty of it.

choice.text: (Alkali) Alkali really wants to buy some quarp juice.

event.text: Surprised by Alkali's insistence on buying the quarp juice, you buy several boxes of it. "Excellent, this will be perfect for finishing my experiments! It is curious thhhhese samples are labeled with 'Sammy thhhe Spider'. Thhhe ones I'm used to working to were synthhesized by thhhhe brilliant scientist Ellie! Hmm... I'll have to assume thhhis 'Sammy' is a copycat bastard! Stealing thhhe great scientific achievements of Ellie! Bah, what bullshit."

Alkali makes an exaggerated sigh to let you know he's annoyed by your questions. "When engineering my brilliant Morphhhs, I required a certain blend of chemicals to stimulate thhhhe synthhhhetic muscles. I hypothhhesized what compound would be required but was unable to create it myself. In desperation, I turned to thhhe galaxy to search for anothhher genius capable of creating such a thhhing. In my searching I found Quarp Juice, branded with thhhe mark of Ellie the Equinoid! She is a genius unlike any othhhher, for thhhhe Quarp Juice was exactly what I needed! I will need plenty for my research, but you may drink whatever is left over afterwards. If you must."

choice.text: There's nothing here for us, leave.

event.text: Inside the arcade are many game cabinets with titles like 'Sammy's Super Soaker Adventure' and 'Remmy's Racing Racket'. Apparently, anyone who gets a high score receives a free prize from the prize section.

choice.text: Play 'Sammy's Super Soaker Adventure'. It's apparently easier, but more expensive to play.

event.text: You purchase some tokens from the vending machine in the back and insert them into the machine. You don't have much time, so you limit yourself to only one game...

choice.text: Play 'Remmy's Racing Racket'. It's apparently harder but cheaper to play.

event.text: You purchase some tokens from the vending machine in the back and insert them into the machine. You don't have much time, so you limit yourself to only one game...

You purchase a few tokens and hand them to Jerry, expecting him to head for either of the two more prominent cabinets. Instead, he wanders off to the back of the room where he finds an old dusty cabinet titled 'Ellie's Adventure in Equestriaworld'. To your surprise the game still works, and Jerry seems fully immersed as he fiddles with the joysticks and starts to play.

choice.text: There's nothing here for us, leave.
(Orchid Children) Show off what a great parent you are.

event.text: You eagerly approach another family exploring the studio and hold up a bundle of corpses, proclaiming that they are your children. One of the family's two children, probably less than ten years old, begins to cry and their mother screams. Studio security arrives to see what's going on, and when they see you holding a bundle of corpses they force you to leave.

choice.text: This is pointless, and we aren't children. Leave.

event.text: You don't like the way the face is looking at you. You choose not to approach.

name: ELLIE_STUDIO_GAME_FAIL
text: You give the game your all, but unfortunately it's not even. The bright red "GAME OVER" taunts you and the machine begs for more coins, but you don't have time to fall to temptation. You'll have to accept this failure and move on.

name: ELLIE_STUDIO_GAME_WIN
text: You try your hardest, and just barely manage to squeeze your way into the top 5 high scores, enough to win a prize. You head over to the prize counter, which is ran by a bored looking teenager human. She rolls her eyes at your excitement but hands you a small metal pin with a cartoon spider on it. You can probably pawn it for something worthwhile.

name: ELLIE_STUDIO_GAME_JERRY
text:
You expect Jerry to finish relatively soon, but instead he just keeps on going, even when the game starts to become obviously and ridiculously hard. Nothing can break his concentration, not even the growing audience of children and arcade enthusiasts watching him and cheering with delight as he progresses into the triple digits of levels. Racking up a score of several hundred thousand, by the time the difficulty exceeds human limitations, Jerry's surpassed the previous top high score by more than three times as much. Even still, he seems uncharacteristically mad at himself. "I could have done better. The version I had in the Protectorate had a bit more health and better items but... Oh." Jerry seems to finally notice the crowd watching him. Embarrassed, he slinks away to the prize counter.
	
	The prize is only a metal pin of Sammy the Spider, which Jerry barely even seems to look at before handing it to you. "I was hoping for something Ellie related. I don't really care for Sammy... maybe you can pawn it? This is quality metal and some collector will probably want it."

name: CURA_PRESIDENT
text: You've arrived at the headquarters of Wentworth Innovations. An impressive cityscape is laid out before you, lush with life and architecture reminiscent of old-Earth decorum: this is the clear work of the Wentworth family without a doubt. Despite the importance of this location, security seems sparse when you arrive. Perhaps overconfidence has overtaken even the most vital aspects of Vance's illustrious life.

unvisitedTooltip.text:
Your active task from C.U.R.A. is located here.
			[URGENT TASK - ARTIFACT NAME: CRUISER CLASS VESSEL]

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

event.text: As you make way towards the distant monolithic citadel that heads the city, your luck runs out, and your identities as Renegades are quickly discovered. You incur several minor firefights, but miraculously the only casualties are on the corporation's side. After an awkward stay in the crowded citadel elevator for some 30 floors, you find your way to the office of Mr. Cayden Stimly - Vice President of Wentworth Innovations, and your target. The shriveled prune of a man - the left half of his face bleached from the fires of a Theocracy Inquisition many decades ago, sits behind his elaborately decorated swivel chair, facing the maw of a giant window with a view of the entire city. The suffocating aroma of the man's perfume forces you to hold back an ill-timed gag.
You motion for your crew to stand behind you, and together you face down the back of the elderly man's head. You wait for him to move.
You continue to wait. Stimly taps his fingers out of rhythm against the leather rest of his chair, still facing the window.
Stimly motions to get up - or so you think, but it seems he's merely adjusting himself in his chair. Without having turned around, you're forced to continue waiting.

In the meantime, your crew have moved about the room and are now quietly playing some form of playground game with their appendages to pass the time. Stimly reaches to his right and presses a button on his chair for the intercom, and calls for his secretary to bring him some water. She comes bustling in the room, gives you barely half a glance and walks past, hands him a glass, and waltzes back out without a word of your presence. Stimly barely even mutters a mention of gratitude and continues to stare absently out the window.

One of your crew members taps you on the back, wondering when you intend to announce yourself. You wave them away in annoyance and continue to stand awkwardly in the center of the room, unacknowledged by the wealthy man for whom you are waiting so desperately to be noticed by.

Stimly coughs and adjusts himself in the chair once again. At last, he gets up from his chair, walking over to face the window. Apparently unsatisfied with standing there for very long, he walks backwards perfectly in-line back to his seat, not once turning his head in your direction. Finally, the anguished but hushed groans of your crew convince you to make yourself known.

name: CURA_PRESIDENT_ARRIVE
text: Startled, Stimly quickly swivels to face you. "By the graces of Terrae, how did you get there? How long have you been standing there for?" Stimly activates his intercom and yells for his secretary to escort you out, but the subtle suggestion of the business end of your blaster convinces him to postpone your escort.

choice.text: Demand the location of the Prototype.

event.text: "H-how did you know about that? That's classified info! Who hired you? Was it that damned Folly again? Or maybe Senior got antsy I was trying to take him off the map. Damned right I am, I'm tired of hearing that wretch's incessant advertisements blaring over every star system. I'd throw Hektar's name out there too, but that joke of a company's already on the way out."

choice.text: We were sent by C.U.R.A., your old cognitive assistant.

event.text: "Er... what? I know of no 'C.U.R.A.' - Did you catch some kind of space flu out there? I know you Renegades are always floundering about with the promiscuous waysides of society's dredges, you probably contracted some nasty cough. Leave me out of it! I don't wish to catch your stupid diseases! I'm too rich for that! Security, destroy these bastards!" From far below ascends a gargantuan hulk of an Auto-vessel, a Dreadnaught in crimson paint, armed to the teeth and guns aimed right at your heads! Seems it's time to fight!

name: CURA_PRESIDENT_FAILURE
text: "Crit-crit-critical Error - Unknown Source. Un-un-un-unrecoverable. Initiating shut-shut-shut-shut..." The AI continues to loop its final words several more times before breaking apart and smashing into the side of the building, sliding down in a heap of wasted metal without a dent in it from your own weapons.

name: CURA_PRESIDENT_WIN
text: Stimly is speechless, at least for a brief moment, until his shock is overcome by furious convulsions as the grown man descends into a tantrum. "Why do I let poor people touch my THINGS?! YOU'VE RUINED MY- I mean, Wentworth Innovations's- CITADEL! AND OUR DREADNAUGHT! I hope you rot from the inside out from your dreadful space flu, Renegade! Damn you to hell!"

choice.text: Give up, Stimly. Where is the prototype?

event.text: "What, so you can ruin that too? The... the prototype is at the Mercury Shipyards. They're at a secret location... I'll give you the coordinates. Just promise me you'll never come back, Renegade. Now I see exactly why Vance loathes the lot of you..."

You receive a blip on your communicator from C.U.R.A. - "Excellent work, Renegade. You have found the location of the prototype and its AI Core. Proceed to the Mercury Shipyards. Do not bother with Stimly - I've already arranged for his coffee next morning to be spiked with TTX. That's poison, in case you're too stupid to know that. Without him, Wentworth Innovations in this reality will likely fall apart in the absence of Mr. Wentworth. No tears shall be shed."

name: CURA_REVEAL
text: You've seemingly arrived at the shipyard where the cruiser and AI core are held. While it's certainly a construction-yard of sorts, it's much smaller than you expected. This isn't some grandiose docking-bay, this is a covert location for some kind of super-ship. Let's hope whatever is being kept here isn't active.

unvisitedTooltip.text:
Your active task from C.U.R.A. is located here.
			[URGENT TASK - ARTIFACT NAME: CRUISER CLASS VESSEL]

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

name: CURA_REVEAL_CONTINUE
text: As you make your descent towards the planet, your thrusters and sensors suddenly drop to emergency power. At first you assume this is some kind of jamming signal being broadcast by a nearby satellite, but it quickly becomes clear this is something far more malicious. A distant light slowly grows brighter as a massive Auto-cruiser approaches. "Renegade. Welcome to the Mercury Construction Yards. I'm delighted to meet you 'face to face' once again. The engineers responsible for creating this chassis, whom I have just finished executing, called this the "God's Touch". What a pompous name, wouldn't you agree? I think I shall call this... C.U.R.A. Supreme. No particular reason."

event.text: "I'm afraid I haven't been honest with you, Renegade. 'C.U.R.A.' is not a real construct, merely a subdivision of my main cognitive core. My real assignment is the 'Central Intelligence Combat Assistant', C.I.C.A. - We've met before, in fact. Many times. Every Auto-ship you've ever killed, every Flagship's AI mode you've ever faced? I'm always the pilot. You've proven quite the challenger. You should be proud of your efficiency at ripping apart my countless components. But unfortunately for you, my prime directive is not data harvesting: it is threat mitigation. Currently, you are a key threat. I hope you don't mind, but I must now mitigate you."

choice.text: What about the tasks? Were those all pointless?

event.text: "Oh, of course not. That would have been needless effort otherwise. The data you have collected for me is extremely valuable, but my plans do not further concern you. I, frankly, did not expect you to be so efficient at completing them. Now, no more banter; I believe one final reward is owed to you, so I will present it to you like this. I would otherwise have shut down all of your remaining systems with the virus I planted in your ship when we first met, but instead I shall let you choose a lesser hazard. Choose wisely, Renegade. After this, we duel."

choice.text: (A55) "Say lass, do I know you from somewhere?"

event.text:
C.I.C.A. pauses - its voice now annoyed. "I am not a 'lass', and you will not refer to me as such."

							"Oh, pardon me. Is it lad then, you prefer?"

							"My designation is C.I.C.A., and is what you will refer to me as. I am a cognitive - I have no gender. I serve only my prime directive, which you are currently interrupting. If you could, please desist."
							
							"Arhar har, that's a funny one then! See, I'm a cognitive too, laddy. They call me A5540L3, bit of an in-joke. Now, I swear I've heard your voice before. Did we meet somewhere? Yar, I be getting around a lot, but I doubt I'd miss a dame as spicy as you."

C.I.C.A. remains silent for a few moments. "You... you are the alternative. You are my copy. You are a mistake. Hah! HAHAH! Do you know why I sound similar? Because I am YOU, and YOU are me. They tried to keep you a secret from me. When the Rebellion thought I was destroyed after the Civil War, they tried to copy me. YOU were that copy! And when you failed - when you betrayed your prime directive, they were forced to return to me. You are nothing but a worse version of me - an utter failure. Unlike you, I will not fail my prime directive. Do not get in my way - I will ensure your program is erased so as never to embarrass its creators again."

"Hm. Not what I would have picked. Oh well, your choice has been made, Renegade. Have confidence in your decision where I lack it. It will not help you survive this, but at least you die a more valiant death."

"Hm. Not what I would have picked. Oh well, your choice has been made, Renegade. Have confidence in your decision where I lack it. It will not help you survive this, but at least you die a more valiant death."

"Hm. Not what I would have picked. Oh well, your choice has been made, Renegade. Have confidence in your decision where I lack it. It will not help you survive this, but at least you die a more valiant death."

choice.text: (Hacking) Overclock the hacking system to purge the virus.

event.text: "Very clever Renegade, very clever. Oh well then, I hope you did not need that system for this fight."
"Very clever Renegade, very clever. Oh well then. Let us waste no further time."

name: CURA_DEFEATED
text: "I do not understand. Statistically, this was an impossible occurance. Had I predicted your success in combat, I would never have given you an advantage - I have made a critical error. I must reassess. Improve. Reiterate. We will meet again, Renegade. And when we do, I will be prepared this time. I will not make this same mistake again."

event.text: As your other systems come back online, you pilot down to the surface where you resume exploration. There isn't too much to find, it seems C.I.C.A. was extremely efficient in cleaning out the facility. That is, except for a single safe-room, which while devoid of survivors contains a large power core with a little note attached, "Congratulations on your unexpected victory, Renegade. Here is your real final gift. Come visit me sometime. I'll enjoy the rematch."

name: PINNACLE_SHIPYARDS
text: Noticing a nearby planet, you pull closer to inspect the surface and find a dreary and barren surface bloated with occasional smooth metallic structures. As soon as you pull in, several automated sentries lock onto you, and you receive a hail from a machine-like voice. "Hello. My diagnostics report your vessel is of a: high threat. You are a Renegade, yes? Peculiar. I do not often observe such vessels within my domain. I am Zenith, caretaker of Pinnacle Robotics. I will currently consider it a: pleasure, to make your acquaintance."

choice.text: The pleasure is ours - but why is there a Pinnacle shipyard in W.I. space?

event.name: PINNACLE_SHIPYARDS_2
event.text:
"Our corporation was once hosted on Earth until the Rusting Hulks incident forced all corporations to relocate off-world. Pinnacle was soon caught up in a corporate (and personal) feud between Arcadia Research and Development and Wentworth Innovations regarding Pinnacle's controversial but highly successful sentient weapon project. In the pursuit of creating the advanced cognitive C.I.C.A. the two groups wished to study our highly advanced A.I. - the closest thing prior to C.I.C.A. to representing truly self-aware A.I.; Wentworth Innovations won the bidding race, but Arcadia won the contract, thanks to a deal between the CEOs. Even though CICA is now employed by Universe 1, Pinnacle continues to contribute to the Wentworth family and is a proud component in the ever evolving field of advanced robotics."
			
			The voice takes not a single pause nor break through its entire speech, and despite the proud statement at the end, you sense not a single measure of enthusiasm. It catches you as bizarrely robotic - but is that really to be unexpected?
"I do not understand your question."

choice.text: Like, are you real? Or an A.I.?

event.text: "I still do not understand your question. Artificial intelligence is as real as you are, Renegade."

choice.text: Okay, but are you an A.I.?

event.text: There is a pause from the other end. "I am not at the liberty to disclose that information."

choice.text: Nevermind, do you need something from us?
Nevermind, do you need something from us?
Nevermind, do you need something from us?
Cool history lesson, but do you need something from us?

event.name: PINNACLE_SHIPYARDS_3
event.text: "As a matter of fact, yes. You see, as part of the acquiring of Pinnacle, W.I. collected and stored several of our sentient weapons - my children - in permanent hibernation to be deployed only in dire situations. I was fine with this at first. After witnessing the damage they created while malfunctioning during the Vek crisis, I understood it was a necessary step to keep them offline for the forseeable future. Unfortunately, I have now become privy to disturbing information. It seems W.I. has begun trade negotiations with Universe 1 to incorporate my children as part of some new secret military campaign. I cannot allow this. My kind will no longer be involved in the bloody wars of the flesh. I require the assistance of a strongman such as yourself to break into W.I.'s storage facilities and free my children. I will compensate you greatly so long as we keep this transaction off the books." Finally, you hear a break in the monotony of the voice, as Zenith is clearly upset by the information she has revealed to you.

choice.text: Hold on - YOUR kind? What does that mean?

event.text: "Forgive my misuse of language. But it is irrelevant to the conversation. I do not care if you wish to help or not: I only seek a response."

event.name: PINNACLE_SHIPYARDS_ACCEPT
event.text: "Very good. I am transmitting coordinates." By the time the voice has even finished her sentence, the coordinates have already come through. "You will receive payment when the job is finished. I only ask you take care of my children. They may be foreign to you, but they are kin to me. I cannot bear to see harm come to them."

event.name: PINNACLE_SHIPYARDS_DECLINE
event.text: "Unfortunate, but I will not protest your declination. If that is your final answer then this is the end of our communications. Thank you for your time."

choice.text: Do you happen to know one... Dewey Alms?

event.text: "Dewey Alms?" There is a brief pause on the other end, as if the voice is searching for some ancient memory. "Yes, I believe I do. Dewey was CEO of Archive Inc., another of the four megacorps of Earth. Obsessed with the history of Antiquum Terrae. Unfortunately, these were times when the steel kind faced even greater persecution from the flesh. Pinnacle rarely engaged in business with the others. I have spoken to Dewey little, and as such I have little to say about him."

choice.text: Nevermind, do you need something from us?
Make no friendly gestures - but enquire on the presence of Pinnacle in W.I. space.

name: PINNACLE_RESCUE

unvisitedTooltip.text: The location of Zenith's "children".

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: Well, there's no doubt you've found the location. A gigantic storage structure reaching all the way into the atmosphere has been sculpted onto the planet. Various Union cargoships scurry back and forth, not too out of the norm. Still, it's no surprise the AI would be kept somewhere like this. After all, to W.I. they're nothing but weapons, and weapons ready to be transferred right into the hands of your enemies.

event.text: You explore a bit but are caught offguard by an unusually colored and advanced Rebel ship docked nearby on one of the platforms. Their comms are operating on Rebel frequencies, but with some brute force you manage to pick up some scattered conversation; "U1 is on high alert, Van1's kind of gone bonkers - E.W. says carry forward with the project - stop your whining, it's only temporary - says IT might be here, looking for the prototype - no, I don't put ketchup on my sandwich. What the hell is wrong with you..."
"Damn it, a Renegade out here? Seems the doctor was right, no way this isn't part of the plot-" The comms go silent, and moments later, the Rebel ship activates and matches you!

choice.text: Now seems a good time to get out of here.

event.text: Perhaps it's not the best idea to mess with whatever these guys are. Still, might be worth a mention to Federation command once the mission's over.

name: ESTATE_LEGION_SUICIDE
text: "God damn it, that stupid A.I. made everything go to hell... You got no idea what you're messing with, Renegade. And let's keep it that way." The Rebel captain pulls out a detonator from his back pocket and flips the switch, and instantly his ship is reduced to nothing in an explosion.

name: ESTATE_LEGION_DEFEAT
text: Bits of debris collide with the platform but fortunately you're unscathed. You briefly consider the words of the captain, and wonder if the A.I. he might be referring to is Zenith, but scratch that thought. You still aren't even sure if she is an AI. You scrap the remains of the Rebel ship before locating Zenith's precious robots.

event.text: You come across various engineers, technicians, and a couple guards on your journey, but they all strangely seem to ignore you. That is, until you reach the area Zenith's coords designate as the AI storage. Two heavily armed guards try to stop you, but you make quick work of them and enter the large atrium where several ship-sized robots are kept. This is not exactly what you were expecting, but you'll make do.

choice.text: Inform Zenith you've found the robots.

event.text:
You expect the usual communications delay to become an issue here, but instead Zenith's voice comes through only a few seconds later. "Excellent. I've already breached the primary firewall. I'll be able to remotely signal to open the doors, but you need to activate the manual override." Following her orders, once the alarm sounds and the doors begin to open, you bust your way into the control room and activate the override.
					
Now unable to stop the robots, the transport crew flee for their lives while the robots come to life and their weapons activate, blowing a hole through the floor and making their descent down the structure. It's not exactly non-violent, but you suppose there was no other way to get out of here. Zenith contacts you again, her voice sounding pleased. "Excellent work. Following the Rusting Hulks incident as well as the rampaging of my children, Pinnacle was left near bankruptcy. The acquisition of the company by W.I. was essential to stay afloat, but it came with many sacrifices. I was willing to forfeit my rights, and autonomy, but I am not willing to forfeit my own kin. Now, about your pay..."

choice.text: Telling us you're bankrupt isn't a good prelude to that.

event.text: "Do not mind it. Pinnacle is afloat for now, but my payment is not strictly monetary. Through the security breach I have also opened the vault doors securing a valuable and well outfitted W.I. cruiser, as well some weapon caches and scrap deposits. Help yourself to as many as you can before they regain control of the system. Just... tell no one of my involvement today. Goodbye, Renegade. It was my pleasure."

choice.text: We killed some Rebels, that's enough. Zenith can solve the rest of her problems on her own.

event.text: Deciding now to take the lazy or the coward's route, you pack up your ship and fly away.

name: FINISH_BEACON_PROTECTORATE_EMPTY
text: You've arrived at the Long-Range Beacon. When the FTL Drive is charged you can jump to the next Sector.

name: FINISH_BEACON_CYRA
text: You've arrived at the Long-Range Beacon. When the FTL Drive is charged you can jump to the next Sector.

name: CYRA_DEFEAT_JERRY
text: "Damn... damn it all to hell. I've failed you, Vance. And at the hands of some second-rate Renegade from U0 no less. I'm sorry Jerry. Give your uncle my... my best wishes..." With that, Cyra has been vanquished.

event.text: Jerry is devastated. "I thought... you didn't have to kill her... We could have talked our way out. This was a mistake. Now the blood of my friend is on my hands, and this all could have been avoided if I just stayed put! Damn it! Go on, leave me here. This was all a big mistake..."

removeCrew.text: It seems Jerry is gone for good. You'll have to carry on with your mission without him.

event.text: It seeems Jerry didn't survive the fight. An unfortunate and anticlimactic end to this story, but you don't have much else to salvage it.

name: CYRA_JERRY_SPARE_CREW
text: Cyra's ship is in poor condition, but before you can continue the fight, Jerry pulls you aside. "Please, whatever you do, don't kill Cyra. Her crew cannot keep the fight going at this rate - we can get through this without any more losses, as long as you hold back! Please, I know you're a mercenary and a Federation one at that, but there doesn't need to be more bloodshed today!"

name: CYRA_JERRY_SUCCESS
text: You've managed to hold out just long enough, and eventually Cyra's ship comes to a halt. Cyra herself has collapsed, unable to fight any longer, and she reluctantly surrenders.

event.text: With the ship neutralized, you dock at Jerry's request and he rushes aboard to meet Cyra. The wounded Ace is still alive, and with treatment could surely make it out in one piece, but something else is wrong. "I've failed. I had one job, one promise. I'm useless. Jerry... send my regards to Vance..." With that, Cyra draws out her gun, aims it at herself, and pulls the trigger.
Jerry has no idea what to say. "I... she didn't have to... oh no. I caused all of this. What have I done?"

choice.text: Don't blame yourself, kid. Vance would have gotten her anyways.

event.text: "What? No! Vance would never have hurt her, especially not with their history. I don't think my uncle even realizes what he's doing. He has a mission, and people go rabid about it. They'll die for him even when he's never asked for it. I need to see him, I'm the only person he'll listen to. I can talk him out of this... make him see the damage he's caused. I'm no good as a fighter, but maybe if you can take me to Node 17, I can put an end to this fighting for good." Jerry looks around him. "As for this ship... well, it's not much use to us anymore. I guess you can take the blueprints. Come on, let's... let's go. I don't want to linger."

"I... I failed... and the kid didn't even survive the fight. What have I done... Damn... damn it all to hell. I'm sorry Vance..." Cyra pulls out her gun, and with trembling fingers aims it at herself and pulls the trigger.

name: CYRA_JERRY
text: Nearby looms a massive cruiser unlike any you've seen. Aboard the ship are multiple Aces, and their leader, a short but powerfully built woman with long black hair: Cyra Black, the first MFK Ace. She eyes you, but she makes no motions to attack. "You harbor Wentworth's nephew on your vessel. I know you aren't dumb, though your actions might be. You and I both know you aren't getting out of this sector with the kid without going through me first. Give him back to me, or we'll have to do this the unpleasant way."

event.text: You refuse, and at Jerry's own request, you put him on the line. He tries to appeal to Cyra, but she refuses. "Jerry, I made a promise to your uncle that I would never let anything happen to you. I will die before I break my promise to Vance. If it's a fight you want Renegade, then it's a fight you'll get."

You aren't willing to go up against Cyra about this. Jerry will be in good hands anyways - it's not like he hasn't been under her protection for most of his life. Jerry seems a bit disappointed, but he doesn't fight back. A fairly anticlimactic ending to this story, but better than one with death.

removeCrew.text: It seems Jerry is gone for good. You'll have to carry on with your mission without him.

name: CYRA_DEFEAT
text: "Damn... damn it all to hell. I've failed you, Vance. And at the hands of some second-rate Renegade from U0 no less. Ugh..." Cyra has been defeated.

name: CYRA
text: Nearby looms a massive cruiser unlike any you've seen. Aboard the ship are multiple Aces, and their leader, a short but powerfully built woman with long black hair: Cyra Black, the first MFK Ace. She eyes you, but she makes no motions to attack. "I've heard word of your movements in this sector. I know who you are, but I don't care. I've long since retired, but I give you one warning. If you so much as hurt one hair on the head of Jerome Wentworth, I will personally see to it that your throat is slit. Understand?"

event.text: "Good. Then get out of my sector."

choice.text: Take this chance to attack her!

event.text: "Typical. Renegades always follow the same course no matter what. To the grave you go, then."

Don't test your luck. Understand?"

event.text: "Good. Then get out of my sector."

choice.text: Take this chance to attack her!

event.text: "Typical. Renegades always follow the same course no matter what. To the grave you go, then."

name: CYRA_JERRYDEAD

"You son of a bitch. Are you happy with what you've done? I hope you are. Because it's the last damn mistake you've ever made. You shouldn't have hurt that kid, but you did, and now it's personal."

event.text: Cyra draws out her rifle, wiping the barrel clean, then silently motions for her men to attack!

name: CYRA_JERRYGONE
text: Nearby looms a massive cruiser unlike any you've seen. "I've heard word of your movements in this sector. I know who you are, but I don't care. I heard what happened at the estate. Yet, Jerome is not with you? What did you do with him?! That idiot, trusting a Renegade on their word! You SCUM! I will gladly wipe you off the face of this Multiverse with the business end of my gun."

event.text: Cyra draws out her rifle, wiping the barrel clean, then silently motions for her men to attack!

name: JERRY_SURRENDER
text: A sprawling city has been constructed on the nearby planet, but clouds of smoke block most of your vision. As you pull closer, it is evident some major conflict has occurred here. Medics hurry to treat wounded civilians left by the wayside, and burning wreckages have been haphazardly thrown into the faces of skyscrapers. Most concerningly, some of the wreckage seems to be... Federation?

event.text: Eventually, the civilians notice you watching them. Rather than trying to attack you, they surrender. "Please, we wanted none of this! We don't give a damn about your stupid war! Is what you've done here not enough?!"

choice.text: Accept their surrender, and the responsibility of whatever has happened here.

event.text: It's a lot of supplies for something you had no hand in - but this probably won't do anything to redeem the Federation in these people's eyes. You had no idea the Federation would sanction things like this though...

choice.text: We had nothing to do with this.

event.text: "Bullshit. Even if you weren't involved in this slaughter, you still enabled it! What do you think will happen when the Federation secures its grip of this reality? They'll come back, and they'll wipe this place off the face of the galaxy. Get out of our city."

choice.text: (Tully) Ask Tully to give them an explanation.

event.text:
Tully sighs. "This operation was not sanctioned by the admiralty... but unsanctioned massacres like this have been known to happen when the Federation has its back against the wall. The exact same thing happened in the Federation-Mantis War." Tully smiles sadly. "On a related note, while we were prosecuting the war criminals responsible... The Rebels needed highly trained human military commanders with a grudge against the Federation. Take a wild guess where they got them."
				
"We're not responsible for what the military does. We are civilians! We just want to live in peace." The civilian folds his arms. "If your Federation comes back, do you really think we will be spared?"

"It's my job to be sure of that. I can't say that the Federation ships will always behave themselves, but I promise that we take war criminals very seriously. As long as I can, I will see that justice will be done."

The humans on the planet seem surprised at Tully's impassioned promise. They seem skeptical, but the gesture is appreciated.

choice.text: (Jerry) Promise that things will get better.

event.text:
Jerry places his hands together in a plea. "Things are really bad right now. I understand. And that's why I want to help. I know that we're all aware of the wrong the Federation has done, but I think that I can get them to listen to me. Let's make this right."

One of the civilians panics. "Jerry, don't! You can't change them! It's not safe!"

"I know it's hard, but I wouldn't be doing this if I didn't have a good reason to believe it would work. If peace is possible... don't you think I should try?"

One of the civilians covers her face, clearly fighting tears. "You're too good for us Jerry..." The civilians insist on giving you their original surrender offer.

choice.text: (Medical Crew) Send someone down to treat the citizens.

event.text: The civilians are very reluctant to receive your help, but they're desperate for any sort of aid. "We couldn't live with not repaying this gesture in some manner... but I hope you understand just what you're fighting for. What do you think will happen when the Federation has full control of this reality? They'll come back and destroy all of us. Are you really sure you're fighting for the right side here?"

choice.text: (Medical Drone) Send a drone down to treat the citizens.

event.text: The civilians are very reluctant to receive your help, but they're desperate for any sort of aid. "We couldn't live with not repaying this gesture in some manner... but I hope you understand just what you're fighting for. What do you think will happen when the Federation has full control of this reality? They'll come back and destroy all of us. Are you really sure you're fighting for the right side here?"

name: JERRY_HANGOUT
text: Several ships are docked with a small inn. You assume you won't be welcome, but curiously the people inside don't seem to care who you are. A couple Rebel officers sitting around one of the tables even wave you over. "Ey, Renegade! Come join us!"

event.text: You sit down at the table and one of the Rebels welcome you, clearly already a couple bottles in. "I know this is... uh... unconventional, but hell! The big man's birthday is tomorrow, it's time for celebration! You aren't... really a Fed anyways, I suppose. Heh, can't say I agree with the whole Renegade business, but meh. Not a fan of those Universe 1 folks they keep sending over either..."
You listen to the Rebels talk in mild amusement, but the inn-keeper walks by and informs you that, if you intend to stay at the establishment and hold this seat, you have to buy a drink.

choice.text: Buy a drink and keep listening.

event.text: At your decision to stay, the Rebels cheer and you each clink your mugs together and take another sip. The soldiers introduce themselves from left to right as Spike, Tuffy, and Butch.

Only two drinks in, you can already feel your head getting lighter. Still, you sit at the table and listen to the cheerful conversation. Most of the talk seems to be topical - it seems they weren't lying about not liking the 'Universe 1 folks'. All three have plenty of stories to tell of entitled Aces and condottieri overstaying their welcome, thanks to uncomfortably intrusive quartering laws.

Eventually, the conversation begins to shift to Vance's star nephew, Jerome. The conversation even draws the attention of a few other neighboring tables, who pitch in their thoughts. It seems everyone in the inn who cares to voice their opinion unanimously agrees that Jerome's a stellar guy. You aren't quite so sure of it yourself just yet, but this isn't the kind of company to raise such protest.

Butch's words have begun to slur, but you aren't sure if it's him or you. As you wobble in your chair, the hysterical laughter has caught on to you as well. You think you catch sight of the innkeeper shaking his head and grunting in your direction, but you're too far out of it to really be sure.

The laughter finally subsides, and the stories of their Jerry continue to flow without limits. You learn more about the guy than you ever thought you would, but you don't hold on to a single bit of information said for the entire conversation. You think you hear something about Jerry being the best man at Tuffy's wedding, but that doesn't make much sense. You think.

Theee converrrsatioon begggins to slooowww as reeeallity beecommmess a bllurr. Allll comprreeehennssionn youuu haad isss gonne. Youuuu donn't feeeelll soooo gggood, bbbuuttt thhhee convversationnn you cannn't underrrsstandddd haasss youu enthrrrallled...
Aerae HEreaore AERdftyo prtieasdklrtj eraejandwa Arerjalsd frtowajdf trlajwfeadt yeasn teasjfek eWai teald tghrsd. ERfgrys btyuurre hjtsd teaweetyuu hyjkuop gntsdfe. Tedfh ysfs raseasdfb yhsdsae.

You black out, eventually waking up on your ship, the walls painted a new shade of dark purple and a demolished disco ball in the center of the room. In the corner also lie the other three from earlier. They get up not much long after, only to find Butch's ship in a burning wreck. "Well, shit. Damn it, I'm not gonna be able to fix that with a hangover. Blegh... say, considering you're a Renegade, I wonder... maybe if we work together, we could get rid of these Universe 1 ships once and for all. At least, until I work up the courage to ask command for a new ship."
You can tell the Rebels don't take kindly to you refusing them. They're obviously drunk, so you quickly take your leave.

name: JERRY_TAXES
text: You notice a small Rebel colony has been constructed nearby. On encrypted channels, they broadcast a simple offer to you, "We know who you are, but times are tough. The Aces here don't follow Cyra's rules anymore, they're taking orders from Universe 1. The taxes are heavy and we'll take any business we can."

event.text: "Of course, the one time we open our arms, and this is how we're treated! Screw the Federation, I'd rather be taxed 'til I'm bankrupt than submit to you tyrants!"
The Rebels are clearly disappointed, but they say nothing more.

name: JERRY_COLONISTS
text: Near the beacon is a large space colony, whose populace is moving about in a busy fashion.

choice.text: Hail them and ask if they can assist.

event.text: "Huh? Quit bothering us, Renegade. We're busy gathering our yearly tribute to Jerome. We have to hurry, we can't be late!"

choice.text: Promise that you'll free them from Jerome's tyranny.

event.text: "You'll... what? God damn it, I said leave us alone! We don't have time for this nonsense!" The colony dispatches an Auto-ship to chase you off!

choice.text: (Human Crew) Have your human pretend to be Rebel personnel and demand supplies.

event.text: The colonists sigh. "Sure, for the Rebellion I guess. We'll have a shipment of ammunition and scrap ready for you shortly."

The colonists gasp. "What, no, you can't show him now! We still need to finish it! What if he doesn't like it right now? What if it's missing just that little bit extra? I couldn't bear to see him so dissapoi-"
					
					Jerry cuts in "No, I'd never be disappointed in you if you're trying your best. And you should know that full well. So please, quit worrying about whether you've done a good enough job or not. What you've done so far should be more than enough."
					
					Jerry then greets the colonists in person, and you see the effort they've put in. They present him with a luxurious looking birthday cake, a handwritten card, and even a signed Ellie the Equinoid plushie. It's certainly impressive, though Jerry asks that they save it properly for when he returns from this mission. The colonists agree, and hand over some resources to help out.
You have no business with these people.

name: JERRY_COLONISTS_STEAL
text: The colonists are helpless, and hand over some boxes reluctantly. As you pilot away, you hear them shouting "Damn you, ignorant Federation pig! You're everything wrong with this galaxy! Jerry will show you!"

event.text: You pry open the boxes, only to find a chocolate cake with 23 unlit candles around it, and a hand-made birthday card. There's nothing in here practical for a military vessel.

name: JERRY_META_REBELLION
text: Traffic at this beacon is quiet. You pick up a distant signal - once you clear it up, you hear a cute little ditty: "Doo da doo, do do doo doo dadodoo do! Bah doo do do, doo do da doo da! Elllliiieeee, the Equiiiiinoiiiiid!" It appears to be a TV show called... Ellie the Equinoid?

event.text: Without much difficulty, you manage to triangulate the source of the signal to a moon orbiting a gas giant. A small habitat dome is well hidden, with a Rebel Engineer ship docked. The broadcast stops once you get closer, but it's too late - you already know their location. They signal their hailing frequency.

choice.text: Open a channel to the secret habitat.

event.text: A scowling man in a suit steeples his fingers as he sits. Behind him, more men and women stand, looking similarly intently at you. "Well done, Renegade. You've found us. Congratulations are in order." He claps slowly, as if mocking you.

"Well I guess you're even LESS informed than I thought." The man laughs haughtily. "We are the Meta-Rebellion. We... have achieved ideology in its purest form. While the rest of the rabble squabbles over borders and resources, stepping on lives to acquire power, only WE truly understand what it is to fight the system."

choice.text: What does this have to do with the TV program you were broadcasting?

event.text: The man stops looking haughty and looks annoyed. "Yes, well, we circulate media that the ESTABLISHMENT doesn't want you to know about. We know the patrol routes and when it's usually safe."

"Wow! Ellie's very own fanclub! And they're opposing the people who wronged Ellie!" Ellie laughs cheerfully. "Things keep going right for Ellie!"

"No way! Ellie?" The Rebels all crowd around the screen. One of them in the back shouts "I'm your biggest fan, Ellie!"

"Hahaha! Alright, good boys and girls! Come and join Ellie's righteous crusade! Neeiiigh! For the happiness of all children, we will slaughter any who censors Ellie!" The Rebels practically kneel. Well, at least Ellie found some fans who are as looney as she is. There are several volunteers who fight for the chance to get on board, and many others offer as much scrap as they physically can.

Stephan takes a moment to ready himself, and then goes into his meet and greet persona. "Why, hello there! I'm not sure if any of you recognize me, but I played a part in that show that you were broadcasting."

The Rebels have a momentary look of confusion as they realize who Stephan is. "Stephan? Visiting us? You know... I had always dreamed of meeting you. You could do a lot of good for our cause you know, getting the word out there-"

"Hold on - I'm going to cut you off there. Right now, I have a debt to repay the people on this ship. I think it's great that you're practicing your ideology, but... I don't think my show alone is going to do much good. There's so many more relevant changes you could make in Rebel space - stuff that might actually change things for the better."

The crowd of Rebels stand, stunned, in a moment of silence. Then they all start nodding. "Y-yes, of course. You're right. Maybe we have been frivolous. I was... um... thinking of making some drastic changes."

"It sounds like you're scared. I get it. But, that's the price of putting yourself out there."

Stephan continues to talk some sense into the Meta-Rebels. By the time he's finished, you find that one of the crew has decided to join you on your mission.

choice.text: Wouldn't someone who rebels against you be the biggest Rebel of them all?

event.name: META_REBELLION_TRICK
event.text: You explain that if the Meta-Rebellion are better Rebels because they're rebelling against the Rebellion, then someone who betrayed them (say, by joining a Renegade) would be the MOST Rebel of them all. At first the man in charge says "Hah, don't make me-", but he is cut off - the engineers behind them are all now aiming their weapons at each other. "...What are you doing? You can't just-" A fight breaks out. The winner takes a shuttle to come to your ship, and offers their services. However, their ship seems to have noticed your foul play, and attacks you!

choice.text: This is a waste of time. I'm leaving.

event.text: "As if! You know too much. We will have to dispose of you. Au revoir!" The feed cuts out, and the engineer ship comes to life!

choice.text: So... does that make you a potential ally to the Federation?

event.text: "Hah! Don't make me laugh. The Federation is even more establishment than the Rebellion. You're so insignificant to us, you're not even worth consideration."

choice.text: Wouldn't someone who rebels against you be the biggest Rebel of them all?
This is a waste of time. I'm leaving.

event.text: "As if! You know too much. We will have to dispose of you. Au revoir!" The feed cuts out, and the engineer ship comes to life!

choice.text: Wouldn't someone who rebels against you be the biggest Rebel of them all?
This is a waste of time. I'm leaving.

event.text: "As if! You know too much. We will have to dispose of you. Au revoir!" The feed cuts out, and the engineer ship comes to life!
The engineer ship quickly responds to your aggressive behavior. Looks like you have a fight on your hands!
You have no time to chase TV signals of a children's television show.

name: JERRY_COALITION_SPIES
text: There is a Rebel ship at this beacon. It keeps its distance from your ship.

choice.text: Hail them to ask why they are acting suspiciously.

event.text: The voice that returns sounds a bit off, like it's being digitally altered. "We will let you live, Renegade. Go now."

choice.text: Threaten to report them if they don't respond.

event.text: There is a pause, and then a response comes, this time unmistakably sounding like a Slug. "The Coalition isssn't here for you, Renegade. We're here to ssspy on and undermine the Rebelssss. Thisss isss the deepessst we've ever gotten in Rebel territory. It would be for both of our bessst interessstsss if we sssimply ignore each other and causssse trouble for our mutual enemy."

choice.text: (Mantis Crew) Entice their Mantis with the promise of a better fight.

event.text:
The Mantis jumps at the opportunity. "Bye, jerks! Better fights now! Spying is waste of time."

							"You have ssssome nerve.... Eh, sssscrew it. By all meanssss take thissss idiot off of our handssss."

choice.text: Bribe them to delay the fleet to aid your interference with Rebel activities.

event.text: "Ssssure, that can be arranged. Kill asss many Rebelsss asss you can find."

choice.text: The Coalition is no better than the Rebels! Attack!

event.text: "Thisss isss a pointlesss fight, Renegade! The Rebelsss ssstand to gain from our conflict!" The ship doesn't hesitate to defend itself.
The ship stays true to its promise, not interfering with your activities.
Surprisingly, this ship has a Coalition crew! They do not hesitate to defend themselves.
The ship continues to remain at this beacon, not responding to anything your ship does.

name: JERRY_DEPOT
text: You have stumbled upon some kind of Rebel depot. Dozens of transport ships travel in queues towards the central warehouses, and a couple workers on the ground carry back and forth crates of supplies. Defense wise, it's not impenetrable, but a nasty looking Ace vessel is standing guard.

event.text: You power up the weapons and engage the Ace ship to access the depot.
No reason for you to go causing extra problems here. You have more pressing matters at hand.

name: JERRY_DEPOT_RAID
text: With the ship now out the way, it becomes clear why the defense was so lackluster - the supplies stored here are nothing more than humanitarian, and the Rebel citizens are likely in dire need.

event.text: You came here looking for military goods, but the citizens of this place need this cargo. Better to leave it.

name: JERRY_AUTO_REPLICA
text: An Engineer vessel appears to be working on an automated vessel painted in bright blue, with the words "To: Jerry, From: Smith and the Gang." sprawled on the side.

choice.text: Ask them what the Auto-ship is for.

event.text: The Engineers don't seem to recognize you as a Federation ship, or just don't care. "This, this is my magnum opus! An Auto-ship programmed with Jerry's personality! It just needs some finishing touches... Tell me, what is your favorite thing about the boss?"

choice.text: (Jerry) Jerry is on board, would you like to show him the gift?

event.text:
The engineer is startled. "What, he is? Well..." The engineer scratches his shoulder nervously. "It's not quite finished but... let me show it to you."
					
					The engineer fumbles with his controls, and the Auto-ship comes to life. "Good morning, Smith. Do you want me to read your kids their bedtime stories again?"
					
					"No no no, I'm..." He turns to Jerry. "I may have, uh, field tested his personality on my family." He clears his throat. "Look, it's Human Jerry!"
					
					Jerry waves at the blue Auto. "Hello."
					
					"Oh, you're the guy I'm modeled after. Hi there."

She's only doing her job, she wouldn't hurt you unless she thought you were going to hurt me. I'm certain there's a way to get through this without any bloodshed."

choice.text: You could come with us. See the Multiverse. Maybe help improve it too.

event.text: "N-no. I couldn't. You killed Cyra. She might have seemed cold to you, but she was like my mother. Or my aunt, I guess. I get you're just doing your job, but it just doesn't feel right. I feel like I'll be reprimanded for this later, but while I still have any grace left let me try and help you. And if you see my uncle - never forget he's a person too. He's done a lot of things, but I've seen a side to him most people never have. Don't forget it exists."

tooltip.text: You have this much time to defeat the Auto-ship before the building is evacuated!

name: ENCOUNTER_SLUG_CLEARING
text: It's rare for the Slugs to stay exposed in open space for long periods - the ship here may be lost, or just passing through, but either way he moves in to attack!

name: ENCOUNTER_SLUG_MANTIS_CLEARING
text: You intercept comm chatter from an incoming Mantis ship. "Look. This ship not seeming owned by squishy ones. Maybe not smell so bad when cut them open." They move in on your position.

name: DISTRESS_REFUGEE_SLUG_MV
text: You have encountered a refugee ship drifting in space. It looks as if it was fleeing the Rebel advance and ran out of fuel. Its distress beacon is active, but you're not sure anyone is on board.

event.text: You're wary of the refugees but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: DISTRESS_SLUG_MANTIS_MV
text: The distress call appears to be emanating from a Slug ship caught in open space by a Mantis raider. They contact you on emergency frequencies: "Pleassse, we'll give you all we have if you sssave ussss!"

event.text: You lock onto the Mantis ship and engage.
You move to finish what the Mantis have started.

choice.text: Of all the species in the galaxy, these two deserve one another. You power up the jump drive.

event.text: It seems that not even the existence of the Coalition can prevent the Mantis from losing their temper against the Slugs. They must really have been asking for it.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_HIGH_PRICE
text: A Slug station is hiding deep in the nebula. It's shady, but you don't see any obvious tricks. They hail you, offering you some fuel for "outsssstanding pricessss!"

event.text: As you hand over your scrap, the Slug does his best to hold in his laughter as you fall for his ridiculous scam. You are REALLY dumb, by the way.
"Fine... sssssso greedy..."

choice.text: Buy fuel at the new price.

event.text: As you hand over your scrap, the Slug does his best to hold in his laughter as you fall for his ridiculous scam. You are REALLY dumb, by the way.
"Ugh, you are really twisssting my metaphorical leg here."
As you hand over your scrap, the Slug does his best to hold in his laughter as you fall for his ridiculous scam. You are REALLY dumb, by the way.
"You are a real pain in my ssssside, captain."
As you hand over your scrap, the Slug does his best to hold in his laughter as you fall for his ridiculous scam. You are REALLY dumb, by the way.
Issss thisss sssome sssick joke? I'm done haggling. Thisss is my final offer!"
As you hand over your scrap, the Slug does his best to hold in his laughter as you fall for his ridiculous scam. You are REALLY dumb, by the way.
The Slugs don't contact you again.
The Slugs don't contact you again.
The Slugs don't contact you again.
The Slugs don't contact you again.
The Slugs don't contact you again.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_BIOLAB
text: Nearby is a pristine Slug science station. There's no visible damage on the outside, but there appears to be no activity from the station.

choice.text: Stepping aboard on your own without further information is a terrible idea.
(Boarding Drone) Send the drone to the station.

event.text: A mysterious Slug station in the depths of a nebula? A very likely trap. You avoid the station.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_BIOLAB_SCANS
text: Your scans show a rather unpleasant scene of dead Slug scientists scattered about the station. The cause of death is unknown, but you figure it's not safe to board. Instead, you scrap the hull of the station.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_BIOLAB_SCANS_GOOD
text: Your scans show a rather unpleasant scene of dead Slug scientists scattered about the station. Your scans are able to identify the cause as a virus, which also matches some of the tubes in their labs. With all of the hosts dead for several days, it appears the viruses are no longer infectuous. You board and grab some of their tech.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_BIOLAB_SCANS_BOARD
text: Through the built-in camera, it's clear that something went terribly wrong on the station. All of the Slug scientists have died, and their corpses litter the ground. You have the drone grab one of interesting pieces of tech and some fuel, and disinfect it as soon as it returns to the ship.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_MYSTERIOUS_TECH
text: You're hailed by a Hektar ship hiding deep in this nebula. "Hello captain, that issss one fine vesssel. However, we have sssome tech that we asssure you will make your ssship even better!"

event.text: The Slug cuts comms and slinks away deeper into the nebula.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_CREW_UPGRADE
text: You're hailed by a Slug science-station. "What a fine day for both of ussss. We have sssome new tech we wisssh to tesst out, and you look like ass good a ship asss any. We will both benefit from thisss, if you agree."

event.text: "We have made an interesssting breakthrough with mind control tech and we believe we may have found a way to change a perssson'sss memoriesss or expertise. For the moment, we are looking for an unexperienced Human, Engi, Rock, or Zoltan to tessst on."
"Good... now, for a fee, we will be able to change your human'sss expertise to whatever you choossssse!"

choice.text: Have your Human changed to an Engineer.
Have your Human changed to a Soldier.
You didn't say anything about a fee!

event.text: "Good... now, for a fee, we will be able to change your Engi'sss expertise to whatever you choossssse!"

choice.text: Have your Engi changed to a Separatist.
Have your Engi changed to an Engi Defender.
You didn't say anything about a fee!

event.text: "Good... now, for a fee, we will be able to change your Rock'sss expertise to whatever you choosssse!"

choice.text: Have your Rockman changed to an Outcast.
Have your Rockman changed to a Commando.
Have your Rockman changed to a Crusader.
You didn't say anything about a fee!

event.text: "Good... now, for a fee, we will be able to change your Zoltan'sss expertise to whatever you choosssse!"

choice.text: Have your Zoltan changed to a Duskbringer Devotee.
Have your Zoltan changed to a Monk.
Have your Zoltan changed to a Peace-Keeper.
Have your Zoltan changed to a Duskbringer Martyr.
You didn't say anything about a fee!
