choice.text: (Manning Drone) Attempt to steer the ship remotely.

event.text: You send your drone over towards the Federation ship, and direct it towards the cockpit. The fires threaten to melt the drone before it can even reach the controls, but it manages to steer the ship away from the station before impact.

The owner of the station returns your hail when you return. "Your counterparts aboard the station explained to me what you just did for us. Please, we aren't a large station, but help yourself to whatever you need. None of us would still be here to have this conversation if you hadn't arrived."

choice.text: (Upg. Hacking) Force the ship to stop.

event.text: You launch a hacking probe towards the Federation ship, and your ship computer soon registers a change in course trajectory. Satisfied, you return to the Union station to inform them that the problem has been resolved.

The owner of the station returns your hail when you return. "Your counterparts aboard the station explained to me what you just did for us. Please, we aren't a large station, but help yourself to whatever you need. None of us would still be here to have this conversation if you hadn't arrived."

choice.text: (Rock Plating) Ram the ship out of the way.

event.text: As your hull impacts the out-of-control Federation ship, you can see the structure of the damaged ship threaten to buckle under the sheer force of the collision. However, your ship computer soon shows a corrected flight path for the vessel, and you return to the station to collect your reward.
As you spool up your FTL drive, you try not to focus on the Federation ship fast approaching in the distance. None of this will matter if you don't stop the Flagship.

Whatever this distress call is for, it won't matter if the Rebels win the battle. As you prepare to jump away, you can see another Federation vessel approaching in the distance - hopefully they'll be able to resolve the issue.

name: SHIP_CRASH_INTO_STATION
text: As the Federation ship races towards the station, you and your crew are helpless to stop it. Fragments from the collision shred your hull as the two constructs are turned into a metallic mist upon impact.

name: NODE17_SPECTATOR
text: A Slug ship is at this beacon. Their captain appears to be eating some alien version of popcorn. "Oh, well if it isn't the sssship everyone'sss been looking for. I wondered if I'd ssssee you here. Thiss really is ssssuch an interesssssting experience. We have no part to play here, but ssssometimesss you just want to see a good ssshow, you know?"

event.text: "Aw crap!-" the Slug is cut off by a Rebel ship flying by. A shot pierces the Slug hull, and the Rebel locks onto you.

name: NODE17_ENCOUNTER_PIRATE
text: A pirate ship comes careening towards you. "God damn it, god damn it, god DAMN IT! We need to get away from this bloody sector! Get out of our way!"

name: NODE17_ENCOUNTER_ENGINEER
text: A Rebel Engineer fleet has taken a bold moment of direct action and engaged the Federation fleet nearby! Though likely only out of necessity, an Engineer vessel breaks off to handle you.

name: NODE17_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_STATION
text: Unfortunately, it seems the Rebels have secured control over this beacon! A hastily thrown together Rebel outpost readies to defend against you.

name: NODE17_PANDORAS_BOX
text: A very strangely colored pirate ship is already here. They hail you. "We are the keepers of the box. Only he who is truly worthy may wield the box's power."

event.text: The pirate moves closer to the screen, staring deep into your eyes for a minute or two. "Yeah sure, why the hell not. Have fun."

choice.text: "WARNING: unknown anomalous artifact detected. Scheduled for [QUARANTINE]."

event.text: The pirate says nothing more. You fly away until you can no longer see them.

name: NODE17_REPAIR_STATION
text: You jump into the system, noticing the nearby repair station signal.

event.text: It looks as though a Rebel Elite is firing on the repair station! You'll have to clear these guys out first before you can get assistance.
It looks as though an MFK Ace is firing on the repair station! You'll have to clear these guys out first before you can get assistance.

name: BOSS_REPAIR_STATION_FIGHT
text: Fortunately, with the Rebels out of the way, you're able to access the station. They're beaten up, but still able to supply you with what you need.

name: LOSTSUN_MISSILES_DRIFT
text: A destroyed Rock ship drifts, its hull picked clean recently. However, you are lucky and find one surviving crate of ammunition.

name: LOSTSUN_SHRINE
text: A team of Lost Sun ships appear to be demolishing a nearby Crystalline shrine. They hail you, asking if you can spare any explosives.

event.text: "We were not expecting a supply ship any time soon, and this may help." They fire a rocket directly into the foundation of the structure, sending the entire thing crumbling. "Surprising. We have not had access to quality ammunitions such as these in a long time. May we keep the spares?"
"Your good will has been noted. Let us repay you, captain."

choice.text: Request that they give the spares back.

event.text: "Fine, but do not think that we will forget this. You may think these come in easy supply, but they do not."

choice.text: Apologize and turn down their offer.

event.text: The Lost Suns do not try to hail you again. You put some distance between yourself and them just in case.

name: LOSTSUN_CACHE
text: An incessant beeping on your radar shows a strange object floating in empty space. It appears to be... a Lost Sun weapon cache?

event.text: Stealing military supplies in Lost Sun territory doesn't sound like a good idea. You leave it be.

name: LOSTSUN_DONATION
text: A Lost Sun fleet appears to be protecting the nearby moon, which houses a relatively large mining operation. On closer inspection, it seems the fleet is poorly armed.

event.text: "A Federation ship, in our sector? Are you another supply runner?" You shake your head. "Hmph. I do not normally request help from strangers who may or may not be welcome, but we are in need of ammunition. Do you have any warheads that you can spare?"
"I see you are not sparing with your supplies. All the same, it was not my place to ask. Something is better than nothing..."
Reluctantly, the Lost Sun captain gives you some scrap as payment.
"This is quite the supply. You surprise me, Federation captain. I suppose I am now in your debt."
Thankful for your large donation, the Lost Suns pay you back with ample scrap.
"Interesting technology. I have heard of it, yes, but our budget is low. This will help us considerably. Thank you, captain."
The Lost Suns repay your tech with some of their own, as well as some scrap.
"As expected. Hurry along then, and hope misfortune does not follow you."
There isn't anything that concerns you here. You fly away.

name: ASTEROID_EXPLORE_LOSTSUN
text: Scans reveal a large asteroid field nearby. Short-range scanners may discover useful materials while we wait for the FTL to recharge.

choice.text: Too dangerous. We'll just wait for the FTL to charge.

event.text: You decide to ignore the asteroids.

choice.text: (Scrap Recovery Arm) Attempt to mine the asteroids.

event.text: You carefully extract as much usable material as possible from the nearest asteroids while waiting for the FTL to charge.

choice.text: (Mining Equipment) Attempt to mine the asteroids.

event.text: You carefully extract as much usable material as possible from the nearest asteroids while waiting for the FTL to charge.

choice.text: (Beam Drone) Attempt to mine the asteroids. [-1|]

event.text: You carefully extract as much usable material as possible from the nearest asteroids while waiting for the FTL to charge.

name: LOSTSUN_CIVILIAN_RESCUE
text: You see a Lost Sun ship attacking an unarmed civilian ship trying to pass through the sector. You doubt the Lost Sun notices you, due to its complete focus on mauling civilians.

event.text: You kick your engines into high gear and chase away the Lost Sun from the civilian. Time for a fight.
The civilians continue trying to hail you. You tune them out and fly away until you're completely alone.

name: LOSTSUN_CHALLENGERS
text: A Lost Sun ship protecting this beacon promptly hails you a little while after jumping in nearby. "A passing ship! We have a challenge for you. Best us in combat, and we shall give you a reward. Accept a greater challenge, and we shall give an even greater reward!"

choice.text: Fight them for a normal reward.

event.text: "Let the battle commence!"

choice.text: Fight them without life support or medical systems.

event.text: "Let the battle commence!"

choice.text: Fight them with a weakened reactor.

event.text: "Let the battle commence!"
"Let the battle commence!"

choice.text: Fight them with severely weakened systems.

event.text: "Let the battle commence!"

choice.text: We aren't looking for a fight.

event.text: "I did not take you for cowards. Oh well, perhaps it is for the best."

name: LOSTSUN_PRISONERS
text: A Lost Sun confinement appears to be keeping several ships from various origins captive. A patrol ship is searching the area, and you won't have long until it sees you.

choice.text: Attack the barricade and free the civilians.

event.text: Your attacks are inefficient, and several countershots get through your defenses. You get out of their range in time but the patrol ship moves in to attack!
You know you're taking a risk, but you could use the extra scrap. You power up your weapons and engage the patrol ship.
You manage to escape the patrol ship. You should still leave the beacon as soon as possible.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Wait for the patrol ship to pass by, then sabotage their defenses.

event.text: Your waiting pays off when the patrol ship passes right by, and eventually passes out of your view. You sneak up to the confinement and lay down the explosives, then fly to a safe distance to watch the fireworks.

Chaos erupts in the Lost Sun structure as explosions ripple across the surface. One appears to have disabled the main power to the shield keeping the civilians at bay, and they escape. The civilians spot you and, putting two and two together, decide to pay you for freeing them.

name: LOSTSUN_ROCK_SPY
text: A Rock spy appears to be hiding in this asteroid field. You don't see them for very long until they've already slipped out of sight.

event.text: There's no reason to be chasing down random Rock ships in asteroid fields. You prepare to leave as quickly as possible.

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Use your improved engines to track them down.

event.text: You manage to catch up to the Rock spy. They don't take kindly to you following them, and attack.

name: LOSTSUN_MANTIS_LOST
text: The red ship at this beacon belongs to the Mantis. With no obvious motives, you aren't sure why they came here.

event.text: Theres no words that need be exchanged. As soon as you begin to approach it is clear that your intentions are hostile, and the Mantis prepare to defend themselves.

The Mantis appear mildly shocked that you reached out to them. Before they can speak however, a Lost Sun ship comes flying out of nowhere and blasts the Mantis ship into oblivion. They seem to identify you as a threat as well.
Contrary to expectations, the Mantis make no attempt to follow. You distance yourself from their ship.

name: LOSTSUN_CHALLENGE
text: A Lost Sun ship at this beacon has already spotted you before it's too late to slip away unnoticed. They hail you.

event.text: "So, you are the Federation Renegade that we have heard so much about, intruding on our sector in some dangerous quest to destroy the Flagship? Brave, and stupid. Stupid that you think you have the right to endanger our sector by drawing the fleet here. If you wish to pass unharmed, you must answer some questions and prove you are worthy."
"We Lost Suns have been fighting a war against the brutal Rock dictatorship for years. For which crime do we hold them responsible and sparked the start of this bloody war?"

choice.text: The use of propaganda to lie to their citizens.

event.text: "The Coalition might be a divisive and problematic side effect, but the true problem originates from the Rock Elders and their lies! Of course, the Federation would certainly love for us to exhaust our resources against the Coalition. Let us teach you a well-deserved lesson."
"That is not even a crime! If you cannot even be mature, then it is clear you do not belong here. Prepare to have your life extinguished."

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) The use of propaganda to lie to their citizens.

event.text: "Expected. Then your untimely death is your fault, and your fault alone."

name: LOSTSUN_CHALLENGE_CORRECT_1
text: "Very good, though that was a question anyone but the Rock people themselves could answer."

event.text: "Which race is the strongest and most pure of any other?"
"You are incorrect. You think pandering to us will get you anywhere? No race is pure! You are not worthy of such treatment. Prepare to be destroyed by filthy mortal flames."

"Bah haha! That is the lie told to us from birth! The Crystals are no gods, they are used as false idols! Clearly, you too believe the lies of the Elders. We will remove you from this world in which you do not belong."
The Lost Sun captain descends into clear rage. "You think this is funny? The Federation is not even a race! I have no time for this idiocy. I will erase your ignorance with fire!"

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) None. There is no such thing as a holy race.

name: LOSTSUN_CHALLENGE_CORRECT_2
text: "Indeed. The very idea that a race was chosen by gods to be superior is flawed, and unproven; any government claiming otherwise is only exploiting these beliefs to control the masses as they wish to secure their own authority."

event.text: "No government is free of lies or scandals. Prove to us that you see through the lies that your precious Federation has been spreading for years."

choice.text: The Federation has been supporting the Lost Suns only to cripple the Coalition.
The Federation is as responsible for the Rebellion as the Rebels themselves.
The Federation has committed as many warcrimes as any of their enemies.
The Federation has never told a lie.

event.text: "Hah! So you are truly a simple minded fool, following what you are told blindly. There is no room for people like you in this galaxy."

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) Your crew does not know the answer.

name: LOSTSUN_CHALLENGE_CORRECT_3
text: "You impress me, captain. I have challenged many, many ships who have passed through here before, and not one has been able to prove themselves. You have my respect. Let me come with you on your journey, so that I may see how a surveyor of truth such as yourself handles such a daunting mission that awaits you."

name: LOSTSUN_ROCK_SETTLEMENT
text: An entire Rock settlement, a remnant from before the Lost Sun's takeover of this sector, is rooted on the nearby planetoid. However that record doesn't seem like it will last long, as a Lost Sun ship is assaulting the settlement's poorly maintained defenses.

choice.text: Help the Rockmen and destroy the Lost Suns.

event.text: Not all Rockmen should be blamed for the antagony of their government. You block the Lost Suns and prepare to fight.

choice.text: Aid in the destruction of the settlement.

event.text: You approach to attack the settlement but the Lost Sun ship stops you. "Renegade, this is not a job for you. Leave this beacon so that we may carry out our duty." You fly a safe distance away before they can reinforce their words with weapons.
You try not to think of all the innocent lives that will be lost because of this attack, and try to focus on doing something aboard the ship instead.

name: DISTRESS_LOSTSUN_CIVILIAN
text: A poorly armed Union ship is stuck at this beacon, evidently out of fuel. They beg you to spare them some capsules so that they can escape the sector before a Lost Sun patrol finds them.

event.text: The Union citizens are grateful for your help.
They don't have much scrap to spare, but decide to lend some extra missiles and perform repairs to your hull.

choice.text: Tell them that you cannot help.

event.text: In a fit of pure desperation and as a last ditch attempt to save their lives, the Unionists power on their weapons and attack you.

name: DISTRESS_LOSTSUN_WRECK
text: You arrive to the location of the distress beacon, but the ship that was once here has been reduced to a singed wreck. It is impossible to discern what faction is used to belong to. You don't know what happened to their attacker, but you figure it's safe to salvage.

name: DISTRESS_LOSTSUN_COALITION
text: A Coalition ship, sent to sabotage the Lost Suns, appears to have already arrived at the location of the distress beacon. Whoever was the original source of the distress is long gone, but the Coalition doesn't intend on letting you go easily.

name: QUEST_LOSTSUN_DISRUPTION
text: A gathering of Lost Sun ships is nearby. They're suspicious of your presence and begin to distance themselves from your ship.

event.text: The Lost Suns are reluctant to respond until you show your Federation badge, which luckily seems to resonate with them. "So, eager to prove your alliance? We have a task for you, but it is of utmost importance. Are you up for a challenge?"

"At the following co-ordinates you will find a Rock comms station set up here to relay information on our revolution to the Rock Elders. We're planning an invasion on the nearby planet which also hosts a Rock settlement, but we cannot do so until the comms station is destroyed. We request that you disable it in any way you can so we can go forward with our attack."

choice.text: We cannot risk our primary mission.

event.text: "Then you already know too much." The other ships disperse while the largest of the group moves in to attack.
Once they see you too avoiding their group, the Lost Suns relax and continue their secretive discussion.

name: QUEST_LOSTSUN_DISRUPTION_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Rock comms station targeted by Lost Suns.

text: You've found the Rock comms station the Lost Suns told you about. It's very poorly armed, though you can't stage a full scale attack without the settlement dispatching reinforcements.

choice.text: Attempt to fire on the station from a distance.

event.text: Your feeble attacks are ineffective on the station, and a settlement ship is sent to chase you off. Your hull takes some damage but after you've put a good distance between yourself and the settlement the ship stops chasing you.
Your hacking is able to temporarily shut down the sensor station long enough to damage their relay systems. You hail the Lost Suns, who jump in shortly after and quickly take over the settlement.
The head Lost Sun ship thanks you for your help, and pays you.

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Prevent the station from calling for help.

event.text: You attack the station, and engage the Signal Diluter while doing so. Despite your attack being clearly noticed by the station, they appear unable to call for help before their relay systems are damaged. You hail the Lost Suns, who jump in shortly after and quickly take over the settlement.
The head Lost Sun ship thanks you for your help, and pays you.

choice.text: (Slug Saboteur) Have your Slug hack into their relay systems.

event.text: Your Slug is able to temporarily shut down the sensor station long enough to damage their relay systems. You hail the Lost Suns, who jump in shortly after and quickly take over the settlement.
The head Lost Sun ship thanks you for your help, and pays you.

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Have your Engi hack into their relay systems.

event.text: Your Engi is able to temporarily shut down the sensor station long enough to damage their relay systems. You hail the Lost Suns, who jump in shortly after and quickly take over the settlement.
The head Lost Sun ship thanks you for your help, and pays you.

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Have your Engineer hack into their relay systems.

event.text: Your Engineer is able to temporarily shut down the sensor station long enough to damage their relay systems. You hail the Lost Suns, who jump in shortly after and quickly take over the settlement.
The head Lost Sun ship thanks you for your help, and pays you.
It's too risky to attack the station. You hope the Lost Suns find a different way to complete their mission.

name: QUEST_LOSTSUN_ESCORT
text: Arriving at the beacon, you find there is already a ship here, a very poorly armed Lost Sun. They hail you. "Good, at last someone came. Our distress beacon malfunctioned and we were not sure someone "friendly" would arrive in time. Our ship ran out of ammunitions, and we had to switch to some weaker weapons. Unfortunately, this also means we cannot protect ourselves from the Theocracy and Coalition hunters. We request that you escort us to the nearest outpost."

event.text: "Your eagerness to assist us has been noted. We will follow you to these co-ordinates."
"So, the things I have heard about the Federation are true? I should've expected this. Go, leave this place and hope you do not fall victim to the same enemies that we are defenseless against."
"No, we do not need your donations or gifts. We only request an escort."
"Your eagerness to assist us has been noted. We will follow you to these co-ordinates."
"So, the things I have heard about the Federation are true? I should've expected this. Go, leave this place and hope you do not fall victim to the same enemies that we are defenseless against."

name: LOSTSUN_ESCORT_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Requested escort location of a Lost Sun vessel.

text: You arrive at the outpost, but it is too late. A large elite Rock ship has already demolished the structure. They spot you and hardly give you a chance to assess the situation before attacking.

name: LOSTSUN_ESCORT_QUEST_RAID_WIN
text: You salvage the ship. Much of the wreckage can be recovered as scrap. You offer to share the spoils with the Lost Suns, but they refuse. You salvage what you can carry before contacting them further.

event.text: "So, our outpost has been... destroyed. This was unexpected. Your aid is much appreciated Renegade, but I must ask one more favor of you. I have tried to be devoted to the Lost Sun cause, but after this tragedy... the loss of many of my friends... I see now this war of ours will lead to nothing but bloodshed. I have nothing left. May I come with you, to experience all that I would never see if I stayed here, fighting a pointless war?"
The Rockman eagerly hurries to gather his things and come aboard. He says a brief, formal farewell to his crew, wishing them luck in their future struggles.

choice.text: Sorry, but we don't need more crew.

event.text: The Rockman looks upset, but he quickly goes back to his usual formal manner. "I suppose this makes sense. You too are fighting a war as well. As promised, payment is due, even if the outcome of this mission has been a failure."

name: ENCOUNTER_LOSTSUN_SUN
text: The Lost Suns have little fear of solar flares. The captain of the ship at this beacon chuckles. "Afraid of a little fire, captain? Let us duel, TO THE DEATH!"

name: ENCOUNTER_LOSTSUN_ROCK_ASTEROID
text: This asteroid field appears to be housing a Rock spy trying to hide from the Lost Sun patrols as it collects information. They obviously aren't interested in letting you escape with their information, and attack!

event.text: You lock weapons with the Rock ship, eager to prove your loyalty to the Lost Suns. The Lost Sun ship shows no cowardice, providing support from the background.

You suppose it doesn't hurt to win the Rock's favor. Assuming you destroy the Lost Sun ship, no one will hear about your betrayal. Suprisingly, the Rock continues to provide fire support against the Lost Sun ship.

name: LOSTSUN_ROCK_CHOICE_ROCK_WIN
text: "You surprise me, Renegade. Perhaps you really do have our best interest in mind." They pay you in thanks.

name: LOSTSUN_ROCK_CHOICE_LOSTSUN_WIN
text: "Interesting. This was not the expected result. You Renegades really are the treacherous scum we have been told. Still, we are in your debt, and we intend to pay it off."

name: BOARDERS_LOSTSUN_FIRE
text: You hear the unmistakable sound of the explosion of a fire bomb and a teleporter's whirl. You aren't sure where they came from, but you have some unwelcome visitors for sure!

name: LOSTSUN_FLEET_UNLOCK1
text: A Lost Sun vessel is nearby, their captain frantically pacing back and forth. "You there- you side with the Federation? You must assist us. It is of the highest importance."

event.text: "Our leader, Admiral Ariadne's personal cruiser has been taken by Inquisition forces at these co-ordinates. You must rescue her under any conditions, or else we are doomed. The Federation is the Lost Suns' only ally, we must rely solely on your efforts for our continued survival."
The Rockman merely grunts and flies away.

name: LOSTSUN_FLEET_UNLOCK2
text: The fleet the Lost Suns mentioned isn't present at the co-ordinates they gave, but the cruiser is! The ship hails you, a gruff Rockman with a scar down his eye staring you down. "The Inquisition has recovered this vessel, and the same shall be for this entire sector. It would be wise for the Federation to cut ties with the Lost Suns and leave at once, or face the wrath of a second Inquisition. It is only a matter of time until the Theocracy rises again; which side do you want to be on?"

choice.text: You're right, the Lost Suns are a pathetic ally to the Theocracy's strength.

event.text: "So you have changed your mind so suddenly? What makes you say these words?"

choice.text: The Lost Suns are rash and violent. The Theocracy knows how to time its strikes.

event.text: The Rockman on the camera changes his composure. "You know nothing then. Too easily persuaded, an unworthy ally to the Lost Suns. Be glad you get off easy, I would much rather squish your head had I orders not to."
"THE INQUISITION HAS NEVER FAILED! We have merely... paused our efforts, until the time is right. The Coalition shall be the spark that reignites the fires of fury in our hearts."

choice.text: Spoken like a true Lost Sun.

event.text: "You dare insult the might and grace of the Elder's holy crusades? You die here!"

choice.text: This isn't a hill to die on. Leave.

name: LOSTSUN_FLEET_UNLOCK3
text: "Yes, and it is safe to say you have passed. The Lost Suns are not sparing with their alliances. If you truly represent the Federation, then you have done a good job showing your loyalty. The Theocracy will resent ever having crossed our path with you on our side."

event.text: "It would be criminal to not extend aid to you as well. I will provide you with quality military supplies to assist you. I have already begun the transfer of the blueprints for this very ship to the Federation, in hopes it will be used in their fight."

choice.text: As a matter of fact, I did overthrow the Rock government once.

event.text: Ariadne breaks into laughter, but stops. "My stars, you ARE the ship we heard about. Overthrow is hardly the word, but you have sent their homeworlds into chaos! Your efforts have been a considerable aid to ours. Allow me to help you in every way I can."

name: MILITIA_CLANSMEN
text: You receive a hail from a Slug ship hiding behind a small moon. Upon closer inspection, it's clear the ship is staffed by Slug Clansmen, belonging to the Exotic Hunter's Guild.

event.text: "A fine sssship for a Multiverssse Traveller! When we heard the Militia accepted any sssspeciesss among their ranksss, I realisssed what an excccellent opportunity it would be to go hunting! But sssince you're here, perhapsss you have some sssspecimenss to donate? We will pay very well!"

choice.text: Draw straws and give a crew to the Slugs.

event.text: The Slugs take your crew back to their ship kicking and screaming. "Thiss one will make an exccccellent trophy! Sssome ssscrap for you, good ssssir."

removeCrew.text: Though your crew will likely be dead soon, you don't think cloning them is a good idea after you just gave them up to murderous hunters.

choice.text: Somehow, the Slugs have not even realised there's no one aboard to send over to them, despite their ability to detect lifeforms...
(Clansman Crew) Claim to be hunters yourself.

event.text: "Ahh, another hunter? To think I thought I wasss the firsssst with thisss idea... Oooh, your sssship isss ssso much larger than mine. You probably have ssso much more ssssuccesss!" The Slug offers his services. Hopefully he doesn't mind hunting Rebels.

choice.text: (Improved Armories) Claim to be hunters yourself.

event.text: "Ahh, another hunter? To think I thought I wasss the firsssst with thisss idea... Oooh, your sssship isss ssso much larger than mine. You probably have ssso much more ssssuccesss!" The Slug offers his services. Hopefully he doesn't mind hunting Rebels.
You engage the Clansmen.

name: MILITIA_AUTOGRAPHS
text: In the distance is a densely populated planet under Militia control, with plenty of traffic to and from. You can likely find a market on the surface.

event.text: Near minutes after landing on the planet's surface you're swarmed by both Civilians, Federation officers, and Militia recruits. It appears they recognize you as a Multiverse Renegade, and are overtaken by stardom. Apparently it's rare to see ships like yours here.

choice.text: Ignore the fans and find a store.

event.text: You push past the crowds, apologizing to them as you go, and eventually find a market to shop at.

choice.text: Sign some autographs, but leave before the fleet can catch up.

event.text: You decide to stick around with the crowd, telling stories and signing autographs. You even receive some gifts, but eventually decide to get going before the Rebels can arrive.

choice.text: Stay back for a while with the fans.

event.text: You decide to stick around with the crowd, telling stories and signing autographs. The longer you stay the more gifts you're showered with, but eventually you have to call it quits before the Rebels can catch up any more.

choice.text: We don't need to go shopping right now.

event.text: You fly past the planet.

name: MILITIA_TEXTWALL
text: A Zoltan Peacekeeper is stationed nearby, speaking with several Militia ships. Eventually, all of the ships but the Zoltan jump away, and you receive a hail.

event.text: "Oh, hello. I am Boline, a Zoltan soldier for the Militia Corps. I've been working hard on a speech that I intend to share during the next meeting of the Galactic Union, but no one wants to listen to it or give me feedback. Would you mind if I shared them with you?"
"Wonderful! I shall now begin." Boline pulls out a massive book, slamming it down on the desk in front of her and pulls open the cover. She clears her throat, and begins to read...
"As I expected... carry on then..."

name: MILITIA_TEXTWALL_TEXT
text: "My fellow citizens of the Galactic Union, subsidiary of the United Federation and regulator of laws in Union territory, I have come to speak with you about a very important matter. Since the dawn of civilization we have been creatures bound to our weapons of war. Every race, Human, Zoltan, Aquarian, Rockman, Mantis, even Engi or Orchid, we have all waged wars not just against each other, but ourselves. It is beyond many of us, unthinkable even, to surrender these tools of destruction... nay, these evil and wicked thoughts that plague our civilizations. We say we wish to evolve, learn and grow, but how can we do this when we still hold so dear to us the ideas of revenge and hatred?"

event.text: "To emphasize my point, let me tell you all a story. Back during the infamous Mantis - Human war, a time when the seeds of thought that would grow to be the Federation had only just barely been planted, the Human people were in dire straits. The far more dangerous and warrior-like creatures that were the Mantis caused havoc among the unprepared human colonies. The Humans turned to the only allies they had at the time, the Engi, hoping for assistance. The Engi reluctantly accepted, but only in turn if the humans would liberate the slaves from the Mantis war camps. The two forces fought for years and years for control over the neighbouring planet Mars, which the Mantis had managed to secure as a stronghold and key point for planning their invasion. Rather than negotiating for a ceasefire, or surrendering, the human people continued to fight the Mantis to near extinction. The Mantis would show the humans no mercy either, and would not stop until humanity had been eradicated."

Boline clears her throat, and flips through a few pages, confused. "The uh... The Mantis are not the only violent race known to have staged such terrible wars. The Rock Inquisitions are perhaps some of the worst battles known to the galaxy. Believing themselves to be superior, the Rockmen sent forth battalions of armored ships staffed by trained soldiers known as the Crusaders to claim other territory in the name of the holy Rock Theocracy. The Chrysolic Faith that drove the Rockmen to such violence was the very same used by the Rock Elders to enslave their population through tactics of fear. Clearly an immoral action, it is known to many that the Rock dictatorship is perhaps one of the most violent and unforgiving forces in the galaxy."

"The religious persecution of the Rockmen government is not the only example of uh... of barbarianism leading to unjust treatment of other races. Going back to the Mantis, the Mantis race has for many years enslaved the Engi race for usage of their excellency at repairs. The Mantis race, due to their anatomy, are often incapable of performing precise work with electronics, though their claws have been known to function in place of screwdrivers or other tools from time to time. It is interesting to compare the differences between the two functionally opposite races. Similar duality is not often seen, though some have commented on the benefits of mixing Orchid and Rockmen crew together, due to the fire-proof nature of the Rockmen because of their hard, though not actually rock, exterior."

"However, it also stands to say that the Orchids may actually function better with the Shells, as their reliance on oxygen naturally would pair them with the plant beings. It is a scientific wonder how a single Orchid is capable of effectively replacing a Life Support system for extended periods of time. Many biologists, many of which coincidentally also happen to be Shells, have attempted to study Orchid biology. For those of you who might not be aware, the Shell race has placed a heavy focus on scientific study, even occasionally abducting tourists or visiting ships to run quick, albeit painless, tests. This has led to many cultural misunderstandings with the less understanding species, such as the Rockmen or Mantis. The Slugs also have a particular interest in the Shells, though not for any innocent reasons. A clan of Slug hobbyists known as the Exotic Hunters Guild has formed, whose specific purpose is to hunt rare or sapient creatures. The Shells are their prime targets, because of their armored abilities."

"Frighteningly, the attacks led by the EHG, that being the aforementioned Exotic Hunters Guild for any of those not paying attention, are near synonymous with the earlier but still relatively recent series of conflicts known as the Slug Expansion Wars. I'm sure many of you here are already aware of the history of the Slug Expansion Wars, but I will share a brief summary of the conflicts for those of you who aren't."

Boline licks the page and flips to the next. She coughs slightly, pounds on her chest, and continues to read. "Starting after the Rebellion's rise to power, the Federation forces were dedicated to clearing out Rebel ships from their territory. This left much of space unprotected from invaders. The Slugs, who had previously been shunned from the Federation for their traitorous nature, took notice to this pattern and began planning a mass migration to new territory. Though they started with nebulous sectors, they soon found themselves courageous enough to attack clear sectors, sometimes even already occupied space. This came to cause issues when the Slugs dared invade Mantis and Rock space, much to the reasonable displeasure of those governments. Both the Hive and Elders declared war on the Slugs, and so they fought for several years. Eventually, the Slugs surrendered and offered back territory. They didn't stop there however, and even offered some of their original territory up as well. This eventually evolved into an alliance that we have come to know as the Coalition."
"This lack of Federation protection over Union space also led to the rise of the Militia. However, I will spare you all this tale, as I know everyone here is for certain familiar with the story."

"I WILL however tell the story of the Coalition, in case you might not be aware. The Coalition is a truce between the Sethnian Kleptocracy, the Urtharean Theocracy, the Yeitiiik Hive, and the Eargen Republic. These 4 races are perhaps some of the most hostile and deadly in the galaxy, and this alliance has caused fear for both the Federation and Rebellion. The Coalition continues to grow in power, and even occupies several of its own sectors. The Coalition has also taken usage of Slug Cealaforming tech, a method of transporting nebulous gases to create artificial nebulas. Though these fake clouds are incapable of forming into stars, they still cause sensors to malfunction and can even generate the same electrical currents as ion storms, a deepspace hazard I'm sure any pilots here are definitely familiar with if you've ever been to a nebula sector."

"Cealaforming is not the only unique tech developed by the Slugs however. Many Slugs take use of Anti-Bio weaponry, which often used to be confused with Particle tech because of their similar orange colors, at least before Anti-Bio weaponry was transitioned to pink. Particle tech was actually developed by the Zoltan race on accident in junction with The Zufquair Corporation. Uh... wait no, that's spelled wrong."

"Wait... is it Zluficar? Zultifigar? I know it starts with a Z..." Boline flips back through her text, searching for something. "Ah, I spelled it right here. Zulfiqar, that's it. Now, where was I... Oh, damn I lost my page. Do you uh, do you want me to start again?"
Boline awaits your response.
"Ok, if you say so!" Boline flips back to page one. "From the top then."
"Oh, ok. Fair enough!" Boline flips the book closed. "Thanks for listening that far at least. So uh, what did you think?"

"Really? You liked it? Amazing! Thank you so much for your feedback. Oh man, no one has ever said anything nice about my speech before, not even my own crew! Hey uh, what if I joined yours? You seem much nicer, and maybe with your encouragement I can even finish this draft in time to present it!"

choice.text: Dear god that was the biggest waste of time in my life.

event.text: Boline looks down at her feet in shame. "Oh... ok." She cuts comms. You probably didn't have to be so rude, but at least you don't have to listen to her ramble any longer.
Boline awaits your response.

"Seriously? Again? I've read my speech to you 5 times already! Are you... making fun of me? Dude, not cool!" Seems you've really tipped her over the edge, because now Boline's weapons have come online!
"Oh, ok. Fair enough!" Boline flips the book closed. "Thanks for listening that far at least. So uh, what did you think?"

"Really? You liked it? Amazing! Thank you so much for your feedback. Oh man, no one has ever said anything nice about my speech before, not even my own crew! Hey uh, what if I joined yours? You seem much nicer, and maybe with your encouragement I can even finish this draft in time to present it!"

choice.text: Dear god that was the biggest waste of time in my life.

event.text: Boline looks down at her feet in shame. "Oh... ok." She cuts comms. You probably didn't have to be so rude, but at least you don't have to listen to her ramble any longer.
You power up the weapons and attack the Militiamen.
You fly past the Militia vessel.

name: MILITIA_DEPOT
text: You spot a nearby Militia station. It seems to be offering supplies to travellers.

choice.text: Submit your ID and get some supplies.
Attack, surely we can get more from them!

event.text: You power up the weapons and attack the Militiamen.
You ignore the Militia station.

name: MILITIA_TRAINEES
text: A Militia training exercise appears to be going down at this beacon. Fortunately, they aren't aiming to kill and are a safe distance away from the beacon.

choice.text: Hail and see if you can get involved.

event.text: The leading commander of the squad responds. "You want to participate in the training? Go ahead - damaging the hull is fine, BUT! Don't mortally wound our rookies. We're reluctantly willing to... tolerate slip-ups if Clone Bays are involved, but regardless it'd be best if you exercised restraint. We'll end the exercise after 60 seconds."
On second thought, participating in this might not be a great idea.

tooltip.text: The training exercise will end in this much time. Make sure not to kill anyone until then!

event.text: There's nothing of use here - you move on.

name: MILITIA_TRAINEES_KILL
text: Seems you accidentally took the training too far, and now there's blood on your hands. It takes a moment for the other ships to realize what's happening, but as soon as they find out you've killed their friends, they immediately abandon the exercise and fire at you. Your hull takes some damage, but you're able to fly away in time.

name: MILITIA_TRAINEES_WIN
text: The commander contacts you in person once the other ships disperse. "Thank you for your help! These are some of our newest recruits, they have little experience in actual combat. I'm sure going up against an actual Multiverse Renegade was quite the experience for them! I don't have much supplies to give you, but here's a combat augment we use for training, maybe you can find use in it."

name: MILITIA_RECRUITMENT
text: A Rebel ship has docked with a Militia recruitment center stationed at this beacon. Quick scans show the Rebels have taken the Militiamen hostage.

event.text: You power up the weapons and attack the Rebels.

choice.text: Contact the Rebels; try to talk them out of it.
(Upg. Cloaking) Cloak and scrap some of the Rebel ships while they're aboard.

event.text: With the Rebels occupied, there's no one around to guard their ships. Under the veil of your cloak you tear off some of the plating and leave quickly.

choice.text: (Monk Crew) Shame the Rebels for their violent ways.

event.text: Your Monk spends the next 30 minutes insulting the Rebels for their barbaric ways, attacking men only doing their duty by defending civilians. The Rebels are so ashamed of themselves several crumple to the floor sobbing. One particularly moved individual offers to join your crew, and the rest agree to leave the Militiamen alone.

choice.text: (Improved Armories) Arm the crew and board.

event.text: Seeing your crew armed to the teeth immediately puts the Rebels into panic, as they seemingly only expected underpaid Militia vessels to try and rescue the station. They surrender and let the Militiamen free. Most stay behind to handle the Rebels, but one soldier wishes to join you!
You fly past the Militia center. Hopefully, the situation will be resolved... no thanks to you.

name: MILITIA_COCKY_ZOLTAN
text: A flotilla of Zoltan vessels is present at this beacon - they seem to be performing training drills related to the endurance of their Super Shields. One ship among the group hails you: "Uh. Renegades, here? Not a common sight in Militia space. You know, you really stand out from the rest of the ships in this sector..."

event.text:
"I mean, your cobbled-up and makeshift tech! Have you no shame, comparing your Federation to our orderly discipline and advanced shield technology? It's no wonder the Union calls for our help. This might be advertised as a 'joint effort', but it really falls upon us to give the local inhabitants safety, seeing as they fell behind on the technological spectrum."
				
				Overhearing the conversation, the commander of the squadron pitches in to save face. "Quit pestering the Renegade. You have not yet seen what the rest of the galaxy has to offer. Such naivete could lead to your downfall!"

choice.text: Point out the inadequacies of the Super Shield.

event.text: You explain that their shield can easily be downed in a reasonable amount of time through specific weaponry fit for such, and throw in the fact that overconfidence, just like their famed Super Shield, cannot guarantee their safety from whatever the greater galaxy holds. Agitated by this comeback, the rookie defies orders to stand down, and attacks you! The commander pleads to avoid unnecessary bloodshed, but it looks like you'll have to make use of some force to discourage your attacker.
You proudly display your weapons to the Zoltan rookie, and they awestruck at the sight. The commander thanks you for clearing the haughtiness of his subordinate and offers a reward.
You proudly display your Artillery to the Zoltan rookie, and they awestruck at the sight. The commander thanks you for clearing the haughtiness of his subordinate and offers a reward.

choice.text: (Upg. Drone Control) Show that you're not so behind on the technological curve.

event.text: You proudly display your sophisticated drone technology, taking the rookie by surprise. The commander thanks you for clearing the haughtiness of his subordinate and offers a reward.

choice.text: (Energy Shield) Show that you're not so behind on the technological curve.

event.text: You proudly display your own Super Shield, taking the rookie by surprise. The commander thanks you for clearing the haughtiness of his subordinate and offers a reward.

choice.text: (Shield Bypass + Bomb) Demonstrate a gap in his protection. [-1}]

event.text: You teleport a payload right in their weapon system, taking the rookie by surprise. He promptly hails you - "Bah, we never expected you Renegades to be such... assholes!" The commander offers you a reward, supposedly for showing his men how to improve, but you suspect the real motive is to avoid any further escalation and get you to leave.

choice.text: (Bypass + Teleporter) Overtake his crew before they can respond.

event.text: You teleport a boarding party through and wipe them out with ease, showing that the haughtiness of the now dead rookie was unfounded. You begin to recover some scrap, but the commander rushes to the scene to stop you!

choice.text: Ignore the arrogant Zoltan and dedicate time to doing something else.

event.text: You didn't ask for anyone's opinion, so it's only fair to tune them out.

name: DISTRESS_MILITIA_KERNELS
text: The source of the distress beacon appears to be an Orchid merchant under attack by a pirate vessel! Should we assist?

event.text: You power up the weapons and engage the pirate vessel.
Orchid ships are considerably well armed, so you hope that they'll be able to save themselves.

name: MILITIA_KERNELS_SAVE
text: The Orchids thank you for your assistance. They explain that they were sent to sell their Kernel weapons to the Militia vessels in this sector. As payment for your help, they offer one for free.

name: DISTRESS_MILITIA_OUTPOST
text: The distress beacon's source is a small Militia outpost under attack by pirates. The Militiamen don't appear to be holding out well.

event.text: You power up the weapons and engage the pirate vessel.
"Hey, who the hell do you think you are- oh crap. Okay okay you win, have fun!" The pirate jumps away. The fatigued Militia station seems defenseless against anything you might try.
"Thank you, it was unlikely we'd have survived that pirate attack otherwise. We cannot offer much other than some fuel that we don't need."

choice.text: Demand they surrender one of their crew as a slave.

event.text: The Militiamen have few options but to give in to your demands.

choice.text: Destroy the station and loot the remains.

event.text: As you expected, the Militia outpost barely defends itself and is destroyed quickly.
You decide not to fight the pirates.

name: MILITIA_AUTOSEARCH
text: You notice two Militia ships nearby squabbling over something. You aren't sure what without listening closer, but it seems to pertain to Auto-ships.

event.text: "Huh? Oh, I didn't notice there was another ship here. We're discussing the possibility of constructing our own fleet of Militia Auto-ships to reduce the number of casualties on the front-lines. But before we can consider, we need to capture one of the Rebel Auto-ships to study. Could you do us a favor and hunt one of them down?"

"Excellent. We've attached the co-ordinates of the ship we'd like to study, but it's located too close to an ASB. If you could lure it away without causing too much damage we'll be able to send in a ship to collect it."
"Oh my, this is marvelous! This will help speed up our development greatly."

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Have your engineer transfer Auto-ship data.

event.text: "Oh my, this is marvelous! This will help speed up our development greatly."

choice.text: (Cognitive Crew) Have your Cognitive transfer Auto-ship data.

event.text: "Oh my, this is marvelous! This will help speed up our development greatly."
"Understandable. Good luck with whatever mission you're on then."

choice.text: We have more important things to do than eavesdropping.

event.text: Whatever they're talking about, it doesn't matter to you. You ignore the Militia ships.

name: MILITIA_AUTOSEARCH_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Militiamen have asked you to bait out an Auto-ship for study.

text: You've discovered the Automated vessel mentioned by the Militiamen. In the distance you can see the ASB satellite swerving towards you.

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Disable the satellite's targeting systems.

event.text: The satellite stops turning immediately, unable to detect your location anymore. You'll still have to lure away the Auto, but now you can do so without the added risk of the ASB.

You launch several flares close to the satellite, confusing its targeting system. Considering how small the discs are you doubt the satellite will be able to destroy them easily, giving you enough time to lure away this ship.
Just as the militiamen warned, the ASB locks onto your precise location and begins firing immediately. Hopefully we don't take too much damage before the Auto flees.

name: MILITIA_AUTOSEARCH_LURE
text: You've successfully lured the Auto-ship away from the beacon. You prepare to follow the ship to its next destination.

name: MILITIA_AUTOSEARCH_QUEST_2

unvisitedTooltip.text: Coords of the lured Auto-ship.

text: You have tracked down the Auto-ship once again. Nearby are the Militia vessels from earlier, already inspecting the Auto-ship.

event.text: "Ah, very good job. The ship is still in working condition, marvelous! Here is your pay, of course."

As you prepare to leave, you overhear shouting from the Militiamen. You turn around to see the Auto-ship has activated once again, and blasts one of the Militia ships to destruction! It moves on to attack you next.

choice.text: (Upg. Hacking) Disable the Auto-ship before it can cause more damage.

event.text: You shut down the Auto-ship immediately. The crew of the destroyed ship evacuate immediately, and only a few lives are lost. The Militiamen thank you.

name: ENCOUNTER_MILITIA_STATION_MISTAKE
text: You run into a Militia station near this beacon, who refuses to let you past. Apparently this beacon requires a toll to pass through.

event.text: The Militia station wastes no time with conversation - the second you refuse their weapons come online!
The Militia station collects the payment and allows you to continue.

name: ENCOUNTER_MILITIA_ESCORT
text: The ruins of what was once a Militia transport drift nearby. A Militia escort, their crew confused and afraid, mistake you for the attackers and prepare to defend themselves! You try to hail them but they won't respond, and it looks like the only way out of this is with a fight.

name: ENCOUNTER_MILITIA_ELITE
text: The vessels of the Elite Defense Cadre are some of the deadliest in the Militia fleet, and for good reason. Boasting highly trained crew, these ships don't mess around in combat. Unfortunately for you, the ship here deems you a threat and attacks!

name: MILITIA_DETECTIVE
text: There appears to be several Militia ships docked around a nearby civilian refuelling station.

event.text: One of the militiamen tries to protest as you dock with the station, but they are cut off by a human clad in a green outfit smoking from a small wooden pipe of Old-Earth design. "Ah, a Renegade, eh? I am Sherlock Haynes. I hail from Earth, though I have since joined the Militia myself. Now I work as a detective for the Militia, but I have been presented by a rather troublesome case. Perhaps you might help?"

"With the mystery of course! Last night, in this very station, a man by the name of Henry Coleman was shot and killed. We suspect he held vital information regarding a Rebel plot, but we aren't sure what. There were only 4 individuals staffing this station, and after this crime now there remains only 3. No ships docked with this station for a full 24 hours before and after the murder, which can mean only one thing!"

"Why, it's elementary my dear... uh, whatever your name is. This means that one of these 3 survivors must be a Rebel spy! The question is, which one could it be? Will you help me, my reality jumping friend, and solve this case?"

"Ah, most excellent! I haven't done much digging yet, but if you need any help just come and talk with me. Here are the three suspects, Mr. Thom Nicholson, Ms. Amy Sheppard, and Dr. Daniel Browne. I look forward to your hypothesis!"
"Ah, too bad. Better go then, I can't have any distractions while I investigate."

Haynes, aboard the other station, receives the hail, only to stare in shock at a mirror image of himself on the other end. "Me, listen. It was Thom. He used the Anti-Personel drone, shot Henry. Both of them are Rebel spies. He learned how to use the Drone Control from Daniel. No time to waste, Rebel attack imminent. Get the picture? Good. Hop aboard, we have a hangar to save."
Clearly something important has happened here, but it does not pertain to you.

name: DETECTIVE_EVIDENCE_MENU
text:
You stand in the station's lobby, observing your surroundings.
	[You will be able to investigate as many times as you want in whatever order you want.]

choice.text: Speak to Sherlock or one of the suspects.

event.text: Who do you want to talk to?
The station has several systems on board. Which do you want to look at?

Sherlock raises an eyebrow. "So, you have come to a conclusion? Who shot ol' Henry?"
			[You will only be able to accuse suspects that you have talked to]

choice.text: None of them killed Henry personally. It was the drone who fired the fatal shot!
Er, nevermind. I need to keep investigating.

event.text: Sherlock chuckles. "Well alright then. Take your time, one can never be too careful about something like this."

name: DETECTIVE_CORPSE
text: You walk over to Henry's corpse. You notice no obvious cuts on the body, though there is a large burn mark on his back. This must have been from blaster fire, but the radius of the wound is too large to have been from a standard hand-held blaster.

name: DETECTIVE_ACCUSE_SHERLOCK
text: You take a long step towards the suspects, then swivel around and point a finger right at Sherlock. "You uh, you're accusing me? You do realize I haven't even been on this station before this day, right?"

choice.text: Sounds exactly like what a killer would say!
Sounds exactly like what a killer would say!

event.text: Sherlock folds his arms and glares at you. "You storm in here, spit on the faces of all my suspects, and then accuse ME of the crime? Get out. Get out right now. You are deranged. This is what I get for trusting a Renegade to handle serious business like this."

name: DETECTIVE_ACCUSE_DRONE
text: Sherlock looks as surprised as the rest of the suspects. "The drone, huh? An interesting theory indeed! But one catch - someone had to have been controlling the drone. Which one was it?"

event.text: Daniel looks shocked that you blamed this on him. Sherlock nods. "Yes, Dr. Browne is the head engineer here, which would make him an excellent suspect. HOWEVER, he could not have done it! If you checked the Oxygen system, then interviewed Daniel about it, you would know he was busy last night performing upgrades. He would not have been able to murder Henry AND upgrade the system at the same time, the Oxygen upgrade simply takes too long."

choice.text: You've already found a solid alibi for Daniel. You know it cannot be him.

event.text: Amy's scowl grows even darker. Sherlock shakes his head. "No, Ms. Sheppard could not have done it. She has no experience with the Drone system, it is too unlikely that she would have been capable of operating a drone long enough to kill Henry."
Thom's eyes go wide. "W-what? No, it can't be me! I don't know a thing about drones!" His easy going country accent suddenly disappears and his voice becomes uneasy.

Sherlock cocks his head. You explain how Thom actually got lessons from Daniel on how to operate drones, not too long before the murder as well. Sherlock contemplates this for a moment. "You're right. Goodness, even I did not catch that!"

Sherlock nods. "Yes, Mr. Thom is right. It was Daniel who was the head engineer on this facility, not Thom. It is too unlikely that Thom would have been able to operate the drone long enough to kill Henry."
Sherlock scowls. "You can't come in here making wild theories if you can't even say who did it! Keep looking."

name: DETECTIVE_ACCUSE_THOM
text: Thom's eyes go wide at your accusation. Sherlock gets up from his spot and walks over to you. "An interesting hypothesis indeed. However, if you inspected the wounds on Henry, you would notice a blaster could not have been the weapon used. Mr. Nicholson only owns a standard grade defense pistol. The only thing on this station capable of leaving such a mark was the Anti-Personnel drone, and Mr. Nicholson has no experience with operating drone systems."

choice.text: Indeed, the drone was instrumental for the murder. And who ordered it to kill Henry? Thom!

event.text: "W-what? No, it can't be me! I don't know a thing about drones!" His easy going country accent suddenly disappears and his voice becomes uneasy.

Sherlock cocks his head. You explain how Thom actually got lessons from Daniel on how to operate drones, not too long before the murder as well. Sherlock contemplates this for a moment. "You're right. Goodness, even I did not catch that!"

Sherlock nods. "Yes, Mr. Thom is right. It was Daniel who was the head engineer on this facility, not Thom. It is too unlikely that Thom would have been able to operate the drone long enough to kill Henry."

name: DETECTIVE_ACCUSE_AMY
text: Amy glares at you. Sherlock gets up from his spot and walks over to you. "An interesting hypothesis indeed. However, if you inspected the wounds on Henry, you would notice a blaster could not have been the weapon used. Ms. Sheppard only owns a standard grade defense pistol. The only thing on this station capable of leaving such a mark was the Anti-Personnel drone, and Ms. Sheppard has no experience with operating drone systems."

name: DETECTIVE_ACCUSE_DANIEL
text: Daniel looks offended that you would accuse him. Sherlock gets up from his spot and walks over to you. "An interesting hypothesis indeed. However, Daniel was busy on the night of the murder. If you inspected the Oxygen system, then interviewed Dr. Browne, you would know that he was busy all night long upgrading the system. This would not have left him with enough time to also have overriden the Drone Control and killed Henry."

name: DETECTIVE_WRONG
text: Suddenly, the lights go out, and blaster fire rings out through the room! When the lights come back on, the suspects and back up reinforcements have already fled. Sherlock shouts at you. "Damn it! Now the real suspect has gotten away! Run, it is no longer safe here with a killer on the loose!" Moreover, you return to find an emitter tapped onto your ship that broadcasted your location to the Rebel fleet, likely installed by the culprit in their escape. You must hurry up!

name: DETECTIVE_TALK_THOM
text: What do you want to ask Thom?

event.text: Thom explains some basic details about his life. He used to be a farmhand on a small terrestrial planet before a Rock Crusader set fire to his town. With nowhere else to go, he decided to join the Militia and protect civilian space so such a thing could never happen to anyone else.

choice.text: Ask if Thom has any connections with the Rebels.

event.text: Thom shakes his head. "N-no sir. I've met plenty of Rebels in my time, but I've never been friends with any. I've always been a Federation citizen, and a loyal one at that."

choice.text: Ask Thom about his job on the station.

event.text: "I manage the essential systems. Back on the farm I had to learn how to operate various equipment, and it's incredible how much that knowledge translates to managing a station! I help with upkeep for the shields and life support, and I buy new parts at the store whenever something is broken."
"I've never actually talked with Henry much. He was always so quiet and reserved. Still, it's so strange to think he's dead..."

choice.text: Ask Thom about the other suspects.

event.text: Which suspect do you want to ask Thom about?

"Amy? She's uh, she's something I guess. She's always yapping at us, and she has the shortest temper I've ever seen. She does a good job though, and I wouldn't ever think she'd be capable of murder! Though, she never did like Henry."
"Dr. Browne? Oh he's such a kind old man, and dedicated to his work too. I can imagine he's quite shocked about the murder, he was always so close to poor Henry..."
For no reason in particular, you decide to spit at Thom. Sherlock glares at you but says nothing.

What evidence do you want to ask Thom about?
			[As you investigate more clues or evidence, more options will appear here]

choice.text: Ask Thom about the Drone system.

event.text: "Nope, never had the head for any of that drone stuff. I trust Doctor Browne for that kind of stuff, because I can't even figure out how to turn the drones on in the first place!"

choice.text: Call Thom out on his lie.
Ask Thom about the Sensor system.

event.text: "No recordings? That sounds problematic. You are a detective though, so surely you can figure this out without them, right?"

choice.text: Ask Thom about the Oxygen system.

event.text: "Oh, that's rather odd. That wasn't me who upgraded the system. I was busy last night during the murder, and I haven't had time to check it since. But I do know it was only level 1 the day before."

name: DETECTIVE_TALK_THOM_LIE
text: You point out Daniel's mention to Thom learning about how to operate the drones. Thom stutters, not sure what to say. You don't push further but take note of this.

name: DETECTIVE_TALK_AMY
text: What do you want to ask Amy?

event.text: Amy doesn't have a lot to share about why she joined the Militia. She thought it would be a good way to escape from her home planet and maybe kill some pirates.

choice.text: Ask if Amy has any connections with the Rebels.

event.text: Amy looks as if she's about to slap you, and probably would if it wouldn't end with her dead. "How dare you associate me with those crapstains! I ain't never been a Rebel, and I never will be. End of story."

choice.text: Ask Amy about her job on the station.

event.text: "Used to work as border patrol, until we got that god damn Anti-Personnel drone. I used to kick pirates in the teeth almost daily, but now I've been resigned to that damn weapons room pressing buttons all day long!"

"Henry? Hah, half the time I didn't even realize he was here. What a weirdo, always spending so much time resigned to that room of his, only coming out for food or water. Him being dead won't change nothin' about life on this station, which is a shame. It's so god damn boring here."

choice.text: Ask Amy about the other suspects.

event.text: Which suspect do you want to ask Amy about?

"Thom's such a pushover. He's always blabbering on about how nice life is here. There ain't nothing good about living on this station, I tell you! Still... Thom killing someone? Unthinkable... unless he's a really good actor, at least."
"That old man? He looks like he's about to turn to dust any second! I always thought he was as lacking a personality as the drones he works on. Maybe that's why he got along so well with Henry."
For no reason in particular, you decide to spit at Amy. Sherlock glares at you but says nothing.

What evidence do you want to ask Amy about?
[As you investigate more clues or evidence, more options will appear here]

choice.text: Ask Amy about the Drone system.

event.text: "The drones? Never touched them. That damn robot stole my job at killing pirates. If I WAS a murderer, I would have gone for the Anti-Person drone instead of Henry. Damn robots can't feel pain anyways..."

choice.text: Ask Amy about the Sensor system.

event.text: "Guess you got no recordings then, or whatever. Aren't detectives supposed to be able to figure things out without recordings anyways? I don't know what you want me to tell you about it."

choice.text: Ask Amy about the Oxygen system.

event.text: "I don't know nothin' about the life support. That's all Thom's doing, not mine."

name: DETECTIVE_TALK_DANIEL
text: What do you want to ask Daniel?

event.text: "Me? I'm just an old fart. Studied drone tech for several years, got a job at Arcadia as an Engineer until I eventually retired. But... I guess retirement just isn't for me, so I signed up for the Militia instead of wasting away in some beach home."

choice.text: Ask if Daniel has any connections with the Rebels.

event.text: Daniel looks down at his feet. "Never been a Rebel, but I did have an experience with them. Back when I worked at Arcadia, I was put in charge of the CICA project. That's the Central Intelligence Combat Assistant, though it's more often referred to as the Free Roamer accident. This was the AI used by the Rebels to construct their automated fleet, but we never expected that they would use it for such evil. After I realized how my tech had been used, I resigned immediately."

choice.text: Ask Daniel about his job on the station.

event.text: "I'm the shipboard Engineer. After I finally talked the others into installing a dronebay and Anti-Person drone, I've been running maintenance on them ever since."

"Oh, poor old Henry. He was such a nice man. I used to eat lunch in his quarters. It's a shame the others never got to know him, because Henry was always so reserved. Oh Henry, how could this have happened to you..."

choice.text: Ask Daniel about the other suspects.

event.text: Which suspect do you want to ask Daniel about?

"Thom is a nice man. I was never as close to him as Henry, but we talked quite a bit, and he has always been a happy fellow. Recently, Thom took a particular interest in the drone system and asked me for help with operating the drones! He's learning pretty quick, but I think he might just be learning to give me something to do. I always wanted to have a student..."

"I wish I had her energy, I was never that amped up even when I was younger. Shame she wastes it all on shouting at us. Thank goodness she spends most of her time complaining to herself while she mans the weapons. I don't like to point fingers, but if any of us 3 were to go so low as to kill someone, I'd say she would probably be my guess..."
For no reason in particular, you decide to spit at Daniel. Sherlock glares at you but says nothing.

What evidence do you want to ask Daniel about?
			[As you investigate more clues or evidence, more options will appear here]

choice.text: Ask Daniel about the Drone system.
Ask Daniel about the Sensor system.

event.text: "The sensors are no longer functional? Oh dear, that's quite unfortunate. Surely even without the recordings though, there is some way to catch the person behind this!"

choice.text: Ask Daniel about the Oxygen system.

name: DETECTIVE_TALK_DANIEL_EVIDENCE_OXYGEN
text: "Oh yes, that was my doing actually! Thom normally works on the essential systems, but last night he was busy working with the drones and I had nothing to do. So, I decided to put my old bones to use and upgrade the oxygen. H..Henry was always complaining about the bad ventilation..."

name: DETECTIVE_TALK_DANIEL_EVIDENCE_DRONE
text: "Oh yes, of course! No ship or station is complete until its been outfitted with drone tech. I spend most of my time working with the system, though Thom has also been spending a fair bit of time in there as well after he asked me for lessons with operating the drones."

name: DETECTIVE_SYSTEM_DOORS
text: You inspect the door system. It appears some work has been done on the blast doors to improve them, though it matters little in this case. All of the suspects and the victim are registered in the system database, so any of them can go wherever they please.

name: DETECTIVE_SYSTEM_DRONES
text: You take a look at the dronebay. Though there aren't too many schematics on the station's computers, you notice an Anti-Personnel drone and a standard issue Combat Drone.

event.text: The combat schematic appears to only have been used a total of 3 times since the system was purchased. Further data suggests it merely came with the system purchase.

The computers inform you the Anti-Personnel drone has been used a total of 38 times since its purchase, though that's not surprising. With the influx of pirates in this sector, the number of boarders this station must see is unfavourably high.

name: DETECTIVE_DRONE_CANNON
text: You inspect the Anti-Personnel Drone's laser. To your surprise, the arm-mounted cannon appears to be much stronger than a standard defense blaster, and certainly capable of leaving a burn mark the same size as the one on Henry's corpse!

name: DETECTIVE_SYSTEM_SHIELDS
text: You inspect the shields system. Everything here seems to be perfectly functional, and nothing is out of the ordinary.

name: DETECTIVE_SYSTEM_OXYGEN
text: You inspect the oxygen system. The system appears to be running at a higher level than usual, and is in pristine condition. From the looks of it, the system was upgraded very recently.

name: DETECTIVE_SYSTEM_SENSORS
text: You inspect the sensors system. It appears someone has sabotaged the computers, and deleted all of the recordings from the night of the murder! There's nothing else here of use, but someone had to have done this...

name: DETECTIVE_SYSTEM_WEAPONS
text: You inspect the weapons system. Several trinkets lay around the room, as well as a small bag with Amy's name on it. This must be her usual station.

name: DETECTIVE_CORRECT
text: Thom realizes he's been caught. Desperately, he fumbles to grab his blaster but is shot in the knee by Sherlock. The other Militiamen run to handcuff him and escort Amy and Daniel to safety. Sherlock holsters his gun and thanks you. "Good work! Now, time we learn what this is all about."

event.text: Thom is tied up to a chair in an empty room aboard Sherlock's ship. Sherlock paces back and forth. "So, you're the Rebel spy?" Thom shakes in his chair, trying to loosen the ropes. Eventually, he gives up. "You don't understand! Everyone I knew, my family, my friends, they were all killed by the Rockmen! Is there any better proof that alien life is a threat to mankind? And during that attack, where was the Federation? Is the Federation really that great when they can't even protect their own citizens!"

Sherlock sits down in the chair on the opposite side of the room and crosses his legs. "So, you joined the Rebellion for revenge?" Thom nods. "The Rebellion offers a chance at the galaxy that the Federation could never give us! The galaxy that humanity deserves!"
Sherlock scoffs. "Alright, hold on the manifesto. All we care about is the information you tried so hard to prevent from getting out." Thom gulps. "I won't tell!"

You slap Thom across the face. "O-ok I'll talk! I was just a dormant agent sent to watch the sector. For a while now the Rebellion has been planning to invade this sector and lay siege to the Militia's hangars and armories, and today that plan is about to be carried out! Aboard the same station I was stationed at was Henry, another undercover Rebel spy. However, he grew too attached to that old man Browne, and when he learned the invasion would put everyone here - even the doctor - at risk, he got weak and was going to snitch. I secured the safety of the Rebellion by killing that coward!"

"Yeah, a real job securing them you did just now, blabbering all their secrets." Sherlock motions for one of the Militia guards to gag Thom and remove him from the room. "Damn it, if his intel's any good then we have a serious situation on our hands. We need to head to the central hangar and alert the General about this, quickly! Your ship seems a lot faster than mine, so I hope you don't mind if I catch a ride."

name: DETECTIVE_HANGARATTACK

unvisitedTooltip.text: The Militia's hangar.

visitedTooltip.text: Visited location.

text: It appears you're too late. Already, it seems the Rebels have begun the invasion. In the distance is a massive Militia ship firing on its own men, which can mean only one thing. The Rebels have already captured the ship, and are using it to lead their attack!

choice.text: Hail the Militiamen and ask if you can assist.

event.text: The Militia general responds. "Yes, for god sake we need any help we can get! A couple Rebel ships got in before we could raise the shield generator, but it's up now. Unfortunately, the Rebels have caused critical damage and that damn Dreadnaught is about to finish it off. We only have so long until the shield falls and we're all doomed! If we can destroy that Dreadnaught - or capture it - we might be able to repair the shield generator and keep the Rebel fleet away!"
You power up the thrusters and intercept the ship as it fires on the generator. Better make this quick!
Fighting a ship like that with a time limit isn't something you're eager to do. You power up the engines and ready to leave this place as soon as possible.
No way in hell you're fighting that thing. You evacuate as soon as possible.

name: DETECTIVE_HANGARATTACK_FAILURE
text: From behind you erupts a massive explosion, as a blue ball of light engulfs the massive shield generator and reduces the entire complex to ash! You've failed, and now that the shield is down the Dreadnaught jumps away and the Rebel fleet floods in.

event.text: You manage to evade most of the ships, but your hull catches several missiles and a nearby Dropship beams some soldiers aboard. Still, this could have ended a lot worse... Though this looks bleak for the survival of the Militia.

name: DETECTIVE_HANGARATTACK_DESTROY
text: Without the Dreadnaught to destroy the generator, the fleet stuck within the shield is rendered useless. They're swiftly overtaken by Militia reinforcements, and a team of engineers goes to work on fixing the damage immediately. The Rebel fleet arrives only to find no way into the hangar. They fire pointlessly on the shields but soon realize their efforts are futile.

event.text: The Militia General thanks you. "Had it not been for you, this building would probably be a crater in the ground by now. We cannot repay you enough for your assistance here, but we can certainly try." The Militia transfers over some supplies, and offers a blueprint for one of their ships to aid the Federation.

name: DETECTIVE_HANGARATTACK_DEADCREW
text: Without the Dreadnaught to destroy the generator, the fleet stuck within the shield is rendered useless. They're swiftly overtaken by Militia reinforcements, and a team of engineers goes to work on fixing the damage immediately. The Rebel fleet arrives only to find no way into the hangar. They fire pointlessly on the shields but soon realize their efforts are futile.

event.text: The Militia General thanks you. "Had it not been for you, this building would probably be a crater in the ground by now. We cannot repay you enough for your assistance here, but we can certainly try." The Militia transfers over some supplies, and offers a blueprint for one of their ships to aid the Federation.

tooltip.text: The shield reactor will be disabled in this amount of time. Be sure to defeat the Dreadnaught before the time runs out.

destroyed.text: The Dreadnaught explodes, scattering the area below in debris, even taking out a few ships on the way down. Fortunately, the generator takes little damage from the explosion.

deadCrew.text: The Dreadnaught has been emptied of crew. The ship falls back down to the surface of the planet, taking out several ships on its way. Fortunately, the generator takes little damage from the impact.

name: ZOLTAN_FASCISM
text: A few smouldering wrecks nearby are being observed by a Zoltan vessel, whose captain is speaking on open comms. At first you think he's blindly talking to himself until you realize he's speaking to you. "Damn Duskbringers, so much pointless bloodshed. This is all the fault of humanity, infecting this galaxy with their diseased ideologies like fascism. If it wasn't for the Rebellion, never would such sinister thoughts have reached our peaceful race."

event.text: "Oh but it is! It's an ideology born out of the stomach, used by jingoists and fake patriots alike to line pockets with war-time economy and supress free speech. It is a mockery of intellectualism and a cog in the eugenics machine." This guy isn't wrong, but the way he speaks makes you realize he may be a bit delusional.

choice.text: If you hate fascists, maybe you can help us with the Rebels?

event.text: The Zoltan mumbles something to himself. "Fighting the Rebellion is a futile effort. The disease of fascism has already infected the galaxy, and there's no cure. But you seem young and hopeful. Perhaps a new generation of right-minded individuals can rectify the course of our politics." The Zoltan sends some equipment your way. "I've been holding onto this since the Civil War. I'm not a soldier anymore, I don't need it. Take it, and send the fascists packing!"

Your crew starts asking the Zoltan various questions, trying to probe for tell-tale signs of mental instability. The conclusion seems to be he's experiencing early cognitive decay, a rare malfunction in Zoltan chassis that can cause erratic thought patterns and irregular speech. However, trying to convince him to find a hospital only seems to confuse him more. Strangely, he thinks you're asking him for a reactor tune-up, and agrees.

choice.text: (Human Crew) Apologise for being solely responsible for inventing fascism.

event.text: The Zoltan nods. "Humanity is a species of nothing but pestilent ideas, fermented with political turmoil and selfishness. You have forever ruined this galaxy with partisan concepts like 'democracy' and 'feminism'. It disgusts me. We were once a pure race, until we came into contact with yours. It is known that humans are a warlike race who can only be controlled by manipulating their even greater greed. Take this, and never return." It's clear this guy is delusional, but you don't mind free scrap.

name: ZOLTAN_FREE_AUGMENT_MV
