text: A Zoltan academy sits docked just outside the beacon perimeter. They're happy to show you the fruits of their labor, and offer something to take home with you.

name: ZOLTAN_FREE_MAP_MV
text: The Zoltans stationed near this beacon are happy to receive you. As they give you the formal tour of their ship you spy some local star charts and mentally log the details.

event.text: Their crew is astonished by your sudden attitude shift, but they won't back down from this aggression.

name: ZOLTAN_TRADE_HUB_MV
text: You come to a Zoltan trade and supply hub - everything the weary traveler needs, provided they have the right documentation.

choice.text: Try to talk your way in.
(Teleporter) Beam directly to the civilian deck.

event.text: You re-materialize in a dark corner of the main concourse and are able to conduct your investigations in peace.

choice.text: (Central Teleport) Beam directly to the civilian deck.

event.text: You re-materialize in a dark corner of the main concourse and are able to conduct your investigations in peace.

choice.text: (Ministry Crew) Present official documentation and pay the entry fee.

event.text: They scan ID that declares your crewmember an official citizen, collect their fee, and let you pass.
You don't have the papers - well, the neuro-laced identity bracelets - to get in, so best not to try.

name: ZOLTAN_FIGHTER_MONK
text: It's risky business being a slaver in Zoltan space, but it appears one soul is daring enough to run his trade here. Not exactly commendable, but still a rare sight.

choice.text: See who they might have on sale.

event.text: "Feds, eh? You look like a fellow who could use a fighter with a little extra bit'a... umph, if you get me. For quite the modest fee, how does a masterful Zoltan warrior sounds to join the ranks of your crew?"

You hand over your scrap to the slavers, but they don't return with the slave promised. You begin to suspect something might be wrong, until they inevitably stumble out carting with them a Zoltan wrapped in a brown robe.

They violently toss the Zoltan onto your floor and apologize, then walk off. You inspect the Zoltan, only to realize they're a pacifist monk! The Zoltan explains their situation, "I was once a trained Zoltan warrior, but I eventually saw the light and joined the Monks, but not long after I was abducted by these men. You have saved me from slavery, and I shall now serve you. As ironic as that sounds."
The Ministry would not appreciate the presence of slavers within their territory. You arm your weapons and approach with hostile intent.
Eventually, the slavers jump away. They surely can't afford to set up their business without getting caught by the Ministry's enforcers.

name: ZOLTAN_ODD_MOON_MV
text: Something strikes you as odd about a moon in the distance.

event.text: You try not to fixate on the moon in the aft scanner as you set the coordinates for the next jump.

choice.text: (Boarding Drone) Send a drone to probe the surface.

event.text: Initial scans indicate a network of caves not far underground. You launch a boarding drone and it breaks through the surface into the cavern below.

Your drone discovers a vast cave network and evidence of excavation. Buried deep below you find a Zoltan scientist, still hard at work. He tells you that all his colleagues are long dead. You decide not to ask questions and offer to let him join your crew.

name: ZOLTAN_CREW_SCAN_MV
text: You arrive at a Zoltan security checkpoint set up in a perimeter around the beacon. "Travelling vessel, you will submit to crew profiling to identify fugitives of the empire."

choice.text: You don't have time for this nonsense. Attack!

event.text: Expecting resistance, their Energy Shield is raised and ready for combat.
The process turns out to be really quick, considering you have no one aboard. So quick infact, that you still have time to do something onboard.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug talk them into letting you go.

event.text: You give the guards permission to dock with the ship, but before they come on board your crewmember slowly advances to meet them. As far as you can tell no words were exchanged, but the guards offer you some supplies and say the ship checks out. Best to not ask questions.

choice.text: (Zoltan Crew) Have your Zoltan talk them into letting you go.

event.text: Your Zoltan talks to the guards in great lengths about the majesty of the Zoltan empire. Convinced that you're nothing more than do-gooders, they let you past.

choice.text: (Mind Control) Make the guards believe they have already checked your crew today.

event.text: The captain of the guard appears on the vid screen "Back so soon friend! Well, no need to waste your time further. Here, take these spare fuel canisters and get on with your mission." Your ship is cleared to pass.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Make the guards believe they have already checked your crew today.

event.text: The captain of the guard appears on the vid screen "Back so soon friend! Well, no need to waste your time further. Here, take these spare fuel canisters and get on with your mission." Your ship is cleared to pass.

name: ZOLTAN_SCIENCE_DOCK_MV
text: What appears to be a Zoltan science ship requests permission to dock.

event.text: They leave without a word.

name: ZOLTAN_LIFERAFT_MV
text: You pick up a Zoltan life raft floating in space. Its inhabitant asks you to retake his ship from the pirates who recently commandeered it. "I'm certain it is clear," he concludes, "that you must not destroy my vessel in the process."

event.text: You focus your fire on the pirates.
You refuse to get his ship back, but still offer to drop him off at the next station. The Zoltan is displeased, but directs you to a nearby starbase just the same.

name: ZOLTAN_TOURIST
text: It appears a civilian ship is under attack by a Zoltan ship! You aren't sure why, but it looks like they need help.

event.text: You give the Zoltan ship no choice but to fight you as you fly towards it full speed.

choice.text: (Peacekeeper Crew) Demand the Zoltans back down.

event.text: Your Peacekeeper cites Ministry law C-T-55 from the Ministry codex, saying that they have no right to attack civilian ships without sufficient reason or permission from a higher authority. As no Zoltan, dead or alive, is said to have full knowledge of the entire codex, the other ship has no grounds to deny the existance of said law. They back down and jump away.
Eventually the civilians are chased out of range, and you are left alone.

name: ZOLTAN_TICKET
text: Not long after you jump in a Zoltan Automated vessel hails you. "You are in direct violation of protocol-S36-T by exceeding the weight limit for Cruiser class vehicles in this zone. Your fine equates to: 10 scrap."

choice.text: Hell no, fight past the ship.

event.text: "Hostile actions registered. Preparing to defend."

choice.text: (Mafan) Debate the fine with the Auto.

event.text: "Protocol-S36-T doesn't apply here, this ship has an MV drive! You'd use an S36-T-MV form to calculate the ship's new weight limits, then add a deduction factor for the personal carrying allotment of each crew member. Then factor in the fee waivers for our sub-category as a science vessel due to my presence..." You're reasonably certain Mafan could go on all day, but a circuit blows somewhere in the Zoltan ship while it tries to follow Mafan's logic, causing the ship to explode violently!
"Fine has been paid. Have a nice day."

name: ZOLTAN_FREEMANTIS_FRIENDLY
text: The Free Mantis and Zoltan don't get along well, so it's concerning to see a Free Mantis ship so far into Zoltan space. A ship from the peacekeeper border police has docked with a massive Free Mantis ship, which can't mean anything good.

choice.text: Board as well and see what's happening.

event.text: You step into the ship only to find a Peacekeeper violently kicking a defenseless Free Mantis warlord on the ground, who is desperately screaming "Stop, stop! I not wanting violence, only friendlyness!", but the Zoltan won't listen.

choice.text: Pull the Zoltan off of the Free Mantis.

event.text: You grab at the Zoltan, pulling them away from the Free Mantis. They shove you away, shouting "What the hell are you doing? All your precious Federation can do now is interfere with foreign matters, isn't that so? I'll put you in your god damn place!" The Zoltan gives orders for his men to attack!

choice.text: Try to reason with the Zoltan.

event.text: You try to reason with the Peacekeeper, but it only infuriates them further. "The Federation should know their place, instead of always interfering with foreign matters. Maybe the Duskbringers are right, and all of you filth deserve to die." The Peacekeeper gives orders for his men to attack!

choice.text: (Ministry Crew) Have your Zoltan reason with them.

event.text: It only takes a single shot to erase the peace-keeper from existence. You help the Free Mantis to their feet. "Thanking you very much Federation, we come here only make friends, but Zoltan not trust us. Me coming with you, much friendlier."
There's no way you're messing with the Zoltan border police in the Zoltan Capital.

name: ZOLTAN_FREEMANTIS_FRIENDLY_REASON_ZOLTAN
text:
"What are you doing? Is this really keeping the peace? The Ministry stands for lawful justice, and yet here you are attacking a defenseless Mantis! Is this what you signed up to the force for?"
		
The Peacekeeper falters for a moment. "I- don't try and get involved in things that have nothing to do with you, Federation!" The Zoltan begins to say more, but is immediately sliced in twain by the Free Mantis, who crawled off the floor while the Zoltan was distracted. You hurry back to the ship before the Peacekeeper ship notices something is wrong, but it's too late. You escape from the ship, but a team of Zoltans beam aboard your ship!

name: ZOLTAN_REVOLT
text: Despite the arrogant nature of the Zoltans regarding their supposedly superior government, many of their kind are dissatisfied with the strict and controlling Zoltan Peace-Keepers instated to, as their name would suggest, 'keep the peace'. It appears a full on riot has started on the nearby planet.

choice.text: Pull closer to survey the chaos.

event.text: It seems the conflict was incited by a Duskbringer soldier giving a rather motivating speech, which inevitably resulted in complete and utter destruction, as civilians overturn Peace-Keeper ground vehicles and orbital satellites open fire on crowds of innocent people trying to flee for their life.

choice.text: Take part in the battle - help the Zoltan civilians.

event.text: You've made up your mind to help the civilians. You attack one of the Peace-Keeper vessels.

choice.text: Take part in the battle - help the Peace-Keepers.

event.text: You've made up your mind to help the Peace-Keepers. You attack one of the Duskbringer vessels.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Cloak and loot some of the buildings while everyone is distracted.

event.text: You swoop down to collect some supplies as quickly as possible before leaving.

choice.text: This isn't our business, ignore them.

event.text: It's not your duty to get involved in the business of everyone else you encounter. You ignore the chaos below.

name: DISTRESS_ZOLTAN_MANTIS_MV
text: Your jump interrupts a Zoltan security ship as it follows a Mantis pirate into an asteroid field. They message you, "Your presence here will continue to be tolerated - but please, do not interfere."

choice.text: Interfere and save the Mantis ship.

event.text: Sometimes you have to bet on the underdog - even on the rare occasions that the underdog is a Mantis warship. You set off for the heart of the asteroid field and engage the Zoltan there.

choice.text: Interfere and help the Zoltan ship.

event.text: You overtake the Zoltans and catch up with the Mantis ship in the asteroid belt. Time to make some friends.
The Zoltans know their business better than most - best to leave them to it. You prepare to jump.

name: DISTRESS_ZOLTAN_HUSK_MV
text: You arrive to find a lumbering Zoltan freighter with no one at the helm. It's a mystery what happened to the crew, but it'd be a shame to let the opportunity go to waste.

name: DISTRESS_REFUGEE_ZOLTAN_MV
text: You have encountered a refugee ship drifting in space. It looks as if it was fleeing the Rebel advance and ran out of fuel. Its distress beacon is active, but you're not sure anyone is on board.

event.text: You're wary of the refugees but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: DISTRESS_ZOLTAN_ARREST
text: It appears a pirate ship here is under arrest by a Zoltan ship. They've secretly activated the distress beacon, and have sent you a short message saying "help".

choice.text: Assist the pirates and attack the Zoltans.

event.text: You arm the weapons and engage the Zoltan vessel.

choice.text: Report the pirates to the Zoltans.

event.text: The Zoltans gruffly thank you and give you some fuel, then go back to dealing with the pirates.
The pirates send you no future messages and are all brought aboard the Zoltan ship, which jumps away shortly after.

name: DISTRESS_ZOLTAN_RAID
text: A Zoltan Peace Brigade is under heavy fire at this beacon by a battalion of Rebel fighters. The distress beacon comes from the commanding ship. They appear to be too busy to notice you.

event.text: It's hard to hear the Zoltan commander over the sounds of gunfire on their ship. "What?! Oh, you've come to provide assistance? We need all the help we can, there's numerous Rebel ships attacking this system! If you're going to help, be quick about it!"

choice.text: Attack one of the smaller Rebel ships.

event.text: Several Rebel ships are scattered around the perimeter, swooping in to assist their comrades when necessary. You pick a ship at random and attack.

choice.text: Take on one of the Elite ships.

event.text: The burden of the attack is being carried out by Elite vessels. You intercept one of them and attack.

choice.text: Take on the ship leading the squadron.

event.text: A powerful MFK Ace is leading the Rebels. If you can destroy it, the Zoltans might be able to win this battle.

name: CAPITAL_RAID_BORING_WIN
text: You salvage the remains of the Rebel ship while the battle rages on in the distance.

event.text: The Zoltans are too busy dealing with the conflict to reward you, so you decide it's a good time to leave before another Rebel ship attacks you.

name: CAPITAL_RAID_ELITE_WIN
text: You salvage the remains of the Elite Rebel ship while the battle rages on in the distance.

event.text: The Zoltans are too busy dealing with the conflict to reward you, so you decide it's a good time to leave before another Rebel ship attacks you.

name: CAPITAL_RAID_SELITE_WIN
text: The MFK Ace has been neutralized. You salvage the remains of the ship.

event.text: Around you the battle begins to die down. The Rebels, watching you defeat their leader, reconsider and begin to jump away. In a matter of minutes the Zoltan forces go from near defeat to conclusive victory.
"You have saved us from a terrible defeat. We are grateful for your assistance. Allow me to repay our debt to you."

name: ZOLTAN_LAWBOOK
text: A Zoltan peacekeeper is straggling behind its assigned fleet at this beacon, looking for something. They hail you quickly, asking if you can do them a favor.

event.text: "I would not normally ask a stranger of this, but we have found ourselves in a very unfortunate position. We have lost our book of law, a utility required for all Zoltan peacekeepers to have on them at all times. We will not be permitted back into our fleet until we find it... or someone else finds it for us. Would you be willing to track it down? We will give the co-ordinates of one of the positions we suspect it may be in."
The Zoltan transmit the suspected location of their lawbook.

choice.text: No thanks, we aren't looking for any side jobs or mercenary work.

event.text: The Zoltan begin to protest but give up and go back to searching.

name: ZOLTAN_QUEST_LAWBOOK_PIRATE

unvisitedTooltip.text: Presumed location of a lost Zoltan law book.

text: At the suspected location of the lawbook you find a smuggler ship. "Ah, I see you've been sent to collect this little book here. Thing is, we could sell this for a giant price as an artifact on the black market. So, if you want it back, you're gonna have to pay us."

event.text: It's one hell of a ripoff, but you're willing to do it if it means you don't have to fight the smugglers.
You aren't paying for the damn book. You'll just take it from them.
"Alright, alright! I'll lower the price. But only this once!"
It's one hell of a ripoff, but you're willing to do it if it means you don't have to fight the smugglers.
You aren't paying for the damn book. You'll just take it from them.
The Smugglers don't attempt to negotiate further.

name: ZOLTAN_QUEST_LAWBOOK_DUSKBRINGER

unvisitedTooltip.text: Presumed location of a lost Zoltan law book.

text: You notice a Duskbringer ship collecting the lawbook from a pirate vessel. You'll likely have to fight them for it if you want it back.

event.text: You prepare to engage the Duskbringer ship.
You aren't interested in fighting the Duskbringer ship.

name: ZOLTAN_QUEST_LAWBOOK_ENGI

unvisitedTooltip.text: Presumed location of a lost Zoltan law book.

text: An Engi ship at this beacon is sitting dormant. You hail it, asking if it has seen the lost law book. "Bound paper object of conduction code has been found. Intentions: keep book safe until owner returns."

choice.text: Tell the Engi that the Zoltans sent you.

event.text: "Likelihood of Zoltans sending Federation ship to retrieve Law Book... favorable." They send over the book.
You prepare to engage the Engi ship.
The law book is likely safe with the Engi. Hopefully, the Zoltans return here to find the Engi and get the book back.

name: ZOLTAN_QUEST_LAWBOOK_OBTAIN
text: Now that you have the lawbook, you can head back to the location of the Zoltan ship.

name: ZOLTAN_QUEST_LAWBOOK_RETURN

unvisitedTooltip.text: Return the lost law book here.

text: You've found the Zoltan ship again. You send over the law book, for which they are extremely grateful. They give you an augment and some supplies.

name: ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE
text: To your surprise, this beacon is inhabited by a Lanius vessel! They don't attack, but instead send you a message.

event.text: "Offer asking. Green! Force want. Core Zoltan collect, bring us." It's hard to understand, but after further discussion it seems the Lanius are interested in the Zoltan shields on this sector's inhabitants, and are asking you for a favor. Capture a Zoltan ship and bring to the Lanius their shield's core, and they will pay you.
"Greater. Location sending." The Lanius attach the co-ordinates of the ship they are wanting the core from.
If the Lanius aren't going to attack, then you will!

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_REGULAR

unvisitedTooltip.text: Tracked location of a Zoltan shield core.

text: The co-ordinates have led you to a regular Zoltan ship. If you want the core, you'll have to clear them of inhabitants first.

event.text: You arm the weapons and approach the Zoltan ship.

choice.text: These Zoltans haven't done anything to us, leave them alone.

event.text: You decide not to fight the Zoltans.

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_STATION

unvisitedTooltip.text: Tracked location of a Zoltan shield core.

text: The co-ordinates have led you to a regular Zoltan station. If you want the core, you'll have to clear them of inhabitants first.

event.text: You arm the weapons and approach the Zoltan station.

choice.text: These Zoltans haven't done anything to us, leave them alone.

event.text: You decide not to fight the Zoltans.

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_DUSKBRINGER

unvisitedTooltip.text: Tracked location of a Zoltan shield core.

text: The co-ordinates have led you to a Duskbringer vessel! They immediately detect that you are a Federation ship and attack. You'll have to fight them either way, but if you want the core you'll have to kill their crew.

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_MONK

unvisitedTooltip.text: Tracked location of a Zoltan shield core.

text: The co-ordinates have led you to a Zoltan Monk! They hail you: "The stars have told us you would come here, in search of the heart that powers our ship. If you wish to take it, you must test your mind."

event.text: The Monks lead you to a room shrouded in complete darkness, and lock the door. You wait inside for several hours completely alone. Right when you think you are about to go insane, you drift into a deep sleep. When you awake, you are back on the ship with a monk and the core!

choice.text: (Monk Crew) Negotiate with them for the core.

event.text: Your Monk crew member seems to have been able to convince the others to give you their core.
You arm the weapons and approach the Monk ship. However, it seems the Monks are trying to escape!

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_AUTO

unvisitedTooltip.text: Tracked location of a Zoltan shield core.

text: The co-ordinates have led you to an automated Zoltan ship. It seems to be in rest mode, so maybe you can stealthily extract the core?

choice.text: (Hacking) Hack the Auto-ship to keep it offline.

event.text: It appears you are successful! The Auto-ship remains offline.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Cloak the ship while extracting the core.

event.text: It appears you are successful! The Auto-ship remains offline.
You decide not to attempt to extract the core from the Zoltan Auto-ship.

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_OBTAIN
text: You observe the core. Now that it has been removed from the ship you can't seem to tell how to reverse engineer it, but you assume the Lanius are aware of that and know how to fix it. However... you might be able to use this to upgrade your regular shields.

choice.text: Bring the core to the Lanius for your reward.

event.text: You contact the Lanius and get their new co-ordinates.

choice.text: Dismantle the core and use it to upgrade your shields.

event.text: You won't be able to get your reward now, but your shield system is running better than ever.

name: QUEST_ZOLTAN_LANIUS_CORE_FINISH

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of the Lanius ship awaiting the shield core you retrieved.

text: You deliver the core to the Lanius ship. "Favor am glad. Bits are belonging you." They transfer over some supplies and offer to trade further.

name: ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_ASTEROID
text: You arrive in an asteroid field and are greeted by a Zoltan guard. "By attempting to access these closed mining fields, you are in violation of the Natural Mineral Protection Act. Your weaponry will be confiscated for processing." You don't have time for this.

name: ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_AUTO_SUN
text: A Zoltan Automated ship appears to be in charging mode near this sun, probably harvesting the solar energy! However, it appears you arrive just in time for it to re-activate, and the ship somehow identifies you as a threat.

name: ENCOUNTER_MANTIS_ZOLTAN
text: You pick up the last broadcast from a rupturing Zoltan freighter: "The Mantis, they're here, please-" You're interrupted by fire off the port bow!

name: ENCOUNTER_ENGI_ZOLTAN
text: You jump into a debris field that used to be a Zoltan cruiser. Unfortunately, its Engi escort takes you for the attacker and retaliates! They refuse all hails.

name: ZOLTAN_MALFUNCTION_INTERROGATE
text: As you arrive at this beacon, the nearby Ministry Auto-ship sparks. "Warning - this space is off limits - ERROR - explanation not found. Sabotage suspected. Engaging self-defense."

name: ZOLTAN_MALFUNCTION_INTERROGATE_SELF_DEFENSE
text: "Aha! I knew it. You did something bad, didn't you? Don't try to deny it. You did something bad and it caught you, so you had to blow it up." No matter how you try to explain, the Zoltan doesn't accept your other explanations. It's likely that this incident will be reported.

name: ZOLTAN_MALFUNCTION_INTERROGATE_MALFUNCTION
text: "Oh really? And where is your proof of this? It seems that all evidence has been conveniently destroyed."

choice.text: (Upg. Sensors) Our ships sensors have a log of the incident.

event.text: The Zoltan looks intently at the logs. "This checks out. Well, in that case, I guess what you did was justified. We'll patch up your ship to offset whatever damage might have been caused."

choice.text: (Ministry Crew) "The ship was experiencing error 632. It must not have received the most recent firmware update."

event.text: The Zoltan thinks about it for a moment. "That explanation is reasonable, I don't think we did update the firmware. In that case, I guess what you did was justified. We'll patch up your ship to offset whatever damage might have been caused."
"I didn't think so. I'll let you go for now, but don't think we'll forget this."

name: ZOLTAN_MALFUNCTION_INTERROGATE_ATTACKED
text: "Ah, now we're getting somewhere. So you expect us to believe it attacked you for no reason? That doesn't make any sense."

choice.text: It must have been malfunctioning or something.
If anyone has been wronged here, it's us. We should be interrogating you!

event.text: "So it's our word against yours, then? Well, I don't think we're getting anywhere, so I'll let you off. Maybe it was a malfunction or something. The thing didn't always work right anyway."

name: NEBULA_ZOLTAN_BATTLEFIELD
text: This nebula looks like it's recently seen two ships exchange fire... with mutually-assured destructive results. Wreckage drifts by your screens and tumbles into the depths of the nebula to be lost to sight. It's hard to determine who the combatants were without closer investigation.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Ask your Slug crew to scan for survivors.

event.text: Despite the destruction filling the system, your crewman is able to pick up the faint thoughts of a life form in the debris - it looks like they won't last much longer without help.

choice.text: Leave the battlefield before other ships arrive.

event.text: You take leave from the battlefield.

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Ask your Shell crew to scan for survivors.

event.text: Despite the destruction filling the system, your crewman is able to pick up the faint thoughts of a life form in the debris - it looks like they won't last much longer without help.

choice.text: Leave the battlefield before other ships arrive.

event.text: You take leave from the battlefield.

choice.text: Leave the battlefield before other ships arrive.

event.text: You take leave from the battlefield.

name: BATTLEFIELD_SURVIVOR
text: Your bring the survivor aboard, but discover their wounds are severe. They won't live much longer.

choice.text: Make them comfortable for their final moments.

event.text: On their death bed, they croak out a series of coordinates and beg you to go there - when you attempt to ask them why, the survivor simply says, "ABADOTH" and perishes.

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay) Get them into the medbay!

event.text: Using your upgraded medical bay, you are able to heal the survivor's wounds and they recover quickly. Grateful to be saved, they offer to join your crew and help however they can.

choice.text: (Clone Bay) Try to clone them before it's too late.

event.text: You clone the individual and let the host pass away. The clone decides to join you - although it has little choice in the matter.

choice.text: (Medical Crew) Have your crew treat them.

event.text: You have your crewmember treat the survivor, and after a tense few moments they successfully nurse them back to good health. Grateful to be saved, they offer to join your crew and help however they can.

choice.text: (Medical Drone) Have your drone treat them.

event.text: You have your drone treat the survivor, and it quickly helps them recover. Grateful to be saved, they offer to join your crew and help however they can.

choice.text: (Healing Bomb) Use your Heal Bomb on them. [-1}]

event.text: Your bomb proves effective at healing the survivor's wounds, and they recover quickly. Grateful to be saved, they offer to join your crew and help however they can.

name: SECRET_WORD_ABADOTH_MV

unvisitedTooltip.text: Mysterious coordinates provided by a deceased crewman.

text: You have arrived at the coordinates given to you by the dead crewman you attempted to save. There doesn't seem to be anything here - no planets, no vessels, and no clue as to what he meant by sending you here.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Ask your Slug crewmember to scan for life forms.
(Telepathic Shell) Ask your Shell crewmember to scan for life forms.
Do a full system scan - though you're sure to lose some of your lead with the Rebels.

event.text: You start the arduous task of a full system scan. This better be worth it.
You have no clue what this was all about, but you decide to not waste any further time to it.

name: SECRET_WORD_ABADOTH_CONCLUSION_MV
text: Suddenly, a Zoltan ship appears seemingly from out of nowhere! "We insist you provide the reason for being here, or face grave consequences."

choice.text: Explain about finding the dead crewman.

event.text: There is a moment of silence, and suddenly the Zoltan ship powers weapons - must have been the wrong word to use... now you've got a fight on your hands!

Your Engi crewman easily recalls the phrase the deadman used from its memory banks. There is a moment of silence, and the ship's captain solemnly thanks you for the information. He wishes you well on your journey, and he offers several upgrades to assist you in exchange for your service to the Zoltan race.

Your Cognitive easily recalls the phrase the deadman used from its memory banks. There is a moment of silence, and the ship's captain solemnly thanks you for the information. He wishes you well on your journey, and he offers several upgrades to assist you in exchange for your service to the Zoltan race.
There is a moment of silence, and suddenly the Zoltan ship powers weapons - must have been the wrong word to use... now you've got a fight on your hands!

There is a moment of silence, and the ship's captain solemnly thanks you for the information. He wishes you well on your journey, and he offers several upgrades to assist you in exchange for your service to the Zoltan race.
There is a moment of silence, and suddenly the Zoltan ship powers weapons - must have been the wrong word to use... now you've got a fight on your hands!

name: NEBULA_ZOLTAN_STUDY
text: You arrive at a Zoltan research facility. They say they are researching genetic distortion due to stasis sleep and prolonged FTL travel. They ask if your crew has the time to undergo a few scans.

event.text: "Alright. Fly safe." You prepare to leave.

choice.text: (Adv. Medbay) Give them your medical records.

event.text: "Thank you! We didn't expect to receive such a significant amount of data regarding your crew's health during FTL travel. Please, accept this for your trouble."

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Request an exchange with the Zoltan science team.

event.text: Overjoyed to come across this opportunity after having remained in Shell space for so long, your Shell has many subjects to discuss, most of which are beyond your understanding. Following a long debate and brainstorming sessions with the Zoltans, they finally are able to return to you, and offer a drone schematic in thanks.

choice.text: (Hibernating Alien) Ask if they know what to do with this.

event.text: "Interesting... I have never seen a creature like this. I'm afraid there's not much we can do with it; its current state is unrelated to stasis sleep. However, with a catalyst, such as quantum fuel, you may be able to awaken it again?"

name: NEBULA_ZOLTAN_ROCK
text: This nebula turns out to be the hiding place of a terrified Rock crew taking refuge from the Zoltan border police. They don't seem prepared to risk your leaving with their co-ordinates, and open fire!

name: NEBULA_STORM_ZOLTAN_SUPPLY
text: You spy two pirate ships lurking in the nebula here. They remain unaware of your presence; you're able to get your scanners to at least identify their cargo: one is carrying the fuel supplies, the other the ammunition. They begin to drift away from each other in the storm.

event.text: You jet toward the pirate with the fuel supplies and engage - hopefully you can leave the ship in one piece!
You jet toward the pirate with the ammunition and engage - hopefully you can leave the ship in one piece!
Sometimes discretion is the better part of valor.

name: ENCOUNTER_ZOLTAN_ELITE
text: Though not all Zoltans choose to align with the extreme views of the Duskbringers, that doesn't mean they all appreciate the Federation. A particularly annoyed Zoltan Elite appears to be fed up with tolerating Federation ships and has decided to attack.

name: CAPITAL_OSMIA_RAID
text: At first, you assume the nearby planet isn't anything important - until your Atlas informs you this is actually the location of the Zoltan Capital! Usually these places are better marked, but Ministry government buildings are rarely seen as tourist attractions. You expected the capital to be on the Zoltan Homeworlds, Osmia, but this most certainly isn't any such place.

event.text: As soon as you approach, it's clear something is eerily wrong. There is barely any activity on the streets near the massive capitol building, and you swear you see several armed patrols stationed outside. Your descent is met with a warning; "Unregistered foreign vessel - desist at once and leave this zone. This is not a time for complacent intervention from reckless third parties."

choice.text: We aren't a reckless third party - we're Federation.

event.text: "I understand that. My statement still stands. This is a matter of importance for the Ministry and the Ministry alone. Now beat it."

choice.text: (Ministry Crew) Talk them into allowing you to assist.
(Harmony Crew) Talk them into allowing you to assist.
(Zoltan Shield) Convince them you are a Zoltan ship.

event.text: The Zoltan doesn't bother speaking to you, instead calling on his radio for backup in dispersing you!

choice.text: It seems there's no convincing these guys.

event.text: You have no interest in bothering the Zoltan citizens or sight seeing.

name: OSMIA_RAID_ASSIST
text: "It seems I have misevaluated your aptitude. I am Allta Foleck, regent and speaker on behalf of Minister Lumei who is not present at this time. As you perhaps have noticed, the capitol has been evacuated, and the city is under lockdown in face of an impending terrorist attack."

event.text: Allta hesitates, but eventually responds: "Not quite. We believe they are a more radical, religious sect of the Duskbringers, almost cult like. They have donned masks of hideous three-eyed beasts and wear sacrificial robes, and their only goal is the total annihilation of the Ministry. We have received news that their forces will be arriving soon and they must be apprehended. Death is the only suitable consequence for these acts of terror."

choice.text: Agree to stay and help fight the terrorists.

event.text: Not too long later, you catch sight of the first of the terrorist vessels approaching. A decently sized cruiser vessel and very well armed, it looks like this is your chance to earn the Ministry's favor.

choice.text: Yeah uh, have fun dealing with those guys. We're out of here.

name: OSMIA_RAID_ESCAPE
text: It seems that, having gotten so low on crew, the ship is now attempting to flee. You don't see this kind of behavior often, but you receive word from Allta. "Do not let that ship escape! We must ensure the terrorists cannot regroup!"

choice.text: (Adv. Navigation) Suggest allowing the ship to escape and track its movements.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Suggest allowing the ship to escape and track its movements.
(Adv. Sensors) Suggest allowing the ship to escape and track its movements.

name: OSMIA_RAID_ESCAPE_OFFER
text: "Absolutely not! You are under direct orders to keep firing on that ship until they are dead! Do NOT attempt to follow them, they are dangerous and must be stopped!"

name: OSMIA_GOTAWAY
text: The terrorist ship jumps away. You can tell Allta is mad, but he manages to maintain his professional composure despite his wavering voice. "Very well then. This is not the most optimal outcome, but... we can make do with this. The capital has been saved, thanks to your efforts. Heheh..."

choice.text: Grab the coordinates of the terrorist ship's new location first.

event.text: While you speak further with Allta, you proceed to discreetly download the trajectory and coordinates of the strange Zoltan ship. You aren't sure where this will lead, but clearly there's something there the Ministry doesn't want anyone near.

name: OSMIA_RAID_WIN
text: You can't help but notice no other ships were present during the attack, and the Zoltan military forces were... very reserved in that they refused to assist you in the fight. Strange, but Allta appears once again to commemorate you. "I think it goes without saying that without your help, we would not have been able to survive that attack. Allow me to show my generosity to both you and the Federation. Now, feel free to carry on with your mission. I would hate to steal any more of your time." You aren't sure where this sudden attitude shift came from, but as promised Allta does deliver a rather large reward, including ship blueprints for a Zoltan cruiser!

choice.text: We have some questions left to ask.

name: OSMIA_RAID_QUESTIONS
text: "Oh? Questions? I'm a very busy man I'm afraid. I'll try to entertain your thoughts, but I cannot stick around for long."

choice.text: Why did none of the other ships help us?

event.text: "We could see that you had the situation under control. With ships as deadly as theirs, we were not willing to risk our more valuable security teams unless necessary. Many citizens and ground patrols were not given full information on the events that were to transpire to ensure there would be no hysteria. That is all, I hope you were not offended."

choice.text: Why were there no other ships attacking?

event.text: "It would seem that we were largely misinformed on the scale of the attack. You see, informants can't get everything right all of the time... With this vessel dealt with, I am certain the terrorists will hesitate before making future attacks, but should we ever need help in the future, I suppose we know who to call... Heheh..."

choice.text: Why were those terrorists' masks so realistic?

event.text: "What reasonable man could try and justify the absurd efforts of mentally unstable zealots? Their dedication to their craft is, as some would say, remarkable, but I would sooner call it disturbing. Never fear though, those ghastly creatures are just the same as any Zoltan, and thank goodness for it!"

"Good, good. You are a very curious individual I see. I appreciate your drive to know more about the galaxy around you, but I must warn you. Try not to go sticking your nose into business you have no part in the future, okay? Bye bye!" Allta immediately hangs up from the call, and an escort is dispatched to ensure you have a 'safe flight' as you leave the capital.

name: OSMIA_UNLOCK_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of the terrorists.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: As soon as you arrive at the location of the terrorists you're taken aback by the location on your Atlas. THIS is Osmia, homeworld of the Zoltan race. Unlike the capital, which at least had a minor indicator of importance upon arrival, Osmia has no such fanfare. How has the Ministry kept an entire planet hidden from the rest of the Federation - and more importantly, why?

event.text: As you follow the coordinates closer to the surface you can see the planet has seen much better days. Similar to most of the homeworlds of galactic empires, it lays in a state of mass disarray, but this is much different. Vegetation is completely absent from almost half of the planet, and that where it can be found it grows erratically. Ancient craters decorate the surface and near them is large amounts of radioactivity. You steer clear of the dead-zones and approach a massive elevated city suspended by several large towers. This is no ruin however - it's bustling with activity.

Suddenly, you're stopped by the same ship as before. Their dialect is strange, though close enough to modern Zoltan that your translator fills in the gaps easily. "Please tell us you have not come to finish us off! Whatever the Ministry has told you is a lie! Please, you must understand, we aren't a threat!"

choice.text: You attacked the capital - that seems pretty threatening.

event.text: "Look, let me explain! I am Malki, and we are the Osmians. We are not terrorists, I can promise you. We are the last of the few non-transformants that the Ministry could not reach. If you care, I can start from the beginning and explain everything. But I believe you might be of a great help to my people, if you're willing."

choice.text: We're in a bit of a hurry here.

event.text: You ignore the protests of Malki and silence the ship before moving in to attack.

name: OSMIA_UNLOCK_EXPLANATION
text: "Okay, okay. Look, why don't we both power down our weapons and meet face to face? If you came this far, you're certainly looking for answers." Reluctantly, you agree and you land your ship near a frozen lake. Malki dismounts from his vessel, revealing himself to look the same as the creatures from before.

choice.text: The Ministry said you were disguised Duskbringers.

event.text: "I'm afraid that's a lie. One of many. As you can see, we are not Zoltans in the same sense that you know. Long long before the Federation, all of us Zoltans looked this way. Back then, we were steaming ahead full force into the interstellar era, driven to be the first of many competing nations. But this competition turned to travesty, and nuclear holocaust became imminent. Osmia was annihilated, and the survivors were forced to flee the planet. For almost centuries Osmia was out of our reach, a solemn reminder of our failure."

"The lost explorers roamed the surrounding nebula, unable to settle for long without devolving into war once again. However, in those mysterious clouds they found something. At the center of the infamous Great Eye nebula was a monolith that held immense, god-like power. The Zoltans came to worship it, and so it brought them unity. This gave birth to the Illesctrian faith and the Ministry who sought to uphold this new peace. The Ministry, however, was brutal with its enforcement, and to justify its cruelty the leadership constructed an ever-large and rapidly expanding codex of laws no man nor army could ever memorize. Through force they assimilated every last Zoltan colony."

choice.text: But what happened? Why are the Zoltans hard-light now?

event.text: "Yes, see, the Great Eye also brought with it the discovery of other, similar tech. Aether, a highly conductive and resistant metal alloy used to forge the ruins around the Eye could be used to create sustainable hard-light generators. This tech enticed the Ministry's top scientists, who saw it as a solution for the Osmia crisis alongside various other tech. Though Aether was used to construct most of Zoltan kind's most infamous technology like our special shields, we also used it to create new part-organic part-mechanical forms to explore Osmia with. This was a success and the explorers were revered as heroes, and many flocked back to recolonize the planet. The current Minister at the time only lived for a little longer until he succumbed to a natural death and was replaced by the new Minister, Lumei."

choice.text: Wait, but wasn't this centuries ago? How is Lumei still in charge?

event.text: "This was indeed long ago, but we'll get to the answer for your question soon enough. Under Lumei's leadership the codex was almost doubled in size and enforcement became even stricter. The Osmian explorers, still held high in reverency by the public, were given seats in the Ministry so Lumei could keep them close to him as pawns. Because of the connection between Aether and the Great Eye, these hard-light forms took on a religious significance as well, and so Lumei himself underwent transformation to secure his power. As the technology became better researched soon the wealthy elite, priests, and eventually even the common people were able to afford such procedures. Supremacy of the transformants took hold and, fearful that this divide might create a split between the Zoltans, the Ministry began to normalize and enforce transformancy."

"Most adamant non-transformants died of natural causes and the newer more 'progressive' mindset took hold. All Zoltans over the age of 7 were to be immediately transitioned into hard-light chassis. The only place the Ministry struggled to touch was, ironically, Osmia itself. A group of non-transformants had taken hold there, seizing control of the territory between the wastelands that had survived the initial holocaust. Eventually the Ministry gave up and spent their effort erasing the importance of Osmia from the rest of the Zoltans - something made easier by the recent discovery of other sapient life. And so, that is how the first of we Osmians came to be. The Ministry wants nothing more than for the galaxy to forget we exist and for us to die out naturally."

choice.text: So, what is it that you needed of us?

name: OSMIA_UNLOCK_QUESTION
text: "Yes, well I suppose it's best I explain why we were there at the capital then, before I ask of you anything... You see, there are a few of our kind left which have not taken refuge on Osmia. They were captured by the Ministry and kept locked away in a secret laboratory under 'protocol 3', in the case of an unforeseen cataclysmic failure of the hard-light forms. We estimate there's likely several hundred of them locked away from centuries ago - each of them an innocent life, as well as a time capsule for ancient forgotten history. We hoped to storm the Capital and force them to release the captives, but as you can see that didn't work out as planned."

event.text: "Don't be. We understand your alliance with the Ministry as part of the Federation took precedence. But now, I'm afraid I must ask of you a favor that is not in the interest of that alliance. Our military is not strong enough to take on the vessel guarding the lab, and our only ship capable, you caused quite the damage to. We cannot offer you the same as the Ministry might, so I expect nothing more than your refusal. But if you accept this plea out of the kindness of your heart, then you will forever have the Osmian people's gratitude."

"Really? I cannot believe this. But I haven't time to thank you any further. I must encourage you to hurry, I cannot say if the Ministry will take action to further protect the specimens in the face of our actions or not. I'll transfer the coordinates immediately. Our transports will be on the way shortly after you arrive. Best of luck. Our people are counting on you."
"Understandable. At least I can thank you for allowing us to continue to exist as we were. Best of luck on your travels."

name: OSMIA_LAB

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of the secret Ministry Lab.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: There is zero doubt in your mind this is the place. Just from the immediate sinister appearance, it's clear this is not an ordinary secret base - if there ever was one. According to the Osmians, the security must be tight, and getting any closer without being detected is impossible.

event.text: As soon as you cross a certain threshold, a Peace-keeper vessel activates. It's a cruiser, and therefore no idle threat. "Entrance to Zone E17 is forbidden. How did you find this place?"
You're done being told what to do by the Ministry. Time to finally give them what they've had coming for a long time.

choice.text: Oops sorry, we're lost. We'll leave!

event.text: You've bitten off more than you can chew this time. The Osmians will need to find someone else to help them.

name: OSMIAN_ARRIVAL
text: Your radar immediately picks up several more pings. You're afraid this means the Zoltans have received reinforcements - but this isn't the case. In fact, it's quite the opposite. The Osmians have arrived, and unlike most of your "allies" in conflicts like this, they're actually providing firepower from the sidelines!

name: OSMIA_LAB_WIN
text: The Osmian troops, though limited in ships, are plentiful in manpower and storm the lab. The Zoltan scientists surrender. You take note of assorted Engi and even a few workers in Federation garb in the crowd, but you're distracted by Malki. "Thank you for your help. Though material offers I cannot extend, I can provide your Federation blueprints for our finest warship. We-" Suddenly, an alarm blares. Something bad is happening!

event.text: Shortly after the alarm, another warning plays over the stereo. You might be getting tired of all these warnings, but this isn't one to be ignored. "Evacuate the premises immediately. Nuclear strike imminent." Panic immediately breaks out, and your radar detects an approaching warhead. Apparently, in case of emergency, the Ministry rigged this place to destroy itself. If your holopad's estimation is correct, you have 10 minutes before the impact.

choice.text: Assist the Osmians in moving the stasis pods.

event.text: Your crew rush over to help, disengaging the pods from their holding compartments and carrying them over to the awaiting Osmian transport vessels. As the timer continues to tick down, you realize there's a much greater issue than the time limit - there isn't enough space for all of the specimens. Malki notices too and is dismayed. "What will we do now? There isn't enough time for multiple trips!"

choice.text: We have to leave them behind!
(Strong Crew) Haul some of the pods onto your ship.

event.text: With the other transports full, the only option is to load the chambers onto your own ship. You bring as many back as possible, but you can't help but notice Malki is still rushing around fruitlessly trying to fit more containers on the other ships.
You apologize to Malki, but he hardly notices as he's already run off to help move as many stasis chambers as possible. You hurry back to your ship and prepare to leave.

name: OSMIAN_LEAVE
text: "Are you insane? We didn't come this far just to leave them behind! We- we have to rescue as many as we can!" You try to explain there isn't possibly enough time to move them all, but Malki won't listen. Eventually, through force, you manage to drag him back to your ship as the rest of the Osmians flee. Though you weren't able to save all of the specimens and the scientists are doomed, at least all of the Osmians and your crew were able to make it away safely.

event.text: From the distance as you leave the planet behind you can see the flash of the detonation. In grim silence Malki watches, unresponsive. "I have failed my people. But... I should have known. The Ministry would sooner destroy its heritage than allow its people to see the truth. It's not like it matters to them. If they ever need new specimens they know they can just attack Osmia again. That lab was merely a formality. If news of our raid gets out at all, I'm sure it'll be spun as an accident, though even that is doubtful."

choice.text: There were Federation scientists there too. Why?

event.text: "You think the Federation didn't know about us? I'm sure they've briefed all the rest that we're some dangerous threat. That way, if we ever tried to start another civil war, the Federation wouldn't hesitate to side with the Ministry. But that's besides the point... I shouldn't be so grim. We didn't save everyone - we couldn't have. But we still saved dozens of our people, and we may finally recover some of our lost history. But, as the leader of my people, I have failed to prepare us for such outcomes: I cannot return to Osmia. I humbly request that you accept my services, captain."

destroyed.text: The strange Zoltan vessel has been vanquished. It causes some damage to the infastructure below when it crashes into the ground, but the Zoltan officials tell you not to worry.

deadCrew.text: The strange Zoltan vessel has been vanquished. It causes some damage to the infastructure below when it crashes into the ground, but the Zoltan officials tell you not to worry.

destroyed.text: You've defeated the ship of so-called Osmians. There wasn't much point - the Ministry isn't exactly going to give you a second reward - but at least this mystery is over. Right?

deadCrew.text: You've defeated the ship of so-called Osmians. There wasn't much point - the Ministry isn't exactly going to give you a second reward - but at least this mystery is over. Right?

destroyed.text: The peacekeepers have been defeated. You expect more reinforcements, but it seems the lab just intends to surrender instead. The Ministry is desperate to hide this truth, but apparently not enough to risk a full-scale war.

deadCrew.text: The peacekeepers have been defeated. You expect more reinforcements, but it seems the lab just intends to surrender instead. The Ministry is desperate to hide this truth, but apparently not enough to risk a full-scale war.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_MONK_GRAVE
text: Though a nebula is still present at this beacon, you can't help but notice strange readings from the nearby moon. With these, you deduct a ship has landed there, but you can't tell what kind.

event.text: As you pilot closer to the moon, you're able to make out a Duskbringer vessel on the surface. Despite perhaps your better judgement, you decide to land anyways, and trail your way towards the ship. When you arrive, you find an arrangement of small stones and an armored Zoltan kneeling over them, crying.

The Zoltan turns to you, and his composure changes from distraught to disheveled and angry. "Renegade pigs? Get out of here, this is hallowed ground!" You pocket your weapons and raise your arms, to signal you come in peace. The Zoltan sighs and goes back to staring at the unmarked graves.
						
"The Federation history books don't tell many stories of the Zoltans' involvement in Federation Wars. I think most people choose to believe we played little to no part at all. But hundreds of thousands, if not more, proud Zoltans gave their lives fighting for the Federation and the Galaxy in the Fed-Mantis War, the anti-Inquisitions, and the Civil War. And what thanks do they get? An unmarked grave here, on some moon in the middle of nowhere in a sector no one but monks visit. And the Ministry is fine with it. They'd prefer people forget our involvement in those wars, as part of their whole... 'non-violence' agenda." The Zoltan spits on the ground away from the graves. "It's shameful, really."

The Zoltan wipes away a tear. "Thank you. I don't know how much you really mean it, but I appreciate it. It's not often I meet people who care to even listen to me without shouting that I'm a radical. I cannot offer much, but maybe I have something that can begin to make up for my mistakes."

choice.text: Mention that the Ministry never showed up during or after the Last Stand.

event.text: "Really shows how little you understand history. The Ministry SENT forces to aid the Federation during the Civil War - and we were sent to fight on the backwater fronts in the middle of nowhere-space handling pirates more than Rebels. The Ministry couldn't afford to keep sending troops when internal affairs were a mess and the Rebels always a threat, so they pulled the plug. And of course, when the war was over, the Zoltans were painted as cowards and traitors, unwilling to serve the very organization they had helped found." The Zoltan turns away from you and goes back to staring at the graves. With nothing else to add, you figure it's best to leave.

"Not even a single mention of the Zoltans. Not one. There's millions of humans, but not a single Zoltan or Engi. And why do you think that is? The same people who paid the bills for those memorials were the rich shady Union scumbags who were playing golf with Wentworth before the war. They didn't WANT to mention the Zoltans on it. And so they didn't. It's why people like Devorak the Deathless turned against the Federation."

choice.text: It is shameful, how they buried your history.

event.text: The Zoltan wipes away a tear. "Thank you. I don't know how much you really mean it, but I appreciate it. It's not often I meet people who care to even listen to me without shouting that I'm a radical. I cannot offer much, but maybe I have something that can begin to make up for my mistakes."

choice.text: You still could have done more.

event.text: "Again and again, the galaxy only seems to prove itself to be a cycle. Why do I even bother trying to atone for the wrongs of the past, if people will spit in my face and ignore everything I say regardless? Fine, if you want things to be this way... then let them be this way!"

choice.text: (Devorak) "In the heat of our fury we all make mistakes."

event.text: The Duskbringer double takes when he realizes Devorak is amongst your crew. They bow towards each other. "Oh my - Devorak! I didn't realize-" Devorak cuts him off. "It is okay. I have made many - too many, mistakes in my life. We were all angry at the Federation, and for good reason. But we must never let our anger turn to violence. We must protest, but we must protest peacefully. How else will progress be made, if not without bloodshed? These are the lessons we must teach ourselves." Still speechless, the young Duskbringer introduces himself as Dovan and requests to join your crew.

choice.text: Leave some scrap as an offering on one of the graves.

event.text: It's a strange gesture for sure, but it's the best you can do with the limited resources you have. The Duskbringer seems to appreciate it regardless. As he wipes away a tear, he says, "T-thanks. I haven't known Renegades to be the sensitive type. Sensitive as in, situationally aware. But perhaps it's unfair to judge a book by its cover." He stands back up and sticks out his hand. "The name's Dovan. I joined the Duskbringers at a dark point in my life, when tensions between the Ministry and Union were at their highest, and everything about the Federation felt.. bleak. But now I realize it was all a mistake. The Federation, for all its flaws, is the only thing capable of uniting the galaxy. The Duskbringers, the Rebels, organizations like those... they're only going to tear this entire Multiverse apart. Do you mind if I go with you? My crew doesn't ever need to know..."

choice.text: (Orchid Children) Leave some flowers on the graves.

event.text: Knowing just what's appropriate for this situation, you run back to your ship and fetch the Orchid children corpses, then scatter them across the graves. At first the Duskbringer thinks you're giving a nice gesture, until he realizes what they really are. "WHAT IN THE NAME OF THE GREAT EYE ARE YOU DOING?! WHAT IS WRONG WITH YOU!?" The Duskbringer runs back to his ship and orders all of his crew to open fire on you immediately.

choice.text: Take no chances - kill the Duskbringer.

event.text: You draw your weapon and shoot the Zoltan from a distance. He dies almost instantly, dissipating into nothing but his armor. You can't help but feel that was a bit unnecessary, but it's too late to undo it now.
For all you know this could be a trap. Better not to approach.

name: NEBULA_MONK_FREE_CREW
text: The nearby monastery hails you. A scrawny monk appears on the viewscreen. "Hello. I recently joined this Monastery, but I soon found a life of isolation out here in these nebulas is not for me. Would you perhaps allow me to come with you? I'm dedicated to my pacifist beliefs, but I can be useful in other ways!"

choice.text: No thanks, we don't need any more crew.

event.text: "Oh... ok." You end the call and carry on.

name: NEBULA_MONK_CONVERT
text: A Zoltan Monastery has been constructed at this beacon. They welcome you, offering a tour of their temple.

event.text: The 'tour' ends up being less of a tour and more of a long sermon about the Monk's religion. You find it rather boring, but one of your crew are convinced. To your surprise, they want to stay behind and join the monks!
Your crew waves goodbye. The Monks sympathize with you, understanding what a hard decision that must have been. As a consolation, they repair your hull and upgrade your reactor for free.

removeCrew.text: You cannot clone your crew, as they are not dead.

event.text: You comfort your crew, explaining that the mission is more important, and that they can return to the monks when you've saved this reality.

choice.text: You have much better things to do.

event.text: You decide not to tour the monastery.

name: NEBULA_MONK_BEGGAR
text: An old, hunched over Monk materializes on your ship, hands reaching out in the shape of a cup. "Hello travellers, I am but a humble Zoltan looking for some spare scrap to make it through my day. Life out here is hard, I'm sure you understand."

event.text: You hand over the money to the old monk.

name: NEBULA_MONK_STRANDED_FED
text: You're shocked to see a Federation ship stuck at this beacon, with their engines in disrepair. "Oh, you've caught us at a bad time. Or actually... a rather fortunate time, for you. We need scrap to repair our engines, and the Monks here have been useless at helping us. We would be willing to sell you supplies for scrap."

choice.text: Give them scrap for their repairs. [-25~]

event.text: "Oh, wow! Thank you so much. We can't let this go unpaid though. Here, while travelling this sector we collected detailed maps of our findings, it should be of assistance. Have some fuel too, we have more than enough, it's only our engines that need fixing."

choice.text: We aren't looking to buy anything.

event.text: You apologize to the Fed ship and carry on your way.

name: NEBULA_MONK_GHOST
text: The nearby Monk ship appears to be moving around strangely, almost as if they aren't sure how to pilot it. A single rusty missile launcher has been mounted on it as well, uncharacteristic of the usually peaceful monks.

event.text: The Monks don't respond to your hails vocally, but rather a message. "Hello. This ship is no longer under ownership by Zoltan Monks. We are Ghosts. This ship is under-armed, we are low on missiles. Can you give some?"
"Your gift is appreciated. Please accept this token of gratitude." You expect scrap or perhaps some fuel, but instead a Ghost crew member materializes on your ship!
"Unexpectedly high quantity of ammo. Please accept this token of gratitude." You expect scrap or perhaps some fuel, but instead a Ghost crew member materializes on your ship!

choice.text: If they're low on missiles, that means they're an easy target!

event.text: You refuse to help the Ghosts, but rather attack them instead.
You apologize to the Ghosts and carry on with your mission.
You ignore the strange monks and move past.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_MONK_ANNOYED
text: A small Zoltan temple has been constructed on a nearby planet, which looks otherwise completely barren.

event.text: "Hello friends. I have received your hail, but I'm afraid I am busy meditating. Safe travels." They end the call.
"I apologize, but I have nothing to offer. Have a nice day." They end the call once again.
"Maybe you did not hear me. I said I have nothing to offer. Have a nice day." They end the call once again.
"Please stop. I have already told you, I have nothing to offer." They end the call once again.
"How many more times will you do this? I am not going to give you anything. Do not hail me again." They end the call once again.

"Fine! If you want something so bad, take this!" You wait in anticipation, but instead of a reward, a hostile Automated ship rockets up towards you, colliding with the hull and immediately entering combat mode.

choice.text: (Monk Crew) Have your Monk hail them.

event.text: "Ah, one of us. I will send an automated vessel up to repair your hull. Have a nice day."
You decide not to bother the temple or the Monks inside.

name: NEBULA_MONK_CHASE
text: You notice what appears to be the exterior of a ship slipping through the clouds before it disappears.

event.text: Whatever it was, you aren't interested in following.

name: NEBULA_MONK_DUSKBRINGERS
text: You spot a strange sight, a Duskbringer ship conversing with Zoltan Monks! You can only imagine they're demanding the Monks hand over supplies in return for their lives...

choice.text: Rescue the Monks from the Duskbringers.

event.text: You interrupt the ships to attack the Duskbringers.

choice.text: Wait for the Duskbringers to leave and contact the Monks.

event.text: Once the Duskbringers jump away, you approach the Monks and question them about the encounter. The Monks chuckle. "No no, they would not hurt us. They are our friends. Though we disapprove of their radical beliefs, we still support them when we can." You nod your head and end the call.
You can't make assumptions. You have no idea what's truly going on over there, and you shouldn't interrupt just in case.

name: NEBULA_MONK_HOSTAGES
text: It appears the nearby monastery is in trouble! A Slug hacker is holding them hostage and broadcasting a message to all nearby ships, demanding they pay an absurd ransom for the Monks.

event.text: "Oh, sssso you want to brawl? Prepare to die then!"
"Ahhhh, at lasssst sssssomeone paysss our reasssonable price!" The Hackers relinquish control over the Monastery and jump away.
"Thank you friend. We thought this was how we would die. The Hackers have held control over us for weeks, and many of us have already starved. May we last few survivors come with you?"

choice.text: (Mind Control) Try to mind control the Hackers to let them go.

event.text: The mind control proves completely pointless, as the Hackers are Slugs. Even worse, you've announced your location and the ship moves in to attack.

choice.text: (Mind Affecting Weapon) Try to mind control the Hackers.

event.text: The mind control proves completely pointless, as the Hackers are Slugs. Even worse, you've announced your location and the ship moves in to attack.
You can't waste your money here. When the Hackers realize no-one is going to pay they'll leave the Monks alone anyways... probably...

name: NEBULA_MONK_PROVERB
text: You receive a strange hail from the ship here. "As the wise Solay Voltar once said, he who lies with the voracious bat-dogs awakes with the space-fleas of Gammos 6."

event.text: The Monk sighs. "It's a proverb. It means one whom associates themselves with those who are devoid of morals shall find themselves in a similar predicament. A warning, so I should say, for one's own situation, living within the Federation."

choice.text: (Monk Crew) "A warning well headed, but not without risks of its own."

event.text: The other Monk nods, and the two launch into a long philosophical discussion about moral principles. You can't understand a word of what they say, but it seems your Monk has convinced the other of your wisdom and they come aboard.

choice.text: How dare you insult the Federation! Attack!

event.text: The Monks refuse to fight, letting you fire on their ship.

choice.text: Ignore them and continue on your way.

event.text: You put the Monk's words out of your mind.

name: NEBULA_MONK_LOST_MAN
text: A Zoltan lifepod is drifting out here in space. The life-pod has minor damage, but the wreck of a peace-keeper ship drifts nearby as well.

event.text: A gasping Zoltan is brought aboard, still wearing their peace-keeper armor. "T-Thank you for saving me! We were tasked with transporting a Monk ship carrying an important Zoltan operative who's undercover. Everything was fine, until a mercenary hired by the Duskbringers showed up and obliterated our ship. The monks fled, but it won't be long before the Mercenaries catch up. I'll upload their co-ordinates to the computer, I hope you will help me."

choice.text: Ignore the lifepod and just scrap the ship.

event.text: You fly past the lifepod and move to the wreckage, which provides some scrap and supplies.

name: MONK_LOST_MAN_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of an undercover operative in peril given by a rescued Peacekeeper.

text: It appears you've arrived just in time. The Mercenary ship mentioned earlier is assaulting the Monk ship. They won't last long, so you intercept their attack and prepare to destroy the mercenaries.

name: NEBULA_MONK_CONVOY
text: A Monk ship hails you. "As you may know, our religion forbids us from participating in violent acts. However, we have had terrible luck with pirates in this sector. Could you help transport us to our destination?"

event.text: The Monks transmit the co-ordinates to their destination.
You apologize and explain you are not an escort. The Monks say they understand and carry on.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_MANTIS_MONK
text: You catch chatter on the nearby Mantis ship. "Look that one, not Monk. Must have good things onboard, we will take them." Since there's no other ships around, it's safe to assume they're referring to you!

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SLUG_MONK
text: It seems the Monk presence in this nebulas has disturbed its natural residents, the Slugs! An irritated Slug ship looking to retake their territory spots you and approaches.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_MONK_SMUGGLER_INTERCEPT
text: A smuggler ship is attempting to sneak its way through this sector. However, when they spot you, they don't take chances and attack!

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_MONK_SMUGGLER_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: You've retrieved coordinates from a defeated Smuggler ship that lead here.

text: You arrive at the co-ordinates of the Smuggler's client, but they appear to be Monks! Very unusual...

event.text: You hail the Monks, but instead a gruff looking pirate responds. "Ah damn, it's the Feds! Prepare the guns men!"
You ignore the monks and move past.

name: NEBULA_MONK_RIFT_FIGHT
text: You come to a quiet part of Zoltan space and encounter an ancient Zoltan wise man who claims to have harnessed the power of a spatial rift, but seems to have been driven completely mad by the power. He's obviously lying, but his madness is most certainly real, as is the rift. "Choose your doom. I have a wide variety of options," he demands.

choice.text: (Reality Manipulator) Seize control of the rift.

event.text: "What- what have you done??? NOOOOOOOOO!" The Zoltan falls to his knees, utterly defeated as the rift in the distance slowly closes and the environment returns to normal. Terrified of your much more real power, the Zoltan submits to your service.
"You like a challenge. So be it!" A wormhole forms and a confused, angry Mantis ship hurtles toward you!
"Do not be fooled, Federation, by a soft underbelly." You detect a wormhole opening up, and seconds later a Slug ship is attacking from the other direction!
"A hardened foe for a hardened veteran." You detect a wormhole opening up, and a Rock ship appears with guns blazing. It appears they were in combat when they were thrust across space-time.
"An unusually masochistic request, but one I shall grant." You detect a wormhole opening up, and a Lanius ship emerges. Hungry for scrap, the ship attacks.
"Do not judge a book by its cover, some foes are stronger than they might appear." You detect a wormhole opening up, and an Orchid ship emerges. Confused, they mistake you for an enemy and attack!
The Zoltan is quiet for a moment, and then whispers, "Are you sure? Well, so be it then." A huge wormhole opens, and from within it looms an Obelisk ship, prepared for war.

name: ZOLTAN_RIFT_SUCCESS
text: When he sees you have emerged victorious, the Zoltan wise man enters a rage. Rifts threaten to tear space apart until, instead, the Zoltan implodes, sending a blast wave of scrap and salvage dragged here from distant worlds in your direction.

name: MONK_WEAPON
text: A monk ship resides here. "We were tidying up this region and we happened to find an awful cache containing a violent weapon! We have no need of such a thing, but if you would make a donation to our cause, we would be happy to let you take it off our hands."

choice.text: Offer some scrap for the weapon.

event.text: "Wonderful! We will put this scrap to good use. Go in peace."

choice.text: (Monk Crew) Pledge to use the weapon responsibly for a discount.

event.text: "Since you are of the faith, we will trust your word. Go in peace."

choice.text: Attack them, maybe you can get it for free.

event.text: The monks respond, regret in their voices. "So it's true, then... those who use violent means cannot be reasoned with..."

choice.text: Tell them you don't want it either.

event.text: "We understand how you feel. Perhaps we will throw it into a star, or present it to the Great Eye."

name: MONK_ORCHID
text: An Orchid ship sits at this beacon, where several monks also reside. It hails you. "Hello! We were looking for Zoltans of the Illesctrian faith. We were hoping that some might accompany us to our space, but they seem hesitant to agree to that. Do you think you might be able to convince them?"

event.text: Your Orchid Caretaker begins to gently talk with the monks about the lives of the Orchids, their duties and beliefs. The monks seem impressed with the ideals of your Caretaker and agree to go. "Wow, that really did the trick! Thank you for your help." The Orchids give you a modest reward for assisting them.

choice.text: (Floral Crew) Convince the Orchids to look elsewhere.

event.text: Your crewmember talks to the other Orchids and convinces them that travel of this kind is challenging for these people and that they're bound to find more eager monks if they keep looking. The Orchids apologize. The monks appreciate your intervention and give you a small tribute for helping them.

Mayeb goes to talk to the monks. "Greetings, my name is Mayeb. This is my sister, P'erpah." She gestures to her other head, which moves a little bit. "P'erpah says 'good day to you-' Ah, how do I say this... '-shiny ones of faith.'"

The monks are intrigued and begin to question Mayeb about her sister. As they talk, Mayeb gently encourages them to learn more about her people. "...and maybe, just maybe... they have some things to learn from you as well, if that's what you care about."

The monks are convinced.

"You are... a strange one, Mayeb. But, you came through for us. Thank you." The Orchids give you a small reward for assisting them.

choice.text: (Monk Crew) Talk the monks into it.

event.text: Your monk talks about the importance of spreading ideals and about how this is the way that the Great Eye is telling them that it's time to make a wider impact. At this, the Monks come around, and agree to accompany the Orchids. "Wow, that really did the trick! Thank you for your help." The Orchids give you a small reward for assisting them.
As you arm your weapons, the Orchid quickly terminates the hail and begins powering up their own weapons.
You decide not to interact with the Orchids.

name: MONK_SUN
text: "Welcome to your trial by fire. The Great Eye demands that we test your mettle. You must experience hardship, at least for a time. You will be forged in the crucible of suffering in order to attain true enlightenment." Looks like they plan to keep you here for a short time!

name: MONK_SUN_TRIAL_WIN
text: "Your trial is over, you have passed! Here is your reward. But take heed, the universe will no doubt have many more hardships to face. Always be attentive to the lessons of the universe."

name: MONK_ATONEMENT
text: It's rare to see Zoltan monasteries outside of the nebula. This one is positioned in the grey zone of a tidally locked planet, such that at that location, it always appears to be dawn.

event.text: "Welcome, traveler, to the light. The Illesctrian Order of Illumination observes all. However, though we look into your soul, we do not judge you. It is only by illumination that one can atone for their misdeeds." The head monk stares into your eyes with an unusually intense piercing gaze.

"Oh dear. Your soul is quite tainted. Even from a glance I can tell that you bring misery to many people. Perhaps there are some small acts of kindness that I am overlooking... but, I can tell that you are hated by many. You are on a dark path."

"You are disliked by many. I can see that you are making many enemies in your quest across the stars. I know not of the precise circumstances, but if you wish to live in peace after your little war is over, you will have to make amends."

"You are a contentious figure. Your actions consistently color you as undiplomatic and even barbaric. I am certain that there are many places you can no longer go and be welcomed, unless you make a sincere effort to change."

"Overall, you seem to have left a bad impression on this galaxy. Perhaps there are mitigating circumstances, but you seem to be sliding in the wrong direction. However, it seems you have shown at least some restraint."

"When I look into your eyes, I can see that you are in balance. If there are any acts that you have done to wrong others, it has been counterbalanced with an act of kindness or heroism. ...Or perhaps you have committed neither?"

"Ah, yes indeed. Upon looking further, you are, in fact, completely balanced. You are neither famous nor infamous. My intuition tells me you do not rock the boat. But that is wise in its own right. We offer you a gift. Go in peace, and always walk in the light."
"You have good karma overall. To noncombatants, you are more likely to bring them peace and safety than you are to exploit or bring harm to them. The light is where you belong."

"I am in awe, you seem to be quite the positive force upon the stars. For one in such a usually violent vocation, you humble me in your ability to bring positive karma to others. Perhaps we could learn a thing or two from you."
You leave the monks alone and focus on ship operations.

name: MONK_ATONEMENT_OFFER
text: "There are people out there who believe you have wronged them greatly. I do not know if you feel shame or regret over any actions you've made, or any situations you have gotten into. However, if you wish to atone for your actions, then let me offer you the chance to do so. Tell me a group you have wronged and present a donation. Once you have done so, please meditate on your wrongs towards that group."

choice.text: Atone for the misdeeds that concern nobody in particular.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Union.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Zoltan Ministry.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Ctl'Yae Gathering.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Engi Harmony.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Crystal Empire.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Outcast Rockmen.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Oro'bache Confederacy.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Free Mantis.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Shell Geniocracy.
Atone for the misdeeds that concern the Slug Kleptocracy.

event.text: "I see... it brings me great sorrow to hear that. However, know that it is not too late. If you ever wish to make amends, please come back, and we will do all we can to save your soul."

name: MONK_ATONEMENT_OFFER_GOOD_KARMA
text: "Although you are regarded well by most, there are people out there for whom you could have. I do not know if you feel shame or regret over any actions you've made, or any situations you have gotten into. However, if you wish to atone for your actions, then let me offer you the chance to do so. Tell me a group you have wronged. Once you have done so, please meditate on your wrongs towards that group."

choice.text: Atone for the misdeeds that concern nobody in particular.
