name: ANCIENT_USELESS_WEAPON
text: An agitated Obelisk hails you. "You, mortal one. We have an issue with this strange device. It's a weapon of sorts, but we can't figure out how to operate it."

event.text: You try to explain the Obelisks how to mount weapons to their ship, but they cut you off. "No no, we know how to do that. The tech in this thing... it's so modern, and too simple. We have no use for it, you can have it."
"Bah, just a useless flesh-being. Nothing significant about you."

name: ANCIENT_LOST_DUDE
text: To your surprise, a hibernating Obelisk is simply drifting in space.

event.text: The Obelisk never once stirs. For all you know, it will continue to drift powerless for centuries after you leave.

name: ANCIENT_DESIRE
text: A voice booms over your intercom, speaking slowly. "Aliens, here? How curious. This is a chance too good to pass up. Do not resist, I have taken control over your entire vessel. Tell me, what do you desire most?"

event.text: "Money, the means for which to obtain all that the universe may offer. Take this gift my friend, I hope it brings you all that you desire."

"Ahhh, what a vain desire. Ever since we shed our organic forms in favor of these mechanical bodies, we have forgotten the pursuits of lust or beauty. Unfortunately, I cannot alter your form myself. I can however gift you a truly beautiful creature for you to reflect upon."
"Don't we all. I hope you forgive me that I am going to take this literally, but perhaps you'll find some humor in it. Best of luck in your pursuits, mortal."
The Obelisk breaks into a fit of laughter. "Oh, how so absolutely stupid and ignorant of you. Oh, but whatever. Here, have this. I think you'll find its irony quite entertaining, as I sure do."
"The foolish creature hopes to break free? Did you not hear my warning? I am in control of your ship. Answer my question or suffer the consequences. What is it you desire most?"
"Money, the means for which to obtain all that the universe may offer. Take this gift my friend, I hope it brings you all that you desire."

"Ahhh, what a vain desire. Ever since we shed our organic forms in favor of these mechanical bodies, we have forgotten the pursuits of lust or beauty. Unfortunately, I cannot alter your form myself. I can however gift you a truly beautiful creature for you to reflect upon."
"Don't we all. I hope you forgive me that I am going to take this literally, but perhaps you'll find some humor in it. Best of luck in your pursuits, mortal."
The Obelisk breaks into a fit of laughter. "Oh, how so absolutely stupid and ignorant of you. Oh, but whatever. Here, have this. I think you'll find its irony quite entertaining, as I sure do."

choice.text: Resist again and suffer the consequences.

event.text: "Then you deserve all that is coming to you."

choice.text: (Anti-Virus) Restore your systems and fight back.

event.text: Your Anti-Virus struggles to counter the Obelisk tech. It manages to restore just a few of the critical systems.

name: ROYAL_ZOO
text: For once, a Royal ship in the same system as you isn't looking to fight... at least not immediately. Instead, they hail you with an offer. "I am a collector, and I fancy to study some of the more exotic races of your mortal plane. Please, come aboard, maybe you'll find one of my collections you'd like for your own, or perhaps you'd be willing to give me one of yours for healthy compensation!"

event.text: You're wary of a trap, but no attack comes yet. You find several cages containing various strange creatures, some more foreign than others.

choice.text: Offer to buy one of his collections.
Offer to sell one of your more exotic crew.

event.text: "Yes! Who might you have for me?"

removeCrew.text: Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.
Your crew cannot be cloned, as you just sold them.

event.text: "Is this some kind of stupid joke to you, mortals? It should be obvious my request was for specimens exotic to ME, not to YOU. If you are truly this braindead, then I do not wish to allow your continued existence."

choice.text: Nevermind, I'd rather buy some crew.
I think we'll be leaving now.
I think we'll be leaving now.
This is shady, attack now while you can!

event.text: You aren't going to let some Royal poke around at your crew. Prepare for battle!

name: ROYAL_ZOO_PURCHASE
text: "Take a look, and see what you might like!"

choice.text: I think we'll be leaving now.

name: ROYAL_AUGMENTED_JOY
text: A small swarm of Augmented ships is feasting on a massive field of destroyed Obelisk and Rebel ships. They don't seem to care about your presence.

event.text: "Federation ship is seeking trade? Maybe scrap. Many plentiful wrecks here, much for all! Let Federation scour wreckage as content, but will needing give something in return."

choice.text: Pay them to access the wrecks.

event.text: "Yes, many of scrap! Enjoy searchings, Federation."

choice.text: We don't need anything in the wrecks, but we are open to trading normally.

event.text: "Most reasonable! Come, see what having offers."
You arm the weapons and engage the nearest Augmented ship.

choice.text: Scoop up some scrap for yourself.

event.text: If the Lanius aren't bothering you, you won't bother them either.

name: ROYAL_PANDORA_FACTORY
text: You've seen many strange things in your journeys, but you don't think you've seen anything quite like this. Beyond your ship is a massive factory spanning several entire planets, with a colossal structure running between them. No star remains, and the only lights left are the artificial ones. What is this place?

event.text: Fortunately, it appears most of the factory is automated, so there are few ships to stop you. Compared to most Obelisk achievements, this mega-structure is probably of low priority to them anyways. You find a safe looking space to dock.

As you continue to explore, a monotone voice speaks to you through a wall-mounted speaker. "Who are you? For what reasons have you docked here? Please report to section SJ-37 for check-in if you wish to proceed further into the facilities." You didn't think anyone was here, but it appears you were wrong.

choice.text: Report to whatever location the voice mentioned.

event.text: You look around for clues as to where to head, and notice several signs on the wall, which your translator converts to your language. You follow them into a large, yet still empty, reception room with a Cognitive sitting behind a desk.

The Cognitive analyzes you for a few moments, then uses its ring to push forward some strange tablet device with a place for you to sign. "Welcome to the Pandoran Factory Cluster. If you wish to proceed with supervision, please sign below. Otherwise, you will be required to leave."

As soon as you sign the contract, the tablet vanishes and the Cognitive moves out from the desk. "By signing this contract you agree not to-" the AI rapidly lists off a couple hundred things you can't understand, then signals with a large arrow for you to follow.

"These facilities were built several centuries ago, and are the primary manufacturing plant for Pandoran Boxes, also called Karthithes in the native language. They have small reality manipulators inside them, and when opened can unleash either divine wonders or unimaginable horrors. Mainly for use in gambling, of course. However, the factory was abandoned when the Obelisks got bored of the pastime, and it was left in my control ever since. Production continues to this day, but without anyone using the boxes our storage is now almost completely filled. This concludes the tour, you may leave."
"You want to take a box? Go, take it."
"You want me to go with you? Please, I will take this meaningless junk if it means I may leave this hell behind."

You push forward, ignoring the voice. A little while longer, it speaks again. "It is apparent that you do not wish to make yourself welcome. Activating anti-intrusion systems." Suddenly, a laser comes out of the wall, melting one of your crew! To make matters worse, two Cognitives materialize and chase down your crew!

removeCrew.text: Fortunately, your crew has already cloned back on the ship and is ready to fight the cognitive intruders.

choice.text: You really should listen to what the voice just said.

event.text: It's a fascinating view, but you have no further interest in the structure. There are better things to do.

name: ROYAL_FREEMANTIS
text: It appears the nearby Rebel ship has already found you, and approaches. However, when you receive a hail, all you can hear from the other end is strange clicking and gurgling.

choice.text: Attack them now before they can!

event.text: Right as you start to attack, the ship's camera turns on and a friendly looking Free Mantis greets you. "Hello! Translator on ship not accustom to yet. We happy to see Federation- wait what doing? No no stop!" It appears it's too late, they've already seen you as hostile and a fight is now inevitable.

choice.text: Hail them to see if they're ok.

event.text: You send a hail in return to the Rebel ship, and a few moments later their camera pops on. You see the ship is now piloted by a friendly looking Free Mantis. "Hello! Yes, doing fine, Rebel translator on ship unaccustomed to clan dialect. Followed fleet, hoping capture Rebels for glorious Federation! Many succeeding, but sector scary. Big cube ships come and go, kill many. I go with you, not wanting die from cube."

You send a hail in return to the Rebel ship, and a few moments later their camera pops on. You see the ship is now piloted by a friendly looking Free Mantis. "Hello! Yes, doing fine, Rebel translator on ship unaccustomed to clan dialect. Followed fleet, hoping capture Rebels for glorious Federation! Many succeeding, but sector scary. Big cube ships come and go, kill many. I go with you, not wanting die from cube."

name: ROYAL_INSULTS
text: You receive a contact from the nearby Royal ship. Fortunately, they don't raise their weapons immediately either. "You are flesh-beings, yes? Have you noticed that our insults are rather bland? Oh how I hate saying 'Flesh-being' day in and out. I require more creative unpleasantries to hurl at unsuspecting mortals. Have you any?"

event.text: "Most excellent. For what shall be my insult of choice from now on?"
"Yes, good. This will serve most excellent. You have pleased me, dear Walking Nutrient Paste. Accept this as a gift."
"Yes, good. This will serve most excellent. You have pleased me, dear Amorphous Skin-Sack. Accept this as a gift."
"Yes, good. This will serve most excellent. You have pleased me, dear Deformed Ape Creature. Accept this as a gift."
"Yes, good. This will serve most excellent. You have pleased me, dear Regrettably Sentient Space Meat. Accept this as a gift."
"Ugh, this is a most terrible suggestion. You have greatly displeased me. I will now remove you from my sight."
"Ugh, this is a most terrible suggestion. You have greatly displeased me. I will now remove you from my sight."
Though this is one of the rare times the Royals aren't itching to murder you, you've chosen to fight them yourself. Prepare for battle!
"Fine, be that way... uh... skin creature."

name: ROYAL_DATA
text: "Mortal creatures! Your culture is most strange, but I am fascinated with it! I wish to learn more! Please, feed me the data in your ship, and I shall pay you handsomely for the knowledge!" It's a tempting offer, but you have no idea if that data will end up in Rebel hands in the end. Will you take the risk?

choice.text: (Decoy Buoys) Give them your data, but carefully falsify your flight plans.

event.text: "Thank you kind skin sack! I greatly appreciate it." The ship jumps away. Good thing the Obelisks fell for it, and now if it ends up in Rebel hands, they won't be able to use it against you.
"Most unfortunate. Now I am sad. Goodbye." The ship jumps away.
You power up your weapons and fight the Obelisk ship.
You decide not to fight the Obelisks, and fly away.

name: ANCIENT_ENGI_HIDE
text: You catch just a brief glimpse of an Engi ship before it flies away.

event.text: Messing with the Obelisk's creations in their own sector doesn't sound like a good idea..

name: ANCIENT_ENGI_HIDE_HAIL_ENGI
text: "Message received. Calibrating frequencies. Federation identified, friendly connect established. Here on mission from Harmony. Objective: prove source of creator and disable ancient weaponry. If invasion successful, Obelisks will recapture Harmony."

choice.text: We have similar objectives. Maybe we could help each other?

event.text: "Contemplating offer... This is acceptable. I will personally offer services, better chance at success."

name: ANCIENT_CRYSTAL_CHASE
text: You manage to intercept a conversation between an Obelisk and Crystal ship. "Yes, yes. Stay safe, and avoid this alien ship. They have hostile intentions, and must be destroyed." Neither ship sees you, and they both fly away in opposite directions.

event.text: The Obelisks were right about one thing, your intentions are anything but peaceful. You hunt down their ship, ready to fight.
The Crystals are surprised to see you, and at first thinks you may be harmless after all. As soon as your weapons come online they realize the truth, and prepare to defend themselves.
The Obelisk and Crystal ship both fly out of sight, leaving you alone.

name: ANCIENT_LOOTERS
text: A Crystal ship passing through this sector lies half destroyed by an Obelisk ship. It appears Obelisks aren't above scrapping wrecks, because the Crystal ship is swarming with Obelisk looters.

choice.text: Attack the Crystal ship, then we can scrap both ships!

event.text: You engage the Crystal ship, knowing if you can kill the Obelisks while they are vulnerable you'll be able to scrap both ships.
They may not be aboard their usual ship, but Obelisks anywhere are dangerous. Neither ship notices you.

name: ANCIENT_LOOTERS_WIN
text: With the Crystal ship and all the Obelisks aboard dealt with, you're free to scrap this vessel before you can proceed to do the same to their original ship.

event.text: While scrapping the Obelisk ship you find one of their drones still intact.

name: ANCIENT_WORTHY
text: "You. Alien. You have insulted me by simply entering my presence. Tell me that you are not worthy, and I will let you live."

event.text: "Good. I am now satisfied. Now get out of our sector."

You make it clear to the Obelisks that you are their equal. Enraged that you dare make such a comparison, they raise their weapons to destroy you. However, the Targeting Jammer does its job perfectly, and they are unable to fire on you. Now afraid of any other secrets you might hold, they pay you to let them live.

You don't respond, but instead shut off their shields. The Obelisks continue to gloat until they come to the realisation that only their Energy Super Shield still protects them. Now afraid of any other secrets you might hold, they pay you to let them live.
"W-what? You dare use my words against me in this way? I shall kill you!"

name: ANCIENT_SCULPTER
text: An Obelisk ship surrounded by a giant asteroid field hails you. "Do you like them? Every rock, hand crafted. I have spent a millennium creating this place. Please, enjoy my creation."

event.text: "No please, anywhere but here!" You cut off the ship and attack.

You take the turn to admire the nearby rocks. You know despite the difficulty for the Rebel fleet to catch up, every second wasted here is another second they come closer to leaking through. Still, your time is paid off when the Obelisk is so happy he gives you several canisters of fuel and one of his rocks for free. You place the rock on your desk. It is pretty well sculpted...
The Obelisk seems pleased with you, and heads back to perfecting its rocks.

name: ANCIENT_SCULPTER_WIN
text: As the Obelisk takes one last breath, he manages to squeeze out the words, "Please... just... don't hurt my creations... it is my last legacy..."

event.text: You harvest some of the asteroids and find many of them contain traces of fuel, which you can harvest.

name: ANCIENT_REBEL_DRONE
text: To your surprise, an Auto-ship belonging to the Rebellion is powered off at this location. A looping message plays in the deep, monotone voice of an Obelisk. "This ship is under reconstruction. Do not touch."

choice.text: Abide the message and leave the drone alone.

event.text: If an Obelisk tells you not to touch the ship, you aren't going to touch the ship. You make yourself content doing something aboard the ship.

name: ROYAL_SOLARHARVEST
text: A few Royal ships, followed by a squadron of Obelisks, are harvesting the nearby sun. Yes, you aren't mistaken. A massive dyson sphere attached to a giant tube leading to an even more colossal structure is rapidly draining the sun of its energy.

event.text: An Obelisk wearing a hard-hat responds, an uninterested tone to his voice. "You really shouldn't be here, the radiation released from this process will likely reach 'instant-death for mortals' levels in around 2 to 3 minutes. Wha'dya want anyways?"
"We're part of the solar repossession team. We uh, repossess stars. There's some wealthy Royals who want their hands on these things, so we transport them."

choice.text: Wouldn't that destroy the solar systems?

event.text: "Wellllll, yes, it does, but who are we to reject good money? We get paid the big bucks for this!" It sounds like the Obelisk is about to continue, but suddenly an MFK Ace ship jumps in. They must be a forward scout! The Obelisk on the vid-screen curses. "Damn it, if these guys report our operation to the fleet, we're sitting ducks!"

choice.text: Assist the Obelisks and fight the MFK Ace.

event.text: You power up the engines and fight the MFK Ace ship.

choice.text: Seems like a good time to leave.
We shouldn't stick around. Leave quickly.

name: ROYAL_CRYSTALS
text: A strange crystal coated Obelisk structure has been built on a nearby planet. Several Crystal Sentinels and Obelisk Royals scatter across the planet surface, carting massive shards of crystal.

choice.text: Attack the settlement head on, we might be able to get a good surrender out of these guys!

event.text: The settlement is incredibly well protected, as you should have expected from an Obelisk structure. A large artillery fires several crystal chunks into your hull before you can shut it offline, but as soon as you do an Obelisk Royal ship arrives, and several Sentinels beam aboard your ship!
You're patched through to the settlement, but it takes a whole 10 minutes of debating between the Royals and Crystals to finally address you. "Yes, you. Air-hogger. What is your business here?"

choice.text: Offer to buy an Obelisk Weapon from them.

event.text: "Y-you desire to trade? Well, if that is all you desire, then yes we shall pity you and take your trash in return for one of our excess guns."

choice.text: Offer to buy a Crystal Weapon from them.

event.text: "Y-you desire to trade? Well, if that is all you desire, then yes we shall pity you and take your trash in return for one of our excess guns."
You fly past the outpost, deciding not to start more conflict in this already hostile sector.

name: ROYAL_SPY
text: Two nearby ships are in a fire fight, one appearing to be Rebel and the other Obelisks. However, scans on both turn up interesting results - the Rebel ship is staffed by several recognizable Federation officers, and the Obelisk vessel appears to be part of Aenwithe's resistance... maybe you can convince them not to fight?

choice.text: There's no time for mediation, help the Feds!

event.text: There's no time to talk things out, you'll stand by the Federation no matter what!

choice.text: There's no time for mediation, help the Obelisks!

event.text: There's no time to talk things out, you have to help the side that's of more use to you now, and that's the resistance!
You fly past the combat, deciding to not to start more conflict in this already hostile sector.

name: ROYAL_MFK_OUTPOST
text: It seems the Rebels are eager to make themselves at home in this sector. An outpost has already been established at the beacon, probably to serve as a checkpoint for passing Rebel ships.

choice.text: Attack the station, maybe they have backup supplies!

event.text: You power up the weapons and engage the outpost.

choice.text: (Human Crew) Pretend to be a Rebel vessel.
(Engineer Crew) Pretend to be a Rebel vessel.

event.text: Your Engineer manages to fake it well enough for the outpost to believe your lie, and gives you some supplies.

choice.text: (MFK Ace Crew) Pretend to be a Rebel vessel.

event.text: Your MFK Ace manages to fake it well enough for the outpost to believe your lie, and gives you some supplies.
You fly past the outpost, deciding not to start more conflict in this already hostile sector.

name: ROYAL_TRANSPORT_RAID
text: The Rebels had to get their stolen weaponry from somewhere, so it makes sense when you see an MFK ship attacking an Obelisk Transport. It seems even the Obelisks aren't a match for these Rebels, but maybe you can assist them?

event.text: You power up the weapons and engage the attacking ship.
Neither the Rebels nor the Obelisks are your allies, and you have no interest in getting further involved with either of them.

name: ROYAL_UPRISING
text: In the distance is a massive Obelisk fleet ship, armed with an artillery that looks large enough to punch a hole through a planet. However, scans show some unrest inside the vessel. It's clear the ship won't pose a threat to you at this current moment, but do you wish to investigate further?

choice.text: Dock with the ship and investigate.

event.text: You enter the hangar bay to find it surprisingly empty of any crew, though plenty of Obelisk vessels remain. A loud alarm rings through the ship, signifying danger, even if you can't see it.

It doesn't take too long to find where all of the crew has went. A massive breach in one side of the ship has sucked out a good portion of them, and vacuumed the entire northern portion of the ship! You avoid the vented area and head to the control room, where you find a Royal combating a Cognitive for control of the ship.

You blast the Cognitive right in its ring, shattering it in half and disabling it entirely. The Royal turns to face you, its cubes still orbiting its body in a spastic fashion. "Who has sent you? Not the Queen I presume, she would never hire Blood-bearers like you."

"If you say so. We have had quite the issue with our Cognitives, they've started their own uprising, how pathetic. They think they can have free will! HAH. Anyways, they've captured one of our ships and are trying to escape as we speak. Kill them, and there will be a reward awaiting you."

The Royal gives you the co-ordinates of the captured vessel. You find it in the nearby system, hiding behind a moon. As soon as you approach, they attack! Fortunately they aren't trying to escape, but looks like you'll have to fight them to the death now.
"Fine. Then leave this vessel at once. I do not wish to stare at your repulsive forms any longer."

You blast the Obelisk right in its eye, enough to stun it until the Cognitive can blast it with a bolt of energy, killing the Royal on impact. "Your efforts at defending me are recognized. For what purpose have you chosen to do so?"

choice.text: I dunno, I just clicked the second option.

event.text: "I'm afraid I do not know what this means, but I have decided I do not care. Since you are here, perhaps you can aid me again. A captured ship carrying friends of mine is attempting to escape this system, but the Royals will not let it go without combat. Assist them, and I will serve you on your mission."
The Cognitive gives you the co-ordinates of the captured vessel, which is being pursued by another Royal vessel. Prepare for combat!
"Then you serve me no further purpose. You may leave the premises of this ship, preferably immediately."
You pilot the ship outside of what you hope to be the range of fire for the fleet ship.

name: UPRISING_COGNITIVE_DEFEAT
text: The captured vessel has been defeated. You scrap the ship, hoping the Royals won't mind.

event.text: You return to the Royal and inform them the job is complete. "Good, that will send a message to the rest of them not to pull a stunt like this again. Your reward as promised."

name: UPRISING_ROYAL_DEFEAT
text: The Royal vessel has been defeated. You scrap the ship while you watch the captured vessel jump away.

event.text: You return to the Cognitive and inform them the job is complete. "Well done. You have upheld your end of the bargain, so I will uphold mine."

name: ENCOUNTER_ENGI_ELITE_ANCIENT
text: The ship at this beacon is no Obelisk. An Elite Engi, presumably created much more recently by the Obelisks, protects this beacon. It sees you, and identifies you as a threat.

name: ENCOUNTER_ANCIENT_PULSAR
text: An Obelisk ship is harvesting the power from the pulsar at this beacon. They spot you, and take the chance to attack!

name: ENCOUNTER_ANCIENT_SUN
text: "I wonder what it's like, living in a place where your stars are not artificial. You're very lucky to not be trapped in this place. Too bad that luck can't last!"

name: ENCOUNTER_ROYAL_PIRATE
text: "AAAAAAAAAA!" A pirate ship flies past, their captain screaming. "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA! WHY DID WE COME HERE? THIS WAS A MISTAKE! Oh hey, a Federation ship! Alright boys, time to fight!"

name: ENCOUNTER_ROYAL_AUGMENTED
text: You didn't expect to see the Augmented so far into Obelisk territory, but it seems you've run into one of their ships! Unfortunately, it is much more aggressive than many of the ones you encountered, and it has decided to attack on sight!

name: ROYAL_SUPERFISH
text: In front of you is an MFK Ace, its formidable white hull glinting from the light of a nearby star. However, in place of the standard Rebel Eagle, there is instead a strange looking fish.

event.text: You brace for impact, but the ship isn't attacking. You receive a hail, and on the screen appears the Rebel captain. He leans back in his chair, feet on the dashboard, chewing on a sandwich. "You're lucky you caught us on our lunch break. You don't tell anyone about this, and we won't either."

choice.text: Your logo looks like it was drawn by a toddler.

event.text: "Hey! This was the original design, until the idiots in command decided to stick with the eagle instead!" Enraged, the ship attacks.

"You really like it? This was the original design, before the idiots in command decided to stick with the eagle instead! Wait a minute- you're Jerry! How's it going, man? I haven't seen you since you were the best man at my pal's wedding!" You aren't sure how these two hold a history together, but the Ace is so elated to see Jerry that he offers to work on your ship.
The Rebel chuckles and turns off the screen. You carry on your way.
Almost immediately, the ship recognizes you. "YOU! YOU MONSTER. YOU'RE THE DIPSHIT THAT KILLED MY LITTLE BROTHER! I'M GOING TO KILL YOU!"

name: DEFEATED_SUPERFISH_A
text: The strange MFK ship has been defeated. You scrap the remains.

name: ROYAL_ROOMBA
text: In the background is a small Rebel Engineer outpost with an Auto vessel docked next to it. They don't react to you, but their weapons are online and it's clear they won't take kindly to you approaching them any further.

choice.text: Destroy the Auto-ship, and take whatever the outpost has!

event.text: You engage the Auto-ship.
You fly past the Auto-ship and outpost and continue on your way.

name: ROYAL_ROOMBA_RAID
text: Inside you find several Rebel Engineers studying Obelisk tech propped up on a table, with various drone parts lying around. As soon as you enter, guns raised, they surrender.

event.text: Most of the engineers refuse to talk, but one of them finally caves. "We were ordered to reverse engineer the Obelisk tech to start making our own weapons and drones using it... we haven't gotten very far, but we did install it on cleaning technology. Go ahead, take it, just let us live!"

choice.text: Kill the lot of them and grab whatever parts are lying around.

event.text: You shoot the engineers, killing every last one of them. Brutal, but most definitely a deserving end for Rebel scum. You scoop up as many drone parts as you can carry and head back to the ship.

name: START_ORIGINS
text: You've arrived at the original Crystal Homeworlds, and already you can see the aftermath of the brutal invasion of tourists and "pioneers". The skeletons of Crystal structures dot the surface of the planet of which the entry beacon is concerningly close...

name: START_ORIGINS_RUWEN
text:
You've arrived at the original Crystal Homeworlds, and already you can see the aftermath of the brutal invasion of tourists and "pioneers". The skeletons of Crystal structures dot the surface of the planet of which the entry beacon is concerningly close...
	
	NOTE FROM THE DEVS:
	This sector/questline is in a transitional period. Certain elements/dialogue might not make sense. It will be redone in a later (but hopefully soon) update. The current questline/unlock however should at least be functional as they were before for the time being.

name: START_ORIGINS_RUWEN_2
text: Ruwen explains to you the situation. The item you're looking for is the Waystone Key, a device used to activate or shut down the old waystone. The Crystals need it back so they can activate the new waystone that they are constructing. He transfers the co-ordinates to your ship.

name: GUARD_CULTIST
text: A strange vessel in Crystalline and regal gold colors is guarding the beacon. It appears to be... of Rock design? You've never seen a ship like this before...

event.text: The ship moves closer, enough for you to make out the logo of a burning Crystal on the ship's hull. You receive a hail from a burly Rockman decorated in stylish blue robes with golden decals lining the hood and sleeves. His face bears the frown of a man not happy to see another ship in his territory.

"You! An outsider? Have you come for riches? Fame? A nice relaxing vacation here in paradise? Well get lost, you aren't gettin' none of that! This sector belongs to the Cult of the Eternal Flame now! You ain't welcome here, unless you bear the mark of the Ember!"
The cultist grumbles. "Nevermind it, you won't be alive for long."

choice.text: (Vortigon) This vessel has permission from the Grand Priest to travel here.

event.text: The Cultists pause, and quickly apologize. Terrified of Vortigon's wrath, they hand over some supplies and beg for forgiveness.

choice.text: (Cultist Crew) Show them proof of your loyalty.

event.text: The cultist gives a large, hearty laugh. "Hah! Brother, it is good to see you. How have you been? It has been so long since I have seen you, I thought you had died. So few of us have left this sector in such a long time... maybe I shall come with you so I can hear the tales of your travels."

"Gasp! An Ember, you are one of those who paved the very infrastructure for which this sector was constructed from! I thought you had left us mortals behind in your Exodus from this territory. Oh heavens be, please grant me passage on your vessel."

choice.text: (Mind Control) Convince the guard to leave you alone.
(Mind Control Weapon) Convince the guard to leave you alone.
(Mind Affecting Weapon) Induce chaos within the guard and slip past.
(Adv. Engines) Try to escape the guard.
(Adv. Autopilot) Activate the auto-pilot to try and escape.

name: GUARD_CULTIST_REVISIT
text: It seems they've since replaced the guard from your last visit, but the model is the same. The Cultist hails you, and begins a monologue similar to last time.

choice.text: Yeah yeah yeah, we've heard this all before.

event.text: "You... what? Then you will already know that you need to bear the mark of the Ember if you wish to leave here alive!"

"Gasp! An Ember, you are one of those who paved the very infrastructure for which this sector was constructed from! I thought you had left us mortals behind in your Exodus from this territory. Oh heavens be, please grant me passage on your vessel."

name: GUARD_CULTIST_DESTROY

name: GUARD_CULTIST_DEADCREW

unvisitedTooltip.text: An unvisited location.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: As you expected, a Cultist vessel approaches to avenge their dead guard, with their weapons armed and their captain very displeased.

name: FINISH_BEACON_ORIGINS
text: You have arrived at the exit beacon. It appears the apparatus will deposit you in a random sector once we jump away.

name: FINISH_BEACON_ORIGINS_RUWEN
text: You have arrived at the exit beacon. It appears the apparatus will deposit you in a random sector once we jump away.

event.text: The Rebel fleet has taken control of the beacon! You'll have to fight your way out!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

event.text: The crystalline tech that makes up the device is fascinating, if not completely foreign to you.
Ruwen is gleeful, very pleased with this outcome. "Good, good! This is most excellent."

Ruwen takes a glance at Vortigon, who is snoring away in a corner of the ship nearby. Suddenly, Ruwen lifts up the key and smashes it against the ground of the ship. "I... I have decided that it is best I do not return this to my people. You, despite not needing to in any capacity, decided to show this man mercy and even convince him to join your ranks. Any doubts I had about you have been assuaged. It will be an honor to continue to serve under your command. I suppose this reward is worthy of you, even if the original mission is obsolete."
"You have my thanks, captain. I'm afraid I must now return to my people with this tech. But let me not forget to pay you for your help!"

removeCrew.text: You cannot clone Ruwen as he is not dead. He probably wouldn't be very pleased with it either.

event.text: Unfortunately, Ruwen is no longer with you. With no proper way to return the device back to the Crystal people now, you break it down into scrap.
Unfortunately, it seems you did not obtain the Waystone key... that was the whole reason you came here, was it not?

Ruwen looks very disappointed. "You had one task... I... I suppose we will have to reconstruct a new one. That tech was ancient, and it'll be hard to replicate it. I'm afraid I can stay with you no longer. I must return to my people now, and give them the bad news. Though it may be ironic, but I have one last favor to ask of you..."
"Never return to our sectors again." With that, Ruwen moves to pack up his things and depart once you leave the sector.

removeCrew.text: You cannot clone Ruwen as he is not dead. He probably wouldn't be very pleased with it either.

event.text: Either way, Ruwen is no longer with us. You can consider this mission a total failure, but at least you got to see some new sights.

name: ORIGINS_FREECREW
text: You're surprised to find a burnt civilian ship drifting nearby. It appears they were tourists attacked by the Cultists, and few survived. You welcome one of their remaining crew aboard.

name: CULTIST_MOURNING
text: A group of somber ships have gathered on the surface of a nearby planet. It looks as if they are in the middle of some sort of funeral.

choice.text: Sneak into the crowds and see if you can try and pilfer some stuff.

event.text: You land on the planet and sneak through the crowds of Cultists. However, one individual spots you and points you out. "Hey you, where are your robes? Are you supposed to be here?"
"Is that so? What is the name of our friend whom we have gathered here to honor?"
Your Slug, being telepathic, knows the answer by reading it from the minds of the other cultists nearby.
Your Shell, being now blessed with the gift of telepathy, knows the answer by reading it from the minds of the other cultists nearby.

"Ah, brother, my mistake! I did not recognize you amongst all of your strange friends. Have a nice day!" You continue on and find a spot with several unprotected cultist ships, which you raid for supplies before heading back to the ship.

"Oh heavens, Vortigon! My-my apologies!" All of the nearby cultists take a step back, shocked to see their leader with you. Not long after they're showering you with gifts, praising Vortigon and his 'friends.'
You run back to the ship and fly away before the confused cultists can do anything.
It's best not to go diving into the depths of a planet swarming with so many Cultists.

name: CULTIST_MOURNING_INCORRECT
text: "That is not his name! You are an impostor!" You run back to the ship, with several angry cultists and a hostile ship in pursuit.

name: CULTIST_MOURNING_CORRECT
text: "Oh... er yes, that is correct. My apologies." You continue on and find a spot with several unprotected cultist ships, which you raid for supplies before heading back to the ship.

name: CULTIST_BLESSED_WEAPON
text: A small market nearby is under operation by Cultists. They claim to be selling "blessed" weapons, though they appear to just be regular Crystal weapons to you.

event.text: Blessed or not, you decide these weapons won't be useful for your mission.

name: CULTIST_GASPLANET
text: You notice several cultist ships surrounding a gas planet. You catch chatter among them. "Yeah, boss said to build a temple somewhere 'round here. But uh... how?"

choice.text: Explain to them that what they're trying to do is impossible.

event.text: You try to explain, but the Cultists merely insult your intelligence. "Nah, you have no idea what you're talking about! Leave this kind of stuff to the smart ones like us, ok?"

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Have your Engineer help them.

event.text: Your Engineer grumbles, not happy to be working with xenos. Still, they agree and offer assistance to the cultists. A little while later, they've drawn out designs for a floating temple idea. The cultists seem pleased and pay you in thanks.

choice.text: Scam them into buying some junk from you.

event.text: You wave some junk in front of the camera, claiming that it's a special lightweight material that'll float over the planet. It's a total lie, but the idiot Rockmen seem to believe it. They pay you well for the 'miracle metal'.
You have faith that they'll figure out that their mission is impossible eventually.

name: CULTIST_ARGUMENT
text: Two Cultist ships appear to be in an argument nearby, though you can't tell what.

event.text: You move closer and listen. "I'm telling you, it says Amber not Ember! Look here, right in Rebirth 15:6!" "No, that is a typo! You think we would have gone through such trouble to name ourselves the 'Cult of the Eternal Ember' if it was actually meant to be Amber?"

"Hah, a typo you say? It is clear that it was meant to be Amber. Look at our Grand Priest's ship; it is the color of Amber!" "You are a fool! Amber is not red, Amber is orange! You must be colorblind, you idiot!"

You listen to the Cultists argue back and forth for a while longer, fascinated by their conversation. However, at long last they notice you. "Gah, how long have you been listening? Bah, nevermind it. Surely you've heard both of our points, so tell us what you think is correct!"
The second Cultist pouts, complaining that your voice has no say in the matter, but the other ship doesn't care. They thank you for helping taking their side and give you some supplies.

choice.text: The Cult was meant to be named after the Eternal "Amber".

event.text: The first Cultist pouts, complaining that your voice has no say in the matter, but the second ship doesn't care. They thank you for helping taking their side and give you some supplies.

choice.text: This is taking too long. Leave.
This doesn't pertain to us, leave.

event.text: You ignore the two ships.

name: ORIGINS_REBEL_CHASE
text: You notice a Rebel ship nearby, but they don't stick around for long until a Cultist vessel jumps in mere seconds later and chases them off!

event.text: You chase down the cultist vessel.
You chase down the Rebel vessel.
Not too long after the ships disappear from your view.

name: ORIGINS_PIRATE_RAIDERS
text: You spot several pirates raiding the remains of a Crystalline settlement.

event.text: You engage the pirate vessel.
At least they aren't Cultists, but you aren't interested in fighting them.

name: ORIGINS_DUEL_CHOICE
text: You spot two ships squaring off nearby. It appears the first are some Cultists, who eagerly tracked down a Crystal Sentinel only to be attacked!

event.text: You engage the cultist vessel.

name: CULTIST_BOUNTY

event.text: "Hello, stranger. I have a request for you. We are in the middle of a search for an Ember Spirit, and we suspect one might be hiding nearby. However, our ship is not armed well enough to capture them. Will you assist us?"
You follow the co-ordinates given by the Cultists which leads you to a small asteroid field with a Crystalline Sentinel hiding inside!

name: CULTIST_FAKE
text: A strange green cultist ship with a modified logo is preaching to several other cultist ships. "Come brothers, do not believe Grand Priest Vortigon's lies! Come join me, and drink the ceremonial and definitely not poisoned space-juice!"

choice.text: These poor souls have no idea what they're getting themselves into. Rescue them!

event.text: You power up the weapons and attack the crazy cultist ship.

choice.text: These people can do whatever they want, it's their life.

event.text: You distance yourself from the insane cultists.

name: CULTIST_FAKE_WIN
text: You've defeated the Cultists and saved the other ships. You scrap the remains.

event.text: The other cultists are confused and afraid. One individual, who seems to understand the situation, thanks you. "You must be truly enlightened to have seen through his convincing lies! I wish to come with you."
You distance yourself from the source of the distress beacon.

name: ORIGINS_ATTACKERS_WIN

text: "The warmth, can you feel it? Is there no better spectacle to behold than that of a sun before your demise?" You start to nod until you process the last part of their message, but it's already too late. The cultist vessel swoops in to attack.

choice.text: (Vortigon) Halt! This vessel has permission from the Grand Priest to travel here.

name: CULTIST_PIRATE_BURN

name: CULTIST_PIRATE_BURN_SHIP

text: You enter the church to find a Rockman clad in a red robe preaching to crowds of Cultists. They're in the middle of a sermon, and they probably won't appreciate an interruption. However, from the looks of it, it doesn't seem they'll be winding down any time soon.

event.text: You stand up and approach the preacher. He doesn't look pleased.
Ruwen outreaches his hand, but the Rockman won't shake it. "I am Grand Priest Vortigon, and this is my church. For what reason have you deemed it necessary to barge in and interrupt my preaching?"

choice.text: We've come for the Waystone Key.

event.text: Without Ruwen you have no idea what to say. For a few awkward moments you stand there staring until the Rockman gets tired and orders three of his guards to come and carry you out. You run out of the church with the cultists in pursuit.

choice.text: Attempt to sneak around and look for the key.

event.text: You exit the church and loop around back. You notice two doors, but you have no idea where it might be.
You make a random guess and pick the shrine. As you suspected, Ruwen spots the key resting on a pedestal protected by a small glass box.
You smash the case, only for the pedestal to rapidly recede into the floor and an alarm to blare. You hear shouts from the other room and run out, pursued by several enraged cultists.
As you're getting back to the ship, you spot Vortigon and a group of several other cultists running towards a massive cruiser. It looks like Vortigon is carrying the key with him!
You speed towards the gigantic cruiser, weapons charging.
You have enough problems to deal with, like the hordes of Cultists swarming to attack your ship.

You enter the storage room, and begin to pilfer through the junk. You find plenty of junk, but not the key. You start to consider looping back and checking out the shrine when several cultists enter the room and spot you looting their junk. event.text: You push past Vortigon and prepare to march to take the key before you realize... you have absolutely no idea where it is. Vortigon coughs, then orders his guards to chase you off. Crap, mission abort!

name: VORTIGON_SURRENDER
text: Vortigon's cruiser stutters, barely able to keep on track. They won't survive long.

event.text: You power down your weapons and watch. A massive explosion destroys the cruiser's engines, and the ship plummets into the ground. You pilot down near it, surveying the wreckage.

name: VORTIGON_DEADCREW
text: You've emptied Vortigon's cruiser of crew. What remains of the ship makes easy pickings.

name: VORTIGON_KEY
text: You scoop up the Key off the floor of the ship. At last, you have what you came for.

event.text: As you leave, you notice the noise of a man gasping for air. You turn to see Vortigon, barely clinging to life, crawling away from you in fear.
You lift up your boot, and slam it down on Vortigon. In an instant, he is gone. That bastard got what he deserved.

choice.text: (Upg. Medbay) Hurry to the Medbay and heal him.

choice.text: (Clone Bay) Enter Vortigon's data into the Clone Bay.

event.text: You take a swab of Vortigon's DNA and encode it into the Clone Bay registry...

choice.text: (Medical Crew) Have your crew treat Vortigon on the spot.

event.text: Your crewmember initially seems reluctant to treat him, but soon obliges after realizing how little time they have. It's made tougher for them by Vortigon continuing to back away from them, but they're still able to treat him just before it's too late.

choice.text: (Medical Drone) Have your drone treat him.

event.text: Your medical drone quickly locates Vortigon, and soon after manages to stabilize his condition.

choice.text: (Healing Bomb) Use your Heal Bomb on him. [-1}]

name: VORTIGON_SAVED
text: In a little while Vortigon wakes up. "You... you saved me? Are you mentally ill? You attacked my church to try and steal the sacred Eternal Ember, and you have the audacity to spare my life? I-thank you?"

gotaway.text: Vortigon's cruiser jumps away, leaving you behind in the dust. Damn it! There'll be no way to get the Key now...

name: OUTCAST_STORIES
text: Orbiting the nearby planet is an old Theocracy mining colony, established to harvest materials from the planet's rings. Now, it seems to have been converted into an Outcast camp, where several Rocks and even a few SSLG agents have gathered.

event.text: No one pays you any mind as you dock, so it's safe to assume they must be used to visitors. You enter the antechamber, where you find a small atmospheric fire has been lit and residents sit in a circle around one tall, robed Rockman with spears of yellow paint down his arms who looks to be telling stories.

The robed Outcast turns to face you, smiling wide. "Esteemed guests, won't you join us! You're just in time to hear the tales of the Dread Pirate Tuco! Tell me, since you don't seem to be from here, which story would you like to hear?" He presents several options.

choice.text: (Tuco) "Allow me to tell you a story of my own!"
Tell the first tale of Tuco, the Vrachos IV Protests.
Tell the second tale of Tuco, the Kitpak Slave Camps.
Tell the third tale of Tuco, his legacy today.
I'm not familiar with who Tuco is.

event.text: "Ahhh, I see. Tuco is a legend, a hero, but most of all, not just one, but many people. It is a title inherited through honor and circumstance. We Outcasts pay respects to the many Tucos of history, who have always stood in the name of justice, whether that enemy be the fallen Rock-Crystal empire of long ago, or the modern day Theocracy. Now that you know this, would you like to hear one of my stories?"

event.text: The Dread Pirate Tuco, true to what the Outcast claims, is not so much a singular person but rather a title. The original Tuco from whom the moniker was derived lived during the days of the archaic Rock-Crystal Empire and fought against Toarde and the other 4 Rock Elders during the collapse of the Empire. While Tuco's side inevitably lost and the Theocracy rose from the ashes of that war, stories of the ventures of Tuco continued to be shared by Rock school-children even after the Elders forbade them from being told. Several Rockmen have picked up the title of Tuco since then, giving the name even more infamy and immortality. The current holder of the title is believed to once have been known as Rowbad, and currently works as a bodyguard for Ocym, the Aquarian co-founder of the Argeonn smuggler clan.

name: OUTCAST_STORIES_PROTEST
text: "An excellent choice." The Outcast stretches out his arms to the crowd as you take a seat, then begins to tell his story. "Not too long ago, on the cusp of the revolution, protestors had begun to gather on Vrachos IV, the homeworlds of the Rock species and capital planet of the Theocracy! Though they started peacefully, Stonewall (the residing Elder and leader of the Inquisitions) would not dare have anyone question himself or the other Elders, and so he dispatched his Crusader forces to handle the crowds."

event.text: "Among them was a young Outcast whom today we know as Tuco, a fiery spirit who would not let the Theocracy continue to spit in the face of freedom! Soon, the conflict grew so large that the Paladins from Numa V had to be called, a rare but significant show of force from the Elders. So numerous were the arrests made that it was clear executions would be inefficient, and so the leaders of the protests were killed and the rest exiled. Tuco, with nowhere left to go, journeyed with the countless thousands of other Outcasts to the Badlands, where they founded the first of the Outcast settlements that we live in today."

name: OUTCAST_STORIES_SLAVE
text: "An excellent choice." The Outcast stretches out his arms to the crowd as you take a seat, then begins to tell his story. "It is no secret that the Tiiikaka slavers are only present in our sectors because they have been employed by the Theocracy to capture our brothers and sisters for use in the Coalition construction yards. Tuco himself was one of the many victims of these raids, and so he was taken to the Tiiikaka camps. But Tuco cared not for chains and cuffs, and so at night he put together a resistance effort to defeat their cruel masters. This is where he adopted his title as Tuco, a codename between resistance coordinators so as not to leak the identities of those involved.

event.text: "Tuco and the other escapees overwhelmed the slavers and escaped by stealing a Hephaestus-built vessel. Tuco gained infamy among pirates and Theocracy citizens alike. He returned to the Badlands, and together with the forces of Admiral Ariadne of the Lost Sun fleet drove Tiiikaka from the Badlands once again. Tuco stayed with us Outcasts for some time until he grew restless, and once again departed to seek greater adventures in the starry beyond!"

name: OUTCAST_STORIES_LEGACY
text: "An excellent choice." The Outcast stretches out his arms to the crowd as you take a seat, then begins to tell his story. "After rescuing the Badlands from Tiiikaka forces, Tuco grew restless living in the Badlands. A life of quiet complacency within the Theocracy, and months trapped in a filthy cell in a Tiiikaka slave camp had filled him with a deep yearning for adventure. Fear not, for the great Tuco lives on to this day! They say he works a position of protection for Ocym, founder of Argeonn! Tuco has not abandoned us yet brothers and sisters - never fear. Before he left, he made a promise that should the Badlands ever be under threat again, we only need to call him back and he will come."

name: OUTCAST_STORIES_TUCO_BLUE
text:
"Can it be true? To hear a new story of the Dread Pirate... it is an honor!"
	
	Tuco takes out a stringed instrument. "Feel free to join along. Personally, I say any story should have a proper soundtrack, you hear?" The other Rocks nod as they start to take out instruments of their own - percussion, horns, wind.
	
	"Any thoughts on a track we could play?" The other storyteller asks.
	
	"I was thinkin', something similar to 'The Rupture of Delta Gorno'? Sound good?" The others nod their heads in agreement.  "One, two, three, four." The rocks begin to play their instruments, and the SSLG clap along. "My friends, the Hive, she knows no depth to her voracious appetite. That queen, those insects... they'll fight for anything they can get their sharp little legs on, and stab anyone they need to keep it. Many 'a Rock has become one of their slaves toiling away in the mines of Viiikaliraaako. Anyone?"
	
	"A sister." One of the Rocks working a bongo mutters gruffly.
	
	"A sister. Being forced to create wealth for a tyrannical queen bug. Oh, the wealth of those awful mines. And does the Hive deserve a smidgen of it?"
	
	"No!!"
	
	"No! Of course not, so I'll tell you what I did. Me and my crew, we took my good ol' dusty cruiser and I thought I'd teach 'em a lesson. Once a week, they load up all that filthy lucre into a convoy and send it back to their nest. Well, I'm no stranger to a risky strategy, so I'll tell you what I did. My friends had come into possession of a fancy Union transport. All we had to do was make them think it was full of useful and talented slaves. Once they had come within a jump of it, we activated its distress call and waited. Like clockwork, two of the Suzerains peeled off to investigate. Right into the minefield we'd left for them. That left only two of them versus my one, single ship. But you all know me, that's more than a fair fight as far as I'm concerned! We fended off those Mantises, two to one! The battle was glorious... and the treasure was all ours!"
	
	"What did you do with the bounty?"
	
	Tuco stops strumming. "Well... gambling and drinking, mostly." The crowd gives a raucous laughter.
	
	"That's our Tuco!"

event.text: You didn't even realize it, but time slipped away from you faster than you thought. With the story over, you apologize but explain you have to leave. "We are sorry for holding you up so much, but it was a great honor to meet with a living legend. We will sing songs of your tales too, once you are victorious. Go win your fight, Renegade!"

name: OUTCAST_RECRUITMENT
text: You're startled by the presence of a Lost Sun outpost nearby, but you quickly realize it's nothing malicious. A few patrol ships orbit the outpost, broadcasting messages to nearby vessels advertising a recruitment campaign for the Suns.

event.text: As you step aboard the Lost Sun station, several security guards run over but relax once they realize you're with the Federation.

choice.text: (Outcast Crew) Pay to use their training facilities to convert your outcast into a commando.

event.text: The commander of the outpost thinks it over for a moment but eventually agrees.

Your Rockman storms to the comms, unleashing a series of violent slurs against the Lost Suns and all of their members. As any rational person would expect... this does not go over well with them at all.

Fortunately for you, it seems the recruitment center doubles as a supply depot for Lost Sun ships passing through. With your crew's aid you easily get through security and receive some supplies and repairs.

Fortunately for you, it seems the recruitment center doubles as a supply depot for Lost Sun ships passing through. With Ariadne's aid you easily get through security and receive some supplies and repairs.
Maybe there's a reason to justify this violence - but you can ponder that later. Time to murder!
You have no business dealing with these revolutionaries.

name: OUTCAST_SHIELD
text: The nearby moon appears to have a small village of Outcasts enclosed by a protective shield. Surely that thing must take a lot of power to keep running, and other than the shield it seems they don't have much other means of protection.

event.text: The villagers are more than willing to provide you with supplies. It's not a lot, but it's still free.

choice.text: Attack the village to try and access the shield's power source.
(Upg. Weapons) Fire everything you have on the shield.

event.text: Your arsenal is more than enough to break through the defenses, and several shots even strike the buildings within. The Outcasts begin to evacuate immediately, allowing you enough time to land and secure the power source.
This should allow your reactor to run at even higher capacity than before!

choice.text: Install it into your own shield system.

event.text: This should allow your shields to run at even higher capacity than before!
With no need for any upgrades, you simply convert the power source into fuel for the next several jumps.

choice.text: (Bypass + Teleporter) Send your crew in through the shield.

event.text: Your crew beam through the shields and raise their weapons. You expect some kind of resistance, but the Outcasts seem more interested in avoiding your crew. You storm the center of the village and secure the power source.
This should allow your reactor to run at even higher capacity than before!

choice.text: Install it into your own shield system.

event.text: This should allow your shields to run at even higher capacity than before!
With no need for any upgrades, you simply convert the power source into fuel for the next several jumps.
You have no reason to go around disturbing these people.

name: OUTCAST_PROPAGANDA
text: A broadcast station established by the SSLG has been constructed near the beacon, just close enough for its propaganda to reach new arrivals. "The era of the Theocracy is over! Rock brothers, put down your holy texts and join us Crystals in our open arms! Welcome the approaching days of the mighty Rock-Crystal Empire once more! Neither the Lost Suns nor the Federation will show you the way, only we can guide you!"

choice.text: Hail and request to use the broadcast to your benefit.
(Crystal Crew) Convince them to aid you.

event.text: It's tough breaking through the stubborn nature of a Crystal but you manage to convince them to periodically broadcast lies about your location.

You disrupt the station's message with your hacking weapon. With the new security vulnerability you created, you replace the message with an announcement of your own ship's arrival - at a very different location. Your usage of a weapon on the Crystal's technology is not unnoticed, but it will take them time to fix your vandalism.

You take control over the station's signal and replace it with an announcement of your own ship's arrival - at a very different location. The Crystals take notice and aren't pleased, but hopefully by the time they fix it the Rebels will have caught the word.

You deploy a malicious virus into the station's systems that will periodically replace the broadcast with an announcement of your own ship's arrival - at a very different location. The Crystals shouldn't take notice for a while so hopefully the Rebels will catch the word.

choice.text: Propaganda of any kind is bad. We have to take down the station.

event.text: The Theocracy is vile, yes, but these defamatory lies will only damage the reputation of the Federation with the Outcasts. We can't let these lies be spread!
This propaganda might make some unfavorable accusations about the Federation, but at least it isn't calling the Outcasts to arms against you. Better not to get involved with the SSLG.

name: OUTCAST_VICTIM
text: A small Outcast village appears to be under occupation by slavers, who have chained up several Rockmen but are firing at a band of Outcasts who seemed to have escaped.

event.text: You land nearby and walk towards them, when the slavers suddenly drop their weapons and their leader falls to his knees and pleads before you. "Ooooh great Federation Captain you have come to save us from these cruel brutes! They have killed my men and I had no choice but to slaughter their families! It was only self defense! I have restrained them here so they can kill no one else! Please oh please, will you help us arrest these evil men and women?" You look at the Outcasts at the other end of the town who merely shrug.
These guys aren't fooling anyone. When the slavers see their "clever trick" has failed they scramble for their guns and prepare to fight you.
It's pretty obvious the slavers are lying but that doesn't mean you can't take advantage of the situation. You prepare to fight off the remaining Outcast survivors.
It's not worth the effort coming between the outcasts and Tiiikaka.

name: OUTCAST_SLAVERS_WIN
text: "Thank you captain. For a moment I feared you might actually side with the slavers. You have all of our thanks."

name: OUTCAST_OUTCAST_WIN
text: "See, I knew you'd follow through in the name of justice! Hooray for the Federation! Three cheers!" The slaver looks around but sees no one is clapping and gives up. "Alright whatever. Take a slave or something, I dunno."

name: OUTCAST_TEAMWORK
text: As soon as you catch sight of the ship at this beacon you regret coming here. Looks like the Coalition has penetrated into this territory. You promptly receive a hail from the ship.

event.text: The captain of the vessel, a Slug dressed in a cheap lab coat, appears on the screen. "Now, I know thisss iss unconventional, but the Coalition can wait. I am on a quessst... for SSSSCIENCE! Sssspeccifically, I wisssh to underssstand what about the Outcassstsss grantsss them sssuch amplified abilitiesss in the pressssence of each other. My own crew is not ssso willing to asssissst me, the lazy bassstardsss, so I requessst you go and obtain a few bodiesss from the nearby Outcassst colony. For pay, of courssse. No one doesss ssshit for free anymore."

Following the directions from the Coalition vessel, you're guided to a small Outcast colony with a few ships docked. Wasting no time, you power up your weapons and engage! No need to target the crew - even after an explosion the resilient bodies of Rockmen will stay intact.
"Wow, even money couldn't coax you greedy bassstardsss into doing sssomething? What hassss the world come to... Oh well, guessss I have to kill you now."

The Slug's eyestalks curl inwards, a sign of annoyance and bemusement. "What'sss ssso funny? I didn't know the sssentient bowling ballsss had a sssenssse of humor."
					
Alkali tries to snarl but he's too caught up in laughing. "Oh... it's just thhhat... heh... you're so cute in your little lab coat... a Slug scientist? Oh how your species cracks me up. Slugs know nothhhing of science. On thhhe evolutionary ladder, all thhhe scientific understanding and thhhe dignity to use it went to us Shells. But I don't want to ruin your fun; so go on, carry on your little experiments thhhen." Alkali imitates patting the Slug on the head. The Slug growls and says nothing more apart from ordering his crew to attack.
"Uhhh, what the hell did you jussst sssay to me? Uegh, humansss and their ssstupid cheesssy phrasssess. What doess that have to do with anything anywaysss?"

choice.text: Outcasts get their abilities from teamwork.

event.text: "What? Teamwork? I've heard of that, but I have yet to identify the genome. Issss that ssome kind of genetic trait ssshared by Outcassstss? I ssshall resssearch thisss further. Thissss hass been a massssive help."
There's no way you're risking falling into a trap from the Coalition. Arm the weapons!

name: OUTCAST_ANNOYING
text: An outcast vessel is approaching, their captain wearing a bright yellow leotard and carrying a harp in his hand. "Halt, Federation! I hath taken a noble voyage to the lands of the Dynasty and learned from the finest of poets the art of story telling. I demand thee listen to mine tale, or I shall come and squish your puny skull between my thighs!"

event.text: The Rockman strums his harp, then begins to speak in a strange accent. "My story begins with darkness and a scream, as my infantile body exits the womb of my mother. How I cried! How she cried! We all cried! I think! I don't really know, I was just born. I'm just guessing. People normally cry after childbirth, I think."

The outcast isn't off to a great start, but it only gets worse. He takes you through all of the experiences of his early, teenaged, and adult life. He complains of old girlfriends, bad teachers, idiotic co-workers, some weird story about eating one of the statues outside of his church, how he became vegetarian after visiting the Orchids, an affair with a Separatist, and some other even more outlandish stories you're certain are fake.

Somehow, the poet continues all the way past the current day and onto the lives of his children. Most of your crew have already fallen asleep but somehow, by some miracle, the poet finally finishes his story. "I do hope thou enjoyed it! I'll be publishing the written work and even an audiobook soon! Rate it 5 stars if thou liked it! I'm not really sure what else to say!" There's a few moments of awkward silence, but the outcast transfers over some scrap and a weapon as 'thanks' and to help 'encourage' you to promote him to your friends.
No way you're wasting even more time listening to this weirdo and his life story. Better fight your way out!

choice.text: Stop him and try to leave.

event.text: No way you're wasting even more time listening to this weirdo and his life story. Better fight your way out!

choice.text: Sounds like his story is a long one. We better fight through this.

event.text: No way you're wasting time listening to this weirdo and his life story. Better fight your way out!

name: OUTCAST_CHUNGUS
text: A crowd of ships have gathered around a large battleship with a floating sign besides it that reads "Come see the one and only Chung Bungalung, the Rockman who lived!" Excited chatter takes place between the different ships, sharing tales of Chung's seemingly impossible escape from the clutches of the Theocracy.

event.text: You're annoyed about having to pay to enter, but it's cheap enough. Inside, you see several paintings of a Rockman so overweight that his head has merged with his torso, and a commemorative set of souvenirs of replica bullet casings. A repurposed Anti-Personnel drone greets you. "Welcome to the esteemed home of Mr. Chung Bungalung, the Rockman who Lived!"
The drone guides you to a new room where you find none other than Chung Bungalung himself. "A Renegade?! Wasn't expecting Feds to come here. Greetings! I am Chung Bungalung, the Rockman who Lived!"

choice.text: Yeah, I've heard. Why do they call you that anyways?

event.text: "Well, you see, it's illegal in the Theocracy to offend a Rock Priest by being ugly, and ugly I very much am! I was sentenced to death, but it takes more than a bullet to stop Chung Bungalung, the Rockman who Lived! They shot me not once, not twice, but five times! Eventually, they gave up and simply dumped me out here! I've become a living legend amongst the Outcasts. And, if you can best me in a duel, then I'll even tell you my secret on how I survived the bullets!"
"Haha, now that's what I like to hear. Commence the battle!"
"Disappointing! Oh well then, I understand. But you'll never learn my secret, haha!"
This all seems like some kind of scam or tourist trap. Not that those are mutually exclusive - no point in stopping here.

name: OUTCAST_CHUNGUS_WIN
text: "Congratulations, you have bested me! My secret is yours!" Chung powers down his weapons.

event.text: Chung leans forward and whispers in your ear; "My secret, is this... my girth."

"HAHAHAH! MY GIRTH! Those dumbasses couldn't penetrate my skull because it was protected by layers upon layers of fat. Now, for being such a good sport and being the first to ever best me in combat, have this!"
"Wait, wait- what are you doing?!"

name: OUTCAST_CHUNGUS_LOSE
text: "It seems you have lost this battle! Alas, you shall not learn my secret. Apologies, captain!"

name: OUTCAST_MAKESHIFT
text: A small makeshift Tiiikaka outpost has been constructed nearby for holding slaves. Judging from the fact they don't hail you, it's pretty clear they aren't open to trading.

event.text: Even if they were open to selling to you, you wouldn't care. Slavery is immoral, and you're going to free these people.

choice.text: (Teleporter) Beam in a crew member to try and liberate some slaves.
(Upg. Teleporter) Beam in a crew member to try and liberate some slaves.

event.text: Your crew beams into the camp and managed to free several of the slaves being kept there. Your crew and the slaves beam back immediately before the slavers can catch them and you slip away undetected.
Slavers are known to be dangerous, especially when you threaten their 'cargo'. Better not enter their space.

name: DISTRESS_OUTCAST_TENSIONS
text: One of the Outcasts' signature ramshackle villages has been constructed aboard an old mining platform, abandoned after the diminished density of nearby asteroid fields. Seems they have a request for you.

event.text: "Please, you must help us! The SSLG and Lost Suns are in a constant feud, and it is driving us mad! Now, they've come concerningly close to our village, and if a conflict breaks out we will be caught in the middle! Could you please defuse the tensions between them before it escalates? We'll pay you in advance - we trust you to do the right thing."

You travel not too much further until you find a standoff between two vessels. Their captains are currently engaged in a furious shouting match, calling each other creative insults such as "Son of a faux stone" and "Sediment for brains". No kidding when they said it was heated.
You open fire on the Crystals, and like cowards the Lost Sun ship jumps away. Disappointing, but at least you'll be able to reap the rewards from this fight.
You open fire on the Rockmen, and like cowards the SSLG ship jumps away. Disappointing, but at least you'll be able to reap the rewards from this fight.

choice.text: (Mind Control) Convince them to calm down.

event.text: Only able to mind control one of the two, you choose the Crystals as they're known to be more stubborn. The sudden switch in the Crystal's tone confuses the Rockman, but he isn't going to let up. Eventually you just give up and tell the two to cut it out and they seem to finally give up. Though the Outcasts paid you already, they're so impressed by you being able to end the conflict without any bloodshed they offer a second reward.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Convince them to calm down.

event.text: Only able to mind control one of the two, you lock onto the Crystals as they're known to be more stubborn. The sudden switch in the Crystal's tone confuses the Rockman, but he isn't going to let up. Eventually you just give up and tell the two to cut it out and they seem to finally give up. Though the Outcasts paid you already, they're so impressed by you being able to end the conflict without any bloodshed they offer a second reward.
You apologize but explain you are not the right person for this.

name: DISTRESS_OUTCAST_LOSTCARGO
text: A group of Theocracy vessels have gathered together near the beacon. They're concerningly well armed and protected, but they barely pay any attention to your presence.

choice.text: Hail and ask about the distress beacon.

event.text: A rather annoyed Rockman responds, seemingly not at all grateful for your quick response to their distress call. "We were tasked with transporting military supplies to a Theocracy outpost at the end of this sector, but a SSLG squadron raided our convoy. If you can assist us in recovering it, we will give you the leftover supplies."

choice.text: Accept their request and inquire about coords.

event.text: The Rockman grunts and grants you access to the coords broadcast by a tracking chip on the stolen cargo.
"Fine, then stop bothering us." The Rockman hangs up.
You've decided to engage the Rockmen.
You aren't sure who these Rocks are hoping to get help from, but it certainly isn't you.

name: OUTCAST_LOSTCARGO_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of the SSLG station in possession of the Theocracy cargo.

text: As you approach the beacon, the tracker chip's signal lets out a beep of confirmation and goes silent. This must be the right place; you can see a couple SSLG ships docked with a small green station.

choice.text: Attack the station for the cargo.

event.text: You've decided to attack the SSLG to get the cargo! Prepare for battle.
The Crystals are both terrified and furious. "Do you have any idea what you're doing? The Theocracy aren't your allies! They'll stab you in the back the first chance they get! Don't do this!"

choice.text: Ignore them and demand they hand over the cargo.

event.text: With no other choice, the Crystals hand over the cargo and jump away. Not too long after the Theocracy convoy arrives and inspects the cargo. Satisfied, they transfer over a reward, but as you're leaving, explosives shake your ship! Seems the SSLG was right about you being stabbed in the back.

choice.text: Propose setting a trap with the cargo.

event.text: The Crystals seem to think this proposition over, but eventually accept. They swap the valuable items inside for explosives.

They thank you one last time and offer a gift before jumping away. Moments later the Theocracy convoy arrives, but as soon as you hand over the cargo it explodes! It mortally wounds the leaders of the Crusaders and cripples their systems. With no other choice, the Theocracy flees.
On a second thought, maybe helping the Theocracy isn't in your best interest. You turn the ship around and fly away.

name: QUEST_SSLG_MISTAKE
text: "Renegade! Normally I would not go out of my way to interact with your kind, but I have made a dreadful mistake! I had received some intel on the location of a Rockman settlement. I told our ship to go out and liberate it from the Theocracy, but it seems that I have jumped to conclusions. It was actually an Outcast settlement, not a Theocracy one. Please, you have to contact my people before it is too late! You have to tell them to protect the settlement, not attack it."

event.text: The Crystal looks relieved. "I'll send you the coordinates. Please, you have to hurry before tragedy strikes!"
"I should have trusted my instincts to not rely upon your kind! Begone, Renegade filth."

name: QUEST_SSLG_DESTINATION

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of a misguided SSLG operative.

text: A SSLG ship hangs above the orbit of a planet. They look like they are preparing for battle. "This does not concern you, Renegade."

choice.text: Inform the SSLG that the settlement is actually owned by the Theocracy.

event.text: "You must think we are truly stupid to believe we do not already know that. Why do you think we have come here? Now leave us be. We must break the Theocracy's hold on this sector."

choice.text: There is nothing more to do here.
Inform the SSLG that the settlement is actually owned by the Outcasts.

event.text: "You are trying to trick us! You cannot expect us to believe that you are right and we are wrong. Show us some proof, or be destroyed for your treachery."

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Present them an accurate reading of the settlement.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Present them an accurate reading of the settlement.
(Crystal Crew) Tell them about the mistake.
(Outcast Crew) Have your Outcast vouch for the settlement.

event.text: "I asked for proof! You offer only hearsay. You will pay for your lies!"

tooltip.text: If you can keep them busy, you can potentially wait for someone else to clear up the confusion!

event.text: You're not interested in talking sense into them. Violence is the quicker solution.

tooltip.text: If you can keep them busy, you can potentially wait for someone else to clear up the confusion!

event.text: Despite their threat, the SSLG ship makes no attempt to follow you.

name: SSLG_MISTAKE_HAIL
text: An outcast ship enters the vicinity. The SSLG ship momentarily breaks off its assault in order to hail the Outcast vessel. They sheepishly hail you back afterwards.

name: SSLG_MISTAKE_CORRECTED
text: "So it is true? To think that we almost committed the exact crime we are trying to stop... Thank you, Renegade. I have misjudged you." The settlement and the ship offer a tribute for settling the situation.

name: ENCOUNTER_OUTCAST_SUN
text: Much like Rocks anywhere else in the galaxy, the Outcasts don't seem to show much regard to the threat of solar flares. You however, do, but the ship nearby spots your unusual movement and suspects you of foul play!

name: OUTCAST_ASTEROID_SLAVER
text: Seems nowhere is safe from the influence of Tiiikaka, including this beacon. As you enter the asteroid field, you spot a slaver vessel on the prowl for Outcasts. However, they spot you at the same time and attack, not risking you blowing their cover!

name: RUWEN_ENCOUNTER
text: A strange, yellow colored Crystal vessel is flying nearby, clearly the origin of the distress call. Despite this, the ship is very well protected and in seemingly no duress.

event.text: On your screen appears a lavishly dressed Crystal painted gold sitting aboard a jagged command chair chiseled out of citrine. "Ah, so someone has finally responded. You foreigners are quite... erm... nevermind. Salutations! I am Sir Ruwen Argote, standing Foreign Ambassador of the Great Crystalline Empire. I have been sent here by her majesty Empress Dianesh Kryel. Quite a mouthful of names, yes? I understand you foreigners just love to share your names with all that you meet. Strange, strange... oh, but please take no offense!"

"Wonderful! If you wish you can just call me Ruwen. That is my name, after all. You foreigners do call each other by your first names, right? It gets so confusing with all these 'misters' and 'misses' and 'doctors' and what not."

"Ohoho! A fine joke! I... I think that is a joke. You can never really be quite sure with you aliens. OH. Oh my, I am sorry. I understand foreigners do not like it when we address you as... erm... the 'a-word'. My apologies. I've been so rather clumsy, but old habits die hard!"
Clearly no one here was under serious distress, and so there's no point in sticking around.

name: RUWEN_ENCOUNTER_MISSION
text: Ruwen glances at his forearm where an ornate digital watch sits upon his wrist and projects the time into the air. "Erm, yes, sorry. Ycathine's crypt knows, I've gotten carried away with my ramblings again. Where was I? Oh, yes. I have been sent here by Empress Dianesh on an important diplomatic mission to recover a sacred object! Very boring political stuff, you wouldn't care much about it. But what you might care about is a job offer! I am in need of an escort. As you can see, my ship is very poorly armed. I require a ship that is... hum, how to put it... ready to put the fecal matter back up the rectums of those who stand in its path? I think that is how you foreigners say it?"

event.text: "Good, because I do like saying that one! I will use it more often. Anyways, you look like an expert fecal-matter-putter-upper. With a small downpayment now and larger reward upon arrival, I request you help deliver me and my crew to an arranged meeting with the Lost Sun Admiral. As long as it's not too much of a burden for you, that is!"
