"Truly wonderful! You foreigners are so kind! I wish my people acted in such manners, but we keep to ourselves so often I think many of us have forgotten what generosity even means. But that's besides the matter. I've sent the coordinates, just clear the path and we'll be right behind you! Try not to commit too many warcrimes in our presense, heh! But no really, please don't commit any warcrimes."

"Oh, terribly disappointing. Never matter, I understand! You foreigners come and go, always busy busy! Well, I'll be here then, waiting I suppose. Idi Tukala! Erm, sorry. That's... that's goodbye in my native language. Apologies."

name: RUWEN_DESTINATION

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of Ruwen's destination.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: You've arrived at the destination Ruwen provided you with. Moments later, the Crystal arrives, jubilant as ever. "We meet again! You have my thanks, captain! As promised, your reward. Now, if you don't mind, I must hurry to my meeting. Idi Tukala! Erm, sorry. That's... that's goodbye in my native language. Apologies."

choice.text: Stay and watch the meeting from a distance covertly.

event.text: You watch as Ruwen approaches a strangely colored Rock vessel. Seems to be a Paladin, a very rare and dangerous segment of the Inquisition usually tasked with protecting important clergy members. Based on the conversation you're eavesdropping in on, Ruwen seems equally confused. "Oh erm... pardon me. I was expecting Admiral Ariadne's envoy to be here. I don't believe I had any business with the Theocracy today!"

The fully armored Rockman barely moves as he speaks to Ruwen, his voice bitter. "The traitors whom you were sent to negotiate with have been apprehended by the Theocracy. The Lost Suns are criminals, and it reflects poorly on your Empire when you come into Theocracy territory and begin to make talks of peace with enemies of the Elders. There shall be harsh consequences for these actions."

Ruwen gulps nervously, and shifts uncomfortably in his crystalline chair. "Hahah, surely you're joking! Yes, the Lost Suns are your enemies, but it is not as though the Empire is looking to draw arms against the Elders! We merely wish to settle this ongoing feud between the SSLG and Lost Sun forces for occupancies of the Badlands! That is all. No need for hostility."

The Rockman squints, his gaze focused firmly on Ruwen. "Do not lie to me. We have already interrogated the criminals for the reason of your meeting. You wish to assist them in their attack on Numa V - in return to gaining access to the waystone device that you wish to rob from us. These are acts of war. The Theocracy might be involved in many other conflicts at this moment, but do not think we will take kindly to such insults." Suddenly, weapons spring from the hull of the Rock ship! They're going to attack Ruwen!
You won't stand for this. You raise your weapons and engage the Paladin ship.
It's cruel, but this was the Empire's blunder, not yours. You can't risk angering the Theocracy like this.
Eventually Ruwen leaves your sight as he passes behind a distant moon.

name: RUWEN_SAVE
text: The Paladin vessel has been defeated. A substantial amount of scrap remains behind to take.

event.text: It seems Ruwen's substantial defenses protected him from any major damage during the fight. Still, he's quite shaken. "By the Empress, oh dear. Had it not been for you, I doubt I would still be standing here. It would be against tradition for me to not extend an even greater reward as thanks to you and the Federation. Though my initial diplomatic mission here has failed, perhaps we have achieved new ground instead!"

"Now, erm, it seems there's little point in keeping past pretenses so let me begin again. I needn't waste your time with much historical mumble, but in short the Empire has been so tolerant of the SSLG's more radical motions as the Empress sees great benefit in gaining access to Theocracy grounds. We seek access to the Waystone, the device originally used to seal our homeworlds away from the galaxy. At first, we hoped the Lost Suns might retrieve it for us in return for more dedicated support. But now it seems those plans have faltered. Now, I must go at it alone. It will be perilous, but I wonder if you might be up for the task?"

choice.text: Agree to escort Ruwen to the Crystalline Origins.

event.text: "Most wonderful! Then, with haste we must go! There isn't a second to lose!"

choice.text: Give me a moment to prepare.

event.text: "Ah, no bother then. You've done quite enough. Now, hopefully for the final time, Idi Tukala! Best of luck with your journeys."

name: RUWEN_JUMP
text: "Are you ready to depart, captain?"

choice.text: Agree to escort Ruwen to the Crystalline Origins.

event.text: "Most wonderful! Then, with haste we must go! There isn't a second to lose!"

choice.text: Give me a moment to prepare.

event.text: "Ah, no bother then. You've done quite enough. Now, hopefully for the final time, Idi Tukala! Best of luck with your journeys."

name: TURBAN
text: Before you is a grand spectacle, a giant sprawling city so tall it blocks out the sun. Massive bridges span artificial ravines with walls lined with store fronts. Half of the city seems to resemble traditional Rock architecture, but many connected segments are only half complete and are seemingly cobbled together out of scrap metal. This is Turban, one of the largest centers for trade, commerce, and culture in the modern galaxy, created quite ironically from the former site of a Chrysolic Church and Inquisition stronghold.

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of Turban.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

event.text: You fly through the city, taking in truly just how massive it is, compared to all of the much smaller Outcast villages you've seen. As a newcomer and a Renegade you are welcomed warmly, and your time in the city is a pleasant one. You meet a humble Aquarian fisherman who convinces you to try a sample of some exotic octopus, an exceptionally elderly Orchid Caretaker who crafts dreamcatchers from his own twigs, and even share an awkward encounter with a very drunken ex-Rebel who claims to be Admiral Vance's long lost brother, who buys you 3 rounds of drinks before passing out. You also find a number of stores selling military supplies with an incredible variety of items to choose from.

You fly through the city, taking in truly just how massive it is, compared to all of the much smaller Outcast villages you've seen. As a newcomer and a Renegade you are welcomed warmly, and your time in the city is a pleasant one. You meet a humble Aquarian fisherman who convinces you to try a sample of some exotic octopus, an exceptionally elderly Orchid Caretaker who crafts dreamcatchers from his own twigs, and even share an awkward encounter with a very drunken ex-Rebel who claims to be Admiral Vance's long lost brother, who buys you 3 rounds of drinks before passing out. You also find a number of stores selling military supplies with an incredible variety of items to choose from.

choice.text: We don't need to stop here.

event.text: To many this place would be worth visiting for the sights alone, but to you it's nothing but another store, and you don't need to go shopping right now.

name: TURBAN_BOMBING
text: As you begin to leave, you catch sight of a shooting star in the sky. Quite strange, considering it's not night time... Then it dawns on you what this is, just in time for you to take cover as a missile barrage strikes one of the nearby towers and sends it crashing down. The attack is followed by a flurry of more missile strikes as Theocracy and Coalition Bombers begin to jump in. The city is under attack!

choice.text: Get back to your ship and flee as soon as possible.

event.text: You take off at once, but you aren't fast enough to escape unharmed. A missile strikes your engines, damaging them badly, while a Coalition Elite spots you and engages!

choice.text: Stay and try to aid the other civilians.

event.text: You came here to save the Federation, but what good is that if you abandon everyone else on your path in doing so? You help pull several civilians out from beneath collapsed debris, but after a missile strike almost costs you your life, you realize if you stay on the surface any longer you'll die. Fortunately, a strangely dressed Rockman in worn priest clothing motions for you to follow him. "Come with me, quickly! We must get to the sewers, we'll be safe from the bombardment there."

You trek through the sewers in silence with your crew, following the Rockman and his lantern through the labyrinth beneath the streets. Eventually, he breaks the silence. "You are noble to stay and help these people. There are few who would. Come, not much further now until we reach the sanctuary." True to his word, only a few turns later and you arrive at a crudely constructed door which you slide out of the way. A repugnant smell assaults your senses but you stifle the urge to gag and take a seat next to a sleeping outcast.

The people in the room pay you little attention, but your companion draws many nasty looks. "Turns out you are a bad omen, Argo. We were warned of your curse, and now look where we are. We should never have given you asylum", spits a young female Mantis with a blood-soaked bandana over her left eye. This insult is met by murmurs of agreement by the rest of the room, who turn their backs to Argo. In defeat, he stumbles over to where you are.

choice.text: Why is everyone mad at you?

event.text: Argo sighs and slumps back, pulling a small canteen from his belt and taking a sip. "Not long ago, I was in nothing but the highest graces of the Theocracy. My father sat at the table of victors when the Elders divided the Rock-Crystal Empire and seized power, but he was denied a place as an Elder. He warned me that the Elders would not be kind to our heritage unless we continued to prove our loyalty. I served as a Chrysolic priest for many years before I married my wife, Iri. Together we had two children, a son and a daughter."

"We both knew that neither of their lives would be easy, but we tried as hard as possible to place them in positions of security. Our son was sent to the Inquisition to be trained as a Crusader, while our daughter was promised a hand in marriage with Toarde, the head Elder. She was but a young child at the time, but what were we to do? The Rock people hated us, they saw us as exactly what we were. My daughter hated me too, and one day she simply vanished from her room in Toarde's palace along with her brother. Toarde was furious, and he blamed me because he had no one else to blame."

"I was exiled from the Theocracy and abandoned by my wife, who chose to pledge herself to Toarde instead. With nowhere to go I traveled to the Badlands, where I found Turban. The outcasts who lived here hated me, but I was able to survive by proving my usefulness as a guide through the unexplored halls of the buildings. I had helped in the planning for the original construction of Turban before it was abandoned, you see. After the outcasts had established full control I was allowed to stay, but they began to call me the 'cursed one'. A homeless prophet who wandered the streets claimed that I would bring destruction to this place. And... well, here we are I suppose."
Argo falls silent, staring at the floor. He sheathes his canteen and the room turns silent once again.

name: TURBAN_BOMBING_COALITION
text: There is a palpable feeling of unease in the room, but every attempt to break the tension goes nowhere. Through the silence you can hear the distant thuds and feel the violent shaking as the bombardment of the city above continues without relent. At this rate, nothing will be left. Hours pass, and you're certain the fleet is making progress on your location. Several times footsteps can be heard outside the room, but no one ever enters.

event.text: Argo begins to hum a tune, some old Rock folk-song, but he's interrupted by an announcement over an old radio in the corner of the room. "Attention all those who remain: return to the surface at once and surrender yourselves. Those who have taken refuge in the sewers or ravines will be quickly snuffed out." You remotely check your ship's radar and see a concerningly large new blip appear. Seems the Theocracy has deployed a cruiser vessel of some kind.

It seems, despite the silence, that the room has unanimously decided to stand together. As the Theocracy search parties draw near, the door to the room is violently torn from its unstable hinges and you soon find your face on the floor with a gun to your head. Barely any sort of fight is put up as the Theocracy outnumbers your group by almost another 10 soldiers. You're drawn out to the surface, where you find the city is now little more than rubble.

The Theocracy team transporting the group splits you and your crew off from the others, handing you over to the Coalition troops by the side. During the transfer however, Argo breaks free from his restraints and takes down one of the Crusaders. In the panic, your crew escape and make it back to your ship while the survivors draw arms and battle against the Theocracy ground troops. You trust them to hold their own this time, but they won't stand a chance unless you can take down that cruiser! Not like you have a choice, because it's already locked onto your vessel and is approaching fast.

choice.text: Try to escape through the sewers.

event.text: You and your crew take off through the sewers, trying to avoid capture. There's a few very close calls but you manage to make it back to your ship and slip away without anyone noticing. You know you should feel guilty, but you can't risk your primary mission.

name: TURBAN_BOMBING_COALITION_WIN
text: The Coalition Cruiser has been defeated. There's little reason to worry about the wreckage hitting anything - Turban's already at its worst.

event.text: It seems the Theocracy's mission is complete, even if some survived. Most of the ships have jumped away, and visibly the survivors managed to scrape through the fire-fight. Among them is Argo, carrying a bloodied staff typically carried by priests such as he used to be. "I am in no way qualified to speak in such manners, but I think it goes without saying we people of Turban thank you. We Outcasts never expected the Federation to aid us in such a way. Assuming it has survived the bombardment, you should find a Rock cruiser on the landing pads outside of the city. It belongs to me, but I want you to have it. I must stay here and help repair the city. Turban will stand once again, I am certain of it."

name: BLACKMARKET_CRYSTAL_KNICKNACKS
text: A Crystalline market is established here, a rare sight. It appears to have drawn a large crowd, and is selling Crystal relics.

name: BLACKMARKET_DESPERATE_SLUG
text: A Slug ship, painted in pirate colors, appears to be trying to make a trade between the different ships at this beacon, but to no avail.

event.text: The Slug captain appears surprised that you reached out to him. He quickly regains his composure. "Greetingsss! This is a mosst fortuitousss day for you. I jusssst ssso happen to be ssselling a rare and powerful weapon, would you be interesssted?"
You hand over the scrap to him, wary of any tricks he might pull. Instead, he deposits a cargo box and quickly jumps away.
You carefully pry open the box and look inside. To your dismay, the "rare and powerful" weapon you just purchased was nothing more than a defense laser.
"Fine, fine. What if I lower the price?""
You hand over the scrap to him, wary of any tricks he might pull. Instead, he deposits a cargo box and quickly jumps away.
You carefully pry open the box and look inside. To your dismay, the "rare and powerful" weapon you just purchased was nothing more than a defense laser.
"You don't know what you're missssing out on. What if I lower the price even more?"
You hand over the scrap to him, wary of any tricks he might pull. Instead, he deposits a cargo box and quickly jumps away.
You carefully pry open the box and look inside. To your dismay, the "rare and powerful" weapon you just purchased was nothing more than a defense laser.
"Urgh, you're really twisssting my leg here. Final price, take it or leave it."
You hand over the scrap to him, wary of any tricks he might pull. Instead, he deposits a cargo box and quickly jumps away.
You carefully pry open the box and look inside. To your dismay, the "rare and powerful" weapon you just purchased was nothing more than a defense laser.
"Ok ok, that wasss a lie. Thisss isss my final offer. Take your time, think it over."
You hand over the scrap to him, wary of any tricks he might pull. Instead, he deposits a cargo box and quickly jumps away.
You carefully pry open the box and look inside. To your dismay, the "rare and powerful" weapon you just purchased was nothing more than a defense laser.
"Aggghh, pleassse! Just buy it!"
You hand over the scrap to him, wary of any tricks he might pull. Instead, he deposits a cargo box and quickly jumps away.
You carefully pry open the box and look inside. To your dismay, the "rare and powerful" weapon you just purchased was nothing more than a defense laser.
"Fine! Jusssst take it! Free of charge! I don't care anymore!"
You agree to take it for free. He angrily jettisons a defense laser out into space and jumps away.
The Slug screams in pure rage and ends the call. Next thing you know, his weapons are up and you should do the same!
You ignore the Slug and hide behind a nearby moon so he won't try to contact you next.

name: DESPERATE_SLUG_WIN
text: With the Slugs dead, you move in to inspect their cargo. You find a cache of cargo boxes, at least a hundred of them. You open them all, finding only Basic Lasers. Looks like they overstocked on these and didn't buy anything else...

name: BLACKMARKET_SHEEPISH_FED
text: You're surprised to see a Federation ship here, or at least one not marked in pirate paint.

event.text: A human captain answers your hail. Younger than typical, and he seems rather embarrassed. "So uh, you're with the Federation too? Hehe... this is a bit of an awkward spot to meet, isn't it?"

"Hah good, so you're a reasonable one. If my squadron leader saw me here... oh boy." He chuckles nervously, rubbing at his neck. "Say, you uh, you wouldn't happen to have any extra space on your ship, would you? Like, for new crew I mean."

His face brightens. "Really? Like, could I come along?" You nod and he jumps with joy. "I'll grab my things immediately." He comes aboard shortly after, bidding his crew goodbye. "You're really doing me a solid, had I stayed on my ship I would have been slammed for sure for being here."

"Oh, right. Should have figured, your mission is probably pretty important anyways." You nod. "Well uh, best be going then, gotta buy those supplies and get out of this sector before I'm caught. Glad to see a friendly face though." He waves goodbye and ends the call.
"Well hey now, let's not forget you're here as well. We uh, ran low on some supplies, and this seemed like a good spot as any to buy some."

"What?! Hey, who do you think you are?" You lie to them, saying you're here to enforce Federation law on the sector. "Really, enforcers now are you? My ass." Next thing you know their weapons are armed and you've found yourself in a brawl!
You grunt in disapproval and hang up. You try not to reflect on your hypocritical actions and watch in shame as the other Federation ship jumps away.
The ship slinks away from you and jumps away after a couple minutes, leaving you alone.

name: BLACKMARKET_VENGEFUL_ENGI
text: A Separatist Engi ship is already here, transferring goods between a slaver ship. Upon your arrival, the slavers beckon for them to speed up the process then jump away.

event.text: You hail the Engi ship. "Mission = vengeance. The Mantis raid Engi homelands, and take [Engi] as captives. The favor has been -returned-." It appears they are selling Mantis slaves.

choice.text: Ask to buy a Mantis slave.

event.text: The Engi are more than willing to sell a Mantis to you, and at a reasonable price as well. They offer a few choices.
You change your mind. Maybe buying a Mantis slave isn't a good idea after all. The Separatists Engi don't seem to mind.
The Engi aren't naturally vengeful, but these are Separatists after all. You don't risk pressing further.
No need to get involved in other people's business.

name: BLACKMARKET_SICK_MARKET
text: An inconspicuous station is posted here, probably an honest trader looking to make a profit somewhere with larger crowds.

choice.text: Contact them to see if they want to trade.

event.text: The station's leader appears on your vid-screen, coughing. "W-what? Oh, sorry. No trading for now, we're all sick. This damn place draws in thousands of ships from all over the galaxy, god knows what kinds of diseases it brings. We're probably dying of some exotic Mantis flu or something, if that even exists."

choice.text: Offer what supplies you can muster.

event.text: "This won't help much, but it's much appreciated. Glad to know there's some kind souls out there still. I can't offer much in return, but we can use our automated repair drones to fix up some hull for you."

The captain isn't sure what that even means, but he lets you do it anyways. After some time the state of their entire crew is looking much better. "I don't know what kind of voodoo magic that was, but I feel great. It's only right if we offer some payment in return."

The station's crew is frightened at first that they're under attack, but soon realize your healing bursts are only improving their condition. "How peculiar, I've never seen medical supplies such as those. Would you be willing to sell them to us, in case this sort of situation ever occurs again?"
"Thank you, this will prove to be very useful. Let us repair some damage for you as well using our automated repair drones."
"Ah well, fair enough. Here, let us patch up your hull with our automated repair drones regardless as thanks."

choice.text: (Medical Crew) Have your crew diagnose their condition.

event.text: Your crewmember runs a few basic tests on the station's workers, and asks them a few questions. They then conclude that the station is in fact suffering from an exotic Mantis flu. Unfortunately they don't really have much advice for them beyond self isolating when possible, but the station's crew seem relieved enough at this information to offer a reward.

choice.text: (Medical Drone) Have your drone diagnose their condition.

event.text: You send your drone onto the station and have it run scans on the crew there, before washing it thoroughly on its return. The scans suggest that the station is in fact suffering from an exotic Mantis flu. You don't really have any advice for them beyond self isolating when possible, but the station's crew seem relieved enough at this information to offer a reward.

choice.text: Take this chance to rob them!

event.text: "Really? Is there no good will left in this whole place?"
The captain thanks you and ends the call. Now you have some free time on your hands.
You have no desire to trade with the station.

name: SMUGGLER_WONDERDRONE
text: "Greetings! You look like a guy who'd benefit greatly from never seen before drone tech! That's right, we bring to you the brand new WONDERDRONE (tm). As you can see, this special drone comes equipped with 4 different weapons! Your foe will never manage to predict what they'll be hit with. This is a steal of a deal kid, you'd have to be an idiot not to take it."

event.text: "Damn it, we got another angry one! Arm the weapons..."
"Aw, that's too bad." You cut comms and leave.

name: SMUGGLER_PLAYER_WEPS
text: A Black Market station is selling unique weapons and drones here which consume less power than normal.

event.text: There's nothing offered that you're interested in buying.

name: REFUGEE_PIRATE_MV
text: Your sensors have picked up a refugee ship drifting through the system, no doubt one of many fleeing the Rebel advance. It doesn't appear to have detected you... or else it is trying to avoid notice.

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the pirate ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range. After a time the distress calls stop.
"Good choice, son. We've both come out of this richer."

choice.text: Try to be a hero. Attack the pirate.

event.text: The pirate ship stops its pursuit and locks weapons onto your ship.

name: PIRATE_NAME
text: You catch a conversation between a few pirates on the ship nearby. They're arguing over something, though it's hard to tell what.

event.text: "Yeah? Whaddya want?" You explain that you want to help resolve their problem. "You want to WHAT? That's pretty weird, but since you're offering... We just uh... legally obtained this new ship, and we can't think of a new name for it. Don't suppose you got any ideas?"

choice.text: Hold on, let us think of more ideas.

event.text: You think of a few more name ideas for the pirates.

choice.text: Give us another minute, we need to think more.

event.text: You think of a even more name ideas for the pirates.
You're beginning to run out of good ideas.

choice.text: Ok, we still need some time.

event.text: You're almost completely out of any ideas.

choice.text: Suggest the name 'Literally a Pirate Ship'.

event.text: The pirates have become very annoyed. "Oh for Newton's sake, just give us a damn name!"
You leave the pirates to their squabbling.

name: PIRATE_NAME_GREAT
text: The pirates have a brief discussion about your suggestion. "Perfect, this will be great! Thank you for your assistance, strange Federation ship. Here is some pay."

name: PIRATE_NAME_HORRIBLE
text: "Not only was that the worst name I have ever had the disgrace of hearing, but you have physically made my ears bleed just by listening to it. My second mate just went into cardiac arrest, and a fire almost started in our engines. It was so bad that I actually feel like vomiting right now. It was so tremendously horrible that I could feel a higher power literally die in disgrace that they created a creature as pathetic as you. I have no choice but to arm my weapons and obliterate you horrible mongrels, so that you cannot pollute and destroy this plane of reality any further."

name: SLAVER_DEAD_SLAVES
text: A slaver is advertising quality slaves for modest prices.

choice.text: Buy an unknown slave for 20 scrap.

event.text: "Ah yes, well about that. We uh... we can't show you... because... because they're all sleeping! Wouldn't want to wake them up."

choice.text: Seems legit. We'll buy one for 20 scrap.

event.text: "Alright alright! They're all dead, we're selling dead slaves, now let us go!" Unfortunately for them, you don't have any intentions of letting them off the hook.
The Slaver ship continues to advertise their "products", so you simply mute all hails coming from their ship.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug check their intentions.

event.text: "It sssseemsss thessse sssslaverss are ssselling dead ssslaves! Hah, what a racket. Gotta admire their gusssto. Ssstill, you ssshouldn't buy anything."
You prepare to attack the slaver ship, ready to make sure they don't scam anyone else.

choice.text: Follow your Slug's advice and leave.

event.text: The Slaver ship continues to advertise their "products", so you simply mute all hails coming from their ship.

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell check their intentions.

event.text: "Thhhese slavers are selling dead bodies! You shhhouldn't hand over anythhhing to thhhem, othhher thhhan a well-earned lesson."
You prepare to attack the slaver ship, ready to make sure they don't scam anyone else.

choice.text: Follow your Shell's advice and leave.

event.text: The Slaver ship continues to advertise their "products", so you simply mute all hails coming from their ship.
The Slaver ship continues to advertise their "products", so you simply mute all hails coming from their ship.

name: SLAVER_DEAD_SLAVES_BUY
text: The Slavers thank you for your purchase and bring the slave onboard. However, it's clear something is wrong. The slave is a completely lifeless, motionless corpse.

event.text: You prepare to attack the slaver ship, furious that they tricked you.

choice.text: Demand they give your money back.

event.text: "Hey now, let's be real here. We never said anything about the slaves being ALIVE. It's all simply a misunderstanding. Best we can do is give you half the scrap back, out of fairness."

choice.text: We won't stand for this! Destroy them.

event.text: You prepare to attack the slaver ship, furious that they tricked you.

choice.text: (Upg. Weapons) Threaten them to give you all of your money back.

event.text: "Okay! Okay! Here, we'll even throw in some extra fuel because we're so kind!"

name: DEAD_CREW_SLAVER_DEADSLAVES
text: You find a number of slaves in the cargo hold. You could use more crew but it won't reflect positively on you for taking slaves like this.

choice.text: Demand the Mantis joins your crew but release the rest.

event.text: You pry open the cage containing the Mantis, only for them to fall dead on the ground. Oh, right...

choice.text: Demand the Rockman joins your crew but release the rest.

event.text: You pry open the cage containing the Rockman, only for them to fall dead on the ground. Oh, right...

choice.text: Demand the Engi joins your crew but release the rest.

event.text: You pry open the cage containing the Engi, only for them to fall dead on the ground. Oh, right...

choice.text: We aren't slavers. Free them all.

event.text: You open the cages, but none are eager to get out. That is when you remember that you were advertised dead slaves...

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL
text: A slaver ship hails you directly, soliciting slaves for fair prices. "Only 35 scrap for a brand new worker! What a steal of a deal. You'd have to be an idiot not to take this offer while it still lasts."

choice.text: Buy an unknown slave for 35 scrap.

event.text: You prepare to attack the slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug check their intentions.
(Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell check their intentions.

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_BETRAY
text: Your crewmember tells you to be wary of the slaves. This whole thing is a scam.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Why suddenly so adverse to business? Oh well, maybe we'll find someone more eager to get the deal of a lifetime at the next beacon!"

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_HUMAN
text: According to your crewmember, the slave being offered is a human.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_ENGI
text: According to your crewmember, the slave being offered is an Engi.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_ORCHID
text: According to your crewmember, the slave being offered is an Orchid.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_ROCK
text: According to your crewmember, the slave being offered is a Rockman.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_MANTIS
text: According to your crewmember, the slave being offered is a Mantis.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

name: SLAVER_BETRAYAL_SLUG_CRYSTAL
text: According to your crewmember, the slave being offered is a Crystal.

event.text: You prepare to attack the treacherous slaver.
"Ah, so we do got a couple of idiots over here!" The slaver hangs up and jumps away.

name: SLAVER_LANIUS_SLAVE
text: You enter a beacon located in a very desolate system, used only as an intermediate waypoint to span the gap between more important systems for FTL travel. There is little here other than a lone civilian station above the beacon. Shortly after arriving at the beacon, you are hailed by a ship sporting black and red paint docked at the station.

event.text: The ship's captain coughs, then speaks, "We have obtained a miraculous metal man, capable of not only living without oxygen, but actively making the air unbreathable. However, our ship's Life Support system can't sustain its incredible qualities for more than a short span of time, so we're stuck here at this station in this miserable system. Agree to buy our metal man and we'll give you the deal of a lifetime."
The slaver is delighted to be freed of their liability and still earn a profit. They waste no time to transfer over the Lanius.

choice.text: Slavery is deplorable. Fight the slaver.

event.text: As you engage, the ship quickly undocks from the station and prepares to fight back.
You put some distance between you and the slaver. Once you're sure they won't bother you anymore, you consider doing something aboard the ship.

choice.text: (Mind Control) Convince them to donate the Lanius.

event.text: Your mind control system is able to easily convince the slaver captain that she should give you the Lanius for free so that they may depart for a more profitable beacon. The Lanius is quickly ejected towards your ship in a small shuttle before the effects of the mind control wear off. Realizing they've been tricked, the slaver separates from the station and powers up its weapons.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Convince them to donate the Lanius.

event.text: Your mind control weapon is able to easily convince the slaver captain that she should give you the Lanius for free so that they may depart for a more profitable beacon. The Lanius is quickly ejected towards your ship in a small shuttle before the effects of the mind control wear off. Realizing that you just fired a weapon at them, the slaver separates from the station and powers up its weapons.

name: SLAVER_DRIFTER
text: A slaver ship is drifting nearby. You can tell just from looking at it that it's running on low to no power.

choice.text: You have no crew to send aboard the ship.
(Upg. Sensors) Scan the interior of the ship.
(Lifeform Scanner) Scan the interior of the ship.

event.text: No need risking the ship or the mission over a ghost ship.

name: SLAVER_DRIFTER_CREW
text: Your crew reluctantly board the slaver ship. Your comms are stable for a while as they tell you what's happening, but suddenly, everything goes to static. After a few suspenseful minutes, the ship comes online and attacks!

removeCrew.text: You're surprised to see your crew member stumbling out of the Clone Bay. They tell you something about Ghosts, but you don't have much time to listen due to the impending assault.

name: SLAVER_DRIFTER_DRONE
text: Your drone navigates around the interior of the abandoned ship, though the image cuts out here and there. Suddenly, a shaky silhouette comes around a corner, and your drone's camera goes offline.

event.text: You try to pull in closer to recover the drone, but the ship comes online!

name: SLAVER_DRIFTER_SCAN
text: You try to detect any lifeforms inside the ship. The results are... strange, with several gaseous lifeforms inside. They don't look friendly either.

event.text: You opt to attack the ship to try and salvage it safely afterwards. The current gaseous occupants, spotting your intentions, prepare to defend themselves.

name: SLAVER_DRIFTER_DESTROYED
text: You may never know what happened to the original crew, but at least the Ghost ship will never bother anyone else. You scrap the hull.

name: SLAVER_DRIFTER_KILL
text: The Ghosts are gone, or at least you hope. You're reasonably comfortable scrapping the hull further, but not enough to stick around any longer than necessary.

name: BLACKMARKET_SUSPICIOUS_SMUGGLER
text: Though it has no conspicuous pirate markings, the ship at this beacon behaves very strangely. You suspect it's a smuggler, but without proof that claim has little bearing.

event.text: You prepare for combat.
You don't approach, but the ship seems aware that you noticed them. "Hey, uh, what are you looking at?"
"Y-yeah? And what about it?"
"O-oh. Yeah, of course. Come aboard!"
You prepare for combat.

name: BLACKMARKET_ENGI_ILLEGAL
text: To your surprise, a Zoltan ship is in the process of arresting an Engi ship. You aren't sure what the circumstances are, or if you should even get involved.

choice.text: Hail them an ask what's going on.

event.text: The Zoltan responds first, the Engi waiting patiently for them. "We are arresting these Engi for purchasing or willingly partaking in the sale of illegal goods or services."
"Impossible. Payment delivered as requested. Transaction completed successfully."
The Zoltan replies; "You have been caught purchasing illegal drugs from a Mantis vendor. This is a violation of both Federation, Zoltan, and Free-Space law."
"Negative. Goods purchased = production amplifiers. Nothing stolen, no illegal actions performed." The two ships continue arguing back and forth.

choice.text: Explain to the Engi that they purchased illegal drugs.
Aid the Zoltan in arresting the Engi.

event.text: You quickly explain to the Zoltan that you intend to help. "Fine, we will accept your assistance. But do not kill the Engi. This is a peaceful operation."
The Zoltan huff when you position your ship between them and the Engi. "You're aiding these criminals? Fine, then expect no mercy."

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Explain to the Engi that they purchased illegal drugs.

event.text: Your Engi is successfully able to explain the situation to the ship. You explain to the Zoltan the misunderstanding and the Engi transfer the drugs over to the Zoltans. Satisfied, the Zoltan ship jumps away. The Engi offer you some droneparts and a drone in thanks.
The Zoltan's business isn't your business, no need to get involved in their matters.

name: BLACKMARKET_ENGI_ILLEGAL_SURRENDER
text: You notice the Engi's hull is getting low, and the Zoltan's warnings of not killing the Engi.

event.text: "Chances of success in combat... low. Surrender, necessary." The Engi power off their weapons and submit to the Zoltan ship. Once all of the Engi have been arrested, the Zoltan captain pays you for your assistance.

name: BLACKMARKET_ENGI_ILLEGAL_KILL
text: You're fearful of the punishment awaiting you from the Zoltan ship for killing the Engi, but you quickly scrap what you can from the wreck.

event.text: "I do believe we told you NOT to kill the Engi, yes? There is no reward awaiting you for this display of unnecessary brutality."

name: BLACKMARKET_ENGI_ILLEGAL_DEFEND
text: You regret the unnecessary bloodshed, but you don't pass up the opportunity to scrap the remains of the Zoltan ship.

event.text: "Aid in combat unexpected. We are now in debt. Accept this gift."

name: BLACKMARKET_MANTIS_ROCK_OFFEND
text: The black market is rather peaceful for a pirate controlled sector, but the Rock and Mantis ship here are in the starts of a conflict. You try to listen to their conversations but it's too risky. Besides, you probably wouldn't be able to decipher their screeching anyways.

choice.text: Ask what the conflict is about.

event.text: Both ships hail you simultaneously, fighting over each other to give you their side of the story.
"Damn bugs are selling the organs of our ancient ancestors! These belong to Rock-kind, not dim-brained flesh rippers." The Mantis ship butts in, and they start arguing again.
"Fine! Death is your fate then. We tear you open first!"
"Pah! You think we will cower in fear at a lowly Federation ship? The Federation's days are numbered, and so are yours."
The two ships are too busy arguing with each other to notice you sneaking away.

"Idiot pebble brained do-nothing brutes! They think we sell organs of ancient ancestor. No. We sell pretty Rocks we find in asteroid. We tear them open, show who boss!" The Rock ship interrupts, and they start arguing again.
"Fine! Death is your fate then. We tear you open first!"
"Pah! You think we will cower in fear at a lowly Federation ship? The Federation's days are numbered, and so are yours."
The two ships are too busy arguing with each other to notice you sneaking away.
No need to get involved in alien conflicts. You fly a safe distance away.

name: BLACKMARKET_MANTIS_ROCK_OFFEND_WIN_ROCK
text: With the Mantis ship dead, you quickly scrap the remains.

event.text: "You surprise me, Federation ship. Rare is it that you defend another ship's honor. We have little to offer you besides spare ammunition."

name: BLACKMARKET_MANTIS_ROCK_OFFEND_WIN_MANTIS
text: With the Rock ship dead, you quickly scrap the remains.

event.text: "We not need help. But... you did save us. Fine, we pay you in... thanks."

name: DISTRESS_PIRATE_VAMPWEED
text: The origin of the distress call is a small Vampweed shuttle being chased by a slaver. They don't have many means to defend themselves.

event.text: The slaver switches targets the moment you draw near. "Another juicy target! So be it!"

choice.text: Wait for the slaver to catch their quarry.

event.text: You graciously wait for the slaver to conduct their business. Once they do, the slaver hails you. "You're a patient one. I take it you want to do business with us, then?"
"A great purchase. May they serve you well, captain..."
"A great purchase. May they serve you well, captain..."
"A great purchase. May they serve you well, captain..."
"Okay then. If you say so...?" Weirded out, the Slaver leaves.
You don't bother getting mixed up in this situation. Your uninvolvement will ensure that nobody will think better or worse of you.

name: DISTRESS_PIRATE_ARGEONN_TIIIKAKA
text: An Argeonn ship is putting out a distress call. A Tiiikaka ship is following it, likely intending to take slaves.

event.text: The Tiiikaka ship seems content with you as their new target!

choice.text: Fight the Argeonn smuggler before the slaver arrives.

event.text: The Argeonn ship has no choice to engage, but it looks like they don't plan to stay!

choice.text: Don't get involved with the pirates.

event.text: You let the pirates settle their own disputes.

name: QUEST_SLAVE_SHIP_DERELICT
text: A crashed slaver ship is adrift at this beacon. The ship barely has enough functionality to hail you. "The crew of this ship was eaten by a horrifying plant monster! Fortunately it wasn't able to find us slaves in the brig..."

event.text: "After it devoured everyone on the ship - except us, of course - it went back to its own ship... Maybe you can find it somewhere in this sector." The slaves send the logs of the derelict ship to you, which helps you determine the likely destination of their ship. You might be able to convince one of them to join you.
The Separatist slave agrees to work aboard your ship as the rest get off at the next population center.
The human slave agrees to work aboard your ship as the rest get off at the next population center.
The Rock agrees to work aboard your ship as the rest get off at the next population center.
You leave the slaves to their own devices - they're lucky enough to have their freedom.

name: PIRATE_VIGILANTE_SCRAP
text: After taking the survivors onto your ship, you scrap the ship. It's been mostly looted already, but you manage to find some resources in the wreck. You drop them off as soon as you reach a safe haven.

unvisitedTooltip.text: You've heard tales of a man-eating plant abomination that eats crew at this beacon.

name: VIGILANTE_CULTIVATOR_SLAVER
text: The moment you jump in, the vessel you've heard about turns to face you. You notice the weapons warming up as you approach. A large Cultivator sneers at you. "You may not wear the colors... but you've been partaking in the slave trade, haven't you? Don't answer. You're going to regret the association!"

name: VIGILANTE_CULTIVATOR_NORMAL
text: The moment you jump in, the vessel you've heard about turns to face you. "What do you want? I have no quarrel with you."

choice.text: Tell them about the slaves that survived his feast.

event.text: "So? I have no quarrel with them either. My hunger is only satisfied with slavers." The Cultivator's stomach (or nearest equivalent) grumbles. "Ugh, and it's never satisfied either."

"We used to have an arrangement with some Tiiikaka ships. We notice a patrol in a government region, we let the others know. They do the same. You know that phrase 'there's no honor among thieves'? Turns out, one of our regular correspondents found an opportunity for a promotion at our expense."

"Wasn't always this big, you know. When my old ship and crew were left for dead, we ran out of supplies. There comes a time you find out what you'll do to survive. But even after I was the only one left, I barely lived long enough before a Shell just so happened to find my ship. They're always looking for Vampweed volunteers, you know. They fixed me up, but I've been hungry ever since."
"I'm a monster am I? Then you'll forgive me if I sample your corpse when I've wrecked your ship!"
"Fine. Neither do we."

name: VIGILANTE_CULTIVATOR_GOOD
text: The moment you jump in, the vessel you've heard about turns to face you. As they hail you, the Cultivator breaks into a toothy grin. "Renegade, I've heard you've been killing some slavers lately. If you're interested in increasing that body-count even more, I've got something you might want to consider."

event.text: "I'm a monster am I? Then you'll forgive me if I sample your corpse when I've wrecked your ship!"
"Then get outta here. We'll handle it ourselves."

name: VIGILANTE_CULTIVATOR_HELP
text: "There's a slaver that's been rising in the ranks of Tiiikaka recently. Their base is hidden at this beacon. I've been planning an attack, but I don't think my ship can go at it alone. The base is guarded by three ships at all times. I might be able to take two, but three won't do, especially if they call for reinforcements."

choice.text: Agree to take on a slaver ship.

event.text: "Perfect. See you on the other side." You and the other ship approach the base. One of the defending vessels charge straight at you while the base provides fire support!
"Stop wasting my time."

name: SLAVER_BASE_ASSAULT_AFTERMATH
text: You help the Cultivator clean up the other ships. Their ship is on its last legs, but before it explodes, the crew manages to beam down to the slaver base. By the time you get down there to follow them, they're already ripping apart the occupants of the base. You meet the Cultivator stepping out of the boss' quarters, picking something out their teeth. "That felt good. Anyway, now that my ship is gone, I'm free to follow you. What do you say?"

event.text: The Cultivator joins your crew. The rest of their crew stay on the base and collect the wealth onboard, freeing the slaves as well.

choice.text: Leave the Cultivator on the station.

event.text: "Hmph, fine then. I'll wait until some unwary slaver comes here for a restock then." You finish scrapping the wrecks around the battlefield.

name: QUEST_SMUGGLER_RAID_START
text: You notice some traffic around a smuggler station orbiting a moon close by. You tune into their comms and hear an offer for a mercenary job.

event.text: A grizzly looking smuggler answers your hail. "Lookin' for a job? Well I got one for you, if you ain't a coward. A rather... expensive and pretty illegal shipment of mine was confiscated by those stuck up Zoltan assholes, saying all of their usual crap. Thing is, this is OUR sector, not theirs. I want that shipment back, and I don't care how so long as it's unharmed. You up for the challenge?"

"Well that's a surprise. Alright kid, I'll transfer over the co-ordinates. Find the depot and kill the guard. Go to the storage room and there'll be a vault. Ain't no way they opened it yet, only I got the passcode, and the vault's super blast resistant. I have no choice but to trust you, so here you go. The code is 7-E-Blue. Don't ask why. Get the cargo and there will be another list of coordinates to bring it back to. I'll be waiting for you there."
"Pffft, figured. Ain't like I want some idiot Fed hauling around my valuables anyways." He ends the call abruptly.
You aren't about to go selling yourself as mercenaries. You have standards.

name: QUEST_SMUGGLER_RAID

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of a smuggler vault confiscated by Zoltans.

text: You've arrived at the co-ordinates given to you. You're still a bit of a distance away, and it's hard to make out how well the Zoltan guard is armed.

event.text: You arm the weapons and prepare to fight.

choice.text: Screw this, fly away before they notice you.

name: QUEST_SMUGGLER_RAID_VAULT
text: As you scrap the guard's hull, a drone pops out from its hull and deploys a distress beacon before self destructing. You quickly break the beacon but it's too late. Their reinforcements will be arriving soon, so you must hurry.

event.text: As anticipated, the vault remains unopened. It is protected by a passcode. The first part is a number.
You're right! Just two more to go. The next part looks to be a letter.
Right again! One more to go. The next is a color.

The lights on the vault door light up green. You quickly open the door and grab the crate inside. Attached are some co-ordinates that you quickly program into your star map and fly away before the Zoltan can arrive.

choice.text: Blow a hole in the door.

event.text: You vaguely remember the smuggler saying something about the door being blast proof, but go ahead anyways. The explosion barely puts a dent in the door, and sets off the alarms. You try to escape but the Zoltan reinforcements arrive just in time to fire a barrage of missiles straight through your defenses before you can escape.

name: QUEST_SMUGGLER_RAID_FINISH

unvisitedTooltip.text: Return the cargo to the smuggler for your reward.

text: The smuggler is already at this beacon waiting for you. "Well well well, I'm surprised you made it. Good job."

event.text: You're wary of giving him the package and he laughs. He hands over half the payment first, and you give over the cargo. He pays you the rest and you shake hands, then he jumps away.
"You don't WHAT?" He yells at you for a while, then ends the call. You're afraid he's going to attack, but instead he simply jumps away.

name: FLOATING_CARGO_MV
text: Not too far from the beacon, you detect a destroyed cargo ship with its cargo scattered nearby, intact.

choice.text: Leave it alone, this looks suspicious.

event.text: You leave the cargo alone and prepare to jump.

choice.text: (Upg. Sensors) Run an advanced scan on the boxes.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Run an advanced scan on the boxes.
(Slug Crew) Have your Slug check the boxes.
(Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell check the boxes.

name: BLACKMARKET_SMUGGLER
text: Out of nowhere, a smuggler jumps in, guns blazing. You don't know why they're attacking, but you have no choice but to engage.

name: BLACKMARKET_REBEL
text: You hardly have time to react before a Rebel ship observing the ongoings spots you and rushes in to attack.

name: BLACKMARKET_FED_ANGERY
text: A large squadron of Federation ships is present at this beacon, firing on the pirates, while a swarm of smaller ships are arresting some of the shoppers. You're accidentally swept up into the chaos when they mistake you for a pirate and engage.

name: BLACKMARKET_FED_AUTO
text: A Federation Auto-ship is dutifully patrolling this beacon, or at least it would have been if its sensors hadn't been torn out of its head by pirates. It scans your ship but is unable to properly identify you due to the damage, and thinks you're a pirate!

name: ZOLTAN_LECTURE_MARKET
text: A Zoltan peace brigade is lecturing some pirates on the importance of good morals. You stop in to watch in amusement when one of the pirates gets impatient and attacks. You're too close to get away, so you have to decide which side you're going to have to take.

event.text: You ready yourself for combat.
You ready yourself for combat.

name: ZOLTAN_LECTURE_MARKET_WIN_PIRATE
text: You successfully dispatch the Zoltan ship. You notice the Zoltan forces are retreating, and it appears the pirates won. You scrap the Zoltan ship quickly.

event.text: "Say, that was some good fightin' kid. Thanks for the help. I'm sure I have something to repay you." You're surprised at the pirates' gratitude and are suspicious of a trick, but the cargo crate they deliver you is surprisingly harmless and contains a shiny new military class weapon.

name: ZOLTAN_LECTURE_MARKET_WIN_ZOLTAN
text: You successfully dispatch the pirate ship. You notice the pirates are retreating, and it appears the Zoltans won. You scrap your victim quickly.

event.text: "We were not expecting Federation reinforcements. Your help is much appreciated. As is Zoltan custom, we are now in your debt and shall pay it off dutifully."

name: SMUGGLER_ASTEROID
text: The asteroid field here isn't the only hazard at this beacon. The smuggler here trying to hide doesn't give you a chance and immediately attacks!

name: BRIGADE_PULSAR
text: You aren't alone at this pulsar it appears, for another Zoltan peace brigade ship appears to be stuck. However, they seem to identify you as a threat and attack!

name: SMUGGLER_UNLOCK_1
text: You beam your crew aboard. You won't have long until reinforcements arrive, but you notice a map with coordinates. It appears to lead to a shipyard of some sort. You mark it down your map and haul out of here.

name: SMUGGLER_UNLOCK_2
text: You're surprised to see the scale of the shipyard, a massive space station commandeered by the Smugglers. Though it's hard to tell, you believe it may have once belonged to a major corporation, likely Hephaestus.

event.text: You're shocked at how few ships guard the station, and you're able to simply enter without any protest. You notice several ship designs you don't recognize, including the same model as the guard from earlier, an early prototype of a Rebel Gunboat. One of them appears to be operational and is protecting a large, cruiser-sized vessel made from the parts of other ships.

choice.text: Attack the ship to get to the cruiser.

event.text: Still, even now, as you move in to attack one of their own ships, no other ships approach even just to spectate. Regardless, it appears that this will be no easy fight.
This place is dangerous, we have no reason to go messing around with the Smuggler clan.
This place is dangerous, we have no reason to go poking around in the Smuggler clan's central shipyards.

name: SMUGGLER_UNLOCK_3
text: The gunboat collapses, scattering debris around the interior of the shipyards. You scoop up the material.

event.text: As you approach the cruiser, a much larger Smuggler vessel uncloaks nearby, and hails you. A tall, slender Slug appears on the vidscreen. "I ssssee you have come for our new prototype cruissser, eh?" The Slug chuckles. "In cassse you aren't aware, that cruissser right there was being built ssspecifically for the boss, Ocym. But, sssseeing how well you dessstroyed that vesssel of oursss I'd say the ssship isss better in your hands. Heheheh..."

choice.text: Accept his offer and take the ship.

event.text: As you get to work on reprogramming the ship to jump back to the Federation hangar, you notice a loud clicking noise from inside. Before you can react, an explosion consumes the entire ship and kills one of your crew! You receive one last hail from the Slug. "You sssshould know Captain, never trusssst a pirate. Now get out of my sssshipyard."

removeCrew.text: Fortunately your crew is able to be revived by the Clone Bay, but the same can't be said for the ship destroyed by the bomb.

choice.text: The AI advises against boarding that ship, as it is very likely rigged with a last-ditch trap. Not like you have any crew to send to it anyway.
Offer a compromise for the blueprints - you can never be too sure with pirates.

event.text: You don't trust the Slug enough to just take the ship, so instead you offer a simple compromise. You request they hand over a copy for the blueprints of the ship, and you won't touch the physical version. Instead of accepting, the Slug breaks into laughter.

"Well you sssee, thisss wass ssupposssed to be a trap. That sssship isss rigged to explode when anyone triesss to take it. But... you ssseemed to have outsssmarted me. Ssssso, I'll make you a deal. I won't give you the sssship, no. But the blueprintsss, mossst certainly! It ticklesss me to think of the Federation usssing Sssmuggler tech... and I can ssshow you a way to hijack enemy frequenciessss too!"

name: QUEST_TUCO_START
text: A pirate station advertising itself as an inn is nearby. They're peaceful and the group inside appears to be made up of all kinds, including Rebels, Pirates, Federation Officers, and various assortments of aliens.

event.text: The bartender, a bulky Rockman who you're pretty sure is a wanted criminal, welcomes you in and offers a drink. Behind you the lively crowd is laughing and chattering away.

You grab your drink, pleasantly surprised to find it filled with a sweet nectar like substance. While drinking, you catch wind of a conversation between a group of pirates discussing someone named Tuco, an infamous pirate who stole a massive sum of money from a Mantis Hive Caravan and spent it all on funding his massive gambling addiction. You also catch the coordinates of his favourite casino.
You have no business with the station.

name: QUEST_TUCO_CASINO
text: The casino in question is no pirate cesspit or ramshackle gambling city. In the distance drifts a giant yacht, with hundreds of ships swarming towards it. It floats above the surface of a humid jungle planet, and in the center is a giant structure hosting what is likely the population of an entire city.

event.text: It's not hard to find the casinos, with a blaring neon sign drawing in people like bugs to a beacon. Inside are rows and rows of slot machines, poker tables, and a few bars.
You aren't going to waste the opportunity while you have it. You feed some scrap into the nearest slot machine, which miraculously seems to accept it as viable currency, and wait.

choice.text: This isn't what we expected. Leave.

event.text: Whatever you had hoped to do here is pointless now.

name: TUCO_SEARCH
text: Before you can even begin searching, a shout echoes throughout the casino. People turn to stare as a Rockman in pirate paint with a filthy moss beard and eyepatch with an elegant tuxedo is dragged out by two burly Rockmen bouncers. On his way out, the pirate exclaims "You can't do this to me! Do you know who I am? I am the dread pirate Tuco, the most feared man in the entire galaxy!" The Rockmen ignore him and continue to carry him outside.

event.text: You aren't sure what you plan to do, but the situation has you curious. You follow them outside to see Tuco heading back to a large cruiser with yellow pirate paint. Not long after, the ship powers up, its weapons come online, and he's firing at the casino! A few enforcer ships fly out to meet him, but it's uncertain who will win the fight.
You power up your weapons and attack one of the enforcers head on. It looks suspiciously like a Rebel transport that was painted over again, but that doesn't matter.
You're sure the casino will have a reward for you if you save them from Tuco's attack.
Whatever you had hoped to do here is pointless now. You leave before the fight can catch up to you.
Whatever you had hoped to do here is pointless now.

name: TUCO_WIN
text: The casino enforcer plummets towards the ground. The rest of the ships, seeing Tuco is now no longer the only threat, retreat. The yacht owners offer a handsome sum of money, and free drinks, to both you and Tuco if you promise not to cause further damage.

event.text: Tuco chuckles as he brings the scrap back to his ship. "Good fightin' there kid. Couldn't have done it better myself. SO, I'll tell you what; this hunk o' junk that I'm disgraced to call my personal cruiser has seen much better days. So how 'bout I hitch a ride on that pretty ship o' yours, and you do whatever you'd like with mine."

name: CASINO_WIN
text: The remains of Tuco's cruiser crashes into the ground, shattering into debris that probably kills a few people. Regardless, it's scrap for you to take.

event.text: Despite all the damage caused in the fight, the yacht owners are extremely grateful for your help. "That idiot has been a regular for years, and he's always causing issues. It's about time he got what was coming to him. Pffft, dread pirate my ass. As generous payment, please accept this scrap and a few of our slot machines!" You aren't sure what you think about the unusual reward, but you aren't going to turn it down.

name: REBEL_TURNCOAT
text: You receive a message from the sole passenger of a small Rebel shuttle. He looks frantic, breathing heavily and visibly sweating. "You're with the Federation, aren't you? Please listen. I must remand myself into your custody. I no longer wish to be associated with the Rebellion. You can take me prisoner if you want, I don't care. I won't be armed. Please decide quickly, I can't afford to wait."

event.text: "Thank heavens. I won't disappoint you." The Rebel quickly docks his shuttle to your bay. He's completely unarmed as he exits his ship. You have the shuttle scuttled for parts after he leaves it.

choice.text: Cautiously accept him on your ship, but have him thrown into the brig.

event.text: "Good enough for me." The Rebel quickly docks his shuttle to your bay. He leaves with his hands up in total surrender. Your crew surround him and escort him to the brig. He does not resist. You have the shuttle scuttled for parts after he leaves it.

choice.text: (Boarding Drone) Have your drone escort him to the brig.

event.text: "Good enough for me." The Rebel quickly docks his shuttle to your bay. He leaves the shuttle with his hands up. He offers absolutely no resistance as your drone escorts him to the brig. You scuttle his shuttle for spare parts.

choice.text: This must be a trick. Keep your distance from the shuttle.

event.text: Once the Rebel realizes you're keeping your distance, he flees and does not look back.

name: MERCENARY_CHASING_REBEL_TURNCOAT
text: Not long after accepting the ex-Rebel onto your ship, a Syndicate ship jumps in. After a few moments, it sends you a message. "I won't take much of your time. There's a reward out for a certain Rebel. You hate Rebels, don't you? His bounty is quite lucrative. If you have any information about his whereabouts, we would be willing to give you a small piece of the pie."

choice.text: Turn the Rebel over to the Syndicate.

event.text: You tell the Syndicate about your Rebel prisoner. The Syndicate promptly teleports troops over to your ship. The Rebel screams and tries to flee, but they have him surrounded. After a short fight, they drag him off your ship, giving you a small amount of resources for your cooperation.

choice.text: (Positive Syndicate Reputation) Use your good standing with the Syndicate to make a trade.

event.text: Given your relationship with the Syndicate, you're able to work something out. The Rebel's face goes white as he realizes what a mistake he has made. The Mercenary smiles and orders his crew to hand you a healthy amount of scrap and a combat augment.

choice.text: (Angel Crew) Have your mercenary handle the trade.

event.text: Your crew's connections to the Syndicate give you a leg up on the bargaining table. The Rebel's face goes white as he realizes what a mistake he has made. The Mercenary smiles and orders his crew to hand you a healthy amount of scrap and an augment.
The ship waits for your response, but seems to lose interest in wasting their time with you, jumping off elsewhere.
You arm your ship and prepare for battle. "So you were involved with this traitor. This payout will be even better than we hoped!"

name: REBEL_TURNCOAT_AFTERMATH
text: The turncoat breathes a sigh of relief. "You are truly honorable, Renegade. I owe you my life. If you're okay with it, I would love to join your crew. If not, I'll get out of your hair once we reach Federation territory."

choice.text: Agree to drop him off in Federation territory instead.

event.text: The Ex-Rebel thanks you for your mercy and promises to spread news of your goodwill.

name: REBEL_COWARD
text: The Rebel at this beacon immediately begins to move away from you. "H-h-hello, Renegade...! I... uh... that is to say..." The Rebel gulps. "W-w-we can talk about this, right?"

event.text: "Y-y-yes, of course! Anyone w-w-who has a powerful thing like that d-d-deserves only the best! Please don't kill us!"

choice.text: (Highly Adv. Weapons) "Encourage" them to surrender generously.

event.text: "Y-y-yes, of course! Y-y-your weapons are surely very strong!! Please don't kill us!"
"Y-y-yes, of course! D-d-does this strike your fancy?"
"Hmm..." The Rebel stares thoughtfully at your weapons system. "Here's my offer. Is that enough?"
"That's it...?" The Rebel stares blankly at your weapons system. "You know what, take it or leave it, this is all I have to offer you."
"Oh thank goodness." The Rebel jumps away quickly, leaving you with the privacy you need to do something on your ship.

name: ATTACK_REBEL_COWARD
text: "AAAAAAIIIIIEEEEEE!" The Rebel screams unintelligibly over the comm as you attack them.

name: REBEL_BOOTCAMP
text: The Rebels have set up a bootcamp for advanced trainees. One of the trainees hails your ship. "Stay away, Renegade, or we'll have to show you what the Rebellion is made of!"

event.text: The bootcamp is abuzz with enthusiasm at the surprise appearance of Jerry, who proceeds to have a talk with them about your mission and goals. The trainees are universally supportive of Jerry's decision, and one of the soldiers even offers to join your cause. The trainees each scrounge for some resources as a gift for Jerry.

choice.text: (MFK Ace Crew) Make a case against the Rebellion.

event.text: The camp is in awe at the MFK that stands before them. He speaks of the folly of the Rebels, that the Federation is worth protecting. The MFK calls upon all of them to do their duty for the sake of humanity and help end this conflict. After hearing out your crewmember, one of the soldiers pledges to join your cause.

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Make a case against the Rebellion.
(Human Crew) Make a case against the Rebellion.
Make a case against the Rebellion.
Keep away from the Rebel bootcamp.

event.text: You ignore the bootcamp to focus on other things.

name: REBEL_CIRCUS
text: On the nearby planet there appears to be a large circus held by some suspicious looking civilians. It's not likely they'll care if you're a Federation ship.

event.text: The circus is much more underwhelming and run down than it appeared from above. Most of the attractions and rides look barely functional and definitely not safe. One exhibit however catches your eye, the freak show. On display are 5 aliens, likely slaves, a Slug, Rockman, Orchid, Zoltan, and Engi.

A bald civilian with an incredibly long beard welcomes you. "Step right up folks, and witness Sazalaraz the All-Seeing! He can see through walls, he can see the future, and he can see into your pockets! So keep a tight hand on your wallet, or next thing you know it might be missing!"
The man looks at you strangely. "You want to BUY Sazalaraz the All-Seeing? Yeah sure, it'll be 20 bucks."
A bald civilian with an incredibly long beard welcomes you. "Step right up folks, and witness Boulder the Boundless! He can lift anything, survive any collision, and feels no pain!"
The man looks at you strangely. "You want to BUY Boulder the Boundless? Yeah sure, it'll be 20 bucks."

A bald civilian with an incredibly long beard welcomes you. "Step right up folks, and witness Sapling the Giver of Joy! A quick inhale of the scent from his leaves and you'll be feeling higher than a kite! Feel free to come forth and have a whiff, but do note, we aren't liable for anything that happens to you."
The man looks at you strangely. "You want to BUY Sapling the Giver of Joy? Yeah sure, it'll be 20 bucks."

A bald civilian with an incredibly long beard welcomes you. "Step right up folks, and witness Namast the Energized! You won't ever be needing an outlet for charging your holopad when he's around! He can provide power to anything, because he's MADE of power!"
The man looks at you strangely. "You want to BUY Namast the Energized? Yeah sure, it'll be 20 bucks."

A bald civilian with an incredibly long beard welcomes you. "Step right up folks, and witness Q-32 the Cyclopean Engineer! He may only have one eye, but he's the master of tech! He can fix anything fast as lightning, debug any problem, and best of all he can't even feel emotions!"
The man looks at you strangely. "You want to BUY Q-32 the Cyclopean Engineer? Yeah sure, it'll be 20 bucks."
You have much better things to be doing.

name: REBELHOLD_REMOTE_COLONY
text: There doesn't seem to be any Rebel ships nearby, and the nearby planet only contains a single settlement. The planet has harsh climate conditions, with regular intense rainstorms - but the human colony below seems to be stable nonetheless.

choice.text: (Human Crew) Send your human to check out the colony.

event.text: Your crew heads down to the planet. The high winds make landing somewhat unpleasant, but fortunately the colony itself is relatively clear.

choice.text: You don't have any human crew, so visiting the colony might be dangerous.

event.text: You avoid the colony. It doesn't seem to have any places of interest anyway.

name: REMOTE_COLONY_MENU
text: Standing in view of the settlement, there are a number of places of interest, with people of many trades working here. You should have enough time to make a deal with one person.

event.text: The general store shopkeep smiles widely as your human approaches the counter. "Well hello there! Welcome to our fine establishment, out-of-towner. Not sure if we have anything that would interest the likes of a space traveler, but feel free to look around!"

The gunsmith looks very rugged, with many trophies of animals that must live on this planet. "Howdy there. I pride myself on my weapons, 'round these parts. Much better than your standard issue military grade firearms. If'n you think you can handle 'em."

choice.text: Buy personal weapons for your crew.

event.text: True to his word, the weapons seem to have a loving craftsmanship applied to them. Your crew carries the assortment of firearms back to the shuttle and returns to your ship.

The owner of the appliance store has her feet kicked up on the counter, reading a book. Once you enter, she glances your human's way, and nods in acknowledgement. The store is mostly full of things people on the planet would need, but there are a few drones for sale.
Your crewmember buys the repair drone and drags it back to the shuttle. It was relatively inexpensive for a repair drone, suggesting they may not have many opportunities to sell these on the planet.
Your crewmember buys the doctor drone and drags it back to the shuttle. It was relatively inexpensive for a medical drone, suggesting they may not have many opportunities to sell these on the planet.

choice.text: Have your crew return to the ship.

name: REMOTE_COLONY_CARPENTER
text: Your human is in the carpentry shop. The carpenter shoots them a quick glare, but doesn't say anything else. The shop isn't very well organized, but maybe you can find something if you look around.

choice.text: Poke around the shop for something to buy.

name: REMOTE_COLONY_CARPENTER_DISCOVERY
text: Your human wanders into a room that isn't lit. Curious, they open a nearby wardrobe, thinking it's part of the store. Inside, however, is a Rebel MFK uniform. Your crew feels something poking into their back, as well as the powering of an advanced Rebel carbine. You receive a hail in the meantime.

event.text: The carpenter is holding your crew at gunpoint. He growls at you. "You don't belong here, Fed."
"Your crew was trespassing. Saw something he shouldn't. I'm not afraid of violence, Fed. You turn, you take this idiot and get the hell off my property."

choice.text: Ask why he hasn't killed your crew.

event.text: The carpenter's glare sharpens. "Let's say I'm a kind and generous soul."

The carpenter sighs. "I tried. Hated the Feds. Hated how they would control us, and yet offer nothing in return. All I wanted was to be left alone. But no, I had to listen to some 'idealists'. Said we could set all humans free, said we'd protect those that can't protect themselves. Family encouraged me to join. But, what do I see? Soldiers, ignored, exploited, forgotten. We were all pawns. So I tried to rise higher. But, it didn't matter. Lotta good men would get depressed, wash out and be swept under. One day, I looked around me, and the only people I recognized were machiavellian wannabes who piggybacked their success on the lives of good soldiers. So, no. I am not a 'Rebel'."

choice.text: We want the fighting to stop too.

event.text: "Hmph. At least from a Fed, I can believe that. You're going after Wentworth, aren't you?" The carpenter lowers his weapon. "I've got a problem with him too. I'll follow you as far as the Flagship, then I'm living my own life. Got it?"

choice.text: We're going to win this war.

event.text: "Hmph, you really think so? The Federation is weak. If you want to see how it's done, I might be able to help." The carpenter lowers his weapon. "Just don't bother me when the mission doesn't require it."
"Good choice, Fed." The carpenter leads your crew member away from his shop, escorting him back to the shuttle. Doesn't look like you'll be welcome here anymore.
Without one more word, the carpenter pulls the trigger, ending your crewmember's life in an execution. Looks like you might not want to stick around here any longer.

removeCrew.text: Your crew, after stepping out of the Clone Bay, shakes their head. Maybe you could have spared your crew that execution.

name: REBELHOLD_WISTFUL_CITIZEN
text: You're receiving a call from a nearby planet, which is quite highly populated. This planet was one of the central points of conflict in the Federation-Mantis war, which might suggest why the Rebels have chosen to incorporate it into their space. The call is civilian, and is not marked as urgent. The signal quality is poor, suggesting there may be some damaged or outdated technology at play.

event.text: The voice is that of an elderly lady. "Hello, passing ship. You're one of those... reality jumpers, aren't you?"

"Oh, that's right. Sorry for the frivolous hail, but I've made a habit of checking the stars for unusual ships using whatever is left of my old, broken down cargo ship. Ever since the Rebels took over this sector, they've done their best to throttle any alien traffic in the region, so I'll take any rarity I can get. Back in the day, I would go gallivanting around the galaxy just like you. Not to other realities, we didn't have that back in my day. Why, I was just pleased to talk to my Zoltan friends back when I still could... See the galaxy, talk to different peoples... But with my health, I can't just go find them, to talk one last time."

"A friend of Zoltans? Well, a lot of us are a stubborn obstinate lot. Friendship between species sure made a lot more sense to me after I left the Duskbringers to join the Illesctrians... A life of fighting is no life, I tell you. Yes, you should be with your friends in your twilight years."

"A member of the Duskbringers who became a monk...? Sure sounds like you have quite the story, sonny."

"Story? You want to hear a story? Well, I never do this, but let me tell you about this time I was with a friend of mine named Obyn..."

You start to zone out as Anurak takes her on a journey of whatever his scatterbrained mind can recall of his life. At the end of it, you realize she has given you a gift for keeping her company.

choice.text: (Monk Crew) Set the lady's mind at ease.

event.text: Your monk talks to the lady, talking in spiritual language. The lady is able to keep up, satisfying your monk with a stimulating conversation. "Oho, I didn't expect a monk of all people to make their way here even when there wasn't a war... Thank you. Please, accept this gift." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Devorak) Have Devorak talk to the lady.

event.text:
Devorak looks at you oddly, but relents. "...so you say you want to see a Zoltan one last time?" Her reply is quick. "Yes, I had quite a few Zoltan friends back in the day, but I haven't seen any in so long."

"One moment." Devorak uses his long range personal teleporter. The lady seems confused.
							
"What do you mean one- Aaaaah!" The lady screams "Did you just...?"

"Personal teleporter. Are you satisfied?"

The two talk for a short time, awkwardly, but when Devorak comes back, he has a weapon and some scrap, apparently a gift from Eleanor.

choice.text: (Duskbringer Crew) Have your Duskbringer talk to the lady.

event.text: Your Duskbringer is clearly uncomfortable talking to an old human lady, but warms up somewhat as the conversation goes on. "That was nice, I guess. You travel with some strange Zoltans, Renegade." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Tintan and Rig) "Your name wouldn't happen to be Eleanor, would it?"

event.text:
"Yes? I'm sorry, sonny, I don't recall your voice."

"You don't know me. I am Rig. I think you might know a Zoltan envoy named Tintan. She had some business here many years ago. She's... here."
							
Eleanor seems excited. "Oh! Well, put her on!"
							
Rig sighs. "...This is as good as we can do." Eleanor seems confused. "I'm not going to get into it. It's stupid. She can't speak to anyone but me right now. But she wants me to tell you that she's glad to hear from you again."

"Tan... What are the odds? Well, you always were a big traveler. ...what exactly is the nature of your relationship?" Rig doesn't answer, instead turning to glare at you. You feel compelled to leave the room and give the three of them some space.

By the time the three of them are done talking, you find a generous amount of scrap and a weapon have been transported into space near you.

choice.text: (Zoltan Crew) Let her talk to another Zoltan.

event.text: Your Zoltan talks with the old lady for some time, as she reminisces with them about her past encounters with Zoltans, her friends. Unfortunately, they don't seem to know each other, but she appreciates it all the same. "That was nice. It's been so long, but now I feel just a bit younger again. Please, take this gift." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Osmian Crew) Introduce her to your Osmian.

event.text: You introduce an Osmian crewmember to her. A sense of awe fills her voice. "The ancestors of the Zoltans still exist?? That's... that's incredible! Who are you? Why have you come here?" She shakes her head. "Well, you think you've seen it all, and then something comes along and changes everything. Please, accept a gift. You've brought me comfort in my late years." A weapon and some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: We're doing our best to change things.
