event.text: "Well, I guess I'm rooting for you then. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

"Don't get smart with me, child! I'm not going to report you to the Rebels. I just want to talk a little bit. I swear that this war has made a liar out of everyone... Back when it was the Mantises - you know, I was never fond of them of course, especially after what they did to this planet - but at least that war was between undivided populaces! Now everyone fights among themselves... I tell you, we got along much better back then, dagnabbit. Is that kind of unity even possible these days?"

choice.text: (Turzil) What we stand for is more important than what we are.

event.text:
"I can identify [with] your struggles. My -own- government wishes to purge what I am for my dissent. But as I fought alongside my -Federation- colleagues, be they Engi, Zoltan, -Orchid- or Human, I have discovered a [purpose] greater than I had ever known. Adversity was the -crucible- that forged the individual you see before you, and [the] friends it had found along the way."

"Ohoho, you are right. Despite your mechanical body, you make that sound almost magical..." she trails off. "Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." A weapon and some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Separatist Crew) Disunity isn't a bad thing.

event.text: Your Separatist goes on a short ramble about the Engi Separatist movement, and about how despite being originally from a hivemind, individuality and found family can persevere. "Ohoho, I have always been impressed by the Separatists, but I'd never connected it to the concept of the Rebellion... Yes, maybe it is a good thing that people are free to choose their own path, whether it be for more freedom or not. Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

"My good lady, I've been around since the Federation-Mantis War. The combatative Free Mantis soldiers and the Hive may seem pugilistic - but that is not the whole story! Why, I myself belong to the original movement of the Free Mantis, the scientists, engineers, architects, thinkers... We left the Hive for something better. Had we stayed loyal to the Hive, the wrongs of Queen Leikonpliiinakra would still stain our appendages! No - things are better now. At least, for those of us in the Free Mantis. We can better ourselves without bringing harm to others."
							
"Ohoho, you know how to give a doddering old fool like me some hope, don't you? Yes... maybe unity hasn't gone after all. If well-mannered Mantises are capable of unifying with humans after a war like that..." She trails off. "Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." A weapon and some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Free Mantis) Disunity isn't a bad thing.

event.text: Your Free Mantis begins to ramble about the schism, and how ultimately it's better to be fighting who they want, and to not fight the people of the Federation. It's more than a little incoherent, but the sentiment is not lost. "Ohoho, this rambunctious little guy is a Federation-loving Mantis? Never would have thought of such a thing back in the day, I tell you. Maybe we haven't lost unity after all, it's just that we're friends with people we agree with instead of people who look like us... Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

"Hah! If the first Dread Pirate Tuco could hear you, he'd spit! The Theocracy Elders have always used our peaceful disagreements as an excuse for violence against us. I do not care for the Rebellion... but I will tell you this. A people fighting amongst themselves is not always a bad thing. I, Tuco, will stand arm-in-arm with any aboard my ship, and that is true unity! And if we have to fight the universe for our right to do so, then we'll gladly do so!"

"Ohoho, you are right. I have been cooped up planet-side for too long... Everything is so much more clear up there in the stars. If my health were better I'd..." she trails off. "Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." A weapon and some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Outcast Crew) Disunity isn't a bad thing.

event.text:
Your outcast tells the old woman a story of the Theocracy cracking down on dissent, and about how the outcasts banded together. Unity can't be forced, your outcast says.

"You're a passionate sort, aren't you? I think you have a good point... I don't know if it really applies to the conflict between the Rebels and the Federation though. Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

"I cannot speak for the human Rebellion, but for the Lost Suns, we did not go to war because there was no unity. We went because false unity is imposed upon us! It's impossible to oppose an organized force with centuries of legacy and wealth behind it unless you have comrades that you can depend upon. And I will tell you this... that I am working with the Federation's Renegade despite the Federation and Lost Sun's disagreements is a sign that unity is not dead."

"Ohoho, you know what you're talking about much better than I do. It's been a long time since someone corrected me so thoughtfully. If I could go back into space, maybe I could gain some of my perspective back..." she trails off. "Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." A weapon and some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) Disunity isn't a bad thing.

event.text: Your Commando speaks of the civil war amongst the Theocracy and the Lost Suns - how the Lost Suns feel more purpose and unity in arms alongside each other than they ever had when in the Theocracy. "You're a passionate sort, aren't you? I think you have a good point... I don't know if it really applies to the conflict between the Rebels and the Federation though. Oh, I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.

"Well, there's only so much we can do. I've wasted enough of your time. I'm sure you've got somewhere to be. Take this and enjoy yourselves." Some scrap is teleported into space near your ship - which you grab.
Eventually, the call cancels. Nothing else happens.

name: REBELHOLD_AUTO_LOREKEEPER
text: An Auto-ship has been stationed here, but it does not turn hostile when it notices you. "Greetings tourist. I am the Lorekeeper, an automated ship tasked with keeping a full history of the glorious Rebellion and all its brilliant victories and rare defeats. A reward awaits those who take the time to listen to our 100% accurate historical retelling."

event.text: "The Rebellion first began in 2757, founded by the now Admiral Vance Wentworth, a brilliant and handsome man who was dissatisfied with the way the Federation operated after 30 years of working under their command." As you start listening, you realise this is going to take a while.

"It is common knowledge that the human race is superior to all other aliens. Therefore, it is the Rebellion's divine right to overthrow the Federation and establish a glorious, human only galactic government. Other aliens will be allowed to exist on the outskirts so long as they avoid communicating with humans."

"The most known battle in Rebel history was the Battle of Node 17, often referred to as the Last Stand. The outcome of Node 17 has never been repeated except for Universe 0, the origins of multiverse travelers. Though the Federation was successful in defeating the Rebels, their celebration would not last for long after the Rebels discovered the mysterious Multiverse technology."

"We owe our collective thanks to the brave heroes who have provided the other Rebels across the realities the chance to bring a better future to their galaxy. This concludes the retelling. Accept this complementary augment and supplies for taking the time to educate yourself."
Almost the second you mute the Auto-ship, its weapons activate and it attacks!
Almost the second you mute the Auto-ship, its weapons activate and it attacks!
The ship does not try to contact you again.

name: AUTO_CIVILIAN
text: You come across a Rebel automated scout ship pursuing a civilian ship, weapons engaged.

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the automated ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range.

name: REBEL_REFUEL_STATION
text: You detect a Rebel ship on an attack approach to a small refuelling outpost. Their weapons are charged, but they're not firing yet.

event.text: The Rebel responds to your threat, "I don't know who you are, but no one defies the Rebel Fleet!" They move in to engage.
The Rebel ship fires some warning shots but eventually powers down their weapons. The outpost seems to have given them what they demanded.

name: AUTO_REFUEL_STATION
text: You detect an automated Rebel scout attacking a small refuelling outpost.

event.text: Detecting the higher threat, the automated ship moves in to engage your ship.
You steer clear of the conflict. The outpost receives a beating but the ship stops its attack before it's destroyed.

name: AUTO_DEFENSE_MAP
text: You find an automated sensor station at this beacon, protected by a singular Auto-ship patroling around it.

choice.text: Attack the automated ship to get to the sensor station.

event.text: You prepare to fight.
You have no need to stir up trouble with the Rebels.

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Use your sensors to attempt to access the data.
(Teleporter) Beam directly onto the station to try to avoid detection.

event.text: Once on board, your crew is able to access and download the long-range scanner's archived information. Your map has been updated.

choice.text: (Central Teleport) Beam directly onto the station to try to avoid detection.

event.text: Once on board, your crew is able to access and download the long-range scanner's archived information. Your map has been updated.

name: AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM
text: An advanced Rebel automated ship remains stationed near a small Rebel space-station. Sensors indicate it's a storage vessel for military goods.

choice.text: Attack the automated ship to get to the storage cache.

event.text: You prepare to fight.
You have no need to stir up trouble with the Rebels.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Attempt to cloak and access the cache.

name: AUTO_DEFENSE_RADAR
text: A Rebel automated ship sits dormant near a Rebel forward radar station.

event.text: The ship powers up and targets you.

choice.text: Keep your distance and wait for the FTL to charge.

event.text: You have no need to stir up trouble with the Rebels.

choice.text: (Combat Drone) Send a drone to distract the automated ship.

name: DEFENSE_RADAR_ACCESS_MV
text: The station in question appears to be capable of relaying information to the Rebel Fleet. You could attempt to hack it to give the Rebels false information.

choice.text: Attempt to manually hack into the station.
Don't risk it. Leave the station.
(Hacking) Use a drone to hack into the station. [-1|]

event.text: You successfully hack into their system and transmit false information about your location. That should hold off the fleet for at least a little while. You also are able to download data about the surrounding beacons.

name: BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE
text: You find a Rebel automated scout floating near this beacon. Despite its pristine condition, it appears to be de-activated.

choice.text: Attempt to download the ship's data stores.
Don't risk activating it, and just strip the ship for any useful scrap.

name: REBEL_DEFECTOR
text: A Rebel ship is patrolling this beacon, and immediately turns to engage. As your crew scramble to battle readiness, sensors detect a short-range teleporter signal. An intruder is on board!

event.text: A flushed and panicky Rebel soldier has teleported aboard. The Rebel, who appears unarmed, repeatedly declares his peaceful intentions. It seems the Rebel life has lost its charm.

choice.text: Accept his proposal, and prepare to fight the Rebel ship.
Reject his offer. You can never trust these Rebels.
(Slug Crew) Have your crewmember check their intentions.
(Telepathic Shell) Have your crewmember check their intentions.
Terminate the intruder immediately. You can never trust these Rebels.

event.text: Your advanced security system easily removes the intruder, but the Rebel ship still needs to be dealt with.

name: REBELHOLD_SUPERFISH
text: You brace for impact as soon as you recognize the formidable hull of an MFK Ace. However, two things are wrong here. The first, their logo is not the usual eagle, but a very poorly drawn fish. The second, the ship isn't attacking. The second question is answered when they hail you. The captain is leaning back in his chair, feet on the dashboard, and chewing on a sandwich. "You're lucky you caught us on our lunch break. You don't tell anyone about this, and we won't either."

choice.text: Your logo looks like it was drawn by a toddler.

event.text: "Hey! This was the original design, before the idiots in command decided to stick with the eagle instead!" Enraged, the ship attacks.

"You really like it? This was the original design, before the idiots in command decided to stick with the eagle instead! Wait a minute- you're Jerry! How's it going, man? I haven't seen you since you were our best man at my wedding!" You aren't sure how these two hold a history together, but the Ace is so elated to see Jerry that he offers to work on your ship.
The Rebel chuckles and turns off the screen. You carry on your way.

name: DEFEATED_SUPERFISH
text: The strange MFK ship has been defeated. You scrap the remains.

name: REBELHOLD_ELITE_CHOICE
text: You jump in your seat when you see the Rebel Elite at this beacon. However, it seems they have not noticed you in return.

event.text: You prepare for combat with the elite.
You don't feel like dying today. You steer clear of the elite Rebel.

name: REBELHOLD_ARCHIVE
text: A large Rebel station is orbiting a nearby planet. It seems to be an archive of data, and is very poorly armed. It is however protected by an MFK Ace. There must be very important data in that archive.

choice.text: Attack the patrol ship to get to the Archive.

event.text: This will be one hell of a fight. You check to make sure everything is in order and ready for battle.
Whatever data that Archive holds, fighting an MFK Ace isn't worth it.

name: REBELHOLD_ARCHIVE_WIN
text: Seeing how you managed to take out one of the strongest classes of Rebel ships ever produced, the station isn't eager to fight back. They willingly surrender their facilities to you.

event.text: There's a lot more in the archive than you had even thought. You take only what you think would be useful, a map of the sector, and a beacon for merchants. You also take the liberty of deleting all data they have on the whereabouts of your ship.

name: REBELHOLD_SPEECH
text: On the nearby planet, there is a massive Rebel city that spans most of the planet's surface. A lot of Rebel and civilian ships are heading towards it, and you can see a stunning light show all the way from your ship. Something important must be going on.

event.text: You avoid all of the Rebel patrols and find a landing pad whose staff doesn't ask any questions about who you are so long as you turn off your weapons when you leave. You leave your Federation badges in the ship and follow all the traffic to a giant stadium.

In the center of the stage is an important looking Rebel politician, surrounded by 3 big screens projecting Rebel propaganda. You can just barely make out what he's saying over all the cheering from the crowd. "Friends and friends to be, we have all gathered here to celebrate the might of the Rebellion! We have received news that the new Rebel Flagship gifted to us by the Multiverse travelers has reached the Federation Capitol! The Federation's days are numbered, and soon the Rebellion shall rise and take its place!"

choice.text: Send one of your crew to assassinate the politician.

event.text: You wish you had brought your ship, but if you go back now it may be too late. You use your handheld scanner to find a good vantage point and send one of your crew to prepare.

choice.text: With you out here on your own, there is little to do.
(Elite Crew) Send your elite to assassinate the politician.

event.text: Your crew swiftly sneaks into the backstage, climbs onto the roof, and draws their rifle. It only takes one shot, and the lifeless body of the politician flops into the crowd, spraying the crowd with blood. Your crew hurries back, taking out two of the guards that try to follow on their way. The Fleet will be too busy dealing with all the chaos you've caused here, and likely won't be concerned with following you for a while.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Your Slug thinks they can hack into the screens.

event.text: Your Slug snickers as they hack into the screens' mainframe. The display goes black for a minute, confusing everyone in the crowd. A few seconds after, they switch to Federation propaganda. After a massively negative reception from the crowd and doubled efforts from the Rebels to counter the attack, your Slug gets tired and switches the screens over to a very explicit program. He breaks into laughter, and you hurry back into the ship before the Rebels can follow. When you return to the ship, you find a Soldier already waiting for you. Before you can raise your weapons, they hold up their hand to stop you. "No need to worry, I am on your side. I was sent to work undercover, but I haven't been able to contact the Federation for days. I was afraid I'd have to steal a Rebel shuttle to get back, but luckily I think I've found my way out with you guys instead."
The politician salutes to the crowd, and they begin to chant "Glory to the Rebellion!" You hurry back to the ship and leave.
Investigating a metropolis so deep inside enemy lines is suicide. Getting out of this sector is more important for your journey.

name: DISTRESS_REBEL_DISTRACT_CHECKPOINT
text: A Union ship waits here. "Oh thank heavens, we thought you were a Rebel at first. We've had to evade them several times, but fortunately they've bought all our excuses so far... We need your help, there is a nearby planet that is being guarded by a Rebel checkpoint. We have family there that we were trying to smuggle back to Union controlled space - would you please distract the checkpoint for us?"

choice.text: Agree and go attract the attention of the checkpoint.

event.text: The moment you approach, the Rebels accost you. "An enemy ship? You have 10 seconds to explain yourself before we destroy you!"

"By my stars, is that Jerome Wentworth? Hey, everyone, come look at who it is!" The entire checkpoint starts to come by the screen to see the famed nephew. The Rebels are all too happy to converse with him for as long as he wishes, giving the Union ship ample time to extract the other humans. One of the Rebels even tries to garner favor with Jerry by giving a present.

Your MFK imposes onto the checkpoint, making all the Rebels stand at attention. Your MFK takes their time, ensuring that no Rebel is near the sensors. Once the extraction is complete, you send your MFK the signal, and he gives the checkpoint a passing grade before departing.

choice.text: (Technician Crew) Inform them you are here to provide a system upgrade.

event.text: Your technician goes aboard the station. The Rebels are all impressed by the presence of a Wentworth Estate employee and allow them aboard. Your Technician powers the station off and pretends to do an upgrade, adding unnecessary but flashy features to their station, describing them as "cutting edge". The Rebels don't suspect a thing.
You decide that getting rid of the checkpoint entirely is the simpler solution.
"We'll find another way, then." The ship goes back into hiding.

name: REBEL_UNION_DISTRACT_CHECKPOINT_AFTERMATH
text: "Thank you for the distraction. We were able to get our families. We should be able to make it back to our home territory on our own." After compensating you, they jump away.

name: DISTRESS_REBEL_DEPOT_PROBLEM
text: The distress call comes from a Rebel munitions depot. "Renegade, this depot is not for you! Warp away, or we will call for help!"

choice.text: Aren't you already calling for help?

event.text: "You... make a good point." The Rebel sighs. "Our refrigeration units on this outpost broke down. All of our perishable food will spoil in less than a day unless we get it fixed. We sent our guard away to find an engineer who can fix or replace it, but they've completely dropped off the map. As it is, we're barely hanging on here. I have no desire to starve. Perhaps if you can help us, we can come to some kind of arrangement?"

They seem relieved to see a fellow human. The engineer diagnoses the problem, and indeed they have no parts to fix it. Fortunately, this component exists on your own ship as a redundancy. The refrigeration unit is fixed.

They seem wary at the prospect of an alien fixing their issue. The Engi diagnoses the problem, and indeed they have no parts to fix it. Fortunately, this component exists on your own ship as a redundancy. The refrigeration unit is fixed.

They seem relieved to see a drone with repair capabilities. It identifies the problem, and indeed they have no parts to fix it. Fortunately, this component exists on your own ship as a redundancy. The refrigeration unit is fixed.

As you dock with the depot, the Rebels desperately send a team inside to attack you. However, this will leave their stockpile entirely vulnerable, allowing your crew free reign to take from the depot.
You also find a leftover missile weapon in the depot.
It would be nice to plunder the depot intact, but it's better to avoid letting the Rebels use it. Maybe this will slow them down some. You take what you can find from the rubble.
The Rebels seem annoyed. It's likely they'll find a way to inform the fleet of your location.
You decide not to bother with the depot.

name: DISTRESS_REBEL_DEPOT_PROBLEM_SOLVED
text: "I guess you'll be expecting payment now, hm? Given your powerful armament, I guess we have no choice. We'll supply you with some missiles. Don't come back here, Renegade."

name: DISTRESS_REBELHOLD_POW
text: An encrypted Federation distress signal comes from an escape pod on a nearby planet. Decoding it, you get the following message: "Escaped POW. Evac requested immediately." In orbit, scanning for the prisoner is an MFK. For the moment, they seem distracted by their current duty of combing the planet.

event.text: As they become aware of you, they immediately switch to targeting you. "Well, well, well. Looks like we've found some more potential prisoners. We'll find the escaped one later."

choice.text: Use the distraction to slip away.

event.text: The MFK's sensors are occupied - this is an opportunity that doesn't come around often. You retreat before they notice you. Unfortunately, you don't have time to do anything as you prepare your escape.

name: REBEL_SELITE_POW
text: The MFK elite was formidable, but you managed to bring them down. You scrap their ship, getting quite the hefty bounty.

event.text: Your upgraded sensors pick up the location of the prisoner very quickly. You send down your crew to the escaped prisoner's hiding spot. Once your crew approaches them, they recognize you as Federation. Your crew welcomes the escaped prisoner aboard. "I knew it was a long shot, but Renegades have been known to make it this deep into Rebel space in the past. Please let me join your crew."

Your Lifeform Scanner picks up the location of the prisoner very quickly. You send down your crew to the escaped prisoner's hiding spot. Once your crew approaches them, they recognize you as Federation. Your crew welcomes the escaped prisoner aboard. "I knew it was a long shot, but Renegades have been known to make it this deep into Rebel space in the past. Please let me join your crew."

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Try to sense the prisoner.

event.text: Your Slug leads a search party looking for the prisoner. Using their telepathic abilities, they're easily able to figure out the prisoner's location. Once your crew approaches them, they recognize you as Federation. Your crew welcomes the rescued prisoner aboard. "I knew it was a long shot, but Renegades have been known to make it this deep into Rebel space in the past. Please let me join your crew."

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Try to sense the prisoner.

event.text: Your Shell leads a search party looking for the prisoner. Using their telepathic abilities, they're easily able to figure out the prisoner's location. Once your crew approaches them, they recognize you as Federation. Your crew welcomes the rescued prisoner aboard. "I knew it was a long shot, but Renegades have been known to make it this deep into Rebel space in the past. Please let me join your crew."

choice.text: Take some time to send down a search party.

event.text: The prisoner was very skillful at hiding - it's quite the undertaking to go looking for them. Eventually, they realize that the search party sent to rescue them is from the Federation, and they reveal their presence. Once onboard, they sigh with relief. "I knew it was a long shot, but Renegades have been known to make it this deep into Rebel space in the past. Please let me join your crew."

name: REBEL_CONSTRUCTION_CREW
text: As you enter the beacon, you notice the planetary system contains a number of construction ships gathered around a Rebel ship. As they are civilians, you might be able to tap into their feeds if you get closer.

event.text: The moment you get close enough, the Rebel ship stops broadcasting and attacks you on sight!

choice.text: (Upg. Mind Control) Wait until the end of the meeting and compel one of the construction ships to fill you in.

event.text: You corner one of the construction ships. Your Mind Control system hums to life, and the captain of the ship responds as if to a friend. "Oh, we're just headed off to enter the final construction phase of the newest Rebel space-dock in this sector. Let me give you the coordinates, if you want to stop by!"

choice.text: Leave before the Rebels notice you.
Attack the Rebel before you leave.

event.text: The Rebel seems so far unaware that you were here and attacks you on sight!

choice.text: (Mind Control) Wait until the end of the meeting and try to compel one of the construction ships to fill you in.

event.text: You corner one of the construction ships. Your Mind Control system hums to life - however, the captain struggles against the system. "Augh! We... are... helping... ttttttoooooo... build... a... spaaaaace dock." Before you can get much more out of the captain, however, the Rebel ship seems to have noticed your activities!

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Wait until the end of the meeting and compel one of the construction ships to fill you in.

event.text: You corner one of the construction ships. Your Mind Control weapon locks on and bursts with its hypnotic energies. The captain of the ship responds as if to a friend. "Oh, we're just headed off to enter the final construction phase of the newest Rebel space-dock in this sector. Let me give you the coordinates, if you want to stop by!"

choice.text: Leave before the Rebels notice you.
Attack the Rebel before you leave.

event.text: The Rebel seems so far unaware that you were here and attacks you on sight!

You get closer to tap into the broadcast. As you listen, you learn that a new Rebel space-dock is almost finished! These ships are going to finalize the construction process. During the speech you're able to glean the directions to the constructed spaceport. As the meeting ends, the construction ships approach the beacon and start jumping away while the Rebel stays at its post.

choice.text: Leave before the Rebels notice you.
Attack the Rebel before you leave.

event.text: You decloak behind the Rebel and ambush them. They are caught off guard, but quickly respond to your aggression!

choice.text: (Cloaking) Try to spy on the meeting.

event.text: You get closer to tap into the broadcast. As you listen, you learn that a new Rebel space-dock is almost finished! These ships are going to finalize the construction process. Unfortunately, you don't manage to find out much before your cloak wears off! The Rebel immediately attacks once they notice you.

choice.text: Keep your distance to avoid being spotted.

event.text: You keep your distance, so much so, that you aren't able to monitor their movements. Even so, you afford yourself the space to work on something else.

name: QUEST_REBEL_INCOMPLETE_DOCK

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Rebel space-dock is being constructed here.

text: With the coordinates you obtained, it's relatively easy to find the space-dock. It's most of the way done, but a few good shots in some vulnerable areas could bring it down. However, as you draw near, an Elite Rebel blocks your path. "So you want to hurt our infrastructure, don't you? I won't let you go any further!"

name: REBEL_DOCK_GUARD_DEFEATED
text: The Rebels scream as you swiftly end their lives. The elite ship was well equipped to defend their structure, but clearly not well enough.

event.text: The construction ships begin to flee. This is your chance to take it down.

choice.text: (Adv. Weapons) All out assault with your weapons system.

event.text: You pummel the dock's structure with your weapons system. The partially completed structure buckles and starts to come apart. Eventually, you reduce large areas of the dock to slag. While they still might be able to salvage this, you have certainly set them back.

choice.text: (Heavy Weapon) Hit the most sensitive spots with your heavy weapons.

event.text: You carefully line up your shots, and knock down the sensitive areas of the dock. Your precise hard hitting blows have exactly the effect you intended: the dock collapses in on itself under its own weight. With one final well placed shot, the mess explodes outwards. They're not making anything out of this anytime soon, but you most certainly are.

choice.text: Rig some explosives at critical areas to greet the Rebels when they come back.

event.text: You set up some explosives hidden in crucial areas, and arm them such that when the Rebels come back to this place and inspect your handiwork, they will be caught in the crossfire. This does mean you won't be able to salvage the wreckage of the dock, but you scrounge whatever materials they left lying around before you leave.
You have enough problems to worry about already. You carry on without any further interference.

name: REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK
text: A small damaged colony lies in the distance. It appears to have once been under Rebel control, but the colonists revolted and broke free. You receive a hail from the colony, marked as urgent.

event.text: "A Federation ship, here in the Rebel stronghold? Here, before us in our time of most dire need? This truly is our lucky day... As you can see, we have recently broken free from our Rebel oppressor. But it was not without loss. The Rebels took some of us as prisoners and are transporting them back to one of their high security containment facilities. We don't have the manpower to save them, but maybe you can? All you need to do is intercept the jailer ship. We placed a tracking beacon on it before it got away, so finding it won't be difficult."

choice.text: Agree to track down the jailer.

event.text: "Oh thank you. I knew we could count on the Federation!"

choice.text: We cannot risk our primary mission.

event.text: While it's a relief to see opposition against the Rebel cause even in their territory, you do not have time to stop by and assist with whatever requests these colonists would ask from you.

name: QUEST_REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK_JAILER

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of a Rebel Jailer detaining colonists loyal to the Federation.

text: You've found the Jailer. They're already charging their FTL drive. You'll have to take them down before they can escape, and hopefully not destroy the ship in the process.

name: REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK_JAILER_SURRENDER
text: The damaged ship hails you. "Y-you were sent by those colonists weren't you? Fine, you can have the prisoners back. Just let us live."

choice.text: Accept the surrender and free the slaves.

event.text: The colonists are grateful for your help. As you do not have time to return to the colony, you drop them off at the nearest station, where they will be able to find a ship to help them. You are paid heavily for your assistance.

choice.text: Screw the mission, let's kill these Rebel bastards.

name: DESTROYED_REBEL_PRISONBREAK
text: You've destroyed the jailer, and no doubt all of the colonists onboard. The colony will never give you a reward now, so you'll have to be content with the scrap from the wreckage.

name: DEAD_CREW_REBEL_PRISONBREAK
text: Without any of the Rebel crew onboard, you're able to scrap the exterior of the ship before checking on the prisoners.

event.text: The colonists are grateful for your help. As you do not have time to return to the colony, you drop them off at the nearest station, where they will be able to find a ship to help them. You are paid heavily for your assistance.

name: REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK_GOTAWAY
text: The Jailer jumps away, and will no doubt arrive at the containment facility before you can catch it. That doesn't mean all hope is lost. You can still track the ship's location, and maybe defeat it before the prisoners are dropped off.

name: QUEST_REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK_FINAL

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of a Rebel Jailer detaining colonists loyal to the Federation.

text: You've tracked down the jailer once again, but they've already transferred crew to a much stronger MFK Ace ship. It won't be an easy fight, and there will be no surrender. If you want to free the colonists, you'll have to kill their crew.

event.text: The Rebels aren't about to back down from a fight. The containment facility activates an ASB satellite to fire upon you.

choice.text: This is far too dangerous. We should go.

name: REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK_FINAL_DEADCREW
text: Without any of the Rebel crew onboard, you're able to scrap the exterior of the ship before checking on the prisoners.

event.text: It is very dangerous to transport all of the colonists back to the colony now. With the MFK Ace still intact, most agree to steal the ship and pilot back. However, one colonist decides to stay with you. You are paid for your efforts as well.

name: REBEL_COLONY_PRISONBREAK_FINAL_DESTROYED
text: You've destroyed the MFK Ace, and likely all of the colonists onboard. You'll have to be content with the salvage the ship provides, and leave quickly before the ASB can destroy you.

name: ENCOUNTER_REBEL_ASTEROID
text: Rebel ships often try their best to avoid hazardous beacons, but it appears a forward scout of the fleet has gotten lost in this asteroid beacon. Upon seeing you, they turn to attack!

name: ENCOUNTER_REBEL_SPY
text: You stumble across a forward scout of the Rebel fleet.

name: ENCOUNTER_AUTO_ION
text: A peculiar Auto-ship with blue lights reveals itself in this asteroid field. "This automated ship is a prototype Ion Deterrence Drone. Thank you for participating in this equipment test."

name: AUTO_ION_WIN
text: "T-thank you ffff-or participa- in this test- test- test- test-" the Auto-ship is silenced by an explosion. In the wreckage you find a still functional, special Ion weapon.

name: ENCOUNTER_REBELHOLD_STATION
text: A Rebel checkpoint identifies you as Federation. "You'll regret coming here, scum!"

name: ENCOUNTER_REBEL_ELITE
text: Rebel Elites are usually only seen in the Rebel Fleet, but it seems one of their ships is protecting this beacon. A fight is inevitable.

name: JERRY_QUEST
text: An MFK Ace ship is conversing with a transport, surprisingly not on an encrypted frequency. However, it seems obvious why. They're talking of nothing important, and you consider just passing them by, when suddenly the conversation shifts. The MFK, addressing the transport's captain, asks, "So, you're heading to the Protectorate, right?" The transport captain nods, briefly taking a cigarette out of his mouth to let out a simple "Yessiree".

event.text: The Ace leans in closer, eager to pry more details from the captain. "Really now? You gotta tell me what goes on in there. Years ago, Vance brought this scruffy little blonde kid to training, said he was his nephew or somethin'. He was some 3 years our junior, but he kicked every Ace's ass in combat practice, then waddled off to go draw a horse with some crayons on the wall. Then one day, Vance came back and yanked the kid. Don't know what happened to him, but I heard after director Black retired, Vance put her in the Protectorate to watch over his nephew."

The other Rebel captain nods, but the look on his face suggests he's growing impatient. "Yeah, yeah. Okay, cool exposition. But why are you telling me this? Aren't you supposed to be off, I dunno, killing Feds? I got a job to do buddy, I can't sit here on my ass all day. Get to the point." The Ace shrugs, displeased about his tone. "Look, what I'm asking for is some... you know, inside info? Surely, you got some if you go to and from that place all day."

The captain shakes his head. "First off, anything I could tell you, I can't. Closed lips on all that jazz. Second off, I don't know shit either. All I'll say is this - rumors are right about Cyra running the place, and she keeps a tight ship. I've never been past the wall. Well, a glimpse. But it's nothin' special. Now, get out of my way." The MFK Ace is indignant that even he has been refused information, but he only growls and moves his ship out of the transport's way. If you want to pursue this, now's your chance.
You take this moment to reveal yourself, and immediately the transport begins to charge its FTL drive. The MFK Ace flings itself to face you, weapons charging. You've gotta be quick about this!

tooltip.text: If you do not defeat the MFK Ace in this amount of time, the transport will escape!

event.text: The Rebel soldiers stare at you, utterly confused. You wait a little longer in desperate hope but, as you should have expected, the Rebels have no intent of giving you the information. The transport immediately begins to charge its FTL drive. The MFK Ace flings itself to face you, weapons charging. You've gotta be quick about this!

tooltip.text: If you do not defeat the MFK Ace in this amount of time, the transport will escape!

choice.text: Weird deja vu, but we've heard this all before.

event.text: This conversation isn't worth your time. You distance yourself from the Rebels.

name: JERRY_QUEST_FAIL
text: It seems you're out of time. In the distance, the transport escapes, and once the Ace realizes this they show an uncharacteristic display of cowardice and run as well!

name: JERRY_QUEST_SUCCESS
text: The transport makes every attempt to flee, and you follow them in hot pursuit. Unfortunately, they manage to slip away - but not all is lost. During the struggle you managed to get a lock on their FTL signatures, and now you can follow them during hyperspeed!

name: REBELHOLD_FLAGSHIP_SURPRISE
text: This is it... The Rebel Flagship. If you are able to destroy this monstrosity, the Federation fleet will have a chance of surviving. Only, it already looks to be significantly damaged, is transmitting a surrender signal, and this isn't even Node 17. What exactly is going on?

choice.text: Contact them. Something seems amiss here.

event.text: The crew onboard the Flagship initially seem terrified of your presence, though take on a slightly more aggressive demeanor to try and disguise it. "Shit, looks like we've been found out here. Whaddya want, you Renegade crazies? Scrap? A second surrender from us? Some sort of "secret ending" to celebrate over?"

The Flagship's captain continues. "Yeah, that's right. Back in whatever reality we were tasked with taking over, the Renegade who U0 tasked with taking us out somehow convinced the Rebel forces there to surrender. Impressive stuff, considering what you lot are known for. And good for us too, because we get a nice honorable discharge instead of getting murdered three times over. Then, on our way back to U1, we ran into some sort of bizarre anomaly and got flung here. Anyways, you never told us what you wanted, so spit it out."
"Well, that's easy to provide. Here you go. And make sure none of your Federation buddies in this reality know about us being here, got it?"

choice.text: Whatever that fancy weapon on your ship is.

event.text: "Oh, uh, that? U1 installed it on our ship before we even set off. They said something about it being a "new top secret weapon" or something of that nature. Unfortunately, we can't just hand it over. U1 command would kill us otherwise. So, how about a compromise?"
You accept the new offer. They then jump away, but not before asking you to keep their presence here a secret.

choice.text: Attack them to get the weapon.

event.text: "Ugh, should've known not to act reasonable around Renegades. Well, if you lot want a piece of this Flagship, we're gonna make sure you get the full package!"

choice.text: A little extra time in this sector.

event.text: "Well, that is something we can do, and odds are we're probably not going to get caught out on it, so I think we could help out by misleading the fleet. Just make sure nobody in the Federation knows we were here, got it?"

choice.text: Escape before they can attack you.

event.text: You give the Flagship a wide berth, in case it suddenly turns aggressive. Fortunately, it makes no attempt to initiate combat, leaving you with some time on your hands to prepare for the real deal.

name: FLAGSHIP_CONSTRUCTION
text: You arrive at the beacon to find yourself in a huge Rebel shipyard, scaffolding and construction drones filling the entire surrounding area! The entire system looks devoted to ship construction, the nearby planets and moons ruthlessly mined to harvest resources for ships of immense size...

event.text: You move closer to the planet's surface, noticing a giant hangar. The ships inside must be enormous in size. Around the outskirts are a few scattered Rebel ships patrolling. You could probably pick any one of them to fight.
You enter the hangar and are left in awe at the sight inside. A massive Multiverse Flagship, still under construction, rests inside. Dismantling this thing could save a whole other reality!

This could very well be just as important as your primary mission. You move in to attack the Flagship, as the crew of construction workers onboard quickly evacuate and are replaced by well trained human soldiers.

choice.text: Get the hell out of here.

event.text: You leave the hangar as quickly as possible and fly away from the shipyard until you're sure you're out of danger.

choice.text: Fight one of the normal Rebel ships.

event.text: You move in to intercept one of the regular Rebel ships.

choice.text: Fight one of the Elite Rebel ships.

event.text: You move in to intercept one of the Elite Rebel ships.

choice.text: Fight one of the MFK Ace Rebel ships.

event.text: You move in to intercept one of the MFK Rebel ships.
You feel the mission is the highest priority and it's too risky to stay in such a dangerous location.

name: FLAGSHIP_CONSTRUCTION_WIN
text: You know with an infinite amount of potential realities there are thousands more Flagships out there, but without this one at least one more reality has been saved. It's a major victory, and there's countless scrap for you to collect, and even the blueprints of a Rebel cruiser left unprotected! Cautious of reinforcements arriving, you take as much as you can and leave. The Fleet will likely be too distracted dealing with this loss to follow you.

name: CONSTRUCTION_NORMAL_WIN
text: It's not much of a challenge nor will it have any impact on the Rebels, but this ship destroyed still means one less crew of Rebels to terrorize the galaxy. You scrap the remains quickly before reinforcements come.

name: CONSTRUCTION_ELITE_WIN
text: It won't have much of an impact on the Rebels, but it's one less elite ship for them to throw at you. You scrap the remains quickly before reinforcements come.

name: CONSTRUCTION_SELITE_WIN
text: The Rebels cannot easily replace their fallen MFK Aces, and every one that you destroy is bound to put a big dent in their reserves. You quickly scrap the remains before reinforcements come, and while you're doing it you find a still functional weapon in the wreckage.

destroyed.text: The MFK Ace has been destroyed. You hastily scrap the remains then check on the transport.

deadCrew.text: The MFK Ace has been defeated. You hastily scrap the remains then check on the transport.

destroyed.text: You defeated the Flagship at this beacon. Hopefully this success bodes well for the rest of your mission.

event.text: Fortunately, the strange weapon you were interested in survived the fight. You carefully remove it from the wreckage of their ship.

deadCrew.text: You've cleared out the Flagship's crew. Though you're normally used to the Flagship having an AI take control under such circumstances, it seems it's either not present or not functional at this time, allowing you to salvage in peace.

event.text: Fortunately, the strange weapon you were interested in survived the fight. You carefully remove it from the wreckage of their ship.

deadCrew.text: You detect no more lifesigns on the incomplete Flagship. You'd expect a ship of that size to have more security measures, but perhaps their computer systems aren't complete yet.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LEECH_PSA
text: A nearby Leech medical outpost hails you. Looks like they have some important message to relay.

event.text: "Mental health is no laughing matter. Depression can be tough to go through, but just remember that you aren't alone. No matter where you are in life, you can't give up. Your family and friends are here for you. If you or a loved one is struggling with depression or suicidal thoughts, seek help and don't let it go untreated."
There's a long pause in the transmission. "Uhm... you know that Clone Bay is basically a murder machine, right? Just how many of your crew have died? You should let us replace it with a Medbay."
"You know what, I'm sick of you people. It's because of monsters like you that the Multiverse feels so hopeless!" A small Leech ship departs from the outpost and trains its weapons on you.

You wait for some dramatic twist or punchline, but nothing comes. Turns out, mental health is serious business. The Leeches offer you some scrap as thanks for listening, and hope you'll take this advice to heart.
Important message, important shmessage. It probably isn't that important enough for you to care.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LEECH_CREW
text: A large Leech carrier, no doubt a remnant of those fabled "glory days" looms in the distance. As you approach, a shuttle detaches from the ship and glides carefully through the asteroids towards you.

event.text: "Please help! I have been drafted into the military, but I know it is nothing but a death sentence. I still have my whole life ahead of me! Please take me with you!"
The Leech apparently won't take no for an answer. After a few more refusals and insults he eventually turns hostile and attacks!

name: NEBULA_LEECH_AMPERE_CONVERSION
text: There's a terminal at this beacon advertising a nearby planet with an Ampere Conversion Chamber - a Coalition-run place that can fast-track Leeches to Amperes, for a price.

choice.text: (Leech Crew) Send your Leech onto a shuttle.

event.text: The Leech secretary at the station seems very unengaged. "The fee is 30 scrap. There is no painkillers and we're not liable for long term side-effects."

Your Leech is covered end to end with electrodes and given an IV. They hesitantly enter the conversion chamber. After several minutes of sustained screaming, the sounds of electrical zapping and the faint smell of burning Leeches, your new Ampere crew stumbles out of the chamber. Aside from the pain, they seem to be no worse for wear.
Your crew returns to the ship, unchanged.

Tyrdeo hails the center. "Hello. It's your president. I'm leaving the sector to travel the galaxy, and I would like some backup. Is there any of you who will come with me?" The center sends you an Ampere right away who seems enthusiastic at the opportunity to travel out of Leech space.
You shouldn't risk contact with them unless you have a Leech, anyway.

choice.text: Do something else aboard the ship.

event.text: You've decided to use this beacon for a short reprieve instead.

name: LEECH_MISSION
text: Looks like a Chrysolic mission has been established nearby by the Theocracy. The permission to build these outposts was part of their trade to support the president against the revolution. It seems even the Inquisition couldn't stop the insurrection, but nevertheless these missions are littered around Leech space.

event.text: The moment you step aboard, you're greeted by the unpleasant musk of unbathed Rock clergymen and Leech bile. You manage to supress the vomit rising in your throat, but catch a few strange looks from the residents.

choice.text: Purchase a Crystal weapon from their shrine.

event.text: You honestly didn't expect the Rockmen to part so easily with their prized Crystal tech, but apparently money surpasses all else.

choice.text: Recruit one of the clergy to work aboard your ship.

event.text: Most of the Rockmen scoff at your offer, but one of the younger priests seems more than eager to go with you. Once on your ship, he attributes his quick change of heart to the smell.
The spiritual always seem to provide help for those of their own kind, though you don't suppose they would be so generous if your Rockman revealed he no longer served the Theocracy.

choice.text: Leave before the stench kills you.

event.text: You draw your weapons and engage.
The Theocracy isn't exactly friends with the Federation, and you can never know how their clergy might respond to your presence.

name: LEECH_MINERS
text: The dense asteroid field here seems to have another secret - a large Leech settlement embedded in one of the larger asteroids. It's camouflaged well, which suggests they don't want to be found.

event.text: Whatever this settlement has to offer isn't worth enduring the already present asteroid hazard. You prepare the next jump.

name: LEECH_COALITION_FEDUP
text: A Coalition ship hails you from nearby. At first you're hesitant of a trick, but they seem to genuinely want to talk. "I can't take it, I can't take it, I jusssst can't TAKE IT! Thesssse Leechesss are driving me mad! I could be in sssome cussshy job blowing up orphanagessss, but apparently Leechesss don't even HAVE orphanagesss! They've already blown them all up! What good isss there when I can't sssenssslesssly murder children?!"

event.text: "Yeah yeah yeah, whatever. Point issss, I need to let off ssssome sssteam. But I can't go killing Leechessss myssself, got one of thosssse wormsss working on my ssship giving me weird looksss while I tell you all thissss. Ssso go blow up sssome Leechessss. I don't care who. Better yet, if you find a not-blown-up orphanage, go blow it up!"
This'll make a good target. Hopefully the Coalition will be satisfied with this kill.
This'll make a good target. Hopefully the Coalition will be satisfied with this kill.
This'll make a good target. Hopefully the Coalition will be satisfied with this kill.

choice.text: (Leech Crew) Your Leech knows the location of the nearest standing orphanage.

event.text: Your Leech leads you to the location of one the last few standing orphanages. They seem surprisingly okay with the notion of destroying it, so you hesitate no longer to burn it to the ground. The Coalition captain launches into a fit of uncontrollable laughter.

"You actually did it? Ohhhh man, that felt sssso good to watch. I think I peed a little... or at leasssst I hope that'sss pee. Doesn't matter. You are an elite sssslayer of Leechesss! I think I will come with you in hopesss we can do thisss more often..."
"Losssser."

choice.text: Wait, did you say you're killing children?

event.text: "Oh crap, forgot you were a Fed. Oh well, guessss I can take sssolace in blowing you up. Jusssst pretend you're an orphan, alright?"

choice.text: Mute the ship and fly away.

event.text: Apparently the Slug is so caught up in his ranting he doesn't even notice you flying away.

name: LEECH_TAVERN
text: Though the nebulas in this sector are sparsely spread out, it's nevertheless nice to see a complete clearing. Looks like many travelers must agree, because a busy tavern has been established nearby.

event.text: Several air fresheners hang from the ceiling, and the faint stains of alien blood decorate the crimson walls. You spot several familiar faces of other Multiverse Renegades, but your attention is stolen away by two drunken Leeches arguing with each other over the state of the Eargen Republic. Judging from their slang, one appears to be a loyalist, and the other a revolutionary.

The revolutionaries are outraged. "You have no place in this, Federation captain! These morons support a leader so incompetent he gave the corpses of dead children to the admiral of one of the strongest military powers as part of a show of 'peace'!" Furious, a band of fellow revolutionary Leeches gather and attack your ship!

The loyalists are outraged. "So the Federation's decided to support these morons? Don't you realize this revolution is only going to perpetuate the same miserable cycle we've been stuck in for centuries?" Furious, a band of fellow loyalist Leeches gather and attack your ship!

choice.text: Don't get in involved, stay and chat instead.

event.text: These morons can argue all they want. You leave them to their devices and go sit down with the friendly faces from earlier, and soon the conversation turns to talk of trading.
No need to go visiting random taverns. Place probably smells like hell too if it's full of Leeches.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LEECH_GARDEN
text: Despite the nebula all around, a small Vampweed outpost is nearby. It's no military base either - the station's massive biodome seems to contain a variety of flora.

event.text: The minute you approach the outpost, a Vampweed ship detaches and attacks! You know they can be territorial, but this is quite an extreme reaction! Maybe you can reason with these guys after roughing them up a bit.

choice.text: (Vampweed Crew) Request access to the outpost.

event.text: It might be a stunning garden for sure, but make no mistake that the Vampweeds are your ally. If they have any reason to attack you, chances are they will.

name: LEECH_GARDEN_VISIT
text: The Vampweeds welcome you aboard the station. They offer you some fuel cells for showing so much interest in their garden.

choice.text: Buy one of their Spore weapons.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LEECH_DARWIN_FTL
text: An ancient Leech structure blankets this beacon in shadow when you arrive. Such ruins aren't uncommon in these parts - but the swarm of vessels darting in and out of it is.

event.text: Before you can even find an entrance, someone aboard the structure hails you. "Attention, Federation vessel. This archaeological site is closed to non-authorized personnel. Unauthorized entry will be its own punishment."

"This site was an FTL relay, dating back to our republic's glory days. As far as we can tell, it's basically a railgun, launching ships up to relativistic speeds to reduce the strain on their FTL drives - but after eons of drifting, it's pointed directly into the surface of a moon a few light-years away."

"I'm... not entirely clear on why you'd still want to come in. The only things to do here are dig out old sections of the relay, or destroy your own ship. Either way, this area is restricted, so I'm going to have to ask that you leave."
Archaeological sites like these are definitely valuable to someone, but nothing here is going to help you on your journey. Time to move on.

"Well now, a Renegade that doesn't have a death wish? Must be my lucky day. The main launch bay is cleared, but we're still trying to dig out all the power systems. It's a damn labyrinth in there - there's hardly enough room to move through areas we've cleared, let alone dig out more.

choice.text: Send in a team of crew to assist.
This ship is not equipped for delicate astroarchaeology work.

event.text: You send your crew in to the work site, where they immediately begin tearing apart any debris that doesn't look structural. A few minutes later, the station's manager runs out to offer you payment, on the condition that you don't attempt to help further.

Your engineer snaps to work, directing workers towards manageable sections of rubble while they arrange a plan for future excavation. The station's manager is impressed and offers you a moderate reward.
You give Tyrdeo's pet bird a command to clear the rubble, and it immediately flies off into an air vent, leaving you to wonder exactly why you thought this would be a good idea.

"Wealsey! Treat time! I know you like to explore, but we have places to be!" You prepare to have to pull Tyrdeo back onto your ship crying, but soon enough, Wealsey returns, trailing a tangled mess of wire from its feet, back into the vent it came from.

A deafening crash echoes through the structure as your haphazard pulling dislodges something on the other side of the vent. All the workers turn to you in anger, but before you can make a getaway, ancient light fixtures begin to flicker on all around the station. Satisfied that you probably fixed more than you broke, the station's manager offers you a reward, on the condition that you not try to help any more.
You shout into the depths of the work site, and hear nothing in response. If Tyrdeo were still alive, he'd be very upset about this.

removeCrew.text: Unfortunately, while Wealsey will likely die in the depths of the work site, there's no way for you to know when it happens. The clone bay and Wealsey's birdcage both sit silently.

choice.text: Bribe them to let you in.

event.text: You transmit your payment to the Leech managing the ruins, and soon light begins pouring out of a small hole in the side of the relay. You move your ship into the opening, and soon find your launch bay; miles of metal and circuitry stretch forth in two clean lines to either side of you - both pointing towards a narrow slice of space between them.

The two rails in front of you begin to glow with the light of a pair of suns, then suddenly seem to vanish from view, replaced by thousands of thinner lines all around you - stars, stretched beyond recognition by your own perception. You hardly have time to look at them, though - within a second, your once-distant destination fills the viewscreen, then the rest of the ship, as you and your vessel are dissolved into a puddle of freshly-heated lunar regolith.

lose.text: Your ship will remain a part of this moon's surface until another, equally stupid traveler displaces it.

choice.text: This is a terrible idea - leave.

event.text: Something stops you right at the last second - whether it's common sense or simple fear, you aren't sure, but either way, launching yourself into the side of a moon is starting to sound like a bad idea.
Archaeological sites like these are definitely valuable to someone, but nothing here is going to help you on your journey. Time to move on.
Whatever those ruins are, they aren't worth your time or energy. Time to move on.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LEECH_LITTERING
text: The nearby Leech ship looks to be dumping out several lumpy black bags from their airlocks near a trash ring. Must be another lazy do-nothing who can't be bothered to recycle.

choice.text: Hey! Stop that! Littering is bad!

event.text: The Leech captain looks at you, bewildered. "H-huh? Uhhh yes, littering. I do apologize. Uh... yeah..."

choice.text: Offer to pick it up for them.

event.text: "O-oh that won't be necessary... Er, actually. You know what, go ahead." The Leech ship quickly jumps away.

choice.text: Demand they pick it up themselves.

event.text: The Leech ship panicks, frightened by the responsibility now placed on them. They power up their weapons!

"Okay, okay. You know what, we're sorry, we're sorry. Please just stop talking to us. You're the police or something? You know we gotta dispose of these bodies somehow! Oh... I said too much..." The Leeches offer you a bribe if you don't tell anyone what they're up to. Your Orchid disapproves, but what are they going to do about it?
Littering is despicable, but you aren't willing to say anything about it. Way to contribute to the problem...

name: LEECH_LITTERING_WIN
text: You float closer to the black bags, and scoop them up into the ship. However, they're oddly... squishy. Pulling open the bag reveals a revolting sight of dismembered Leech organs, recently cut apart. Looks like these guys were trying to hide the evidence!

event.text: It's repulsive to think about and probably not all that ethically clean, but you aren't one to pass up such an opportunity.

choice.text: Toss the body parts back into the void.
(Clone Bay) Collect some DNA swabs and clone them.

event.text: The frightened and most certainly traumatized Leech that emerges from your Clone Bay proceeds to panic, and demands to know who you are. Once you've explained the situation, they calm down and agree to work. Probably because they're afraid you'll kill them too.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LEECH_FAKE_STORE
text: The most upbeat Leech you've ever seen - a Leech in a Cordovan hat - greets you. "Why hello there! Welcome to my fine establishment. I'll have you know that this is the most well equipped weapons store in the cluster! I sell amazing weapons! Just ask, whatever you want! I probably have it!"

event.text: "Stop, you're making a huge mistake! This is the deal of a lifetime!"

choice.text: Let this opportunity pass you by.

event.text: The Leech blocks you from leaving."Are you sure? There's so many good things on sale here. Don't you just want to take a quick look around?"
You don't let the salesman budge your resolve.

name: FAKE_STORE_BROWSE_1
text: "I can't wait to wow you with my impressive merchandise. What'll it be?"

choice.text: Ask if they have a Sehkmet Minelauncher.
Ask if they have a Nyx Missile Launcher.
Ask if they have an Asclepius Missile Launcher.
Ask if they have a Momus Missile Launcher.
Ask if they have a Pre-emptive Ion Blast.
Ask if they have a Stun Bomb.
Ask if they have a Conservative Bomb.
Ask if they have a Burst Laser 2.
Ask if they have a Halberd Beam.
Ask if they have a Cinquedea Pinpoint.
Ask if they have an Energy Stunner.

name: FAKE_STORE_BROWSE_2
text: The shopkeep waits to hear what you want to buy.

choice.text: Ask if they have a Sehkmet Minelauncher.
Ask if they have a Nyx Missile Launcher.
Ask if they have an Asclepius Missile Launcher.
Ask if they have a Momus Missile Launcher.
Ask if they have a Pre-emptive Ion Blast.
Ask if they have a Stun Bomb.
Ask if they have a Conservative Bomb.
Ask if they have a Burst Laser 2.
Ask if they have a Halberd Beam.
Ask if they have a Cinquedea Pinpoint.
Ask if they have an Energy Stunner.
Ask them if they even have anything at all.

event.text: "Why, yes! Of course we do! This is a store, after all. Just ask, and I'll see if we have it!"

choice.text: Ask them to give you some examples of items they have in stock.

event.text: "Well, uhhhh... this is a bit embarrassing, but all I've got right now is a crate of starving crazed giant alien spiders. But! There's a special deal on right now, so you can have it for free!"
"Oh well, your loss!"

"Here you go, enjoy!"
							
You hear frantic scratching sounds coming from inside the crate as it's brought aboard. The moment it's open, two spiders spring free and start rampaging through your ship. You're not sure why you thought this was a good idea.

"Here you go, enjoy!"
							
You hear frantic scratching sounds coming from inside the crate as it's brought aboard. The moment it's open, two spiders spring free and look as though they're about to go berserk, but before they do, the Queen roars at them. They cower slightly, and once you're certain they're no longer aggressive, your crew is able to feed them and they calm down.

choice.text: Ask them to give you some examples of items they have in stock.

event.text: "Oh, uhhhh..." The leech stares blankly. "Yeah, this is awkward to admit but... I was actually just wasting your time for no reason. But it was fun to pretend that we were a shopkeeper and a customer, wasn't it?"

choice.text: You've had enough of this. Attack him out of sheer, unbridled frustration.

event.text: "So that's a 'no', then? ...Yeah, that's fair."
"You know what, you're a pretty nice guy. I did have that first thing you asked for, actually. If I give it to you, do you mind if I join you?"

name: DISTRESS_LEECH_CARGO_LOST
text: There's a big mess in this asteroid field, with a lot of boxes floating in space. A Leech ship presumably involved with this hails. "We're in some pretty deep doodoo here. My cargo bay wasn't locked down properly and it came open at the worst time. You gotta help us!"

choice.text: (Magnetic Arm) Help the Leeches collect their strewn cargo.

event.text: Your Magnetic Arm is easily able to collect the cargo and direct it back into their bay. There is much relief amongst the Leeches. "Oh joyous day! Our stuff! For your aid, we'll give you a little reward. Out of all the races in this galaxy, our people are the ones who deal the most with asteroid fields, so we know a thing or two about autopilots. We can upgrade yours!"

choice.text: Take some time to help the Leeches collect their strewn cargo.

event.text: It takes quite some time to collect the lost cargo. Unfortunately, it's so time consuming that the Rebel fleet is able to gain on your position. The Leeches also seem to be somewhat impatient. "This will have to do... though it would have taken much longer without your help. For your aid, please take this reward. Out of all the races in this galaxy, our people are the ones who deal the most with asteroid fields, so we know a thing or two about autopilots. We can upgrade yours!"
You're not interested in helping them sort their problems out. In fact, you might just cause a few more for them.

choice.text: Focus on escaping the asteroid field.

event.text: You devote your energy to piloting away from the asteroids.

name: DISTRESS_LEECH_ETERNAL_COMATOSE
text: A small Republic colony is sending out a distress signal. "Something awful is happening... People are going to sleep and just... not waking up. Even the Clone Bay doesn't fix it. If you have any medical knowhow, please help us out."

event.text: After you dock with the colony, Anurak starts working. "Ah, yes! Your spiritual journeys have taken you down a dark and poorly lit path. No wonder you all keep dosing off!" Anurak begins to mix up his remedy. Tossing in some herbs, he grinds his remedy into a fine paste and begins to smear it onto their faces. The patient begins to stir. "You all need something to look forward to!" Anurak scribbles some notes onto a piece of paper and foists it into the hands of the Leech who contacted you.

choice.text: (Alkali) Have Alkali figure out what's going on.

event.text: After you dock with the colony, Alkali begins examining the patients. "My first guess is a lack of proper nutrition, perhaps compounded by a small illness and low morale." Alkali begins to set up vitamin shots for some of the patients. "Thhhere's somethhhhing wrong withhhh your food. If you get thhhhat sorted, thhhhat should be thhhhe end of it."

Your medic goes down to the colony and begins to check on the patients. After running a few tests, the medic determines that their food source is contaminated. While this alone wasn't enough, they then contracted a Leech illness that caused them to fall asleep with no hope of recovering. Your medic begins to feed the patients some vitamins, and that begins to rouse them, though they still may take a bit to wake up.

Your Shell goes down to the colony. After some tests, they determine that an illness the Leeches contracted caused them to lose consciousness, and without proper nutrition, they had no way of reviving. Since the Leeches are eating, the conclusion your scientist comes to is that their food source is contaminated. They prescribe vitamin tablets to all the afflicted and return to your ship.

choice.text: (Adv. Medbay) Examine them in your upgraded Medbay.

event.text: You accept some of the patients into your Medbay. Your advanced medical systems are able to flood their systems with nutrients and causes all of them to stir. Your medical bay reports that they were suffering from a somewhat common Leech illness, and had near total malnutrition. You tell them that they may want to examine the food they've been eating.

choice.text: (Quarp Juice) Give them something that will put some pep in their step.

event.text: You give the patients some of your Quarp Juice. After a few moments they jolt awake, practically bouncing off the walls. They still don't look well, but they start thanking you with a crazed mania atypical of their species.
The Leech in charge of the distress call looks concerned. "Are you sure that stuff is healthy...? Oh well. At least they're up and about again." The Leeches give you a gift for your assistance.
You have some free time to spend doing something else.

name: LEECH_COMATOSE_COLONY_GRATEFUL
text: The Leeches thank you profusely. "Thank you so much... we didn't know why a common sickness would put us to sleep like that. What could have happened to our food? We will have to look into it. In the meantime, please accept this gift."

name: DISTRESS_LEECH_GRAPHITI
text: Through the asteroid field here, you're surprised to find a Federation vessel, covered in heavy graffiti! They hail. "A band of pesky teenaged Leech delinquents came by, drew all kinds of nasty things on our ship, stole our cargo, called me some horrid name. It sounded like they said 'boomer', whatever that means. Could you be a pal and go get back our cargo?"

event.text: You follow the Fed ship's directions until you find a small Leech shuttle with 3 or so Leeches inside. As soon as you approach, they start laughing at you and shouting various uncreative insults.

choice.text: Send a little warning shot to scare them.

event.text: You lock the weapons onto one of the passing asteroids near the shuttle. The explosion doesn't seem to frigthen the adolescents, but rather seems to egg them on. "Hey old man! Keep that up, and I'm gonna call my dad on you!"

"Hey! I said not to do that! Alright, now you're in for it!" You detect a distress signal being broadcast from the shuttle, and moments later an Ampere ship jumps in. "You been touching my son? I'm going to carve out your skull and use it to drink my regurgitated bile!"
"Hah! No! What're you going to do, tell my dad or somethin?"
"Wait crap, please don't! He'll be super mad! I'll kill you!" The Leech ship attacks!

The Leech struggles for a few moments, the uncontained power of teenaged angst rivaling that of one of the most sophisticated manipulative technologies in the galaxy. Inevitably, he gives in. "I think I will give you the cargo. And, I will learn to respect my elders."

choice.text: Bring the cargo back to the Fed ship.
(Mind Control Weapon) Give us the cargo.

event.text: The Leech struggles for a few moments, the uncontained power of teenaged angst rivaling that of one of the most sophisticated manipulative technologies in the galaxy. Inevitably, he gives in. "I think I will give you the cargo. And, I will learn to respect my elders."

choice.text: Bring the cargo back to the Fed ship.
(Upg. Weapons) Pull a trick shot and start blasting up all the asteroids.

event.text: Losing all self control and embracing your inner wild-side, you spin the ship around in circles, blasting up countless hundreds of asteroids. The Leeches are no longer quite so unfazed. "Dude, I think this guy is a psychopath. What the actual hell even WAS that?" The Leeches hand over the cargo, afraid you might snap at any moment and kill them too.

choice.text: Bring the cargo back to the Fed ship.

event.text: You aren't an errand-man. They might not have their cargo, but this ship is more than capable of handling some teenagers.

name: LEECH_GRAPHITI_RETURN
text: "Oh thank Newton. That'll show those brats not to deface government property."

name: NEBULA_LEECH_DELEGATE
text: It appears you're receiving a long ranged transmission with Zoltan encoding, marked as urgent. To the Zoltans, all matters are 'urgent', but it still might require your attention.

event.text: "Before the time of the current president, Tyrdeo, the Eargen president Oertiss led an unsuccessful invasion against Zoltan space. His leadership was cut short when his soon to be successor Aerkae led a siege on Oertiss' palace and hacked him into tiny bits which were embalmed and kept as trophies."

choice.text: Cool history lesson, but why are you telling us this?

event.text: "Have patience. The Ministry was satisfied with Aerkae's appointment, but to prevent future attacks it was agreed upon that the Ministry may install up to 3 embassies within Leech territory that would also serve to ensure further... incidents would not occur. This has been upheld by all subsequent Leech presidents until now. Under Tyrdeo's leadership, it seems he has become so overwhelmed with the current revolution, he has turned ignorant to the effects of the Inquisition and furthermore the Coalition being allowed in his territory."

choice.text: Please, just get to the point.

event.text: "We are nearly there. As the Ministry supports the Federation, it is within the Coalition's best interests to prevent Federation and therefore also Ministry intervention in conflicts involving them. They appear to be afraid to take action directly however, and thus have hired the Tiiikaka slaver clan to enslave our delegates and ship them off to other stretches of the galaxy. As a Federation ship, we request that you travel to these co-ordinates and put an end to this." The Zoltan hang up without so much as a please or thank you.
The Zoltans can deal with their own problems. Traveling through Leech space is dangerous enough.

name: LEECH_DELEGATE_CAMP

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Ministry embassy is under siege by Tiiikaka raiders.

text: As warned, a band of Tiiikaka pirates have taken control of the embassy at the given coordinates, and are rounding up the Zoltan officials and taking inventory.

event.text: You've seen enough - time to put a stop to this!
Apparently, the slavers weren't prepared to see a well armed Federation ship out here. They quickly hurry back to their ship and take off.

choice.text: Purchase one of the Zoltan slaves.

event.text: The slavers are startled by your sudden appearance, but once they realize your offer is in earnest, they quickly go along with it.
It's risky getting involved with slavers. Tiiikaka isn't known for showing mercy, and you don't want to get caught on their bad side.

name: LEECH_DELEGATE_CAMP_WIN
text: The Zoltans are shaken, but alright. Not long after, a Zoltan war vessel armed to the teeth jumps in, and you recognize the voice as the same one from earlier. The Zoltans introduce themselves with a brief "We'll take it from here", then begin reorganizing the embassy. Again, you receive no thanks, but you do at least talk them into giving you a reward.

name: ENCOUNTER_LEECH_PULSAR
text: Though this forsaken sector might be mostly asteroid fields and nebulas, apparently a pulsar has found its lovely way here to bother you some more, while a Leech ship locks on and attacks!

name: ENCOUNTER_LEECH_VAMPWEED
text: According to the stories, Tyrdeo pissed off the Vampweed Premier so much by handing him a handpicked bouquet of flowers during a diplomatic meeting, that he outright declared war on their entire species. Hilarious story yes, but unfortunately the Vampweeds are the exact opposite of their Floral brethren and aren't quite so hesitant to attack passerbys like yourself!

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_ENCOUNTER_LEECH_ELITE
text: Though most of the Eargen military has fallen behind, the Amperes have remained a major threat thanks to the Coalition's support. While a majority of the Ampere forces are dedicated to helping in Coalition efforts, many still remain in Leech space to fight off threats. Threats like you, apparently.

name: ALKRAM_MEET
text: Curiously, a fleet of Eargen ships have congregated here as they're fired upon by revolutionary vessels. It's an unfortunate skirmish to get caught in, until you spot an unusually decorated craft flying among the ships.

event.text: The strange vessel seems to be a battleship of some sort, bearing the paint of a Leech general. You can't look at it for long however, because an Ampere vessel has spotted you and assumes you're hostile!
It's far too risky to get any closer to the conflict. You put as much distance from yourself to the other fleet ships as possible.

name: ALKRAM_MEET_WIN
text: With the ship out of the way, you turn your attention back to the strange Leech ship, but see it has slinked away from the combat. It's heavily damaged, and the interior view shows wounded soldiers and one heavily armored Leech wiping blood off of his teeth using his tail.

event.text: "So, you've come to kill us? Another one of Tyrdeo's pawns. Do what you may, but know that the Republic will fall. I have put into motion things you cannot undo by simply killing me. Cut off a Leech's head, and it'll only grow back stronger!"

choice.text: We have no idea who you are.

event.text: The Leech pauses, and his two eye slits squint tighter than normal. "You look too high standing to be an agent of that purple parasite. My introduction is irrelevant, so I will spare you the details. I am Alkram Tripae, former general of the Eargen Republic under leadership of President Oertiss during the Federation-Mantis War. Now, in my old age, I have taken to ensuring the stability of the crown by ridding it of its current incompetency."

choice.text: Crown? I thought Tyrdeo was president.

event.text: "Exactly my point. That exuberant, dimwitted moron carries with him a shiny golden crown and fancies himself king, yet he has done nothing but lead our kind into even greater turmoil. If you do not fight for Tyrdeo, and are most certainly not of the Rebellion, then I figure you must be Federation in some respect. This skirmish is only a minor one - soon, we will reconvene at Tyrdeo's mansion where he is hiding, and seize the Republic. If you stand for the same liberties as the Federation claims then I hope you will join us." Alkram transfers over some coordinates and immediately goes back to focusing on his crew.
