event.text: You didn't come this far to give up now. There's nothing left to do but destroy this ship. Fail, and the Federation is doomed, succeed and save this reality forever. The stakes are high, but you don't have time to think about them as you get ready to fight.

choice.text: (Nights) Nights seems to have something say to Vance.

name: SHOWDOWN_NIGHTS
text: Vance pauses, and appears on the vid screen. Nights scrolls up closer, taking another swig of his beer. "Ssssay... what wassss your name again?"

event.text: Vance grunts and scowls. "Admiral Vance Wentworth. What's it to you, slime pinata?"
Nights chuckles and takes another sip. "Heheh... Admiral Vance Wentworth, huh? More like... Wentworthlessssss! HAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAH!"

Through Nights' intoxicated laughter and hiccuping you can hear Vance growling, as his eye twitches in annoyance. At last, you've found validation for keeping this slimey asshole on your ship. Too bad you can't delay the inevitable any longer - it's time for a showdown!

name: SHOWDOWN_TULLY
text: Vance pauses, and appears on the vid screen. Tully steps foward, arms crossed behind his back. "Wentworth. Please, listen to me, not as an adversary, but as your old friend. Don't do this. Think of what you're doing, is all of this really worth it? You'll kill trillions of people and for what? To settle some petty score? You've built an empire that can compete with the Federation - why can't you just be satisfied with that?"

event.text: Vance's glare softens, but the determined look on his face doesn't falter. "This is well beyond simple revenge, Brodric. Have you never wondered why we still carry the title of Rebellion? Because it keeps our ideals and our mission true to the heart of every man who marches under our banner. To simply co-exist with the Federation is to willingly allow not only trillions but a near infinite pool of people continue to suffer."

"This multiverse will only know peace when the Federation has finally been dissolved and a new, glorious civilization can be built where the barbaric xeno-lifeforms can continue their malpractices in their own private suffering while humanity is allowed to prosper as we were always destined to do. The people of Universe 0 had their chance, but they have failed. It takes a person of diamond will to be able to commit to the lesser evil. I do not want to fight you, Brodric, but don't think our history will stop me from fulfilling my purpose."
With that, Vance ends the call immediately and his ship goes back to charging its MV Drive. Tully looks defeated, but you don't have time to contemplate. It's time for one final showdown!

name: SHOWDOWN_JERRY
text: As you approach the Flagship's artilleries lock onto you, preparing to blast you into oblivion. Before they can discharge however, Jerry quickly hails the ship, using confidential Rebel access codes. You wait for the response...

event.text: Though the Flagship never stops running, onto your bridge teleports the formidable figure from before. Vance has arrived. He takes a few steps towards you, glancing at Jerry in confusion.
"The Federation has fallen on hard times, if you should feel it necessary to kidnap my nephew and use him as bait to stop me from achieving inter-reality peace!"

Vance chuckles. "And what, he just willingly joined your crew? Don't be ridiculous. My nephew's loyalty to the Rebellion is unmatc-" Vance is cut off by Jerry. "They're telling the truth, uncle! I'm tired of the Rebellion. What are we even fighting for? You can't possibly rule a single reality, let alone an infinite number of them! Are you really going to outcast the dozen other sapient species? Your plan makes no sense!"

You can see Vance's eyes starting to narrow. "You stupid boy. You're just like your mother, aren't you. Blinded by false morality, unable to progress because you're too busy trying to drag the simple, ignorant creatures that should be serving us out of the primordial ooze they belong in! Yes, my plans sound grand, and that's because they are! But it takes a man of commitment and courage to accomplish that which I have set out to do. I'll be damned if anyone, family or not, keeps me from the greatness that awaits an existence under my rule."

Jerry stutters, unsure of how to react to this insult. Vance makes a simple gesture with his hand, as if to shoo him away. "I advise you all to make whatever futile preparations you need. I shall return to my ship, and I will not let any further interruptions impede me." Vance presses a button on his belt, and teleports back off to the Flagship in the distance.

Jerry collapses to his knees, shocked and speechless as how easily he was betrayed. "I should have known..." Jerry chokes up a sob, and holds his head in his hands while tears form puddles on the ground.

removeCrew.text: Jerry sits in the corner, crying. The Flagship approaches, weapons charging. You want to console him, but you have to get going.

event.text: Suddenly, Jerry gets back up to his feet, wiping away the tears. "Well, there's only one thing left to do now." He draws out a massive Gatling gun. You aren't sure where he got it from, but you don't have the time to question it.
With Jerry armed and ready, it looks like there's nothing left to do but fight!
Before you can proceed on to the Flagship, Jerry pauses, and walks out of the room.

removeCrew.text: You have no idea where Jerry is going, but you follow him.

event.text: Jerry enters the room where the Equinoid is sleeping...

removeCrew.text: You have no idea what Jerry is doing, and watch in confusion.

event.text: Then, Jerry proceeds to mount the pony! "Alright. Now I'm ready."
Before you can proceed on to the Flagship, Jerry pauses, and walks out of the room.

removeCrew.text: You have no idea where Jerry is going, but you follow him.

event.text: Jerry enters the room where the Equinoid is sleeping...

removeCrew.text: You have no idea what Jerry is doing, and watch in confusion.

event.text: Then, Jerry proceeds to mount the pony! "Alright. Now I'm ready."

name: SHOWDOWN_WIN
text: You watch in triumphant jubilation as the Flagship explodes. You've won this battle!

name: TRUE_VICTORY
text: As the MFK Flagship is destroyed, and Vance with it, you know your mission has been a success. The Rebellion will struggle to recover without their leader, but this won't be their death. You retrieve the nearby Paragon from the wreckage, and bring it back to your ship. Knowing there is little time left to lose before the fleet catches up, you take one last look at your crew. To detonate this bomb means the collapse of the Multiverse, and MV drives will simply cease to function. This will mean an end to the war... but it'll kill you and your crew, as well as strand billions of people from around the Multiverse. The choice is yours, captain. How does this end?

choice.text: Detonate the Paragon; end this war.

event.text: You know what you have to do. This war must end, no matter the cost. You've been given this chance, and you won't pass it up. Your crew understands, they signed up to this knowing very well they might die. You say your last goodbyes, and activate the bomb...

choice.text: Destroy the Paragon; save your crew and your fellow travelers.

event.text: This isn't your choice to make. You can't decide the fate of the entire Multiverse. You lift the Paragon, then bring it hard down onto the metal floor, smashing the seemingly invulnerable piece of tech into a million pieces. This war might never end, but if it does, it won't be because of the actions of one person.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW
text: You look around at your crew, who are standing, waiting for your verdict.

choice.text: Ask the Beacon Eater about this.
Ask Tintan and Rig about this.
Ask the Orchid children what to do.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_DETECTIVE
text: "We've come far, yeah? To think, not that long ago I was just working on a simple murder case, and I thought that was the most excitement I'd see in my whole life! Now look at us! I must say, it would be a terrible shame for my legacy to end like this, but whatever you choose, I'm onboard."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_TULLY
text: "To think, I was worried about a silly civil war when such greater things were happening behind my back. How could I go back to the Federation now that I know it's all for naught? Vance, my oldest friend, is gone. I should have remorse, but he was gone long before this conflict. Don't let me influence your decision here, I haven't got a single right to sway your mind. You're the Admiral now, captain."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_A55
text: "Arg lad, it's been fun serving you. End of the day, don't matter much if I was built by Rebels or not when I got to be a part of your crew, matey. It'd be a mighty shame for the pirate king to die like this, but only because it's one hell of a story I could never tell!"

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_JERRY
text: Jerry looks down at his feet. "I... I think it's a good thing my uncle is gone. Not to say I hated him, but for the good of the Multiverse it's only best. I suppose this makes me the hero Vance always wanted me to be, just not in the way he expected. Savior of the Multiverse is a pretty good title! I'm glad I met you, captain. I'll stick with you to the end, whether that's today, tomorrow, or the end of time itself."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_ANURAK
text: "Oh dear, Shellskenbry! This is really quite something! I don't... I don't know what to make of it all! But, you want my opinion on this? Oh I'm not very good with decisions. No no not at all! Uhm... oh my... uh... uh... I think you should do it! The bomb! The bomb... is what you should do. Yes. Uhm. I don't know why. It's just what first comes to my head. I think if I tried to explain it I might change my mind and I don't want that kind of indecision right now! Just... just do it quickly, okay? Oh I hope it doesn't hurt..."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_DEVORAK
text: "That bastard Vance finally got what was coming to him, and I am damn glad I was aboard the ship that did it. If that does not clear my name to the eyes of the Federation and the Ministry, then I'll be damned. As for me... Blowing up myself along with the rest of time and space sounds like a pretty fitting end to my story. I've served my purpose - don't let me hold you back from pulling the trigger."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_MAFAN
text: "I'm grateful, captain! Look at all these new places I was able to go, all these wonders I was allowed to experience! Frankly, I'd love for the opportunity to write about everything I've experienced here... but don't let that stop you from doing what needs to be done. I don't mind concluding my life by being at the epicenter of a massive meta-cosmological explosion."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_TURZIL
text: "It is [untraditional] for an Engi to feel emotions. It would seem my -logical- receptors have been clogged by most unusually pleasurable feelings in your company. This is not the mission I signed up for. But I do not regret it. I must [remind] you however, that my people still need me. My absence would cause -disastrous- consequences. But so would the continuation of the war. A troubling dilemma. Most troubling."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_MAYEB
text: "All I've ever known is my life in the gardens, tending and advocating for plants that can't fight for themselves. Those plants, not to mention most life that exists out there, know nothing about Rebels, multiverses, Obelisks, interstellar wars... What I'm trying to say is, if we have to lay down our lives so that they won't be tread underfoot by forces they can't even comprehend, then I'm behind you all the way."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_IVAR
text: Ivar is drinking some of his nicest wine in celebration, and offers you a glass as well. "Me? I think the multiverse is a nice thing. Sure, it might be dangerous, but I don't believe in limiting ourselves out of fear. Hah, but don't listen to me; I'm not gonna tell you what to think. Let's just share a glass before you make your decision. If you do decide to end it, just give me a minute or so to make sure the crew is drunk and happy first. Got it?"

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_TYEREL
text:
Ty E'Rel is leaning back in his comfy chair, with his roots up on his ottoman. The desk is neatly arranged, all the papers are put in their proper places. As he meets your gaze, he gestures to the chair next to his. The two of you sit, wordlessly relaxing after a long and arduous journey. Resting here, he appears even older than he usually does. Eventually, you get up to leave, but as you open the door, you finally hear him speak. 

	"You should do it." 

	He doesn't say anything more.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_ALKALI
text: "Hahahah! I knew thhhere ain't no shit like immortal demigod aliens. We sure put the fear of science in thhhhose narcissists. I'll be highly disappointed if you flick thhhat switch and I don't get to rub my victory in thhhat bitch Nerva's stupid little face. Hah!... Erm. Sorry. You're alright, kid. I expected worse when we first met. Don't let it go to your head hearing it coming from me; thhhough I wouldn't blame you if it did."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_OOJ
text: "Pur too look-loo kik pik ripple steep." You have no idea what this means, but the sentiment behind it is not lost when OOJ shapes himself into a large heart. You give the giant blob a hug as he jiggles in your arms.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_ELLIE
text: "Hahahah! Ellie is on top of the world! On top of the Multiverse! Neeeiiiigh!" Ellie spins around in circles. "It would be a shame for Ellie to die now! She still has a duty to all the children, all the children who will never see Ellie again if she died! Don't blow the bomb superfan, think about what you'd be robbing the Multiverse of!"

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_STEPHAN
text: "We've come so far! Maybe... maybe after this, I really am a hero. Something for children to look up to... Even if they'll never know what we've done. I don't... I don't care what happens next. You've given me a chance at redemption, and that's all I care about. Thank you, captain."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_NIGHTS
text: Nights scowls at you, but on his face you can see the faintest line of a smile you've ever seen in him outside of when he's being smug. "For the record, I ssstill hate you. But compared to everyone I hate, I hate you sssslightly lessss than the ressst. Anywayssss, thisss sssure hasss been a real sssshitty trip. If you're tellin' me I gotta blow myssself up after all of thisss, I'm gonna ssstrangle you." Knowing Nights, this is likely the closest thing anyone will ever come to for being his friend. Hopefully he isn't being serious about strangling you though.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_SLOCKNOG
text: "Beat being king, the name Ssslocknog isss going down in hissstory as ssssavior of the universssse! Hehehe. Wait, if we blow that bomb, no one will know about thisss, will they? Ehhh, ssscrew thossse guysss. If you want my sssay, I sssay blow it. I got nothin' to go back to anywayssss."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_IRWIN
text: "I... I don't know what to think, mate. All thisss time I thought I wasss some hot ssshot Renegade hunting the biggessst game in the Multiversssse... and all thisss time I've jussst been an insssignificant ssspeck in the grand ssscheme of two different massster plansss. I feel like I'm having a moment of introssspection and I HATE it. Pleassse, don't let me live to sssee myssself become a good perssson. The Multiversssse sssucksss anywaysss. That bomb'll do only good."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_ALKRAM
text: Alkram grunts, pretending to be indifferent to the situation. "When we first met, the most important thing on my mind was overthrowing Tyrdeo. Yet, now that seems so insignificant... I'm a soldier, not a speaker. Lemme put my words as blunt as possible for you. Only way my people or ANY people are ever gonna learn, is when we stop relying on other people to fix our problems. This whole Multiversal War thing isn't helping anyone when the Federation, Rebellion, Coalition, or god knows who else keeps intervening and 'fixing' everything. I implore you to blow that bomb and put things the way they were before for the sake of everyone."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_TYRDEO
text: "Oh sweet heavens I feel faint. Is it true? We're alive? Remarkable. You're the first person not on my payroll to stand at my side while facing such adversity. I cannot thank you for all you've done for me. It feels out of place for silly old me to have any say in this... but I'd like to keep living. And I'm sure you would too. Heh... What do you think happens if we die to that thing? Are we gone for good? Oh I don't want to think about it."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_FREDDY
text: "Good work chap, this is truly a spectacular moment and I couldn't think of any better way to spend it than sipping tea at the end of time. You do intend to blow the bomb, yes? Don't worry about me, the Free Mantis haven't relied on my support for years. They'll be scared, yes, but they'll make do. No more Multiverse means no more Rebels, and maybe things will finally settle down for once. My days were numbered anyways. A Mantis can only live so long."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_KAZ
text: Kazaaak seems uncertain of what to say. "For first time in long time, I am not knowing what to say. You are greater warrior than I ever was. But think, if we do not detonate Paragon and return home, we could achieve so much more! We could be greatest heroes in all of time! How could you pass up this chance?"

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_ARIADNE
text: Even in the face of this great triumph, Ariadne remains stoic, save for a faint smirk on her face. "When I offered my services to you captain, I didn't expect you to drag me across the Multiverse into the pit of demigods to overthrow the Rebellion. But - it's been an honor. However, my initial mission is not complete. The Theocracy has not yet been defeated. I'm afraid that bomb of yours will do little to stop the Elders. I understand this is not my call to make, but I hope you have considered the weight of this decision."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_RUWEN
text: "I feel as though I have served a purpose far greater than the one I set out to. You are truly the most remarkable, accomplished captain I have ever had the honor of meeting. You remind me of someone else I met long ago, another Federation captain.. But even they couldn't come close to this! But, would the destruction of the Multiverse be worth it? Think of the wonders that this technology could accomplish. It's much the same situation as my people - there will be chaos in the beginning, but I'm certain things must settle eventually. No war can truly last forever!"

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_DIANESH
text: "To think, I merely joined your vessel as a trial to judge you foreigners. I think it is safe to say you have passed that test, and with flying colors. I wish I had the same fervor, to go jumping across the Multiverse just to save reality. This Multiverse tech has been the ruin of many civilizations, but it has also been the birth and savior of so many more. Had you asked me any other day, I would say to detonate that bomb in an instant. But now, I can only wonder if it's best left unused..."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_TUCO
text: "This whole journey I've felt drunker than I ever did back on Sky-Drifter. It's been one hell of a trip. But hah, I can drink to this victory!" Tuco pulls out a remarkably still intact bottle of booze and downs it in seconds. "My glory days are long since over. The Multiverse doesn't need me, and frankly no one needs the Multiverse either. But if we do live past this day, I'd love to share another drink with ya, pal."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_EATER
text: "Sparing words, difficulty communication. Symbolic gestures appropriate of more timing." The Beacon Eater retracts his mighty spikes for the first time since you met and reaches over to give you a hug. You didn't know Lanius could even do that. You prod further but it seems the Beacon Eater has nothing to say about the Paragon. For a creature that's been alive longer than the Obelisk Empire itself, it's not surprising he cares little about his own mortality anymore.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_ANOINTED
text: "From ancient ruins I heard mention of Paragon. But never in even dreams was I thinking I find it! If I am Anointed, then you are divine beyond doubt!" The Anointed bows to you. "For centuries my people revere Obelisks as gods, but now I am knowing of their true menace. I could not thinking any better end to their empire than the destruction of Multiverse."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_DESSIUS
text: "Oh grandfather Aneidio, if only thou could witness me now! Y-you. You are not worthy of a title. You have ascended past such mortal things. You have but completed in such short time what the legacy of all 16 Reapers could never. What are you? I dare not insult you with conjecture. But if you should accept my humblest opinion, then hark and listen. This Paragon, oh foul creation, is a tool of the Obelisks. An antithesis to their power yes, but of their making. Should it not seem to you most cruel after all of this to give them their way and let it be their invention that divide reality? The Obelisks will fall, but the Multiverse is a fact of our existence. Would it not be sorrowful to deprive reality of such a beautiful thing, to defile nature once again with the patent of cruel gods? Think these thoughts I ask of you, but do not let me be the one to stop you."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_VORTIGON
text: You find Vortigon is not with the rest of the crew, rather he has crumpled into a ball in the corner of the ship. "Oh you, Almighty Slayer of the Infernal Cube Demons, Saviour of the Multiverse, and Grand Lord of Being Above Average, everything I have ever known is a lie. I have SEEN the Ember spirits with my own eyes and I have killed them with my hands. How could a god bleed? Divinity is a lie. I cannot live with myself. I have led so many men and women astray, I have poisoned the masses with tainted lies. Yes, I believed them too, but if fate was not the one that put me there, then it was my own hubris. I ask you one final favor. I do not care what you do with the Paragon, it's far beyond my worries. But if we live past this day, take mercy on me and see to it I never return to my home. Cast me into the abyss before you sentence me to looking into the eyes of my victims once more."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_BILLY
text: "Thissss isssn't quite what I expected when I joined your crew. But hey, if there wasss any doubt about a galactic hero, an interdimenssssional hero sssure asss hell doesssn't pay taxesss! Oh, and uh... thanksss for not ssstabbing me in the back, like everyone elssse hassss. Now, assssuming we live, do you think I could ssstart ssselling Paragon merchandise? I could immortalize your image forever! But if you don't mind, I'd really like to go home. I have ssso many thingsss I need to fix, and if our journey endsss here, I'll never get the chance."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_SYLVAN
text: Sylvan puts a tentacle on your shoulder. "Ssstranger... in the many yearssss I've lived in thisss wild Multiverssse, I've ssseen about all there isss to ssssee. Or at leassst, ssso I thought, until I met you. The moment I firssst sssaw you, I knew you were going to be ssssomething. Ssso many runsss, eh? Feelsss like agessss, but to you it could have just been hourssss. Oh look at me rambling. Don't worry about me ssstranger. There'ssss an endlessss amount of me'sssss, and regardless of what happensss with that Paragon, we'll ssssee each other again." Sylvan winks at you and slithers away.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_QUEEN
text: The Queen lets out a soft pur and nudges you with her head. You aren't sure if she can comprehend the full scope of what's happening, but it's a heartfelt gesture nonetheless.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_OBYN
text: "Your heroics are unlike any other, captain. That fateful day we met, where you promised I would be a hero of the Federation, I did not expect this, and suspect you didn't either! My legend has been told, but it lacks an end. I've come to terms now with the truth. My people are gone. Maybe it's time I join them in the great beyond, if it's even real. If you choose to activate the bomb, well, I'd be content with that ending."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_SYMBIOTE
text: Tintan and Rig hobble over. "We cannot lie, it was hell like this in the beginning. But in this troubling journey we've come to terms with our situation. Forevermore we shall be known as Rintan." Rig's stomach rumbles. "What? Tinrig? That's stupid! God damn it. We're working on it. But our point was this; thank you. We weren't grateful at first, but now we realized you saved us. Though, we must ask one selfish thing. It would be a shame for this revelation to go to waste. Are you sure the Paragon would solve everything?"

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_TONY
text: "Captain, I know we haven't seen eye to eye since we met. You were in the middle of a war to save a damned universe, and you stopped to save a Leech who was actively sacrificing people to save his own skin. Now, I'm not going to pretend that you've made me into some smiles-and-sunshine powered hero, but you've given me a bit of perspective. And all I can see right now is a problem that's way, way bigger than any of us. I know I always wanted to be immortal and rich, but what the hell is the point of being immortal if the whole damn Multiverse knows you as someone who abandoned a chance to save everyone just to keep themselves safe?

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_GUNTPUT
text: "In journey, I have seen both sides of technology. Good, bad. You undoubtedly are good. You fight for justice, even if actions sometimes questionable. Obelisk, purest form of technological corruption. This Paragon, it is fascinatingly grey. Most evilest of weapons, yet also only thing capable of ending technological evils! Glad I am not in your shoes, the decision ahead is incomprehensible in its difficulty. I am just glad I gave you second chance."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_METYUNT
text: "I have so little to say except... thank you. Thank you for giving me a second chance. Before we met I was nothing but a traitor, despised by my people and kept around only for my usefulness. While I may never be able to make it up to those I have betrayed, at least I have been given the chance to redeem myself through this journey."

name: TRUE_VICTORY_CREW_WITHER
text: "You've come so far - I'm impressed! For a mortal you're surprisingly resilient. But I implore you not to forget the mission. The Paragon must be detonated for the Obelisks to truly be defeated. I understand the sacrifice that must be made here, and trust me I don't look forward to it either. But our lives are just a drop in the ocean of those ruined by the Obelisks, Rebels, and even the Federation with the Multiverse tech in their hands."

event.text: The children are gravely silent.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_BOMB
text: The shockwave of the bomb spreads further outwards, first consuming your ship, then the entire Obelisk Homeworlds, erasing every last Obelisk and Vance's entire fleet. Around the Multiverse, billions of MV drives ceased functioning, much to the confusion of everyone. Inevitably, the Federations and Rebellions of many realities were able to work out a truce, knowing the lopsided balances of power would only spell the end for them both. Though your sacrifice will never be known, you've put an end to the unending war, and restored every reality back to the way they were before.

win.text: Your victory will echo through the Multiverse for all time.

name: TRUE_VICTORY_SAVE
text: With the Paragon destroyed, you return to the Obelisk Homeworlds. The MFK Fleet awaits you, but when you show them the wreckage of their Flagship, they stand down. Even afterwards, the tales of your victory are spoken around the Multiverse. It seems your victory has earned you more than just another day to live - you'll forever be immortalized as the single ship that stopped the entire Rebellion. Without the original Vance, the many Rebellions of each reality struggled to gain leadership, and inevitably it spelled doom for the Rebellion. Their society collapsed, and the Federation quickly retook as many realities as they could. Though the conflict will inevitably continue for an eternity, at least things have calmed down at last.

win.text: Your victory will echo through the Multiverse for all time.

tooltip.text: The MFK Flagship is charging its MV drive. If you cannot destroy it before this time, it will escape! Nothing, not even destroying its engines, will stop this timer.

finalBoss.text: This is not the victory you hoped for, but it's one nonetheless.

tooltip.text: The MFK Flagship is charging its MV drive. If you cannot destroy it before this time, it will escape! Nothing, not even destroying its engines, will stop this timer.

finalBoss.text: This is not the victory you hoped for, but it's one nonetheless.

tooltip.text: The MFK Flagship is charging its MV drive. If you cannot destroy it before this time, it will escape! Nothing, not even destroying its engines, will stop this timer.

finalBoss.text: This is not the victory you hoped for, but it's one nonetheless.

tooltip.text: The MFK Flagship is charging its MV drive. If you cannot destroy it before this time, it will escape! Nothing, not even destroying its engines, will stop this timer.

finalBoss.text: This is not the victory you hoped for, but it's one nonetheless.

name: ENCOUNTER_SIREN_UNKNOWN
text: Before you even have time to react, a foreign vessel comes barreling towards you! You've never seen or heard of a ship like this, but you don't have time to question it, get ready to fight!

name: SIREN_UNKNOWN_ESCAPING
text: Whatever these aliens are - looks like they aren't above traditional cowardice. Scans show their FTL drive has been powered up and they're now trying to escape!

name: SIREN_UNKNOWN_GOTAWAY
text: The mysterious alien vessel has escaped into the abyss. You can't linger around for long, but maybe some day you'll see these things again.

name: INFESTATION_RACE
text:
This beacon is under the control of the Brood. However, there doesn't appear to be any hostile ships. Instead, a dome on a nearby planetoid broadcasts a message, which appears to originate specifically from within a tacky-looking obstacle course race-track.

"Step right up, step right up! This race right here, right now is the finest racing event in the whole galaxy! Yessirree, come on down to bet on the fastest giant alien spiders you'll ever see! And if you happen to have a spider of your own that can contend with our fastest specimens, don't be afraid to sign up! But beware, you're not playing in the little leagues!"

choice.text: (G.A.S.) Submit your own Spider as a contestant.

event.text: The host welcomes you excitedly. "Wonderful, wonderful! We have a guest contestant here today! We haven't had a Renegade compete in our event yet. Please note, you may not use any Pheromones, Juice or bodysuits to enhance the speed of your runner."

choice.text: (G.A.S. Morph) Submit your Morph as a contestant.

event.text: The host begins to welcome you, but then looks quizzically at the spider you show them. "I've... never seen a spider like this..." He stops to think for several seconds to look closely at the suspicious Spider Morph.

choice.text: Place a bet on a random spider.

event.text: You place your bet on one of the Spiders.
The Brood make no further attempt to contact you.

name: SPIDER_RACE_MORPH_BEGRUDGING_ALLOW
text: The host sighs and shrugs. "Leave it to a Renegade to surprise you. I guess I can accept this as a contestant. Please note, you may not use any Pheromones, Juice or bodysuits to enhance the speed of your runner."

name: SPIDER_RACE_SPIDER_STARTING
text: Your Spider skitters down to the tracks. The race is about to start. The announcer begins to count down. "3... 2... 1..."

choice.text: (Spider Queen) Cheer on your Spider with a friendly roar.

name: SPIDER_RACE_SPIDER_CHOICE
text: "And tell me, which of your lovely Spiders will you be entering today?"

event.text: "Oh my! Is that the queen of the spiders? How impressive! She looks quite big, though. She might be able to handle the obstacles, but in terms of raw speed, she'll be outclassed by most of her progeny! Let's see what she's got in store."
Your Spider skitters down to the tracks. The race is about to start. The announcer begins to count down. "3... 2... 1..."

"Good heavens! What on earth is this? This spider sends a chill down my spine... just as all spiders should! Only some crazy advanced alternative Brood could have come up with this, we are truly among a friend!"

"Good heavens! What on earth is this? This spider sends a chill down my spine... just as all spiders should! Only some crazy advanced alternative Brood could have come up with this, we are truly among a friend!"

"Counter-intuitive choice, I must say. Weavers are known to be much less swift than other spider species... but their intelligence is surprisingly great. I can't say I'm expecting you'll win, but you could certainly have something up your sleeve."
"Naturally. The common adult spider is the spider of choice for this contest. Very fast, capable of racing. Let's see how good it races."

"Hmm, let me guess. You think that because hatchlings are the fastest, it'll be able to win? Well, you're not the first to try it, but I'll warn you that the obstacles that your spider will have to navigate around are pretty tough for an inexperienced hatchling. But we'll see, even the smallest contestants can pull through."

name: SPIDER_RACE_MORPH_STARTING
text: Your Spider-Morph skitters down to the tracks. The race is about to start. The announcer begins to count down. "3... 2... 1..."

choice.text: (Malform Queen) Cheer on your ally with a friendly roar.

name: SPIDER_RACE_MORPH_CHOICE
text: Which Morph are you entering?

event.text: "Is that a... golden queen? I have no concept for how fast she'll be. I'll be watching with interest."
Your Spider-Morph skitters down to the tracks. The race is about to start. The announcer begins to count down. "3... 2... 1..."
"That looks like a weaver. Ordinarily I'd say it's a bad idea, but I have no clue for this thing. I can't say I'm expecting you'll win, but you could certainly have something up your sleeve."
"It certainly looks like a common adult spider. Very fast, capable of racing. Let's see how good it races."

"Hmm, let me guess. You think that because hatchlings are the fastest, it'll be able to win? Well, you're not the first to try it, but I'll warn you that the obstacles that your spider will have to navigate around are pretty tough for an inexperienced hatchling. But we'll see, even the smallest contestants can pull through."

name: SPIDER_RACE_RESULTS
text: Your spider crew goes down to the racetrack. You and the rest of your crew members sit in anticipation as the countdown begins...

event.text: Your spider skitters across the field so deftly, it's a thing of beauty. It almost seems to ignore the obstacles, weaving through the racetrack as if there's absolutely no challenge whatsoever. All of the other competitors are left in the dust. The audience collectively gasps in awe. As your spider passes the finish line, the audience stands and applauds your spider's stunning display. Your spider looks incredibly proud of itself. The emcee stammers. "H-how? That's a world record! I've never seen a spider go that fast. We have to enter you into the hall of fame!" You collect your winnings, on top of a bonus for setting a record!

Your spider gets a quick head start. Your spider quickly overcomes each obstacle and circles the racetrack with ease. Try as it might, the other competitors trail behind, but aren't able to get close. The crowd goes wild for your spider's deft maneuvering across the field. The emcee declares your spider the victor as it goes over the finish line. "We were dealing with a shark here, folks! This is one quick creepy-crawly!" Your spider chirps happily on the podium. The hosts award you with a sizable pile of scrap.

The race starts with a bang, your own spider managing to keep up with the frontrunners. You watch as your spider bobs and weaves through all the obstacles, keeping a good pace. It's a tense, close race all the way through. Each of your crew members cheer as your spider darts closer and closer to the finish line. Just near the end, your spider gains one final burst of speed necessary to pass the finish line. Your spider won! "And there's your winner! Charlie Brown from outta town takes it! A stunning upset!" You're awarded 100 scrap for your spider's effort.

The race starts with a bang, your own spider managing to keep up with the frontrunners. Having to deal with the speed of the other spiders and navigating the obstacles is difficult. Your spider struggles to keep amidst the frontrunner spiders - but keeps up all the same. As the spiders get near the finish line, your spider goes all out to barely eke out a second place victory. The emcee announces the winner, but you celebrate your spider's silver medal with the rest of the crewmates. As the runner up, you still get a modest reward.

The race starts, and your spider does its best. However, as much as it keeps up, the lack of experience is obvious, and your spider doesn't manage to make its way to the front of the pack. Your spider puts in a valiant effort, but ultimately several spiders manage to make it to the finish line before yours does. It could have gone better, but your crewmates applaud your spider's effort.

The race starts, but your spider seems unprepared. It's quickly apparent that your spider is not a racer, and falls far behind the other spiders. Your spider puts in a half hearted effort to finish the race, but it's obvious even from the start it's going to finish among the last. Your spider returns, seeming sheepish.

The race starts, but... The crowd erupts in laughter as your spider sluggishly drags its way across the field. In a humiliating display, your spider doesn't even manage to finish the race before being dragged off the field. The people aren't going to forget your embarrassing display any time soon.

You place your bet on the spider that charms you the most. You watch as the spiders skitter across the racetrack, circumventing obstacles and going across the field at a blistering pace. You seem to have made a good choice, as your pick manages to retain its spot among the frontrunners. At the last moments, your pick manages to gain a burst of speed to sprint across the finish line, securing a stunning victory!

You place your bet on the spider that charms you the most. The spiders all clump together, making it hard to follow your own choice, but it's clear that none of the frontrunners are yours. The spiders cross the finish line one by one, your own pick placing somewhere in the middle. Looks like you missed out on a payout.

name: INFESTATION_SLAVERS
text: A Tiiikaka vessel is offering slaves to passing ships for incredibly cheap prices. You inquire further, and they explain: "We have come to join the spider selling business, son! There's bank to be made, haha! Alas... we must depart with some of our long-time labourers due to lack of space. For a quality price, how does a new worker sound?"

event.text: "A good choice, my boy! They'll be sure to do you well."
"A good choice, my boy! They'll be sure to do you well."
Last thing the Militia needs to deal with is slavers selling spiders to other ships. You'll take care of these pirates for them!
"Your loss, son!" The slaver hangs up.

name: INFESTATION_ORPHAN
text: This system is empty of ships. Out of boredom, you run some scans on the nearby planet and find that it actually has a long running cave system! Maybe worth a look?

event.text: You plunge deeper into the cave, and not too far in you hear the sounds of a child crying.

You head towards the crying until you come across a Rockman child, being chased by a giant spider! You're about to shoot when you realize the sound you heard aren't crying - it's playful laughter. Several times the Rockman trips, with the spider patiently waiting for them to get back up before continuing to chase them.

You raise your weapon and shoot at the spider, but it barely hurts them! Several weavers come crawling out from the surrounding tunnels, alerted by the gunfire. You're chased back to the ship with the spiders in pursuit!

You holster your gun and cough, signifying your presence. You attempt to speak to the Rockman. "Visitors? We so rarely see those! This is my friend Charlotte, and I am Wilbur! She watches after me ever since my parents' ship crashed here!" You question Wilbur further and learn he has been here ever since he was merely an infant.

choice.text: Offer to take Wilbur with you.

event.text: "You would take me away? I haven't been off this planet in years! Just, let me say goodbye!" The Rockman runs over to the spider and give it a large hug, then runs over to join you. As you leave the cave, you turn back to see the spider watch you leave. If you had known better, you'd even have said it looked sad.

choice.text: Request to see the wreck site.

event.text: "Sure!" Wilbur motions for you to follow and runs through the tunnels. You follow until you enter a large room with a massive ship wreck, covered in eggs, lying dormant. "The ship no longer functions, but feel free to scrap it! I've already removed anything sentimental years ago."

choice.text: Continue on your current path and ignore the sound.

event.text: You continue travelling until you come across bits of an old, tarnished Rock Cruiser webbed up along the walls. You quickly check for spiders, and once you're certain you're alone you gather up as much as you can carry and bring the salvage back to the ship.

choice.text: Nope nope nope, get out of here now.

event.text: Best not to go spelunking in a sector infested with giant alien spiders.

name: INFESTED_WRECKAGE
text: Nearby drifts a small wreck of a civilian vessel.

choice.text: Impossible to perform a salvage without any crew or further scans, the risks are too high.

event.text: The wreckage continues to drift past you, seemingly lifeless.

name: BROOD_CIVILIAN
text: The Brood might mostly target the Militia, but they are still pirates. A civilian vessel is under attack here from a Brood vessel!

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the pirate ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range. After a time the distress calls stop.

name: INFESTATION_CIVILIAN
text: You receive a hail from a Civilian vessel. "Help, we're under attack from a ship full of spiders! Why does this stuff always happen to us?!"

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the infested ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range. After a time the distress calls stop.

name: INFESTATION_SHELL
text: A Shell science vessel is watching an infested vessel sporadically flicker back and forth around the beacon. They hail you shortly after you jump in. "Hello. We are looking for an infant spider to study. We understand thhhe risk, and will pay if you go thhhrough withhh it."

choice.text: Send a team aboard the infested vessel to capture a hatchling.
Yet another scientist that will have to find help somewhere else.
(Teleporter) Beam back a spider without any risk.

event.text: You lock onto the spider and beam them back aboard your ship. Once captured, you hail the Shell vessel...
"Understandable. Not everyone has a taste in science."

name: INFESTATION_MAFIA
text: A violent battle is being held between the Militia and Brood. In the distance is a large, well armed pirate yacht firing away.

choice.text: Board the yacht, it's large enough that you could look around without being noticed.

event.text: You step aboard to find a large variety of races of all shapes and sizes walking about. The interior is lined in a crimson wallpaper and the floor a velvet carpet. It looks like some kind of weird hotel... and a strangely well armed one like that.
As you continue deeper into the yacht you notice two doors. One marked "Night Club", and the other "High Grade Military Explosives [Off Access!!!]"
You step into the night club only to find a spider seductively dancing around a pole on a stage in front of other pirates. You promptly close the door and head over the explosive room instead.
You fly away from the battle.

name: INFESTATION_MAFIA_EXPLOSIVES
text: The walls of the room are lined with explosives, many of which have small skulls printed on them.

event.text: Your crew grab as much ammunition as they can carry, until a Duskbringer in bright red armor bursts into the room, holding a small bomb. "Feds, in my territory? Oh, now you've really made me mad!"
As you run to leave, you're chased down by the Duskbringer and several other Brood members. Even when you undock from the yacht, you're followed by an unusually colored Duskbringer pirate.

choice.text: Leave, we shouldn't be stealing from pirates.

name: INFESTATION_BAKE_SALE
text: You jump when you notice a Brood ship docked at the beacon, but they make no move to attack. Instead, they advertise a small bake sale with some donuts and cider. "For spiders, by spiders, of spiders!" says a pirate with a hatchling pet on their lap.

event.text: "Oh, so generous, we don't get many customers. Hopefully you intend to pay though, dearies. Donuts cost 999 scrap in these parts!"
"Ahuhuhuhu... come back any time..." The Brood ship hangs up.

"Oh, don't be silly.. You aren't going anywhere without paying! Ahuhuhu... I bet you'll make a great ingredient in my next cake!" You notice your engines functioning at lower power, they must be using a combat augment!"
Your engines return to full power, and you turn your attention to the incoming fight.

name: INFESTATION_PURGER
text: All around you are the charred remains of what once were ships. No life signs are detected aboard any of them. In the center of the wreckage is a small civilian station with a heavily modified Auto-guard defending it.

event.text: "Another one of you? Stay away, stay away! We don't want any of you spider freaks! Get any closer and you'll meet your end just like all of these other infested wrecks!" It appears the civilians are delusional.
You can't let these civilians keep murdering other ships. You'll have to take out their Auto-ship to stop them.

choice.text: Heed their warnings and stay away.

event.text: You aren't particularly interested in messing with that Auto-ship. You avoid the station.

name: INFESTATION_PURGER_WIN
text: The Auto-Purger has been dealt with. You scrap the remains of the ship.

event.text: "AAAAH, THE SPIDERS, THEY'RE EVOLVING!" The civilians mute the comms and several large, expensive laser cannons extend from their hull. These guys mean business, and it's probably best to leave them alone now. Fortunately, that leaves you further time to investigate the Auto-ship, where you discover a special Laser weapon!

name: DISTRESS_BROOD_CIVILIAN
text: A Brood vessel is firing upon a civilian ship, the same one that has sent out the distress signal. The civilians won't stand a chance unless you do something.

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the pirate ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range. After a time the distress calls stop.

name: DISTRESS_INFESTATION_CIVILIAN
text: There's two ships at this distress beacon, but only one is still under control by its original owners. An infested vessel is hunting civilians, and it looks like they're almost upon them!

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the infested ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range. After a time the distress calls stop.

name: DISTRESS_INFESTATION_CRASH
text: On the nearby forest planet appears to be the origin of the distress signal.

event.text: You pilot closer to the surface, where you spot a wrecked EDC Militia ship stuck between two trees. Two Militiamen, one with bright orange hair, and the other with a long scar down his face and a pair of round glasses, are bunkered down, rifles drawn, facing towards a hill.

You exit the vehicle and walk towards the Militiamen, who quickly shush you before you can speak. In a slow whisper, the red head says "Be very very quiet, or these spiders will hear us. There's a massive hive here, and we have to get out." The one with glasses shakes his head an disagreement, "No, we heard a supply cache was taken by the spiders. We have to get it back!"
You run back to the ship, careful not to awaken the spiders. Though their friend stays behind, stupidly decided to take back the cache all on his own, the red head offers to stay with you.

choice.text: Agree to go after the cache.

event.text: You hurry towards the hive, followed by the spectacled Militiaman. Stepping further into a cave running through the hill, you find the cache covered in webbing. You haul it over your shoulder back to the ship, but a swarm of spiders now alert to your location follow!
You don't know what's down there, but you can't trust anything in this sector.

name: INFESTATION_PHOTOGRAPHER
text: You assumed most of the civilians had evacuated this sector, but one ship is searching through the wreckage of several large carriers.

event.text: "Ugh, JJ is going to be pissed - Oh, hello. It's very fortunate you've shown up. I'm from the Trumpet, a small newspaper in the Coreworlds. Our lead photographer was sent here to get some pictures of the sector, but he's gone missing. Perhaps you could search him for us? We aren't armed well enough for this sector..."
You leave the civilian ship alone.

name: INFESTATION_PHOTOGRAPHER_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: You were asked to search and rescue a lost photographer.

text: You've arrived at the co-ordinates given by the civilians. A terrestrial planet, though with few signs of civilization, is located within the system limits. This must be the place...

event.text: It doesn't take long to find the photographer. A human so thin his ribcage looks like it's about to escape his chest stands triumphant over a horde of spiders, who crawl around him in submission. He shouts to your ship. "Fear me, for I am the spider man! King of the spiders, and soon to be king of man!"
From the ground rises a beaten but still functional Federation ship, staffed mostly by spiders. The "spider man" jumps aboard the ship, and rises to fight you!

name: INFESTATION_PHOTOGRAPHER_DESTROY
text: The wrecked ship falls back down the ground, crushing several hundred spiders and sending many more flying. With the horde dispersed, you land as well and quickly gather some salvage.

event.text: Unfortunately, this means the photographer is dead. There's no reason to report back to the civilian ship now.

name: INFESTATION_PHOTOGRAPHER_DEADCREW
text: The now crewless vessel falls back down the ground, crushing several hundred spiders and sending many more flying. With the horde dispersed, you land as well and quickly gather some salvage.

event.text: Unfortunately, this means the photographer is dead. There's no reason to report back to the civilian ship now.

name: INFESTATION_PHOTOGRAPHER_SURRENDER
text: As the Federation ship smokes and shutters, you receive a hail from the once-photographer. "Ok, I no longer wish to be king of the spiders!"

event.text: The Federation ship pilots back down to the planet's surface and the human dismounts.

choice.text: Drop him off at the nearest station for the reward.

event.text: You drop off the photographer at the nearest station, where the civilians from earlier are waiting. Grateful, they give you a generous helping of fuel and scrap.

choice.text: Offer him a position on your ship.

event.text: With his previous two occupations as a photographer and "king of the spiders" having been put to an end, he is more than willing to work for you.

choice.text: Ignore him and finish him off.

name: ENCOUNTER_INFESTED_ENGI
text: It's an unusual surprise seeing an Engi ship so deep in such a dangerous sector. You attempt to hail them, but only get back a garbled response followed by hissing. The ship must be infested with spiders!

name: INFESTATION_IRWIN
text: These are the last known co-ordinates of the Renegade hired by the Militia. Some strange facility has been constructed here, and a massive civilian transport ship is in the process of leaving the planet. You spot a distant, strangely shaped vessel parked outside the entrance.

event.text: You pull closer, careful not to be spotted. It seems you failed to spot a second ship, a large Mantis cruiser in Brood colors. You land behind one of the massive solar panels and tune into the conversation between the two ships. It seems Irwin is speaking with an unusually well-dressed Brood member in what seems to be a painted Ace uniform.

"Heheh, hey there Virgo. Look, I know thisss looksss bad but..." Irwin is cut off by the imposing figure.

					"I do not have time for your shit anymore Irwin. Vael is getting tired. Tired of your incompetence, tired of your belligerence, tired of your insane crackpot conspiracies about a puppeteering agency that rules the Multiverse! You had ONE job, to recover the DNA. And what happened? You come slithering back to me with nothing. Now, they're about to blow the whole nest to hell. You expect me to TOLERATE this?"
					
					"Well... yessss? Look, it wasssn't easy convincing the Defenssse Cadre to hire me after the Vek dissssassster ruined the reputation of Renegadessss!" Irwin continues to protest but is cut off once more.

					"It doesn't matter. Too much time has passed. The window of opportunity is slim. Vael has cut a deal with the Brood, they will recover the DNA for us. We have no more use for you, Irwin. You are nothing but a loose end." Virgo draws his laser and aims it right at Irwin.

Seems this Irwin fellow might have information of use. You jump out from your cover and draw your own weapon. Virgo shows no signs of disturbance but merely retracts his weapon and hurries back to the Brood ship, which immediately powers up its weapons! Irwin to no surprise rushes back to his ship, but is stopped by a missile from the pirates, destroying his engines.

You watch as the Slug desperately pleads for his life, but the assassin pays him no attention. He shoots only once and the Clansman falls to the ground in a puddle of his own green blood. Virgo orders the pirates behind him to destroy Irwin's ship before they go. Seems this is your cue to leave as well.

"Heheh, hey there Virgo. Look, I know thisss looksss bad but..." Irwin is cut off by the imposing figure.
					
					"I do not have time for your shit anymore Irwin. Vael is getting tired. Tired of your incompetence, tired of your belligerence, tired of your insane crackpot conspiracies about a puppeteering agency that rules the Multiverse! You had ONE job, to recover the DNA. And what happened? You come slithering back to me with nothing. Now, they've blown that nest to hell and we have no way of recovering the samples! You expect me to TOLERATE this?"
					
					"Well... yessss? Look, it wasssn't easy convincing the Defenssse Cadre to hire me after the Vek dissssassster ruined the reputation of Renegadessss!" Irwin continues to protest but is cut off once more.
					
					"It doesn't matter. Too much time has passed. The window of opportunity is gone. We have no more use for you, Irwin. You are nothing but a loose end." Virgo draws his laser and aims it right at Irwin.

Seems this Irwin fellow might have information of use. You jump out from your cover and draw your own weapon. Virgo shows no signs of disturbance but merely retracts his weapon and hurries back to the Brood ship, which immediately powers up its weapons! Irwin to no surprise rushes back to his ship, but is stopped by a missile from the pirates, destroying his engines.

You watch as the Slug desperately pleads for his life, but the assassin pays him no attention. He shoots only once and the Clansman falls to the ground in a puddle of his own green blood. Virgo orders the pirates behind him to destroy Irwin's ship before they go. Seems this is your cue to leave as well.

name: INFESTATION_IRWIN_WIN
text: The Brood cruiser has been defeated. It falls to the ground in a heap, and you scrap its remains.

event.text: When the Slug sees you approaching he immediately pretends he was never scared at all, but around his strange blunderbuss-like gun his tentacles have gone white. "Glad we Renegadessss know how to ssstick up for each other! Now, what's your rate? I know this kind of ssservice isssn't free. I'm not sssstupid."

choice.text: We aren't looking for pay. But we wouldn't mind information.

event.text: "HAH! What a riot. Let'sss be clear here. Information issss money. Money issss everything, and everything isss money. There ain't no sssane man in thisss Multiverssse who worksss for free. Kindnesss isss jussst a meansss to an end. Favorsss are blank checksss. You're a Renegade, don't play me for a fool. We aren't philanthropisssts, we're mercenariesss. Murdererssss with a price tag. I've been in thisss busssinessss long enough to know that."

choice.text: That's not the point. Tell us about this Virgo fellow.

event.text: "Whatever you sssay. Virgo isss...erm, wasss an Angel. Asssasssin for big daddy Vael of the Ssssyndicate. He wassss my mossst recent client, but the isssue iss Vael doessssn't normally deal with roguesss. Hissss mercsss usssually work for him, and his patience with me wasss ssshort. Virgo wasss his reassssurrence I would follow through."

"Ssstealing sssome kind of DNA. Thessse G.A.S., the Vek, bla bla bla, they're all basssed on the sssame ssstuff. I ain't a biologissst, I dunno what I'm talking about. Point isss, Vael caught wind Sssenator Wright wasss getting cold feet and was gonna blow the top off thisss whole thing. I wasss SSSUPPOSSSED to bring Vael the DNA before the big boom, but I like being alive, you know?"

choice.text: Didn't you use to be a Clansman?

event.text: "Yeahhhh. I WASSS. But I got tricked by that asssshole Billy Hektar into getting wrapped up in hisss little ssslave trade. Wasss going fine until one day I decided to bring along a friend of mine, a ranger named Ssssylvan. I thought he'd want to help, but inssstead he acted all weird. I realized he wasss a risssk, but rather than jusssst dying like I wanted, he blew up my fleet and leaked my involvement in Hektar to the Guild. Thing issss, ssslavery actually breakssss one of the sacred rulessss, and so I wasss kind of booted. Lesssson isss, trussst no one! They'll alwaysss turn on you. Or they could be a sssecret agent ssent by the Multiversssal Order!"

"That being sssaid, I need a ride. My ship isss toassst. Ssssince you're a Renegade, I'm sure you could alwaysss ussse more help. Ssso, let'ss ssstrike a deal! I join your crew, and we sssplit the profitsss half and half. Deal? No!? Alright well, I guessss we can figure out the numbersss later... Oh, and sssseeing asss I won't need my ssship anymore, you do whatever with it."

name: INFESTATION_NEST
text: You've arrived at the Spider Hive. The planet is appropriately spooky for what you're dealing with. In the skies, the Militia and Brood forces fight for control over the planet, but you're able to slip through the chaos and land on the surface near a giant cavern.

event.text: You receive a distant hail from Montgomery, though it cuts in and out. "You made - delivery ship damaged - bombs are lost in cavern - need you - find them and - destroy the nest - Brood inside - careful!"

You plunge into the darkness, guided only by the light from your own ship through empty labyrinths of bedrock. You pass by what appears to be the wreck of a Militia vessel, evidently the one carrying the bombs. You find them, fortunately, undamaged in the cargo and haul them back onto your ship.

choice.text: If we don't detonate these, no one else can.

event.text: You keep on going, ever wary of the fact you could easily meet the same fate here as the first ship if you fail. Eventually the tunnels lead to what is presumably the center of the cavern, a massive near perfectly spherical room with walls lined with holes containing tens of thousands of eggs. There's no way this was the product of nature. This room was designed with intent.

choice.text: Stealthily begin setting up the bombs.

event.text: Your crew rush to wire the bombs without waking up the spiders. From what you remember, these are the same design as the ones used against the Vek on Earth. Just one of those was capable of creating an explosion visible from space and caused massive earthquakes across the planet, so you can only imagine what kind of impact three of them will have. And you sure as hell don't want to stick around to see it.

While wiring the third and final bomb, one of your crew trips and drops a metal plate from the bomb on the ground. At once, it seems as though every spider in the entire cavern lets out a cry. In a matter of seconds a massive roar silences them and a monstrous creature the size of three men erupts from the ground. This must be the queen, and she sure isn't happy. All 8 of her eyes lock onto you, but she doesn't attack. It almost seems as if she's giving you a warning.

It seems like suicide almost, but the last thing you want to risk is angering the spiders. From all you've seen so far, they seem more intelligent than the Militia is willing to admit and maybe, just maybe, you can make it out of here without anyone dying. The queen seems to notice this behavior and backs away from you. Around her several hatchlings cling to her legs, but they scatter when she turns and crawls though a hole in the hatchery walls. It almost seems as if she wants you to follow.

You crawl through the tunnel and find yourself now standing in a massive rectangular room with ships and lab equipment. You wipe away some of the dirt caked onto the walls and find underneath is rusted metal. This was a research center at some point, but judging from the smell, the staff are all dead. You see the queen walk over to a row of tubes on the walls, where you find many exotic creatures, some of which seem eerily similar to the G.A.S., Vek, and other insectoid monstrosities used by the Brood. You glance over at a nearby desk where you find a letter addressed to, of all people, Oscar Wright. Next to it is a dongle containing blueprints for some kind of cruiser model, which you slip into your pocket.

"Dear Senator,
																	There has been a change of plans. Your methods for testing the insectoid DNA have deeply disturbed both me and the council. My team found a new candidate anyways. There will no longer be a need to continue your experiments. I would like to remind you that the only reason you are where you are today is because of your history with the Admiral, and in his absence the new leadership is not as generous. I am writing this only out of the best of intentions for your well being. If you don't want to wake up with a bullet in your head, I advise destroying all evidence at all costs.
																	
																	You know what you have to do, Oscar. Do not fail the Rebellion again.
																	Sincerely, Dr. E.W."

You aren't sure what to make of this, but you don't have much time. Montgomery calls out from behind you, ordering that you drop the letter. "Turn around slowly, captain. Put that paper down and come with me. We need to detonate the bombs and leave."

Montgomery cuts you off before you can finish. "What reason do you think the EDC is here? Did you really think the Brood was behind all of this? That some stupid pirates could just breach the security of the Union's Coreworlds? No, but the Federation has been concerningly ignorant to the Senator's intentions. The Brood is real, yes, but they were nothing before this. We gave them the insectoids to release. We planted the Vek on Earth. It was an awful decision in hindsight, yes, and that's why we're here. The experiment was a failure. We cannot risk exposing the Senator's ties to the Rebellion. I'm afraid you're now a liability. But disposing of liabilities is what I'm best at."

choice.text: Abandon the lab and the spiders and leave.

event.text: You take one last look at the queen and hurry out of the lab. You spot a massive EDC Cruiser which Montgomery boards. In the distance the horde of spiders chase after you, but you're too fast. Both of your ships escape just in time as the bombs fill your ship with a blinding light. Once it finally subsides, Montgomery hails you one last time. "You saw nothing down there, understand?" You nod your head. "Good. You will be rewarded for your assistance, but I hope you understand that it would be a poor decision to speak of what was down there to anyone else."

choice.text: Take no chances, shoot the queen.

event.text: It would be suicide to try anything else here. You blast the queen, but your shot hardly does anything against her hardened exoskeleton. She charges at you as do the rest of her offspring, and they tear one of your crew limb from limb. You have no choice but to retreat back to the ship and hurry out of the cavern. From a distance, you pull the trigger and the bombs detonate at once, creating a blinding flash of light that seems to engulf everything. And then, in an instant, the light subsides and nothing is left but a monumental crater in the face of the earth. The Brood forces, seeing their failure, jump away, and the Militia thanks you. The G.A.S. are no more.

removeCrew.text: Fortunately, your crew is able to be recovered thanks to the Clone Bay, but they'll likely suffer from permanent arachnophobia from now on.

choice.text: You lack a team to setup the detonation sequence.
Leave with the bombs and give them to someone better qualified.

event.text: Now having safely recovered the bombs, you leave the cavern and hail Montgomery. A Militia ship breaks off from the fighting to retrieve the explosives and gives you a reward.

choice.text: This is too risky, we can't do this.

event.text: You can't risk going up against an entire hive of spiders on our own! You pull away from the battle.

name: INFESTATION_NEST_WIN
text: Montgomery in the end was not enough to stop you. Though the rest of the crew aboard his vessel were likely oblivious to his intentions, they were necessary casualties.

event.text: While scrapping the crashed wreckage, you hear the moan of a dying man and find Montgomery, impaled by part of the debris. He turns to you, and with his final breath he mutters, "No evidence. An Ace... never fails." He raises his hand, still holding the detonator, and flips the switch. Instantly, the nearby Renfield bombs activate and the countdown to decimation begins.

choice.text: We have to rescue the queen!

event.text: You run back into the hatchery where you find the queen comforting several wailing hatchlings. The droning sound of the bombs as they count down drowns out your cries but the queen spots you, and somehow understands the severity of the situation. You make your way back to the ship and take off, rushing through the tunnels as the walls shake and the inferno behind you expands. In the end it comes down to almost a matter of seconds as you kick the engines into maximum thrust and take off from the planet.

So many different questions are left running through your head. Why was the Rebellion testing the spiders and the Vek? What is the 'new candidate'? Who is Dr E.W.? You aren't sure if any of these questions will be answered, but you can't linger for too much longer. The queen, while safe, is obviously disturbed by the loss of her children. Had you not saved her, the entire species would have likely gone extinct. All you can do now is be glad another Ace is dead, and carry on with your mission. Maybe some day, whether it's you or another captain, someone will get to the bottom of this. You pull out the dongle from earlier and download the blueprint data onto your ship for later.

name: NEBULA_STARGROVE_STORM_REVISIT
text: You've been here already, and there's nothing left of interest.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_SUN_REVISIT
text: You've been here already, and there's nothing left of interest. The sun here makes it too dangerous to do something onboard the ship, you'll have to leave as soon as possible.

text: You've been here already, and there's nothing left of interest. The sun here makes it too dangerous to do something onboard the ship, you'll have to leave as soon as possible.

text: You've been here already, and there's nothing left of interest. The pulsar here makes it too dangerous to do something onboard the ship, you'll have to leave as soon as possible.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_ASTEROID_REVISIT
text: You've been here already, and there's nothing left of interest. The asteroids here make it too dangerous to do something onboard the ship, you'll have to leave as soon as possible.

name: STARGROVE_GRAVASTAR_REVISIT
text: You've been here already, and there's nothing left of interest. The Gravastar makes it too dangerous to do something onboard the ship, you'll have to leave as soon as possible.

name: FINISH_BEACON_STARGROVE
text: You've arrived at the exit...

name: NEBULA_FINISH_BEACON_STARGROVE
text: You've arrived at the exit...

name: STARGROVE_HIGHWAYMAN_INITIAL
text: A ship guarding the exit beacon warms up their weapons as you approach and sends a message. A cocky-looking pirate appears onscreen. Swords line the back wall of his communication room as he smirks at you. "Ah, somebody wants to leave, huh? I'm afraid you're not doing so for free." The highwayman gestures behind him. "Y'see my weapons? I've got a Pre-Igniter, and you can say goodbye to your precious shields if you dare defy me... And don't even think about cloaking! You have no chance, so just give me your scrap and move along."

choice.text: I don't even have shields, dumbass.
We don't even have 100~. Could we make some other deal?

name: STARGROVE_POST_HIGHWAYMAN
text: Looks like the highwayman's ship is gone now, but a Rebel Auto-ship has taken control of the beacon! You'll have to fight your way out!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_TUCO
text:
Tuco laughs. "Well, Zirc, looks like you survived the aftermath of that heist after all. I see you've been promoted."
	
	"Oh, it's you, 'Captain.' Surprised you actually found a crew willing to put up with you."

	"Which one of us is currently rotting away in Hell? ...Well, I guess we both are, but the difference is, I'm not trapped here."

	The highwayman rolls his eyes. "I take your point."

	"Well, what do you say? Why don't you let us through, as a favor to your old captain?"

	"Oh sure. But only if you pay me back for all those drinks you kept leaving on my tab. I'll just append it to the discount I would have given you."

event.text: The Highwayman looks surprised as you give him what he wants. "Well, Captain, it looks like people do change. Color me impressed. I won't trouble you any further."
"Hah. I knew you would never pay back your debts. I'll take it from your corpse."

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_KAZ
text:
Kazaaakplethkilik clicks and tilts his head. "Where is Malaakepikipilthen? He is accompanying your raid, yes?"
	
	"He's dead. Took on too many Rocks at once." The Highwayman shakes his head. 

	"Kazaaakplethkilik always knew he'd go out that way. A careless pirate is a dead pirate." Kazaaakplethkilik flexes a scythe menacingly. "Don't you go making the same mistake he did."

	The Highwayman pauses. "...You know, Kaz, I've always respected you. If you're going to leave without paying, I won't stop you."

event.text: "Bloodthirsty as ever, are we? I'll make you regret that."

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_A55
text:
"Yo ho ho. 'Twere a beautiful act o' piracy ye committed. My hat is off to ye."

	"So you heard. Yes, with such a nice ship, how was I supposed to avoid swiping it?"

	"Yar har har. I be getting it perfectly fine. What say ye give us free passage?"

	"Gotta make a living, you understand. I'll give you my extra low friends discount. What say you?"

event.text: "Much obliged, Captain A55. Have fun committing piracy."

choice.text: We don't even have 20~. Could we make some other deal?

event.text: Zirc stares at A55 and mutters. "Ah, whatever. Sounds like you're not even worth robbing. You can go."
"Then we'll find out who the better pirate is. Fine by me!"

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_NIGHTS
text:
Nights starts laughing. "It'ssss what'ssss hissss name! Cowering in the oven, hoping to not be found. Hahahaha!"

	"Nights..." The Highwayman glares. "There's no way I'll miss the chance to crush you into a fine paste."

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_FIGHT
text: You have no intention of letting some two-bit pirate take your hard-earned salvage. You warm up your weapons system.

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_NOSHIELDS
text: The highwayman looks befuddled. "You... you made it all the way through the Stargrove without shields...? What's wrong with you? How did you even...?" The highwayman clears his throat. "You know what? Forget the fee. Just go. I'm actually kinda scared of you."

event.text: "What? But I was letting you go! Ah, whatever! You'll regret your arrogance, Renegade!"

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_PAY
text: The pirate gleefully collects his toll from you. "Move along, Renegade. We have upgrades to perform."

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_RENEGOTIATION_FAILED
text: "So be it! You'll die here and now."

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_THREATEN
text:
You inform the pirate that your ship is fortified against ion attacks, which counters their strategy. This will not be as easy as they think.
	
	"Bah. You are well protected, it's true. You have my respect. In that case, I'll offer you my friends-only discount. Or would you prefer to do this the hard way?"

event.text: The pirate collects his toll from you, with a slight frown. "Move along, Renegade. We have upgrades to perform."

choice.text: We don't even have 60~. Could we make some other deal?

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_TRACKING
text: The highwayman fires his tracking flares, disabling your cloaking system for 20 seconds.

tooltip.text: You've been affected by tracking flares!

name: STARGROVE_EXIT_RENEGOTIATE
text: "How unfortunate! Lucky for you, I am a reasonable pirate. I will accept the following instead of scrap: 10 of every resource or two of your crew"

event.text: You send two of your crew members over to the pirates, condemning them to a life within the Stargrove. Perhaps it will be a mercifully short one.

removeCrew.text: Your crew are not dead, though it's tough to say how long they'll be alive.
Your crew are not dead, though it's tough say how long they'll be alive.

choice.text: You do not have two crew members to offer.

event.text: The pirate collects his toll from you, with a slight frown. "Move along, Renegade."

name: ENEMY_AUGMENT_EXPIRES
text: Your systems finally manage to overcome the enemy's assault! It will be a fair fight from here!

name: ENEMY_AUGMENT_EXPIRES_REACTOR
text: Your systems finally manage to overcome the enemy's assault! It will be a fair fight from here!

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_ITEMS_TWIN_PULSARS
text: Your ship arrives near a pair of twin pulsars. Stuck at a Lagrange point in between these two stellar objects is the wreckage of an ancient, ruptured Crystal battleship. The pulses of the two pulsars crash against each other, which may prove particularly hazardous to the integrity of your ship.

choice.text: (Upgraded Piloting) Have your ship navigate through the destructive interference.

event.text: As it turns out, your ship is capable of avoiding the majority of the danger by following the patterns of the waves closely. It's tricky to harvest the ship while you're moving along with the destructive interference, but you're able to salvage substantial scrap, as well as an elite Crystal weapon!

choice.text: (Ion Resist) Rely on your ion protection to carry you through.

event.text: It's a bumpy ride, but your ship's defenses against ion damage manage to endure the brunt of the hazardous approach. You're able to salvage substantial scrap, as well as an elite Crystal weapon!

Your ship is buffeted from wave after wave of ionic interference, fluctuating wildly in intensity. The combined forces seem to reverberate through your hull, causing severe damage. Fortunately, the wreckage bears substantial scrap, as well as an elite Crystal weapon!

choice.text: Avoid the twin pulsars as much as possible.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_ITEMS_SUN_JUNK
text: A massive debris field closely orbits a nearby star. It contains both natural rock formations and refined metal, suggesting that a structure may have collided with a large asteroid. A gas giant orbits the same star farther away.

choice.text: (Defense Drone) Let your defense drone protect you as you harvest the wreckage [-1|].

event.text: You approach carefully, letting your defense drone pick off any asteroids that get close to you. While there are no identifying markings on the wreckage, the metals within the field seem to be of human origin. Determining anything else about the faction is impossible, but the scrap is yours for the taking.

choice.text: (Rock Plating) Let your armor protect you as you harvest the wreckage.

event.text:
As you draw closer to the wreck, the debris pelts your ship.
				You rely on your armor to protect you. While there are no identifying markings on the wreckage, the metals within the field seem to be of human origin. Determining anything else about the faction is impossible, but the scrap is yours for the taking.

You brave the dangers of the sun and debris field. Doing so leaves you open to bombardment from both sources. While there are no identifying markings on the wreckage, the metals within the field resemble that of human design. Determining anything else about the faction is impossible, but the scrap is yours for the taking.

choice.text: Avoid the asteroid field. Seek shelter behind the gas giant.

event.text: The gas giant gives you enough protection to do something aboard your ship.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_PULSAR_RUIN

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of a ruin.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: In low orbit of the pulsar here, there appear to be a series of large cubical structures surrounded by a thick asteroid field. You may be able to salvage the structures, but the pulsar will make you extremely vulnerable.

event.name: STARGROVE_RUINS_ASTEROID_ENTER
event.text: As you approach, you notice a small ship amongst the ruins. Its power emissions are minimal, but it's clearly still active.
As you near the structure, the ship flares to life and begins charging weapons! You'll have to deal with it before you can explore further.

Attempting to navigate an asteroid field in orbit of a pulsar is dangerous enough, and you're certain that provoking another ship on top of it will end badly. Hopefully you'll be able to jump before the hazards can wreak too much havoc.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_FREE_SCRAP
text: As you arrive, you spot nothing but stars as far as the eye can see. You are able to track down a destroyed Auto-ship, which carries nothing except the charred remains of its weight in scrap and missiles. However, it is surrounded by live munitions which may go off if you get too close.

event.text: The munitions don't pose a threat as you use your arm to grab the wreckage.
The munitions don't pose a threat as you use your arm to grab the wreckage.
