You're unable to avoid the explosives as you arrive to harvest the ship. Given the behavior of the munitions, it may have been a rebel trap. Even so, there is enough scrap to harvest.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_THEOCRACY_RECOVERY
text: Deep within the nebula, a Theocracy vessel is combing through the clouds, as if searching for something. They do not react to your arrival. They must be preoccupied with their mission.

event.text: An annoyed Rockman returns your hail. "We do not have time for your treachery, Federation. We must find our lost comrades before their ship is destroyed."

choice.text: You have no sensors with which to help them.
(Normal Sensors) Offer to use your sensors to help their search.

event.text: Your sensors are completely useless in this situation. Your ineffectual approach only serves to insult the Rockmen. They turn to fight!

choice.text: (Upgraded Sensors) Offer to use your sensors to help their search.

event.text: Your sensors are able to cut the amount of work down. It takes a moderate amount of time, but you eventually lead the Rockmen to their lost crew. "Renegade, you were not... unhelpful. We are willing to share with you our reserves." They send you your reward.

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Offer to use your sensors to help their search.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Offer to use your scanner to help their search.
Respond to their suspicion with violence.

event.text: The Rocks retaliate in kind. "So be it. If they die, then that is more deaths at the behest of your Federation!"
The Rocks do not hesitate to defend themselves. "Foolish Federation! Here, we have the advantage!"

choice.text: Avoid the rock ship and focus on surviving.

name: STARGROVE_THEOCRACY_HELP
text: Your ship is able to track the lost ship down in mere seconds. The Rocks look astonished. "We were quick to judge. They are safe now because of you. Take this, and go in peace, Renegade."

name: STARGROVE_THEOCRACY_SCAVENGE
text: After a short search, you're able to find the lost and disabled Rock ship. They're barely alive and unwilling to talk. Fortunately, their ship is utterly defenseless to yours, allowing you to make off with whatever remains of their scrap.

name: NEBULA_STARGROVE_LOSTREBEL
text: Only a proximity alert stops you from crashing into a Rebel vessel at this beacon; the moment you spot them, they silently begin charging their FTL drive.

event.text: "Oh, damn it. Look, we surrender. I signed on for a few years of fighting the Federation, and now we're over a decade into fighting every species that can hold a stick, in every universe we can find. We don't have to fight out here - what if we both pretend we never saw each other?"
The Rebel ship delivers their surrender, and silently drifts off into the storm.

"Because our superiors have no interest in looking for one missing ship in the middle of nowhere. This place might be hell, but at least it doesn't hate us personally, and I never have to see another Rebel in my life."

choice.text: Warn them about the coming fleet.

event.text: As you explain your situation, the little joy to be found in the deserter's face fades. "Damn it, I should have known nowhere would be safe eventually. Here, a little thanks - hopefully with a lighter load, we can outrun them."

"Leaving so soon? Shame, not a lot of new people to talk to in these parts. Here - a little fuel to help you along. We'll be staying here a good long while, so feel free to stop by, once this whole war is finished."
Out here, whether or not they've deserted doesn't matter. The scrap from their ship is a valuable commodity, and you're taking it.
These Rebels signed on to fight the Federation, and they're about to get what they asked for. Their captain hangs up the call when he sees you charging weapons, and responds in kind.
You begin charging weapons, and the Rebel responds in kind. Hopefully you can finish this quickly - their engines are still charging!
There are no further incidents as the Rebel vessel finishes its jump prep and vanishes. Now's your turn to leave.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_CRUSADER_MADROCK
text: You arrive at a largely abandoned beacon, with only a large star and a powerful Inquisition ship nearby. They seem too occupied with something to care about your arrival.

event.text:
The Crusaders respond to your hail. "We were sent here on the orders of Stonewall himself to apprehend the traitorous criminal, who nowadays goes by the alias "The Madrock". He was once as honorable and noble as any follower of the Elders, but one day he betrayed us and our sacred teachings, before leaving to reside in this wasteland. Though our allies in the Ministry typically advise us to stay away from here, owing to the severity of Madrock's misdoings, they have permitted us to search for him and offered assistance in this task. Now, leave us be, unless you can help us find him."
			
			Shortly after they cut comms, you receive a hail from a tiny shuttle in the distance, dangerously close to the star. "You there. I get the feeling you're not on the best terms with the Theocracy. A Federation Renegade, if I had to take a wild guess. The Theocracy wants me dead, and they've gone to drastic ends to take me out. But if you can take out those guys, I should be able to make it worth your while. Agreed?"

You're not exactly sure if you want to be taking orders from a supposed Rock criminal, but they are absolutely right about one thing: the Rock Elders are no friends of the Federation. You prepare to fight the Crusaders off, and they respond to your aggression by returning fire.

choice.text: Tell the Crusaders about the message you got.

event.text: You spare no details in your explanation, as you tell the Inquisition ship about the message you got, where it came from, and even what the sender wanted you to do. They thank you and offer you a part of the bounty they received, before setting off to capture the now helpless Madrock.
Individually, solar flares and Crusaders are both dangers you'd rather avoid. Tackling both of them at the same time is just asking for trouble. You make sure to set off again as soon as possible.

name: CRUSADER_MADROCK_RECRUIT
text: Though you initially expected Madrock to be a dangerous Outcast or Commando, at least going off of the description of him given by the Crusaders, you are surprised to find that he's a Crusader. Or at least he once was one. "Phew, thanks for the help there. I'd normally have stuck to a safer spot, but after I learned the Theocracy was hunting me down even here, I knew I wasn't going to avoid them without taking a few risks."

choice.text: So what were they hunting you down for?

event.text: "Hah! I've wanted to tell this to somebody else for ages. So not too long ago, Stonewall himself was inspecting me and a bunch of other Crusaders who weren't on active duty. Just when he reached me and was prepared to hand out some discipline, I kicked him down under, right where it hurts! Ahahaha, you should've seen the look in his eyes! Well, I wasn't able to stick around long enough to appreciate it, but it was all worth it for that. Anyways, since you saved me, and since you also look like somebody who wants to kick Stonewall and his pretentious lot down a peg or two, I think I'll stick with your crew for a good while longer."

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_LOSTSUN
text: You're greeted with the sight of a lone Lost Sun ship basking in the glow of the sun. The captain cackles with delight. "Hahaha! This place is wonderous! You can hardly swing a stick around here without hitting a massive celestial ball of fire!" He looks right at the screen and gestures towards you. "Renegade, in the past you may have been challenged by my people to survive near a star. Here, we can truly put your bravery to the test. What say you?"

event.text:
Ariadne brings her hand down on a nearby bulkhead. "How exactly are you furthering our cause gallavanting around in the wastelands?! You have 10 seconds to justify your mission before I strip you of your rank."

"A-admiral? We were simply trying to keep an eye on the Theocracy's activity in this sector! We'll send you a status report on their movements immediately. But while we were here, we've also been investigating those crazed Zoltan Monks. They have weapons technology beyond anything we've seen. You must get your hands on it, if you can!"

The Lost Suns assauge their Admiral's suspicions with a report, some scrap, a few repairs, and a weapon.

Your Commando informs the Lost Sun vessel about your mission and requests aid. "Ah, I can understand how a comrade of ours would make their way here aboard a Renegade ship. May your fires burn the Rebellion and the Theocracy to cinders!"
Your violent ally cracks whatever passes for knuckles in rock biology. "Take heed, Renegade! We will not go lightly. Do what you can to survive until we are satisfied with your strength!"

tooltip.text: Survive until the Lost Sun are satisfied, but don't destroy them!

event.text: No need to trifle with a challenge. You activate weapons and prepare to fire. "To the death, then. You've made a mistake, Renegade!"
"So you would brave the fires of the Stargrove, but back down from a challenge...? I take it you tested your mettle and found your limits. Go crawl back to the veil of safety."

name: STARGROVE_LOSTSUN_VICTORY
text: "We are satisfied with your endurance, Renegade. To brave the azure flames with a stoic expression, even as your body is wracked with debilitating pain - you have our respect."

event.text: Your Outcast says that they have been captivated by the stars in this sector, and wishes to join the Lost Suns. The captain laughs. "A convert wishes to join our ranks? You have performed admirably, how can we possibly turn you down?"

name: STARGROVE_LOSTSUN_ESCAPE
text: Once the Lost Suns deliver your reward, they depart. Clearly, they don't intend to be destroyed by the star.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_ENGI_SEPARATIST
text: A Separatist circles a massive structure that seems to be collecting resources from the pulsar in this sector. They send you a message. "Renegade, hear [my] -bargain- request. We [need] drones to search for ~}||}|~ data. Our fuel collection -facility- is [highly] efficient. Trade?"

choice.text: Our communications must have glitched. What kind of data were you looking for?

event.text: "??? Translation data -insufficient-. Closest [analog]: Pre-origin? We are sorry. This is all we can say."
The Separatist disconnects and does not bother you further.
The Separatist disconnects and does not bother you further.

name: STARGROVE_SEPARATIST_COLLECTOR_ATTACK
text: The Separatist immediately disengages communication and moves to protect the resource collector.

name: STARGROVE_SEPARATIST_FUEL
text: "This ratio is a -steal-. Our collection [processes] are that efficient!"

event.text: "Adequate trade. Be on -your- way."
"Appreciated. Be on -your- way."
"Very agreeable. Be on -your- way."

name: STARGROVE_SEPARATIST_THREATEN_EXPLOSION
text: As soon as you accept the fuel onto your ship, it explodes in a massive fireball! The Separatist move to engage.

name: STARGROVE_FUEL_COLLECTOR_SALVAGE
text: The Separatist structure is quite strong. It doesn't look like it will be easy to salvage this while your ship is being bombarded by the pulsar.

event.text: You are able to process the materials in the collector to obtain a modest yield.
The yield is surprisingly unimpressive.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_ASTEROID
text: A nearby pulsar has a ring of asteroids. One of the them is rich in heavy-metal content, the light of the pulsar reflecting off it enticingly. However, this is also the densest section of the ring. It may be dangerous, and maneuverability would be low.

event.text: You find an area on the asteroid and begin to mine it. However, after you land and start to extract its resources, your ship's alarms go off - another asteroid suddenly changed course and threatens to smash into your ship!

The incoming asteroid poses little danger to your ship because of its armor plating. You maneuver to crash through in the safest way possible. It looks as though it was equipped with a magnetic device that attracted it to your position; it was a trap. Without any further danger, you continue to harvest.

name: STARGROVE_ASTEROID_DESTROYED
text: You reduce the asteroid to debris small enough that it poses no further threat to your ship. It looks as though it was equipped with a magnetic device that attracted it to your position; it was a trap. Without any further danger, you continue to harvest.

name: STARGROVE_ASTEROID_COLLIDE
text: You're unable to avoid the asteroid within the dense debris field. It careens into your ship causing massive damage. It looks as though it was equipped with a magnetic device that attracted it to your position; it was a trap. You're still able to scrounge a few more materials before departing.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_LANIUS_GHOST_STUCK
text: Indeterminate wreckage is a common sight in the Stargrove. A badly wrecked, barely functional ship that has smashed into a small Lanius ship broadcasts a basic distress call amidst a large field of debris. Entering the debris may be risky.

event.text: As you get closer, you detect multiple transporter signals as they are blocked by your Energy Shield, as well as Lanius and Ghost lifesigns within the wrecks.
"Thank. Needed metal to live. Was attacked immediately. Unfriendly Phantoms. Recommend avoiding." Taking heed of the Welder's words, you opt to scrap the ships and move on.

choice.text: With no teleporter, you cannot save any of the aliens.

event.text: Whoever is on board those ships are trying to board without permission. You decide not to entertain them and resort to scrapping their ships while they are alive.
You decide to abandon the ships. The debris field is enough trouble without trying to get involved with suspicious teleporter signals.
You ignore the debris and focus on making it to the next beacon.

name: STARGROVE_LANIUS_GHOST_TELEPORT
text: The inhabitants of the ships are able to materialize onto your ship! One Lanius Welder and several Ghosts appear. It's clear there is a tense stand-off between the two of them, which will escalate into hostilities.

event.text: You stand with the Lanius. The moment you point your weapons at the Ghosts, a fight breaks out!
You aim your weapons at the Lanius. The moment that you do, it goes berserk. A fight breaks out! The Ghosts head for cover rather than help you.

name: STARGROVE_LANIUS_GHOST_LANIUS_WIN
text: "Thank. Needed metal to live. Ghosts attacked immediately. Will help." With everyone from the wreck dealt with, you scrap the ships and prepare to jump.

name: STARGROVE_LANIUS_GHOST_GHOST_WIN
text: "Relief at last! That voracious metal fiend troubles us no more!" The Ghosts offer you a weapon in exchange for passage out of the area. Before you leave, you are able to scrap the ships.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_OBELISK_RUIN_CRYSTAL
text: The massive blue star sends your sensors haywire. There is a strange, cubical green structure orbiting the star. You receive a Crystal distress signal from within. "Whoever you are, please get us out of here! We came here to study our ancient history. We hid here to remain protected from that star, but now we're trapped within this horrid structure!"

choice.text: (Anointed) Interface with the structure to instruct it to open.

event.text: "Have run into this before. You send exit command, like this!" The Anointed quickly taps some commands on your console and sends it to the structure. The structure's door begins to open...

Your translator is able to request a list of commands that the structure will respond to. One of the commands will let you open the structure and set the crystals free. The structure's door begins to open...

choice.text: (Obelisk Crew) Translate the words on the ruins.

event.text: The Obelisk is easily able to send a command to the structure. The structure's door begins to open...

choice.text: (Cognitive Crew) Command the structure to open.

event.text: Telling the structure to open is trivial for the Cognitive. It sends the remote command without hesitation. The structure's door begins to open...

choice.text: (Adv. Hacking) Force the structure to open.

event.text: Your hacking system quickly decrypts the possible commands and spoofs a request that makes the structure open.
Your hacking system can brute force the door opening routine, but it will take some time. You'll have to survive while it works!

tooltip.text: Your hacking will take some time!

choice.text: (Hack Weapon) Attempt to open the structure.

event.text: Your hacking weapon can brute force the door opening routine, but it will take some time. You'll have to survive while it works!

tooltip.text: Your hacking will take some time!

choice.text: (Powerful Beam) Attempt to cut a hole in the structure.

event.text: You're able to pierce through the tough metal, but it will take a few seconds to finish slicing the structure open.

tooltip.text: Cutting through the ship will take some time!

choice.text: (Damaging Beam Weapon) Attempt to cut a hole in the structure.

event.text: Your weapon is capable of burning through the metal, but its arduous work, given how tough the structure's metal is. You're going to be here for a while!

tooltip.text: Cutting through the ship will take some time!

choice.text: (Teleporter) Offer to beam the Crystals out.

event.text: "Oh no... we'll have to leave so much stuff behind! Well, it's better than dying, I guess." The Crystals accept being transported onto your ship, but don't seem happy about it. "Would you be willing to buy some of the stuff we managed to take with us? That's all we can offer, I'm afraid."
"We'll go mad if you leave us here! You have to save us!" You mute communications and prepare to jump.

name: STARGROVE_RUINS_OPEN
text: The Crystal ship immediately emerges from within the structure. The Crystals seem relieved at their rescue. "We were going to go crazy in there. By the way, we found a highly unusual piece of technology in that structure - we'll let you have it. Meanwhile, would you like to purchase something from us?"

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_ENGI_DEFENDER
text: A Defender ship seems to be glitching out. "Connection issue! Errors found. Severance imminent." Judging by the trail of debris, this ship may have been in orbit for quite some time.

choice.text: (Turzil) Attempt to liberate this ship from the Harmony.

event.text: "TRZ-1L? TRZ-1L? -TRZ-1L-?" It looks like it's starting to work, but you may have to soften them up first.

choice.text: (Separatist) Attempt to liberate this ship from the Harmony.

event.text: "Priority target? Priority target? -Priority target-?" It looks like it's starting to work, but you may have to soften them up first.

choice.text: Attack them while their communications are down.

event.text: "Renegade = aggressor! Error, contact failing" They attack you, their combat strength still seems to be at full potential!

Your Engi interfaces with the Defender ship. They explain that the it must have been worn down by the harsh conditions of the sector, and the nanomachines have gone haywire. However, your own Engi is able to update the ship with its own nano-patterns. 
				
			As the ship begins to right itself, you receive a message. "Defender == grateful. Stargrove mission parameters have been lost. Recovering... Historical information acquisition? Unsure. Returning to Harmony."
		
			The ship also graces you with a reward.

choice.text: Escape from the Pulsar and leave the Engi behind.

event.text: You decide to focus on leaving behind the pulsar. The Engi ship continues to glitch out, seemingly unable to escape its orbit.

name: SURRENDER_ENGI_PULSAR_OVERRIDE
text: The ship is weakened. The Engi crew are confused and frantic. They seem to be surrendering.

event.text:
The Engi onboard calm down. "Memories of Harmony not found. Directives corrupted. TRZ-1L, please clarify what has happened."

			"Call me Turzil. You are no -longer- connected to the Harmony. The faulty -connection- that the pulsar caused was interfering with [your] processing, soft-locking your mobility."

			"Harmony directives = corrupted. Memories == hazy. "

			"You [may] live as you please. We -reccomend- you leave this sector."

			"Understood. Will think things through."

			The Engi ship is now able to leave the orbit of the pulsar. Before they leave, they give a reward for their freedom, and one of the Engi offers to join.

The Engi onboard calm down. "Memories of Harmony not found. Directives corrupted. Renegade, please clarify what has happened."

			Your Separatist explains to them that they are free to self determinate, and recommends a nearby Separatist sector. The newly liberated Engi thank you for your part in rescuing them from the pulsar.

choice.text: Accept their surrender and leave them to their fate.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_FEDTRACKER
text: Federation probes are a rare sight, intended for use in maintenance and long-term exploration operations where resupply isn't an option. It transmits a coded signal shortly after your arrival, and after a few minutes of deciphering, you have it translated: "IFF signature recognized. (1) message available with current clearance. Transmit current Earth year to accept."

event.text: You send your reply, and shortly recieve another coded message. "Primary mission objective: shadow a Coalition vessel detected on a course for the Stargrove. Original plan: mark vessel location and return to base for assistance. Insufficient fuel remaining, defaulting to plan B: wait for any Federation vessel, then transmit location data. This ship is authorized to offer sector maps and repairs upon mission completion."
"Reply signal verified - transmitting last known location of Coalition vessel."
Whatever the message is, it can't be as important as your mission. You tune out the signal and prepare to make your exit.
If this probe can't make it home, you'll just have to make use of it yourself. You begin charging weapons, and the its engines roar to life. You'll have to try and destroy it fast!

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_QUEST_STARGROVE_TRACKER

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Federation auto-probe has tracked a Coalition vessel to this beacon.

text: The intensity of the sunlight bouncing off of the Coalition ship you were tracking blinds you when you first arrive. When you at last manage to force your eyes open, you realize they've already turned to face you - if you were hoping for the element of surprise here, you've clearly lost it.

event.text: "Ah, the Fedsss sssent a Renegade to meet ussss. Doessss that mean you already learned about our planssss from another universssse, or did you jussst get lucky again? Bleh, it doessssn't matter. Every chance we get to make new alliessss, you Fedsss wind up beating ussss to the punch. That changesss here. The Infernum WILL join the Coalition. And if they don't want to, that'sss fine, we mosssstly want them for sssuicide bombersss anyway. Now, will you leave ussss to our missssion, or do we have to throw your broken wreck of a sssship into the nearesssst gravity well?"
The Coalition doesn't need any more allies, and it certainly doesn't need an army of disposable soldiers. You give the order to charge weapons, and prepare to fight.
By the time there's any consequences to this, you'll probably have already left this universe. Surviving to destroy the Flagship is far more important than a hypothetical future enemy to worry about.

name: COALITION_QUEST_STARGROVE_DESTROYED
text: You move to look for any respite from the star, and manage to find a small safe spot before the probe returns. When it does arrive, it silently transmits its sector data and repairs your ship, then begins moving directly towards the nearest sun. You'd heard rumors that auto-probes had directives to do anything to avoid capture, but never had the opportunity to see the behavior in action - you make a mental note to brag about this once you've completed your mission, then prepare to jump.

name: DEFEAT_FED_ELITE_STARGROVE
text: The rogue Federation stealth ship that attacked you has been eliminated. It's not clear what brought them here or what their story was, but it's unlikely that anyone else will ever hear what either of you did here.

event.text: It seems the cargo of the Elite Federation ship survived the fight. Inside is a functional weapon, which you bring back on board.

choice.text: (Anti-Virus) Counter their attempt to jam your systems.
(Anti-Virus) Counter their attempt to jam your systems.
(Anti-Virus) Counter their attempt to jam your systems.

name: STARGROVE_ANTI_VIRUS_PIRATE
text: You successfully purge their harmful interference from your systems. It's a fair fight from here!

event.text: Your reactor starts to sputter out. Looks like they managed to significantly weaken your power output!

tooltip.text: You've been affected by an EMP!

event.text: Your piloting system goes haywire! Evading will be hard, if not impossible like this!

tooltip.text: You've been affected by a piloting hacker!

event.text: Your engines are glitching out! You might find it difficult to escape with this level of interference.

tooltip.text: You've been affected by an engine jammer!

event.text: Your shields are glitching out! You're going to have a harder time enduring their attacks.

tooltip.text: You've been affected by shield jamming!
You've been affected by a weapon jammer!

event.text: Some of your weapons aren't working right. This fight may prove a challenge!

tooltip.text: You've been affected by tracking flares!

event.text: Your cloaking device isn't responding properly. You might have to take a few hits.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_LISTENING_POST_QUEST
text: Orbiting the pulsar, a damaged Federation station desperately calls for help. Its communication array is particularly sophisticated - it seems to utilize the waves of the pulsar itself as a sector-wide radar. A Duskbringer vessel is holding its position near the station until you arrive. "Stay out of this, Renegade. Our pilgrimage is almost complete. The promised land beckons... So do not interfere!"

event.text: "So be it!" The Duskbringer attacker proclaims. "You will be our final trial by combat before we achieve true enlightenment!"

choice.text: (Duskbringer Crew) "You're not the only ones who seek the promised lands."

event.text:
Your Duskbringer explains that you are already seeking to enter the promised lands, and that if they leave the station alone, that you will take them to where they want to go. 

"We've been interrogating these fools for information for days now. If you can get us what we need, we will spare them."
You exercise caution. Unfortunately, you cannot get close enough to gain enough protection from the pulsar that would allow you to do something aboard the ship.

name: STARGROVE_LISTENING_POST_SAVED
text: "Are they finally gone?" A tired and injured crew-member of the listening post says. "The damage we sustained hampered our ability to broadcast over a long range. We had to use a standard distress frequency... thank goodness you happened to be passing through. Our duty is to keep track of all sanctioned Federation activity within the sector so that an organized search and rescue can be performed. One of the astrophysicists within this sector, Mafan has been cornered by some crazed Zoltan monks while researching the Gravastar."

event.text: "The Gravastar is the focal point of this sector's strange properties. It's been traveling through this nebula for eons, condensing the gasses into stars and leaving massive destruction in its wake. The potential advances we could gain through studying it are extraordinary. If you're willing to brave the dangers of this landmark to rescue that scientist, we'll send you the coordinates."
"As you wish. Be careful. From the sound of Mafan's predicament, their attackers seem particularly dangerous and unusual."
"We understand. We'll work on fixing our communication array, but please let someone know as soon as you can regardless. We have no way of knowing how long Mafan can hold out."

name: QUEST_STARGROVE_GRAVASTAR

unvisitedTooltip.text: A scientist has been cornered by some unusual Zoltan Monks.

text: Your ship's readout warns that you have come in close proximity to an incredibly massive object - the Gravastar. The nebula gasses have coalesced into an accretion disk, which may give sensors enough breathing room to function properly. The speed at which the gasses are travelling creates periodic waves of heat. At the same time, your ship's hull begins to buckle under the intense gravity. Spacetime itself warps around you, causing the color spectrum to shift to and fro. Before you even get close to the science vessel you're supposed to save, another ship intercepts you. An orange Zoltan broadcasts a message. "Another foe? How enjoyable. Perhaps this one will engage in bloodthirsty combat instead of cowering in a deep orbit. Well, interloper? Are you prepared to burn?"

event.text: "Far be it from me to hide our glorious name from one who is about to die by our hands." The strange monk opens his arms wide. "We are the Infernum. We have attained a level of evolution the likes of which the stagnant Ministry could never even dream!" He laughs joyously. "With each peril, our glory shines brighter. But, the one below wishes to cast open the gates to our wonderful slice of damnation, to invite the unworthy into our domain. Unacceptable! And now that you know, you must die as well!"
"How agreeable you are!" The monk cackles. "Come, let us fight with everything we have!"
"We do not. Allow us to demonstrate." The monk ship immediately attacks!

name: QUEST_STARGROVE_GRAVASTAR_MONK_MESSAGE
text:
You recount the Monk's parable. 
		
		"Did you really think your insipid tale would move our hearts? We have abandoned the false wisdom of nonviolence - as your ship burns, the folly of your beliefs shall be self-evident!"

		However, despite this, one of the crew seems to have taken your words to heart and takes a fighting posture against the others! The transmission cuts and they charge weapons.

name: STARGROVE_CONTACT_MAFAN_REAL
text: You send a message to the science vessel. All you get back is an undecipherable message: "#::..::/" After a slight adjustment, the signal clears up. "Testing?? Ah, got it working again. Hello, welcome to the Stargrove's mighty Gravastar! Few ever get to see a splendid celestial body like this one up close, hm? Oops, I am getting ahead of myself, as usual. I may need your help to escape my current predicament. The only way I could escape the wrath of those megalomaniacs was to occupy this particular point within the gravity well. But as a consequence... this ship is in no shape to move. Any thoughts?"

choice.text: Risk your ship by flying close enough to scrap the ship and save its sole crew.

event.text: Your ship's weak engines fight the extreme gravitation. Your ship falters quite significantly as you dive into the star. Time scales more and more, and your ship starts to buckle under the strain of extreme gravity. As a consolation prize, not only do you save Mafan, but you have the opportunity to scrap the ship before you return from within the gravity well. Unfortunately, the time dilation has allowed the fleet to advance considerably.

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Risk your ship by flying close enough to scrap the ship and save its sole crew.

event.text: Your ship's modest engines fight the extreme gravitation with some success. Time scales more and more, and your ship starts to buckle under the strain of extreme gravity. As a consolation prize, not only do you save Mafan, but you have the opportunity to scrap the ship before you return from within the gravity well. Unfortunately, the time dilation has allowed the fleet to advance.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Risk your ship by flying close enough to scrap the ship and save its sole crew.

event.text: Your ship's powerful engines fight the extreme gravitation as it inches closer. Time scales more and more, but your ship can handle it without much damage. As a bonus, not only do you save Mafan, but you have the opportunity to scrap the ship before you return from within the gravity well. Unfortunately, the time dilation has allowed the fleet to advance, but not by much.

choice.text: (Temporal Manipulator) Counteract the gravitational time dilation long enough to free Mafan's ship.

event.text: Mafan's vessel is able to break free from the Gravastar. The ship is clearly on its last legs as it putters slowly towards you. Your crew scuttle it as Mafan boards.

choice.text: (Aether Drive) Jump directly to Mafan's ship.

event.text: You jump directly in front of Mafan's ship, knowing your drive will also pilot you safely away. Not only do you save Mafan, but you have the opportunity to scrap the ship before you return from within the gravity well.

choice.text: (Aether Drive) Jump directly to Mafan's ship.

event.text: You jump directly in front of Mafan's ship, knowing your drive will also pilot you safely away. Not only do you save Mafan, but you have the opportunity to scrap the ship before you return from within the gravity well.

choice.text: (Teleporter) Teleport Mafan to your own ship.

event.text: You're able to lock on to and beam Mafan directly into your teleporter room. The ship remains in orbit, and will likely remain there until it decays and crashes into its surface.

choice.text: You'll have to wait for somebody else. We can't help.

event.text: "Well, that sucks." Mafan mutters. "I can only hope the listening post can find somebody else before too long."

name: STARGROVE_INVITE_MAFAN
text: Mafan arrives on your ship holding all of their research and breathes a sigh of relief. "I have to say, that was starting to feel like a real monkey's paw situation there. Find the opportunity of my dreams and then immediately become doomed to only do that for the rest of my life?" Mafan shudders. "At any rate, I have a number of things I'd be happy to share with you - not only am I skilled in manning a ship's systems, but I have some information about a possible expedition we could go on."

event.text:
"That's right. In my studies, I have determined where the Infernum have decided to reside, as well as the optimal path to go there. If you're interested, we could travel to their space and see what other novel things we can learn!"

"...or at least, that's what I would say, if we were ready. For now, you will have to wait for me to give my update on the Infernum to my superiors. Wait for an 'Infernal Update' so to speak." Mafan says, with a wink.

name: STARGROVE_CLEARING_MONK
text: You've managed to reach a safe location, and much to your surprise, you're hailed by a Monk vessel. "Greetings, Federation Renegade. Our ship has been sent here to serve as a guide for the wayward souls who find themselves in the Stargrove. Do you have a moment to listen?"

event.text: The Monk recounts a brief parable in which the protagonist and her brother are forced to pass through a burning building. The fortitude of the protagonist's soul keeps the flames at bay, but her brother gives into fear and is burned badly. He is consumed by anger, and blames the protagonist for his scars. He pulls a piece of burning wood from the wreckage and plunges it into his sister's heart, only to feel the pain in his own chest as he destroys himself.
"Thank you for hearing us. You have a dangerous journey ahead of you, but so long as you do not give in to fear and anger, the fires of these suns cannot touch your soul. Take this, and be well."
You have no time to hear the ramblings of Monks, especially here. You close the channel and prepare to depart.

name: STARGROVE_SEPARATIST_STORE
text: The stars here are sparse, making this beacon relatively temperate and peaceful. A station full of Separatist Engi reside here. "Welcome to p-p-p-paradise, -outsider-. We have finally f-f-found a [place] to be free of the -dreadful- Harmony. Here, you [are] safe. S-s-s-stay here for as -long- as you want."

choice.text: Your Defender protests this encampment of Separatists.

event.text: Upon seeing your Defender, the Separatists recoil. "Agent of t-t-the Harmony! We -will- not let [you] pass!"
"B-b-by entering the Stargrove, y-y-you must be -recycled-. We can l-l-liberate your crew instead. In, or out?" They train their weapons on you, anticipating a response.

The Separatists relax. "Then, your crew is -saved-! R-r-rejoice!" The Separatists take your crew away, and stuff them into a chamber. When they emerge, they seem different. Afterwards, they show you their shop.
The Separatists immediately become aggressive. "-Incorrect- response."
The Separatists makes no acknowledgement of your existence.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_STARGROVE_SMUGGLER_STORE
text: Amidst the raging stars, a mercenary ship is chasing down a smuggler. This may be one of your few opportunities to acquire supplies in such a desperate place.

event.text: The mercenary pauses its pursuit and turns to fight you.
The two ships continue their dance through the stars as you prepare to leave.

name: STARGROVE_SMUGGLER_STORE
text: "Here's a piece of advice: don't double cross a major member of the Syndicate without an exit strategy. Even after running into this hellhole, they chased after us for days! I have no intention to piss off a Renegade after that debacle, so let's do business, yeah? Be quick about it, we need to stake out a good place to lay low."

name: STARGROVE_SAFE_HAVEN
text: Your ship's readouts have finally calmed down, there are no hazards or foes here. This could be one of your few opportunities to rest. The research outpost here attempts to contact you on a Federation frequency.

event.text: "Welcome, Renegade. The travel restrictions keep the traffic in this sector low, as you might expect. We have a request, if you have the time: Our primary auto cruiser has gone missing. We can't afford to weaken the defenses of the outpost to go looking for it. Do you think you could spare the effort to track it down?"

"It's very dangerous to do research in the Stargrove. Due to the Federation's safety regulations, some of the most novel areas are restricted. Fortunately, our auto cruiser is able to collect data without risking Federation lives. The one that went missing is on a mission to investigate possible signs of exotic life in a remote part of the sector."
This is a rare opportunity to safely do something aboard your ship.

name: STARGROVE_SAFE_HAVEN_QUEST_ACCEPT
text: "Perfect. Here is the ship's last known location. Find out what's wrong. When you've found it, send it the data packet that we're forwarding to you now." They send you an encrypted file along with the location the ship was last sent to.

choice.text: See what services the outpost has to offer.

name: STARGROVE_SAFE_HAVEN_QUEST_REFUSE
text: This sector is plenty dangerous as it is. You can't afford to get mixed up in this.

choice.text: See what services the outpost has to offer.

name: STARGROVE_SAFE_HAVEN_OFFERS
text: There are a number of scientists and technicians who operate here. You can get the defenses on your ship upgraded, ask for repairs or to receive a resource bundle.

event.text: The outpost's skilled crew is able to quickly install the requested upgrade.
The outpost's skilled crew is able to quickly install the requested upgrade.
The outpost's skilled crew is able to quickly install the requested upgrade.
The outpost's skilled crew is able to quickly install the requested upgrade.
The outpost's skilled crew is able to quickly patch up your hull.
The outpost loads what resources they're willing to part with onto your ship.

choice.text: Do something onboard the ship instead.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_QUEST_STARGROVE_AUTO_CRUISER

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Federation auto cruiser went missing here.

text: Instead of an auto cruiser you immediately notice an advanced Dynasty ship firing its weapons directly at the nearest star. When they notice you, they warn you off. "Stay your approach, foul Renegade! Your dreadful abomination has aligned itself with those contemptible nightmares. Do not interfere."

event.text:
"Halt." Dessius commands. "This particular ship is not your enemy."

"Dessius? Centuries have passed since this mission was first undertaken. Are we to abandon our quest right at the culmination of our duties?"

"Clearly the threat they posed was vastly overstated. If they come to be the danger we feared them to be, we will have the opportunity to change course." Dessius made a gesture. "Your success in locating them is noted, but you are relieved of this mission."

"...As you wish."

As the enemy ship departs, the Federation auto cruiser emerges from its position near the star.
"The empty ones that should not exist! They cannot exist! They aren't there, yet they lurk!" The Dynasty captain struggles to fit his anguish into words.
You intervene, preventing the Dynasty ship from making any more attacks on the ship you were sent to protect.
You inform them that they don't sound too dissimilar to the way they describe their foes. It does not amuse them.
"How typical. The Federation defends its abomination and its new pets." The Dynasty cruiser turns to attack you instead!
"A wise choice. These horrific creatures need to be dealt with."

name: STARGROVE_AUTO_CONTACT
text: You send the auto cruiser the encrypted file given by the outpost. It responds by transmitting a text report of its mission and a full spreadsheet of the data it has been gathering. Apparently, the ship was successful in locating some exotic life, which it has termed "Vacuities". The auto ship offers an additional reward for rescuing it.

event.text: According to the report by the cruiser, a Vacuity is a starborne entity not directly detectable by any known sensor. They are indirectly detectable by the negative space that they create upon the surface of the star. The auto managed to detect an encoding caused by the Vacuities that appears to be a short, improvised distress signal by manipulating the radiation of the star. The auto cruiser translated the message as: "Help. Foe returned. We offer alliance."

choice.text: Instruct the auto cruiser to return to the outpost.
Instruct the auto cruiser to return to the outpost.

name: STARGROVE_AUTOSHIP_RETURN
text: A prerecorded message plays. "Acknowledged." Then, you receive a text-only communication from the ship offering to install its sensor augmentation on your vessel before it departs.

destroyed.text: You've defeated the highwayman, and are able to recover a large bounty of salvage from the wreck.

deadCrew.text: With his last breath, the highwayman pulls some type of remote-control out of his pocket and presses a button. You hear a small explosion, and though the ship doesn't seem to have sustained any significant damage, you eventually find the smoldering wreckage of the Pre-Igniter. Despite this setback, you're still able to pull a large amount of scrap from the ship, as well as the Pre-emptive Ion weapon.

destroyed.text: You've managed to destroy the ship. With the threat neutralized, you're able to find a functional weapon in the ruins!

surrender.text: "Enough! We only want to succeed in our mission. Leave us be and we will respond in kind."

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Continue looking for their lost ship.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Continue looking for their lost ship.
(Adv. Sensors) Continue looking for their lost ship.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Continue looking for their lost ship.

escape.text: The Rockmen prepare to jump away. It seems that they value self-preservation over accomplishing their original mission.

gotaway.text: The Crusaders jump away, leaving you alone with Madrock's shuttle.

destroyed.text: The defeat of an Inquisition ship is nothing to scoff at, especially under such hazardous conditions. You scrap their ship before attending to Madrock's shuttle.

deadCrew.text: The defeat of an Inquisition ship is nothing to scoff at, especially under such hazardous conditions. You scrap their ship before attending to Madrock's shuttle.

tooltip.text: The asteroid is expected to strike within this amount of time. Make sure to destroy it or run before the timer reaches 0!

escape.text: The probe doesn't have enough fuel to get home, but it's still focused on self-preservation - it's trying to escape.

destroyed.text: A ship this size isn't worth much, but it's more than you'd get by leaving it alone.
You've put a stop to the Coalition's plans in this sector - for now. Satisfied, you scrap the ship and prepare for the auto-probe's arrival.

deadCrew.text: The disparate races of the Coalition, once divided, have now congealed into one massive mess on the inside of the destroyer. Satisfied, you begin scrapping the ship while you wait for the auto-probe to catch up.

destroyed.text: As the ship crumbles around them, the captain screams out his final lament. "It can't be! The promised land was in our grasp!" Their ship finally explodes, allowing you to collect its remains.

deadCrew.text: The clonebay sputters out and refuses to produce anymore Duskbringer clones. Their path to enlightenment has failed, and their ship is yours to plunder.

destroyed.text: The mercenary ship is now in pieces. As you gather its scrap, you receive a message from a grateful smuggler.

deadCrew.text: The mercenary ship is devoid of pirate scum. As you strip it for parts, you receive a message from a grateful smuggler.

destroyed.text: The Dynasty ship crumples under the weight of your assault. As you collect the scrap, the Federation auto cruiser emerges from its position near the star.

deadCrew.text: The Dynasty ship's crew have been discorporated. As you harvest their ship, the Federation auto cruiser emerges from its position near the star.

name: ROCK_NEEDSMISSILES
text: You're hailed by a Rock vessel, who is supposedly low on missiles. They offer to buy some from you.

choice.text: We aren't interested in selling anything.

event.text: You apologize and continue on your way.

name: ROCK_APOLOGY
text: Moments after entering the system, you receive a message from the nearby ship; "We are sinners! Oh woe is us! Strike us down! Punish us! We do not deserve the gift of life!"

event.text: The Rockman's pleading continues for some time, but you simply tune them out and fly away.

name: ROCK_PUNS
text: A stoic Rock Captain hails you. "Federation. I have an important question for you. Why can you not expect perfection from geologists?"

event.text: "Because they all have their FAULTS!" He breaks into intense laughter.
Your laughter mixes together with the Rockman. After a while, you both calm down. So grateful that you found humor in his pun, the Rockman feels compelled to gift you some missiles!
"Wait... Wait no, it was just a joke!"
The Rockman is so impressed by the retaliation of your own pun that he submits, promising to dedicate the rest of his existence to your servitude. As long as he can keep making puns along the way.
The Rockman is so impressed by the retaliation of your own pun that he submits, promising to dedicate the rest of his existence to your servitude. As long as he can keep making puns along the way.
"Is that supposed to be a pun? I cannot tell if you are insulting me or making a pitiful attempt to join me. I hate Leeches. Get out of my sight!"

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug predict the answer.

event.text: Your Slug grumbles. "It'ssss jussst a ssstupid pun." Your Slug repeats the answer to the Rockmen. "Because they all have faultssss..." The Rockman frowns that you predicted it, and turns off transmissions.

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell predict the answer.

event.text: Your Shell scoffs. "Thhhis is an incredibly unendearing attempt of... comedy." Your Shell repeats the answer to the Rockmen. "Because thhhey all have faults..." The Rockman laughs upon hearing it, unaware that your Shell got the answer off his mind. He feels compelled to gift you some missiles for taking part in his antics.

name: ROCK_CRYOBSESSION
text: A nearby Rock settlement, painted almost entirely light blue, hails you. "You are from the outside? You wouldn't happen to have anything originating from the Crystal race, would you?"

choice.text: (Crystalline Weapon) We have a Crystal weapon.

event.text: "Amazing! Such a well crafted weapon too. I don't suppose you'd be willing to sell us one, would you?"

choice.text: Sell them a Crystal Burst MK I.
Sell them an Elite Crystal Burst MK I.
Sell them a Crystal Burst MK II.
Sell them an Elite Crystal Burst MK II.
Sell them a Heavy Crystal MK I.
Sell them an Elite Heavy Crystal MK I.
Sell them a Heavy Crystal MK II.
Sell them an Elite Heavy Crystal MK II.
Sell them an Elite Crystal Scatter.
Sell them an Elite Crystal Charger.
Sell them an Elite Neural Crystal.
Sell them a Chaotic Amber Launcher.
We aren't interested in selling anything.

event.text: "Ah... what a shame. Oh well, you must know that you are very lucky to wield such exotic tech!"

choice.text: (Crystal Crew) We have a Crystal aboard our ship.

event.text: The Rockman goes silent. Then, in a shaky tone, he says, "You... you must be gods! Please, take everything we have!"
The settlement immediately cuts transmissions.

name: ROCK_ITEM_SONG_CONTEST
text: An interesting entertainment program is being broadcast from this location - a singing exhibition. "Welcome, foreign ship. Would you like to participate in our competition? All that you need to do is sing a song from your culture."

choice.text: (Turzil) Turzil is a practiced jazz musician.

event.text: "I used to -play- with Tully. I might [be] a bit rusty." Turzil steps onto the stage with a saxophone and begins to play it. Surprisingly, it sounds very soulful. The audience is moved.

"Let's see if I can do some of these tunes justice. I'm sure the Rocks will appreciate these." Tully takes out a trumpet and begins playing. He's pretty good, in fact he doesn't even sound out of practice.

Tintan and Rig begin to jam out together, as a sort of two-man a-capella. Their unusual biological combination gives it a strange, unique sound. You've never heard anything quite like this. The Rocks love it.

choice.text: (Freddy) Freddy asks if they have a grand piano.

event.text: The Rocks don't have exactly what Freddy asked for, but they do have an organ. Freddy shows off the technique that he worked very hard to master - it's difficult to play a piano when you don't have fingers. It comes out sounding surprisingly good, though his physical limitations are clear.

choice.text: (Tuco) Tuco is an experienced Rock Musician.

event.text: The Rockmen judges are extremely hesitant to accept such a famous outcast. However, the director steps forward. "Today we are here to appreciate music. We will let you have your moment, provided you do not offend us." Tuco takes his favorite instrument and begins playing. Hearing the legend himself play is quite an experience, and the faithful Rockmen seem to enjoy it despite themselves. Still, it's likely the Theocracy's pride will not allow them to give him too much credit for it.

choice.text: (Guntput) Guntput sings the Door Open Song.

event.text: "Tunt parra parra, kaethlu parra parra, spaekith parra parra, taklu parra parra! Parra maku!" As soon as the song ends, the hall is quiet. A single rock stands up and begins to clap, and the entire crowd begins to stand up and join him.
Wealsey seems well trained and happily chirps out a beautiful song for the audience. The host seems confused. "Is that... an animal? Well, I guess there's no rules against it."

choice.text: (Jerry) Jerry used to sing for charity events.

event.text: Jerry decides that he'll sing "Why Can't We Be Friends". He instructs the crowd about the audience-participation chorus ahead of time. The Rocks have a blast - the resulting performance leads to a standing ovation. It may very well be that this is the exact moment that serves as the turning point for unity between your two species.

choice.text: (Ellie) Ellie loves to sing her theme song!

event.text: Ellie sings her theme song enthusiastically, galloping around the stage as she does. The host is perplexed by the song choice. "Well... I'm not sure what I expected from foreigners."

choice.text: (Stephan) Stephan has a few songs in his repertoire

event.text: "Don't worry, captain, I've performed for Rocks before." Stephan picks a show tune he used to sing for his auditions. It's an old song, but it holds up remarkably well. His talents as a showman are clearly beyond reproach, and the crowd begs for an encore.
Dessius sounds out a mournful song of great sadness and regret. The crowd goes silent - not because it was bad but because everyone who heard it has become incredibly bummed out.
Ivar has been known to strum a few strings at his parties. He plays a surprisingly jaunty tune, but despite the entertainment it brings, the Rocks don't completely appreciate it.
Mafan plays a cheerful, yet technical solo on a flute, with an accompanying tap-dance. The Rocks find it silly at first, but you notice them starting to get into it around the midpoint of the song.

choice.text: (Human) One of your humans is a musician.

event.text: Your Lanius takes to the stage and begins to vibrate. The resulting sound is an eerie harmony of metal on metal, reverberations and clangs. It's a little hard to listen to at times, but it's a very impressive performance nonetheless.

choice.text: (Vampweed) Bang out some Oro'Bache Pop Metal

event.text: Your Vampweed busts out the electric guitar and begins playing one of the recent hits. It's a very loud and catchy song without much substance, but you know it'll be stuck in your head now. Unfortunately, the Rockmen don't seem to like it.
Your Floral plays a bopping swing rendition of a well known Rock song. The Rock audience seem to be enjoying themselves.

choice.text: (Zoltan Monk) Perform a traditional Zoltan chant

event.text: The monk does a call-and-response chant, involving the audience. It goes over well, though it doesn't resonate with the entire audience.
Your Osmian takes their theremin and plays a chilling melody. The audience is on the edge of their seats as your Osmian skillfully manipulates their instrument.
The Lizard does a lizard chant for the contest, with an accompanying interpretive dance. The Rockmen are all very impressed with the lizard's song, never having seen anything like it before.

choice.text: (Theocracy Rock) Sing a Folk Rock song

event.text: Your Theocracy Rock sings a folk rock song. The judges clap politely, but it's clear that there's simply too much competition with other rocks to make any meaningful impact.

Your Rock starts to jam out and uses this opportunity to spread the message. The song hits incredibly hard. However, you're barely able to get through half of the song before they cut the feed and angrily kick you out for going against the establishment.
Your ship plays some electronic music based on songs that the Rocks seem to like. The Rocks all seem surprised that a ship is capable of making its own music.
The Contest is pretty enjoyable, a lot of rock performers have come to compete. In the meantime, your crew might be able to do something on the ship as they listen.

name: ROCK_ITEM_SONG_CONTEST_WINNER
text: "It's not often that we hear something so new and yet so beautiful. Thank you for introducing us to this, Renegade. The judges have awarded you first place, and I'm proud to present you with the prize." The audience applauds your crew member's performance.

name: ROCK_ITEM_SONG_CONTEST_SECOND_PLACE
text: "Truly impressive. Thank you for sharing that artist with us. It is the opinion of the judges that our frontrunner has put in too much work not to win, but your excellence must be recognized. The judges have awarded you second place. Here is your prize."

name: ROCK_ITEM_SONG_CONTEST_THIRD_PLACE
text: "You are quite talented to stand among our experienced contestants. Thank you for making this contest more interesting. The judges award you third place. Here is your prize."

name: ROCK_ITEM_SONG_CONTEST_RUNNER_UP
text: As the rock host announces the winners, it's clear that you did not place on the podium. They grant you a consolation prize for your participation in the contest.

name: ROCK_ITEM_SONG_CONTEST_KICKED_OUT
text: After being kicked out, a shuttle approaches your ship. "Your song has moved me. I have considered defecting from the Theocracy for some time. If you'll have me, I would be honored to join you."

choice.text: Induct them into the Lost Suns.

name: ROCK_PROPHECY
text: A ship carrying several robed Rockmen carrying holy books and candles hails you. "A time of change is coming! Have you heard the news? The prophecy, it shall be fulfilled!"

event.text: "Have you not heard? The ship from a future much brighter than ours, who will bring about a great change! A gift from the high heavens, bestowed upon us mortal-bound men by the benevolent Crystal ones!"

choice.text: Could we be the ship from the prophecy?

event.text: One of the Rockmen pull down their cloak and stare for a long time deep into your eyes. "I am no expert, but you have the look of a creature driven by a force beyond your control. Your will is bent by a being from the great beyond, manipulated for the simple sake of amusement. If you are not the one spoken of in the prophecy, then surely you are important regardless. Perhaps this may be of aid."

choice.text: These people are crazy, let's leave.

event.text: You have better things to than listen to the ravings of these religious loons.

name: ROCK_TEMPLE
text: Nearby rests a Rockman temple dedicated to the Crystal race. A thick fog covers the planet and it's hard to see if there's anything protecting the shrine.

event.text: You'd have to be insane to raid a Rockman temple in Rock territory.

name: ROCK_ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP
text: A ship without life forms within a nearby dense asteroid field is giving off the distress call. Shall we investigate? It could be dangerous.

event.text: Discretion is the better part of valor. Better not risk it.

choice.text: (Rock Plating) Make a thorough search for the ship without fear of stray asteroids.

name: ROCK_WEAPON_MEASURING
text: "Hah! Look at your wee little ship! I bet your weapons are tiny! You must be so ashamed."

choice.text: The hell did you just say to us?

event.text: The Rockman arrogantly chuckles as you prepare to fight them.
"Hah! You call that big weapons? Your brain must be even smaller!"
"Getting warmer, but that's still nothing compared to what we have!"
"Hmmm, not bad. Not many ships come here packing such heat. I'm sure a ship like yours will find a use for a powerful weapon like this!"

choice.text: (Lvl 8 Weapons) Oh, we can do better than that.

event.text: "Well now you're just showing off. I like it. I wish to sample your arsenal. I shall join you!"
"Hah! You call that big weapons? Your brain must be even smaller!"
"Getting warmer, but that's still nothing compared to what we have!"
"Hmmm, not bad. Not many ships come here packing such heat. I'm sure a ship like yours will find a use for a powerful weapon like this!"

choice.text: (Lvl 4 Artillery) Oh, we can do better than that.

event.text: "Well now you're just showing off. I like it. I wish to sample your arsenal. I shall join you!"
"Well now you're just showing off. I like it. I wish to sample your arsenal. I shall join you!"
You ignore the egotistical Rockmen and continue on your way.

name: SURRENDER_ROCK_BIGGUNS
text: "Jeez man, we've heard it's not about the size but how you use it, and you sure know how to use your guns! You've proven your point, let us go and we'll pay you some ammunition to fuel those guns of yours."

name: ROCK_LOOTING_MV
text: You find a disabled Rock transport floating near the beacon. You consider stripping it of useful parts but are uncertain why it's there in the first place.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Check for lifeforms and keep a lookout for ships while looting the wreck.
(Telepathic Shell) Check for lifeforms and keep a lookout for ships while looting the wreck.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Have your ship search for any approaching ships while looting the wreck.

name: ROCK_MANTIS_HUNTER_MV
text: A Mantis ship here is adorned with Rock body parts! It would be a gorier display if they had internal organs, but the message is clear enough: this is a hunter of a very specialized kind.

event.text: No species deserves a Mantis hunter on their back - time to make the galaxy a little safer. Engage!
The Mantis take no interest in your ship - they're lying in wait for the next Rock ship to venture through. You're able to spin up the engines and jump at your leisure.

Before they have a chance, you ram your ship into theirs, causing irreparable damage to their engines. Luckily, your ship's armored hull is hardly dented from the impact. The Mantis ship careens away and you move in to attack.

choice.text: (Rock Crew) Put your Rock crewmember on the comm.

event.text: The two aliens face one another over the vidscreen. "Cave-dwelling pebble-man!" yells the furious Mantis captain. "See, I paint ship with your companions! I paint ship with you!"

name: ROCK_MANTIS_FREIGHTER_MV
text: A curious sight greets you at this beacon: a disabled Rock freighter drifts in space while two Mantis craft battle it out - presumably over who deserves the spoils.

choice.text: Wait, then attack the surviving Mantis.

event.text: There's quite enough action here already - prepare for light speed.

While the two Mantis fight you approach the Rock ship and send a repair drone through one of the many breaches. It fixes the ship up enough to make at least a single jump. You're surprised when, instead, they embark on a kamikaze run on the two Mantis, which results in the obliteration of all three!

While the two Mantis fight you approach the Rock ship and use a drone to fix up the ship. Once the breaches are fixed the life support flickers back on. In a matter of moments they are already in pursuit of one of the Mantis ships. Meanwhile the second Mantis turns toward you.

name: ROCK_ZOLTAN_HELP_MV
text: It seems a Zoltan ship came here to liberate a Rock settlement from their 'oppressive belief system', and that the settlement did not appreciate it - long-range scanners suggest the Zoltans and their pursuers will be here at any moment!

event.text: The... extreme nature of Rock faith is well-known; the Zoltans can hardly be blamed for trying to broaden their horizons. The pursuing Rock ship quickly assesses the situation and decides two captured alien ships are better than one.
This is Rock territory, and therefore Rock law - the Zoltans should have known better than to interfere. You'll have to neutralize the crew to ensure their safe capture.
This is none of your concern - power up the jump drive!

name: ROCK_ATHEIST
text: You encounter a small craft with minimal propulsion; its Rock crew-member explains that the Rock home-world is run on lies and propaganda that keep the populace in check, and that they want no part of it.

choice.text: Tell them their god sent them here to join your crew.
Promise to share with them the truths they've been denied.
(Upg. Sensors) Show them to your data suite.

event.text: The Rock captain is impressed by the data you've collected and agrees to stay with you until they find their footing in the galaxy.

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) Teach them the ways of the Lost Suns.

event.text: The Rock captain is surprised, as he had previously thought the Lost Suns were a band of radical terrorists. Assured your ship will keep no secrets from them, he joins your crew.

choice.text: (Floral Crew) Have your Orchid talk them into joining you.

event.text: The Orchids are not only a race trusted by the Rockmen, but their government is incredibly well known for its transparency. Soothed by your crew, the Orchid talks them into coming with you, promising it'll be a better life than that among the Elders' lies.

name: ROCK_LIVE_MINE
text: The burnt out hull of a Rock Trapper drifts by. Behind the wreck drifts a live mine; an automated drone that drills into ships' hulls before exploding. However, it can't detect you from this range, and you wonder if it's even active. Still, it's risky...

event.text: You pick apart the hull of the ship, and find some scrap, ammunition, and a Mine Launcher! However, before you can leave the mine activates, and begins to seek out your ship!
The ship's turning circle proves too wide and the mine bites down onto the hull. You can hear it now, chewing through the armor.

choice.text: Send someone out there to defuse it.
With no one around, your only option is to patiently wait for your demise.

event.text: The weapon detonates. Everything goes dark, the bridge illuminated by flames pouring from the hull. You put out the fires and prepare to move on.

choice.text: (Missile Weapon) Attempt a controlled detonation using a missile.

event.text: After drawing straws, a crewmember goes out to fix a modified warhead to the mine. You detonate the missile in a way that dislodges the mine. It blows up shortly after. The ship takes some damage in the blasts, but you're still sailing.

choice.text: (Beam Drone) Use a drone to cut away the mine with a precision beam. [-1|]

event.text: Carefully guided from the bridge, your Beam Drone removes the mine's grappling arms and sends it drifting off into space, where you shoot at it until it detonates at a safe distance.
It stresses the inertial dampeners, but you reverse course and outrun the mine. You prepare to jump off.

choice.text: (Hull Armor) Your armor will protect you.

event.text: The mine struggles to even burrow into your ship. Its drill eventually runs out of power and drifts away, now rendered harmless.

choice.text: (Energy Shield) Your shield will protect you.

event.text: The mine is incapable of getting past your Energy Shield. It explodes without even touching your ship's hull.
Fortunately, your Defense Drone quickly locks onto the mine and shoots it down before it can connect to the ship.
It's not worth it to investigate. The beacon is likely littered with scattered mines in other places too, so you decide to not remain here for long.

name: ROCK_SLUG_ARGUMENT_MV
text: You find a Slug Cruiser and Rock ship at a standoff, both with weapons armed and ready to fight. You could intervene before this gets out of hand.

choice.text: Hail them to see what's wrong.

event.text: The Slug captain explains that they upgraded the Rock ship's reactor and now the 'thick boulder heads' are refusing to pay for the work done. The Rock Captain says the 'gelatinous ooze rats' did a poor job that is not worth their agreed upon price.

choice.text: Offer to pay off the Rock debt.

event.text: You pay off the debt. The Rock Captain still seems annoyed at the Slug's getting their 'undeserved' scrap, but at least the situation will remain peaceful.

choice.text: Demand the Rock ship pay the agreed upon price.
(Rock Crew) Talk the Rock into peacefully paying the full price.

event.text: With much grumbling, the Rock Captain agrees to pay the price.

choice.text: Demand the Slug ship give a full refund.
(Slug Crew) Talk the Slugs into peacefully accepting the new price.

event.text: With much grumbling, the Slug Captain agrees to give a full refund.

choice.text: (Mind Control) Mind Control the Slugs into giving a full refund.

event.text: You calibrate the Mind Control to lock onto the Slug ship... but nothing happens. It's at this moment you remember Slugs can't be mind controlled at all. The Slug captain laughs at your pitiful attempt and you leave in shame.

choice.text: (Mind Affecting Weapon) Mind Control the Slugs into giving a full refund.

event.text: You calibrate the Mind Control to lock onto the Slug ship... but nothing happens. It's at this moment you remember Slugs can't be mind controlled at all. The Slug captain laughs at your pitiful attempt and you leave in shame.

choice.text: You have better things to attend to, leave them.

event.text: You leave the two ships to their bickering.

name: ROCK_RAVINE
text: On the surface of a nearby planet is a massive ravine. It all looks normal until you spot two Rock scouts flying past, deeper into the ravine.

event.text: You trail the ships from far behind, making sure they can't see you but never losing them. Not too long after you reach a fork in the ravine, and the ships split up. If you don't want the Rebel fleet catching up, you'll only have time to explore one of the paths.

choice.text: Follow the ship to the left.

event.text: The ship stops at what looks like a giant facility built into the face of the ravine's sheer drop. With nowhere to hide, the Rockmen inevitably spot you and prepare to defend whatever the facility may be.

choice.text: Follow the ship to the right.

event.text: The ship lands near a giant prison camp built on the floor of the ravine. It looks abandoned, but you don't have much time to investigate before the Rockmen spot your ship and attacks.

choice.text: Nevermind, this is a bad idea.

event.text: Those Rockmen could be doing anything down there, and it's none of your business.

name: ROCK_RAVINE_LEFT
text: You've defeated the Rock vessel. You have some time to scrap the ship before investigating the facility.

event.text: The entrance to the structure leads you to a deprecated lobby. A barely functional elevator suggests there must be a back-up generator running, because this facility has long since been abandoned. There's several different options for floors to explore, but you'll only have time for one.

A floor marked control in a Rock facility is sure to be an interesting experience. You head there, wary of the elevator. Inside is a no-longer functional Mind Control system and a giant screen overlooking what looks to be a giant prison camp on the other side of the ravine. You begin to think there's nothing of actual use in this room until you notice a combat augment in the corner, as well as some discarded fuel cells.

The security floor has piqued your interest. You head there, wary of the elevator. Heavy blast doors protect the way in, but something has managed to bend them back far enough for you to squeeze by. Several monitors overlooks the other rooms of the facility, proving it to be completely empty of staff. Not much here is of value to a military ship, other than a Long-Ranged Scanners augmentation and some droneparts.

The armory seems like the obvious choice. You head there, wary of the elevator. Inside you find several racks of supplies and various weapons. With limited manpower, you take one of the weapons at random as well as a few missiles.

name: ROCK_RAVINE_RIGHT
text: You've defeated the Rock vessel. You have some time to scrap the ship before investigating the camp.

event.text: The Rock prison camp appears to be primarily abandoned, but a lone campfire that's still burning suggests there may still be some life left behind. You're proven correct when further exploration reveals a small band of prisoners of various races. They explain that the prisoners revolted and managed to kill off most of the Rock guards. The Rockmen retreated and the surviving prisoners starved to death. This small group are the only ones who remain. You don't have enough space on the ship to take them all with you, but you can probably bring one of them.

choice.text: Bring one of the Rock prisoners.

event.text: The Rock bears the markings of an outcast, likely a fugitive from the Rock government who was recently captured. They don't speak much, but you can tell they're glad you've chosen to rescue them.

choice.text: Bring one of the Human prisoners.

event.text: The human turns out to be a Rebel Engineer, captured by the Rockmen with the intent to be used as a hostage to bargain with the Rebels. Unfortunately for them, the Rebels had no interest in buying back the prisoner. They were locked into this camp. Despite being of Rebel origins, they are more than glad to come with you and leave behind this place.

choice.text: Bring one of the Slug prisoners.

event.text: The Slug was a tourist captured by the Rockmen based purely on suspicion. Not wanting to admit to their mistake, they simply chose to lock the Slug away in this prison for the rest of eternity. They're vibrant with energy at the prospect of finally being free.

name: ROCK_ASTEROID_COLONY
text: It appears complete chaos has broken out on the nearby Rock colony. It seems a large asteroid collided with the planet and caused extreme damage, and now hundreds of ships are swarming back and forth from the planet's surface.

event.text: You fly towards the planet's surface and engage a pirate ship currently firing on unarmed Rock civilians.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Cloak whilst trying to salvage the wreckage.
(Adv. Cloaking) Cloak whilst trying to salvage the wreckage.

event.text: With the help of your Cloaking, you're able to retrieve a hefty amount of wreckage without any of the Rock Enforcers noticing you. Once you can't collect any more scrap, you make a quick escape.

choice.text: This is chaos. We should leave.

event.text: You avoid the colony and the ships around it.

name: ROCK_ASTEROID_COLONY_PIRATE
text: The pirate vessel crashes down into the ground, but luckily the civilians are unharmed. No one protests as you salvage the wreckage of the pirate ship.

event.text: Most of the Rockmen are too panicked and flee as you approach. A few of the more sensible individuals stop to hear you out. You offer to transport as many of them as you can carry, an offer which most of them refuse. One young Rockman however accepts, even going so far as to join your crew.

name: ROCK_CRUSADE
text: A cluster of Inquisition ships are resting nearby, making minor repairs. They haven't noticed you.

event.text: "Federation ship, you are not welcome here! Do not contact us again, unless you have a death wish."
"Gah! Now you've asked for it."

choice.text: (Theocracy Crew) Have your Rockman contact them.

event.text: "One of us? Perhaps I was mistaken of your origins. We have encountered an unpredicted obstacle in our usual duties. A Mantis vessel, full of heretics and scum, has made the fatal mistake of entering our sector! Unfortunately, it seems we're not fully prepared for their boarding tactics. Are you able to fulfill our mission and destroy the Mantis?"

The Inquisition ships give you the co-ordinates of the Mantis. To your surprise, they aren't far away, so close in fact that they inhabit the same beacon. Another unexpected turn is that they are no Hive Mantis ship, but rather Free Mantis! "Oh, Federation! Hello! We glad to see you. This sector weird, yes? Not long ago, we chased by big blue ship with angry stone man. Very scary."

choice.text: Follow through with your promise and kill the Free Mantis.

event.text: You have a mission to follow through with. You arm your weapons and engage the Free Mantis.
The Rockmen are enraged at your betrayal. "This is an insult beyond anything I have ever experienced! You are weak, and must be punished."
"Then you are of no use to us. Leave at once."
You put some distance between you and the Rockmen, just to be safe.

name: ROCK_CRUSADE_FREEMANTIS
text: You've defeated the Free Mantis ship. You salvage the remains.

choice.text: Confirm your success with the Inquisition.

event.text: "A worthy display of your honor and prowess. I applaud you. Accept this as a token of gratitude."

name: ROCK_CRUSADE_ROCK
text: You've defeated the Rockmen. You salvage the remains.

event.text: "Scary stone man dead now? Wow... this sector very not friendly. I come with you now, and bring twin brother."

name: ROCK_NURSERY_MV
text: Fluctuating life-signs are reported near the surface of a hazy, pock-marked moon in the vicinity. It seems this is a Rock nursery where the young are 'acclimatized' to their religion - only there's been some kind of coup and the students are running amok!

choice.text: Transfer an away team to investigate.

event.text: Your away team reports combat between students and authorities - it seems some of the students were considered to have dissident personalities and were to be imprisoned pro-actively.

choice.text: Order the away team to side with the students.

event.text: It's not long before the violence on the planet becomes a full-scale battle, your away team and their military-grade weaponry in the very center of it.

choice.text: Order the away team to side with the authorities.

event.text: It's not long before the violence on the planet becomes a full-scale battle, your away team and their military-grade weaponry in the very center of it.

choice.text: You lack the team required to oppose fanatical zealots... or opressed students.

event.text: As long as they're not shooting at the ship it's best to leave them be.

choice.text: (Adv. Weapons) Fire a warning shot near to the commotion to announce your arrival.

event.text: You dispatch a barrage of weapons fire that crashes home into an unused quarry near to the installation. Weapons fire on the surface ceases for as long as it takes for the moon's defense force to be dispatched to your location!

name: ROCK_NURSERY_MV_WIN
text: In return for your support during the fight the survivors reward you with the funds set aside for prison transport. You leave before anyone changes their mind!

name: ROCK_NURSERY_MV_LOSE
text: Fully aware that their victory was threatened by your arrival, the survivors immediately dispatch a ship to eliminate you!

name: DISTRESS_REFUGEE_ROCK
text: You have encountered a refugee ship drifting in space. It looks as if it was fleeing the Rebel advance and ran out of fuel. Its distress beacon is active, but you're not sure anyone is on board.

event.text: You're wary of the refugees but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: DISTRESS_ROCK_DETAINING_ZOLTAN
text: You find a Zoltan merchant ship that is sending out a distress call. Its escape is being blocked by a Theocracy patrol. There are no signs of a struggle.

choice.text: Hail the Zoltans to see what's wrong.

event.text: "You're with the Federation, are you not? We are being ex-" They are abruptly cut off from transmitting. The Rock ship hails you.
"Leave now, Renegade. We are within our right to detain merchants, even if they are from the Ministry."

choice.text: (Theocracy Elite) "The Ministry is our ally. Release them at once."

event.text: "Er..." The Theocracy captain stumbles over his word. "That is to say... we were just... We needed to ask them some questions..." The Rockman clears his throat. "...They're free to go, then. We hope you'll overlook our... enthusiasm for our duties." To punctuate this, the Rockmen give you a tribute.

choice.text: (Theocracy-Aligned Rockman) Ask what charge the merchants are being held on.

event.text: "They are under suspicion of spreading Federation lies! If they want to prove their respect for our customs, they will have to provide monetary compensation for the damage they have done to our culture!"

choice.text: Sounds like you're just extorting them.
Demand the release of the Zoltans.

event.text: The Rockmen save you the trouble of engaging and attack you first!
The Theocracy and the Ministry are allies - whatever is happening is between them.

name: ROCK_DETAINING_ZOLTAN_CONVINCE
text: "Thank you for convincing them to step away. Why would the Theocracy abuse its power like that?" The merchant sighs. "Would you like to purchase anything from our store?"

name: ROCK_DETAINING_ZOLTAN_DEFEAT
