text: "Thank you for intervening on our behalf, Renegade. We never suspected the patrol would abuse its power like that... Would you like to purchase anything from our store?"

name: DISTRESS_ROCK_OUTCAST_PREY
text: The distress beacon leads you to a half-destroyed Outcast ship, ravaged by what seems to be the nearby pirate ship. Their previous target disposed of, they now turn to you!

name: ROCK_OUTCAST_SAVE
text: You check on the victim, and to your surprise find a survivor! You help them on your ship.

event.text: "So much for freedom... as soon as we saw a way out of this hellhole that the Elders imposed on us, pirates picked us apart. Is the harsh grip of our presumed leaders a necessary evil to protect us? Either way, what me and my brothers had in mind absolutely went off the wrong foot. Where am I even supposed to seek shelter?"

choice.text: Encourage them to join the Lost Suns.

event.text: "You have a point. This was the original plan, but unfortunately we never managed to contact them in our makeshift escape. The teachings and expertise they can offer will reinforce me, despite the misadventures encountered on the way." With your ties to the Federation, it doesn't take too much time to pinpoint the location of a nearby Lost Sun ship that can arrange the transfer.

choice.text: Encourage them to rejoin the Theocracy.

event.text: "It remains to be seen if I can just backtrack and be accepted again... but it's for the best." Your new passenger informs you of the location of a station in their native system, and you plan a course there.

choice.text: Encourage them to seek shelter at the Sister-Species Liberation Group.

event.text: "I have heard a little about this cause. I don't know if I can find peace among the Crystals, but their intentions seem genuine." Your new passenger informs you of the location of a station in the neighbouring systems they managed to hear about when they weren't drowned by the propaganda of the Theocracy.

choice.text: Encourage them to remain an Outcast.

event.text: It's harsh, but you reveal to them that anybody making a run from the Theocracy should endure what is roughly survival of the fittest, that many of their peers don't always make it. "Yes, I suppose you have a point... You've convinced me, Renegade. Without a vessel or crew to roll with now though... I shall stay with you then. My chances will significantly improve under your care." Seeing as their former vessel is in no state to fly, you gather what can still be of use from it.

name: ROCK_OUTCAST_LOSTSUN

unvisitedTooltip.text: You agreed to escort an Outcast survivor to the Lost Suns.

text: You've arrived at the system, and you've spotted the expected Lost Sun ship. They are wary, but you patch the Outcast through.

event.text: After explaining their journey, the Outcast expresses their desire to join the Lost Suns and vouches for you in return for the help you provided. They accept their new recruit, and offer you military supplies for your deeds.

name: ROCK_OUTCAST_ROCK

unvisitedTooltip.text: You agreed to escort an Outcast survivor to a Rock station.

text: You've arrived at the system, and you've spotted the Rock station. You feel at unease sticking around, and you start to regret your decision, but the Outcast opens comms.

event.text: After explaining their journey, the Outcast expresses their desire to reintegrate the Theocracy and vouches for you in return for the help you provided. The Rockman at the other end though doesn't seems so eager to accept them back. "Foolish, foolish... why should we offer refuge to filth, who decided to splinter from the grace of those who paved the way for our-"

A second figure comes and interrupts their peer. "Silence, brother. Yes, this one... he has strayed, but few are those who recognize their mistakes, and even fewer are those who seek to repent toward our ways. Let him in, at once. As for you, foreigner... your compassion will be rewarded. We will permit you to dock and access our services, once the refugee will be under our responsibility."

name: ROCK_OUTCAST_SSLG

unvisitedTooltip.text: You agreed to escort an Outcast survivor to a SSLG station.

text: You've arrived at the system, and you catch sight of what seems to be SSLG infrastructure in the horizon. You approach cautiously and are hailed by a Crystal demanding your reasons to be here, and you let the Outcast speak through.

event.text: After explaining their journey, the Outcast expresses their desire to seek shelter among the Crystals and vouches for you in return for the help you provided. They eagerly accept, and not only do they award you a spare weapon, one of the liberators wishes to join your cause in belief that more Rockmen can be helped on the way.

name: ROCK_ASTROLOGER
text: There's a small Rock colony at this beacon: most notably, there is also a massive telescope in orbit. It seems there's an astronomical laboratory here.

event.text: "A ship! It's been too long. Oh, an outsider? Well, that will have to do. The Theocracy hasn't been listening to us recently. On behalf of the Rock Astrologer Association, I implore you to listen and give me some assistance."

"There is a crystalline comet making its way through this sector. Comets are common in Theocracy space, but there are some that have some fascinating properties. I believe this comet could contain many secrets about the past of the Crystals."

choice.text: Why wouldn't the Theocracy be interested in investigating?

event.text: The 'astrologer' gives a hefty sigh. "They used to. Back before the Crystals rejoined the galactic scene, these comets were the only trace of their existence we had. We would chase comet after comet, and no matter how little they turned up, we would still have the funding to chase them down. But now that we can physically talk to the Crystals, the Theocracy no longer sees the value in it. They see chasing comets as menial busywork, and refuse to give us any funding... But that doesn't mean it isn't worth it!"
"Fantastic. You may keep what you find, but please send me the data when you get it!"
"Hpmh. Astrologers get no respect these days."
"Fantastic. You may keep what you find, but please send me the data when you get it!"
"Hpmh. Astrologers get no respect these days."
This area seems to be of low priority to the Theocracy, so you have ample time to spend.

name: QUEST_ASTROLOGER_COMET

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Rock astrologer asked you to seek out a comet passing through this beacon.

text: You arrive at the site of the comet that the Astrologer tasked you to find.

name: COMET_DWELLERS_ASTROLOGER
text: "Incredible... we've searched so many of them back in the day and never heard of Crystals dwelling within them... could this be a recent development?"

choice.text: Scuttle whatever else you can find on the comet.

name: COMET_ASTROLOGER_ANCIENT
text: Inside of the comet is, surprisingly, some strange green, cubical technology. It all looks very old and not exactly in the best shape, but the quality of the craftsmanship is apparent even having been so ancient.

event.text: "Incredible! Never in my wildest dreams did I ever expect anything on this level... Ah, what a shame that this technology did not end up in our hands, but it is their fault for never listening to us!"

name: ROCK_SUN_CHALLENGE
text: You are immediately messaged by an imposing looking Rock war vessel, "You're the ship off to 'save the Federation', aren't you? And you expect to survive with that hunk of junk?"

choice.text: "We're going to save them or die trying."

event.text: "The latter being more likely. Still... we can potentially help you and your precious fleet, but you'll need to prove yourself first. Meet us at these coordinates." They jump away.
"One ship is not the same as a fleet, but at least you've got some fire. Meet us at these coordinates if you want to prove to us that the Federation is worth saving." They jump away.
"Heh. Like I expected. If the Federation is as weak as you it deserves to fall." They jump away without another word.

name: ROCK_SUN_CHALLENGE2

unvisitedTooltip.text: An Inquisition vessel has requested that you meet them here so they can judge your prowess.

text: You arrive at the coordinates given and find yourself dangerously close to an M-class star! The other ship messages you, "Let's see how long your puny ship can handle this heat! Prepare for a challenge!"

name: ROCK_SUN_CHALLENGE3

unvisitedTooltip.text: The Inquisition vessel you held out against transmitted these coordinates.

text: You arrive at a massive Rockman shipyard and notice the ship that had just tried to kill you is docked and already being repaired. "Well fought! I must say I did not expect you to survive."

event.text: "I am convinced of your strength and pledge to assist your cause. Let us patch up your hull, and provide you with some supplies."

name: QUEST_ROCK_MARRIAGE_START
text: A Rock captain hails you: "It is improper of me to contact off-worlders, but this is an emergency. We were on our way to deliver our passenger to her new husband - the Grand Basilisk of Numa V - when our engines broke down. Will you take possession of her and make haste to Numa V?"

event.text: "You surprise me, off-worlder. Thank you. The passenger will be with you momentarily." She refuses to enter the main hold and prefers to wait in the cargo bay.
Arranged marriages aren't on your list of worthy causes. You leave the Rock to their business.

name: ROCK_QUEST_MARRIAGE
text: A vast tunnel network near the surface of Numa V indicates an advanced Rock civilization. This must be where you were asked to deliver the passenger.

event.text: Realizing arrival is imminent, the passenger - silent so far - pleads with you not to hand her over. She's interrupted by the Grand Basilisk's Chief Aid: "To the alien vessel holding the Basilisk's wife. Deliver her to us. You will be rewarded... well."
"May your children erode into dust!" she screams as she's bundled into the waiting shuttle. The Rock guards on board hurriedly drop off an exotic piece of technology and return to the Grand Basilisk.
"I was led to believe your kind did not know mercy. I will join you. But quickly, we must jump away - they will not tolerate..." She's interrupted by weapons fire from the Basilisk's escort!

name: ENCOUNTER_LOSTSUN_ROCKHOME
text: A Lost Sun ship, seeking out Rock citizens to capture and take back to the Stronghold as prisoners, identifies your ship. "Traitorous coward! A Federation vessel, out here, giving aid to the Rock Elders' followers? You are scum! I will roast all of you alive." They aren't exactly correct, but you doubt arguing will help.

name: ROCK_CRYSTAL_WAYSTONE
text: It seems you've discovered the Crystalline Waystone, the device used to enter the Crystal Homeworlds. The beacon is shockingly empty, despite the boom in tourism that eventually lead to the exodus of the Crystal race back to the galactic scene.

event.text: Better not risk it. The Rock people are unlikely to respond well to vandalism.

choice.text: (Crystal Crew) Have your Crystal crew activate the device again.

event.text: Are you certain you want to do this? You will immediately be taken to the Crystal Homeworlds.

name: ENCOUNTER_ROCK_ELITE
text: The Rockman Crusaders were once recruited to enact the Inquisition, a brutal invasion of other worlds deemed full of heretics to instate the 'wisdom' of the Elders. The Federation has officially put an end to the Inquisition long ago, but the Crusader rank has not yet been disbanded. They can still be seen on patrols to fulfill the schemes of the Elders and protect their claims from outsiders, such as yourself.

name: ROCK_ZOLTAN_PARASITE
text: A Rock station nearby is mass-broadcasting a request for medical aid. "Medical assistance required at Station R-0735Q. Need help extracting parasite. Will pay."

event.text: The Rockmen are mildly confused that a Federation ship is offering to help, but don't complain. "We are representatives for Zulfiqar Industries. Yesterday, CMO Rig Bramston arranged a meeting on these premises to discuss a solution to his... medical issues. Seven years ago, he was in a company meeting alongside a Zoltan envoy named Tintan, when a Slug vessel arrived and deployed a 'prank' on the meeting, melding the two into one being against their will. As you can understand, reversing this has been a top priority for both Rig and Zulfiqar for the past seven years, but nothing we have attempted since has worked, and Rig's vitals - or rather, Tintan's, are showing signs that she is growing dangerously unstable over time, and may be at risk of detonation. As you might imagine, we are now in quite the dilemma and need to operate immediately."

"My god... Tony? Is that you? How are you here?" You have no idea what's going on, but Tony explains. "7 years ago, Tony's was nothing but a small chain - local only to the Republic. I hoped to change that by expanding into genetic experimentation; what army could turn down Mantises with the durability of a Rock? I met with representatives from Zulfiquar to discuss how we'd go about securing test subjects, then a Slug ship arrived and... demonstrated my ideas on them. The surgeons had no idea how to handle the situation. Tony's eventually went galactic when we started the loan program, but I never forgot about you, Rig."

The Rock station owners are completely baffled as to what is happening, but together you, Tony, Rig, and Tintan discuss the situation. It becomes clear Rig and Tintan won't be free of each other any time soon, but with Tony's help you might just be able to track down the Slugs responsible and get revenge.

Anurak passes the afflicted Rockman a bowl of soup. "How is this supposed to help?"
					
					"Eh? Isn't it obvious? It's good for you!"
					
					Rig drinks down the soup and looks pensive. "How strange. The situation doesn't feel as unnerving as it used to."
					
					Anurak smiles. "What did I say? A little soup will do you some good! And, of course, it's helping the little one that's resting in your stomach."
			
					Rig looks hesitant. "How long will this last?"
					
					Anurak shakes his head. "Don't be stupid! You can't just drink soup once and expect to be fine forever. It has to be a part of your diet."
					
					Rig looks annoyed. "Well, what am I supposed to do? I don't know how to make that kind of soup."
					
					Anurak makes a forceful beckon. "What's that? You want me to make you soup every day? Well, if you insist." 
			
					With a resigned sigh, Rig and Tintan decide to tag along. The other Rocks look somewhat displeased that the situation wasn't properly resolved.

choice.text: (Alkali) Invent a pretext to study this intriguing specimen.

event.text:
"Oh dear! Thhhhis won't do at all! I regret to inform you thhhhat thhhis patient cannot be operated on." The Rockmen look confused. "Yes, if we cut thhhhe patient open, thhhhe Zoltan might undergo a transphhhhasic rupture, destroying bothhhh patients. If you let me take a look at thhhhe specimen- er, patient, I will no doubt be able to come up withhh somethhhhing safer."
			
					The Rockmen seem concerned. "Aren't you going to leave?"
					
					Alkali nods. "We have very important business. But we will release thhhe patients upon curing thhhhem."
					
					The Rockmen sigh. "Fine. Payment on cure only, though." For the forseeable future, it looks like Tintan and Rig will be joining your crew. They're not happy about having to stick together, but at least with Alkali, they might have a chance for some proper treatment.
			
					Still, you could have sworn that Alkali muttered something under his breath that sounded like "Too easy".

choice.text: (Mind Control) Convince the two to live in symbiosis aboard your ship.

event.text: Even under the effects of the mind control, it takes a lot of convincing to get the two to agree with forever existing among one another. Their life forever changed, now remarkably for the better, they thank you, and even ask to join your crew. The Rock station is confused as to what has happened, but Rig seems certain this is the right option in his stupor and the Rockmen agree to let him go.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Convince the two to live in symbiosis aboard your ship.

event.text: Even under the effects of the mind control device, it takes a lot of convincing to get the two to agree with forever existing among one another. Their life forever changed, now remarkably for the better, they thank you, and even ask to join your crew. The Rock station is confused as to what has happened, but Rig seems certain this is the right option in his stupor and the Rockmen agree to let him go.

choice.text: (Surgeon Drone) Perform surgery on the Rockman.

event.text: Without hesitation, the surgeon drone bursts into the station and makes a beeline for the patient at top speed, knocking over any Rocks that stand in its way. It applies anaesthesia, and then precisely makes an incision in Rig's abdomen. It removes the shivering Tintan, sealing up the incision as soon as possible. As it finishes up its treatment on both patients, the Rockmen approach, impressed. "Considering the level of care administered, we are willing to give a healthy reward. Where did you find this technology?"

"Arr, me systems say it's not possible, but I'll give 'er a go anyway." A55 slashes open Rig with a swing of his hook. The Rock grunts in pain as A55 extracts the Zoltan, all the while administering aid with his limited Doctor Drone capabilities. It's a makeshift job, but he manages to close the wound and treat both patients. The Rockmen look at you with concern, but relent. "What you did seems risky. And is that a pirate drone...? No matter. You did what you said, so we'll give you a reward for it."

choice.text: Your Doctor drone isn't capable of performing surgery of this caliber.
Your Medic informs you that a field medic is not qualified for this job.
Your Shell Scientist doesn't have sufficient familiarity with Rock or Zoltan biology to keep both patients alive and healthy.

event.text: Your Mantis, ever assured of its abilities, pushes past the Rockmen and marches into the room where the "infected" Rockman is being held. In a single swipe, it cuts straight through the stomach. The convulsing Zoltan falls out, quivering on the ground. The makeshift Rock medical team rushes in to fix the injured Rockman and physiologically evaluate the Zoltan. They aren't pleased with your solution, but they pay you as promised anyways.

choice.text: Suggest they simply put them out of their collective misery.

event.text: "Your advice is worthless. We cannot simply assassinate both a high ranking Zoltan official and our own commander. We ask that you leave, and we will wait for a more helpful ship to arrive."

choice.text: Offer to try and perform surgery.

event.text: "Do you have any training in operating of either of the two species? Or any species at all?" You shake your head. "Then get lost. We will wait for someone who knows what they are doing to arrive."
You ignore the Rock station and carry on your way.

name: ROCK_HOMEWORLDS
text: This beacon has landed you concerningly close to a densely populated Rock planet. You double-take when the ship computer informs you that this is no ordinary Rock planet, but rather Vrachos IV, the home planet of the Rock race.

event.text: The ship computer informs you on a few other details. Vrachos IV was largely abandoned because the massive industrial mining on the planet's surface led to a disastrous lack of necessary natural resources. This city, the capital of the Rock civilization, is one of the only few that remains populated. It is under strict control by one of the five Rock Elders, Stonewall. His incredibly uncreative name goes well in line with his uncreative methods of punishing dissidents, which usually involve torture and public executions.
The city below is bustling with activity, and far in the distance lays Stonewall's palace, blocking out the sunrise. It's not the biggest building here, but it commands the most attention.
You came to this reality to make a change and the Rock government is no better than the Rebels. As you approach the palace however, a gigantic Rock cruiser exits, ready to combat you.
A giant Rock city is no place for a Federation ship. You power up the thrusters and back away from the planet's surface.

name: ROCK_HOMEWORLDS_VICTORY
text: No ship can outmatch you, not even a mighty Elite Rock Cruiser. Now defeated, the remains of the cruiser go down into flames, destroying the vast garden leading up to the Palace's entrance. It's plenty to scrap, but you don't have much time with the Rock soldiers running out to meet you.

event.text: Along with the Rockmen comes Stonewall himself, extremely irate at the damage you caused. "What have you done! You have proven your point, everywhere you go you only bring destruction and disrupt our ways of life! What is it that you want, why have you come here to ruin this day? Will simple money be enough to make you leave?"

Reluctantly, the Rock soldiers put down their guns and a hefty sum of scrap is brought out for you. This won't have much lasting effect on the Rock government other than an increase in security, but atleast this will help with your primary mission.

choice.text: Use Stonewall as a hostage and bargain for an even greater reward.
The ship AI suggests taking Stonewall as a hostage. Unfortunately, you lack a proper team for this option to be considered.
We came here to make a change. Assassinate Stonewall now.
You came here to make a change. Fire all weapons on Stonewall.

name: ROCK_HOMEWORLDS_VICTORY_KILL
text: You swiftly draw your blaster and blast Stonewall straight in the chest. The mighty titan of a creature falls to the ground in a thud, and the Rock soldiers are sent into chaos. You rush back to the ship but are stopped by the surge of Rock citizens breaking down the palace gates. A large horde of onlookers, witnessing your brave execution of their long-time brutal dictator, have been pushed to revolt, and they are stampeding to take down the soldiers.

event.text: It's a violent fight, and there's heavy casualties on both sides, but with your trained military crew you help sway the tide in the civilians' favor. Once the battle is for certain over, the civilians thank you for your help. Most march on to take control of Stonewall's palace, but one Rock, a Crusader who turned on his masters, stays behind. "You have done us a considerable service, and I cannot let this go without thanks. Our kind may finally be free from this oppression, and this could very well be the start. I want to stay behind and keep fighting, but I also know a Federation ship passing through here with such a powerful loadout has a very important mission awaiting them, and they can use all of the manpower they can get."

Hopefully this newfound spark of hope you've started among the Rock people won't be smothered by the reinforcements the other Elders are bound to send. You can't risk your mission any further, so you power up the engines and fly away from the city.

name: ROCK_HOMEWORLDS_VICTORY_KILL_AUTO
text: You aim the entire ship's array of weapons and fire at will on Stonewall's spot. It's a pretty brutal display, but the mighty titan of a creature is swiftly terminated under the barrage of your weaponry, and the Rock soldiers are sent into chaos. A large horde of onlookers, witnessing your brave execution of their long-time brutal dictator, have been pushed to revolt, and they are stampeding to take down the soldiers.

event.text: It's a violent fight, and there's heavy casualties on both sides, but with your menacing automated cruiser looming above, you help sway the tide in the civilians' favor. Once the battle is for certain over, the civilians thank you for your help. Most march on to take control of Stonewall's palace, but one Rock, a Crusader who turned on his masters, stays behind. "You have done us a considerable service, and I cannot let this go without thanks. Our kind may finally be free from this oppression, and this could very well be the start. I want to stay behind and keep fighting, but I also know a Federation ship passing through here with such a powerful loadout has a very important mission awaiting them, and they can use all of the manpower they can get."

Hopefully this newfound spark of hope you've started among the Rock people won't be smothered by the reinforcements the other Elders are bound to send. You can't risk your mission any further, so you power up the engines and fly away from the city.

name: FINISH_BEACON_UNEXPLORED

unvisitedTooltip.text: An unvisited location.

visitedTooltip.text: This is the exit beacon. Go here to travel to the next sector.

text: You've discovered the exit beacon out of the sector. Once the FTL drive is charged you'll be able to leave this sector.

name: NEBULA_FINISH_BEACON_UNEXPLORED

unvisitedTooltip.text: An unvisited location.

visitedTooltip.text: This is the exit beacon. Go here to travel to the next sector.

text: You've discovered the exit beacon out of the sector. Once the FTL drive is charged you'll be able to leave this sector.

name: UNEXPLORED_FRONTIER
text: A slightly worn down Union ship waits here. "Howdy, Renegade. We frontiersmen have been looking to settle on a quiet world far away from the war. We don't got a sophisticated sensor system like your fancy cruisers do, and our weapons aren't much to look at. We were hoping to settle a world 'round these parts... but as we got closer we thought we might have seen signs o' one of them pirates. D'ya reckon you could go check to see if it's safe?"

choice.text: (Upg. Sensors) Use your advanced sensors to get a detailed reading.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Use your scanners to get a detailed reading.
Agree to go investigate the area.

event.text: You decide to prey upon the ship. Since you're so far out and they're cut off from civilization, this action won't likely harm your reputation.

choice.text: Leave them to their own devices.

event.text: The voice on the other end mutters. "Can't depend upon anybody, I s'pose..."

name: UNEXPLORED_FRONTIER_SMUGGLER
text: A smuggler is situated in orbit around a nearby planet. As you draw close, they hail you. "You lookin' to do business, or make trouble?"

event.text: You make your answer clear by warming your weapons. "Trouble it is."

choice.text: Tell them about the settlers to gauge their reaction.

event.text: "Look, pal. We're just passing through. We have more important things to do than yanking some banjos away from hillbillies. Now do you want to buy something or not?"

choice.text: Buy a weapon from the smuggler.

event.text: Pleasure doin' business with ya, pal. I got some more stuff if you want to see it.

After you finish shopping, you return to the settlers to report on the situation. "...it was just a passin' smuggler? You're sure...? Well, I'm not going to argue with you, I guess. If they turn on us then that's on you, buddy."
"...it was just a passin' smuggler? You're sure...? Well, if you say so, I s'pose. If they turn on us then that's on you, partner."

choice.text: Tell them about the settlers to gauge their reaction.

event.text: "Yeah, so? Why should we care? Eye up our paint, buddy. We smugglers avoid drawing attention to ourselves." At this moment, you become aware that the planet the ship is in orbit around has a small hideout. "They wanna be our neighbors? We'll be quiet if they will. Now do you want to buy something or not?"

choice.text: Buy a weapon from the smuggler.

event.text: Pleasure doin' business with ya, pal. I got some more stuff if you want to see it.

After you finish shopping, you return to the settlers to report on the situation. "...A den o' smugglers? Well... that's a darn shame, but if ya'll are sayin' they're no threat, then we'll give 'er a go. If they turn on us then that's on you, partner."
"...A den o' smugglers? Well... that's a darn shame, but if ya'll are sayin' they're no threat, then we'll give 'er a go. If they turn on us then that's on you, partner."

name: UNEXPLORED_FRONTIER_SLAVER
text: Looks like a slaver is here. They're not immediately hostile, but if they remain in the area, the settlers will be captured.

event.text: The settlers will likely want them dead - and you're willing to help them out.

choice.text: Tip them off about the settlers, for a price.

event.text: You offer to sell them the location of a helpless ship. "Not bad, they should be ripe for the plundering. Here's your commission." After paying you, the slavers take off to harvest their prey.

choice.text: Leave them and report on your findings.

event.text: "...So there was a ship? And you didn't manage to destroy them? That's a pity... I guess we will look elsewhere for our settlement. This will be dangerous."

name: UNEXPLORED_FRONTIER_VAGABOND
text: At first, the "evidence of pirates" appears to be little more than debris from a wreck. However, once you get closer, it comes to life. It's a Vagabond ship, and they're hailing you. "For what purpose do you intrude upon our domain?"

event.text: No need to overcomplicate this, these Ghosts might pose a threat to the settlers.

choice.text: Ask them if the settlers can live on this planet.

event.text: "Wherefore this planetary body, far beyond any civilization?" You tell them that's why they want to come. "Truly, their actions are commendable. We had not taken action to settle this territory yet... perhaps, we may join them?"
"Vagabonds? Wantin' to help? My stars, things might be goin' our way after all!" The ship departs for the planet that they had come to settle.

choice.text: Ask them if the settlers can live on this planet.

event.text: "We have already claimed this territory! ...yet, there is no edict that decrees we cannot share. It is fine! They may come." You tell them that's why they want to come. "To strive through thine own means... Such wisdom. We are akin. We grant them sanctuary."
"Vagabonds? Offerin' us some good ol' fashioned hospitality? Things might be goin' our way after all!" The ship departs for the planet that they had come to settle.

name: UNEXPLORED_FRONTIER_OTHER_SETTLE_LOCATION
text: Instead of exploring the system, you use the data you've collected on the sector to find the absolute best place for the settlers to settle. Not only are you able to find a garden world and a perfect path to get them there, but doing so will also save them supplies due to the superior climate of the new planet you've found. "My stars! You've found an even better planet fer us? Yer a legend! I reckon we owe you a little more gratitude than we're capable of givin'!" As they said, they give you all that they can.

name: UNEXPLORED_PIRATE_INVESTIGATE_NONE
text: You can tell that there is no pirate ships in the area. Not only that, but the data that you gather shows that there is a string of debris - and using your computer's extrapolation, you manage to discover a large bounty of debris! You can scrap this once you're done helping the settlers.

choice.text: Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: It seems like the planet itself is safe too. With all this information at your fingertips, you send them all the data that you've collected. "Mighty kind o' you to go the extra mile, there pardner! This place seems ideal for settlin'. Here's a little something for your trouble."

choice.text: Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: As it happens, there are already settlers on this planet, who seem to have had a similar idea. The settlement seems entirely peaceful. You send this data to the settlers who have contacted you. "Boy howdy, I wasn't 'specting such a turn o' events. Still, I'd reckon a whole planet's big enough fer the two 'a us. Thanks a bundle."

name: UNEXPLORED_PIRATE_INVESTIGATE_SMUGGLER
text: Your ship's readings say that there is a smuggler at this location.

choice.text: Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: Although there is a smuggler, they are alone, and likely only in the area for a short time.

choice.text: Spend time using your map data to find a better place for them to settle.
Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: The planet the smuggler is in orbit around has a smuggler's hideaway. Even if the ship is destroyed, the smugglers will still maintain a presence in the area.

choice.text: Spend time using your map data to find a better place for them to settle.

name: UNEXPLORED_PIRATE_INVESTIGATE_SLAVER
text: Your ship's readings say that there is a slaver at this location.

choice.text: Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: Although there is a slaver, they are alone, and likely only in the area for a short time.

choice.text: Spend time using your map data to find a better place for them to settle.
Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: The planet the slaver is in orbit around has a slaver's hideaway. Even if the ship is destroyed, the smugglers will still maintain a presence in the area.

choice.text: Spend time using your map data to find a better place for them to settle.

name: UNEXPLORED_PIRATE_INVESTIGATE_VAGABOND
text: Your ship's readings say that there is a ship wreck occupied by Vagabond Ghosts at this location.

choice.text: Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: The Vagabond ship is the only sign of intelligent life in the sector, however.

choice.text: Spend time using your map data to find a better place for them to settle.
Collect data on the planet's surface.

event.text: The Vagabonds seem to be settling the planet's surface.

choice.text: Spend time using your map data to find a better place for them to settle.

name: UNEXPLORED_VAGABOND_AFTERMATH
text: "Vagabonds? That don't bother me one bit. I ain't 'fraid of no ghosts!"

name: UNEXPLORED_FRONTIER_NONE
text: The "evidence of pirates" appears to be little more than debris from a wreck long past. While the quality has degraded, it's still scrap that you can harvest.

event.text: "There weren't no pirates? Just flotsam? Whew! We'll begin settlin' immediately. Here's a reward for your efforts." The ship departs for the planet that they had come to settle.

name: UNEXPLORED_PIRATE_NO_SETTLEMENT_AFTERMATH
text: After disposing of the pirate and dispatching their ship, the area is clear. There is no pirate hideaway here - this should answer any follow up questions the Frontiersman has.

event.text: "So there WAS a pirate. Thanks for handling them for us. Hopefully none o' their friends come looking for them..."

name: UNEXPLORED_PIRATE_SETTLEMENT_AFTERMATH
text: After disposing of the pirate and dispatching their ship, you find the hideaway that the pirates had been staying at. This area is likely too dangerous to settle, especially after you just killed one of them.

event.text: "A pirate hideout...? All the good planets done been scooped up already, I reckon. Back to the drawin' board..."

name: UNEXPLORED_ORCHID
text: An Orchid ship resides here. "Renegade! We need you to help us out. One of our people went missing in this nebula. We Orchids don't like nebulas very much, that's why we're taking a break out here. Sure, some of us are willing to put in the work to explore them, but we need to photosynthesize, and nebulas tend to get in the way. Anyway, you'll be able to search it much faster than we can. Think you can help us out?"

choice.text: Tell them you'll keep an eye out.

event.text: "Thank you! Here is the data you need on the missing person. Once you zero in on the target, we'll meet you there!"
The Orchids frantically turn their comms off as you attack them.

choice.text: Tell them there isn't much you can do for them.

event.text: "We understand."

name: UNEXPLORED_ORCHID_FOUND_AUTO_DESTROYED
text: "You... you can't make me go back! They... they'll never accept me once they find out the truth!" The Orchid sighs. "I... I tried a human salad. And... it was good. Carrots. Lettuce. Tomatoes... They're tasty... and so I kept eating them... And then I got to wondering... how the plants on Rt'lak Et tasted..." The Orchid shivers. "They'll find out what I've done! I can't go back!"

event.text: You hold the Orchid until the ship comes back. As the other Orchid ship comes in, they notice the destroyed Auto-ship. "What happened here...? Clearly we will have to look into this further. Thank you for helping us find the missing person. Here's the other half of your reward!"

choice.text: Offer sanctuary and leave before the Orchids arrive.

event.text: "Really? We'd better get out of here fast. Please avoid Gathering space if you can!"

name: NEBULA_UNEXPLORED_ORCHID_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: According to your readouts, the missing Orchid may be at this location.

text: Your ship tells you that you've found the location of the missing person. A lone Orchid hails you. "Dammit! I've been found! Leave me alone!" As he screams at you, a Federation Auto-ship attacks you, as if to keep you away!

name: UNEXPLORED_SEPARATIST_ONLY
text: The binary stars that this beacon orbits around have no natural satellites. No planets, no asteroids, nothing. However, there is a single Separatist ship.

event.text: You hail the Separatist. They reply somewhat gruffly. "The Harmony hasn't -looked- in this region. Just want to be [left] alone. These stars... remind of -something-. Something better." The Separatist pauses and then repeats. "Something -better-..." After a few moments the Separatist speaks up again. "Do you have [anything] destructive that might aid -seclusion-?"

choice.text: (Beacon Eater) Offer to eat the beacon to ensure their privacy.

event.text: "Impressive, never even considered it. Please, -demonstrate-." The Beacon Eater devours the beacon, devouring enough of it that any further damage will collapse it. "My freedom is finally [assured]...? It seems unbelievable. Please, take this gift. I will -finish- the job after you leave... eventually. Might look around the sector one last time before I do."

"You know, there are some Separatists who visit the Stargrove for just the same purpose as you coming here. Maybe you should join up with your kin that have made that same decision?"

					"Stargrove... a [very] useful suggestion. Other Separatists have -found- answers there? Then we [will] go. -Appreciate- it."

choice.text: (Mine Launcher) Offer to lay mines to protect from the Harmony.

event.text: "Agreed. Show me how you plan to do this." You deploy your Mine Launcher to wall off the beacon such that any attempt to stray from the beacon will damage a ship, leaving just enough of a gap to slip through before finishing the job - you would prefer to take a reward after all.
"This should be effective. I hope this reward is suitable." Once they give you their material reward, you finish the mining job. Time to move on.
"Appreciated. Can -program- drone to deliver Magnetic [Payload] directly to Harmony vessels." The Separatist trades you an ion weapon, and gives a small tip as well.
"Appreciated. Though, it will take work."
The ship begins to take evasive maneuvers. It seems ready to fight!
The solitary ship makes no moves, providing an opportunity to do something on your own.
The ship begins to take evasive maneuvers. It seems ready to fight!
The solitary other ship makes no moves, providing an opportunity to do something on your ship.

name: UNEXPLORED_MAROONED_OUTCASTS
text: A nearby unsettled planet has a crash site. It seems to have been a Theocracy Jailer.

event.text: Going down to the crash site, you find a small encampment of outcasts. Upon learning you are not affiliated with the Theocracy, they invite you to have a meal with them. Their leader speaks up. "We crashed this ship onto this world a few months ago, and they haven't come 'round. We don't even know if they were looking for us. We're just happy to be free." He pauses. "However, since you are able to find us, this means we might be discovered some day. We either need to find out what's wrong with the cloaking device that we salvaged from the ship, or we need some munitions."

choice.text: (Cloaking) Let them look at your working cloaking device.

event.text: You show them your cloaking system, and using it as a reference point, your crew and their encampment are able to fix up their broken cloaking device. "Amazing! Now we can hide ourselves whenever they come near. We'll give you something that we set aside in case we had to fight."

choice.text: Offer them a large stockpile of munitions. [-15}]

event.text: The village head is pleased. "Thank you, we will make good use of this." They reward you with some of the scrap that had been left over from the crash and a derelict weapon they can no longer use.

choice.text: (Explosive Replicator) Synthesize a stockpile of munitions. [-7}]

event.text: The village head is pleased. "Thank you, we will make good use of this." They reward you with some of the scrap that had been left over from the crash and a derelict weapon they can no longer use.

choice.text: Offer them passage on your ship.

event.text: The outcasts seem to be attached to this land they've been working on, but they relent and decide to take passage on your ship and get off at the next neutral station. One of them decides that the safest place would be on your crew.
"So there is nothing you can do? Well, we have time. Hopefully we can prepare for the Theocracy in some way or another."
You take this opportunity to rest.

name: NEBULA_FEDERATION_GIFT
text: A Federation ship is exploring the nebula here. "A friendly face? It's dangerous to go alone! Take this!" The nearby Federation vessel dispenses a weapon for your aid.

choice.text: Thank them and do something aboard the ship.

event.text: You thank the Federation ship and move your new weapon into the cargo.
You power up your weapons and prepare to engage the ship.

name: NEBULA_NEW_PLANET
text: To your surprise, there is no nebula at this beacon at all. The beacon appears to be freshly made, and the people who placed it here likely made a mistake with labeling it. In the distance is a large, unexplored and unpopulated planet, suggesting this location is desired for colonization.

event.text: You pull closer to the surface of the planet, revealing a few distinct features. A large ravine running along the planet's surface, a crater along with the asteroid responsible for it, and an expansive flat region with few noticeable landmarks, at least not from this high up.

You can officially add spelunking to the list of things you didn't expect to be doing on this mission. The trip goes smoothly, and on your way you encounter several valuable looking gems which you'll no doubt be able to make some scrap off of.
The asteroid left a considerable amount of rubble in its wake, and large portions of harvestable material have been exposed. You'll be able to refine this into fuel back on the ship.
After some exploring it becomes clear that you aren't the first ship to have explored this planet. A ship has crashed here, and the survivor is thankful for you rescuing them.
You'll leave the exploration to people with with more time on their hands. Who makes these beacons anyways?

name: NEBULA_SIGNAL
text: This beacon appears to be empty, but you're detecting a very weak, looping encrypted signal from in the nebula.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug decode the signal.

event.text: The signal is difficult to decode, but you're able to break it. It appears to be the location for a pirate cache on a nearby planet!

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell decode the signal.

event.text: The signal is difficult to decode, but you're able to break it. It appears to be the location for a pirate cache on a nearby planet!

choice.text: (Cognitive Crew) Have your Cognitive decode the signal.

event.text: The signal is difficult to decode, but you're able to break it. It appears to be the location for a pirate cache on a nearby planet!
You don't have time to try and figure out this signal.

name: NEBULA_SIGNAL_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of a pirate cache.

text: The cache is filled with supplies and even a brand new weapon! Unfortunately, it seems another pirate vessel has also come looking for the cache. A fight is unavoidable.

name: NEBULA_TRADER
text: It's hard to see why, but this beacon is apparently a tourist destination. One of the ships at the small station is offering a deal.

event.text: You have no need for their services.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_PIRATE_STATION
text: The nebula at this beacon is thinner than usual. A pirate station is operating nearby, though it doesn't appear to receive much business.

event.text: The pirates show you several crates of supplies that they are offering.
This station is run by filthy pirates and was likely stolen. You'll be doing justice by killing them.
Whatever illegal services the pirates could offer, you aren't interested.

name: NEBULA_STORM_PLATFORM
text: Nearby lies a dormant Slug cealaforming station. They must have been harvesting the nebulous gases when the ion storm started, and have now taken refuge in the station. Next to it is a platform, unprotected.

choice.text: Raid the platform while the Slugs are hiding.
The storm is too much of a risk. Ignore the platform.

name: NEBULA_STORM_ITEMS
text: You jump into the middle of a plasma storm. Multiple recently incapacitated ships loom in the shadows, briefly illuminated by the lightning.

choice.text: Manually search the wreckage for survivors and equipment.
You have no crew to send out to plunder any remains left.
Avoid the risk and wait to jump away unscathed.
(Upg. Piloting) Have your pilot carefully explore the debris.
(Scrap Arm) Use your Scrap Arm to collect some of the wreckage.
(Magnet Arm) Use your Magnet Arm to collect some of the wreckage.

name: NEBULA_DUEL
text: There may not be sound in space, but the flashing from deep in the nebula suggest a battle is being raged, but you aren't sure by whom.

event.text: You aren't willing to take the risk to get involved in the conflict.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_HUNTER
text: A pirate ship hails you. "We have an offer for you, if you're interested in some scrap."

event.text: "This sector ain't a friendly place. You know why? Slugs. Filthy bastards, good for nothin' except making punching bags out of. Interested in killing some for us?"
"Excellent! Follow us..." They lead you to a nearby Slug ship. "Kill these ones, and you'll have an excellent reward awaiting you!"

choice.text: (Nights) "Good point! How about a gift, fellow hater?"

event.text: Nights' impersonation of a Rockman is pretty impressive. The pirates believe it. Shortly after you hear a sharp scream from their crew as the gift wrapped bomb he sent them explodes. They scramble to attack you.

choice.text: (Slocknog) Feign interest while Slocknog hails the Slugs.

event.text: "Excellent! Follow us..." They lead you to a nearby Slug ship. By the time you arrive, the Slug is ready for a fight. You have no difficulty flanking and destroying the pirates.

"Good looking out for usss, Ssslocknog."

Slocknog smiles. "We're on a sssensitive missssion. Would any of you like to help?"

A volunteer from the Slug ship agrees to accompany you.

Sylvan calmly, but menacingly offers to let them reconsider their words. "My god, you let one of th-"
					
					A crewmate stops them. "Wait! Isn't that... Sylvan? The Merchant?" The bravado quickly fades from the pirates. "L-look! We didn't mean nothin' by it! We'll give you all we can spare! Just don't kill us!"
"No no no no!" The pirates panic at the prospect of having to fight Sylvan.

choice.text: (Irwin) "How 'bout a duel? Ten pacesss, turn and draw. Winner takessss all."

event.text:
The pirate grimaces. "Loath as I am to lay eyes on a Slug, if you want me to be the one that kills you, then I'll do it." Irwin and the pirate stand at either side of the airlocks connecting your ship. They take 10 steps and... "Draw!"
					
					Irwin turns around, shooting the pirate before he can even get his gun up. He notices that the pirate behind him also draws his and shoots him as well. The rest of the pirates put their hands up, clearly defeated. You take what you can from their ship.

choice.text: (Billy) "I ssshould hire ssssomeone to kick your asss for that! Or better yet, I'll do it myssself!"

event.text: "Yuck, the only thing worse than a Slug is a rich Slug. You sicken me."

choice.text: (Slug Crew) "You talk a lot of trassssh for sssomeone in tentacle ssslapping dissssstance."

event.text: "My god, you let one of those filthy creatures live on your ship? You are disgraceful!"
You ignore the pirates.

name: NEBULA_SLUG_HUNTER_WIN
text: You've defeated the Slug vessel. The pirates wait for you to finish scrapping the ship.

event.text: "Good work, you have done this sector a great service. Your reward..."

name: NEBULA_WHALE
text: A large blip on the radar is detecting a massive ship moving around this nebula. Its giant size suggests it may even be a fleet ship.

event.text: You dive deeper into the nebula, and are swatted out of the way by a giant tail! Luckily no harm comes to the ship, but you're left in shock. The object you detected was no fleet ship at all, but rather a humongous space whale!

choice.text: Explore the insides of the whale.

event.text: Space whales are cool, but they aren't worth wasting any time on.
If a fleet ship is lost this far out in the nebula, it's very likely of Rebel design, and you should avoid it at all costs.

name: NEBULA_MINE_WRECK
text: The husk of an emptied Trapper vessel drifts into the nebula. Around it lie a few mines, but it's hard to tell whether they're still active.

event.text: Scrapping the wreck isn't worth accidentally activating the mines. You move on.

name: NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED_MV
text: Your ship emerges quite far away from the beacon. You see a Rebel ship waiting nearby, undoubtedly stationed to look for you.

event.text: You raise your weapons and engage the Rebel ship.
You use your cloaking system to slip further into the nebula undetected.

name: NEBULA_PIRATE_SMUGGLE_MV
text: A smuggler ship arrives shortly after you. Judging from the fact that it is attempting to avoid your ship, you assume that it's trying to hide deeper in the nebula.

event.text: You power up your weapons and move in to engage.
It jumps away after a time.

choice.text: (Adv. Weapons) Activate your advanced weapons threateningly.

event.text: They hail you, "There's no need for aggression... Perhaps this would convince you to look the other way?"
You prepare to engage the Smugglers.

name: NEBULA_AUTO_DEFENSE_ITEM_MV
text: An advance Rebel automated ship remains stationed near a small Rebel space-station. However, without functioning sensors it is impossible to tell what is inside.

choice.text: Attack the automated ship to get to the station.

event.text: You prepare to engage the automated vessel.
You distance yourself from the ship.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Attempt to stealthily access the space station.
(Upg. Cloaking) Use your stealth to access the space station.

event.text: You successfully sneak by the ship and access the station undetected.

choice.text: (Hacking) Try to hack the station to prevent an alert.
(Hacking Weapon) Target the station's alarm with your hacking weapon.
(Upg. Hacking) Hack the station to prevent an alert.

event.text: You successfully hack into the station and sever the connection to the automated ship, accessing the station completely undetected.

name: NEBULA_LOST_SHIP_MV
text: A heavily damaged Federation ship is hiding in the nebula at this beacon. Before you have time to make contact with them, they fade into the nebula.

choice.text: Attempt to follow and help them.
Keep your position, they can handle themselves.

event.text: The ship never resurfaces, leaving you alone at the beacon.

choice.text: (Teleporter) Lock onto their life-signs with your teleporter.

event.text: You beam the Federation crew aboard. One gladly joins your crew, the rest wait to be dropped off at the next station.

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Pump extra power into your sensors and try to track them.

name: NEBULA_ROCK_RACIST_MV
text: A Rock armoured transport nearby looks to have lost its bearings, but when you hail they grow suspicious: "Whatever life-form you are, we find you repugnant. We seek no aid. Leave. Now."

event.text: You prepare to fight.

choice.text: (Rock Crew) Offer to lead them out of the nebula.

event.text: The Rock grudgingly transfer control of their helm to you and you steer them to a thinner part of the nebula. They're not sure what to think, but transfer over some supplies all the same.

name: NEBULA_MANTIS_CHOICE_MV
text: Navigating the fog blind, you practically bump hulls with a Mantis ship. They hail you: "Pah! This transgression will be overlooked. Nebula, very dangerous. Next time, Feds all die."

choice.text: There won't be a next time. Open fire!

event.text: You prepare to fight.

choice.text: This place is dangerous enough. Move on.

event.text: The Mantis ship jumps away after a short time.

name: NEBULA_REBEL_CHASE_MV
text: You spot a Rebel ship in the nebula ahead and stay off their radar. Try to engage?

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Try to track them as you move to engage.

event.text: As soon as they see you they make a run for it. You squeeze what you can out of the malfunctioning sensors and are able to keep track of them long enough to get in firing range.

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Try to track them as you move to engage.

event.text: As soon as they see you they make a run for it. You squeeze what you can out of the malfunctioning sensors and are able to keep track of them long enough to get in firing range.

choice.text: (Lifeform Scanner) Use their life signatures to follow.

event.text: Your augment's ability to keep track of their life signatures within the nebula proves useful. You catch up to the ship and prepare for a fight.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your crewmember check for their life signatures to follow them.

event.text: With the help of your crewmember, you're able to track down the Rebel ship. They opt to engage you instead of trying to flee again.

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Have your crewmember check for their life signatures to follow them.

event.text: With the help of your crewmember, you're able to track down the Rebel ship. They opt to engage you instead of trying to flee again.
You try and stay out of sight. You doubt they saw you.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_WATER_PLANET
text: Through the clearing in the nebula here you can see a large water planet, from which there appears to be 10 separate distress calls. A large cubical structure can be seen from the planet's surface. It's inactive, and you can't tell what it is from this distance.

event.text: It appears that all of the distress beacons are originating from the same area, a large crater with a massive ship wreck. The structure you noticed earlier begins to unfold, revealing itself to be a large gun! You won't have much time until it starts firing on you, so you'll have to pull away now if you want to avoid damage.

choice.text: We can take a few hits, pull in closer to inspect the wreck.

event.text: While the giant cannon charges, you investigate the wreck. It's huge, probably the size of one of the Rebel fleet ships, if not a little bigger. Suddenly, a giant beam fires from the structure, tearing through the ship's engines! It's quite the scratch, but you'll be able to fix it.

choice.text: (Obelisk Crew) Your crew desperately needs to tell you something.

event.text: Your crew explains the structure on the planet below is a massive anti-aircraft gun meant to enforce a strict quarantine over the planet. Somehow it has remained functional for a millenia, and with their help you temporarily deactivate the artillery remotely so you can approach safely.
Something isn't right about this planet. You power up the engines and pull away.

name: WATER_PLANET_LAND
text: On the planet's surface you find a crashed life pod with an engineer inside, surprisingly still alive. Once they're stabilized, you figure you might as well investigate the area around while you wait.

name: WATER_PLANET_INVESTIGATE
text: A gigantic leviathan class creature patrols the waters around the wreckage, but you're able to sneak around it. Though most of the ship is on fire, you find a lot of fire extinguishers lying around, a tablet like device with sector maps, and a hangar bay with some mech suits.

event.text: You grab as many fire extinguishers as you can. It's definitely not what you expected, coming here, but you'll take it.
A female voice comes from the device, saying something about 'emergency mode', but you ignore it and download the data.

choice.text: Grab some scrap and parts from the hangar.

event.text: The suits are in disrepair, which is fortunate for you. You salvage as much as you can carry.

choice.text: (Adv. Weapons) Fire everything you have on the leviathan.

event.text: It's entirely pointless but cathartic as you unleash every weapon you have on the creature. Most of your shots miss or are rendered worthless by the water but you'd like to think you showed that fish who's boss.
With the creature out of the way what will you do next?
You grab as many fire extinguishers as you can. It's definitely not what you expected, coming here, but you'll take it.
A female voice comes from the device, saying something about 'emergency mode', but you ignore it and download the data.

choice.text: Grab some scrap and parts from the hangar.

event.text: The suits are in disrepair, which is fortunate for you. You salvage as much as you can carry.

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_DEATH_BY_GAS
text: A civilian ship desperately hails you. "The space gas- gas too thick- oxygen system damaged- too much... gas..."

choice.text: Unfortunate for the civilians, but you cannot risk helping them, unless you can pinpoint their location.

event.text: Only one life signature is detected on board, but you beam them back with your teleporter. The civilian explains that an encounter with a pirate led to a breach in their life support and a technical malfunction. Nebulous gases were sucked into their ship and the crew all suffocated. Now that they are the only survivor and their ship is worthless, they offer to work aboard yours.

choice.text: (Lifeform Scanner) Lock onto the civilians and quickly rescue them.

event.text: It appears you're mostly too late, as only one life sign is detected. Still, you hurry to bring them back onto your ship. The civilian explains that an encounter with a pirate led to a breach in their life support and a technical malfunction. Nebulous gases were sucked into their ship and the crew all suffocated. Now that they are the only survivor and their ship is worthless, they offer to work aboard yours.

choice.text: (Anaerobic Crew) Send in your crew to help.

event.text: Without any fear of suffocation, you send in your anaerobic crew to assist. The civilian explains that an encounter with a pirate led to a breach in their life support and a technical malfunction. Nebulous gases were sucked into their ship and the crew all suffocated. Now that they are the only survivor and their ship is worthless, they offer to work aboard yours.
You can't waste time helping the civilians. You move past them.

name: NEBULA_DISTRESS_SEARCH
text: The distress beacon here is emitting from a small ship requesting aid in finding someone.

event.text: You can't waste time helping the ship. You move past them.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_ENCOUNTER_REBEL_LIGHTNEBULA
text: This beacon has a clearing from the nebula, revealing more of the distant space. However, it appears a Rebel ship has already arrived and is now approaching quickly!

name: NEBULA_STORM_REBEL
text: You arrive in the middle of a plasma storm. Despite the harsh conditions, a Rebel scout seems to be waiting for you.

name: NEBULA_STORM_AUTO
text: You jump into a sector of the nebula beset by a plasma storm. An automated Rebel ship stationed at the beacon moves in to attack.

event.text: You prepare for combat.
You successfully lose the ship in the storm.
By using your advanced cloaking system you easily lose your pursuer in the storm.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_ENCOUNTER_SUN
text: It seems that the nebula here has condensed into a newly born star. It's quite the spectacle... but also very deadly. A Slug vessel is admiring the star, but upon seeing you decides to attack instead!

name: NEBULA_STORM_BOARDING
text: You find two heavily damaged ships floating nearby, the remains of a battle. You begin to harvest some usable debris when you hear the sounds of someone beaming aboard followed by the shouts of a boarding party.

name: UNION_BREACH
text: A Union vessel, severely damaged from a huge hull breach, desperately hails you. They explain that they barely managed to escape from a pirate. They need to transfer crew over to a different ship.

choice.text: (Rock Crew) Let them aboard but station your Rock as extra security.
(Soldier Crew) Let them aboard but station your Soldier as extra security.
(Hive Elite) Let them aboard but station your Mantis as extra security.
(Boarding Drone) Let them aboard but station your drone as extra security.
(Adv. Sensors) Let them aboard but keep constant scans running on them.

event.text: You explain your mission is too important to be transporting civilians. They're clearly distressed but are powerless to do anything but accept this.

name: UNION_FREEMANTIS
text: You're contacted by a Free Mantis ship, piloted by a rather lost looking captain. "Oh, great greeting. You not yet run away, so I assume you friendly. We come here by mistake, looking for Federation sector to enroll in military. Now, we hunted by Militia. Very unfortunate. Think you could do favor and convince Militia we good?"

choice.text: Agree to track down the Militia ship hunting them.

event.text: "Much appreciate, friend." You follow their directions and find the Militia ship has already arrived in this system. They haven't noticed you.

"Yeah, what do you want?" You explain the Free Mantis ship they're hunting is only trying to pass through the sector peacefully. He rolls his eyes. "A Zoltan reported that there was a Mantis causing trouble in the area. We'll arrest that bug, obviously. What do you expect us to do?"
The Militia ship is bound to cave in if you can do enough damage to their hull. You ready the weapons.

choice.text: (Free Mantis Crew) Talk to the Militiamen.

event.text: Your Free Mantis walks onto the camera, waving with a big goofy grin. The Militiamen however, are not quite so pleased. "You may be fooled by their sickening facade, but we will never forget! What did all those men and women die for in the Fed-Mantis war if we're just letting the Mantis work alongside us now? You are the reason this galaxy, hell, this Multiverse has gone to shit." They end the call immediately and attack!
"Ugh, fine. This will go badly, mark my words. If they cause any more trouble, we'll have no choice but to kill them."

choice.text: Go back to the Free Mantis.

event.text: If you've learned anything on your mission, it's that the best way to deal with problems is through brutal murder. You power up the weapons and prepare to destroy the Militia ship.
"Ah. Very well. Best luck on mission!"

name: UNION_FREEMANTIS_WIN
text: You've killed the Militia ship. You've saved the Free Mantis for now, and scrap the remains of the Militia ship.

choice.text: Go back to the Free Mantis.

event.text: "You... you kill them? W-why? That unnecessary. We not want dead civilians. We just want safe travels. Still... you save us. I pay you as thanks, but hope you not do this in future."

name: UNION_FREEMANTIS_SURRENDER
text: The Militia ship is near destruction. The captain looks at you desperately. "What... are you serious? You're going to kill us for some bloody Mantis?"

choice.text: Let the Free Mantis go and we'll spare you.

event.text: "Jeez, you people are insane. But fine, we'll let them through. These Mantis refugees will be the deaths of us all..."

choice.text: Go back to the Free Mantis.

name: UNION_FREEMANTIS_REWARD
text: "Many thanks! You have done great favor for us. We in debt to you captain. How can repay you?"

event.text: The Free Mantis aren't very good at repairs, but they all work together and manage to repair a decent portion of your hull.
The Free Mantis transfer over some fuel.
The Free Mantis gladly hand over a portion of their scrap stores to you.

name: UNION_EFFICIENCY_ENGINEER
text: A nearby Union ship sends out a transmission boasting that they can upgrade certain weapons to be more power efficient. It will likely be expensive.

event.text: The engineer offers to upgrade the following weapons.

choice.text: Upgrade your Anti-Hull Laser Mk III.

event.text: You give the weapon to the engineer, allowing him to work on it.
After a short time, your weapon is returned to you, clad with an optimization.

choice.text: Upgrade your Frost Laser Mk II.

You turn down the offer and continue on your way.
The engineer unfortunately informs you that you have no compatible weapons that he can work on. You thank him anyway, and waste no further time.
You power up your weapons, signaling your hostile intent.
You turn down the offer and continue on your way.

name: UNION_OUTCAST_REFUGEES
text:
There is a heated argument going on at this beacon. An outcast ship escorting an unarmed transport is standing off against a Militia ship. Their chatter is on an open channel.

"...and they have nowhere else to go!"

"Not our problem! You think we can just let your people intrude upon our homes, spouting your crazy nonsense?"

"You do not listen! We are apostates! We are open to learning your customs if it will give us somewhere to live."

"Yeah, that's how it starts. And then you start taking offense to our ideas and replacing it with your own. We're not that naive!"

event.text:
Tuco slams the wall as his voice booms into the comm. "WHAT AM I LOOKING AT HERE?"

"Who... who are you?" The patrol asks.

Their question is answered by the other ship. "The Dread Pirate Tuco! He's come to help us!"

"Oh crap, the Dread Pirate? This is way above my paygrade... Fine! You can stay. Just... Just don't make a mess!" The Militia patrol warps out.

"The Dread Pirate Tuco has saved us! Hail Tuco, our savior!" The outcasts cheer on your ship and lavish you with as much as they can in tribute. Tuco chuckles as he takes a swig. "When you're that good, your reputation alone can do it for you."

choice.text: (Outcast Crew) Recommend that the outcasts continue along.

event.text:
Your crewmember hails the escort and suggests that they continue moving.

"We have come so far, and are always told to keep going."

Your outcast tells them that they will find what they are looking for, but not here. The captain relents, and the ships leave.

choice.text: Recommend that the outcasts continue along.
Accuse the patrol of being prejudiced.

event.text: The Outcast responds to your hostile actions by powering weapons.
You've heard enough. This Militia ship seems unreasonable. They are surprised at your sudden attack and respond in kind.
Their shouting match is none of your business.

name: MILITIA_OUTCAST_REFUGEES_LEFT
text: "I'm impressed. I thought those pesky refugees would never leave. Don't worry, we'll pay you for your time." The captain sends you a small amount of resources.

name: MILITIA_OUTCAST_REFUGEES_LEFT_DEAD_ESCORT
text: The Militia patrol sends a message. "Not that we aren't grateful for stepping in, but that was a little excessive, wasn't it?"

name: MILITIA_OUTCAST_REFUGEES_STAY_VIOLENCE
text: The leader of the refugees hails you. "Wherever we go, violence seems to follow. Is that the natural state of the world? Still, we are appreciative for you taking our side. We can only hope this doesn't backfire onto us."

name: MILITIA_OUTCAST_REFUGEES_STAY
text: The leader of the refugees hails you. "We thank you for sticking up for us. Maybe now we can actually live our lives in peace. We will provide you what we can for helping us."

name: UNION_DRUNK
text: A Union ship accosts you. "Hey! You... jerk!" The owner of the ship seems to be intoxicated. "This whooooole war thing. This is your fault! Yoooouuu... Renegade. None of this rebellion woulda happened if it wasn't for... you know... the Federation being dumb and slow. Now my business is slumping because yooooou and your multiversal war are getting in the way!"

choice.text: (Nights) "Your businesssss isss failing becausssse you SSSSUCK."

event.text:
The drunk tries to respond, but before he can, Nights cuts him off. "Oh, you're jusssst failing becausssse the timessss are bad, it'ssss not your fault? Let me guessss, before the Rebelssss it wassss your wife. Or maybe your competitor did ssssomething unfair? Sssshut up, you're jusssst a failure. Own it."

"But I... but you..." The man tries desperately to counter Nights, but he falters. The sound of stumbling footsteps can be heard as one of the other men on the ship tends to the comms. "Well, I think you did us all a favor for that. Why don't we just give you this and we'll both be on our way?"

choice.text: Engage him with a well reasoned debate.

event.text: You explain to him the importance of your mission, but he completely dismisses all of your well-formulated arguments with the standard variety of fallacies. You politely attempt to inform him of his fallacious reasoning, but for some strange and unknowable reason, this doesn't get through to the angry drunk man. You realise this is leading nowhere and leave the ship and its rants behind.
You engage in a tiring shouting match with the guy. Eventually, something that you say strikes a nerve. He attacks!

choice.text: Threaten to blow his ship to pieces.
Actually blow his ship to pieces.

event.text: "AND THERE IT IS! Look everyone, I'm being repressed!" The Union ship returns fire!
The ship continues to broadcast nasty words at you, but you pay it no mind.

name: UNION_MINING
text: It appears a civilian mining operation is being held in an asteroid field nearby. There are perimeter markers surrounding the field informing unsanctioned personnel that they shouldn't enter the region.

event.text: Most of the ships have docked with a nearby outpost out of reach of the asteroid field, but one ship is still in the process of mining some asteroids.
You move in to attack the mining ship.

choice.text: (Mining Beam) Mine some of the asteroids on the outskirts.

event.text: You use your beam to gather a decent supply of scrap and fuel from the asteroid field.

choice.text: (Beam Drone) Mine some of the asteroids on the outskirts. [-1|]

event.text: You use your drone to gather a decent supply of scrap and fuel from the asteroid field.

choice.text: (Scrap Arm) Mine some of the asteroids on the outskirts.

event.text: You use your drone to gather a decent supply of scrap and fuel from the asteroid field.

choice.text: (Mining Drone) Mine some of the asteroids on the outskirts. [-1|]

event.text: You use your drone to gather a decent supply of scrap and fuel from the asteroid field.
You have no interest in the mining operation.

name: UNION_MINING_CONFRONT
text: Before you can leave, the harvester from earlier notices you. "Hey! What do you think you're doing? This is a restricted area, we can't just have random ships barging in here like they own the place!" You can tell that your ship being significantly larger than theirs is the only reason they're not attacking outright.

event.text: You're not going to let anybody tell you what to do, regardless of the legality behind it. The Union ship doesn't hesitate to defend themselves.
You turn off the comms and prepare to jump. Even if nobody actually died here, you doubt your actions would do much to improve the reputation that Renegades have garnered in the Union.
You transfer some scrap you collected over to their ship. They barely hesitate before accepting it and clearing you to leave the field.

name: UNION_MINING_DESTROY
text: It appears the mining ship was carrying large fuel stores. One of your shots must have ignited the cargo bay, because the mining ship explodes. Luckily your ship isn't harmed, but none of their cargo survived. You quickly scrap what's left before reinforcements arrive.

name: UNION_MINING_KILL
text: With the mining ship crew dead, you find large stores of fuel onboard.

name: UNION_FACTORY
text: A small partially automated weapon factory lies in the distance. It's protected by a single Militia ship.

choice.text: Hail the factory and ask if they need anything.

event.text: One of the staff of the factory responds. "You wanna help? We have a delivery to make, but our courier is behind schedule. We have some replacement parts that need to be delivered to an anti-ship battery on a nearby world. Are you up for it?"
"Get to it when you can. They'll pay for your delivery fee."

choice.text: Apologize, the destination is too far out of the way.

event.text: You apologize and end the call.

choice.text: Hail the factory and ask if they need anything.

event.text: They don't respond to your hails.

choice.text: Attack the guard to get to the factory.

event.text: You prepare to attack the Militia ship.
You abandon interest in the factory.

choice.text: Attack the guard to get to the factory.

event.text: You prepare to attack the Militia ship.
You have no interest in the factory.

name: UNION_FACTORY_CHOICE
text: Without the guard to protect them, the few civilian workers scatter. You have the factory all to yourself, but it won't be long until reinforcements arrive. What will you grab?

name: UNION_FACTORY_QUEST

unvisitedTooltip.text: You have a delivery of ASB parts to drop off at this location.

text: You arrive at the planet that requested the parts you currently carry. They are surprised to see that their courier is a Renegade, but they are pleased to have received the delivery. They offer a modest payment.

event.text: As you deliver the parts, a Rebel ship enters the system. "So, the Renegade scum is running errands for their masters? Hah, you do more good like this than you ever did fighting our glorious cause."
As you face the enemy ship, the planetary defenses turn on you. It looks like despite your delivery, they'd rather side with the Rebels. Your reputation precedes you, apparently.
The Union planet offers you ASB assistance out of gratitude for your delivery.
They don't seem willing to help. Your reputation could be better, after all.
Rather than help you out, they turn their weapons on you. It looks like despite your delivery, they'd rather side with the Rebels. You must have really ruined your own reputation, somehow.

name: UNION_CARAVAN
text: It's extremely rare to see a Suzerain ship outside of the Mantis Hive, but even more so in Union territory. One particularly brave Suzerain ship is attacking a Militia caravan. The escort is poorly equipped and hardly stands a chance.

event.text: You prepare to attack the Suzerain ship.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Cloak and rob the Transport while they're distracted.

event.text: The Militiamen hardly even realized what happened before you've made away with some supplies. They're too busy with the Mantis to stop you, so you get away scot-free.

choice.text: (Hive Elite) Demand the Suzerain ship stand down.

event.text: Your Mantis berates the Suzerain captain for leaving their territory unprotected to do silly things like "robbing meatsacks". Despite the irony of this, the Suzerain aboard the enemy ship seems ashamed and jumps away. The Militia ships offer a reward, but one of their guards offers his services to you, afraid the Suzerains might return and attack the caravan after you leave.

choice.text: (Flares) Use the flares to lure the Suzerain away from the caravan.

event.text: The Suzerain almost immediately spots the flares and diverts, assuming it's a distress call sent to another nearby vessel. While they're distracted, you escort the Militia ships away. Seems they took quite the hit from the attack, and along with their reward one of the Militia guards offers his services to you, not wanting to risk facing the Suzerains again on the remainder of the trip.
It's a hard choice, but messing with a Suzerain is not something you look forward to doing.

name: UNION_CARAVAN_GIFT
text: The escort ship took a lot more damage than you first realized. Their life support failed during the fight and their crew asphyxiated. Luckily, the transport is still alive, and they give you some of their cargo as thanks.

name: UNION_SMUGGLER_PAYMENT
text: You find a Union ship talking with an Argeonn ship. You get the feeling that even if they're not fighting each other, they're not on the friendliest of terms either.

event.text:
"Look, I'm sorry. I thought I'd have the scrap to pay for those, but after a nasty run-in with Tiiikaka, I was forced to cash out for some repairs. Surely you can understand that, given what your job entails?"
			
			"My sympathies are irrelevant to my profession. Argeonn terms stipulate that payments are always made either in advance or on the spot... and deliveries are not handed over until the payment is made. Unfortunately, you'll just have to do... without those items. Unless your friend here can assist you?"

choice.text: Offer to help pay for the delivery.

event.text: You pool some of your scrap together with the small amount the Union ship still has. It's not cheap, but you're able to pay the full cost up front. The smugglers hand over the delivery before jumping away.

The captain of the Union ship hails you. "Thanks for helping me out there! I had to use those guys to retrieve some of my personal belongings from deep inside Rebel territory. Unfortunately, I can't really pay you conventionally in return for your help, but I should be able to give you a spare weapon of ours."

choice.text: Threaten them to hand over the delivery.

event.text: "...An unwise decision. Then again, expecting a different result would have been... foolish, given that you are likely unaware of the... fragile nature of this cargo." They power up their weapons and face you. Judging by their comments, if you want to get whatever it is that the other Union ship is interested in, you'll have to avoid blowing up their ship.

choice.text: [Reputation: 2+] Convince them to hand over the delivery.

event.text: "Given your extended business history with us, surely you would know that we do not... easily deviate from our standard practices. But at the same time, losing a potential customer would be... unfortunate. If you are willing to vouch for them, then I think we can make an... exception this time." They turn to face the Union ship. "However, do not expect any leniency when we... arrive for payments." The Union captain gladly agrees, and receives their delivery from the smugglers. The Argeonn ship jumps away after making the transfer.

The captain of the Union ship hails you. "Thanks for helping me out there! I had to use those guys to retrieve some of my personal belongings from deep inside Rebel territory. Unfortunately, I can't really pay you conventionally in return for your help, but I should be able to give you a spare weapon of ours."
Even from a distance, you can still feel a fraction of the tension between the two ships. Eventually they jump away in opposite directions.

name: UNION_SMUGGLER_PAYMENT_WIN
text: You hand over the delivery from the smuggler ship to the Union ship. Their captain speaks with you during the transfer. "Thanks for helping me out there! I had to use those guys to retrieve some of my personal belongings from deep inside Rebel territory.
