Unfortunately, I can't really pay you conventionally in return for your help, but I should be able to give you a spare weapon of ours."

name: DISTRESS_UNION_CLINIC_HARMONY
text: There is a Union clinic under attack by a Harmony vessel at this beacon. Noticing your approach, the Engi ship sends a message. "This = Harmony affair. Do not interfere."

event.text: "This facility = commonly utilized by Separatists and Rebel sympathizers. Unacceptable levels of tolerance towards deviance detected. Correcting the error. Repeat: Do not interfere."

choice.text: (Zoltan Crew) "You are in violation of Federation Statutes 105.2, 105.5 and 105.9!"

event.text: Your Zoltan angrily quotes the Federation regulations that prohibit attacks on medical personnel, and treaties codifying neutrality in treating the wounded regardless of ideology. The Engi struggles to make a compelling counter-argument, and eventually gives up.

"The Harmony is [acting] as -discordantly- as usual. Unaligned clinic = common good. Harmony vessel = Tyranny. Do something -useful- for [once]: and never return."
					
					"Priority target: detected. Separatist = must be dealt with." True to their word, the Harmony ship charges its weapons and changes targets.

"The Harmony is -willing- to go too far for its ends. You cannot control -everyone-, nor should you try. On behalf of your human -allies-, you must halt your aggression and pay restitution."
					
					"TRZ-1L detected. The Harmony demands: your unconditional surrender. Defiance of the Harmony's directives = unacceptable." The Harmony ship immediately engages your ship!

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Have your Engi find a compromise.

event.text: Your crewmember seems hesitant, but relents. Through your Engi, you're eventually able to convince the Harmony to let the residents go free.
The staff of the clinic don't seem happy with your compromise. Still, they find it within themselves to give you a small reward for their freedom.

choice.text: (Defender Crew) Convince your Defender to talk them out of it.

event.text: Your Defender seems hesitant, but relents. The Defender convinces the Engi vessel that this action endangers the good standing between the Harmony and the Federation, and that there are better ways to enact the Harmony's will.

choice.text: (Positive Harmony Reputation) Use your good standing with the Harmony to convince them to stand down.

event.text: You tell the Engi that you wouldn't be making a big deal out of this if it didn't matter. The Engi put up a little bit more resistance until you finally manage to get through to them. "Renegade: has good standing. Will defer decision for the time being."

choice.text: Try to talk them out of it.

event.text: "Federation ship = warned. Punitive action ensues." The Engi ship breaks off its attack on the clinic to face your ship instead.
The Harmony is an ally to the Federation; you decide to trust that they are acting in good faith.
"Error. Non-compliant Federation ship detected." The Engi ship breaks off its attack on the clinic to face your ship instead.
The Harmony is an ally to the Federation, you decide to trust that they are acting in good faith.

name: DISTRESS_UNION_LANIUS_MISTAKE
text: An errant Lanius ship is attached to a Union station. Both the ship and the station are sending out a distress call. The station's distress call reads "Mayday! We're being eaten by a Lanius! Please save us!" The Lanius, however, only produces a garbled screeching.

choice.text: (Damaging Beam) Cut the ship off the station.

event.text: With a swift strike, the beam manages to separate the ships. The Lanius detaches and gives the station a wide berth without warping away.

choice.text: (Beam Drone) Cut the ship off the station.

event.text: The drone precisely separates the ship from the station. The Lanius detaches and gives the station a wide berth without warping away.

choice.text: (Lanius Crew) "Lanius ship stuck. Doesn't mean harm. Wants to trade for scrap. Has goods. Broken translator."

event.text: The station's comm officer seems relieved. "So we're not under attack? Well, let's get out there and fix it then." In short order, the station and Lanius are separated, and begin to trade, with your Lanius serving as the intermediary. The station pays graciously for your help.
"Thanks. Have treasure. Very grateful."
The vessel continues to screech, but it defends itself. However, for some reason, it doesn't detach, therefore having no maneuverability.

choice.text: Try to communicate with the Lanius.

event.text: Both the ship and station continue to hail, but you pay them no mind.

name: UNION_LANIUS_SOLVED_NO_TRANSLATOR
text: The commander of the station hails your ship out of gratitude. "We were definitely screwed without your help. Please, take this token of our appreciation. Although... the ship isn't attacking or leaving. It's just broadcasting a message on repeat. What do you think it's trying to say?"

event.text: The ship tries in vain to get a response. Eventually, it jumps away. "Well, I guess we don't have to worry anymore."

The ship sends out a message that sounds like a windchime. It leaves behind a gift and scoops up the scrap that you have given it. "So it wanted to trade... I guess we weren't in danger after all. Well, I'm glad this got sorted."

choice.text: Pick up the gift the Lanius left behind.

event.text: The ship sends out a message that sounds like a windchime. It leaves behind a gift and scoops up the missiles that you have given it. "So it wanted to trade... I guess we weren't in danger after all. Well, I'm glad this got sorted."

choice.text: Pick up the gift the Lanius left behind.

event.text: The ship sends out a message that sounds like a windchime. It leaves behind a gift and scoops up the drones that you have given it. "So it wanted to trade... I guess we weren't in danger after all. Well, I'm glad this got sorted."

choice.text: Pick up the gift the Lanius left behind.

name: QUEST_UNION_HOTHEADED_CIV
text: A nearby civilian settlement hails you. "Renegade, come in! I know you're probably busy, but a friend of mine is in danger and I don't know where else to turn. One of those Slug hackers scammed him and took control of his account, so he borrowed a shuttle and went off to give them a piece of his mind. The poor guy's gullible and naive, but he's also a huge hothead. Do you think you have time to save him?"

event.text: "Thank you. I'll send you the transponder for his ship. As far as payment, I wish I could give you more, but this is all I have."

choice.text: We don't have time for this.

event.text: "I thought that might be the case..." The civilian hangs up, disappointed.

name: QUEST_UNION_HOTHEADED_CIV_SPOT

unvisitedTooltip.text: You were asked to look for a reckless civilian in pursuit of hackers.

text: Following the transponder, you detect a well-hidden Slug ship preying upon a civilian shuttle.

choice.text: (Upg. Hacking) Hack their mainframe before they notice you.

event.text: You manage to hack into their ship's computer and revert all the permission changes to the accounts they've preyed upon. "What the... Our profitssss! You'll regret thissss!"
"Oh... sssshoot! The Federation found ussss!" They quickly change targets to attack you.

name: UNION_HOTHEAD_GRATITUDE
text: "Let me check... yes! I can access my accounts again. You're a life-saver, Renegade. Let me see what I can spare..." The civilian sends you some scrap as a reward.

name: ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_STATION_UNION
text: This Union station is no friend of yours. Now inhabited by pirates, it's aiming its entire arsenal straight at you!

name: ENCOUNTER_COALITION_UNION
text: A Coalition ship is slinking around the area, no doubt hunting for Unionists to pick off. Spotting you instead, it decides you'll be a nice challenge for it and attacks.

name: RST_START
text: A small orange vessel probing the nearby beacon stops when it notices you and sends a distress call. Out of curiosity, you pick it up. "Foreign vessel, this is Surveyor 192 from the R.S.T. corporation. On behalf of the company I formally request any information you may have regarding the whereabouts of Dr. Renfield."

event.text: "Unfortunate, unfortunate... however, you do appear to be a military vessel, yes? Or at least a very well armed civilian. We have the general coordinates of where we believe Dr. Renfield to be. We hope to locate him, but we suspect he may be in danger. Our vessel is too poorly equipped to handle it alone. Could you take a look for us? R.S.T. will reward you handsomely if you succeed."
"Alright! Transfering coordinates as we speak. Good luck captain! Oh, and thanks for the help."

choice.text: Remind me who Dr. Renfield is?

event.text: "Oh, my apologies! I assumed everyone here knew... Dr. Renfield is a brillaint physicist, perhaps the greatest of our time! Among his most crowning achievements was the invention of the aptly named Renfield Bombs! Their explosive potential is greater than any previously known nuclear device of any species! They were used to eradicate the Vek on Earth, but the resulting explosion caused massive flooding. The incident did not... reflect wonderfully on the R.S.T. corporation, but that doesn't matter right now."
"Alright! Transfering coordinates as we speak. Good luck captain! Oh, and thanks for the help."
"Understandable. We will not waste your time any further! R.S.T. out."
"Understandable. We will not waste your time any further! R.S.T. out."

choice.text: Oh yeah I know all about Renfield. I think he was my brother or something?

event.text: "Brother? What? Renfield doesn't have any siblings! Ugh, it's like no one takes anything seriously anymore." The ship hangs up.

name: SPIDER_QUEST_START
text: You find a number of ships fleeing from a small space station. A squadron of Militia vessels have been deployed around the area. One ship hails you: "Civilian, this system is restricted. We must request that you leave immediately."

choice.text: We're no civilian ship, what is the issue?

event.text: "A Federation military vessel? My bad then. This station has been infected by some kind of weird... giant alien spiders. Think you could clear this station of the infestation, without causing too much damage?"

The Militiamen give you clearance to engage the station, but give two last warnings. "We aren't sure what these things are, but they seem to be able to keep the station's systems functional. If you have to cause some damage that's understandable, but please do not cause very much, we can't go around destroying civilian property."

"Oh, Commander Haynes! Pardon me sir, I didn't realize you were aboard! Yes sir, spiders! Of the giant alien variety!" The Militiaman stands up straight and salutes awkwardly, almost falling backwards in the process. Haynes goes a bit green in the face. "Great... spiders... when you say giant, how big exactly do you mean?" The Militiaman contemplates for a moment before responding, "Hmmm... about the size of a man? The babies are like the size of dogs. Very big. Hence the descriptor, sir! Uhm... sir?" You notice Haynes has left the room, and upon checking the cameras find he's throwing up in the restroom. He should get over it soon.

The Militiamen give you clearance to engage the station, but give two last warnings. "We aren't sure what these things are, but they seem to be able to keep the station's systems functional. If you have to cause some damage that's understandable, but please do not cause very much, we can't go around destroying civilian property." You have some of the other crew pull Haynes out of the restroom and prepare for combat.

choice.text: Perhaps this isn't the best idea.

event.text: You apologize but inform the Militiamen you can't help. Before you leave you make a point to tell Haynes you turned down the request, and a wave of relief floods his face before he returns to losing his lunch.

choice.text: We're no civilian ship, what is the issue?

event.text: "Well, I'll be! You're the ship who was sent out to take care of that spider issue. Unfortunately, there's still some spider problems on the outskirts here. Don't suppose you could take care of these ones again, could you?"
The Militiamen give you clearance to engage the station. "Just as before, please try and be careful! We can't go around blowing up civilian property!"
You navigate away from the station, but you stay in the system long enough to do something on the ship.

name: INFESTED_STATION_WIN
text: You've cleared out the spider infestation from the station. The Militiamen thank you for your help, and payment is given for your effort.

event.text: "Not sure there's much I can tell you. Things came from the Brood, one of those pirate clans that live out in abandoned space. Commander Montgomery could tell you more than me, but he's busy handling the infestation elsewhere. Seems the spiders have finally got so out of hand that even the Brood can't control them anymore, and now's our chance."

"We hired another Renegade sorta like you a while back to help but from what I understand he hasn't been of much use. I'd be hesitant sending in another loose cannon, but considering you handled the situation so delicately here why the hell not. I'll transfer the coordinates for the Brood stronghold to you. Best of luck."

choice.text: Accept the reward and carry on.

name: INFESTED_STATION_WIN_REPEAT
text: "Thanks again for the help! Hopefully we'll be able to clear these things entirely out of civilian space in a while from now."

name: INFESTED_STATION_SURRENDER
text: "You've caused too much damage to the station's hull! You need to stop damaging it! Kill the spiders or quit and we'll get someone better for the job. We'll pay you for at least trying to help if you do."

event.text: You can tell you're only being paid so the Militiamen can be assured you'll leave, but it's better than nothing.

choice.text: No no, we can do this!

event.text: The captain of the other ship sighs. "Fine, but make sure not to destroy it."

name: INFESTED_STATION_DESTROY
text: "God damn it, we told you not to destroy the station!" Highly displeased with you, the Militiamen demand you leave the system.

name: KESTREL_UNLOCK
text: As is customary in Union space, several corporate advertisements from the planet nearby play over your radio. You listen to them idly as you browse the nearby shipyards, gazing at various antique vessels. One in particular catches your eye, a Kestrel in seemingly full working order! You don't get to look at it very long though, when one of the advertisements catches your ear. It seems one from "Dewey Alms", CEO of Archive Incorporated, has an outgoing request for any capable mercenary vessel.

event.text: Your mission here is for the Federation, you can't be getting sidetracked with other mercenary work.

name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_OFFER
text: It seems these shipyards are in fact owned by Archive, so it's not difficult to get in touch with a correspondant who patches you in to Dewey directly. "Renegades? I have experience with your types. Before we begin, I would like to make it clear that, while I might be the CEO of Archive Inc., in this request I am not speaking on behalf of the company in any way. It would be... bad PR to get involved with more inter-dimensional Renegades after the disaster of the 'Rusting Hulks' incident. I'm sure you understand."

event.text: "Good, good. Heh, don't worry. We aren't skirting the Union's laws or anything with this. I just don't want any backlash from a personal affair. As you may or may not already know, Archive specializes in the... well, archival of Antiquum Terrae (or as you might know it, Old Earth) technology and culture. This matter concerns one of my most prized antiques, a 23rd century 'Kasparov', the first FTL-capable ship produced by humankind. Originally made to transport passengers to and from Tau Ceti. A remarkable achievement... but she has been stolen by pirates! I can't gather why... sure, she marks a new age in exploration and discovery, but why would a pirate want such an outdated piece of technology?"

"But to who? Plenty of Kasparov crafts were made. This particular model would be of no interest to anyone but an avid historian or ship enthusiast like me. Never the matter. My request; hunt down those thieves and secure the Kasparov. I haven't in mind any particular reward, but I'm sure we can work something out. Name your price."

event.name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_OFFER_KESTREL
event.text: "Huh? That old thing? Oh, I can most certainly part ways with it. I jumped on purchasing one when they saw a sudden resurgence in popularity at the end of the Civil War, but now it seems everyone has one. Good deal then. One last thing - I've programmed the coordinates for the pirate ship into my assistant, Gana. He's just a machine, and not a very personable one at that, but he'll be sufficiently useful in combat. Best of luck captain. Godspeed!"

event.name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_DECLINE
event.text: "You won't help then? What a loss... I'll have to find someone else then. Good day, captain."

choice.text: Do you happen to know someone named Zenith?

event.text: "Zenith? As in the Pinnacle CEO?" You nod your head. "Well, yes, I know the name. One of the four corporations that used to dominate Earth. Never talked very extensively with her - she was obsessed with the nebulous future, while I care more about the concrete past. Never the matter, why do you ask?" You shrug and mention your brief run-in. "Ah. What a coincidence. For such an infinitely large Multiverse, it sometimes feels so small..."

"Now then, that aside, back to that Kasparov issue - I can't fathom why anyone would steal it. Plenty of Kasparov crafts were made. This particular model would be of no interest to anyone but an avid historian or ship enthusiast like me. Never the matter. My request; hunt down those thieves and secure the Kasparov. I haven't in mind any particular reward, but I'm sure we can work something out. Name your price."

choice.text: [Federation Database] What was the 'Rusting Hulks' incident?

name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_PIRATE

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of the thieves.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: You've tracked down the pirate ship at Gana's coordinates. Seems it's a Brood ship - you've heard about these, but you suspect Dewey intentionally left that little detail out of the job offer.

event.text: Remember - you need these guys to surrender to find the location of the 'Kasparov', so try not to kill them!

choice.text: We aren't picking a fight with the Brood.

event.text: You're sure there was something significant about this encounter, but it's too late now.

choice.text: [Federation Database] Read more on the Brood.

name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_QUEST_2
text: "I'm not saying! Oh, wait. You can literally kill me right now. Alright, fair game. We were hired by Hideo Tanaka, CEO of Hephaestus. I'm sure you've heard of him. He heard Archive had this big fancy ship called the 'Molotov' or... whatever. He didn't want anyone else to know he was stealing it though, so he hired us to do it. I've told you everything, now let us go!"

choice.text: One last thing - where is the ship now?

event.text: "Weren't you listening? It's at the nearby Hephaestus Shipyards. They're probably gonna break it down for transport or whatever." You manage to convince the pirates to hand you the coordinates, and watch as they jump away moments later. What a bunch of cowards.

name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_RINGSHIP

unvisitedTooltip.text: The location of the stolen 'Kasparov'.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: You were suspicious of a trick at first, but this is most certainly the right location. In the distance you can see what is definitely the Kasparov, and a small Hephaestus depot by which the 'Kasparov' is being inspected. You catch some radio chatter between ships. "Yeah, boss says we gotta bring this 'Shakarov' thing to Mr. Tanaka's collection. God knows breaking this thing down is gonna suck, but if we screw up he's probably gonna sell us to Tiiikaka. Make sure there isn't a scratch on this or we're toast!"

choice.text: Demand they give back the Kasparov.

event.text: "What? Who the hell are you? Why are you here? Whadd'ya want with the 'Ivanov'?"

"Yeah yeah, Makogonov, shmakogonov. Oh, you're one of them MV people. With the fancy blue chemtrails or whatever. Archive sent you, didn't they? Look buddy, I don't care one bit about Alms's beef with Mr. Tanaka. But Tanaka is the one who pays the man who pays the man who pays the man who pays the man who pays me. So I ain't giving up this 'Shirov' thing without a fight, you hear?"

choice.text: Well, if it's a fight you want...

event.text: "Crap, we actually doing this? I shoulda known not to mention combat in front of a mercenary!"
You've come quite far - but this isn't worth it. You can't go picking fights with giga-corporations.

name: KESTREL_UNLOCK_QUEST_3
text: It seems most of the other ships were just automated construction drones. The depot's skeleton crew surrender, allowing you to secure the Kasparov and contact Dewey.

event.text: "Incredible! I shall see to it that your efforts do not go unpaid! I shall forward those Kestrel blueprints to you immediately. Oh, and if you still have Gana on you, feel free to keep him. He's better suited to a military vessel anyways. Before you go though, who did end up being the culprit?"

choice.text: Hideo Tanaka hired pirates to steal your ship for his collection.

event.text: "That old assbucket. I should have known. Hideo takes whatever he wants from anyone he wants, even a fellow Union megacorp. Oh well. As Grandfather would say... well Grandfather didn't say much. He mostly just talked about satellites. Anyways, I thank you for your services. Best of luck on the rest of your mission."

name: COREWORLDS_EARTH

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is Earth, the Homeworld of the Human race.

text: You've discovered a planet all too familiar. It's Antiquum Terrae, more often referred to as Old Earth, the homeworld and origin of the Human race! Though most of the planet has flooded, a few large and densely populated cities remain.

event.text: On the planet's surface is a museum and large memorial park. The ship computer informs you the subject matter involves the Mantis invasion of Earth. Attendance is free but it'll likely take a lot of time to browse the place.
You land on a large platform and exit the ship. You take a long stroll through the park and come across several plaques detailing things about the war. One in particular stands out to you.

"It all looked bleak for the citizens of Earth until the creation of the very first Pre-Igniter tech, invented by Jackson Newman. This augment was then merged with a powerful laser model developed by Zulfiqar Armaments, a busy corporation that has since grown to be very wealthy and powerful in modern times. Though the weapon was once considered a super-weapon so long ago, it is likely it would still stand the test of time and be very efficient in modern combat."

As you keep reading, you notice a section describing the locations of the parts of the weapon. "After the war was over the weapon was dismantled and many of the parts were repossessed." Maybe if you can track down their locations, you can re-assemble the gun!

choice.text: Read on the location of the barrel.

event.text: "The first part, the barrel, was originally given to a man by the name of Alaster Williams before it was stolen by a Mantis warlord and passed down across many generations. It is a valuable heirloom in their family, and it is highly unlikely they would surrender it to anyone, especially those who defeated them in the war."

choice.text: Read on the location of the base.

event.text: "The second part, the base, was buried alongside the creator of the weapon and its tech. The gravesite is among those of every soldier lost to the Mantis invasions."

choice.text: Read on the location of the Pre-Igniter.

event.text: "The final part, the Pre-Igniter was stolen by a Smuggler. It has been circulating the black market for many years, repossessed many times. Though it would serve as a valuable collectors item, the augment itself is told to no longer function as intended due to years of misuse by pirates."
With all of the information you need to collect the parts, you hurry back to the ship.

choice.text: We don't have time for wild goose chases around the sector.

event.text: You don't have time to go learning history. You pull away from the planet.

name: QUEST_GATLING_BARREL

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of the Gatling Barrel.

text: You have arrived at a busy Mantis warcamp on a small moon. Several ships lay on the surface, the largest being a Suzerain and no doubt where the Gatling barrel is held.

choice.text: Hail them and try to negotiate.

event.text: A Mantis with a long scar running down their face responds. "Yes? What reason has ship called me?"

choice.text: We've come for the Gatling Barrel.

event.text: "What? You mean spinny stick? You not dare take spinny stick! Precious heirloom passed down from grandfather, not plaything of stupid Federation captain!"

choice.text: Then we'll have to take it!

event.text: The Mantis shrieks and ends the call, and the Suzerain ship comes to life. It rises to meet you. If you had to guess, the 'spinny stick' is kept on that ship and you'll have to empty it of crew to get it.
"No! No! No! Not care who are! Shoo! Not welcome here." Despite the Mantis's tantrum, the only option that remains is to take it from him.

The Mantis shrieks and ends the call, and the Suzerain ship comes to life. It rises to meet you. If you had to guess, the 'spinny stick' is kept on that ship and you'll have to empty it of crew to get it.

choice.text: This is risky, we should leave.

event.text: You decide against pulling closer to the camp and stay far away from the moon.

name: QUEST_GATLING_BASE

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of the Gatling Base.

text: The graveyard at this beacon isn't quite what you expected. Rather than a spooky field or dark and stormy swamp planet, it appears to be a nice flat patch of grass decorated with the tombs of the fallen soldiers. You aren't sure if you really want to go grave robbing these people.

choice.text: We have a war of our own to fight. If these people were alive, they'd understand.

event.text: You inspect the gravesite and realise there's nothing to suggest where the Gatling Gun might be buried. You pick out a few graves that sound familiar, but you aren't sure which one. You think the plaque said who it was, but you'll have to remember who.

You start digging, but all you find inside is a rotting corpse. Disgusted and disappointed, you prepare to leave, when an Elite Federation ship swings by and spots you in the act. "Assholes! You'd dare dishonor the heroes buried here?" They raise their weapons and attack!
You start digging to find that you were correct! Inside the grave is the Gatling Base! You have your crew haul it back to the ship.
As you're leaving, a Federation Elite flies past, spotting you in the process! "Assholes! You'd dare dishonor the heroes buried here?" They raise their weapons and attack!

You start digging, but all you find inside is a rotting corpse. Disgusted and disappointed, you prepare to leave, when an Elite Federation ship swings by and spots you in the act. "Assholes! You'd dare dishonor the heroes buried here?" They raise their weapons and attack!

You start digging, but all you find inside is a rotting corpse. Disgusted and disappointed, you prepare to leave, when an Elite Federation ship swings by and spots you in the act. "Assholes! You'd dare dishonor the heroes buried here?" They raise their weapons and attack!

choice.text: We have better things to do than dishonoring the dead.

event.text: You ignore the graveyard and fly away.

name: QUEST_GATLING_AUGMENT

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of the Pre-Igniter tech.

text: You spot an armoured Smuggler Station orbiting the beacon, soliciting to a few smaller ships. It's surprising they can operate here despite the swarms of Militiamen protecting the beacon, but this is the place you're looking for.

event.text: You hail the Smugglers and explain the situation. The captain gives a wheezy chuckle at your explanation. "Is that so now? Well I've been struggling to get rid of this crap for a while now, and at last I found someone willing to pay a price for it! Hell, I'll even offer you a special 'Jumbo Deal' with some extra supplies for only a minor price increase!"

choice.text: Buy the "Jumbo Deal" along with the Pre-Igniter.

event.text: You aren't going to pay these smugglers anything! You raise the weapons and attack. The other few ships shopping scatter as you approach the station.
You ignore the station and fly away.

surrender.text: "Christ! Stop, stop! You've caused enough damage! You one'a Wright's cronies? What the hell do you want?"

event.text: "That stupid ring ship? You were sent by Archive, weren't you! We don't have it anymore, alright? We were contracted to steal it for another collector!"

destroyed.text: The Brood ship has been destroyed... which means you won't be able to track down the 'Kasparov'. You've failed the mission, so it's best not to return to Dewey.

deadCrew.text: The Brood pirates have been killed... which means you won't be able to track down the 'Kasparov'. You've failed the mission, so it's best not to return to Dewey.

destroyed.text: It seems the Hephaestus staff weren't kidding - they'd rather fight to the death than face the wrath of their boss.

deadCrew.text: It seems the Hephaestus staff weren't kidding - they'd rather fight to the death than face the wrath of their boss.

name: VAGABOND_SEPARATISTS
text: "Identity of Federation vessel confirmed. It is implied your allegiance promotes your ability to assist. Currently at large: Separatist saboteur 'B0N-N3' and Wraith outlaw 'Clydeo'. Have eluded capture from Harmony for too long. Request: Federation vessel holds off criminals until Engi reinforcements can arrive. Is this deal acceptable?"

event.text: "Transfering coordinates. Should your vessel fail at forcing the outlaws into surrender but still manage to eliminate them, alternative though lesser pay will be given. Top priority of Harmony: making sure further sabotage attempts by Separatists are unsuccessful."
The Engi hang up without another word. You know that their robotic nature and stricter culture leads to customs you might consider abrupt, but must they be so rude?

name: VAGABOND_SEPARATISTS_OUTLAWS

unvisitedTooltip.text: Location of Separatist and Wraith fugitives searched by the Harmony.

text: A fairly large Separatist vessel is nearby, confirming that this is the correct location. Your approach seems to have alarmed the outlaws. "Say, Bonbon, does that Federation vessel strike you as out of place?" "Your assumptions are [correct]. This Federation vessel has -recently- been in contact with [Harmony] owned vessels. Your suspicions of malcontent are [justified]."

choice.text: Do what you came here to do.

event.text: If you remember correctly, you were told by the Engi not to kill these guys if you can. You'll have to wait for the Engi to arrive or force them to surrender!

choice.text: Offer to shelter them from the Harmony.

event.text: "You wouldn't be able to do shit to help us! We're outlaws, the Federation don't want none o' us! We ain't just some normal criminals, we're fightin for the liberation of Bon's people! Leave us be or do what you gotta do, I ain't dilly dallying."
If you remember correctly, you were told by the Engi not to kill these guys if you can. You'll have to wait for the Engi to arrive or force them to surrender!
As you start to depart, you're stopped again by the outlaws. "You ain't going to destroy us? Why? The Harmony's not paying you enough?"

choice.text: We aren't puppets to the Harmony. We're Multiverse Renegades. We enforce the law as we see fit.

event.text: "Vigilantes? Who woulda thunk it-" The outlaw is suddenly cut off by gunfire as a Harmony ship jumps in. Looks like reinforcements arrived sooner than expected!

choice.text: Pretend you did your job and take the pay.

event.text: Once the outlaws have been captured, the Harmony ship contacts you again. "The Federation vessel has proven instrumental. Delaying outlaws raised chances of success by 75%. It is likely the Harmony will be requesting your assistance again."
You've heard the stories of the way the Harmony treats the Separatists. The Engi might be the Federation's allies, but that doesn't mean you can't stand against them.

choice.text: Conflict was not on my mind today.

event.text: "Hmmm. You're an awfully strange buncha mercenaries..."
It's not a good idea to go through with this when they've already called you out. You slink away into the distant nebulas far away from the beacon.

name: VAGABOND_TRASHKING
text: This beacon contains an immense amount of pollution, with various chunks of debris stuck in its orbit. Even outside of the planet is a concerningly large concentration of trash.

choice.text: Try and pick up some of the debris.

event.text: You start to collect the scrap when you're stopped by a Vagabond ship. "Halt! All that which is not living and enters the bounds of this orbit is that which belongs to our lord, the trash king!"

"Do not tell us you have not caught word of the trash king's rule!" When their cry is met by a blank stare on your end, the Ghost seems to deflate. "Alright. Follow me." The Ghost leads you to a massive castle built entirely out of garbage, and into a grand throne room.
You are met by a large Mare Alpha wearing a paper mache crown that barely manages to stay on his gaseous 'head'. "I, am the trash king! Bow before me breathers!"
"Good. You please me. If you are wishing to leave this place hands full of my precious trash, you must prove thineself in gladiatorial combat!"

choice.text: Fight one of his strongest ships.

event.text: "A challenge! So let it be! Call forth my champions!" The trash king ushers for one of his strongest ships to fight you.

choice.text: Fight one of his weaker ships.

event.text: "A challenge! So let it be!" The trash king ushers for one of his vessels to fight you.
The trash king growls. "I said BOW!"
"Good. You please me. If you are wishing to leave this place hands full of my precious trash, you must prove thineself in gladiatorial combat!"

choice.text: Fight one of his strongest ships.

event.text: "A challenge! So let it be! Call forth my champions!" The trash king ushers for one of his strongest ships to fight you.

choice.text: Fight one of his weaker ships.

event.text: "A challenge! So let it be!" The trash king ushers for one of his vessels to fight you.

choice.text: Don't tell us what to do!

event.text: You arm the weapons and attack the Ghosts.
Nothing seems of interest here, and so there's no use in further surveys of the area.

name: VAGABOND_STORM
text: This beacon might not be near any immediate nebulas other than those far off in the north, but it does have a large Vagabond camp set up on the nearby planet. Brief scans show the inhabitants are moving about quickly.

event.text: You're undisturbed by the Ghosts as you land on the planet, but as you approach the camp one of them stops you. "Why have you come? The great northern storm drifts closer every minute! Their electric fields will decimate our computers. We advise you leave at once!"

choice.text: Offer to stay and help move their equipment.

event.text: "You wish to help? Then we will not impede you - so long as you understand the risk." You order your crew to start dragging the various equipment, like moisture farms, solar panels, and an express coffee maker, indoors. The Ghosts weren't lying either, you can see the clouds moving closer at a concerning rate.

Your crew hurry inside the shelter set up by the Ghosts. The storm eventually envelops the entire planet, and for almost an entire day you're stuck inside with the foul scented Ghosts. Still, they couldn't be happier to have you as their guests. When the storm eventually does clear, they give you one of their finest weapons as a gift.

You order the crew to keep working, even as most of the Ghosts retreat inside. By the time the clouds consume the planet, trapping you in total darkness, you stumble your way into the shelter but notice one of your crew is missing! You're stuck inside for almost a day with the Ghosts, who at least prove to be charismatic hosts.

When you're finally free, you search everywhere for your crew but can't find them. Looks like they're gone for good. Their sacrifice wasn't entirely in vain however, as your efforts saved the Ghosts most of their vital equipment. Knowing the toll the day has had on you, they offer a large amount of scrap and one of their finest weapons.

removeCrew.text: If your crewmember is dead, it hardly matters. The Clone Bay would have been powered off by the storm and unable to clone them regardless.

event.text: When you're finally free, you search everywhere for your crew but can't find them. Looks like they're gone for good. Their sacrifice wasn't entirely in vain however, as your efforts saved the Ghosts most of their vital equipment. Knowing the toll the day has had on you, they offer a large amount of scrap and one of their finest weapons.

removeCrew.text: Thankfully, the Backup DNA ensured that you can recover your crew despite the power disruption caused by the storm.

event.text: This storm is going to be devastating, and you can't risk being stuck in it. Unfortunately, you're too late. A powerful shockwave strikes your ship, crippling the engines and causing an electrical fire. Even worse, looks like a Dynasty ship, forced all the way out here by the storm's movement, is here as well now!

choice.text: The onboard ship AI refuses to allow you to approach the camp without any extra crew - many Auto-ships have been lost to ravenous Ghosts. This security measure ensures that this number doesn't go any higher.

event.text: You receive only a brief response from the Ghosts. "A storm approaches fast. It is imperative we relocate. It is advisable you leave soon." You aren't so sure about the legitimacy of this claim, but you won't be able to do much else with the Ghosts here anyways.
You content yourself with watching the Ghosts scurry about as you do something onboard the ship. You can't help but notice, however, that the clouds in the distance seem to be approaching fast...

name: GHOST_REBEL_TRUCE
text: A Rebel ship already occupies this beacon, but surprisingly they hail you instead of fighting. "I should attack you... but this sector is littered with Ghosts and we've finally caught a break from the clouds."

event.text: "Good, glad to see we can both agree on something." You sense it's awkward for the both of you to be here, but you decide to take your mind off it by doing something else.
The Rebel captain yells at you as you both prepare for combat, "This is why the Federation must fall!"

choice.text: Pay them to delay the fleet.

event.text: The Rebel captain isn't sure how to respond, but it's clear he doesn't want to turn down the scrap. He reluctantly accepts, and promises to give the fleet false information when they return.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_VAGABOND_FLEETCRASH
text: Scans are turning up something large on the nearby lava planet. Looks like it's a massive Dynasty class-F Dreadnaught! Completely trashed of course, it'll probably never fly again... but that hasn't stopped a horde of Vagabonds from taking residence.

choice.text: Try to scrap some of the outer regions of the ship.
(Scrap Arm) Use your Scrap Arm to scrap the outer regions of the ship.

event.text: Your Scrap Arm allows you to collect a decent amount of the wreckage quickly. You're certain the Ghosts must have spotted you during the salvaging, but for some reason they never attempt to stop you.

choice.text: (Magnetic Arm) Use your Magnetic Arm to scrap the outer regions of the ship.

event.text: You put your Magnetic Arm to good use, collecting loose scrap around the outside of the ship in almost an instant. Hopefully they won't miss what you've scooped up.
The crackling static through your stereo eventually shifts into discernable words. "This place of ours we call home is not for the Federation's taking. We will trade, if you have missiles."

choice.text: Give them some missiles to access a store.
Ignore their request and scrap the wreck.

event.text: "You are a person of terrible motivations, and I shall kill you swiftly." An elite Ghost ship flies out of the wreck to meet you.
That's not a wreck-site anymore, it's a home to probably a couple dozen Ghosts. Best not to intrude on their space.

name: NEBULA_VAGABOND_ACID
text: "Hail good traveler! I am Domodius the explorer, privy to all knowledge that one might need on these dark nebulous clouds. All except for one vital fact whom eludes me. I have heard the legends of a so called... 'acid' nebula. Yet I have never seen one myself! I must find it!"

choice.text: Not sure. Could you describe one?

event.text: "Well, they're of green hue. And have the nature of a nebula. That's really it."

choice.text: Lie and say you've heard about them.

event.text: "Really?! I am amazed! Please, please, you must tell me where!"

choice.text: (Mind Control) Give him a very 'convincing' lie.

event.text: "Ooooh, ooooh! I must head there at once! Thank you for your assistance, oh seer of those things which beg of being seen!"

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Give him a very 'convincing' lie.

event.text: "Ooooh, ooooh! I must head there at once! Thank you for your assistance, oh seer of those things which beg of being seen!"

choice.text: Tell the truth. You've never seen one.

event.text: "That's alright! Had we explorers seen all the starry sky had to be seen, why then there would be nothing left to be an explorer OF! Safe travels friend, and may this aid you."

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Offer him your detailed map data.

event.text: Domodius takes a look at the data you've given him. "Hmmm. Inconclusive. Still, this proves you are a purveyor of fine knowledge and a keen explorer with an eye for discovery! If I join you, our combined intellect should be unrivaled!"

choice.text: (Long-Ranged Scanners) Offer him your detailed map data.

event.text: Domodius takes a look at the data you've given him. "Hmmm. Inconclusive. Still, this proves you are a purveyor of fine knowledge and a keen explorer with an eye for discovery! If I join you, our combined intellect should be unrivaled!"

choice.text: (Slip Scanner) Offer him your detailed map data.

event.text: Domodius takes a look at the data you've given him. "Hmmm. Inconclusive. Still, this proves you are a purveyor of fine knowledge and a keen explorer with an eye for discovery! If I join you, our combined intellect should be unrivaled!"

choice.text: (Aenwithe) "Yuck. Yeah, I know what those are."

event.text: Aenwithe explains that acid nebulas don't come from this reality, or any others like it. This seems to satisfy Domodius. "I have never heard of this... edition of captains you speak of, but it sounds most horrible. I've never been so glad to live in this reality. If you are so knowledgeable, then I shall come with you, so that our combined intellect should know no limits!"
"Oh, a shame! So long then, oh voyager of the interdimensional threads of the cosmos!"

name: NEBULA_GHOST_BOO
text: The nebula appears empty, but not long after you jump in all of your lights go off. A few seconds later, your main screen flickers to life. You sit back in anticipation, watching the blinking cursor as it begins to type...

event.text: "BOO!" The word flashes on the screen, shortly followed by the text, "Have I caused you fear?"
The screen goes blank, and then a Ghost beams onto the bridge. "Hah! You cause me sensations of joy. That is an emotion I have not felt in many cycles. I think I'll stick with you, breather."
The computer shuts off, and a set of Ghosts apparate on the bridge, and make their move towards you. You ready your crew for combat.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_DONATION
text: Ghost Vagabonds usually inhabit their ship for long periods of time until the damage becomes too major to be ignored. The Ghost ship at this beacon is on its last breath, but unexpectedly the Ghost crew makes no attempt to attack your ship. A quick scan shows why; their weapons are barely functional and the engines are leaking fuel fast.

event.text: For once, you're the one initiating the combat. You power up your weapons and prepare to destroy the already-crippled wreck.

choice.text: Pay them scrap to fix up their hull. [-35~]

event.text: The Ghosts make no attempt to communicate with you, and eventually slip back into the clouds, leaving you all alone.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_BREEDER
text: A Slug vessel is already at this beacon, surrounded by several Vagabond ships. Oddly enough, none of the Ghosts are attacking the Slug, nor is the Slug scrapping the wrecks.

event.text: The Slug captain responds in a frustrated tone, constantly looking around himself and occasionally turning around to yell at his crew. "Yesss, you're Federation. We're a sssscience vesssel, and we've recently taken up trying to breed Ghosssstssss. Turnsss out they don't breed. Ssso..."

choice.text: Offer to buy one of their test subjects as crew.
(Ghost Crew) Have your Ghost explain Ghost reproduction.

event.text: Your Ghost types out its response on a small tablet so that the Slug can understand. According to them, the Ghosts 'age' through the collection of natural gasses they assimilate into their body. Once they reach a maximum size, they become known as an Alpha. Once in the alpha stage, they can divide to create a new Ghost.

"What?! Thissss doesssn't even make sssenssse! Ugh... this busssinessss issssn't the right place for me. You're sssaying thessse big guysss are important? Fine, take one. What point issss there to it anywayssss..."

The scientist eagerly investigates the device, looking into every crevice and studying every inch. You consider complaining about the slime but don't want to break him from his concentration. After a while he punches the machine, and yells something. "I musst try thissss! How much?"
The Slug can hardly control himself, tossing you the scrap and running off with his latest bounty.
The Slug shouts something insulting about wasting his time, and heads back to his ship in a tizzy.
You shrug and end the call. You doubt the scientist minds.
Slugs, even scientists, cannot be trusted, nor do you wish to aggravate a clan of Ghosts. You decide to stay at a distance from their shady dealings.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_GHOST_GASGIANT
text: Looks like a Vagabond ship is scanning the nearby gas giant, but quickly hails you when you jump in. "Isn't my darling beautiful?"

event.text: "Don't be silly! I know you can see. She's quite large!" It doesn't take long to realize they're referring to the gas planet. "Say, can you do me a favor? My darling hungers! I must feed her. But I lack the food. You must bring me a wreck. I heard a demon lingers about! But, perhaps you'd prefer to go after some Rebels instead..."
Looks like the 'demon' in question is... a Rebel Auto-ship? Well, you'll have to kill this thing either way, get ready to fight!
Fortunately, there's a Rebel ship not too far from here. You can pick these guys off pretty easily, you hope.
"Ok... Say goodbye to the Federation captain, darling!" The gas giant remains silent, swirling in the distance silently judging you.

name: GHOST_GASGIANT_FEED
text: "Yes, yes! Oh you are triumphant! My darling shall not go hungry again tonight!" The Ghost links the wreck with his own vessel, then uses it to slingshot the wreckage into the gas giant. The ship spirals away out of visibility as it is consumed by the planet. "Good. You deserve a most generous reward!"

name: NEBULA_GHOST_FEDMORALITY
text: You've become accustomed to not seeing many Fed ships around - so seeing one here comes as quite the shock. Even weirder, their weapons are powered and hull shows some minor damage. They must have just been in combat.

event.text: The vessel's captain looks up, distracted. "Huh? Oh! Well, look who it is. I thought we were all alone in these clouds - save for the Ghosts, that is. Was trying to clear out a camp of them not too far from here, bastards are stranded! I can just keep taking trips back and forth as much as I like!"

"Hah! Well, why not? Easy scrap, and makes the nebulas just a little less crowded. Once the Rebellion is out of way, the Federation will probably move a bit further out, might as well get started clearing out the riff-raff."

choice.text: Help them clear out the Ghosts.

event.text: Your offer to help delights the Federation captain. He leads you to the Ghost camp, where you spot out your target.

choice.text: Attack one of the Mantis wrecks.

event.text: As you move in to attack the Vagabonds, you watch as the other ships move to fight the Federation vessel. Hopefully you can both pull through.

choice.text: Attack one of the Engi wrecks.

event.text: As you move in to attack the Vagabonds, you watch as the other ships move to fight the Federation vessel. Hopefully you can both pull through.

choice.text: Attack one of the Zoltan wrecks.

event.text: As you move in to attack the Vagabonds, you watch as the other ships move to fight the Federation vessel. Hopefully you can both pull through.
"Gah! What the hell are you doing?" You mute the vessel and attack.
The Federation vessel looks to be too preoccupied to notice or care about you.

name: GHOST_FEDMORALITY_FINISH
text: "Good work there! We showed those gas freaks what for-" the Federation ship is cut off as a blast from a Vagabond vessel tears their hull right in half! "Get lost, breather!" You quickly wipe out the second Ghost ship, but the Federation ship won't last much longer.

event.text: "Th-thanks. This is why we've gotta have our backs at the Federation, this galaxy is full of unprovoked dangers!"

choice.text: It's for the best. Let them die and scrap their ship.

event.text: You feel a little guilty, but these guys were hardly free of sin either. The blood of this day's murder is on your hands alone now, but you should be able to move on pretty quickly.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_ANGERY_SLUG
text: You're hailed by an angry Slug captain. "God damn Ghosssstssss! The nebulae are OURSSSSS! I had enough issssuesss to deal with, I can't deal with a Federation ssship here too."

choice.text: Show them that you aren't messing around.

event.text: "Sssshould have known you'd try thisss. Better I desssstroy your ssship than the Ghossstsss claim it themssselvesss."
"Fine... But don't let me sssee you back here."

name: NEBULA_DRIFTER_CHOICE_GHOST
text: An abandoned wreck, lights off and seemingly-empty, drifts nearby. It doesn't respond to your hails.

event.text: You send a shot directly into the hull of the wreck, causing an explosion to erupt that sends warped metal flying. Ghosts aboard or not, it doesn't matter anymore. Unfortunately, with the debris scattered into the depths of the nebula, nothing salveagable remains.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_INSANE_ROCKMEN
text: You're hailed by the Rock ship at this beacon as soon as you jump in. Their crew are curled up on the ground, rocking back and forth. The captain shakes the camera violently, yelling at you. "GHOOOOSTS, GHOOOOOOOSTS! ARE YOU A GHOST?"

choice.text: (Ghost Crew) Show them your Ghost crew.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_INSANE_ROCKMEN_GHOST
text: The Rockman lets out a scream so high pitched you didn't think it was even possible for vocal cords to make. Suddenly, he falls over, twitches, and literally dies. Your Ghost must have given him a heart attack, if Rockmen even have hearts. With the rest of their crew too insane to do anything, you scrap the exterior of their ship.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_UPGRADERS
text: The beacon appears empty, but you reconsider as static noises echo through your halls. You rush to the engine room to see three Ghosts examining the FTL drive.

choice.text: Fight the Ghosts before they can damage your system.
(Mind Control) Leave them be, but have the mind control ready just in case.

name: NEBULA_VAGABOND_ORCHID
text: Looks like an Orchid ship, of all things, is the source of this distress beacon. One of their crew hail you - "Please help! We were sent by the Gathering to negotiate with one of the Goul clans who keep burning our colonies, but our captain was taken hostage and they won't give him back!"

event.text: You follow the Orchid ship's directions to a Vagabond war camp populated mostly by Gouls. You request to speak with their leader directly: "Does the life of this frail plant thing concern you to a degree that would drive further ambitions to seek our favor in release? If you wish for this floral being not to suffer any longer, then you must prove your worth and destroy a Dynasty vessel who has been troubling my people."
The Vagabonds direct you to a Dynasty vessel not too far. Prepare for battle!

choice.text: Refuse - just attack the Vagabonds instead.

event.text: "Predictable as always! Don't expect the life of this Orchid to persist much longer after this battle!"

The two Gouls speak back and forth for some time, but finally reach a consensus. Having frightened them with foreboding warnings of a potential Orchid invasion in collaboration with the Dynasty, the Gouls don't seem eager to keep the Orchid hostage any longer. Once safely returned, the Orchids pay you for your assistance.
You apologize to the Orchids, but these aren't matters for you to get involved in.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_ESCORT
text: A poorly-armed civilian ship is emitting the distress beacon. Lost and afraid, they request you escort them to their destination and protect them from the Ghosts.

event.text: The civilians thank you, and pay you some scrap as a down-payment. They promise there will be more at their final destination.
The civilians are surprised by your sudden hostility, but have no choice but to fight.
We don't have time to help every civilian dumb enough to wander into the Ghost nebula. You turn down their request and charge the FTL drive.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_ESCORT_DESTINATION_GOOD

unvisitedTooltip.text: You were asked to escort an unprepared vessel to these coordinates.

text: The civilians thank you for your help, and pay you the rest of the scrap.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_SLUG_GHOST
text: A Slug ship hails you. "Ghosstsssss or not, we don't care. The nebulassss belong to the Kleptocracy and the EHG, not to the Ghossstsss, and certainly not to the Federation!"

name: NEBULA_GHOST_AUTO_ESCAPE
text: It looks like a Rebel Auto-ship was exploring this sector, but got lost in the nebulas. Now attempting to return to base before Ghosts can capture it, it raises its weapons to defend itself from you while its FTL drive charges.

name: NEBULA_GHOST_LANIUS
text: Lanius aren't common sights in nebula sectors, but they're drawn to the Ghosts. Natural enemies, the Lanius prey on the Ghosts to absorb their ships. The Lanius here don't care that you're not Ghost, and attack regardless.

name: NEBULA_ENCOUNTER_VAGABOND_ELITE
text: You catch sight of the remains of a seemingly former Elite ship which would make for a bountiful salvage, but are soon taken by surprise when the "wreckage" turns to face you, revealing that it's now inhabited by Ghosts! With that craft re-invigorated by a second breath, it is up to you to put it to rest, and for good.

name: UNLOCK_GHOST_QUEST
text: A Rebel Marauder, painted white with a strange logo on the back, hails you. "Greetings, traveler! We are the Ghost... uh... Spook Chasers! We have a unique proposition for you..."

event.text: "Maybe you've heard of the Dynasty's scuffle with the Rebellion? Well, it all went down when they took out one of the Rebels' first Flagship prototypes! This instigated a large scale war, and bla bla bla... Thing is, that Flagship is still around! In fact, it's in this very sector!"

"Now, you're probably thinking we're some Rebels. Wrong! Used to roll with that pack, but we ain't any more. We're mercenaries, and we were sent by the Federation to take out this goliath. Turns out it's in the hands of the Vagabonds now - more specifically a clan called the Haunts, led by some jackass who calls himself Goziodeon. Help us take out these sons o' bitches, and we'll split the bounty half and half. Deal?"
"Perfect! We'll transfer the last known co-ordinates of the ship. See you there."
The captain mutters something under his breath. "Fine, we'll find some other ship who's willing to kill some silly ship in return for the largest bounty ever made in galactic history!"

choice.text: A Rebel ship is a Rebel ship. Attack!

event.text: The only good Rebel is a dead Rebel. You prepare to attack.
You don't care to deal with wackos, especially out here. You hear the captain sigh as you end the call.

name: GHOSTBUSTER_KILL
text: As the ship explodes, you feel a menacing presence as hundreds of whispy shapes float out of the hull. You've probably done something really bad, but what does one cursed timeline mean anyways?

name: UNLOCK_GHOST_QUEST_2
text: You arrive at the beacon, but there is seemingly no ship here. You stare long into the clouds and catch the sight of an orange tail-wing slipping through.

event.text: You slip through the nebulas after it, only to find a massive gap in the clouds where there resides, right in the center, the old Rebel Flagship. "Good, good, you made it! Now give us a hand, would you?", shout the Spook Chasers, as they fire on the Flagship to no avail.
You're no coward. If you want to have any hope of defeating a real, multiverse traveling Flagship at the end of this mission, you should be able to take this one out as well.

name: UNLOCK_GHOST_DAMAGE
text: You notice your companion, the Ghost hunters, fly past. Though their weapons haven't been able to do much against the Flagship, a salvo of theirs finally makes its way into the Flagship's engines, shutting them down. However, teleporter signatures indicate that you've been boarded yet again.

name: UNLOCK_GHOST_QUEST_WIN
text: The gargantuan ship, for which you've heard so many legends about, finally gives one last quake before an explosion in the engines causes it to erupt into flames and explode. The Flagship, and the Vagabonds with it, is dead... yet again.

event.text: The Ghost Hunter hails you. "That. Was. LEGENDARY! Do you know how rich we're gonna be? Wait, yes yes. Your payment. Considering the bounty from this will be enough for us to buy an entire moon, maybe even a small planet, I suppose it doesn't hurt to give you something extra-special. We have a new cruiser that we've been working on, and I couldn't think of anyone else more worthy of piloting it than you."

"Oh, oh! One last thing. With this we'll never have to work another day in our lives. It does me no harm to pass this onto you now. More members of the haunt still roam this galaxy, and you're as good a choice as any to take the rest of them out!"

gotaway.text: The civilians jump away. They'll no doubt fulfill their intentions and inform the Rebels, especially now that you've attacked them.

destroyed.text: The civilians have been defeated. You aren't exactly proud, but at least the Rebels won't know your location.

deadCrew.text: The civilians have been defeated. You aren't exactly proud, but at least the Rebels won't know your location.

surrender.text: "We never done nothin' to nobody! If there's a shred o' hospitality in that black heart of yours, you'll accept our capitulation!"

destroyed.text: With the Frontiersman ship destroyed, you can scrap the remains of their ship. However, their ship was of poor quality, leaving you to take less of a yield than you might expect.

deadCrew.text: The crew is dead, leaving their ship's cargo up for grabs. However, as it turns out, pretty much everything they brought was agricultural equipment meant for settlements. You take what you can.

destroyed.text: The Coalition ship breaks apart. You hasten to contact the civilian ship.

deadCrew.text: No more life signs detected on the Coalition ship. You hasten to contact the civilian ship.

destroyed.text: The Coalition ship breaks apart. You scrap what remains.

deadCrew.text: The Coalition ship has been emptied of crew. You scrap their hull.

destroyed.text: The Coalition ship breaks apart. You hasten to contact the Federation ship.

deadCrew.text: No more life signs detected on the Coalition ship. You hasten to contact the Federation ship.

surrender.text: You've weakened the Coalition station. The Theocracy ship is waiting for the signal.

choice.text: Signal them and pretend to leave.

event.text: The Rockmen jump in. "Halt, Federation scum! You are outnumbered! Make yourself scarce!" You make a show of panicking and flying away from the station, but the Rocks let you listen in on their channel.

The Slug is the first voice you hear. "Sssso you've come back. Come closssser, we took damage. You'll have to help patch ussss up."

The Rocks hesitate. "Have you reconsidered our request?"

"You're sssstill on about that? You civilian Rockssss really are thick. Sssstop being an idiot and repair ussss."

"Even after all that, you still refuse?"

"Know your place. We joined forces to fight the Federation, not to ssssing Kumbaya. Now get to work."

choice.text: Come back out of hiding and launch a surprise volley.

event.text: The station is so preoccupied, they don't notice your finishing volley warming up until it's already tearing their station apart.

choice.text: Wait and see how this plays out.

event.text: The Rocks, frustrated, do a quick patch-job on their station.

"You have our gratitude. You are a captain of your word. We have done all we can for our people. Finish them off. Or don't. It's your choice. We will be leaving now." The Theocracy ship pays you for your time and leaves.
The Coalition ship sends out a mayday. "Coalition sssstation to Theocracy Envoy! We're under attack again!! ...Hello?"
"An impulsive decision, but an understandable one. We are both better for their absence. We will simply have to live with the other Coalition races for now." The rockman pays you for your time.
"Did you forget the plan, or did your bloodlust overtake you? Harumph. It was a foolish plan to begin with."
"An impulsive decision, but an understandable one. We are both better for their absence. We will simply have to live with the other Coalition races for now." The rockman pays you for your time.
"Did you forget the plan, or did your bloodlust overtake you? Harumph. It was a foolish plan to begin with."

surrender.text: Their resolve seems to be wavering. You might be able to demand the prisoners' safe return.

choice.text: Demand the surrender of the prisoners.

event.text: "Bah. They weren't cooperating regardless. What makes Vampweeds so special, anyway? Lousy biased Shells."
The prisoners did not survive. You decide not to signal the ship that sent you on the mission, lest you aggravate them.

destroyed.text: As you emerge victorious and the ship breaks apart, you see sparks begin to fly from the enemy ship...

event.text: The resulting explosion of the enemy ship sets off a chain reaction to a larger explosion, as the nebula itself catches fire too! Unfortunately, the enemy ship's remains were damaged in the explosion, resulting in a lower quality yield.
The sparks subside. It must have been some residual wisps from the explosion.
It looks like the other fight has already ended. The R.U.E.S. managed to win, but it looks damaged. It jumps away before you can engage it.
It looks like the other fight has already ended. The R.U.E.S. managed to win, but it looks damaged. It jumps away before you can engage it.

destroyed.text: The ship breaks apart and you quickly salvage what you can.

event.text: The outpost hails you, "The pompous bastards expected free service just because they defeated the Federation. Take this for the help."

deadCrew.text: With the crew dead you quickly salvage what you can.

event.text: The outpost hails you, "The pompous bastards expected free service just because they defeated the Federation. Take this for the help."

destroyed.text: The outpost hails you, "Thank you! I don't know what we did to anger the Rebels, but they were ready to kill us. I'll show you our goods and patch up your hull."

deadCrew.text: The outpost hails you, "Thank you! I don't know what we did to anger the Rebels, but they were ready to kill us. I'll show you our goods and patch up your hull."

escape.text: It appears the Rebels are trying to escape once again!

destroyed.text: You scrap the wreckage of the Rebel vessel.

deadCrew.text: With the crew dead, you scrap the ship.

escape.text: After watching their squadron get destroyed, it looks like their leader is prepared to turn tail and run.

gotaway.text: The Rebel ship jumped away.

event.text: With the threat gone, you contact the Federation outpost. They respond, "Our location has been compromised! Take everything you can and please drop our survivors off at the next station." One soldier offers to stay and fight.

destroyed.text: You scrap the wreckage.

event.text: With the threat gone, you contact the Federation outpost. They respond, "Our location has been compromised! Take everything you can and please drop our survivors off at the next station." One soldier offers to stay and fight.

deadCrew.text: With the crew dead, you scrap the ship.

With the Rebels now taken of, the station is now clear of threats. The Militiamen are relieved, and one of them offers to join you in thanks.

escape.text: They are powering up their FTL! If they get away, they will no doubt warn the fleet of your position!

gotaway.text: The scout jumps away. They are sure to have informed the fleet of your position. You must get to the next Sector as soon as possible!

destroyed.text: With the Rebel ship destroyed, you take the time to collect what little scrap remains. They had already made their delivery to the civilians.

deadCrew.text: With the Rebel crew dead, you strip their ship for equipment. They had already made their delivery to the civilians.

destroyed.text: With the ship destroyed, you quickly collect useful resources.

deadCrew.text: With the crew of the Rebel ship dead, you salvage what you can.

destroyed.text: With the ship destroyed, you quickly collect useful resources.

destroyed.text: The Rebels destroyed, you pick the bones of their ship and wait for the small Engi ship to catch up.

deadCrew.text: The Rebels destroyed, you pick the bones of their ship and wait for the small Engi ship to catch up.

destroyed.text: With the Rebel ship destroyed you are free to contact their would-be victim.

deadCrew.text: With the Rebel ship defeated you quickly salvage what you can and move to contact their prey.

destroyed.text: There's no time to salvage all of the wreck, the fleet is still nearby. Get ready to jump!

deadCrew.text: There isn't time to salvage the enemy ship but your crew made off with a few nearby materials. Prepare to jump.

destroyed.text: You scrap the remains of the Rebel ship quickly.

deadCrew.text: You scrap the remains of the Rebel ship quickly.

destroyed.text: The Rebel ship splinters apart, reduing your foe to nothing. Once you are victorious, your Federation ally wraps up their fight with the Duskbringer. You scrap your defunct foe as they finish.

deadCrew.text: The last Rebel crewman falls silent. Once you are victorious, your Federation ally wraps up their fight with the Duskbringer. You scrap your defunct foe as they finish.

destroyed.text: The destruction of the MFK Ace is an occasion to celebrate on its own. You scrap the remains.

deadCrew.text: The death of the MFK Ace's crew is an occasion to celebrate on its own. You scrap the remains.

destroyed.text: The ship breaks apart. You scrap what remains.

deadCrew.text: No more life signs detected on the ship. You scrap what remains.

destroyed.text: You quickly salvage what you can from the station.

event.text: Amidst the blasts from the Anti-Ship Battery, the cargo ship escaped from the chaos. They jettisoned some scrap towards your ship before jumping away.

event.text: Amidst the blasts from the Anti-Ship Battery, the cargo ship escaped from the chaos. They jettisoned some scrap towards your ship before jumping away.
You take your time taking the loot on board, making sure to keep them distracted the whole time, in order to allow the Union ship to finish its job.

destroyed.text: Little survived the explosion on the station. You scrap the hull and move on.

deadCrew.text: The security checkpoint contains what seems to be a bucket of fake ID's, though they've all been marked as such. You move on to scrap the station.

surrender.text: "WAIT WAIT WAIT!! Hear us out! Take everything we have, just please don't kill us!!!"

event.text: "Oh, thank goodness! Please, take it!" The Rebels seem to be physically shaking as they hand over their loot.

escape.text: Somewhat predictably, the frightened Rebels appear to be fleeing.

gotaway.text: "GET OUT OF HERE, PUNCH IT YOU FOOL!!!" The Rebel captain screams at the pilot. The ship speeds away.

event.text: By the time the battle is over, it's too late. The satellite crashes into the surface of the planet before you can stop it.
By the time the battle is over, it's too late. The satellite crashes into the surface of the planet before you can stop it.

deadCrew.text: You've defeated the cocky Zoltan captain and his crew, but you can't stick around. The other ships will no doubt be on your tail after your lack of restraint.

destroyed.text: You've defeated the commander of the Zoltan flotilla. The other ships flee in fear, leaving you in peace to salvage what you can. This massacre of Zoltans however has tainted your image to the eye of the Ministry.

destroyed.text: The Zoltans have been defeated. You scrap the ship.

event.text: Without the Zoltans in the way, you return to the Free Mantis ship, and help the Warlord to their feet. "Oh thank you, kind Federation. This is why Free Mantis always have Federations back! Just wish Zoltan not so mean..."

deadCrew.text: You've neutralized the Monk ship, meaning you will be able to obtain the core from their Zoltan shields.

deadCrew.text: The Zoltans have been defeated. You scrap the remains of their ship.

destroyed.text: Zoltan Auto-ships aren't too different from Rebel ones, which you've killed many of, so it's no surprise you came out victorious.

choice.text: Report back to the Dynasty ship.

destroyed.text: As you begin scrapping the ship, a hail comes in from a nearby outpost.

event.text: "This is Ministry Outpost 47-P. You are harvesting a Zoltan auto patrol ship. I demand answers. What happened here?"

choice.text: It must have been malfunctioning, it attacked us.

event.text: "I figured as much. Care to tell me why?"
"I'm well aware. Always on the fritz, that stupid thing. But that's not a good enough reason to destroy it." Satisfied, the Zoltan waves you away.
"Yes, I... I guess it is. What I mean to say is, what gives you the right to destroy our property?"

choice.text: It attacked us for no reason. We had the right to destroy it.

event.text: The Zoltan looks even more flustered. "W-well, look, all I'm trying to say is that you can't just go around blowing up Zoltan defense platforms. I'm just asking... don't you have a reason for what you did?"

choice.text: It attacked us for no reason. We had the right to destroy it.

event.text: The Zoltan looks almost relieved. "While I respect your honesty, I will be forced to report this. The Ministry can't just ignore this. But seeing as how you're on an important Federation mission I can offer you something to help with desperate times. Just try not to do too much more damage to our infrastructure."
"I know... look, just, can't you at least tell me why you did it?"
"You're right. I'm sorry for wasting your time." The Zoltan sends you a tribute as an apology.

destroyed.text: The Hacker ship has been destroyed. You salvage the remains.

event.text: "You have done us a great service. We have little earthly possessions to give you, but help yourselves to our excess fuel stores.

deadCrew.text: The Hacker crew has been killed. You salvage the ship.

event.text: "You have done us a great service. We have little earthly possessions to give you, but help yourselves to our excess fuel stores.

destroyed.text: As you scrap the Smuggler ship, you're surprised to find a small device showing marked coordinates, likely for their intended client. Worth a look?

event.text: If the Smugglers were planning anything, it's worth taking a look.
They're not worth the trouble. You prepare to leave.

event.text: You speak with who you believe to be the undercover operative mentioned earlier. "Thank you, it appears my cover has been blown. A shame... event.text: The Monks jump in shortly after. "You have done well. It is a shame we must rely on violent savages such as yourself, but this a cruel and uncaring galaxy. Please accept this monetary donation as thanks."

event.text: "Why have you done this? Those were our friends! They would not dare harm us, and yet you have killed them! Needless violence causes nothing but suffering. Leave, now!"

deadCrew.text: You've defeated the Duskbringer ship. You salvage the remains.

event.text: "Why have you done this? Those were our friends! They would not dare harm us, and yet you have killed them! Needless violence causes nothing but suffering. Leave, now!"

surrender.text: They are clearly not putting up a fight. Are you sure you want to destroy them?

event.text: You continue the assault.
You power down your weapons and after a time the ship slowly limps away. They refuse all communications. You can't help but feel somewhat guilty.

destroyed.text: You can't help but feel somewhat guilty as you search through the debris. It was probably a trap... right?

deadCrew.text: You begin to strip their ship and don't find anything that would indicate they were on anything other than a peaceful mission. Perhaps you were too hasty.

destroyed.text: You defeat your assailant, but the peace ship has jumped away in the commotion.

deadCrew.text: You defeat your assailant, but the peace ship has jumped away in the commotion.

surrender.text: "You have brought us the brink of destruction. We apologize... perhaps we were wrong after all. Will you spare us?"

choice.text: You have only proven yourself to be intolerant and rash. We will be doing the galaxy a favor by ridding it of you.

event.text: You continue the assault.
Suddenly all indications of the Rebel ship fade away and a Zoltan fleet appears around your ship. The captain of the ship you met previously materializes on your bridge.

destroyed.text: The Rebel ship explodes, but the wreckage fades away to reveal a Zoltan fleet watching you. It appears this was a test, and you failed.

deadCrew.text: The now empty Rebel ship fades away to reveal a Zoltan fleet watching you. It appears this was a test, and you failed.

surrender.text: "Hold! This is not a fight! We are merely trying to help you achieve enlightenment! Clearly, we have failed. We offer you a premature end to your trial."

event.text: "You have failed your trial, but we acknowledge the virtue you have shown by admitting fault. Consider your actions today."

tooltip.text: This is the time remaining for your "trial by fire" as administered by the Monks.

surrender.text: "This accursed weapon is the reason for your bloodlust, is it not? Then take it and cease your barbarism."

destroyed.text: In their dying moments, the monks have made sure the weapon went down with them. Their ship hardly yields any reward.

deadCrew.text: With the monks dead, you can easily pick the weapon they found off of their corpses.

destroyed.text: The Duskbringer ship explodes violently, securing your victory. Your Federation ally wraps up their fight with the Rebel not long after. You scrap your defunct foe as they finish.

deadCrew.text: The final Duskbringer explodes, cursing your name as they die. Once you are victorious, your Federation ally wraps up their fight with the Rebel. You scrap your defunct foe as they finish.

destroyed.text: The strange Rock ship is dead. Aboard the wreck you find the pieces of a sector map, but not enough to make anything out.

deadCrew.text: While scrapping the strange Rock ship, you find a map of the entire sector. You enter it into your computer and continue with your salvaging.

destroyed.text: The Duskbringers have been bested by you once again, and their ship is yours for scrapping.

deadCrew.text: The Duskbringers have been bested by you once again, and their ship is yours for scrapping.

destroyed.text: The Duskbringers have been defeated, despite the considerable strength of their ship. You scrap its remains.

deadCrew.text: The Duskbringers have been defeated, despite the considerable strength of their ship. You scrap its remains.

destroyed.text: The station has been felled thanks to you. With nothing left to guard the Auto-ship, you carefully undock it.

deadCrew.text: The station has been felled thanks to you. With nothing left to guard the Auto-ship, you carefully undock it.

surrender.text: "Stop, stop! We're not your enemy! Stop firing and we can explain!"

event.text: "Look, we're not from Universe 1. Not all of us support those genocidal reality-hoppers. I joined the Rebellion during the Civil War because I thought Vance would finally bring lasting peace to the galaxy - but this? This is just too far. We're on our way to deliver supplies to a Duskbringer outpost in the sector. We could spare some of the supplies if that'll satiate you."

choice.text: Ex-Rebel or not, we aren't letting any supplies get into the hands of the Duskbringers!
Rebel scum is Rebel scum. There'll be no excuses.

destroyed.text: You've successfully killed the Duskbringer ship, and it appears the other pirates have done the same with their opponents. It doesn't take long until the pirates overtake the Duskbringers, and the remaining ships from the squadron flee.

deadCrew.text: You've successfully killed the Duskbringer ship, and it appears the other pirates have done the same with their opponents. It doesn't take long until the pirates overtake the Duskbringers, and the remaining ships from the squadron flee.
