name: FILLER_EQUINOID
text: Scanners are showing intelligent life forms on a nearby planet. No match for them can be found in the database.

event.text: You land a small shuttle in an enormous field, whose only occupants are small, brightly colored, six-legged, horse-like animals. Could they be what your scans picked up?

choice.text: Bring some of the creatures on board to sell.

event.text: This isn't the time for exobiology. You head back to the ship.

choice.text: (Nights) "Oi, lisssten up you freakin' horssse thingsss!"

event.text: Nights drunkenly stumbles forwards, shouting at the horses randomly. This scares them away, but fortunately you follow them back to the location of a crash site where you find a barely alive Engi Defender and a lot of scrap. Nights might be a hungover idiot, but at least he accidentally brings you into a lot of beneficial situations.

After a moment, your crew tells you that these are simple beings, who enjoy a peaceful life. Your Slug puts the horse into a calm state, and you even manage to bring back a specimen. Without any fear of the horses, you explore further and even find old wreckage on the planet of an Engi ship, though the inhabitant is dead.

After a moment, your crew tells you that these are simple beings, who enjoy a peaceful life. Your Shell puts the horse into a calm state, and you even manage to bring back a specimen. Without any fear of the horses, you explore further and even find old wreckage on the planet of an Engi ship, though the inhabitant is dead.

choice.text: (Jerry) Jerry wants to pet a horse.

event.text: You shrug and let Jerry go. To your surprise, he returns in the shuttle with one of the horses with him. Who the hell even is this guy?

choice.text: (Crystal Equinoid) Let your Equinoid freely roam.

event.text: You drop your Equinoid off on the planet. Though clearly different to the other Equinoids, it gets along perfectly fine with them. When it eventually returns to your ship, it is accompanied by another Equinoid. Seems it found a mate by pure chance.

You land your ship near one of the herds and let them roam around. Unfortunately, they scare off the other horses. Dismayed, your Cyberpony roams around regardless, and soon finds a well obscured crashed Engi ship. Inside is a Separatist, and they seem more than pleased to have a way off this planet.

choice.text: (Tamed Equinoid) Let your Equinoid freely roam.
(Untamed Equinoid) Let your Equinoid freely roam.

event.text: You drop your Equinoid off on the planet, and it eventually mingles with the rest of the herd. Unfortunately, you're not able to call it back. What were you expecting to happen?

removeCrew.text: Your Equinoid is not dead, and thus cannot legally be cloned. Assuming cloning regulations extend to non-sapient life forms.

choice.text: (Mind Control) Pacify the ponies and steal one.

event.text: Under the effects of the mind control the pony does nothing to resist you, allowing you to collect it with little difficulty.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Pacify the ponies and steal one.

event.text: Under the effects of the mind control weapon the pony does nothing to resist you, allowing you to collect it with little difficulty.
You ignore the readings and prepare to move on.

name: FILLER_EQUINOID_SELL
text: The seemingly docile creatures quickly turn violent when you show your hostile intentions. They stampede with terrifying force, charging the ship before you have time to react.

name: FILLER_SICK
text: You arrive to find a small research station putting out a distress signal. There is no response to your hails.

choice.text: Dock with the station and investigate.
You cannot risk going in alone.

event.text: It's not worth risking your crew like this.

choice.text: (Boarding Drone) Use a drone to investigate.

event.text: The logs show that a number of the crew on this station died from the effects of a parasite that caused cannibalistic notions in the human mind. Knowing it is far too risky to enter, you stick to salvaging the exterior.

name: FILLER_PLAGUE
text: You arrive near a damaged and dilapidated space station. It appears to be abandoned but you detect faint life signatures on board.

choice.text: Board the station and look for survivors.
The AI advises against boarding without any reinforcements aboard your ship.

event.text: While waiting for the FTL drive to charge, you skirt around the edge of the station and collect some scrap.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Your Slug senses lifeforms aboard the ship, none of them look promising.

event.text: Following your Slug's advice, you decide to avoid the station. While waiting for the FTL drive to charge, you skirt around the edge of the station and collect some scrap.

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Your Shell senses lifeforms aboard the ship, none of them look promising.

event.text: Following your Shell's advice, you decide to avoid the station. While waiting for the FTL drive to charge, you skirt around the edge of the station and collect some scrap.

choice.text: (Lifeform Scanners) Run scans on the station.

event.text: Scans show quite the depressing scene inside. Most of the crew are already dead, and they show signs of disease. It's best not to go anywhere near the station, and just scrap the hull instead.

Human corpses are scattered across the station. You find the source of the signal, a lone survivor that locked themselves in a storage closet. They desperately cling onto your drone while sobbing. Knowing what a traumatic experience it must have been, you run some evaluations but ultimately decide they're stable enough to be of help. You quickly retreat with them in tow back to the ship, and hope they can recover enough to be of some use.
You decide you need what supplies you have.

name: FILLER_EXPLORE
text: Scans reveal a large asteroid field nearby. Short-range scanners may discover useful materials while we wait for the FTL to recharge.

choice.text: Too dangerous. We'll just wait for the FTL to charge.

event.text: You move on from the asteroid field.

choice.text: (Scrap Recovery Arm) Attempt to mine the asteroids.

event.text: You carefully extract as much usable material as possible from the nearest asteroids while waiting for the FTL to charge.

choice.text: (Magnetic Arm) Attempt to mine the asteroids.

event.text: Your magnetic arm is not well suited to the task, but it is able to salvage a very small portion of space junk drifting around nearby.

choice.text: (Mining Equipment) Attempt to mine the asteroids.

event.text: You carefully extract as much usable material as possible from the nearest asteroids while waiting for the FTL to charge.

choice.text: (Beam Drone) Attempt to mine the asteroids. [-1|]

event.text: You carefully extract as much usable material as possible from the nearest asteroids while waiting for the FTL to charge.

name: FILLER_SELL_DRONES
text: You see a Union space station with heavy damage. You receive a message, "We've been hit hard by the war. We need more drone parts to speed up our repairs. We'll buy some from you if you have extra."

event.text: "Thank you for your business."
"Thank you for your business."
"Thank you for your business."
You have no need for the station's services.
The station is surprised by your sudden hostility, but prepares to defend themselves.

name: FILLER_SELL_MISSILES
text: There is a black market hub here. You receive a message, "These are dangerous times. If you have extra military-grade explosives, we'll gladly pay you for them."

event.text: "Thank you, this will help greatly."
"Thank you, this will help greatly."
"Thank you, this will help greatly."
You have no need for the station's services.
The station is surprised by your sudden hostility, but prepares to defend themselves.
You decide you have nothing you want to trade.
The ship is shocked at your sudden offense. It readies what little defense it's equipped with.

name: FILLER_REFUEL
text: A ship refueling station is stationed at this beacon. We can purchase fuel here.

event.text: "Thank you for your business."
"Thank you for your business."
"Thank you for your business."
You have no need for their services.
The station is surprised by your sudden hostility, but prepares to defend itself.

name: FILLER_REPAIR
text: You see a small station fitted with hundreds of Repair drones. You receive an automated message, "We don't know who you are and we don't care, but this is the right place for some ship repair!"

event.text: "Thank you for your business, no refunds!"
"Thank you for your business, no refunds!"
"Thank you for your business, no refunds!"
You have no need for the station's services.
The Auto-station wastes no time powering up its defenses.

name: FILLER_SOLARWRECK
text: The charred remains of a ship well beyond recognition drifts near the sun at this beacon. It won't be long until the strong gravitational pull of the star pulls it in, but there might be enough time for you to salvage a chunk of it.

choice.text: (Hull Armor) We can approach with little risk.
Ignore the wreck, the sun is enough to deal with.

event.text: You ignore the crew.

name: FILLER_HELP_MINERS
text: You come across an asteroid mining colony. They message you immediately, saying, "Greetings. Our supplies of mining explosives have run out ever since the Rebels blockaded this system. Do you have any extra explosives?"

choice.text: (Explosive Replicator) Use the replicator to synthesize the missiles for them.
(Missile Weapon) Offer to blast through the mine with your Launcher.

event.text: "I don't think you quite understand. I understand your... enthusiasm... but it's not exactly 'union friendly' to use military ballistic weapons in mining operations. Perhaps it's best we don't make any trades..."

choice.text: (Bomb Weapon) Offer to solve their problem by using a controlled explosion from your bomb. [-1}]

event.text: "Curious. I did not consider the practicality of using a bomb for such matters. I suppose it should be safe enough. You have my permission."

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) Offer to teach them how to construct makeshift explosives.

event.text: Your commando, being both an experienced arsonist and knowledgeable in the ways of explosives, explains to the miners how the Lost Suns have been using "recycled" ammunition to save costs. Thoroughly impressed by this knowledge, the colony's leader grants you access to some of their latest spoils.
"I understand. Good luck out there. We'll try to make do with what we have."

choice.text: (Upg. Sensors) Use your Sensors to scan the wreckage.

event.text: You scan the battlefield, and with the aid of your Sensors, you are able to salvage a moderate amount of material from the wreckage. You prepare to jump.

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Use your Sensors to scan the wreckage.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Use your Sensors to scan the wreckage.
Ignore the wreckage and continue on.

event.text: You ignore the wreckage.

"Thank you! We need to scan this planet for life before we can begin terraforming, but our sensors can't get the necessary power to scan through this atmosphere. We've got a schedule to keep, any chance you can help?"

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Set sensors to maximum and scan.
(Bonus Power Crew) Send your crewman to overcharge their systems.
(Osmian Crew) Generate a hologram to overcharge their systems.
(Slug Crew) Check if your Slug senses any presence.
(Telepathic Shell) Check if your Shell senses any presence.

event.text: "We understand. Best of luck on your mission, sir!"

name: FILLER_CONFUSED_MANTIS
text: You receive a hail from a nearby civilian Engi vessel. Their Captain appears on your screen: "Strange bug. Can you assist in debugging?"

event.text: "Federation vessel has made fatal logic error. Virus != present. Bug refers to: insectoid. Problem-solving skills of squishy organics preferred to stringent Harmony protocols."

choice.text: Explain that you can't do any programming and leave.

event.text: The Engi try to convince you that you don't understand, but you insist and cease communications.

name: FILLER_CONFUSED_MANTIS_PROBLEM
text: "Found malfunctioning Free Mantis. Believes it is human. Will receive input only from human or fellow Free Mantis. Danger Evaluation: Extremely High. Provide assistance."

choice.text: Send a shuttle with an away team to help.
You have no one around to assist.
Leave them, a cornered Mantis is too dangerous.
(Human Crew) Send your human crewmember to communicate with the Mantis.

event.text: The Mantis is grateful to see 'another human', and introduces himself as Robert Smith. He explains he's from a nearby human colony and would appreciate being returned there.

choice.text: (Free Mantis Crew) Send your Mantis crewmember to communicate with the Mantis.

event.text: The sight of a Free Mantis calms down the cornered insectoid, who introduces himself as Robert Smith. He explains he's from a nearby human colony and would appreciate being returned there.

choice.text: (Mantis Crew) Send your Mantis crewmember to communicate with the Mantis.

event.text: The Mantis is terrified at the sight of your crewmember. He lashes out, instantly killing your crew and turning on the Engi. You have no choice but to leave.

removeCrew.text: Fortunately, dismemberment is one of the many cases your Clone Bay readily covers. That doesn't make it hurt any less, but your crew are probably used to it by now.

choice.text: (Hive Elite) Your elite Mantis is a natural leader. Send them in.

event.text: The Engi are visibly uncomfortable in the presence of your Mantis. They enter the room where the troublemaker is kept, and in a matter of minutes has slit their throat. When they return, they explain: "It was one of brainless Free Mantis types. Only solution was to kill." The Engi seem satisfied and pay you for your "efforts".

choice.text: (Mind Control) Use your Mind Control system to calm him down.

event.text: The Mantis calms down and communicates thanks to the Engi and yourself for helping. He requests to be dropped off at a nearby planet, at the human colony where he was raised. They are grateful for his return and offer a reward.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) Use your Mind Control weapon to calm him down.

event.text: The Mantis calms down and communicates thanks to the Engi and yourself for helping. He requests to be dropped off at a nearby planet, at the human colony where he was raised. They are grateful for his return and offer a reward.

name: FILLER_CONFUSED_MANTIS_HOME
text: The colony is a mining operation that specializes in FTL fuel. Robert's family, the head engineers, are excited to see him, and are very grateful for his return. Apparently he ran away to 'join the Federation' like his older brother, but was never accepted onto a ship.

choice.text: Offer him a position on your ship.

event.text: He graciously accepts, having always wanted to serve in the Federation.

choice.text: Ask if they can take a look at your engines.

event.text: They are happy to take a look, and are able to offer some suggestions for improvements.

name: FILLER_REFUGEE_NO_DISTRESS
text: Your sensors have picked up a refugee ship drifting through the system, no doubt one of many fleeing the Rebel advance. It doesn't appear to have detected you... or else it is trying to avoid notice.

event.text: You're wary of the refugees but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: FILLER_CROPS
text: Scans show a remote settlement being blockaded by a pirate ship. The ship hastily messages you, "Stay out of this, or you'll be next!...Concentrate fire on..."

event.text: "You asked for it!" They pull away from the planet and move in to engage.
It's just not possible to save every civilian affected by this war. You prepare to jump.

choice.text: (Fire Weapon) Show the pirate how to intimidate settlers: burn their crops!

event.text: The pirate watches as you start to light the meager crops on fire. In a few moments the settlement surrenders, offering tribute to leave them alone. The pirate seems impressed.

choice.text: (Ballistic Fire Weapon) Show the pirate how to intimidate settlers: start fires in their crude dwellings. [-1}]

event.text: The pirate watches as you teleport an incendiary explosive into the settlement. As the settlers scramble to put out the fires, their rudimentary planetary defenses power down. Forcing their surrender was laughably easy, but the pirate seems impressed with your tactics and agrees to share the settlement's 'tribute'.

choice.text: (Particle Tech) Show the pirate how to intimidate settlers: burn their crops!

event.text: The pirate watches as you start to light the meager crops on fire. In a few moments the settlement surrenders, offering tribute to leave them alone. The pirate seems impressed.

name: PIRATE_STATION_CROPS_RESULT
text: With the pirates gone you signal the station. "We appreciate what you've done, but there'll just be another ship looking to profit from our isolation soon enough. Sorry we can't give you more."

name: FILLER_CLAIRVOYANT
text: The yellow ship at this beacon startles you, and you realise it's a Clairvoyant! You assume it must be lost, being so far away from a nebula.

event.text: The Slugs, confident in their ability to take you, make no attempt to get away and engage you directly in combat.
"Eugh... Federation... Yessss, we are lossst. No need to rub it in. We were chassssing ssssome filthy Fed- er.... criminalsss and wandered too far. Much too far. Could you ssspare ssssome fuel?"
The Slug quickly scoops up the fuel and brings it back to his ship.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug make the trade.

event.text: "One of ussss? My missstake... I did not think fellow Kleptocrianssss journeyed out thissss far intentionally..."
Knowing you have a Slug aboard your vessel, the Clairvoyants seem much more open, and you feel confident enough to accept their payment without suspecting some kind of trick.

choice.text: (Upg. Weapons) Keep your weapons powered while making the trade.

event.text: "I sssee you flexing your weaponssss over there, Feddy boy. You can put thossse away, I jusssst need the fuel..."
Knowing you're armed to the teeth, you doubt the Clairvoyants will try anything, and you feel confident enough to accept their payment without suspecting some kind of trick.
It's too risky approaching an Elite vessel like this.

name: FILLER_EXPLODED
text: A critically damaged civilian carryship is nearby. Scans show their life support is beyond non-functional, and they won't live long.

choice.text: Dock with the ship and save as many of the crew as you can.
(Lifeform Scanners) Run a scan on the ship, just to be certain.
(Upg. Sensors) Run a scan on the ship, just to be certain.
It's too late. We should just carry on.

event.text: There's no chance the civilians survived that explosion. You move on.

name: FILLER_TIMER
text: You're hailed by a desperate civilian station. "Please, you have to help! Our scanners detect large asteroids approaching our station, but we're defenseless against them!"

event.text: You find the asteroids in question. You only have so much time until they hit the station.

choice.text: (Hull Armor) Block the asteroid with your vessel.

event.text: As the asteroid comes closer it's clear you won't get away as unscathed as you had hoped, but fortunately it's still recoverable. The station is grateful and offers a reward.

It only takes one shot from your weapon to blast the asteroid back into space, scattering tiny chunks in all directions as if it were made of glass. The civilians in the station cheer for your quick and easy success and reward you.
Too dangerous. We'll just wait for the FTL to charge.

name: CIVILIAN_ASTEROID_APPROACHING_WIN
text: "Thank you for your help! We'll have to make sure this won't happen in the future. But for now, here's payment for your help."

name: CIVILIAN_ASTEROID_APPROACHING_FAIL
text: You were not able to stop the asteroids in time. They smash into the civilian station, sending debris in every direction. Some of it hits your hull, causing minor damage.

choice.text: This is a great opportunity. Let's dock and see if we can find valuable supplies.
This is a huge risk. The AI advises against boarding the vessel.
We're in a hurry, let's just quickly pull some scrap off the ship.
Something is off here, let's just leave.

event.text: You ignore the abandoned wreck and fly away.

name: FILLER_GHOSTSHIP_SCRAP
text: You recover what you can before making preparations to jump away.

name: FILLER_GHOSTSHIP_BOARDED
text: The Ghosts follow your crew-members back on board the ship!

name: FILLER_ARGEONN_SALESMAN
text: A ship with conspicuous Argeonn markings is orbiting a nearby moon, broadcasting a simple message claiming to have equipment available for sale.

choice.text: Attack him before he can attack!

event.text: You raise your weapons and attack the pirate!
This seems far too sketchy to trust the offer. You ignore the smuggler.

name: CONTACT_PIRATE_SALESMAN
text: The ship responds: "Come in, under the banner of Argeonn I welcome you! I have many things, many things... would you care to take a look?"

event.text: As soon as you start to reverse your ship, the pirate reveals hidden weaponry and sets off in pursuit. You'll have to fight him to escape!

choice.text: (Slug Crew) "Sssir, we can dock, but I sssensse that we better plan on making a purchassse..."
(Hacking) Disable their Weapon system before docking.

event.text: You receive a hail as soon as your Hacking system finishes: "What have you done!? You can never trust a Federation ship! Here, take your 'standard toll'. I really should do business elsewhere, scum."

choice.text: (Targeting Jammer) Disable their Weapon system before docking.

event.text: You receive a hail as soon as your jamming takes effect: "What have you done!? You can never trust a Federation ship! Here, take your 'standard toll'. I really should do business elsewhere, scum."

name: DOCK_DRONE_SALESMAN
text: A human in an exquisite suit meets you on board. "Welcome to my ship! We specialize in drones of all kinds, can I interest you in any?"

event.text: "Many thanks for taking this off my hands! Just a word of advice... try not to let the authorities see you with it for another couple jumps."

"Ah, I'm sorry to hear that! Pleasant journeys." Once back to the helm, a series of explosions rocks your ship. The pirate ship has powered its weapons! You receive a message, "You shouldn't waste people's time Captain!"

choice.text: Move in to examine the station.

event.text: You decide it's not worth the time to examine.

choice.text: Fend for yourself, attack and escape.

event.text: You move in to attack the Rebel ship.

choice.text: Bribe the Rebels to release the civilian ships.
(MFK Ace Crew) Pretend to be a Rebel ship.

event.text: Rebel forces are bloated with washups, conscripts, or disheartened officers who are only in its ranks because their reality was conquered by Rebels first. The Rebel running the checkpoint barely even glances at your MFK Ace's outdated Rebel ID before deciding to let you past.

choice.text: Take a chance and request they free some civilians.

event.text: At first the Rebels don't buy it, but you manage to pull some trickery to convince them that several of the civilians were cleared for release. The officer in charge is satisfied with this at first while you start taking civilians on board, but eventually grows impatient and decides he's had enough of your ruse.

choice.text: Take this chance to do something aboard the ship.
(Engineer Crew) Pretend to be a Rebel ship.

event.text: Rebel forces are bloated with washups, conscripts, or disheartened officers who are only in its ranks because their reality was conquered by Rebels first. The Rebel running the checkpoint barely even glances at your Engineer's outdated Rebel ID before deciding to let you past.

choice.text: Take a chance and request they free some civilians.

event.text: At first the Rebels don't buy it, but you manage to pull some trickery to convince them that several of the civilians were cleared for release. The officer in charge is satisfied with this at first while you start taking civilians on board, but eventually grows impatient and decides he's had enough of your ruse.

choice.text: Take this chance to do something aboard the ship.

event.text: You engage the Rebel ship.

choice.text: (MFK Ace Crew) Pretend to be a Rebel ship and deliver the supplies yourself.

event.text: "Oh, are you the one command sent to start making these deliveries? Great, take these and bring them down there to those colonists. They'll be waiting for you."

You fly down to the planet surface where you drop off the supplies. The colonists are confused as they don't recognize you, but they're glad for the help and offer some repairs and some work on your weapons system.

choice.text: Wait and steal the supplies from the civilians.

event.text: You decide not to bother the Rebels.

choice.text: Go looking for the Rebel ship.
No time to search, you prepare to jump away.

event.text: You decide not to go hunting for Rebels.

choice.text: (Upg. Sensors) Perform a scan of the area.

event.text: You quickly find the Rebel ship's location and move to intercept.
You find the Rebel ship hiding on a nearby asteroid. You are able to get a shot off and permanently disable their engines before they notice you.
You find the Rebel ship hiding on a nearby asteroid. You are able to get a shot off and permanently disable their engines before they notice you.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_ABANDONED
text: You have encountered a refugee ship drifting in space. It looks as if it was fleeing the Rebel advance and ran out of fuel. Its distress beacon is active, but you're not sure anyone is on board, and its communications seem to be down.

choice.text: Unless you desire to be ambushed by a threat, you're not going out there on your own.
(Boarding Drone) Use a drone to investigate.

event.text: You don't take chances with ghost ships.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_REFUGEE
text: You have encountered a refugee ship drifting in space. It looks as if it was fleeing the Rebel advance and ran out of fuel. Its distress beacon is active, but you're not sure anyone is on board.

event.text: You're wary of the refugees but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_DISEASE
text: You locate a nearby human mining colony where an unknown disease has spread virulently. They are setting up a quarantine to contain it but a riot has broken out.

choice.text: Send in your crew to help control the crowds.
Your vessel currently lacks the manpower required to handle a crowd.
Ignore their request and move on.

event.text: Unfortunately your mission is too important and you're not willing to risk your crew. You prepare to move on.

choice.text: (Rock Crew) Send your Rock crew-member to prevent a riot.

event.text: It's unlikely the Rock's impressive immune system is susceptible to a human virus so you send it in. It is able to intimidate the workers long enough for the colony forces to set up a quarantine. Their leaders offer a reward and assure you they will try to find a cure as soon as possible.

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Send your Engi to calm down the infected.

event.text: With no fear of catching the disease, your Engi crewmember helps reassure and organize the infected humans. Calmed by its extensive knowledge of human physiology, the infected submit to the quarantine in the hopes that a cure can be found soon. The colony leaders offer a reward for helping to prevent an ugly incident.

choice.text: (Ghost Crew) Send your Ghost to calm down the infected.

event.text: Because of your Ghost's gaseous nature, they have little fear of catching the disease. However, rather than calming the crowds, your Ghost sends them into even greater panic. Assuming the entity is an omen of death, it takes some time for your Ghost to reinstate order. Going along with the crowd, they play with that idea, affirming to the colonists that if they do not listen to their leaders, he will return to reap their souls. This is surprisingly effective, and you're paid for your help.

choice.text: (Obelisk Crew) Send your Obelisk to calm down the infected.

event.text: The rioters are silenced by the strange box shaped figure. Thoroughly distracted by the foreign creature, the crowd does not notice the riot control is able to sneak in and neutralize the rioters. The law enforcement offers a reward for your troubles, as well as your effective methods resulting in no lives lost.

choice.text: (Medical Drone) Send your drone to treat the infected. [-1|]

event.text: Being highly advanced and designed for situations like these, your drone moves through the crowds, dispensing tissues and lolipops, and administering a "treatment" of pure water. The crowd is thoroughly convinced that this has actually helped them, and returns back to their homes. The law enforcement thanks you.

choice.text: (Medical Crew) Send your crew to treat the infected.

event.text: Knowing just how to handle this, your medic dons a mask and moves about administering a "treatment" of pure water. The crowd is thoroughly convinced that this has actually helped them, and returns back to their homes. The law enforcement thanks you.

choice.text: (Adv. Medbay) Use your Medbay to help synthesize a cure.

event.text: Your military-grade medical computers are easily able to isolate the cause of the virus, a previously unknown spore that was unearthed during excavations. You are quickly able to inform the colony's leaders of your success in reverse engineering a cure.
"Thank you so much! We don't have the funds to hire outside help and it would have taken our staff weeks to figure that out. Here, take this as payment!"

choice.text: (Med-bot Dispersal) Use the Nano med-bots to accelerate the dispersal of the cure.

event.text: You reconfigure your ship's Nano dispersal system. In a matter of minutes all of the workers are cured. The leaders can hardly believe what you have achieved. They offer you what they can as payment.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_FIRE
text: You find the source of the distress call, a small research station. It appears a small laboratory fire got out of control and is threatening to destroy the station. Their fire suppression system is not responding.

choice.text: Send your crew in a shuttle to help put out the fire.
You have no one aboard to handle a station-wide fire.
Dock and try to rescue the survivors.

event.text: You coldly shut off communications and prepare to leave. Your crew seems upset but you assure them that nothing could have been done.
You coldly shut off communications and prepare to leave. You're upset about the situation, but the ship AI assures you that nothing could have been done.

Your crew tears through the airlock directly into the fire. You've never seen someone move that fast. It disperses as much fire suppressant as possible into the heart of the blaze and eventually the fires start to die down.
With most of the fire under control, the scientists are able to help secure the station. They offer you their sincere gratitude and a generous reward.

choice.text: (Elite Crew) Send your elite crew-member in.

event.text: Your crew, armed with years of elite training for situations like this, finds their way into the station and begins to suppress the fire.
With most of the fire under control, the scientists are able to help secure the station. They offer you their sincere gratitude and a generous reward.

choice.text: (Repair Drone) Send your Repair drone into the fire.

event.text: You send the Repair drone in and it methodically puts out the fires. Once it has made some progress, the rest of your crew helps to secure the station.
They offer you their sincere gratitude; the station would have surely been destroyed without your assistance. They transfer a small reward and an additional drone schematic.

choice.text: (Extinguishers) Use your tech to suppress the fire.

event.text: You quickly grab some extra extinguishers from the storage and attach a hose to the suppression system, then move through the station, putting out the larger fires.
They offer you their sincere gratitude; the station would have surely been destroyed without your assistance. They transfer a small reward and an additional drone schematic.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_SATELLITE
text: The distress signal is coming from a small space station orbiting an uninhabited planet. Their satellite defense system has gone haywire and their repair crew can't approach without being fired on. They're looking for help to fix or disable it.

event.text: You consider your options.

choice.text: Simply fire on the defense system from a distance.

event.text: You use your ion weaponry to disable the gun long enough for their repair crews to fix it. They message you, "I've never seen a weapon like that before! Thanks for your help. Please accept this reward."
Your Energy weapon ends up causing more damage to the defense system instead of ionizing it. No one was harmed but they don't seem happy with your solution.

choice.text: (Cloaking) Use your Cloaking to disable the system.

event.text: You use your ship's Cloaking to try to prevent the defense system from getting a lock. However before you are able to safely disable the system your cloaking gives out and you are forced to destroy the satellite. No one was harmed but they don't seem happy with your solution.

choice.text: (Upg. Cloaking) Use your Cloaking to disable the system.

event.text: You use your ships Cloaking to prevent the defense system from getting a lock. Once closer, you hasten to disable the system without damaging it. It was a sloppy job but they appreciate it and offer a reward.

choice.text: (Adv. Cloaking) Use your Cloaking to disable the system.

event.text: Your ship's Advanced Cloaking allows you to approach the defense system without an issue. Once closer, you are able to safely disable the system. They thank you for your help and offer a reward.

choice.text: (Engi Crew) Remotely repair its targeting system.

event.text: Your crew-member is able to remotely fix the glitch in the defense AI, allowing the repair crew to close in and finish the job. The station gives you its thanks along with a reward.

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Remotely repair its targeting system.

event.text: Your crew-member is able to remotely fix the glitch in the defense AI, allowing the repair crew to close in and finish the job. The station gives you its thanks along with a reward.

choice.text: (Lanius Crew) Your crew offers to help.

event.text: Your Lanius crewman appears to have a solution. The Lanius simply jumps out of the airlock towards the satellite. Apparently its lack of heat signatures renders it hidden from the satellite's targeting sensors. Once there he simply melts it down into scrap. You quickly pick him up and prepare to jump before the station can question your methods.

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Block the satellite's targeting capabilities.

event.text: With the satellite unable to lock onto anything, the repair crew move in and finish the job. The station gives you its thanks along with a reward.
You can't help them so you prepare to move on.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_MINER
text: You arrive at the distress beacon near a small asteroid belt and find a ship with pirate markings partially crushed between two large rocks. It must have been illegally mining the belt without proper equipment.

choice.text: Try to dislodge the ship by shooting at the rocks.
Destroy and loot the ship. They're just pirates.
(Damaging Beam Weapon) Carefully cut the ship out.

event.text: You use your beam to make a few precision cuts in the asteroid. The ship gives a quick burst of thrust and the rock crumbles away. They thank you and offer some of the resources they have collected.

choice.text: (Damaging Pinpoint Weapon) Attempt to meticulously cut out the pirate ship.

event.text: In a rather baffling decision to the rest of your crew, you take the increduously long time to chip away at the asteroid with your Pinpoint. You're certain the fleet has caught up by now and you've barely made any impact, giving you no choice but to abandon the pirate ship.

choice.text: (Beam Drone) Have your drone cut the ship out.

event.text: You program the drone to work carefully around the trapped ship. In a short time it allows the ship to easily slip out of its cage. They thank you and offer some of the resources they have collected.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_ESCORT
text: Once you arrive at the location of the distress call a civilian ship hails you, "Thanks for responding to our beacon. Our FTL navigation has gone haywire and we can't plot a course to the nearest depot to get it fixed. Could you lead us there?"

event.text: "Take this bit of scrap as a down-payment. We'll use your jump signatures to follow you. You're really helping us out here."
"Alright... If you're not going that way I guess it can't be helped. We'll just wait for the next ship to come."
The civilians are shocked by your sudden hostility, but have no chance to escape.

choice.text: (Advanced Navigation) Have your navigation software calculate and upload route instructions to their ship.

event.text: "We're receiving your transmission... Wow, I didn't know that chain-jumping was possible with this class of ship. We'll get back in a single jump! Thank you so much, please accept this."
You power up your weapons and engage the Rebel ship.

choice.text: (Targeting Jammer) Disable the Rebel weapons so the Fed ship can escape.

event.text: Your targeting jammer locks onto the Rebel's systems, shutting their weapons offline. Still not having seen you, the Rebels struggle to get their weapons back while you slip away to the other side of the system with the Federation ship you saved.

choice.text: (Flares) Use the flares to make a distraction so the Fed ship can escape.

event.text: A confident shot from the flare dispenser launches the small disc right onto the visor of the Rebel vessel, temporarily blinding and distracting the captain. The Federation vessel escapes with you to the other side of the system.
The Rebel's preoccupation with the Federation ship allows you to slip away undetected. However you can't help but feel you should have helped them.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_COLLISION
text: You follow the distress beacon to a tiny asteroid belt. You find a small ship struggling to maneuver through the field.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_COLLISION_2
text: They respond: "Help! Our shields are down and we won't last long!"

choice.text: Try to shield their ship with yours.
Don't risk our ship. Leave them to their fate.
(Defense Drone) Use a Defense Drone to protect their ship. [-1|]
(Overcharger Drone) Use an Overcharger Drone to protect their ship. [-1|]
(Repair Drone) Send a Repair Drone to fix their Shields. [-1|]
(Repair Cluster) Launch a repair bomb into their Shields. [-1}]

event.text: Your bomb immediately brings their shields back online before either of you can take any further damage. They offer you some military supplies as thanks for saving them.

choice.text: (Teleporter) Offer to beam them aboard your ship.
(Hull Armor) Shield their ship with yours and escort them out.

event.text: You succeed in preventing them from being entirely destroyed, your improved hull taking the brunt of the asteroids that make it past your defenses. They offer you some of the scrap and fuel they were mining out of the asteroid as thanks.

choice.text: (Repair-Bot Dispersal) Repair their shields with the nanobots.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_RESCUE
text: The distress beacon is coming from a civilian ship. It appears it is being chased by a pirate.

event.text: You power up your weapons and engage the pirate ship.
The fight brings them out of your immediate scanning range; however, after a time the distress calls stop.

choice.text: (Adv. Weapons) Fire a warning shot from your strongest weapon.
(Flares) Fire off a flare to distract the pirate.

event.text: Confused, the pirate didn't expect to find another ship at the beacon. Assuming the flare was just a warning shot and you're packing a bigger arsenal, they back down and jump away/

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_STRANDED
text: It appears the distress beacon is coming from the surface of a nearby moon. Your sensors are picking up a single life form.

choice.text: Go down to the surface to investigate.

event.text: You have an important mission, you can't waste time investigating.
You give them the fuel.

choice.text: (Fuel Conserver) Show them how to wire up their own conserver.

event.text: You break out the manual for your conservation device and give it to the civilians. Whatever they throw together won't be nearly as efficient, but it should get them somewhere.

choice.text: (Emergency Manual) Teach the civilians how to produce fuel onboard.

event.text: You clone the data from the emergency manual and pass it onto the civilians. Whatever they throw together won't be cost efficient, but it should get them somewhere. This is digital piracy by the way. Scum.

choice.text: Apologize, wish them luck, and continue on.

event.text: "We understand... Please send help our way if you meet anyone trustworthy."
"Wait, what are you doing?" You ignore their cries for mercy and move in to attack.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_FACTORY
text: The source of the distress beacon appears not to be a ship, but a large factory. You can't see anything noticeably wrong, but it is definitely the right location.

event.text: Upon further inspection it is clear something is very wrong. A fire has broken out in the factory, and your ship's computers are being overloaded with signals as thousands of distress beacons are activated at once... it's a distress beacon factory!?

choice.text: Try to rescue any workers who might be trapped.
(Signal Diluter) Block out the signals and approach.

event.text: You feel immediate relief as the barrage of signals comes to an end. With that distraction out of the way, you manage to escort several of the workers onto your ship before you have to pull away to avoid the debris. Though you drop most off nearby, one offers to stay. Probably because it pays better than their old job, if you had to guess.

choice.text: (Fireproof Crew) Send in your crew to rescue the workers.

event.text: You might not be able to pull the ship close enough, but you can send your crew over by themselves. Your crew returns back on the shuttle with several other workers unharmed. Though you drop most off nearby, one offers to stay. Probably because it pays better than their old job, if you had to guess.

choice.text: Leave now before your ship is consumed by the inferno or your systems stop functioning entirely.

event.text: The business of this factory isn't a concern of yours.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_IDLE
text: At the source of the distress beacon you find an idle Mantis ship with all of its weapons offline. You aren't sure what happened, or what you should do.

event.text: You're wary of the Mantis but figure it's safe to do something on the ship.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_CRASH
text: You arrive at a lonely, starless planet drifting through space. A quick scan of the surface reveals a ship crash landed on the far side of the planet. It's in shambles, but there is a chance someone may have survived.

event.text: Even if someone did survive, there's not much you could do to help them.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_FEDERATION_LOST
text: Despite the distress beacon, no ship is in sight. Quite strange...

choice.text: (Adv. Sensors) Collect the logs of the most recent arrival.

event.text: You keep on moving with your mission.

name: FILLER_WORK_START
text: You are immediately contacted by a settlement, "Hello, travelers. Your ship seems to be outfitted for combat...care to take up a bit of mercenary work?"

event.text: You explain you aren't in the mercenary line of work.

name: FILLER_INVASION_START
text: You receive a request, "All of our military ships have been destroyed or damaged during the rebellion. However, there have been reports of a Mantis war camp only a few jumps from us. Can you help?"

choice.text: Pledge to do what you can.

event.text: "Thank you! If you can just give us a count on their numbers perhaps we can get the Rebels to help."
There's no way you are crazy enough to want to take on a Mantis war-band.

name: QUEST_FILLER_INVASION

unvisitedTooltip.text: You've been asked to survey a Mantis war camp.

text: You find the Mantis encampment but there are far too many of them to count accurately. You send a long range message back to the settlement with your findings but unfortunately there's not much you can do. It would be suicide to attack directly.

event.text: You fire at their fuel depot, but a shot from the surface rips the missile to shreds. They must have a planetary defense system set up already! You try to get away but a nearby patrol ship moves in to attack.

choice.text: (Fire Bomb) Teleport fire bombs into key structures.

event.text: It appears they have not set up a Teleporter disruption field yet. You deposit one bomb in a fuel depot and another in the barracks. Mantis comm channels fill with panicked chatter and you watch a number of structures go up in flames.
With most of their ships and forces focused on the chaos, you slip undetected to a nearby depot. You find some useful resources and an Engi slave who gladly accepts your liberation.

name: FILLER_QUEST_CREWDEAD_START
text: You arrive to find a number of ships convening around a station. There is some unencrypted chatter between the ships, you tune in and listen for anything interesting.

name: FILLER_QUEST_CREWDEAD_START_2
text: Overhearing their conversation, it seems that they need to take possession of an enemy ship intact.

event.text: If they wanted your help they would surely ask for it. You prepare to leave.

name: FILLER_QUEST_CREWDEAD_CONTINUE
text: They quickly scan your ship and say, "A bandit has made off with some very important cargo, though I doubt they have any understanding of what it is they stole. We need you to capture the ship intact. It is imperative to the mission that you do NOT destroy the vessel. Understand?"

event.text: "Great, we'll relay their coordinates. Remember, do NOT destroy that ship! Remember, we'll be right behind you."
"We understand. Hopefully we can find a solution to this on our own." You prepare to jump.

name: QUEST_CREWDEAD_MV

unvisitedTooltip.text: A band of merchants has asked you to recapture a ship hijacked by pirates.

text: You find the ship that you were asked to capture intact. You're not sure why, but they stressed that it's of great importance that you kill the crew WITHOUT destroying the ship.

name: FILLER_MERCHANT_REQUEST
text: You arrive at a populated sector. One merchant seems to be mass-broadcasting a request for a mercenary ship to aid him. Shall we respond?

event.text: You have no need to talk to the merchant.

name: FILLER_MERCHANT_DELIVER

unvisitedTooltip.text: You've been tasked to deliver droneparts to a station.

text: You arrive at the location given to you by the merchant. You are supposed to deliver drone parts to a station here.

name: FILLER_MERCHANT_INVESTIGATE

unvisitedTooltip.text: You've been asked to investigate on a missing delivery ship.

text: You arrive at the last known location of the merchant's delivery. You begin to scan for the lost ship.

name: FILLER_MERCHANT_INVESTIGATE_DELIVER

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the original delivery point of the lost cargo.

text: You find the station that had ordered your cargo. You drop it off and they respond, "Ignoring the fact that this is days late, we really appreciate that you delivered our materials. We realize how dangerous this sector is these days. Take this as payment."

event.text: "Great. Take this bit of fuel as a down-payment. We'll be one step behind you, following your jump signatures. Don't want to take any risks now, do we?"
"We understand. Not everyone is confident they can survive in these hostile times, let alone take the responsibility of protecting others."
The civilians are shocked by your sudden hostility, but have no chance to escape.

name: FILLER_DELIVERY
text: You jump to the beacon and discover an Argeonn vessel orbiting the beacon. They hail you with a proposal. "Say, that's a nice ship you got there... But I am sure a bit of scrap could make it run even better. Care to make some quick, easy cash?"

event.text: The smuggler wastes no time retaliating.

choice.text: This already sounds shady... move on.

event.text: You tell the smuggler you have no interest, and prepare to leave. They don't seem to mind.

name: MERCENARY_DELIVERY_INTEREST
text: "You see, I am a little short on fuel, but I still have to make a delivery of some... less than legal goods. If you can deliver them to these coordinates, the profits are all yours. Of course, if you have some spare fuel yourself, I'd pay you nicely for it."

event.text: They transmit the coordinates to your computer and teleport a very suspect-looking crate into your cargo hold. You scan it for explosives, just to be safe, but it's nothing more than Slug narcotics.

choice.text: Count us out. We're not smugglers.

event.text: "Your loss." They immediately activate their cloak, and presumably leave.

choice.text: Sell them a bit of your fuel.

event.text: You transfer over some fuel to the mercenaries. It's not much, but they seem satisfied, and in return they give you some scrap.

name: QUEST_MERCENARY_DELIVERY_END

unvisitedTooltip.text: You offered to transport the contraband of a smuggler to their client.

text: You arrive at the beacon. There's already a ship there, waiting for you. "So... got the goods?"

event.text: "Fine, fine." They pass over the payment, and you send over the narcotics. Easy money.

name: FILLER_STORE_RESCUE
text: Once you arrive at this populated region, you immediately pick up a distress signal. A small shuttle is asking anyone who'll listen for help protecting their family from a Rebel ship. Unsurprisingly, no one has yet responded to their request.

choice.text: See if you can assist them.

event.text: It seems that a small space dock has done something to anger the Rebels. The store there is run by his family and he pleads that you rescue them. He uploads the coordinates of the station to your navigation system.
You block the channel and prepare to jump as soon as possible.

name: QUEST_STORE
text: You follow the directions given to you and find the hidden space dock. The owner hails you, "I got a message that you were coming. I don't normally offer goods to strangers, but I'll make an exception. Take a look."

name: QUEST_STORE_RESCUE_MV

unvisitedTooltip.text: A Rebel ship is harassing a space dock at these coordinates.

text: Once you arrive at the beacon you detect a Rebel scout assaulting a compound on a nearby desolate moon.

choice.text: Engage the Rebel and rescue the space dock.

event.text: You lock onto the Rebel and move in to engage.
After a time the ship powers down its weapons and jumps away. No life-signs are detected on the moon.

name: FILLER_CONSTRUCTIONYARD
text: You come across a space station under construction. You receive a message from their command tower, "Greetings. We recently lost contact with a cargo ship that was set to deliver more construction materials. Could you help us figure out what happened to them?"

event.text: "Great. Thanks for your help. I've marked their last known coordinates and sent over some supplies to help you get there."
"I understand." Transmission has been cut.

choice.text: (Lanius Crew) Offer to have your crewmember help.

event.text: "Interesting. So this metal man can help us make some of these unique parts out of scrap? That would be a huge help." Your crewmember checks over the blueprints and quickly converts some of their base metal sheets into the specialized parts.
"Amazing! This robot thing could save us a ton of time. Could I buy it off you?"

choice.text: Ask your crew if they agree.

event.text: Once your Lanius crewmember understands the situation it appears to like the idea of assisting with construction in deep space. Much less dangerous. They offer you some goods in exchange.

removeCrew.text: Your Clone Bay obviously does not revive your crewmember since they did not die.

choice.text: Our crew is not for sale.

event.text: "A pity. In terms of payment, here's some of the scrap metal we don't need now that we've got necessary parts."

name: FILLER_HIVECHOICE
text: You find a Hive Mantis and a pirate ship battling each other. They both seem to recognize a threat in you. Either way, a battle is inevitable, but which do you engage head on?

event.text: You attack the Mantis head on, weapons blazing. Your attack doesn't faze them, but the pirate takes the chance to flee.
You engage the pirate, firing all you have towards them. Your show of aggression works, and the Mantis hurry away to find an easier fight.

choice.text: (Flares) Launch a flare and get away.

name: FILLER_AUTOCHOICE
text: An automated satellite rests nearby, with an Auto-guard protecting it. The satellite spots you and alerts the guard.

event.text: You prepare to attack the guard, knowing the satellite will be helpless against you without protection.

choice.text: Avoid the guard and destroy the station.

event.text: You slip past the guard ship and move to attack the satellite. It appears the guard is programmed to not go within a certain distance of the satellite and is unable to chase you.

choice.text: (Flares) Launch a flare and get away.

name: AUTO_CHOICE_SNEAK_WIN
text: With the station disabled, the guard deactivates. You scrap both ships.

name: FILLER_INFORMANT
text: "Oh good heavens, that's a Federation Renegade! If we turn their location to the Rebels, we'll be rich! Wait, did I just say that on open comms?" The nearby Union ship mutes themselves, then immediately activates their engines!

choice.text: Attack, we can't let them escape!

event.text: You can't let this information get out!
"The Federation is outdated in its philosophies! The Rebellion will offer us a glorious galaxy... nay, Multiverse free from xeno scum!"

Jerry knows what it's like to have been a Rebel, and he reveals the truths of the Rebellion's brutality and hypocrisy to the civilians. They're so taken-aback by this knowledge they even offer supplies towards your cause.

Your MFK Ace knows what it's like to have been a Rebel, and they reveal the truths of the Rebellion's brutality and hypocrisy to the civilians. They're so taken-aback by this knowledge they even offer supplies towards your cause.

Your Engineer knows what it's like to have been a Rebel, and they reveal the truths of the Rebellion's brutality and hypocrisy to the civilians. They're so taken-aback by this knowledge they even offer supplies towards your cause.

choice.text: Then you leave us no choice but to silence you.

event.text: You tried to reason with the civilians, but you've failed. The only option now is to kill them before they can escape!
"Alright, alright! You've made your point... and ours. This is why the Federation will fall, because when things go south, all you savages know is to use your guns!"

Your mind control won't last long enough to change their opinion of the Federation entirely, so instead you persuade them that informing the Rebels might put them in more danger than it's worth. Satisfied, you leave the civilians behind.
"You know what, I've changed my mind. The Federation rocks!" That was surprisingly simple...
"You know what, I've changed my mind. The Federation rocks!" That was surprisingly simple...

choice.text: (Engineer Crew) Pretend to be an undercover Rebel spy.

event.text: "Wooooow, you're a spy? That's soooo cool. I wish I was a spy. Wait, can I be one?! I'd love to help!" They eagerly come aboard, much to the discomfort of your crew. You aren't sure how long this cover story will last, but this person seems oblivious enough that maybe it'll just work out fine.
You aren't going to resort to murdering civilians, no matter the context. Unfortunately, this means the Rebels will only be faster at finding you.

name: FILLER_DISTRESS_ASB
text: You arrive at the source of the distress beacon, but find only a pirate! "Now, listen up. See that planet over there? On the surface is a series of active Anti-Ship Battery systems that I am now in control of. I am the only one stopping them from firing on you, and I don't really have a reason to keep doing that... but I think we can make a mutually beneficial deal here..."

event.text: "A wise, wise choice captain. I'll keep those ASBs offline... for now at least..."
"Tsk tsk. Well, I did warn you..." The pirate wasn't lying - the nearby ASB systems activate immediately and lock onto your location!

choice.text: (Signal Diluter) Disable his control over the ASB systems.

event.text: "Wait... wait! What have you done!? God damn it! You have no idea how hard it was to gain access to those! You're gonna pay for this!"

choice.text: (Upg. Hacking) Take access of the systems yourself and redirect them onto the pirate.

event.text: "Tsk tsk. Well, I did warn y-... wait, why are those aiming at me?! What have you done? Crap, you've ruined everything!"

choice.text: (Saboteur Crew) Take access of the systems yourself and redirect them onto the pirate.

event.text: "Tsk tsk. Well, I did warn y-... wait, why are those aiming at me?! What have you done? Crap, you've ruined everything!"

choice.text: (Upg. Mind Control) "Convince" him to keep the ASBs offline.

event.text: "Mmmm, you make a good point. Tee hee!" The pirate immediately slumps over. Apparently the mind control had some very adverse effects on him. We better get out of here before he wakes up.

name: FINISH_BEACON_FLEET_ELITE_REAL
text: You've found the exit beacon but the Rebels got here first! You must survive long enough to be able to jump to the next sector.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FINISH_BEACON_FLEET_ACE_REAL
text: You've found the exit beacon but the Rebels got here first! You must survive long enough to be able to jump to the next sector.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_ELITE
text: The Rebel fleet has found you, and a nearby ship turns to engage. The cruisers in the distance are firing on you!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_ACE
text: The Rebel fleet has found you, and a nearby ship turns to engage. The ship that approaches is no regular Elite, but rather an MFK Ace! Much stronger than most Rebel ships, if you can defeat it, it may delay the fleet a little longer.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_ACE_S8
text: The Rebel fleet has found you, and a nearby ship turns to engage. The ship that approaches is no regular Elite, but rather an MFK Ace! It is much stronger than most Rebel ships, and while you may still defeat it, you should save your strength for the Flagship.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_FLEET_ELITE
text: The Rebel fleet has found you, and a nearby ship turns to engage. The cruisers in the distance are firing on you!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

text: The Rebel fleet has found you, and a nearby ship turns to engage. The ship that approaches is no regular Elite, but rather an MFK Ace! Much stronger than most Rebel ships, if you can defeat it, it may delay the fleet a little longer.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_AUTO_SUN
text: The Rebels must not want to waste lives by tossing ships into the Stargrove. They have sent Auto-ships to track you down!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

name: FLEET_AUTO_BLUEGIANT
text: The Rebels must not want to waste lives by tossing ships into the Stargrove. They have sent Auto-ships to track you down!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_FLEET_AUTO_BLUEGIANT
text: The Rebels must not want to waste lives by tossing ships into the Stargrove. They have sent Auto-ships to track you down!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

name: FLEET_ELITE_FEDERATION
text: The Rebel fleet has taken control of this beacon, but they have been met with opposition from Federation forces. As the ships rage on in combat in the distance, an Elite ship breaks off to fight you.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_ACE_FEDERATION
text: The Rebel fleet has taken control of this beacon, but they have been met with opposition from Federation forces. As the ships rage on in combat in the distance, an MFK Ace ship breaks off to fight you.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FINISH_BEACON_FLEET_ELITE_FEDERATION
text: You've found the exit beacon, but the Rebels have already arrived, and an Elite is dispatched to track you! The Federation forces are retaliating, but you must still jump as soon as possible to the next sector.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FINISH_BEACON_FLEET_ACE_FEDERATION
text: You've found the exit beacon, but the Rebels have already arrived, and an MFK Ace ship is tracking you down! The Federation forces are retaliating, but you must still jump as soon as possible to the next sector.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_AUTO_REAL
text: Though the background ships suggest heavy Rebel presence, not many Elites linger. It appears they merely function as carriers for the massive fleet of Auto-ships now swarming towards you. Uh oh...

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

name: FINISH_BEACON_FLEET_AUTO_REAL
text: You've found the exit beacon, but the Rebels are already here. Though the background ships suggest heavy Rebel presence, not many Elites linger. It appears they merely function as carriers for the massive fleet of Auto-ships now swarming towards you. Uh oh...

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Auto.

name: NEBULA_LIGHT_FLEET_AUTO_REAL
text: Though the background ships suggest heavy Rebel presence, not many Elites linger. It appears they merely function as carriers for the massive fleet of Auto-ships now swarming towards you. Uh oh...

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

name: FLEET_CHAOS
text: You're expecting to find the Rebel fleet here, and indeed you have. However, the fleet seems to be in chaos as a massive star has mysteriously appeared at the beacon! Furthermore, the ships here are much stronger than you expected. Get ready to fight!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

event.text: Before you can even power up the engines the gnome begins screeching. You're too distracted by it to continue, and the Rebel ship has already locked onto you!
Before Jerry can get another word out the gnome begins screeching. You're too distracted by it to continue, and the Rebel ship has already locked onto you!

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the Elite.

destroyed.text: You've managed to defeat the fleet ship, but you hardly have enough time to salvage more than a single fuel canister.
You've managed to defeat the fleet ship, but you hardly have enough time to salvage more than a single fuel canister.
You've managed to defeat the Gunboat, but you hardly have enough time to salvage more than a few resources.

destroyed.text: You've managed to defeat the Flagship, but you hardly have enough time to salvage more than a few resources.

deadCrew.text: You've managed to defeat the Flagship, but you hardly have enough time to salvage more than a few resources.

name: NO_FUEL_FLEET
text: The Rebel fleet has caught up to you. You detect significant fuel reserves in one of their closer fighters and move in to attack. Maybe you can still pull this off.

name: NO_FUEL_FLEET_DLC
text: Your pilot deftly avoids incoming artillery fire from the surrounding fleet while you try to sort out exactly what your plan is... One of the many approaching fighters gets into weapon range and your scanners detect it has surplus fuel. Maybe you can still pull this off.

name: NO_FUEL_REFUGEE_FRIENDLY_MV
text: A refugee ship fleeing the Rebel advance enters the system. It seems surprised to see you stranded, and admits it was following you from afar in the hopes of you leading it to Federation space. While it doesn't have much fuel to spare, it recognizes you are part of the Federation and offers to split its remaining fuel with you.

name: FUEL_EXPLORE_MV
text: Although your lack of fuel cells prevents your ship from jumping, you can still use your impulse engines. Will you spend some time exploring the nearby system?

event.text: You don't want to risk anything.

name: FUEL_APPROACH_MV
text: A ship approaches. They hail you saying, "You need some fuel? We'll prepare to dock to help."

choice.text: Request that they keep their distance.
(Adv. Sensors) Run a detailed scan with your sensors before responding.
(Long-Ranged Scanners) Run a detailed scan before responding.

name: FUEL_FREEMANTIS_CONFUSED
text: Fortunately, it seems a Free Mantis ship has come across you, and immediately hail. "Ah, Federation! You looking like in distress. Needing resources? We sell some to you! Will trade in turn for fuel."

event.text: "Oh? Price too high? Yes yes, we can lower!"
"Oh, yes my bad. Will give small amount of resources for free then!"

choice.text: Do you have any fuel to spare?

event.text: "Huh? No, we use last of fuel jumping here. Does not meaning you not want resources?"
"Here you go!" The Free Mantis hand over the supplies.
"Oh, and take some fuel friend!"

choice.text: Wait, but didn't you say you're out of fuel?

event.text: "Huh? Not knowing what mean. Anyways, goodbye!" The Free Mantis jump away.
"Huh? Ok!" The Free Mantis jump away, leaving you vastly confused.

name: FUEL_SELLER_DISTRESS
text: A small ship arrives with a message, "This automated ship will provide refueling services once a monetary exchange is complete. Complimentary amounts of fuel are available in emergencies only."

event.text: "This ship has registered that your one-time complimentary emergency fuel allowance has been consumed."
"Automated refueling complete."
"Automated refueling complete."
You prepare to attack the auto ship.

name: NO_FUEL_REFUGEE_DAMAGED
text: A refugee ship fleeing the Rebel advance enters the system, having picked up your distress beacon. While it doesn't have much fuel to spare, its hull looks damaged - it is in bad need of scrap and is willing to trade fuel for it.

event.text: The refugees thank you for the parts, and gladly pass along the much-needed fuel. They wish you well on your mission, and declare their support for the Federation.

Your Engi analyzes scans of the extensive damage to their hull, calculating potential repair costs. The refugees grumble and protest, but in the end, they admit that their need for repairs is greater than their fuel surplus and offer a better trade.

choice.text: The helpless refugees make easy targets. Attack them.

event.text: Panicked, the refugees immediately surrender as your weapons power up. They pass along their fuel and what few other supplies they have left in exchange for their lives.

name: NO_FUEL_REFUGEE_PIRATE
text: A refugee ship fleeing the Rebel advance enters the system, having picked up your distress beacon. While it doesn't have much fuel to spare, it is in bad need of armaments and is willing to trade for them.

name: FUEL_ON_REBEL_WARNING
text: A ship responding to your distress moves in. Unfortunately it turns out to be an automated Rebel scout. It immediately reverses thrust after scanning your ship.

name: FUEL_OFF_ENGI_DUBIOUS_MV
text: As you drift through space an Engi ship passes through. From listening to their com channel it sounds like they're discussing making repairs on their ship.

event.text: They clearly are busy because they don't notice your ship at all.

choice.text: (Hull Repair Drone) Offer to help repair their hull.

event.text: They happily accept your offer for help. Once the drone does its work they transfer over some fuel for your trouble.

name: FUEL_OFF_ROCK_WRECK
text: As you await either salvation or death, your attention is drawn to a sea of debris drifting past the starboard view port. The chunks gliding by grow bigger in size until the stern of a Rock frigate, gutted in some distant war, comes into view.

event.text: Perhaps there's some viable fuel left on board; a small away team boards the vessel.
The Rock don't take kindly to aliens picking through their belongings, no matter how decrepit they may seem, and you don't take risks in Rock territory.
The ship appears to be entirely lifeless. Your crew is able to find some usable fuel cells after a brief search.

name: FUEL_OFF_ROCK_CURIOUS
text: A curious Rock ship comes in for a closer look at you. They refuse all hails.

event.text: The Rock people are not renowned for their generosity. If it's fuel you need, it's fuel you must take!

name: FUEL_SHELL_SCANS
text: A Shell ship cautiously approaches, running basic scans on your vessel to make certain this isn't a trap. Once they're satisfied, they hail you. "Stuck? Lost? We'd be happy to help, but no service in thhhhis galaxy is free. We'd like to run some scans on your crew to bring back to thhhe Geniocracy. Harmless, we promise."

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Your Shell wishes to explain something.

event.text: Your Shell explains that in their culture, it's completely ordinary to take tests on strangers, and generally seen as an insult to refuse. They confirm the tests should be completely harmless as well.

name: FUEL_OFF_SHELL_SCANS_QUEUE
text: The Shells line up your crew in a queue, and pass them through what looks to be an exaggeratedly large x-ray. True to their word, the scans feel like little more than a soft tingle, but they take a long time. Soon it becomes clear it'll be several hours until you're done, and the Rebel fleet is constantly drawing closer.

choice.text: Just wait and finish the scans.

event.text: You watch the clock impatiently, but eventually the scanning comes to a close. "Thhhank you for your cooperation. My superiors will be very pleased. As promised, thhhhe fuel."

choice.text: (Mind Control) 'Convince' the Shells to stop early and give over the fuel.

event.text: Fortunately, the Shells are not telepathic like their Slug cousins, and the system is very effective on them.

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) 'Convince' the Shells to stop early and give over the fuel.

event.text: Fortunately, the Shells are not telepathic like their Slug cousins, and the weapon is very effective on them.
"What? We cannot stop now, thhhhe data is inconclusive at best, completely unusable at worst! Thhhis is an insult to our deal!" Outraged, the Shells attack!

name: FUEL_ON_SLUG_CHUCKLE
text: A poorly armed Slug ship cruises by and offers assistance. Their captain seems to be chuckling to himself, perhaps at the prices he's charging.

event.text: You know better than to do business with a Slug who seems like he knows something you don't. He jumps off with another chuckle.

choice.text: (Slug Crew) Have your Slug make the purchase.

event.text: As soon as he sees your crewmember the Slug stops his incessant chuckling. The exchange appears to go smoothly although you wonder what mental battles are telepathically occurring between the two Slugs.

choice.text: (Telepathic Shell) Have your Shell make the purchase.

event.text: The Slug continues chuckling for a little moment, but soon stops when he realizes something isn't quite right. The exchange appears to go smoothly, although you wonder what mental battles are telepathically occurring between the two species.

name: FUEL_ON_SLUG_OVERPRICED
text: A mobile Slug fuel depot enters scanning range. "My pricesss are fair, but I asssk one thing - do not insssult me with negotiation!" You check out his price list.

event.text: The trader looks shocked. You're struck by the sense that this is the first time anyone's ever paid him these prices.
The trader looks shocked. You're struck by the sense that this is the first time anyone's ever paid him these prices.
You offer a more reasonable price but the Slug is outraged! He moves in to attack!
The Slug captain ends all communications and jumps away, leaving you alone once again.

name: FUEL_ON_DYNASTY
text: From a distance approaches a Dynasty vessel, lured to your distress call. Their radio static roughly translates to "The demon's heart still beats! Can you hear it!?"

event.text: "Good! Then, beware the heart, traveler! It bleeds, but still it beats!" You assume that's all, but the Ghosts eject a crate of fuel at you, then jump off!
"Then he shall strike you down! Watch most carefully, they could be anywhere!"

choice.text: These Ghosts are insane. Attack them before they can do the same!

event.text: The demon's heart, whatever that means, can wait!

name: GUARD_UNION_CRIMINAL
text: Something seems off here. Usually, the Militia wouldn't bat an eye at ships like yours, but now, you catch suspicious chatter on the guard ship.

event.text: It seems your track record has caught up to you. The guard's crew have heard enough of the crimes you've been committing, and they don't intend to let you into the sector!

name: GUARD_UNION
text: The Militia are tasked with protecting Union space, and have instated a guard to prevent unlawful entry to the sector. Luckily, you don't fall into this category.

event.text: You now have some time to do something on the ship.
Your human sends over their Federation ID, which the Militiamen scan and, once verified, transfer over a crate of supplies.
Your medic calls the Militiamen and requests medical supplies, to which they respond by sending over a Medi-Cluster Bomb and some ammunition for it.

"A Federation soldier! You must be a very important vessel! I'm afraid we have little to give other than this spare Mine Launcher. I've never been a fan of the things myself, but maybe you'll find use in it."
The Militiamen immediately adopt a salute posture upon seeing Haynes aboard your ship, and transfer supplies over.

choice.text: Change your mind and leave the guard alone.

event.text: You apologize and end comms. The guard makes no attempts to communicate further.

name: GUARD_UNION_DESTROY
text: You have defeated the Militia guard. Whatever might have been in their cargo has for certain been destroyed, but you can at least salvage some supplies from the ship.

name: GUARD_UNION_DEADCREW
text: You have defeated the Militia guard. Without crew on board to stop you, you can investigate their cargo. You find a weapon to bring back to the ship, and move on to scrap their hull.

name: GUARD_UNION_FOLLOWUP
text: By killing the Militia guard, you have no doubt caused them to dispatch reinforcements to track you down. Watch your step as you explore the sector.

The guard smiles at seeing the Engi Brigade Leader. "Turzil, it's good to see that you've made it here safe and sound. We'll give what we can."
It takes the guard a moment to register who is in front of him. "Doctor, you have business in this sector? We look forward to hearing about your report."
The guard nods. "Of course, Ambassador. We'll send over whatever you need. Good luck on your mission."

event.text: "What? Yes, but how did you get that name?" He pauses for a moment. "Are you the ship they told me was coming? Thank god, we're getting our asses handed to us. Senator Wright did not prepare the EDC for the Brood and we've barely been able to keep the situation under control."

choice.text: We heard there was another Renegade here. What happened?

event.text: "When we realized we didn't have the manpower to take down the Brood AND destroy the G.A.S. nest, we called for backup. Some ex-Clansman named Irwin claimed he was the right pick, but that dumbass went missing a day after we hired him. No one trusted him so we slapped a tracker on his ship, which is how I know he isn't dead. But I don't have the time to track him down. If you could find him and hopefully get his ass back into the fight, that'd be great."

"We're about to launch an assault, but we need to ready the Renfield Bombs first. The Brood's lined up all of their defenses and we could use any additional fire support you could offer. I'll transfer the coordinates over to you."

name: GUARD_STARGROVE_CRIMINAL
text: The guard ship hails. "Renegade, I have a warrant out for your arrest. If I were any other post, I would round you up right here and now and turn you in. But that's not my job. My sole duty is to ensure the safety of all travelers. If we get into an engagement and you are forced to flee, or - heaven forbid - you were to win... then your life would be agonizing for what little of it remained. I'll give you one chance, Renegade. I can divert your ship somewhere else and then you'll be someone else's problem."

event.text: It seems like the guard was expecting this. Violence was the only way.

event.text: After long last you make your way to the checkpoint entrance. Fortunately, the SSLG has little reason to get involved with you as well, so as long as the Theocracy can hold out long enough for you to get through safely, then this sector should prove to be a welcome rest from the chaos elsewhere in the galaxy. Though, your luck rarely seems to go that way...

name: GUARD_BADLANDS
text: An Outcast guard, much better armed than usual, spots you and approaches cautiously. "I suppose it would be... very unlikely the Theocracy would send a Renegade to do their dirty work. But perhaps you have caught word of the Theocracy's plots? We dare not venture out of this sanctuary, so we cannot be certain if the Inquisition fleet approaches."

event.text: "Very well then. Perhaps with the presence of a Federation vessel, they will think twice of disturbing us here. But that is only wishful thinking..."
