text: An Elite Rebel ship comes barreling towards you, its entire array of weapons ready to go. You assume this must be the ship sent by the guard to hunt you down and prepare to defend your ship.

name: START_ESTATE
text: Arcadia might be the new corporate poster-child of the Union, but Wentworth Innovations remains ever churning out its supply of drone and AI tech. Working in concerning openness with the Rebellion, the industrial titan is responsible for the production of the majority of the Rebel Auto-ships you'll encounter outside of Universe 1. There's plenty of human faces to see around, but expect most of the fighting to be done versus murderous automations.

event.text: As you approach the entrance beacon, you receive a message of confirmation from C.U.R.A. - "You've found your way here. Congratulations. Now you merely need to avoid dying until you can reach the Headquarters. I've marked the location on your map. Do not fail me, Renegade. This is your final task."

name: GUARD_ESTATE
text: Almost immediately following, an automated vessel appears, branded with the Wentworth iconography. "Greetings, valued guest! Unfortunately, unauthorized clientele are not welcome on these premises. Through sophisticated and patented algorithms developed by the top engineers at Wentworth Innovations, I have been able to determine that you are: [FEDERATION SCUM]. You must be stupid coming here, hehe! [INITIATING ASS-KICKING MODE]."

event.text: You lock your weapons onto the guard and move in to attack.

choice.text: (Hacking Weapon) Attempt to deactivate the drone.
(Engineer Crew) Access the drone's mainframe and disable it.

event.text: Your Engineer shuts off the Auto-guard, allowing you to pass.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the guard.
(Adv. Piloting) Activate the auto-pilot to try and escape.

name: GUARD_ESTATE_DESTROY
text: You have defeated the Auto-guard. You salvage the remains.

name: GUARD_ESTATE_FOLLOWUP
text: By killing the Auto-guard, you have no doubt caused them to dispatch reinforcements to track you down. Watch your step as you explore the sector.

name: REINFORCEMENTS_ESTATE

text: A nearby Auto-ship swivels and scans your ship. "Apologies, dear customer, but I'm afraid you have been permanently barred from entering Wentworth Innovations property for all foreseable futures. On behalf of the company, please die."

name: START_JERRY
text: You've finally arrived, and it seems the transport you followed has too. Before you is a massive wall with major security measures in place. You hide behind a small asteroid cluster while you watch the transport submit their ID. "Apologies for the delay. Had a little encounter with some pesky Feds..."

name: GUARD_JERRY
text: As the transport is let through, almost immediately a vessel spots you. There's some shuffling, and then an MFK Guard is dispatched to handle you. "Halt! This sector is off-limits! Wait... are you a Renegade?"

event.text:
"Jerry? Don't scare us like that! When did you leave?" One of the other voices pipes up. "You idiot, it's a Renegade - this isn't our Jerry, this is a Renegade Jerry."
				
			"Yeah, that's right. I'm not your Jerry. But I want to talk to the me from this place. Is that okay with you guys?"

			You hear chatter as the MFKs discuss the situation. "Can we trust a Jerry that isn't ours?" "It's JERRY we're talking about. I don't want to hurt him even if he is a little different." "We're dealing with a Renegade. Who knows what they're doing to him." "No way, let's put our Jerry in his position - would you want some random guard to take him out out of sheer paranoia?"
			Eventually the voices stop arguing. "You can go see Jerry on one condition. Promise you won't hurt him."

			"I wouldn't. I just want to talk. If he's anything like me, I know he'll listen."
			
			"You can go, then. Behave yourself."

choice.text: Crap, looks like there's no avoiding this!

event.text: "Damn it, we got another Fed over here! Initiate the lockdown immediately!" The MFK Ace ship immediately locks onto you, and in the distance alarms begin to play in the city below.

name: GUARD_JERRY_DESTROY
text: The MFK Ace ship has been defeated. As their ship explodes, you catch their captain, collapsing to her knees, utter her final words. "God damn you and the Federation. You'll rue this day once Cyra gets ahold of you..." You ignore this premonition and scrap the ship.

name: GUARD_JERRY_DEADCREW
text: The MFK Ace ship has been neutralized. You catch their captain, collapsing to her knees, utter the final words, "God damn you and the Federation. You'll rue this day once Cyra gets ahold of you..." You ignore this premonition and scrap the ship.

name: GUARD_JERRY_FOLLOWUP
text: Seems there's no luck for you - the ASB remains locked onto your location and the barrier's defenses are only preparing themselves further. There'll definitely be reinforcements sent after you, but for now you've got to push through, and do so quickly!

name: REINFORCEMENTS_JERRY

"You've got gusto kid, too bad that enthusiasm was pointed towards us rather than something that won't get you killed! I was sent here to do business, but my friend was on that guard ship. This is personal, you bastard."

text: "Target found. You are wanted for: destruction of sector guard. Do not resist destruction."

name: START_SLUGHOME
text: You've taken a large risk coming here. Slugs are known for being dangerous tricksters and cheaters, but now you're in the lion's den. Trust nothing here, not even the silence around you.

name: GUARD_SLUGHOME
text: The Elite guard here sends you a brief, to-the-point message. "To enter there issss a fee. Pay it or we will kill you painfully." You glance at the computer and are shocked to see the absurd price! You knew Slugs were greedy bastards, but this is extreme.

choice.text: We won't pay that! Try your hand at negotiating.

event.text: "You... you are actually paying? What a sssstrange creature you are. Very sssstupid too, I'd imagine."
"Ssome people are jussst so temperamental. It'ssss mere pocket change!" You give the Slugs no chance to negotiate and attack.

choice.text: (Slocknog) Convince them to let you through.

event.text:
"I, Sssslocknog, have returned. Let ussss through."
			
			"I did not realize you were aboard, Sssslocknog. Thingssss were always much better when you were in charge. You may passss."
			
			"We wissssh to ressssupply. Would you let ussss have accessss to your sssstoressss?"
			
			"Yesss, help yoursssself."

choice.text: (Knight Crew) Your Knight has some discipline to teach to that Clairvoyant.

event.text: Your Knight makes their way towards the comms, and upon seeing them, the Saboteur at the other end displays what seems to be discomfort. Instead of exchanging words however, the Knight merely enters into what seems to be a trance state, joined in by the Clairvoyant at the other side.

After a short time, your Knight shakes off the daze and appears triumphant, while the Slug at the other end collapses. One of their colleagues hails back: "If thisss isss the caliber of subordinatesss you keep, there isss no way we can ssstand up against you. Take thisss and let us ssswallow our ssshame."

choice.text: (Mind Control) Your mind control will not work, as the guard is staffed by Slugs.
(Mind Affecting Weapon) Your Mind Affecting Weapon will not work, as the guard has Slug crew onboard.
(Adv. Engines) Try to escape the guard.
(Adv. Piloting) Activate the auto-pilot to try and escape.

name: GUARD_SLUGHOME_NEGOTIATE_GOOD
text: "Hmmmm, an interesssting proposssitttion. Maybe we can make thisss mutually beneficial? What if we throw in a weapon, and lower the price?"

event.text: "Ah, well now you are jussst adding insssult to injury." You must have offended them hard, because their weapons spring out of the hull, not usually a sign of friendly intentions.
"Ssssee? We are not all unreassssonable. Pleassssure doing busssinesss with you."

name: GUARD_SLUGHOME_DESTROY
text: You have defeated the Slug guard. Whatever might have been in their cargo has for certain been destroyed, but you can at least salvage some supplies from the ship.

name: GUARD_SLUGHOME_DEADCREW
text: You have defeated the Slug guard. Without crew on board to stop you, you can investigate their cargo. You find a weapon to bring back to the ship, and move on to scrap their hull.

name: GUARD_SLUGHOME_FOLLOWUP

name: START_CLAN
text: Your arrival in Guild territory has been all but a few minutes past but you're already on edge. The EHG isn't inherently hostile to the Federation, but your ship would make a fine addition to their hangar's collection... All the same, you might be able to make some friends here as well.

name: GUARD_CLAN
text: Instead of the usual guard ship you might expect in most sectors, a well lit hunting lodge awaits visitors here.

event.text: You step into the lodge and are greeted by a pleasant aroma of exotic spices, most of which are illegal to own in Federation territory. There's pleasant chatter from the guests all around, and while most are Slugs, there's several other races here too. The crowd doesn't seem to notice or care you're here, which is a good sign.

choice.text: See if anyone around the lodge has something to sell.
See if anyone around the lodge has something to sell.
Start a bar fight for the hell of it.

event.text: You walk over to the bar, and pick up a glass of awful smelling liquid, then smash it over the head of one of the nearby Clansmen. "Oi lad, what the bloody hell are you doing?" The Clansman draws his rifle, followed by several of his friends, and they rough up your ship, bringing the bar fight back to you. This was a really stupid idea.

choice.text: Welp, not much reason to stick around.

event.text: You're undisturbed as you move past the lodge. Hopefully that bodes well for the rest of this sector.
"Ah bugger, we got a bogey on ussss! Arm the gunssss!"

choice.text: Ignore the Lodge and go on your way.

event.text: You're undisturbed as you move past the lodge. Hopefully that bodes well for the rest of this sector.

name: START_NIGHTS
text: According to Slocknog, this sector should currently be underway with the Crown Theft Festival. Nights will likely be hiding somewhere at the Royal Palace, so if you're hoping to watch the fireworks you'll have to head there.

name: GUARD_NIGHTS
text: Guarding the entrance is a ship unlike any you've seen. As black as the abyss around it, the ship hails you as soon as you jump in. "Now why would a Federation sssship come here sssso sssoon after the fugitive and traitor Sssslocknog returns from the dead? Very sssusspiciousss, yess?"

event.text: The Slug chuckles. "You forget captain, I can read your mind. Now, we can't have accomplissssssess to traitorssss running about, Nightssss would kill me! Guesssss we'll have to kill you firsssst."

choice.text: (Mind Control) Your mind control will not work, as the guard is staffed by Slugs.

You've never seen ships like this before, and the Federation has no information on them, but you suspect this sector might be swarming with them...

name: START_SHELLHOME
text: This sector does not host the homeworlds for which the Shells came from. After a long competition with the Slugs for control of their original sector, the Shells gave up and migrated to a new sector.

name: GUARD_SHELLHOME_CRIMINAL
text: Something seems off here. Usually, the Shells wouldn't bat an eye at ships like yours, but now, you catch suspicious chatter on the guard ship.

event.text: It seems your track record has caught up to you. The guard's crew have heard enough of the crimes you've been committing, and they don't intend to let you into the sector!

name: GUARD_SHELLHOME
text: You receive a brief but to-the-point hail from the Shell guard. "Visitors are welcome, so long as you do not harbor any Slugs. You will be required to undergo brief scans until you may pass."

event.text: Fortunately, you have nothing to fear. You let the Shell ship scan the biometrics of your crew before carrying on.

You know that you have a Slug on board, but you agreed to the scan anyways. The Shell ship quickly identifies your Slug crew. "You are smuggling a Slug aboard your ship! Damn it, hurry to thhhe weapons!"
You've decided to ignore any possibility of a peaceful resolution, and turn to destroying the Shell ship immediately.

choice.text: (Mind Control) You will allow us to pass.

event.text: "I will allow you to pass. Have a nice day."

choice.text: (Mind Control Weapon) You will allow us to pass.

event.text: "I will allow you to pass. Have a nice day."

choice.text: (Mind Affecting Weapon) Induce chaos within the guard and slip past.
(Shell Crew) Convince them to let you past.

event.text: Your Shell speaks briefly with the guard, but it seems they have already convinced them to let you pass without further question.

choice.text: (Radiant Crew) Convince them to let you past and donate supplies.

event.text: Your Shell speaks briefly with the guard, but it seems they have already convinced them to let you pass without further question. The guard also transfers over some supplies, seeing a Radiant is aboard your ship.

choice.text: (Alkali) Convince them to let you past and donate supplies.

event.text: Alkali speaks briefly with the guard, but it seems he has already convinced them to let you pass without further question. The guard also transfers over some supplies.

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the guard.

name: START_MORPH
text: This sector is supposedly home to the Shell Geniocracy's finest scientists and where their primary genetic research is performed. However, the strange Atlas entry here leads you to assume something is up...

event.text: Over your radio blares a brief section from the Geniocracy anthem, followed by a distressed pre-recorded message. "Thhhis is Professor Alkali, lead research and spearhead of the Geniocracy science district and genetic enhancement project. If you are hearing thhhis, I advise leaving as soon as possible. My team and I are currently locked in Lab Omega. We made a terrible mistake... our latest creations, thhhe Morphhhs, thhhey've gone loose. Worse yet, thhhe Rebellion has arrived from unspecified regions. Thhhis sector is not safe. I repeat, thhhis sector is not sa-" The message is cut off as a distant shadow approaches, revealing itself to be a ship!

name: GUARD_MORPH
text: Before you is a Shell guard, though it's of highly unusual colors. A flat, unfaltered gray hull sets it apart from their usual appearance. Even more peculiar, the ship hails you, speaking complete nonsense. "Speke eek! Yip yoo, urple roo. Kip kip too roo, sploo purp jook!" A small grey blob shows up on your screen, making odd spastic gestures with its body.

event.text: It seems whatever these Morphs are, they haven't taken kindly to you ignoring them, and open fire!
"BIK BIK, TALA TALA TOOLA TOOLA! OBOT RIPPLE DUE!" Whatever the hell that means, it seems the Morphs aren't willing to talk. Get ready for a fight!

choice.text: (Shell Crew) Convince them to let you past.

event.text: Your Shell attempts to speak with the Morphs, but that only seems to anger them further. Looks like they don't think highly of the Shells...
Your Morph jiggles a bit, and speaks to the guard. This seems to pursuade them into giving you scrap, though you can only imagine what conversation was just exchanged...

choice.text: (Adv. Engines) Try to escape the guard.
(Adv. Piloting) Activate the auto-pilot to try and escape.

name: GUARD_MORPH_FOLLOWUP
text: The likelyhood of the Morphs having reinforcements to send after you is near zero, but you have no idea what else you might find in this sector...

name: START_COALITIONHOLD
text: The Coalition Stronghold has always been a curiosity. It was originally a regular sector completely void of nebulas, but not long after the Coalition took control of it the designation of the sector had to be changed in accordance of the numerous nebulae that appeared.

name: GUARD_COALITIONHOLD
text: It doesn't take long for the elite guard to notice you. "You will rue the day you came here, Federation ship! You know the best part about being an elite? I get to be creative with how I kill the likes of you. Which system do you value the least?"

event.text: "Are you joking? You must really like a challenge! I sure do, but your wish is my command."
"I see you do not fear our weapons! I'd call you a fool, but I think that has already been established by you coming here."
"I see you know very well that you can't hide from us!"
"So you wish to be rendered a sitting duck? I can't say I agree with your choice, but who am I to judge a dead man?"
"Hoping for a quick death I see! Take one last breath captain, and make it count."
"You must be a fool not to fear the havoc we will cause to your crew!"
"You must be a fool not to fear the havoc we will cause to your crew!"

choice.text: (Anti-Virus) Prevent any hacking attempts of theirs.

event.text: The Coalition captain chuckles at your silence until he realizes his cyber-attack against your systems has been completely ineffective. Angered by his failure, he attacks.

name: START_HIVE
text: You've arrived in the Mantis Hive, territory usually deemed forbidden for most. Regardless of whether you came here willingly or not, you're here now. Make sure you get out while you still have a crew to escape with.

choice.text: Kazaaak seems to have something to say.

event.text: "We... we are finally at Hive? I was not thinking I would see this place for longer time. If we are here... that means I can speak to Leikonpliiinakra. I can tell her to pull out of Coalition! There is only one problem. To access royal palace, we will need coordination of Bishop. How we will earn allegiance of Bishop, I am uncertain..."

name: GUARD_HIVE
text: Seems the Hive is protected by no Suzerain vessel - a Bishop, one of the strongest Mantis warriors alive, is stationed here aboard a bright white guard vessel. "Very unlucky you come here, for now you are dying! Heheh.. Federation captain will rue day in which he thought he could infiltrate Hive!"

event.text: You rush to defensive positions as the guard approaches menacingly.

You hope Kazaaak might be able to reason with the guard and convince them to let you go, but instead it only seems to anger the guard more. "You shelter this traitor aboard vessel? I care not what claims he makes of the Queen, I knowing the stories, and he is not one of us!"

choice.text: (Mantis Crew) Try to persuade them to let you go.
(Hive Elite) Persuade them to let you go.

event.text: Whether the Mantis still desire to hunt you or not, they would not dare question the authority of an Elite soldier of the Hive. You are allowed to pass.

text: A Suzerain ship jumps in shortly after you do, its weapons already online and firing! "Fleshbag intruders! You kill guard, we kill you!"

name: START_DYNCAP
text: This is the capital of the Spectral Dynasty. This ancient faction of Phantoms has been on a path of war lately, which has led them directly into conflict with the Rebellion. Why they're so aggressive - and their sectors littered with ruins - is still a mystery to the Federation.

name: GUARD_DYNCAP
text: Looks like the ship protecting the entrance is a Reaper vessel - one of the guardians chosen by Dessius the Prime Reaper himself. They hail you - "The Federation is not permitted within that of Dynasty lands. Speak your business and we will see if you are deserving of an exception. Choose your words poorly, and you will face certain death."

choice.text: We seek asylum from the Rebels in your sector.

event.text: "You speak nonsense. Did you gather nothing from the databases surely provided to you by your Federation? These lands are ravaged by the Rebellion's demons. You speak only lies, and I wish not hear them any longer."

choice.text: We wish to learn the customs and history of your people.

event.text: "What, of our collapsing society and the lifeless wastes of times long past? I could hardly relate. All the same, if you speak the truth, then present your tourism permit with official stampage from Dessius himself."

choice.text: Ah yes, about my uh... permit.

event.text: "I am to assume this means you do not wield one? Then you should already know that entry will not be permitted. Enough wasting of my time."
"T-this is not a pass. This is but mere scrap metal. O-oh. I see now. I shall, erm, take this offer, but request that you make your flight through these lands fast before I have time to regret it."
"Yes, this pass is most serviceable. Please proceed."
"Yes, this pass is most serviceable. Please proceed."

choice.text: (Mind Affecting Weapon) Induce chaos within the guard and slip past.

name: START_ROCKHOME
text: You have arrived in the Rock Homeworlds, a dangerous sector ruled by the Rock Elders, a council of corrupt Rockmen who spread lies of their supposed demi-god status to enforce their authority.

name: GUARD_ROCKHOME
text: This beacon is protected by an Elite Rock guard, piloted by Rockman Crusaders and Crystal beings. "Outsiders are not welcome here! The holy texts mandate that heretics are to be removed from this plane of existance."

choice.text: Well... maybe the holy texts are wrong?

event.text: "How dare you scoff at the words of the Elders! What lies have you been fed, to have such erroneous thoughts?"

choice.text: You are the ones who have been fed lies.

event.text: "You are simple minded, and foolish. It is those such as you who stand in the ways of the enlightenment promised by our crystalline gods! The Inquisition shall make quick work of you."

choice.text: (Rock Crew) Share with them the truths that your Rockman has learned.
(Crusader Crew) Share with them the truths that your Crusader has learned.

event.text: It takes an in-depth conversation between the two Crusaders before any progress can be made. "You have... you have presented ideas of a reality vastly different from the one I have been raised to believe in. Yet... there is a ring of truth to your nonsensical spewings. I must think this over. I will come with you, so that I may experience the outside world myself and decide what I shall believe."
There will be no negotiating with the Rockmen. You arm your weapons and prepare to fight.
The Rockmen are immediately silenced when your Paladin gets involved. They proceed to transfer some supplies and allow you to pass.

text: "Outsiders! The Federation has done enough damage to this galaxy, we do not need you invading our territory and destroying our ways of life! You might have defeated our guard, but your wave of terror ends here!"

name: START_CRYSTALHOME
text: You have arrived in the newly founded homeworlds of the Crystalline race. Much of this place is under construction as their citizens flock from their original homeworlds, but there is still no doubt that the Crystals hold a strong grip over this sector, and they aren't eager to let foreigners ruin their lives for a second time.

name: GUARD_CRYSTALHOME
text: The guard hails you, and while their captain's face is featureless as always, their tone suggests they would be wearing a frown. "Blagh, more aliens? It is like you foreigners have a death-wish!"

choice.text: Try to talk it out with them.
(Crystal Crew) Convince the guard you are harmless.

event.text: "It is our mistake! Apologies, it is so hard to tell which ships belong to us with so much diversity in this galaxy... welcome home, brother!"

choice.text: (Sentinel Crew) Convince them you're harmless and request supplies.

event.text: "It is our mistake! Apologies, it is so hard to tell which ships belong to us with so much diversity in this galaxy... welcome home, brother! Let us help you..."

"Ambassador! It seems we have made a severe mistake in our judgement! May you accept our dearest apologies; we did not mean to impede on your business with these acquaintances of yours... Please, make yourself at home. We will ensure that you are not bothered by any troublesome visitors."

Your cultist falls to their knees and makes out a long prayer to the Crystals beneath fits of sobbing and incoherent rambling. Hit with a mixture of disgust and pity, the Crystal guard offers you a "blessing" if it'll make you leave faster.

choice.text: It is clear that a fight is inevitable.

event.text: The Crystal cruiser watches you in silence a little longer, and you begin to wonder if they don't intend to attack. However, as soon as you attempt to move out of their way, they power up their weapons!

name: START_LOSTSUN
text: This sector appears to be the stronghold of the Lost Suns, formidable Rock warriors who rebelled against their tyrannical government. Bittersweet allies with the Federation, the Lost Suns themselves shouldn't be too hostile towards you, but don't expect a warm welcome.

name: GUARD_LOSTSUN
text: Three fortified stations and a squadron of heavily armored guards protect the entry beacon. It doesn't take long until they notice you. "Federation ship, your presence here is noted. What is your business in our sector?"

event.text: "An unfortunate truth that our sector often serves as a unwelcome connection between neighbouring sectors. You must wait here for an inspection and pay a fee, and we will deem if you are worthy to pass."

choice.text: Agree to the fee and inspection.

event.text: The inspection is long and arduous, but goes through without a hitch. "I see nothing of concern aboard your ship. But be warned, Federation captain. You might support our efforts, but we all know your motivation. An end to the Rock government is as beneficial to you as it is to us. Should we have a different target, your thoughts of our mission might not be so gracious."

"I see you are too cheap to pay for the potential threat you bring to our sector. Or perhaps you have something to hide, or that your motives are not simply to pass through as you say? It matters not, you will be dead soon."

choice.text: We wish to use this sector as a rest from the Rebel threat.

event.text: "Bah, you are ignorant if you think this sector is safe from their control. Your presence here will surely bring the fleet, which will doom us all! If you wish to travel through here unharmed, you must give us your flight plans, so that the Rebels might pass through quickly in pursuit of you."

choice.text: Agree to giving them your flight plans.

event.text: You know this will accelerate the fleet by a dangerous rate, but you have little other options. "I hope you know, that should the Rebellion purge this sector as it has to so many others because of your foolishness, our thankfulness for the Federation will quickly fade."

"So you are one of those pathetic creatures who thinks all those around him are beneath him, and deserving of the consequences of his petty whims? We shall teach you a lesson, and cleanse you from this world in the holy fire!"

choice.text: We have heard the legends of your resistance, and wish to learn more.

event.text: "You think we are naive? Stupid enough to believe you come here in search of knowledge? You are a military ship, bearing guns and the Federation sign. We do not appreciate lies. If you wish to safely pass, you must hand over a portion of your ammunition and droneparts."
It's not easy to part with a bunch of resources, but it was a better choice than getting on the Lost Sun's bad side. The Rockman makes no further comment, but lets you through.
"No surprise, men of war are often too attached to their silly playthings of destruction. We have seen many people like you, and now we will make there be one less."

choice.text: (Lost Sun Crew) Convince them to let you past.

event.text: Your Lost Sun speaks briefly with the guard, but it seems they have already convinced them to let you pass without further question.

choice.text: You don't have time for explanations. Fight your way through!

event.text: The Rockman chuckles. "Then blessed death awaits you, a death fit for a soldier whose wisdom does not extend further than how to shoot his gun."

name: GUARD_LOSTSUN_DESTROY
text: You might have made a dangerous mistake tangling with the Lost Suns, but it's a mistake you can live with. What does it matter if you angered a few Rocks, right? You hurry to leave before the reinforcements can catch you.

name: GUARD_LANIUS

choice.text: Ignore their strange message and try to move past.

event.text: Despite the foreboding message, you decide to try and move past the guard. The Lanius don't seem pleased by your lack of a response and turn aggressive.

choice.text: Give them some scrap, perhaps it's what they want?

event.text: The Lanius ship dispenses a few Lanius soldiers, who scoop up the scrap and are pulled back into their ship.
"Up all, thank yes. Donation, accept return." A Flak launcher is ejected from their ship.

name: GUARD_LANIUS_COMMUNICATE_LANIUS

name: GUARD_BLACKMARKET
text: An incredibly well armed ship of originally Rebel design now claimed by Argeonn's smugglers is guarding the entry beacon. They demand you pass a quick inspection or pay a fee before you may enter. You've never seen this model of ship before, but they've got a large artillery cannon pointed right at you!

event.text: The smugglers don't look surprised at all, as if this was a usual occurrence. You hurry to arm the weapons.
"Ah, got something to hide? Well, scrap is scrap..."

choice.text: [Reputation: 2+] Remind them of your good standing with Argeonn.

event.text: "Ah, the Renegade who has done so much to help our cause... Yes, I think we can make an exception today. Wouldn't want to risk your patronage, would we?"

"You think YOU deign to ssssearch a pirate who became KING? You sssslime. If I wissssh to ssssmuggle ssssomething passsst you, you will LET me do sssso, and thank me for the privilege of letting me passss without a tribute!"

choice.text: (Kazaaakplethkilik) Warn them not to offend the legendary pirate.

event.text:
You inform the guard that Kazaaakplethkilik Tiiikazpakaziiika is aboard your ship and will be offended if they set foot aboard your vessel and search it.
			
			"I... see. I would hate to offend someone so respected. We will waive the fee this time. Carry on."
			
			"You are being wise today." Kaz says, chuckling.

"Beg your pardon. I have some very important cargo here. I'm doin' some very important work for Argeonn, and wouldn't you just hate to inconvenience the Dread Pirate?"
			
			"Ah, Tuco? I thought you were already here. Shows what I know. You may pass, make sure you don't blow it all immediately this time."
			
			"Bite me."

"Tell me somethin' laddy. Do ye see this access code?"
			
			"Ah, Captain A55. It's good to see you've decided to do business in this sector again."
			
			"Aye. I got me some important business. This ship ain't got nothin' this sector wants to avoid."
			
			"True or not, your access code is still valid. Welcome back."

name: START_VAMPHOME
text: You have found yourself in the heart of the Vampweed Confederacy - the origin of the Orchids. Massive freighters and scores of ships come in and out of this sector every single day. The Orchids are especially populous in this sector, but this deep in Confederate territory, the pride of the Vampweeds runs deeper than anywhere else. The beacon is guarded by a powerful elite Confederacy ship, extracting a toll from ships wishing to enter the bustling trading hub.

name: GUARD_VAMPHOME
text: The Confederate guard blocks your path. While the beacon's appearance has the look of a standard kiosk meant to screen passersby with a toll, this one seems to be taking a more aggressive approach. "Stop right there, multiversal traveler. Before you're allowed to enter, you're going to have to pay our toll and give us a full explanation of why you've come here."

event.text:
The guard looks relieved to see a familiar face.  "Welcome home, Premier! I wasn't aware you had left. We haven't gotten word from HQ in some time. But seeing you does put me at ease."

Ivar nods. "Good to see your wits are sharp. Just be careful - if any Coalition ships come through here, don't let them enter."

The guard looks nervous. "Are we expecting a skirmish?"

Ivar shrugs. "All I'm saying is, I think we've got a problem. Make sure to let the other ships know."

"Will do, Premier."

The guard looks relieved to see a familiar face.  "Welcome back, Ambassador. It's good to see that you're safe. We haven't gotten word from HQ in some time."

"As I feared. I believe the Coalition may be making its move on our home."

"The Coalition? That's not good, I waved one in here not too long ago..."

"We will address the problem if we can. Stay on your guard."

"Will do, Ambassador."
The guard looks relieved to see a familiar face. "Welcome back, Doctor! You're always welcome within our borders. I'll waive the fee, of course. I hope your meeting with the Premier is productive."

choice.text: (Cultivator Crew) Explain that you are just passing through.

event.text: "A Cultivator is aboard your ship?" The guard looks more at ease. "So you're just passing through... Well, make sure the outsiders don't try anything. I will give you the Cultivator discount, of course."

text: "There was a time I might have sided with the Federation, but seeing the kind of barbarians it employs to 'enforce peace and prosperity' across the Multiverse has shown me! This is for all my fellow greenbloods you massacred on your way here to disturb the peace, scum!"

name: GUARD_MONK

event.text: You move past the Auto-ship.
It might be small, but any portion of scrap you can get will help.

name: GUARD_MONK_FIGHT

name: START_HEKTAR

name: GUARD_HEKTAR
text: "Greetingsssss, valued cussstomersss! Welcome to Hektar Indusssstriesss (tm)'sss Hektar MEGA-MARKET(tm). It'sss alwaysss wonderful to ssssee new debtorsss in thessse partsss!"

choice.text: Thanks - wait, did you just call us debtors?

event.text: "Oh ho, another one! You new arrivalssss alwayssss ssseem ssso sssurprissed. Yessss, I'm afraid you are in masssssive debt to Hektar Indussstriesss! Didn't you know that every U.W.U. point you collect comessss with a fee of 625 ssscrap? Yesssir, you now owe ussss a total of 2500 ssscrap! Quite the predicament..."

choice.text: Well, what do we do about it?

event.text: "Oh that'sss quite sssimple. You pay it, or you ssstay here forever. Don't worry if you do end up ssstaying, Hektar Indussstriessss sssellsss just about everything you need to live a painfully adequate life of a minimum wage worker! Good luck!"

choice.text: Surely there's SOMETHING we can do!

event.text: The Slug laughs. "Yeah, ssssure. You could go track down Mr. Billy Hektar himssself and asssk for your debt to be cleared! Hah, get real."
This is criminal! If the Federation isn't aware about this, then you'll have to take matters into your own hands, starting with this ship.

name: GUARD_AUGMENTED
text: "You are visitors? You carry one of us, so you allowed in. What reasons have you come for?"

event.text: "You found live one? Most mysterious! You must go to leader, her gloriousness will wanting to see! This sector filled with ruins of ancient beings, we are augmented! We assimilate with ancients, become stronger. Our leader, strongest, assimilate with gods! Go to her, she surely give good reward."

choice.text: See if they have any of this "ancient tech" to offer.

event.text: "Certainly, but nothing free! We offer some things, but wanting scrap in return. Fair trade, yes?"

choice.text: We aren't paying for anything, attack!

name: ATLAS_MENU_LEARN
text: The Atlas is used to guide ships through hyperspeed, and ensure they do not jump into hazardous conditions. To do this, sectors must enter the co-ordinates of their start beacon into the Atlas so that ships may be directed to it. Your Atlas is currently pulling from the Federation Database, but may be updated with new coordinates you find on your travels.

event.text:
Locations of interest have been marked in certain sectors to denote a possible location that might be of benefit to visit. Usually, these do not come with coordinates attached, so you will have to find them yourself.
			Some sectors do not have locations of interest marked, but that does not mean they don't have any. It only means said location is currently unknown to you.
			Some sectors have multiple locations of interest.

The [!] marker is present in two forms. On sector names, it means that they are a Unique variant, generally the Homeworlds of a species. On beacon labels on the sector map, it denotes important locations or quests that are not overwritten by the Rebel fleet until your visit, letting you trigger them even if the fleet is present.

Throughout your travels, you might receive special coordinates to a special sector. You will only be able to visit these sectors once, but may do so during any period of hyperspeed travel before sector 8. Do note that doing so will override any Quests you would have found in the next sector.

choice.text: What is the Rebel threat level?

event.text:
The Rebel threat can mean a few things. Sectors with a higher threat level have a larger concentration of Rebels, but it also represents the chance of encountering an MFK Ace at a fleet controlled beacon in that sector.
			Very Low - No MFK Aces on fleet beacons
			Low - 10% chance of encoutering an MFK Ace
			Medium-Low - 20% chance
			Medium - 30% chance
			High - 50% chance
			Very High - 75% chance
			!CRITICALLY HIGH! - 100% chance
			Sectors with a rank of High or above will also always have an Ace on Rebel controlled exit beacons.

Some sectors have special kinds of fleets. These will be written in parenthesis next to the fleet threat level.
			(Auto) - Rather than Elite Rebels, you will encounter strong Auto-ships instead. There is no chance for an Ace to spawn.
			(Neutral) - Additional Federation backup will be supplied with a neutral ASB. Aces can spawn if the threat level permits.

event.name: DATABASE_LOREDUMP
event.text: You, captain, are now a central part of the largest known conflict in not just the galaxy, but the multiverse itself. After the conclusion of the original Federation Civil War in Universe 0, your home reality, the Galactic Federation defeated Admiral Vance and the Rebellion, securing their control over the galaxy.

The Federation struggled with various other conflicts, most notably a cold war between the dangerous Coalition Alliance endorsed by the Slug Kleptocracy, Mantis Hive, Rock Theocracy, and Eargen Republic. This conflict finally escalated into the invasion of Aquarian territory, resulting in heavy losses. After the Coalition's attack temporarily destabilized the Federation once again, Vance ran a covert operation from the Rebel Stronghold to attempt to salvage the heavily protected ancient ruins that the Coalition had been seeking as well.

Though the full details are unknown, it is believed that among these ruins Vance's team salvaged the first Multiverse Drive, which he would reverse engineer and install on the remaining Rebel fleet. After a Federation raid on the Rebel Stronghold, Vance and his men fled to Universe 1 and allied with the Rebellion of that reality to overthrow the Federation. Universe 1 now acts as the center of the Interdimensional Rebellion's operations, while Universe 0 leads the counterattack.

Fruitless as though it might be, both sides are now locked into a seemingly unending conflict, invading realities to secure the strength and survival of their own faction. Make no mistake - though the Rebellion continues to perpetuate their title of a brave uprising, the Rebellion is well beyond a simple insurrection. Though intel is sparse, it would appear Universe 1 has been transformed into a desolate, industrial dystopia fueling the eternal gears of war that seek nothing less than the total annihilation of the Federation and all non-human species.

The whereabouts of U0 Vance are currently unknown, though sightings of suspicious movements of the privately trained MFK Ace corps, undyingly loyal to Vance Prime, have been seen all around the Multiverse. The MFK Aces will likely prove to be your greatest threat, along with the powerful redesigned Flagship model dispatched to this reality to destroy the Federation base and secure a Rebel victory.

This is where you get involved. As a Renegade hired by the Federation your goal is simple - destroy the Flagship, and it is highly unlikely the Rebellion will be willing to dedicate any further efforts to capturing this reality. It is far more practical for them to divert the remaining Rebel forces to a different reality. If you fail, it is certain the Federation of this reality will fall, and this will become just another piece in the Rebels' arsenal of enslaved realities.

event.text: The magic hat makes you feel warm and fuzzy, despite being crafted in an incomprehensible and non-euclidean shape and color which eludes your mind. As soon as you put it on, it feels as though there is nowhere you couldn't go if you put your mind to it.

choice.text: You're good with what you have. Get a head start on the fleet!

event.text: You decide not to take anything extra, and carry on.

name: START_BOON_MENU
text: It seems a gift awaits you. From uncertain origins it's labeled, in strange penmanship, "A gift from the observers, on behalf of the last challenger to find us. We sincerely await meeting you. See you soon, perhaps?"

tooltip.text: Recover your boarding crew.

inactiveTooltip.text: Unavailable: You cannot do this while in danger!

name: START_BEACON_GNOME_TIP
text:
Before you can board your ship you notice an ominous whispering. It grows louder and louder as you try to identify the source and you catch some strange glances, until at last you stumble across a mundane garden gnome.

	All at once the whispers cease, leaving you alone with the gnome. Its presence is ominous despite its banal appearance, and you can't help but feel as if you're meant to bring it with you...

	[CHAOS MODE UNLOCKED - To activate Chaos Mode, locate and select the gnome on the right of the hangar screen]

name: START_BEACON_EXPLAIN
text: Finally suited up and ready to go, you take a look at your beacon map. Looks like you still have a while until the fleet becomes an immediate threat, so you can spare some time to do something on the ship if you wish.

choice.text: A strange beacon lays nearby. Do you want to activate it?

event.text: The beacon beeps and a cascading signal ricochets outwards into the depths of space. You don't know who's listening or where they are, but hopefully they're friendly - or carry good loot.

name: BROKEN_START
text:
CAUTION. Incompatible mods have been detected, breaking some core functions of Multiverse. It is mandatory that you re-evaluate your modlist to eliminate issues, and use mods that were meant for Multiverse in mind. 
	
	Common cause of issues;
	Beginning Scrap advantage
	Engi Scrap advantage
	Any fleet removal mod
	Just about any mod made prior to the release of Multiverse that modifies events

name: OPTION_INVALID
text: Dude, that's cheating. How are you seeing this right now?

name: QUIT_GAME
text: Bye bye!

name: TEST_HEKTAR_STORE
text: Demo Store.

name: CHAOS_MODE
text:
As you pick up the gnome, a ghastly red glow fills the hangar. You look around but none of the other people around seem to notice or care. Slightly unnerved, you bring the gnome back to your ship.
	
	[CHAOS MODE ACTIVATED]

name: CHAOS_MODE_RESET
text: Suddenly, as if by magic, the gnome reappears on your ship. It begins to scream at you, and your hull collapses partially. Maybe you should be more careful with keeping the gnome safe next time.

name: DETERGENT_MODE
text:
DETERGENT MODE ACTIVATED!
	Daring Renegade, you've proven your courage and chosen to activate DETERGENT MODE! And courage you will need, for many trials and tribulations await you in the journey ahead! You will need bravery, strength, cunning, and most importantly true grit to face the challenges that DETERGENT MODE will throw at you.
	
	Best of luck, Renegade. May you rise above the rest and stand true in the face of DETERGENT MODE.

name: EXTRA_LIFE_HEAL
text: "CATASTROPHIC HULL FAILURE IMMINENT - ACTIVATING EMERGENCY PROTOCOLS." Your hull has been repaired, and your resources have been restocked!

name: DOOR_OPEN_SONG_NEW
text: Before stepping on board however, the Lizard begins to do a chant, dancing around in circles. "Tunt parra parra, kaethlu parra parra, spaekith parra parra, taklu parra parra! Parra maku!" After finishing, they pause and look at you.

event.text: "This is Door Open song! Lizard culture involves many dances and chants. In the way you knock on door for entry, we dance the Door Open Song! It is a song for both requesting faithful entry, and for giving thanks for granting it. Very sacred, very important."
The lizard hangs its head, dejected, but says no more.

name: DOOR_OPEN_SONG_KNOW
text: As per usual, the Lizard begins to sing the Door Open Song. "Tunt parra parra, kaethlu parra parra, spaekith parra parra, taklu parra parra! Parra maku!" After finishing, they pause and look at you.

event.text: The lizard hangs its head, dejected, but says no more.

name: DOOR_OPEN_SONG_GUNTPUT_NEW
text: "Federation. You have done good service for my people. I do not foresee... good future for them. But still better than in Hektar labor camp for rest of days. I will not go with them. I have failed them. I will serve you instead, in efforts to save reality and someday free rest of my people." As Guntput steps aboard your ship, he raises his spear and shakes it twice, chanting a strange song while dancing around in circles. "Tunt parra parra, kaethlu parra parra, spaekith parra parra, taklu parra parra! Parra maku!" After finishing, he pauses and looks at you.

event.text: "This is Door Open song. Lizard culture involves many dances and chants. In the way you knock on door for entry, we dance the Door Open Song! It is a song for both requesting faithful entry, and for giving thanks for granting it. Very sacred, very important."
"Very well. I will be a good staying guest. But do not disappoint me, as I have disappointed my people."
"What? Really? You are really refusing? And to think I started liking you. Hmph."

name: DOOR_OPEN_SONG_GUNTPUT_KNOW
text: "Federation. You have done good service for my people. I do not foresee... good future for them. But still better than in Hektar labor camp for rest of days. I will not go with them. I have failed them. I will serve you instead, in efforts to save reality and someday free rest of my people." "Tunt parra parra, kaethlu parra parra, spaekith parra parra, taklu parra parra! Parra maku!" After finishing, he pauses and looks at you.

event.text: "Very well. Off on great journey we go!"
"What? Really? You are really refusing? And to think I started liking you. Hmph."

name: DOOR_OPEN_SONG_METYUNT
text: Instead of immediately stepping on your ship however, Metyunt wiggles his arm awkwardly and mumbles some incoherent words. You stare at him and he stares back in silence.

event.text: "Oh... er... the Door Open Song. I think. It's uh... a lizard thing. Request for entry or whatever. Just say yes and let's get it over with."
"Right, right. Sorry about that. Just some dumb tradition. You know how those things are. Or maybe you don't, we only just met."
"Oh? Oh well. I can't say I'm surprised, but I am... uh... confused?"

name: THE_JUDGES_NEW
text: A strange vessel approaches, and on your screen appears three aliens dressed in long robes and their faces covered with ornate masks. The first, a Zoltan, speaks. "Hello. We are... the Observers. Maybe, long ago... we have met. Maybe not. We do not recall. But now, we have returned. We seek knowledge. You seek... what do you seek? We will find out, yes?"

event.text: "Allow us to get... introductions out of the way. I am Thest, Judge of Diplomacy. I seek... travelers who make it their passion to make peace with all species. Prove to me your... dedication to building bridges and I shall grant you... great boons."

The second judge, a Separatist, appears next. "[Hail], for I am: Corby - Judge of Technology. Judge of Technology! Mission of observation summary: analyze trends between travelers with [advanced] technology. Technology! Do you -possess- t-t-t-technology? Of the advanced form? Provide proof. Rewards await. name: SYLVAN_PREIGNITER_WIN
text: "AAAAH! AAAAAAH! TREMOR DYING! TREMOR DYI- Gaaaaaaah!" Tremor and his mighty ship have fallen. You scrap its remains.

event.text: Tremor might be dead, but your job here isn't finished. As you approach the alien structure, it becomes apparent that the sheer size of the colossal fleet ship is enough to fit a thousand-fold of your cruiser...

You traverse the interior of the ship as sparking electronics jut out of the walls, sometimes scraping against your hull in the tighter areas. Inevitably, you find a room resembling the Weapon Control, but you're forced to travel forward on foot.

Your crew come across a massive cubical power source plugged into the wall, which they assume to be the Pre-Igniter. However, it's uncertain whether pulling it out will trigger any sort of alarm, since the ship itself still seems to have power in a few locations. How much faith are you willing to put into the ancient alien security?

Your crew carefully eject the Pre-Igniter from its slot. All seems well for a few seconds until a green light starts flashing and a muffled robotic voice starts spewing out alien garble your translator can't comprehend. You quickly hurry out of the ship followed by 2 automated drones dispatched to deal with your crew!

choice.text: Leave it and grab whatever salvage you can instead.

event.text: Your crew dig around and grab anything they can carry back to the ship that won't risk setting off a trap. Maybe the Pre-Igniter will be the prize of some other future explorers instead.

name: SYLVAN_LIZARD_STORY
text:
"Alright ssstranger! Have you ever heard the tale... of the furry, one-eyed tree lizard thingssss? Ssstupid, I know, but it'sss all true I promissse. I've ssseen them with my own eyesssstalksss!"

	Sylvan chuckles. "But in all ssseriousssnesss, there'sss a colony of friendly yet primitive creaturesss nearby. However, they've been through tough timesss lately. Hektar Indussstriesss, perhapsss you've heard of them, have been taking advantage of them for ssseveral yearsss, ssstealing them away for lessss-than-willing labor." You take note at the particular emphasis of disdain when Sylvan mentions 'Hektar'.

	"When I caught word of thisss, I ssstepped in. I can't watch over them forever, ssso I had a friend of mine, a Zoltan monk named Anurak, ssstand guard. However, I haven't heard from him in weeksss. I'm getting worried, but I'm kind of held up with thisss merchant busssinesss. Could you be a friend, sssstranger, and take a quick look? It would mean a lot."

event.text:
"Sssso, he'ssss on board? I would like to sssspeak with him."

			Anurak is brought to the communications console. "Sorry to make you worry, Sylvan! Got mixed up in my past for a bit, had to flee. Assassins, and all that. Anyway, I'm a pacifist now, did I tell you that?"

			"It'ssss certainly a relief to hear that you are okay, but what of our friendssss?"

			"Yes, well, I took who I could. If I'd have stayed, you know they would have blown me up. My people are big on deaths with collateral damage, you know. Kind of baked into our energy bodies." Anurak clears his throat. "I will find them and do what I can, as I promised. Don't you worry."

			"Many thankssss, old friend."
"Many thankssss, ssstranger!"
"That'ssss alright, ssstranger. No hard feelingssss."

text: You've arrived at the coordinates Sylvan gave. You can see a large populated planet in the distance with several massive wooden and concrete structures spanning across the trees on the surface. It startles most of the nearby inhabitants, who turn to face your ship.

text: You rush around helping the lizards arm their defenses when a blue and yellow Slug vessel appears in the sky and descends to the planet's surface. When they see you however, they seem startled. "Oh... You aren't ssssupposssed to be here! Thissss planet isss under ownerssship of Hektar Indussstriesss(tm)! Ssshoo! Get out! Renegadesss aren't welcome!"

choice.text: This is a Zoltan sector. You're Slugs.

event.text: "Uhm... ssshit. Okay, fine. Uh... How much I gotta pay you so you buzz off? Thesssse lizardsss aren't worth your damn time."
Undoubtedly, you have damned these lizards to life in the Hektar sweatshops. But who cares? Money!

You aren't some corrupt Zoltan politician looking to be bought off with some scrap. You have morals (probably) and you'll do all you can to defend these lizards! "Ugh, what isss it with you Renegadesss and sssuddenly getting a conssscience!? I ssswear a year ago none of you cared..."

text: The Hektar ship comes careening down, getting caught in several trees and bringing down a structure or two. As some lizards rush to assess the damage, you find Guntput surveying the sky. "One down, but many more to come. Inevitable full enslavement of our people... we are in dark days. You have saved us, but only temporarily. How am I meant to protect my people?"

choice.text: Offer to take as many of the Lizards you can with you.

event.text: Guntput seems hesitant at your offer. "Technology is dangerous to our ways of life. Technology leads to warring, to violence. We must not taint our culture with your sins. How could we be certain you are not the next Hektar, coming swoop us up and exploit for money?"

"Technology Schmechnology. We have soup. I promised to protect you and that's what I'll do. You all liked my soup, didn't you?" Remembering the taste, two of the lizards decide that they want to join in at the promise. The rest of the lizards quickly gather to discuss, but when another Hektar ship jumps in behind them and sends an entire neighborhood plummeting off of its tree, they quickly scurry aboard your vessel. You fly away, unnoticed by the approaching Hektar fleet.

choice.text: You're right, technology is dangerous. That's why you want to be on the winning side.

event.text: No reason to make your situation worse. You decide to avoid the outpost.
You arm the weapons and engage the station!

choice.text: (Rock Crew) Request that the Outcasts give you a missile weapon.

event.text: "Allow me to see what we can provide. I'm sure we have something extra in storage."

name: ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_ASTEROID

choice.text: (Upg. Piloting) Attempt to escape from the pirate.

name: ENCOUNTER_PIRATE_NO_ESCAPE_MV
text: Once you arrive, your screen lights up with warnings. A nearby pirate seems to have advanced hacking tools and they have tried to shut down your Engines. Your crew manages to keep them barely operational and you move into attack.

event.text: Your Engines are down, and you prepare for combat.
Your engine system is restored to full power.
Your Hacking System automatically counters the digital assault and you move in to fight the ship.

name: SLAVER_OFFERS
text: The slaver welcomes you aboard and shows you their "wares".

event.text: "A great purchase. May they serve you well, captain..."
"A great purchase. May they serve you well, captain..."
"A great purchase. May they serve you well, captain..."
You're not interested in their line of trade.
Slavers are the scum of the galaxy. You'll be doing great justice by wiping this one out.

choice.text: (Upg. Teleporter) Use your teleporter to attempt to board the ship and release some of the slaves.
Ignore the slaver and continue on your way.

event.text: You're not interested in slavers.

choice.text: Draw straws and send a crew-member over to the slavers.

event.text: The chosen crew-member leaves without complaint, knowing you had no choice.

removeCrew.text: You briefly consider cloning a replacement, but decide to respect the Federation laws regarding simultaneous duplicates.

choice.text: "Logic error: request cannot be met. This is an automated vessel. Demand: refused."

event.text: How stupid do these guys have to be to demand crew from an automated vessel? You'll have time to think about it after you'll do the world a favor by ridding it of these clowns.

choice.text: We will never surrender one of our crew to slavers!

event.text: You prepare to fight the slaver.

choice.text: (Spider Crew) "Give" them your spider and let them cause havoc.

event.text: "Wait, what is thi- OH GOD AHGHWHAHAGGHHAHHH" The slaver falls to the floor as the spider tears out his throat, and moves on to consume the rest of the crew. While it might have killed everyone aboard, including the slaves, the hull of the ship remains intact for you to scrap.

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Attempt to out-run the pirates.

choice.text: [Reputation: 1+] "You're such a good customer, all services are cheaper!"
Hire the mercenary to delay the Rebels.

event.text: Once the mercenary finishes counting the scrap, they nod in approval. "You're the boss! I'll get right on it..."

choice.text: Hire the mercenary to scout the sector.

You're not interested in their line of trade.
Mercenaries are hardly any better than Rebels, just troublemakers with shifting allegiances. Time to cut the Syndicate's ranks short another member.

choice.text: Ignore the mercenary and continue on your way.

event.text: You're not interested in mercenaries.
"You made the right decision, friend."
"Too bad... You will regret this decision!"

choice.text: (Upg. Engines) Attempt to out-run the pirates.

name: SMUGGLER_OFFERS
text: The smuggler pats you on the back and welcomes you into their cargohold.

event.text: "Many thanks for taking this off my hands! Just a word of advice... try not to let the authorities see you with it for another couple jumps."

Smugglers might usually be known for their military sales, but Argeonn transports plenty else. Who knows what kinds of harmful items have traveled through this ship's cargo into the hands of all kinds of bad actors. The only responsible course of action is to take these guys down.

choice.text: Ignore the smuggler and continue on your way.

name: RUINS_SALVAGE
text: With the ship now out of the way you're free to inspect the ruins.

choice.text: (Anointed) Translate the words on the ruins.

event.text: "Will trying my best. Words of forefathers rusty in mind, but gist I am getting right. Stand back."

choice.text: (Runic Translator) Translate the words on the ruins.

event.text: Your translator does its best to decipher the lengthy runes scribbled across the walls of the gargantuan ruins. The output, fortunately, is legible, though you can't say for certain its accuracy.

choice.text: (Obelisk Crew) Translate the words on the ruins.
(Cognitive Crew) Translate the words on the ruins.

event.text: An automated vessel is scanning the wreckage. There's no way you can access whatever the structure holds without first taking care of the ship.
Whatever is in these ruins, you need them. You attack the other ship!
Your Engineer struggles to shut down the Auto, but they do manage to change its primary directive to fleeing the beacon, leaving you alone with the ruins.
Whatever the ruins have to offer isn't worth the effort.

name: RUINS_TRAP

unvisitedTooltip.text: This is the location of a ruin.

visitedTooltip.text: Explored location. Nothing left of interest.

text: In front of your ship is a massive cubical cruiser, its exterior covered in small green lights. Though the ship is completely unmoving, the dim glow from the lights suggests there must still be some form of power aboard.

event.text: It's very possible the ship might contain something of value, but you can't guarantee it. Do you want to send a team aboard?
Your crew find the interior of the ship void of oxygen, and scans show no life support has ever been installed on the ship. How do we proceed?

choice.text: (Anaerobic Crew) Send in the anaerobic crew.
(Orchid Crew) No breaches detected, the Orchid should be able to provide oxygen.
We have nothing to proceed with.

event.text: Unfortunately, you have no choice but to pull away from the cruiser.
Whatever the ruins have to offer isn't worth the effort.

name: RUINS_TRAP_CONTINUE
text: As soon as you are inside, the crew find themselves in a large antechamber, decorated with various artifacts you don't recognize, resting on what appear to be pressure sensors. You could probably grab one of them, but you don't know what will happen, if anything.

choice.text: There's a weapon here, grab it!

event.text: You grab the weapon, and as soon as you lift it from its pedestal an alarm sounds in the ship. An atom shaped drone comes out of the walls, weapons primed and firing down at your crew!
Your crew run back to the ship, pursued by the drone. You try to seal the airlocks quickly, but unfortunately the drone make it aboard. Get ready to defend the ship!
Fortunately, you're able to teleport back all of the crew in time. The drone is left behind on the ship as you pull away.

text: A massive cubical structure, possibly a station, is caught in the gravitational pull of the nearby star, and is slowly pulling closer. Though the inevitable destruction of the station cannot be avoided, there might be enough time to salvage whatever might be aboard.

event.text: As you approach, it becomes clear the environment is too hazardous to go through with this without taking a hit. You're going to have to bear a solar flare or two, unless you have the right defenses.

choice.text: Continue, we can take a hit.
(Adv. Shields) Our shields will protect us.

name: RUINS_STAR_PROCEED
text: A solar flare rocks your ship, starting a fire. Still, you press forward and dock with the station. With the timer ticking, your crew explore the interior. They find what appears to be a crew drone of sorts, but an inferno has consumed the room!

choice.text: Grab the drone and get out!

event.text: Your crew grab the drone, pulling it back, but it's a lot heavier than expected. Working together, they manage to drag it out of the fire, but another solar flare passes by, rocking the hull once again. Most of your crew make it back to the ship, but one of them trips, dropping the drone. Scans show the star is flaring up again, and you only have time to save one of them!
You leave your crew for dead, taking the drone and head back to the ship. You manage to pull away before the flare hits, but the wreck takes it full blast and is torn in half!

removeCrew.text: Fortunately, the Clone Bay revives your crew. You can tell they're mad about the situation, but they'll get over it soon enough.

event.text: You leave the drone, dragging your crew back to the ship and pulling away before the flare hits. The wreck takes it full blast and is torn in half, undoubtedly destroying the drone with it too.

choice.text: Save both but risk some more damage.

event.text: You pull the ship closer, taking the force of another solar flare. Luckily, you're still able to save both your crew and drone and fly away.
Thanks to your teleporter, you're able to beam up both your crew and the drone before another solar flare hits.

name: SALVAGE_DEFAULT_MINEFIELD
text: You stumble across an abandoned minefield. Certainly dubious, but also a potential source of a large amount of ammo and scrap. However, being careless would prove to be risky.

choice.text: You have no sacrificial crew to send in the minefield.
(Crusader Crew) Your Crusader knows a lot about explosives, and can also take a hit.

event.text: Though your Crusader knows quite a lot about explosives, the real reason he's a good choice is his thick skin. With little danger to their well-being, they return with an impressive haul, though it's not as good as you might have gotten with a larger team.

choice.text: (Paladin Crew) Your Paladin knows a lot about explosives, and can also take a hit.

event.text: Though your Paladin knows quite a lot about explosives, the real reason he's a good choice is because of his impressive resilience. With little danger to their well-being, they return with an impressive haul, although their slow speed prevents them from gathering more without letting the Rebel fleet gain time.

choice.text: (Lanius Crew) Your Lanius can melt down some mines for scrap.

event.text: It won't yield any functional ammo, but it's low risk for some reward. You send out your Lanius to liquify as many mines as they can.

choice.text: Don't risk it, just bring back a few of the outliers.

name: SALVAGE_DEFAULT_DRONE
text: Oddly enough, it appears a pair of Boarding Drones have been abandoned here in the abyss. You can break them down for parts easily, but if you scanned them for the schematics you might risk activating one.

event.text: The schematic isn't worth the risk. You salvage the drones.

You attempt scanning, but due to your distance you're unable to get a read. You pull closer, but accidentally move a little too close, triggering the drones! Fortunately you still recover the schematic, but now they're onboard!

choice.text: (Energy Shield) Approach without any fear of intruders.

event.text: Fortunately, your Energy Shield greatly simplifies the process. You retrieve the schematic without having to deal with any resistance.
Fortunately, your Engi is able to disable the drones before scanning them.
Fortunately, your Engineer is able to disable the drones before scanning them.

name: SALVAGE_DEFAULT_PIRATES

choice.text: Send a team to see what loot might be inside.
You cannot send a team, since you lack one.

name: SALVAGE_DEFAULT_CACHE
text: A small supply cache has been embedded into a small asteroid nearby. You'd have gone right past it if not for a small, indiscernable short-range signal broadcasting from within.

choice.text: There's no available crew to send.
(Boarding Drone) Attempt to open the cache.

name: SALVAGE_DEFAULT_SHRINE
text: A small shrine located nearby drifts abandoned through space. Typically, you find these closer to more densely populated Illesctrian temples, as a sort of stopping point for ships that can't make the whole journey.

choice.text: Raid the shrine for any valuables.

name: SALVAGE_DEFAULT_COLONY
text: The ruins of a little colony appear to have once been located on a nearby atmospheric planetoid. You can't be certain if anyone is left.

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_NOTHING
text: Tully appears to be waiting in his cabin. "Sorry, don't have much to talk about. Maybe check in with some of the other crew?"

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_GENERIC_1
text: You find Tully polishing his blaster, whistling some song you've never heard before. "This? Oh, this is an old marching song back from the Federation-Mantis War. Of all the things that've stuck with me the most, it's funny to think it's the music. I guess the rest you just don't really want to remember, you know?"

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_GENERIC_2
text: You ask Tully if he has any lasting grudges on the Mantis after the Federation-Mantis. "The Mantis? Certainly not. My life was saved by a group of Mantis. The Hive's another story. But if you let yourself blame the wrong people for too long, you'll fall victim to your own spite. Just look at Vance - I can't ever let myself end up like him."

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_GENERIC_3
text: "Funny thing, did you know Vance hates his last name? He told me that once: his parents weren't great people. Not that it's any excuse how he ended up, but you know. That's why they call him Admiral Vance, not Admiral Wentworth. Poor kid got mocked so hard during training, calling him 'Wentworthless'. Well, I don't envy those people now."

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_GENERIC_4
text: Tully walks past you in the hallway, and you give him a cursory nod. Tully blinks, scowls, and continues to walk away before he stops again.

event.text: "Oh, uh... sorry Captain, it's nothing. I'm just used to being the one in command. If any of my officers pass by and don't salute me, I make them drop and give me 50. I don't suppose it's appropriate to do that here, though."

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_GENERIC_5
text:
You notice a collection of movies on the table in Tully's room. All of them seem to be on similar material - Federation wars. The Federation-Mantis War, the Inquisitions, the Civil War, and a couple smaller ones you aren't too familiar with. Tully spots you looking at them and says, "I've started collecting documentaries on the wars I've lived through out of curiosity. You'd be amazed how wildly inaccurate some of them can be." 
		
	Tully picks up a rather provocatively titled one called 'The Red Menace: Earth's Last Stand'. "I mean seriously, this one uses footage of Coalition Bombers when the Coalition didn't form until after the Civil War! And it claims the Mantis were using clone armies! Cloning technology wasn't invented until several decades later, and it was by the Shells! There has never been a clone army deployed in all of our known galactic history!"

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_FREDDY_1
text: You find Tully and Freddy chatting together idly, reminiscing about the Federation-Mantis War. "You know, I met a young Free Mantis during the war after I escaped from captivity. Funny thing is, I gave him a nickname. Freddy. Ain't that such a coincidence?" Freddy nods his head. "Oh, ain't that swell! What a coincidence indeed. You ever met him again after you were rescued by the Feds?" Tully shakes his head and Freddy frowns. "Oh, well that's just a shame. Maybe some day you'll meet him again?" Tully shrugs. "Maybe some day, just maybe..." Both wave to each other and walk away. You aren't sure if you should say something.

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_FREDDY_2
text: Freddy appears to be teaching Tully about Mantis dialect. To his surprise, Tully already knows most of it. "Well well, you never fail to impress me, Admiral! You speak near perfect Yeitiiik! Better than even my contemporaries!" Tully smiles but doesn't accept the compliment. "Oh, I was taught by a Mantis and I just kept practicing. Comes in use for diplomacy sometimes. It was also just funny to spook Turzil sometimes."

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_TURZIL_1
text:
You spot Tully walking over to Turzil and staring at his arm plate. "Turzil, I've got to ask. Where'd the yellow come from? I swear the last time we spoke you were grey!"

"-Blushing-. Please, do [not] inquire. It is... embarrassing. But... does it look bad? Perhaps I should remove it. Yes, I will do so."

Tully realizes his error and puts his palms on Turzil's shoulders. "No no, I didn't mean like that! It suits you, buddy! Some time you gotta teach me how to paint, alright?"

Turzil seems to shrink a bit. "Y-you want me to -teach- you how to paint? Together? Privately?"

Tully nods but seems a bit unsure. "Yeah? Not sure why you say it so weirdly... but yeah! But not now, we've got more important things to do."

"Yes. -Yes-. Of course. More important things. Of course..."

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_TURZIL_2
text: You poke your head into Tully's quarters for a moment only to find Turzil in there instead, staring blankly at the wall. You think he's shorted out, but he turns around startled like he's been caught. In his hand is one of Tully's hats, which he throws on the shelf and goes running out past you. You decide to say nothing about it.

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_ALKRAM_1
text: You flick on the cameras to view the other ships and see what the crew are doing. You watch in the kitchen as Tully walks in to grab some food, followed several minutes later by Alkram. Both pause when they see each other, and Tully's hand inches closer to his rifle. The cameras experience some interference as Alkram begins to build a slow electric charge. The two stare at each other, both ready to draw, frozen in place. The standstill finally comes to an end when the microwave beeps, signifying Tully's pasta meal is ready. He sighs and abandons his gun, and Alkram calms down as well. Though no words are ever exchanged, they share a nod of mutual agreement and sit at opposite tables to eat.

name: SOCIALIZE_TULLY_DEVORAK_1
text:
Devorak and Tully both cross paths in the hallways, and almost immediately Devorak starts to reach for his sword. Stretching his fingers, he begins to slide it out of his holster. Tully's eyes slant and he slides his hand towards his blaster. 

"Devorak."
"Tully?"
"Put the sword down."
"The sword?"
"Yes, the sword."
Devorak blinks. "Oh, right. Sorry, sorry! I didn't meant to put you on edge! It all must be very confusing, but you must understand I am the sword!"
"You're... what?"
"I'm the sword!"
"Okay... cool I guess? I can't say I understand, but it's good to see you again. I saw your speech. I don't know if the Federation would be inclined to forgive you for betraying them initially, but I for one am glad to have you back."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_NOTHING
text: You find Haynes pacing the hallways, talking to himself and looking at the floor. When he sees you, he pauses momentarily. "Sorry, lost in thought. Maybe go talk to someone else right now, I'm mulling things over. Detective stuff, and all that."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_1
text: "No offense, but I've never really liked the label 'Renegade'. People seem to slap it on anyone who travels between realities nowadays that isn't a Rebel, but it carries a certain stigma. I've never really been the mercenary type."

choice.text: Doesn't working for us make you a Renegade now?

event.text: "I... I suppose it does. Fair point. I have been... humbled?" Haynes temporarily removes his pipe from his mouth. "Grrr, I guess I'm a murder hobo now. I kill babies. Or something. But uh... please try to refrain from warcrimes while I'm onboard. I get that you can get away with a lot in this profession, but I'd at least like to be able to sleep at night after this."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_2
text: Before he started traveling the Multiverse himself, Haynes used to live on Earth. However, he had to leave his home behind when Archive Inc. could no longer hold back the Vek threat. It's quite the sad story, and his isn't the only one like it out there.

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_3
text: "My parents were huge history buffs. Everyone who lived in Archive was. Makes sense, it's even in the name. There's some famous runes about a guy named Sherlock Holmes who lived in the ancient empire of Britannia who could solve any mystery. My mother loved to read the legends, and though she didn't believe Sherlock was real, she jumped at the chance to name her son after him. That son being me, of course. No siblings. There can only be one 'greatest detective'."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_4
text: You ask Haynes if he smokes or not, since you never seem to smell it. He looks surprised at the notion and removes his pipe from his mouth. "What? Oh, of course not. Great deductive skills though! No no, tobacco's quite rare now that Earth's flooded and the drug market's saturated with all kinds of Slug junk. The pipe was a gift from my grandfather, who got it from his grandfather, who got it from his... and so on. They say it belonged to a guy named... er... Star-line? Stelen? Oh, father would be so disappointed in me for forgetting. Either way, it's a precious heirloom. I hate to admit it, but it's kind of fun chewing on the end. Clearly grandfather agrees, because there were toothmarks even before my own."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_5
text: You overhear some screaming from somewhere else on the ship and race towards it. Expecting intruders of some sort of worse, someone's fingers falling off from another space plague, instead you find Haynes screaming like a child in a corner of the ship as a tiny arachnid scuttles around on the floor. Carefully, he draws his firearm and aims it at the bug, blasting it to smithereens. Only after it's dead does he see you watching him, and meagerly slinks away in shame.

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_6
text: You find Haynes contemplating something in his quarters. "There was a time I might have considered myself a patriot. Now, I'm not capitalist nor a warm-blooded Unionite, but I was proud of, if nothing else, the raw achievement and progress the Human race was able to accomplish against all the odds. Most species have some access to Aether or were from a time when Aether was still being made, but Humans? We paved our way all on our own. And we used to be grateful to be a part of the galaxy! The Engi, the Zoltans, they were our friends! We fought arm in arm against the Hive, but that BASTARD Vance had to change everything! And his cohorts, Tanaka and Stimly, god what I wouldn't give to be the one to put lead in all three of their skulls. I doubt anyone needs to tell you this, but the Rebellion is the scourge of the galaxy; I can only hope the Union will some day get past this and we can all see the Rebellion for what it really is. It's not a glorious movement of human progress - it threatens to set the whole damn Multiverse back to the metaphorical stone age."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_7
text: "You ever wonder what becomes of the people in the cases you solve? Well, I guess you wouldn't. But as a detective, I can't help but think about it. I think about it a lot, actually. Poor Amy and Daniel, not only did they have to deal with the death of their coworker and the arrest of another, but the twist they were working with two spies at once." Haynes sits down in a nearby chair and pulls out his pipe and goes to light it, only to remember he doesn't smoke. "God. Maybe I'm just stupid, you know? Even the greatest detective in the Multiverse can be an idiot sometimes. Worrying about nonsense like this when so much more is at stake."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_8
text: As you approach, Haynes smoothens out his jacket and straightens his hat. "You know, it's the outfit that makes the man!" He contemplates that piece of wisdom for a moment, shrugs, and walks off.

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_9
text: You find Haynes reading a book titled "A Study in Scarlet", which he closes when he spots you. "Ever wonder why it is people call me by my last name? I mean, I'm literally named after a legendary icon of Old Earth culture and yet everyone just calls me Haynes! It drove my mother to the brink of madness, but I always found it humorous. Oh well."

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_GENERIC_10
text: You spot Haynes doing some trick shots for the other crew with his pistol. He's a pretty good shot, but those bullets have to go somewhere - and you don't like the number of holes you've been noticing around the ship lately. You make a mental note to talk to him about it, but not right now. Never discipline a crewmate while they're holding a gun, even if they're usually well-mannered like Haynes.

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_FREDDY_1
text:
Upon spotting Haynes, Freddy rushes over before Haynes can shut the door on him. "Greetings Mister Haynes! Do pardon me for the intrusion, but I have an inquiry and I believe you're the right person to ask."

Halfway hidden behind his door and quivering slightly, Haynes asks what 'inquiring' Freddy is refering to. "Ah yes, well, I was wondering how much you knew about what I believe is the mythological empire of Britannia. Is it true they were said to wear hats like mine, and had delightfully posh accents?"

Haynes seems confused. "Well, for one, Britannia was real. It's not a myth. As for the hats, I couldn't tell you. The only surviving photographs are during some ancient wars, nothing of regular day attire. Is that everything?"

Freddy nods, disappointed. "Good. Okay, bye." Before Freddy can even respond, Haynes has already slammed the door shut.

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_FREDDY_2
