text: As you step out into the hallway you watch Haynes rush past, not even saying a word to you. He closes the door behind him and vanishes into the next room, and moments later Freddy walks in. "Captain! How delightful to see you. I don't mean to interupt whatever it is you're doing, but have you happened to seen Haynes? I had some questions on Old Earth history but he said he had to use the restroom and dashed off!"

choice.text: Lie and say you haven't seen Haynes.

event.text: You shrug and apologize, telling Freddy you haven't seen Haynes anywhere. "Ah, real shame. I wished to learn all he had to teach on the history of tea! Oh such a delightful drink it is, of all the marvels ever shared between species I think none can compare."

"Oh thank you Captain! Well, off I go!" Freddy dashes off down the hallway. You carry on with your business, uncertain what to think about the occasional shrieks of fear and slamming doors you can hear on the other end of the ship.

name: SOCIALIZE_HAYNES_KAZ_1
text:
You've started noticing wherever Kaz goes on the ship, Haynes will always go somewhere else. Kaz clearly has noticed too, because you find him speaking to Haynes in the kitchen. "Have I insulting you in some way? Kaz break many hearts back at home and perhaps leave some orphans during the war, but Kaz never crossing paths with you or Haynes clan. You are too young to have fought in war and I not kill many Humans anyways. So, what is problem with Kaz? Why are you fearing me?" Haynes remains silent and meager, unlike his usual self.
			
Kaz grows more and more impatient at the silence, finally snapping. "ANSWER ME FLESHBAG! ANSWER KAZAAAKPLETHKILIK OR I WILL MAKE IT PERSONAL VENTURE TO SLEEP WITH EVERY WOMAN OR MAN YOU EVER LOVING! Erm... many apologies. I am working on temper. But please, answering me. If you are hating me at least say why! I am stubborn as all Mantis are, but that is not meaning I cannot improve. We are on same team, no?"

choice.text: Encourage Haynes to talk to Kaz.

event.text:
Haynes gulps but finally speaks up. "It's just... it's nothing to do with you, Kazekpik... Kak... uhm... what's your name again? Sorry."
			
Kaz laughs a little and tells Haynes to just call him 'Kaz'.
"Kaz. Right. It's nothing to do with you. Back on Earth, there were these giant creatures called the Vek. They were insect-like and whenever I see a Mantis I just... it just brings back memories. I prefer not to talk about it."

Kaz nods. "Ah. My sincerest apologizing. You might finding this strange, but once time long ago Kaz winds up on Earth in pod, and recruited into mech squad to fight Vek! Very fun, but mech pilot not life for Kaz. Once I was getting money to buy shuttle off-world I said goodbye, but from that experience I cannot blaming you! Vek very scary indeed! It is okay, Kaz will not bothering you. But if you ever need buddy to blowing up giant insects with, I will gladly join!"

Kaz notices you entered the room for the first time since the conversation started and nods in your direction. "Yes, yes. I give deepest apologies. Not wanting to hurt Haynes' feelings, just wanting to know answers." Kaz wanders away, and Haynes mouths a silent thank you in your direction before grabbing his food and hurrying back to his quarters.

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_NOTHING
text: You find Jerry standing by one of the rear windows, staring intently out in the abyss beyond. "Oh, hi Captain. I'm okay right now. Maybe go check on the other crew?"

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_1
text: Jerry comes stumbling out of his room, an odd moment in which he isn't wearing his glasses and his hair is even more of a mess, and approaches you. "Captain, I think there's something wrong with the ship's water supply! Someone might have poisoned it! We need to warn everyone immediately!"

event.text: "The water tastes... well it HAS taste! Water isn't supposed to taste like anything! I'm not quite sure what p-poison tastes like, but what else could it be?"

choice.text: Only extra filtered water has no taste.

event.text:
"You mean - the water on this ship isn't filtered?! Good god, no wonder uncle said space was dangerous! You must have so many diseases! Captain, we need to fix this!" You assure Jerry that your ship's water is normal and probably doesn't carry any diseases.

"Really? In the Protectorate our water never tasted like anything! Wow... space is so mysterious!"

choice.text: Oh good god it's been poisoned!!!

event.text: Deciding to mess with Jerry, you flick the emergency switch and order all of the crew to line up in the break room. Once they have gathered, you remind everyone that water does, in fact, usually have taste, and SHOULD have taste.

choice.text: It's fine Jerry, go back to sleep.

event.text: "A-are you sure Captain? I'm not joking, there's something wrong!" You assure Jerry there's nothing wrong and urge him to go back to his quarters. Jerry stumbles off, still alarmed.

"Captain please, please! Why aren't you responding?! There's poison in the water!" Jerry starts to cry, pulling on you and trying to get a response. You say nothing, doing your best to act like a statue. Eventually Jerry gets so exhausted he passes out, and you can't help but feel this was a bit unnecessary and cruel.

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_2
text: Jerry asks you if the ship has any nightlights. You figure Jerry's asking for himself and apologize, but instead he seems concerned for someone else.

event.text: Jerry motions for you to follow and leads you to a small crack in the ship where a little plant is growing. "Plants need light to survive, right? I'm worried he'll die here if he stays out of the light too long." You're amazed Jerry cares this much about an inconsequential plant, but you assure him you'll get something figured out for it.

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_3
text:
You notice an Equinoid plushie in the back of Jerry's quarters and decide to ask him about it. "Oh, well I got that a long time ago when I was just a little kid! My uh... my mother... she always said I got my love of Equinoids from my father. Not that I ever really knew him, but you know. When I was young I used to watch the 'Ellie the Equinoid' show almost daily! Man, the guy who played Ellie sure was dedicated to his role. Oh! And for my 7th birthday, Vance had some guy dress up as Ellie and come to my birthday party! Though, Vance never liked Ellie... or Equinoids. As a kid I never really got it, but now I feel like it was some weird personal grudge."
	
Jerry shrugs. "Either way, that plushie is old. I've had it since before I was even in Vance's custody. I had a blowout with my uncle one time when I refused to kill some Equinoids on a hunting trip, and he was... well he was pretty mad. I was so scared I hid all of my Ellie stuff under the floorboards so he couldn't take it away! Not that I think he ever would have. For as much as he hated Ellie, he loved me more..."

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_4
text: "It was always uncanny, everywhere I went in the Protectorate people would follow me. If I was ever in front of a crowd, no matter what I said they'd always cheer for me. People would come up to me in the streets and push past my guards, just for a chance to shake my hand or ask me something. There was one girl who kept at it though: I couldn't tell if she was a stalker or... I don't know. I can't really remember her name but I think it started with an 'L'? I thought she was just some soldier, but Sebastian said apparently her father's rich. Like, really rich. I kind of miss all that praise though... but uh, well it was never really earned. I don't want to be cheered on for things my uncle did, good or bad. I want to be cheered for things I've done. Maybe some day I'll be more than just the Admiral's nephew..."

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_5
text: "I've been to Universe 1 a couple times. Never longer than a week, and the tour was kept pretty tightly bound. It's... it's..." Jerry seems at a loss for words. "It's very... industrial. It didn't feel like a place people lived in. Yet, they do. Trillions. A whole galaxy's worth of humans. Everywhere was either too pristine to the point of sterile, or was some automated death machine factory. Safe to say, I didn't like it there. The Rebellion has changed. I was too young to really remember the original civil war, but it couldn't possibly have been like this? Who would have supported it? Who DOES support it?"

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_6
text: "Captain, do you mind if I ask a question? About the Federation?" Jerry rubs his arm uncomfortably.

event.text: "Okay... uhm... why does the Federation have Engi in it? My uncle told me the Engi don't even understand the concept of democracy, or civil rights, or... anything the Federation seems to stand for! The Engi remind me of the Rebellion... one species, totalitarian, and terribly unimaginative outside of creating new death machines. Why would you allow them into the Federation?"

choice.text: The Federation stands for peace, not democracy.

event.text: "So... so if the Rebellion was willing to talk peace, and to stop fighting, you'd let them into the Federation? And the Hive, and the Theocracy, and everyone else? The Federation banished the Slugs once, surely they can do it again with the Engi!" Jerry seems genuinely confused but doesn't want to risk asking more questions right now. He wanders off instead to ponder the situation.

"My uncle says it's because the Federation is too afraid to get rid of them. Then the Federation must be pretty weak... My uncle says the Engi are too weak to be soldiers, so the Federation's engineer force is comprised almost entirely of them instead. If the Engi don't even fight for the Federation, how can you trust them?" Jerry seems genuinely confused, and totally oblivious to the influences of his uncle playing over him. At least you can tell he means it all in innocent earnesty, but for his sake he better shake these views soon.

"So... so the only reason the Harmony is in the Federation is because you're too afraid to get rid of them? Then the Federation must be pretty weak... My uncle says the Engi are too weak to be soldiers, so the Federation's engineer force is comprised almost entirely of them instead. If the Engi don't even fight for the Federation, how can you trust them?" Jerry seems genuinely confused, and totally oblivious to the influences of his uncle playing over him. At least you can tell he means it all in innocent earnesty, but for his sake he better shake these views soon.

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_GENERIC_7
text:
"Uncle always told me my father was a deadbeat and a smoker. My mother... when she was alive, didn't talk much about him. I don't think I even know his name. I wonder if he loved me. Vance told me he didn't. He couldn't have, with how he treated our family. Family is the most important thing of course. Vance said I should be proud to be a Wentworth, and not a... whatever my father's name was. When my mother divorced him, she changed her name back to Wentworth."
	
	Jerry seems to realize he's been rambling about himself for a bit and stops. "Do you have any family, Captain?"

event.text: "Oh, right, you're from U0. It must be so strange there. I hear very mixed descriptions of that place, no one can seem to quite agree what it's like. At least, not in the Rebel circles. In the Protectorate, people seem to think it must be identical to Universe 1, but having seen U1... I would be shocked if that was the case. At the very least there'd have to be more than just humans everywhere! Well uhm... I hope we all make it through this Captain, and you can go see your family again! I don't really have any family anymore... but I guess I'll have to make do."

"Oh... Well, my uncle always told me family is what makes civilized creatures strong. It keeps us organized and together, away from violence. That's why the Mantis are so violent, they don't have proper family structures!"
			
Jerry blinks. "Sorry that sounds... sounds like something my uncle would say. Vance always had a lot of ideas, and he always wanted to make sure everyone understood them. Myself especially. I guess those things really stick with you."

Jerry seems shocked by this notion. "Nothing?! But... that's not what Vance told me. Family is what makes civilized creatures strong. Keeps them organized and together, and away from violence. That's why the Mantis are so violent, they don't have proper family structures!"
			
Jerry blinks. "Sorry that sounds... sounds like something my uncle would say. Vance always had a lot of ideas, and he always wanted to make sure everyone understood them. Myself especially. I guess those things really stick with you."

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_NIGHTS_1
text:
Nights stumbles into the cafeteria, bottle in hand, smiling wide and smugly. This isn't the first time it's happened - he does this whenever he's come up with some new brilliant joke. Everyone turns to look at him, except Jerry who's engrossed in a book he's reading.

"E-Everyone! *hiccup* In honor of the good Rebel Admiral, I've written him a poem!" Nights clears his throat and pretends to read from a scroll. "There once wassss an Admiral Vance, who took a career-changing chance! Fought the hive in a war, and they made him quite sssore, and now nothing remainsss in hisss pance!"
	
Everyone in the room groans, and Jerry winces. Nights seems to accept this as a call for more and slides up to Jerry. "Hey kid, do you know what a pen isss?" Jerry, utterly confused and very uncomfortable, nods his head. "Uh... yes?"

Nights spreads his arms wide and exclaims "Well hey, at leasssst *hiccup* one Wentworth doessss! HAHAHAHAHAHAH HAAAAH HAAAHAHAHA! IT'SSSS FUNNY- IT'SSSS FUNNY BECAUSSSSE HE HASSSS NO-"
	
Jerry suddenly jumps down his chair and grabs Nights, hoisting him off the ground and shaking him. "DON'T YOU DARE SPEAK ABOUT MY UNCLE IN THAT MANNER YOU WORTHLESS, DISGUSTING, DRUNK, SLIMEY WASTE OF SPACE! YOU ARE THE REASON THE REST OF THE GALAXY SEES THE SLUG SPECIES AS NOTHING BUT A WORTHLESS PILE OF DEGENERATE ROT!" Jerry throws Nights down, making him roll across the floor in a stunned haze. The room has gone completely silent, with everyone else in utter shock. Jerry says nothing, not even an apology, and leaves the room.

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_TUCO_1
text:
You try to take a brief snooze to ease your mind but are promptly awoken by angry shouts from another room. You follow the sounds into the break room, where it seems Tuco and Jerry are sitting across from each other playing some kind of gambling game with a deck of cards.

"Oh, Captain! Would you like to join us? Tuco is teaching me how to play his favorite game, 'Boarden'. I'm not quite sure I get it, but it's a lot of fun!"

Tuco slams his fist on the table, sending a couple colorful tokens that have been placed around flying. "Don't GET IT? Bloody hell, kid, you're the best god damn gambler I've ever seen. I've gone against the greatest Boarden players in the galaxy and you're whooping my ass. I'm not even going easy!"

Jerry blushes. "Oh... sorry. I'm not trying to make you look bad..." Tuco laughs.

"Don't worry about it kid. Just uh... never go gambling in public. There's a lot of people out there who don't like to lose, and you'll probably end up dead sooner or later. But if you ever DO wanna go... just invite me, alright? I wanna see those sons of bitches get their due."

name: SOCIALIZE_JERRY_IRWIN_1
text:
Irwin notices Jerry painting an Equinoid mural on one of the ship's walls. Taking interest, he slithers by and observes it. "Ssssay, kid, you got a talent for that. Where'd you learn how to draw ssso well?"

Jerry smiles, "Oh, my uncle used to take me hunting in Guild space. I had a sketchbook back then which I would draw the Equinoids and other wildlife in."

Irwin nods enthusiastically. "OH, you're that one kid who'sss rich uncle forked an arm and a leg over to ussse our hunting groundsss! Alwaysss good to sssee a fellow hunter! Ever tried Equinoid meat? They tassste... ssparkly? I made a soup bowl out of an Equinoid skull once. Lot of remarkable thingsss you can do with a ssskeleton. Oh, and rugsss. Wonderful rugsss, their hidesss make. A good hunter utilizesss every part of their kill!"

Jerry frowns, upset. "Oh I... I never... uhm... I never killed the Equinoids. My uncle did. I just drew them, watched them graze, you know... uh... not much of a hunter."

Irwin realizes his mistake and seems genuinely sorry. "Oh, my bad. Sssorry kid, it'sss jussst sssecond nature to me. Probably for the bessst you're nothing like your uncle."

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_NOTHING
text: Ellie appears to be sleeping standing up in her quarters. However, when you take a step closer, she draws a knife and points it at you. "Oh, sorry! Ellie didn't see you there! You shouldn't bother a horse when she's sleeping! Go find someone else to play with!"

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_GENERIC_1
text:
"Doo da doo, do do doo doo dadodoo do! Bah doo do do, doo do da doo da! Elllliiieeee, the Equiiiiinoiiiiid!" Ellie snaps her fingers and spins around on one foot, bobbing up and down to the off-beat rhythm of the Ellie theme song. You try to talk to her but she cuts you off, screaming "DO NOT INTERRUPT THE THEME SONG!" 
	
You think you shouldn't interrupt the theme song.

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_GENERIC_2
text: "I miss my friends! Dora, Cammie, Remmy... We used to have so much fun together! Solving mysteries aboard the Equinox, roaming the galaxy, drinking quarp juice... mmmm... quarp juice! So tasty and delicious!"

event.text: "Only the most wonderfulific deliciousfulness in the whole galaxy! It's made from freshly squeezed Quarp! And many many many many additive sugars! Yay!!!"
"It's a fruit, idiot."

choice.text: I don't think Quarp is real.

event.text: Ellie laughs. "Wow superfan, you really are dumb." Ellie says nothing more and gallops away.

choice.text: Offer Ellie some Quarp Juice from storage.

event.text: Ellie nods her head eagerly and takes one of the juice boxes, but as she starts to drink it she spits the pink liquid out. "EWWWW! GROSS! This isn't what quarp juice tastes like! And there's a spider on the box! Stupid stupid buffoons, children don't like spiders! Spiders are gross and icky and scary! Children love horsies! Like me! Neigh!"

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_GENERIC_3
text: You make the mistake of accidentally calling Ellie 'Stephan' once, and she reacts rather oddly. She turns to look at you in response for a brief moment before catching her error, immediately spinning back around and pretending she didn't hear you. When you try to get her attention by the name 'Ellie' again, she still doesn't respond. It seems she's fallen into some strange trance, or maybe is pretending to be asleep. You'll have to be more careful next time.

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_GENERIC_4
text: "It's a shame you're so old superfan! You look just about the age to not quite have been born in time to witness my show! You have no idea about the wonderificness you missed! Not that you COULDN'T have watched it while you were older, silly! It's soooo good it spans generations! Ellie is eternal! Ellie is forever."

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_GENERIC_5
text: Ellie suddenly leaps towards you and grabs you in a gigantic bear hug, squeezing you so hard you feel like your organs might rupture. "I LOVE hugs! Yay!!! Hugs!! A long time ago there was someone else I used to hug a lot! I don't... I don't remember her name. So strange. But I remember the hugs!" There seems to be a strange sadness in Ellie's voice, but it quickly dissipates as her scattered psyche loses focus and proceeds to the next random adventure.

name: SOCIALIZE_ELLIE_JERRY_1
text:
You notice Jerry watching Ellie strangely. Ellie wanders over to him, offering him an imaginary lollipop. Jerry accepts out of courtesy and follows it with a question. "Hey uh... Ellie? Have we ever met before?"
	
Ellie cocks her head. "Probably! All the children have watched my show before! Everyone knows Ellie, everyone loves Ellie! You must be another fan!!!"
	
Jerry nods. "Well yeah, I know you're Ellie. The real Ellie. By the way I'm uh... honored to meet you. I loved your show when I was younger. My favorite show, actually! But I just... I swear we've met. Like, personally. You seem... so familiar, and I don't know why."
	
Ellie says nothing, seemingly not even hearing the question. Instead she hops away to offer candy hallucinations to someone else. Jerry hangs his head and sighs, then returns to his quarters.

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_NOTHING
text: Stephan is sitting in his quarters, staring at the battered mask of his old costume. Tears running down his face, he doesn't realize you're watching him until you clear your throat. "S-sorry I can't... I can't talk- talk right now." Looks like you'll have to search elsewhere for conversation.

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_GENERIC_1
text: "I've been an actor since the day I flunked out of university. I started running a side gig at a traveling carnival as a mascot, where I befriended one of the carnies. That was Paul. We never saw eye to eye on a lot of things. Politics, especially. But we did both have higher hopes for ourselves and our futures than just some carnival shitshow. He had dreams of making his own TV show, and when I told him I had always wanted to be an actor - we had a crazy idea. We pooled our money, and we started recording after work in the big tent. I'd wear my costume and we'd do some basic family friendly comedy. It was a strange time. The Federation was still relatively new, and the Union was still recovering from the Fed-Mantis War. Things looked good for a while, after the Federation managed to put an end to the Inquisitions. People wanted light, fluffy entertainment. Something to just laugh at and forget about that dreadful war. We never expected to find such success... But we blew up! We got a small segment at the end of some big front runner cartoons on a major Union network, and soon started up the Ellie the Equinoid show for real! Things were so hopeful back then... god... and now it's all come to this." Stephan burries his face in his hands, signalling his story is over.

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_GENERIC_2
text: "I'm a bit ashamed I didn't fight in the Federation-Mantis War. I'm a bit too junior, but not by much. Regardless, I've been a supporter of the Federation since day one. Or I suppose, more accurate, I've been anti-anything that's against the Federation. The Rebellion is a scourge on the Union, the brainchild of people who really, truly think a galaxy where every species is isolated from eachother is a good one. That it's the only way to maintain peace, somehow. Wentworth is an idiot, not a mastermind. He's not really the one who turned the Rebellion into a death machine. It was his corporate interest friends, always whispering in his ear during nights of secret society poker games, that led us here. Frankly, the thing that ruined the Union wasn't even remotely the immigrants, it was the xenophobic masses who wanted rid of them so badly they were willing to tear the whole damn nation apart." Stephan shakes his head in disgust.

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_GENERIC_3
text:
"I wonder what happened to Elena... it's been so so long. Do you think she knows? About me, and Ellie? When she left me, it wasn't this bad. It wasn't mania, it was just obsession. To think, if I had just gotten my act together..."
	
Stephan lingers, tears forming in his eyes. "No... I can't... I can't keep dwelling on this. I'm going to tear myself apart if I keep this up. I need to forget Elena. I need to forget the Wentworths, and my old life. I need to be a new Stephan. No longer a circus freak, no longer Ellie. Thank you, Captain, for showing me this light."

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_GENERIC_4
text: "Captain, do you fear death?" Stephan stares at you blankly, and his deadpan delivery almost makes you wonder if it's meant to be a joke.

event.text: Stephan nods. "Then we're in the same boat. This dread, this fear of existence... sometimes it makes me miss the numbness of being Ellie. I didn't know fear, or death, or dread. But is that worth becoming a monster? I guess not. Nothing is. I find so often we try to escape ourselves, escape our mortality, that we let ourselves become something we're not. We become the worst we can be, because when we're our worst, when we hate everyone else and see everyone as an enemy, then death seems like the least of our worries. Now, there is nothing left for me to fear but death. I've lost everything, and yet I still cling to my life. God, I'm such a mess..."

"Interesting. Then I suppose I am jealous of your bravado." Stephan smiles weakly. "In a sense, I almost miss the numbness of being Ellie. I didn't know fear, or death, or dread. But is that worth becoming a monster? I guess not. Nothing is. I find so often we try to escape ourselves, escape our mortality, that we let ourselves become something we're not. We become the worst we can be, because when we're our worst, when we hate everyone else and see everyone as an enemy, then death seems like the least of our worries. Now, there is nothing left for me to fear but death. I've lost everything, and yet I still cling to my life. God, I'm such a mess..."

"I'm afraid I'm not that philosophical, Captain." Stephan laughs. "If you haven't noticed, I used to play a horse in a show for 11 year olds. I'm not exactly a brainiac. If you're asking those kinds of questions though, then keep at it. We need more people who think critically about this existence, and don't rush headfirst into the fray..."

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_GENERIC_5
text:
"When the Ellie show was still new, and just a little circus sideshow Paul and I ran, one of our biggest struggles was naming the character. That was, until I met a lovely young lady. Her name was Elena, and she became the center of my world. When we started dating, I started calling her by a new nickname. Ellie. Pretty little Ellie lingered in my thoughts every day, every moment of my life. It sat there, brewing, just long enough that one day it just... came to me. 'Ellie the Equinoid'! I just... shouted it. Heh. Paul was startled by the outburst, but it didn't take any convincing. It was a perfect name, and it stuck. The executives we were trying to pitch the show to loved it as well, but most important Elena thought it was fantastic. And so, Ellie came to be."
	
Stephan looks at the floor. "And now, the name Ellie carries not just one but two sorrows for me. A reminder not only of my disastrous career and descent into madness, but the love of my life I couldn't keep."

name: SOCIALIZE_STEPHAN_JERRY_1
text:
Jerry cautiously approaches Stephan, taking a seat next to him. "So uh... you're the actor who plays Ellie?" Stephan nods. "Who PLAYED Ellie. That gig is up. I don't... I shouldn't ever go back. Nor could I, with this... mess. And uh, who are you?"
	
Jerry seems almost disappointed the man doesn't know him. "Oh, I'm Jerry." Stephan nods. "Jerry. Right, good name. Well, to what do I owe the pleasure, Jerry?"

Jerry shrugs. "It's just... have we ever met? In the costume you felt familiar, but without the costume you feel even more familiar. I just don't know from where, is all."
	
Stephan sighs. "I'm sorry, kid. I've met so many people, so many fans, I just can't remember them all. Maybe when you were younger you attended a tour or something? If your parents used to ta-"

Jerry cuts him off. "Oh, no. I never really knew my parents. My mother died when I was young and I never met my father. My uncle raised me for most of my life."

event.text:
Stephan leans back and gives a courteous smile. "Well, your uncle must have been a good man then, because you seem like a nice kid."
			
			Jerry shakes his head. "Well... not a lot of people think he's a 'good man' around here. My uncle is uhm... Vance Wentworth."
			
			Stephan stops cold, his pupils retracting. "You... your uncle is who? I'm sorry I think I... I misheard you." Jerry repeats himself. Stephan wavers. "Your... your uncle is... Wentworth? Like... No... no no no... Oh my god..."
			
			Jerry looks at the terrified man, afraid he might be on the verge of another breakdown. "Stephan, are you okay? What's wrong? Do I need to get you to the medical room?!"
			
			Stephan steadies himself, trying to pretend like everything is fine. "It's nothing... it's nothing. Don't worry about it kid." Stephan forces a smile. "I'm sorry for worrying you, that's all. Wentworth for an uncle or not, you seem to have turned out alright. Probably better than however your father could have raised you, yeah?" Stephan chokes back some tears. "I-I'm sorry about your mother. And your father. And everything... Oh god Jerry I'm so sorry..." Stephan can't hold it back any longer, and breaks down sobbing. Jerry, still utterly confused, holds the man in his arms and consoles him. The tragic irony of the situation will, perhaps, forever be lost on him. But maybe it's for the best he never learns who his father really is.

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_NOTHING
text: Turzil appears to be in sleep mode, though a sticky-note has been stuck lazily to his forehead. Underneath barely legible scribbles it says "DO NOT DISTURB". Assuming you can take a hint, you probably shouldn't bother him.

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_GENERIC_1
text: You find Turzil's room full of half-painted canvases of beautiful scenery. The Engi spots you looking at them and pushes you out of the room and shuts the door. Seems Turzil still struggles with expression even after separating from the Harmony.

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_GENERIC_2
text: You find Turzil walking around the ship missing his left arm. "My arm is -currently- behaving poorly. Until it accepts its proper [function] as an arm, it will remain in timeout."

event.text: "I fail to understand your [query]. Are you asking the normalcy of arm malfunctions? If so, they are not... -uncommon-, at least amongst malfunctioning Engi. As the Harmony connection erodes, so does the sense of uniformity. Individual components become rogue minds, the body is segmented. Few Separatists retain -existence- as one entity for long. I have [held] on longer than most, but my time will come as well."

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_GENERIC_3
text: You find Turzil banging himself against the wall repeatedly. You try to help him, but he stops you. "Do not [worry]. I am simply -applying- percussive maintenance. I was [informed] it is effective by Human engineers. Do not temper with my [maintenance] procedures, if you would."

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_GENERIC_4
text: Turzil approaches you, bearing a question he seems uncomfortable asking. "I carry a request for insight into the concept of emotions. The Harmony simulation dampens the experiences of -stimulation- in the mind, and once free it can be [hard] to adjust. Are emotions made to be painful? Is the experience of sorrow meant to create inescapable misery? Is pain supposed to cause an inescapable sense of discomfort?"

choice.text: That's kind of the point of emotion.

event.text: "Is it? I... I [cannot] comprehend this. Why would life be designed to know such miseries? Why were the Engi -built- to experience them either? I miss being incapable of emoting. I miss not being able to miss things. Although... I do not [miss] the Harmony. This is an unfortunate yet irreconcilable paradox. I hate being a machine."

choice.text: You'll probably get over it soon.

event.text: "That is fortunate to hear. I am still attempting to [gain] control over my rebellious components and re-unify. Perhaps my -cerebral- components are malfunctioning as well. I will have to make adjustments."

choice.text: I am an empty husk devoid of all feeling.

event.text: Turzil stares blankly at you, unsure how to interpret your response. "Is this... meant to be a -joke-? I apologize. I will seek [counsel] elsewhere."

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_GENERIC_5
text: Turzil approaches meagerly, holding a canvas in his hands. "Captain, I -seek- critical input. As the one -appointed- leader of this crew it is only safe to assume your guidance must be sought on all [crucial] matters. I desire critique. I have engaged in: art." Turzil flips the canvas around to show you a portrait of Admiral Tully of the Federation, painted with broad strokes in a sort of surrealist manner with a heavy use of orange and yellow.

event.text: "Unexpected response. Your use of 'great' is [confusing] in ways I do not understand. Is this the elusive irony? I understand in some subcultures -compliments- are meant to be derived as insults. I will, however, opt to give you the benefit of the doubt. I will keep my art in hopes it will... inspire more pleasant emotions."

"I detect strategic [deployment] of vagueness. I will choose to interpret this as a polite negative response. Thank you for your feedback. I must further -hone- my abilities. I will discard this failed attempt."
"Expected response. I will waste no further time in discarding my frivolous doodles. I apologize for the [interruption], Captain."

choice.text: Why don't you show this to Tully?

event.text: Turzil immediately pulls back the paper in shock. "NO!" A light blinks near Turzil's monitor to signal a soft reboot, and he regains his composure. "No, that will not be necessary. I sought only direct input from the [captain]. I will -stash- my foolish scribbling and perhaps seek better ventures with my time."

name: SOCIALIZE_TURZIL_GENERIC_6
text:
"Pertinent -query-. How does one pronounce the word [INVALID ENTRY]?" Turzil's screen blinks and sparks fly out of him. "Error, failure to pronounce [INVALID ENTRY]."

Again, Turzil's screen blinks and he sparks more. This repeats several times and you start to get worried he'll hurt himself, so you encourage him to stop.

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_NOTHING
text: Anurak has quarantined himself in his quarters, claiming he has entered mandatory meditation time. Judging from his movements earlier you suspect he may have food poisoning from a bad batch of soup, but either way you shouldn't bother him.

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_GENERIC_1
text: "Shellskenbry, I have a very important question for you! Well actually maybe it's not that important but uh it is a question and it's a question for you! Uhm... does your underwear ever mysteriously vanish?"

event.text: "Ever since I started hiding in the Ministry Capital, my underwear has been randomly vanishing! I think I may be cursed! Oh this isn't the first curse I've had... I hate curses! A blight on my life, just like all my missing underwear! If you see a nice pair of bright blue briefs do let me know!"

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_GENERIC_2
text: "Ah, hello Shellskenbry! Wonderful day we're having!" Anurak salutes to you.

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_GENERIC_3
text: "I miss my caravan! Oh if only I could go back to my old life! Not the Duskbringer part, that's not what I meant by my old life! Don't think I want to be a Duskbringer again, because I don't! I want to go back to the caravan, and continue living as a nice, friendly, cowardly monk. It was a lot safer and a lot nicer. It was a little refuge for anyone who needed it. It didn't matter who you were or what you had done. As someone who's made a lot of mistakes in their past, I'm in no place to judge anyone looking for repentance. My secret? I just don't ask. I can only hope that if I forgive everyone, eventually they will come to forgive me."

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_GENERIC_4
text: Anurak comes running out of the kitchen carrying a bowl of soup. He forces it into your hands, demanding that you taste it. He's in such a panic he won't even tell you why.

event.text: By the time you've barely even gotten the surprisingly tasty liquid down your gullet, Anurak is already prodding you. "Is it good? Oh by the Eye I think I used too much salt! It's ruined! I'm sure it's ruined, I've ruined the damn soup! I'm a terrible chef, and I can't even make soup with the right amount of salt! Oh woe is me!"
"Does it? Really? Crap, I don't remember how much extra salt I added now! Now I'll never be able to replicate this recipe ever again! I'm such a fool, I never pay attention to anything!"

choice.text: It's fine, though it is a bit too salty.

event.text: "I knew it! IT'S RUINED!" Anurak falls to the ground, sobbing. "I've ruined the soup, ohhhh it's awful! What do I do?! I can't remove salt! I have to start all over!" Suddenly, the Zoltan hops back to his feet. "Yes, I'll start over! And this time, I'll make the best damn soup you've ever had!"

choice.text: It's terrible. I regret drinking it.

event.text: "I knew it! Oh damn it! I'm never making soup again! No no that's a lie... I will definitely make soup again. And then I'll cry about ruining it again! Oh why am I like this? Why can't I just be normal?!"
Anurak continues to look at you expectantly, but when you finally make it clear you aren't trying the mystery liquid, he runs off to find some other crew to taste it.

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_DEVORAK_1
text:
Anurak, carrying a large pot of soup, manages to grunt out a question to Devorak, asking if he'd like any soup. Devorak turns to him, stares him dead in the eyes, and says, "I don't want your damn soup!"
	
Anurak drops the pot, and his arms go slack by his sides. "Oh... oh. I... I..." Tears begin to form in his eyes, when Devorak starts maniacally laughing. "HAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAH! I'm only joking friend! Of course I'd love your soup!" Devorak nudges Anurak and winks, and the two begin to laugh together. After witnessing all of this, you're starting to think being in the Duskbringers has had some very adverse effects on both of their mental health.

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_DEVORAK_2
text: You find Anurak and Devorak sitting at a table, playing some board game. As you walk past, Anurak shouts for you. "Oh Shellskenbry! Would you like to play?" Devorak nods. "Yes, we are playing the classic game of Jakeir. An exciting strategy game, I think you would enjoy!"

event.text:
You take a seat at the table, and Anurak starts to explain it before Devorak cuts him off. "No, no need old friend. The Captain can figure it out as we play, yes? Let us not waste time with instructions."
			
			Anurak seems fairly annoyed. "But what if the Captain doesn't figure it out? How will they enjoy the game then? It would be tragic, a calamity! Oh god this game will be ruined if th-" Devorak shushes Anurak. "Calm down, you worry too much. You musn't panic about everything, you will kill yourself with such worrying."
			
			Anurak's panic only furthers. "No, don't you understand?! You don't worry enough, you just rush headfirst into everything! Why can't you be more of a coward like me! There is safety in caution, and you are nothing but a steadfast fool! GAH!"
			
			Anurak flips the table over, spilling the game pieces everywhere. You both look at him while he takes a few heavy breaths. "I know... I know you're not a Duskbringer anymore, Devorak. But you still act like one! You rush into everything and never think anything through!"
			
			Anurak storms off, and Devorak turns to you. "I just wanted to play a game. What was that?"

name: SOCIALIZE_DEVORAK_NOTHING
text: Devorak is meditating in his quarters. As you watch him from the door way, he pokes a look at you and closes his eyes again, signalling that you better find someone else to make conversation with.

name: SOCIALIZE_DEVORAK_GENERIC_1
text: "They say a warrior is only as good as their weapon. I say a weapon is only as good as the warrior that carries it." Devorak bows, confident you grasp the wealth of depth in this wisdom.

choice.text: Isn't that basically the same thing?

event.text: "No. It is the same thing but reversed. The transitive property does not apply." Devorak bows again.

"No. Do not agree. You can understand, but you cannot agree until you have learned this lesson for yourself. It cannot be taught, only experienced. This too, must be experienced, not taught. And so, you will learn, that everything I could ever tell you is pointless and can be learned elsewhere. This is my greatest advice." Devorak bows again.
Devorak scowls. "There is no need for insults. I'm trying to give wise advice. Whether you want to accept it is not my problem, but rude words is how you make enemies."

name: SOCIALIZE_DEVORAK_GENERIC_2
text: "It was a catastrophe, what happened back there in the city. I did not expect such brazen behavior from the Duskbringers. I... I guess I was deluded into thinking Zoltan supremacists would not be so hypocritical as to attack fellow Zoltan civilians? But of course, it was my greatest mistake to expect anything resembling reason from a fascist. To them, those people were 'necessary sacrifices'. I am disgusted by the justifications used by the people I once so proudly called myself a member of."

name: SOCIALIZE_DEVORAK_GENERIC_3
text: "I AM THE INCARNATION OF DEATH! I HAVE SEEN DARKNESS AND TASTED THE BITTERSWEETNESS OF THE END! AND YET I AM WITHOUT DEATH! I AM THE DEATHLESS ONE, HE WHO IS IMMORTAL, WHO IS FREE OF THE BINDS OF LIFE! HAHAHAHAH! BASK IN MY PRESENCE AND WITNESS WHAT LIFE CAN BE WHEN IT HAS NO MORTAL LIMITS! HAHAHAH!"

event.text: Devorak clears his throat. "Uhm, yes. Sorry about that, just had to get it out of my system. Have I uh... mentioned that I think the Clone Bay has some... adverse effects on the Zoltan chassis? I think my neural framework may have decayed just a little while I was a Duskbringer. So, I apologize ahead of time for any chaotic outbursts."

name: SOCIALIZE_DEVORAK_GENERIC_4
text:
"It's curious to me the suicide bombing is the tactic that everyone focuses on with the Duskbringers. I suppose it's just the taboo and the extremity of it that draws people's attention. But the Duskbringers employ a lot more than just bombing, it's more about warfare at any cost. Once, my team was racing against a Kleptocracy aquatic unit to capture an Aether supply line from the Dynasty. Being trained in such field, we were sure the day was lost. But then, one of my compatriots fell into a pool with the Slugs in it. They all died of electrocution. The Zoltan died too, but of course we had a Clone Bay nearby."
	
Devorak ponders this story for a few moments. "Actually, I guess that would be a form of suicide bombing, technically. But that was just a bad example, okay?"

name: SOCIALIZE_DEVORAK_GENERIC_5
text:
"I am willing to sacrifice myself for the greater good of whatever noble cause requires it." Devorak bows, although it seems he isn't done.
	
"That said... I would generally prefer a Clone Bay be available nearby. Just because I'm willing to become a martyr doesn't mean I'm stupid about it. I'd rather live if I had the choice."

name: SOCIALIZE_MAFAN_NOTHING
text: Mafan points at a sign on the door of their quarters that says 'office hours are cancelled.' The screens in the room have massive walls of figures and numbers that suggest there may be science happening right now.

name: SOCIALIZE_MAFAN_GENERIC_1
text: Mafan harrumphs while reading some news reports on the nearby console. "When you go on a long term expedition into the 'grove, the galaxy feels like an entirely different place by the time you get back out. Still, would have been nice to get out and have the Rebel and Duskbringer problems already dealt with."

event.text: "...and that may as well be us, is that what you're saying? Logical stance, but I still think my talents would be better served in a science ship than a war zone."
Mafan groans. "Ugh, tell me about it. Feels like you step out during one conflict and by the time you're back two more have started! Lousy thugs intruding on my stargazing."

choice.text: You only notice when something's wrong.

event.text: Mafan thinks for a moment. "Ah, you've caught me in my cognitive bias. I need to be more careful around you. That's embarrassing. "

name: SOCIALIZE_MAFAN_GENERIC_2
text: Mafan is humming when you enter. There's a map of the Stargrove unfurled on the desk. "Ah, captain. I hope you're doing well. I was just reminiscing a little bit. Do you have any questions?"

event.text: "Remember where we met? The Gravastar is one of the most massive objects in this entire galaxy. When such a massive object speeds into the pass of a gigantic nebula, much of the gasses coalesce into dense clusters of stars, and create other fascinating phenomena! It's truly a remarkable event that has been happening for longer than any known civilization."

choice.text: Why are scientists drawn to the Stargrove?

event.text: "The safe areas of the galaxy are much easier to study. Every species that has a homeworld has been studying it for as long as they've lived there. But dangerous places... they require much more care to study. And in our cutthroat world, where new discoveries are hard to come by, it makes sense to go where there is so much left to uncover."

choice.text: Does the Stargrove have any special significance to you?

event.text: "Like any of the spacefaring races, our distant ancestors could not always travel the stars. They looked up at the night sky with their telescopes and saw a truly remarkable phenomenon. The Zoltan homeworld is very near the Stargrove, and we have always dreamed of achieving FTL spaceflight in order to see it up close. Even with all our modern advancements, it is still a hostile place to survive within."
"No? Don't be so incurious, captain!" Mafan shakes their head sadly. "Well, I suppose there's no accounting for taste. Carry on."

name: SOCIALIZE_MAFAN_GENERIC_3
text: After hanging out with Mafan for a few minutes, they hand you a piece of handwritten paper that seems to have been torn out of one of their notebooks. It's a feedback form, asking whether you enjoyed your conversation, if there's any topics you'd like to cover and what number you would rate their conversations numerically. "If you wouldn't mind taking this little survey, I would be happy to know!"

choice.text: Fill it out with polite responses.

event.text: "Ah... is... is that it? I always used to get this response from my students. Oh well, I guess if it's fine, then it's fine."

choice.text: Fill it out with funny responses.

event.text: "What the...? You graded me poorly on hygiene? How does that even make sense? But thank you for the 69/10, that's definitely the highest score I've ever gotten."

choice.text: Ask why they're giving you a survey.

event.text: "Oh, well it's standard practice, right? I know it's only handwritten, but I couldn't find whatever the version is that everyone else uses."

name: SOCIALIZE_MAFAN_GENERIC_4
text: You catch Mafan eyeing an escape pod. "You know, I've had to use these pods on occasion. It's really cramped, and sometimes it takes a while to get anywhere. You ever land in a primitive pre-spaceflight society and have to draft all the paperwork using whatever you can find on that planet, in the hopes the Ministry sends a scout your way? Not my idea of a fun time."

name: SOCIALIZE_MAFAN_GENERIC_5
text: You ask Mafan about the danger of researching stars. "Oh, it's no trouble at all. Submit the right paperwork, and the Ministry doesn't care one bit." You ask about the threats to their personal safety. "Oh, come on. We've got space-ships, what's the worst that could happen?" A fiery death, you say. "Yeah, but that can happen on your planet too, you know! Sure it's less likely, but you're also less likely to enjoy the warm glow of stellar phenomena. But it does mean that I have a pretty high research assistant turnover rate..."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_MAFAN_1
text:
You find Mafan feeding paper to Rig. Mafan looks over and says "...oh, don't mind me, captain! I'm just showing Tintan some of my art. I like to sketch things on occasion, and I'm sure it gets boring in there."

	Rig makes a grumpy sound. "I'll try anything to get her to shut the hell up whenever she's bored. Feed me all the paper you can."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_MAFAN_1
text:
Alkali squints at Mafan. "I don't understand your need to wander into danger, Mafan. You can hhhhave the graduate students collect all that researchhhh for you."

	"And you're just going to trust the data that someone else gathered for you? No, the measurements have to be done just right! Otherwise, you're just asking to print a retraction."

	"Not if you penalize your graduate students with great prejudice. Fear is a potent motivator."

	"But that requires social interaction! No thanks. I'll just do it myself."

name: SOCIALIZE_ANURAK_MAFAN_1
text:
Anurak is hovering next to Mafan's desk. Mafan is trying to wave them off. "For the last time, not right now! You're getting soup rings on my graph paper!"

"It's good for you. It'll help you think." Anurak said, pressing the bowl against Mafan's face.

"I know, you've said that eight times now." Mafan pushed Anurak away. "I'm busy!"

"Are you sure?"

"Oh, look! It's the captain! Why don't you offer the captain the rest of your soup?"

"Shellskenbry? Oh, we were just having a wonderful time. Please help me convince this young scientist to have some soup."

choice.text: Try to lead Anurak away from Mafan.

event.text: You express interest in Anurak's soup and beckon them over. "Shellskenbry, glad to hear you haven't lost your taste buds. These scientists sure are a cranky sort, are they not? Always complaining about stains. Have an appetite for once!"

choice.text: Tell Mafan to just drink the soup already.

event.text:
"Do you think I haven't tried? I've had 3 bowls! I'm completely full." Mafan sighs. "Fine, fork it over."

Anurak is cheerful. "Shellskenbry, you've done it!" Anurak hands Mafan a bowl of soup. 

Mafan pretends to drink it down, but clearly just pours it into a test tube under their labcoat pocket. "There, I drank your soup, are you happy?"

"Yes, of course. Now, one more thing before I leave. Do you want some soup?"

name: SOCIALIZE_MAYEB_MAFAN_1
text:
You find Mafan and Mayeb in her quarters. "Mayeb, I must know! Do Stars, or rather, does radiation have a flavor? Does it make you feel satiated?"

	Mayeb tilts her head. "...Well, your people find beauty in visual things as well, do you not? For us, that visual beauty is not unlike culinary taste."

	"That's a fascinating way to think of it! What is art but a culinary delight for your eyes?" Mafan scribbles some notes down.

	"As for satiation... yes, we do start to feel drained if we're in the dark too much. And the artificial light you find on non-photosynthevore ships just taste stale. It doesn't make your appetite feel sated in the least."

	"You know what? I completely get it! We should install better lighting in this place."

name: SOCIALIZE_TYEREL_MAFAN_1
text:
Mafan and Ty E'rel are sitting at a table in the common area, passing notes back and forth. As you step closer, you notice that the notes are actually what appear to be tedious beaurocratic forms. Mafan will pass Ty E'rel a form entitled "survey request for personal information in use of interpersonal bonding.". Then Ty E'rel passes out a filled form of several, overly clinical responses in professional language. Then, Ty E'rel will fill out a form requesting information about the current status of Mafan's family members, and their well being.

	Mafan smiles as you enter. "Oh, hi Captain. Ty E'rel's great - finally, someone with some actual social skills, am I right?"

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_MAFAN_1
text:
Ariadne and Mafan are sitting behind a screen, watching simulated stellar phenomena.

	"Impressive, Doctor! But what if we made it spin... even faster?" Ariadne says, with excitement.

	"Yes, yes! But before that, let me show you what increasing the density does first at this speed." Mafan says.

	They continue to play around with the simulator for what feels like hours. You can't get a word in edgewise.

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_MAFAN_1
text:
Kazaaakplethkilik and Mafan seem to be having a spirited discussion - they're both raising their voices, but neither of them seems angry.

	"The best defense is a good offense!" Kaz says. "If killing foe, not needing to fix self up afterward! Winning fast, saving time. Time is scrap!"

	"I understand your perspective. But most particular offensive strategies have a blind spot of some sort! Protecting yourself gives yourself a chance to recalibrate your approach and think about how best to survive. This also allows you to escape easier!"

	"Escape is defeatist! Need heart of a winner to claim victory! Hesitating is death on the battlefield. Slay fast, your enemy cannot prepare themselves."

	"I cannot disagree more, you can think your way out of anything if you have strong enough defensive preparations!"

choice.text: Agree with Kaz. Offense is better.

event.text:
"Renegade is fighting many battles, and knows how to securing victory, just like this legendary pirate in front of you."

			Mafan shakes their head. "Well, I guess I can't argue too much with two experienced fighters. But I will alawys prioritize keeping myself safe and living to think for another day."

choice.text: Agree with Mafan. Defense is better.

event.text:
"I'm glad you think so. All the experiences you've had... you've needed to prepare yourself for any number of different situations, right?"

			Kaz laughs. "The Renegade was beating me. But I am thinking I needed more overwhelming offense, not more hiding."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_MAFAN_1
text:
Freddy taps Mafan's shoulder. "How do you do, old chap! Might you be the stargazing professor that we pulled aboard?"

	"Yes, Professor at Subset Academy."

	"Chuffed to meet you, allow me to introduce myself. I'm Freddy. Intellectual of the Free Mantises."

	"Oh, is that so? Aside from our current mission, I only ever hear about the Free Mantises from Ministry news reports. According to them, you're all... well..."

	"Ah, my brainrotted comrades have quite the barbaric reputation, don't they? No, no. The original Free Mantises were brilliant minds who left the Hive on political differences."

	"Is that so...? I'm surprised the Hive even has enough of an education system to have intellectuals. How did you come to be?"

	"The hive has no schools. Before our exodus, we'd have a lovely chat with the smarter slaves and take interest in learning materials that we salvaged from raids. One thing led to another, and what would become the Free Mantis agreed with those that we were told to slaughter and enslave."

	"Fascinating..." Mafan blinks. "Well, perhaps I can meet a Free Mantis astrophysicist one day."

	"Ah, Luziiio! Remind me to introduce you when our mission is over!"

name: SOCIALIZE_BREACH_TRIO
text: Ariadne, Mafan, and Kazaaak are gathered in the cargo hold, sharing a bottle of Rockman liquor. You can't hear what they're talking about from this distance, but whatever it is, they're discussing it very loudly.

event.text:
"I tell you, I don't know what Pinnacle was thinking when they made those damn robots, they were worse to deal with than the Vek."

                "Yes, yes, glowing lady always telling me 'no kill', but is very easy to say when rockets not pointed at you! Commander ordering me to use no weapons, but smashing into them with mech is no weapon!"

                "And Dewey with hish stupid... stupid... what'd he call it, the :!;;#?"

                "The train?"

                "YES! That thing broke so, so many times! I wanted to... to jump back BEFORE the war started just to tell him to- *hic* armor the thing up!"

                "You know it no work! He have train, mean lady have train, acid man have train - All get broken! Fancy one just more expensive to break!"

                "At least Kern understood the scale of what we were fighting - I never felt safer than when I saw R.S.T. terraforming those bugs out of existence."

                "I- I liked the A.C.I.D. launchers more; I wish I could have looked at Detritus's labs. I don't think I've ever seen a better solvent. What I wouldn't give to have a tub of the stuff..."

                "Yes, drunk Zoltan be needing strong acid on ship, great idea. Why not just opening airlock now, save time on hull breach?"

                "If you two are going to start bickering, I'm putting the bottle away. I don't want to explain to the Captain why Mafan's lab coat is scattered across the cargo hold."

"And then I jumping next to Vek, and it slam into building, destroying both! Island was saved, and we go to attack volcano!"
                
                "You know we were supposed to protect the people in those buildings, right?"

                "Bah, not important if timeline saved! Cannot sweating over every broken egg!"

                "That's- that's not how that one goes."

                "Oh, and you be knowings right way now? You lightweight, lightbulb!"

                "Hey, you- you :;!#!:. I fought in the same war you did, AND I tried to save people."

                "Freezing them into their apartments feels like cheating, Mafan."

                "Hey, they all got thawed out later. They gave me a mech that shot ice, there's only so much you can do with that."

                "You had to pilot other mechs at some point, right?"

                "Barely! Most of the time I hopped into a new timeline, they shoved me right in that stupid frozen artillery. It was cold in there!"

                "Can you even be feelings cold? Me think you just like to complain."

                "HEY! Nothing is safe from getting frozen, it just takes more. I hypothe- pothesi- THINK that if you dipped an Engi into liquid nitrogen, it'd stop working even if it didn't 'feel' it!"

                "Oooh, is sounding like very good idea. Thinkings we can find Engi for test? You never telling me science can be fun."

                "I really shouldn't let you two drink together anymore."

                "Hey, we're- *hic* getting along this time!"

                "Somehow, that's worse than seeing you bicker."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_NOTHING
text: "Apologies Captain, I'm just giving the hat the old spit-shine! Well, trying to. My mucus has appeared to have stained the fabric and I'm having issues removing it. I'll be busy for a while, maybe you should check on the others!"

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_1
text:
You hear a knock on your cabin door and open it to find Freddy standing there. "Captain, I wish to share with you some gifts from my people! I've received a shipment of some various items from my old clan, gifts of sorts, that they wish to share with you! I'll just leave these here for you." 
	
Freddy places down a large box full of crayon drawings, a several hundred page long fanfiction titled "How I married the Renegade Captain and how we defeated the entire Rebellion and Ministry together part 1", and some unwarranted and explicit photography. You put the box in a safe spot and make a mental note to be more grateful Freddy doesn't act this way.

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_2
text: You find Freddy scribbling away in a small notebook of his. You ask him about it, to which he responds, "It's a journal, where I practice the different galactic dialects I've been learning. Could you help me, actually, Captain? I've been trying to master the Human language of Pan, but I've been struggling with some strange exceptions. Do you speak Pan well by chance?"

event.text: You help explain some of the strange intricacies of Pan to Freddy, and he scribbles away dilligently in his journal. "So, the rule is 'i before e except after c'? Yet there are dozens of contradictions. I'm terribly confused. I think I am beginning to understand though. Oh, if the Hive had only known how much the Fed-Mantis War would set us back, would we ever have made such a mistake? Oh why even ask. Of course we would have. It's simply in our nature..."
"Damn! Okay, I'll continue chiselling away at it myself. No worries."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_3
text:
In a rare display of egotism, you find Freddy bragging to the rest of the crew about his prized decorated shield. A hush overtakes the room as Freddy spins a tale of his encounter with the dreaded Bishop Kyiiiapitet, the leader of the 3rd Royal Brigade during the Fed-Mantis War.
	
"Kyiiiapitet made it his quest to eradicate the Free Mantis by his very own two claws, and the time soon came when my clan was next on his list. Already he had taken the lives of more than half of my former companions from the war, and I wasn't going to be the next! And I wasn't!"

Freddy thumps the ground with his shield, a prideful look in his eye. "That day was the same day the Free Mantis abroad revered me as their leader. It was also the day the Hive forbade the import of tea from the Union. Spiteful bastards."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_4
text: Out of curiosity, you inquire what Freddy's original Mantis name was. "What? Why would you need to know that? My name is Freddy, plain and simple. It has been so long since I last spoke native Yetiiik I can barely even remember how to pronounce it. 'Tiifleeiiik', I think. Eugh."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_5
text: You ask Freddy why he acts so different from the other Free Mantis, and if there are more like him. "What, more that do not poison our brains with brain rot? Of course, there are thousands of us! It's just that... well, we're the 'smart ones'. I mean no ill will to my less situationally aware brethren, but they are perhaps not the best representation of our culture. The original Free Mantis were engineers, scientists, architects, the thinkers who knew the sins of the war and fled from the Hive. When the Federation did not accept us, we organized into nomadic clans and founded the Free Mantis. The educated among us remain aboard more organized colony ships and rarely get involved in intergalactic affairs, or work for the Union or the Federation. I hope that is a sufficient answer."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_6
text: You spot some of the crew struggling to fix some minor damage in one of the subsystems with a welding torch, but before you can assist, Freddy enters and offers to help. With great proficiency he wields the torch and seals the hole quickly and efficiently. When he spots you watching him, he merely explains: "While my dream of having opposable thumbs may never come true, I see no need to remain unskilled in that of handy work. It is not our biology that holds us back so much as it is our lack of a proper educational system."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_GENERIC_HAT
text: Freddy approaches, lugging behind him a wagon full of hats. You aren't sure where he got them from, but before you can inquire, he asks: "Captain! I was looking for a bit of fashion advice and was wondering what you thought about me changing my hat." Freddy gestures towards the pile.

event.text: "An excellent choice! I will try it on immediately!" Freddy tosses off his hat and places the Fedora on his head. "Thank you Captain! Now I'm looking stylish!"
"An excellent choice! I will try it on immediately!" Freddy tosses off his hat and places the Jester Hat on his head. "Thank you Captain! Now I'm looking stylish!"
"An excellent choice! I will try it on immediately!" Freddy tosses off his hat and places the Sombrero on his head. "Thank you Captain! Now I'm looking stylish!"
"An excellent choice! I will try it on immediately!" Freddy grabs a second tophat and places it on his head. "Thank you Captain! Now I'm looking stylish!"
"Alright, fair enough then Captain! I'll trust your word for it. I am quite fond of this hat... it's so dapper! Dapper is a word, right?"

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_KAZ_1
text:
While idly browsing the recreational room, Kaz bumps into Freddy, and the two glance at each other for an odd moment. Kaz bows and apologizes. Freddy accepts his apology but raises another question. "Might I ask, oh dreaded thief of legends, why it is you are always looking at me so strangely? You seem like a good fellow and I doubt you mean for me to take offense, but it is quite odd."
	
Kaz blinks, taken off-guard. "Oh, err. Well it's just that, well, thinking that Free Mantis are supposed to all be stupid, no? Drugs rotting braincells and all that. You not seeming stupid like rest though. You are not taking pheremones then, I assume?"
	
"Oh, uh. No, I don't. I played a pretty crucial role in the development of the synthetic pheromones concoction used by Suzerains and Bishops during the war, and I was able to recreate a more... 'experimental' recipe that the Free Mantis use. I never intended for it to be used in such masses, but that damage cannot be undone. Alas. But please, try not to call my people stupid. They're doing their best."

name: SOCIALIZE_FREDDY_KAZ_2
text:
You notice Freddy approaching Kaz on one of the cameras and tune into the audio feed out of curiosity. "Good morning, Mr. Plethkilik. I was wondering, if you don't mind me asking, why it is your translation files are still so broken? I've seen you speak beautiful Yetiiik and from what I understand you received a very comprehensive underground education."
	
Kaz shrugs. "Kaz is Mantis, pure and true. I may not always be greatest servant to Hive, but I cannot shaking inner nature as warrior. Because of this, other races fearing me. I get little practice speaking other language. Kaz also learning speak beautiful words from writing many love letter to beautiful Mantis woman. Kaz not finding much attraction to non-Mantis woman, so he not writing many love letter in other language either."
	
Freddy nods, although it's not the answer he expected. "Uhuh... alright. Well, if you ever bear the interest, I may be able to share with you some things I've learned. Mantis women, and warrior blood or not, I think you should find great benefit in communicating more fluently with other races." Kaz agrees, and the two shake claws and part ways.

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_NOTHING
text: "Kazaaakplethkilik does not wish to speak right now. He is busy concentrating! Yes, concentrating very hard. On what, you might ask? Concentrating. Kazaaakplethkilik must learn the art of concentrating! So stop bothering me. You are breaking my concentration!"

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_1
text: With Kaz busy eating in the cafeteria, you take a quick look around his room, wondering if there may be anything of concern he's smuggled onboard. In a small box in the corner of the room you find some... compromising pictures of the Mantis queen. You jump when you hear the door open and Kaz enter the room. "You looking at Kaz things? Oh, heheh. There are more of those if you are wanting look at them, Captain."

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_2
text: "Kaz sometimes gets flirtations from women outside of Mantis species. Now I not wanting to sound old here, but I am not quite understanding allure of interspecies relationships. Perhaps it is cultural thing? In Mantis life, love and need to reproduce are pretty much same thing. Kaz has burning passion for attractive woman, but Kaz cares more about making many Kaz junior in galaxy. What great honor it is, being child of LEGENDARY THIEF!"

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_3
text: Feeling there's no better person to ask, you inquire with Kaz whether the rumors are true Mantis women will attempt to behead their mates. "What? Where are you hearing such silly nonsense. Kaz never sleeps with crazies, no no, but even when he makes bad judgement it is never HEAD they try to cut off! Some try to take limbs as trophies as proof of having sleep with Kaz, but never head. You should stop reading whatever source it is you are getting such weird ideas from. I am not thinking it is good source."

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_4
text: While patrolling the ship you notice a red streak across the floor. Alarmed, you follow the trail into the kitchen, where you see Kaz busy sawing off the arm of some unidentified corpse on the counter. You're about to react, after a moment of temporary shock, when he reacts with glee to see you. "Captain, you are just in time! Kaz is preparing most wonderful dish for you and crew! Arm stew! Delicious, nutritious, everything growing boy or girl needing to be big and strong! Come, come, there is great feast on horizon!" Kaz digs into the corpse's skull and yanks out an eyeball and hands it to you.

choice.text: Accept the gift and join the feast.

event.text: Reluctantly, you gulp down the eyeball, shivering as you feel it rupture in your mouth. Kaz doesn't seem to understand your disgust but is delighted you've accepted his offering.

choice.text: Refuse the eye but allow the rest of the crew to decide if they'll join the feast.

event.text: You shake your head and give the eyeball back to Kaz, who frowns but shrugs. "Well, delicious eating is not for everything then. Kaz will still serve rest of crew if they are wanting! Waste not want not, that is what they are saying."

choice.text: Tell Kaz he cannot serve a corpse to the crew.

event.text: Kaz drops his posture for a moment and looks dumbfounded. "Oh... I was... I was just trying to make special meal for you and crew. I was not meaning to offend. Arm stew is such sought after treat in Hive. My apologies, Captain..." Kaz saunters away, drawing his corpse with him.

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_5
text: "Great Kazaaakplethkilik is needing new laugh! Very unsatisfied with current one. Is sounding more like Kikikik, when thinking it should be sounding like Kakakak! So if you are hearing sounds of deranged man trying to losing kidney stone, it is just me practicing."

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_6
text: "Perhaps this is worrying of thing to say, but Kaz is empathizing with the Admiral Wentworth for loss of babymaking organ. If Kaz was losing it, he maybe becoming genocidal maniac too! Er... that does not sounding as flattering as I first thought. Maybe not then. There are other ways to make Mantis woman happy in bed, I think. Maybe Wentworth is needing taught such skills."

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_GENERIC_7
text: Kaz approaches you meekly, one of the few times you've seen him not boasting his overconfidence. "Captain, I am wondering if you are able to answer one of Kazaaakplethkilik's many questions. His experience with Renegades are small, and it is vast culture he is wishing to learn more of. How might you defining the Renegade spirit?"

choice.text: We're guns for hire with no permanent allegiance.

event.text: "Ah, well there is something of nobleness in such a role, Kaz is thinking. A force of nature then, perhaps you are considering yourself? Or is Kaz too much stretching? Eh. Either way, Kaz can getting behind it."

choice.text: We're a force for good that makes money for our troubles.

event.text: "Force for good until you are being hired by bad guys? Or are you implying you have never taken contract from well paying client with bad intent? What if you are not knowing intent? So many implications I am thinking you are overlooking, but Kaz admires your resolve for good deeds."

choice.text: We're murderous, dangerous. I kill babies.

event.text: "Ah. Oh... First part, Kaz is thinking not too dissimilar from himself. Second part... I am recommending maybe you should not being so forthcoming with sharing. Just some legal advice, but I am not lawyer."

choice.text: I have dementia. What's a Renegade?

event.text: Kaz laughs, and keeps laughing, but slowly comes to a stop when you continue to stare blankly at him. "Errr... You are very... funny Captain. Heheh... uhm... I am hoping you are at least."

name: SOCIALIZE_KAZ_CLONEBAY_1
text: While idly checking on the crew you notice Kaz has dropped off of the crew manifest. Panicked, you check the cameras but fortunately he seems to already have cloned. You rush to the Clone Bay to ask him what happened but he's already gone. You follow him until you find him dragging a Mantis corpse back to his quarters.

choice.text: Did that Mantis board our ship?

event.text: Kaz pauses but shakes his head. "No no, this is corpse of me, Captain! Kaz wanting cadaver so he can find which parts of him are squishiest and most cuttable. Must remake armor to account for all weak-points so that Kaz may becoming invincible!" You caution Kaz against abusing the Clone Bay like that but he doesn't seem fazed. "It is most okay Captain, Kaz is not minding the pain or dark abyss. My solution to dreadful existiancial dillema is that Kaz is simply not care. Ship of Theseus can eating my feces."

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_KAZ_1
text:
Kazaaakplethkilik and Ariadne seem to be amusing themselves with some of the games in the rec room. They're playing an ancient analog game of two robot boxers that punch each other. 

	"Too slow, too slow!" Kaz says, but then in his exuberance accidentally makes a mistake "Ah, worthless controls...!"

	"This is it! Say your prayers, bug!" Ariadne says attempting to capitalize on Kaz's mistake. Although she has a better handle on the controls due to having actual digits, they're far too large for the tiny game. "Captain! I demand you retrofit this game to fit our hands!"

	"Yes, yes! Not finding out who the best fighter is this way!" Kaz says. You make your retreat before they make any other unreasonable demands.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_NOTHING
text: Tuco appears to have passed out on his bed, half covered by his sheets and snoring so loud from across the hallway you thought you were under attack. You try to get him to wake up but it's clear he's deep into a beer-coma. Seems you'll have to find someone else to talk to.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_1
text: You notice an assortment of musical instruments strewn around Tuco's room, various oddities he's brought along. You ask Tuco if he knows how to play all of them and he nods. "Most, at least. There's a couple I'm learning. Music is a big part of the culture of us Outcasts, along with storytelling. It's something the Theocracy has tried to oppress. Church music is an affront to music, let me tell you. I'd rather listen to a Hektar jingle on loop for the rest of my life than endure another second of a Chrysolic hymn."

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_2
text: While in the middle of a game of 'Boarden', Tuco laments to you about the Theocracy's ban on gambling. "The Elders tired of people 'wasting' their money in casino districts instead of using it as donations to the Church." Tuco slams his fist down angrily on the breakroom table, sloshing some of his beer onto his playing cards. "I'll be damned if I give one bloody cent to those robed, preachy megalomaniacs. Say what you want about a gambling hobby, but at least it's a good time."

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_3
text: For as long as Tuco's been on your ship you haven't been able to ignore a large belt he wears across his plated shoulder. A series of teeth or other sorts of similar organs from all sorts of species, primarily Rockmen, are stitched into the belt's fabric. Eventually, you work up the courage to ask Tuco about it. "Oh, this? This is my friendship belt! In it I have stitched a piece of memorabilia of all the friends I have met in my travels. Look, this one here is from Admiral Ariadne!" Tuco points excitedly at various teeth and lists off an impressive list of names. "Would you like to contribute to it, Captain?"

choice.text: Give Tuco one of your teeth.

event.text: Awkwardly, you do your best to pry one of your less useful teeth from your mouth, and eventually resort to using the classic string and door trick. Painful as it is, Tuco is immensely grateful and immediately leaves to begin working on stitching in your tooth.
Weirded out by the offer, you do your best to politely decline. Tuco is clearly disappointed but doesn't seem to be too offended.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_4
text: You hear a knock on the door to the cockpit and open it to find Tuco, who asks to enter. "Hello... Captain..." Tuco runs his hands down his face, struggling to get his words out under a drunken stupor. "Can... I... uhm... the database? Fed. Database. See it... can I? Please?"

choice.text: Give him access to the database.

event.name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_4_ACCEPT
event.text: Tuco nods excessively and mumbles what you think is him saying thanks. He awkwardly sits himself in the chair next to you and pulls up the database with your help, and scrolls down to the T-section. He pulls up various articles regarding himself and scans the information. "I can't... ugh... my head hurts. I can't... this... reading. I will... AGH-" Tuco grabs his head. "Headache. I will read this... later. Goodnight." Tuco gets up and stumbles his way out the door and back to his quarters.

event.name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_4_REFUSE
event.text: "Blagh... what a load of... crap..." Tuco fumbles to imitate throttling himself, or perhaps you, then turns and stumbles out the door. You ignore his aggression and hope it'll go away once the hangover has passed.

choice.text: Ask him why he needs it.

event.text: "I want... AGH-" Tuco stumbles over, slamming against the wall. "Stupid... migraines..." Tuco rubs at his cranium, trying to restore his train of thought. "I want... to read what they've written about... me...?" You notice the uncertainty at the end of his statement.

choice.text: Give him access to the database.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GENERIC_5
text: You find Tuco drunk sitting in some odd corner of the ship, curled up in an awkward position with the broken cover to what you think was a ventilation shaft. As you approach, he begins to shout random things at you but none of them make it through the translator. You decide now isn't the best time to talk and leave.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_NIGHTS_1
text: You stroll up to Nights, who is as always holding a drink in his hand, but smiling wider than normal. In his own words, he claims to have become much more "bearable" since he got a drinking buddy. You wonder who he's referring to until Tuco walks into the room, also holding a bottle, and toasts to Nights.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_NIGHTS_2
text: Having noticed that both Tuco and Nights have been missing for hours, you go looking for them. Eventually you find both of them passed out in the cargo bay, surrounded by empty beer bottles, and both of them partly undressed. You know you won't be able to wake either of them up any time soon, and set a reminder to check back in an hour.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_NIGHTS_3
text: While doing your regular patrol of the ship, you hear two bottles clink and turn to see Tuco and Nights sitting closely together in a closet. Tuco shouts to you, "Captain! Would you like to join us?", clearly not too enthusiastic about it but trying to be polite. Nights scowls but doesn't take back the offer.

event.text: You shrug and take a seat across from the two. Tuco pours you a shot and you all toast together and take a drink. The three of you make idle, rather awkward conversation until you eventually decide you've had enough and leave.
You decline the offer and briefly consider admnonishing them. Instead you decide to let them be and caution them not to drink too much.

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_ARIADNE_1
text: Several of the crew are sitting together in the kitchen eating when Ariadne walks in. As soon as she enters, Tuco bows and slides a chair out for her. "My princess, please, would you have a seat?" He snickers and Ariadne scowls. "You call me a princess again and I'll pop your damn head off. We've known each other for years and you know damn well I ain't royalty." You expect some kind of standoff, but instead she smiles and sits down. "I will, however, kindly accept the seat."

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_ARIADNE_2
text: Ariadne appears to be assembling some sort of explosive device in her room, while Tuco stands by holding a toolkit. You warn Ariadne against doing such dangerous things in the crew quarters, but she dismisses you. "The last time you told me that, you said I needed 'supervision' in case something went wrong.
