Now I have supervision." She points to Tuco who waves with his free hand. "If something goes wrong, it's my room that'll be blown up anyways. Assuming I survive the blast, I can sleep on the floor if it comes to that."

name: SOCIALIZE_TUCO_GUNTPUT_1
text:
Whilst in the middle of recovering from a hangover, Tuco has planted himself in a booth in the ship's kitchen with the lights turned off. You notice a large pot with some liquid brewing and moments later Guntput barges in, carrying several weird herbs. He dumps them into the pot and stirs it. "GOD DAMN IT YOU BLOODY LIZARD, KEEP IT DOWN! I HAVE A HEADACHE!" Guntput says nothing, instead pooring some of the liquid into a bowl and dashing over to the irate Rockman. "You. Drink Guntput's liquid. Now."
	
Tuco pushes him aside. "I don't want your damn liquid, I have a hangover. Go away!" However, Guntput insists. "No. Drink." He scrambles onto the table and begins to force the liquid down Tuco's throat. You think things are about to get violent, but Tuco gives up and downs the bowl. "Good. This will help headache. You will thank Guntput later. You must stop drinking so much." Guntput leaps off the table and scurries away before Tuco can respond.

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_NOTHING
text: Ariadne is tinkering with some explosives on her workbench, and ignores you as you enter the room. You try to speak to her but are cut off: "Go away. If you distract me I might blow us all to hell. Go bother someone else right now."

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_GENERIC_1
text: "Statistically speaking, in the Multiverse there must be at least one reality in which the Elders have already been defeated. In fact, if I understand the science behind it, I believe there would in fact be infinite. Some people in my homeland would find it wise to tell me I should be satisfied with this. But that is utter nonsense. Just because a million, or a billion, or a trillion, or a blaze knows how many people have a better life doesn't mean I can't aspire to make the lives better for the people I know!" Despite the resoluteness of this statement, you feel an air of open-endedness to Ariadne's statement, as if she's expecting your opinion as well.

event.text: Ariadne seems content with your response. "Good. We are on the same page. As we should be, considering the aim of your mission. Let us both just hope we can make a change after all." Ariadne gets up, nods to you, and walks away.

"What? So you mean to suggest then I should just sit idly and allow millions of my fellow Rockmen and women to suffer at the hands of tyrants? Your logic is nonsense and it is clear to me you speak from instinct rather than intellect. Your very mission in which I have promised to help consists of taking direct action to better the lives of many despite the infinite multitudes of the Multiverse." Ariadne grumbles and walks away, although noticeably lacking a bit of her usual arrogant confidence.
You say nothing and instead nod along passively. Ariadne grumbles and walks away lacking a bit of her usual arrogant confidence.

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_GENERIC_2
text: Ariadne spots you in the recreation room watching some of the other crew and takes a seat next to you. Weary she's trying to test you once again, you make sure to give her extra attention. "There is a school of thought popular within the Theocracy that suggests the... 'breeding class' - that being, women, ought not to wear the same rights as the men. That in fact, despite our near identical anatomies, we are different enough to warrant such exclusion." Ariadne pauses to allow you to process this information. "I would recommend, Captain, if you have ever found yourself sharing these kinds of thoughts, that you discard them. And if you meet those who refuse to discard them their own, then I advise a swift exit of whichever room it is in which you had the displeasure of meeting them."

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_GENERIC_3
text: You find Ariadne tinkering with the Weapons system. "Of the interiors of every ship I have yet seen, I have never seen one that contains so many randomly scattered missiles in my life. Why do you pile them haphazardly like you have? I am going to build you a shelf. And you will keep your missiles on the damn shelf. And if you don't, I will build you a fixture for your chair which will slap your face upon each hour of every cycle for the rest of our duration aboard this vessel."

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_GENERIC_4
text: "The last person who called me princess, I smashed their head open with my fist." Ariadne scowls at you, despite you not having done anything.

event.text: "No. And that is why your head is not mush between my hands." She smiles, although you can't help but feel intimidated anyways. Although no extra words are spoken, it is clear the unspoken sentence is "Don't you dare ever call me princess or you'll be next."

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_GENERIC_5
text: "I was mortified to find that some people find it apt to compare my Lost Suns to that of the Free Mantis and Duskbringers. To the first, I am not so much offended as confused. I cannot say I share a great affinity for the drug-obsessed Mantis, but I do not spite them either. But the Dusks? How is a democratic, justice driven revolution by the oppressed masses at all comparable to a fascist uprising by the bourgeoisie? When I find who started this, I will cause them great suffering. Perhaps I will strand them in a Dusk sector, so that they may experience first hand the difference. Hmph."

name: SOCIALIZE_ARIADNE_GENERIC_6
text: "It is shameful that even now, so far into the future, we still suffer from the plights of sexism and homophobia. At least, in the Theocracy as it is. In other places it is perhaps different, but it seems to be the inclination of the religious masses that any group with less than a persistent drive to produce a shapeless army of new zealots must be oppressed and brainwashed. Anything less than a total, liberal institution must be abolished to achieve universal liberty. If I am still alive when the Lost Suns have acheived their victory, then I forsee myself to be one to carry this fate out." Ariadne's gaze shifts to you. "When the time comes, if it does come at all, then I advise you do not stand in my way. There is a great fire on the horizon, and nothing will be able to put it out once the match has been lit."

name: SOCIALIZE_VORTIGON_NOTHING
text: Vortigon is kneeled over before the ship toilet, hands clasped to his chest and making a strange sound. At first you consider he might have food poisoning, but you quickly realize he's praying. Knowing better than to disturb the Grand Priest in a moment of prayer, you'll have to talk to someone else.

name: SOCIALIZE_VORTIGON_GENERIC_1
text: "Your Federation ships are boring! Where is the flair? The colors? If you wish to be feared, you will need a better color scheme than paste with faded orange!" Vortigon crosses his arms, disappointed.

choice.text: Hey, I didn't make the colors!

event.text: Vortigon keeps his arms crossed, but doesn't seem to have anything more to add. Seems you've put him at a loss for words.
"At least you can admit it! I look on with disgust at all these ships, and I see nothing that appeases me. This whole galaxy needs to be taught how to pick a color palette."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_NOTHING
text: You spot Rig talking to himself, and for a moment consider asking him if he's okay when you hear a rumbling sound from his stomach. You quickly realize he's having a conversation with Tintan and decide not to intrude. It's rare to see the pair getting along, so you'll have to find someone else to talk to.

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_GENERIC_1
text: You hear a deep rumbling from Rig's stomach and ask if Tintan is doing okay. "Is Tan doing okay? She's stuck in my stomach, of course she isn't okay! Hmph." With a sneer, he comments further, "Just be glad you can't hear her like I can. The stream of insults and cursing is ceaseless. Even when I'm trying to sleep she keeps shouting at me. Some real wonderful 'symbiosis' we have going on, indeed."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_GENERIC_2
text:
"Rig and Tintan does sort of roll off the tongue, doesn't it? When everything's gone wrong, at least you have the little things to look to sometimes, you know?" Rig pauses as he gets feedback from Tintan on his little discovery.
	
"Well excuuuuse me for trying to have a bit of happiness in my life. You miserable little wench, I bet you were just as insufferable before this! At least people don't have to hear you whine now!" Another pause.

"BY THE CRYSTAL SPIRIT, YOU DID NOT JUST SAY THAT! YOU BITCH! I HOPE YOUR CHASSIS DISSOLVES IN STOMACH ACID!"

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_GENERIC_3
text:
Rig seems a bit perturbed. Well, more perturbed than usual. "You know, before this happened I used to go to church quite often. Chrysolity was a staple of my life. It made me a bit of an outsider in Zulfiqar, since most of those executive guys weren't too tied to their faith. Of course, everyone had to SAY they went to church, or else the Elders would have taken us down quick as lightning. But me? I was a faithful believer. But this? This makes me question if there is really any sort of benevolent entity out there. And if there is, why this? Why me?"
	
There's a pause as Tintan seems to be talking. "Oh great, thanks for the input Tan. I really just was dying to know that you thought I was a dumb shithead idiot because I went to church. Like no Zoltan ever has been religious. Not like you have a whole damn government-subsidized nebula full of monks or anything! The Ministry is practically a theocracy as well! Why do you think our species get along so well?" There's total and uncomfortable silence, as Tintan seems unable to retaliate.

"Yeah, shut you up did I?" Another rumble. "Oh go to hell."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_GENERIC_4
text: Despite the two never seeming to get along, you notice Rig still refers to Tintan as just 'Tan', almost affectionately. You could ask them about it, but it might set them off on another argument.

choice.text: Why do you call her Tan?

event.text: "You mean why the nickname? Oh, I dunno. Hard not to get at least a little attached to the woman living inside your stomach, even if she's an unbearable wench sometimes." He smiles. "She reminds me of most Rockmen I know. A stubborn asshole who can say the most offensive, insensitive things and yet still somehow be likable." He listens to the rumbling in his stomach. "Oh don't go soft on me now Tan. It just doesn't feel like you unless you end your sentence by calling me some new variation of a slur."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_GENERIC_5
text: Out of nowhere, Rig suddenly starts to scream. "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAH! OH MY GOD! AAAAAAAAAAH!"

event.text: "I just remembered how messed up this all is! Oh my god, this is horrifying! This is abhorrent! How the hell did we get here? I have a living person in my stomach and I'm just carrying on as if everything is NORMAL! THIS IS NOT NORMAL!" Rig falls to the ground and begins to sob. His stomach is silent, and if you had to guess Tintan is going through something similar. It is incredibly messed up, but hopefully as soon as the mission is over you can get them the medical attention necessary.

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_BILLY_1
text:
One day, almost out of nowhere, Rig storms into the lounge where Billy is relaxing and hoists him up off the ground. "YOU DID THIS DIDN'T YOU?! YOU'RE RESPONSIBLE FOR RUINING MY LIFE! I JUST KNOW IT, YOU SLUG PIECE OF SHIT!"
	
Billy, although startled, isn't about to let this go without a fight. "HAH! Oh god I wisssh it wasss! Sssservess you right, Rockman! You know Hektar sssellsss the sssuperior productsss, but becaussse you have all that rich church money to pump up your marketing, you jussst got better exposssure! Of courssse you'd try and pin thisss on me! You think I'm the kind of assshole who'd ssstick two people into a body blender? Come on, I have more ssstyle than that! I might be cold but I'm not cruel! If my credit with Vael wasss any better I'd just have had you killed, ssssimple and painlesss."

Rig tosses Billy down in a heap, still seething but trying to calm down. "Right, forgot you were too busy trying to pay off your crippling debt to a serial murderer. Pffft, but really? Hektar selling better products? Hah! You wish! Zulfiqar sells reliable, affordable, and standardized equipment for ships of all kinds. Your modular shit is a short lived novelty for crack addicts and pirates! That hideous, eye-wrenching blue and yellow color scheme makes me want to puke! You keep telling yourself it was Zulfiqar that put you out of business if it's what lets you sleep at night - but deep down, you know it's just because your company isn't worth the crate of slime you evolved out of."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_TONY_1
text:
Tony and Rig are sitting across from each other, in the middle of a conversation. "Rig... how did you ever recover from the 'incident?'"
	"Recover? I wouldn't exactly say I 'recovered.'"
	"I mean, you seem fine enough. Functional-"
	"FUNCTIONAL? Tony, I have a ZOLTAN LIVING IN MY STOMACH! I am not okay in the slightest, every waking moment of my existence is pure misery and I don't even know why I haven't ended it yet!"
	"Well uhm... besides that, I mean. How did you cope after we parted ways?"
	"I DIDN'T. I didn't cope at all! I could barely hold my job, I was depressed all the time, I had to go to therapy daily. 7 years isn't enough time to get over that kind of thing. A whole damn lifetime isn't enough! And that goes double when IT NEVER GETS ANY BETTER!"
	Tony seems to take this in. "So... you're saying that me being like this isn't my fault? That this is normal?"
	Rig shrugs. "Normal? Probably not. Your fault? Hell if I know. But you're not alone in this. If we walked away from that even remotely normal it'd have been a miracle. We're both still alive, we're rich as all hell... it could be worse."
	
	The conversation continues, changing topic to other more trivial things like soap operas. You decide to stop listening and go back about your duties.

name: SOCIALIZE_SYMBIOTE_TONY_2
text:
Rig approaches Tony suddenly, proposing a new idea. "I want to buy a ship, when this is all over."

Tony is very confused. "A ship? Okay...?"

"Yes, a ship. For the three of us. Hopefully when Tan and I are separated. We can call it something stupid, like 'The Unholy Mistake'. We'll fly it around, and go kill some Slugs probably."

Tony seems pleased with this idea. "A Slug hunting gig doesn't sound too bad. But... let's not get genocidal here. We just kill the BAD Slugs, okay?"

Rig nods. "Okay, deal. The bad Slugs. And maybe when it's all over, we can go launch the ship into a moon with one of those Leech railguns as a standing testament of our burning hatred of this existence."

"Crash it with US on it?" Tony seems deeply frightened and disgusted by the idea.

"Uhm... well it wasn't what I was thinking, but maybe. Hopefully, by then, we'll hate living at least a little bit less. To be honest, I kind of just want to name a ship 'Unholy Mistake'. We're rich enough to crash a couple dozen of them anyways."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_NOTHING
text: As you approach Ruwen in the hallway, he seems startled and turns to face you but relaxes when he realizes you're the Captain. "By the crypt, you scared me! Sorry, I'm trying to get some sleep right now. Ever since I woke from stasis I've had a dreadful case of insomnia, and to remedy it I try to wander the halls. I got the advice from a friend I met on a diplomatic mission, actually! You aliens and your... creative solutions. I do hope to try and get some shut-eye before the mission carries on though, so if possible I'd appreciate it if you left me alone for a while."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_GENERIC_1
text: "CARTYK!" Ruwen bangs a fist down on the table in front of him and clutches his arm in pain. He looks back up to you, embarrassed. "Apologies for the foreign expletive... it's just these stiff joints, Captain! It's no secret cryosleep doesn't exactly... do wonders for the body. I forgot to do my stretches this morning and I am terribly regretting it! I think you'll get used to the random shouting in time, and again I do genuinely apologize! Just be glad your translator hopefully doesn't know what any of it means."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_GENERIC_2
text: You notice Ruwen's room is decorated by a number of odd trinkets from seemingly all over the galaxy. You won't have time to ask about all of them, but if you wanted to, you could probably get at least one story out of Ruwen.

choice.text: What's the black and red armor?

event.text: "This? Oh, this was a gift from Kataaagingi, the owner of Tiiikaka. It was part of one of my... less successful, but more interesting diplomatic excursions. I was on a personal quest to convince the pirate lord to end the slave trade in Imperial space. The agreement DID happen, thankfully, but it didn't stop the enslavement of Crystals entirely. Unfortunately, the Theocracy is known to employ Tiiikaka quite often, and it has become common practice for Crystal slaves to serve on Inquisition vessels. Any Crystal not in Imperial space is still vulnerable, but at least Imperial space itself is safe. Mostly... and only from slavers... Mmm..." Ruwen scratches his chin uncomfortably. "The armor is cool though! It's made for a Mantis so I can't exactly wear it, and they pulled it off of a dead guy... but... well it looks cool on a shelf?"

"Now that, that is a fine piece of weaponry. Foreigners make such fascinating guns sometimes - I wish we Crystals had such craftmanship." Ruwen runs his large golden hand over the gun. "It was a gift from chairman Irwin in the EHG, as part of an agreement I made near the beginning of my career as ambassador! Some Clansmen had begun hunting my kind, as you would expect of course, and it was my task to put an end to it. Irwin was surprisingly diplomatic, though I hear he isn't chairman anymore. Unfortunate. I learned much of Slug culture from him!"

"Oh crypt, Irwin, yes! I forgot you were on this ship! My dearest apologies! However did you get the boot anyways? That... is the expression, yes?"
					
Irwin moans. "Ssssome basssstard betrayed me and threw me in the gutter! But let'sss not linger on it. It'sss been yearsss, and it'sss a ssssore sssubject ssstill." Ruwen nods. "Oh of course, of course! I didn't mean to upset you! Well, I'm glad you're still alive at least! You must teach me more about your kind at some point. I am truly so curious."

choice.text: What's the vaguely humanoid ball of trash?

event.text: "That? That's uhm... a bunch of trash that some Free Mantis bunched together into a shape that I think is meant to vaguely resemble myself. It wasn't part of a diplomatic mission, they just followed me around until I'd accept it. Oh, such strange creatures. I don't mean to sound rude but I am quite glad they seem to be the outliers. Oh, if we had reentered the galaxy only to find you were ALL of such... stup...er, creativity... I don't know what we'd do!"

choice.text: You still have the sculpture in your room though.

event.text: "Well, yes. It's quite endearing, no? Strange or not, I can't hate the creatures. They meant well, and fortunately the sculpture doesn't smell."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_GENERIC_3
text: "Captain, might I ask what species you like the least? I'm intending to collect data from all sorts of sources and compile a list to understand the effects of certain bias on how people interpret species!"

choice.text: I don't feel comfortable with this.

event.text: "What? Why not? Oh, is this another taboo in your culture? My apologies, it is not uncommon for my kind to talk about species in such manners. I will refrain from asking you such questions in the future."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_GENERIC_4
text: Ruwen notices a splotch of blue showing through his yellow skin paint. "Oh by Ycathine's crypt, I'm terribly sorry! This is so embarrassing, I should go cover this up immediately!"

event.text: "Oh, right, this problem seems so strange to you. You see, some cultures find nudity to be taboo. In a similar vein, high ranking Imperial officials are forbidden from showing their bare skin in public. An ambassador, one of the most honorable positions, must always be coated in yellow. Even if you do not mind, I refuse to break such important tradition. I will go cover myself, goodbye Captain."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_GENERIC_5
text: Ruwen laughs to himself, reminiscing on some inside-joke he's practically bursting at the seams to tell you. "Ironically, Captain, this is the second time I've been recruited aboard a mercenary's vessel to travel to Node 17 and destroy a Rebel flagship! One time is crazy enough, but twice?! By the crypt, they'll never believe me when I tell the stories back home!"

event.text: "Who? Oh, the crew of the original Kestrel? Well... in some ways they remind me a lot of you Captain! Determined, creative with their morals... possibly insane with occasional symptoms of psychopathy. But both of your hearts are in the right place! I hope so at least."

choice.text: Never call me a mercenary again.

event.text: "Oh dear, did I offend you? God, I am so clueless with these things... I am so so sorry, Captain! I shan't ever make the mistake again. Though, it is worth mentioning... the Syndicate wasn't a thing back then. Mercenaries were, in essence, the same thing Renegades are now. The Kestrel's Captain could even be considered the first Renegade, if you want to think about it that way!"
Ruwen sees you nodding and begins to nod himself, mimmicking your movements with a cautious uncertainty. Eventually, he shuffles away, unsatisfied with his own inability to prolong your interest.

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_TURZIL_1
text:
Turzil wanders over to Ruwen, who is applying a new coat of his yellow paint. "Observation: you have a stunning shade of yellow. That is my: favorite -shade- of yellow. Request: may I borrow some [paint]?"

Ruwen scoots a bucket of paint over to Turzil carefully, warning him to be careful because it's a very special and expensive kind of paint. Turzil thanks him awkwardly and continues to stand there. "Er... I'm sorry strange robot thing, but I know very little about your culture. If you're attempting to flirt with me, I'm afraid my heart already goes out to another woman! I hope you don't take offense..."

Ruwen blinks but Turzil isn't responding. "Are... you okay?" He gets up and shakes Turzil a little, still without a response. Ruwen looks to you for help. "Captain, it seems the Engi shut himself down. I have no idea how these things work, but I fear this may require the attention of a medical professional or a technician, of which I am regrettably neither."

name: SOCIALIZE_RUWEN_DIANESH_1
text:
Dianesh approaches Ruwen, carrying a stack of letters which she lays in front of him. "Ruwen, why have you been sending me so many unsigned letters? You do realize we're both on the same ship...?"

"Uh... uhm... I don't know what you mean, Empress! If someone is sending you mysterious letters, it could be anyone!"

"Ruwen, you've been using the Imperial stamp on all of them. There's literally only two people on this ship who own that stamp, and that's us."

"Oh... oh. Uhm. Did you read the letters?"

"No, not yet. I have no idea what they're about, but I'm just confused why you're sending them."

"DON'T READ THEM!" Ruwen scoops up all of the letters and rushes to the airlock, where he dumps them all out into space. "Oh crypt, that was a close one... phew..."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_NOTHING
text: Dianesh bows as you approach, and you bow in return on instinct. You expect her to say more, but when no response comes, you awkwardly wave hello. "Do you have no question in mind for me?" She sighs. "I'm afraid I'm not one for unprompted small talk. As Empress it's my duty to maintain my regal posture, but rarely is it my duty to chat. With such limited conversation topics on both of our minds, why don't you speak with someone else today?"

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_GENERIC_1
text: "There are few terrors that can keep me up at night more than the pitiful fact that my species' history has been lost not only once but TWICE! Again and again we are struck with tragedy, a genocide of legacy." Dianesh says all of this, but doesn't elaborate on either incident.

event.text: "The first happened eons ago. Exactly when, I couldn't tell you, since that history is lost. It involves the great emperor Ycathine, who ruled during what is believed to be the darkest period of our history. At the end of a terrible civil war, which left the species divided across the galaxy, he swore to seal himself away with all remains of that war forever. This tale has since been mythologized as the tale of Ycathine's Crypt, and most don't even seem to believe it's real." Dianesh waits a few moments, then smiles smugly. "However, as Empress, I'm privy to a bit more information than the common man. While I don't know for ceerrrrrtain that it's real... I have no reason to suspect it isn't, either. Now, enough chatter. If I speak too long about the past, I'll forget the present even exists."

"You already know the second. When we were forced to leave our homeworlds by the savage invasion of pioneers, we left behind countless relics and landmarks that simply couldn't be taken with us. I can only imagine what travesties have defaced them now." Dianesh sighs. "Some day, we will return and take back those lands. Even if we don't remain in seclusion, there is much heritage that we must recover unless we are simply to forget the last century entirely. Now, enough chatter. If I speak too long about the past, I'll forget the present even exists."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_GENERIC_2
text: You spot Dianesh taking some strange powder from a vial. She coughs a few times and shivers once she has it down, then notices you watching her. "Don't you have better places to be than spying on me?"

event.text: "What is what stuff?" Dianesh scowls and stashes the vial in her pocket.

choice.text: That vial of powder you just took.

event.text: "Hmph. So I was not as careful at hiding it as I thought. I didn't expect nosy captains to be sticking their face in my 'private' quarters. Fine. It's Riapel. The stimulant we Crystals use to accelerate geode growth. The health impact on Crystal biology is minimal, but it has somewhat of an addictive effect. If you don't use it for too long after a steady dose of it, like all drugs, you experience withdrawals." Dianesh says nothing else about it, as if the rest is obvious. You can tell she doesn't like talking about it.

choice.text: But why are you taking it right now?

event.text: Dianesh's scowl grows even more spiteful. "Because I am experiencing withdrawals. Are you always so clueless? Because if I'm going to have to spell everything out for you, then this is going to get real tiring real fast." You mumble an apology and leave before things get more tense.

"A-Am I a drug addict?! Wow, what tact you have. I hope you're as frank to all your friends, because you must truly be their favorite person to hang out with." Dianesh folds her arms. "I don't know, AM I a drug addict? I take the same stimulant every other damn Crystal does, just a bit more of it. Since you just love asking questions you have no right to ask, why don't you ask me everything else about my life, huh? Am I a virgin? What's my favorite fetish? Do I hide dead bodies in my closet?"

Dianesh walks up to you, grabs you by the neck, and flings you out of her room. "Get the hell out of my room, and STAY out of it. Or else next time I'll teach you what it feels like to have a piece of rock lodged in your forehead."

Dianesh walks up to you, grabs you by the neck, and flings you out of her room. "Get the hell out of my room, and STAY out of it. Or else next time I'll teach you what it feels like to have a piece of rock lodged in your forehead."

choice.text: Are there dead bodies in your closet?

event.text: Dianesh walks up to you, grabs you by the neck, and flings you out of her room. "Get the hell out of my room, and STAY out of it. Or else next time I'll teach you what it feels like to have a piece of rock lodged in your forehead."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_GENERIC_3
text: "The life of a Crystalline Empress is a hard one. I had to undergo vigorous, constant training not only from my mother on all the obscure etiquettes I would need but also my father. You see, a Crystalline Empress is also functionally a warrior queen. I am the head of state and chief military commander, and so I am expected to be a competent warrior myself." Dianesh doesn't seem to find this memory pleasant, but keeps going anyways. "I am the first female head of state in the Empire for nearly 13 centuries. Most didn't expect highly of me. I've always had the extra burden on my back of having to prove to everyone I'm worth remembering in history for more than just the novelty of being female. I am not just an 'Empress'. I want to be a part of history, forever. I want to be remembered for MY accomplishments, and not just the circumstances of my birth."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_GENERIC_4
text: "My people have never been too particularly attached to their faith. There has always been religion, but it is a footnote of our history. Never did I feel too strongly about it until I witnessed just what the Theocracy used it for. Having known what it feels like to be revered as a goddess, I now know for certain there can be no god. No higher being with any dignity would allow their image to be disgraced by the sorts of egregious means of worship and oppression committed in their name. If I had the power to strike the Elders down like they so claim, then I would have done so ten times over. No person should ever be forced to endure such machiavellian psychological shackles."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_GENERIC_5
text: Out of curiosity, you ask Dianesh just how the Elders managed to erase all memory of Crystals from the galaxy. "Hmph. I was wondering when you might ask. It is a common misconception among foreigners that the Rockmen and Crystals lived closely together throughout all of the Rock-Crystal Empire. Our two civilizations were spread apart by the length of several systems, and we Crystals have always been isolationists. The Elders didn't have to try hard to chase us away, because we were barely here to begin with. Most galactic civilizations were still fledgling and had barely interacted with us at the time. Most probably assumed we were just a mutation, or they had imagined us, if they even knew we existed at all."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_ARIADNE_1
text:
"So, I take it you are Empress Dianesh then." Ariadne takes a seat across from Dianesh, and the two women stare at each other a bit uncomfortably.

"Yes, I am her, and she is me. You are... the Lost Sun Admiral. I apologize if I forgot your name."

"Ariadne." Ariadne announces her name with a piercing effect, making sure Dianesh never forgets it. The air between them is tense, although not necessarily hostile.

"So, have you come here to tell me I am another corrupt, evil autocrat who's rule must be expunged from the face of existence like the Elders? If that is your intent, then I advise you just cut to the chase and say it."

Ariadne shakes her head. "On the contrary. I came to say I have a lot of respect for you, girl, both personally and in your leadership. I'm a revolutionary, but I'm not a radical. I know you were born into this, you didn't seize this power yourself. From what I can tell you seem to be doing a good job. I know you have your people's wellbeing in your heart and mind at all times, and that's ultimately what matters most in a leader."
	
Dianesh nods, although a bit confused. "Uhuh... Well I am pleasantly surprised to hear that then. Your men haven't been the most... polite to mine, with all that feuding between the Suns and the SSLG. But really, I assure you, my intent is not just to extend my power. If you want a Rock democracy, by all means you can have it. We are two distinct species now, and I have no delusions about it. But I do think there are many benefits to a renewed sistership between us. One where we are equals, and not the basis of a religion."

"Good. I'm not a fan of imperialism, but I'm sure we can make something work. But if you double cross me, I will-" Dianesh cuts her off. "You will what, crush my head with your own bare hands? No need to finish that sentence, because I was only going to tell you the same." The two women smile at this mutual understanding and shake hands.

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_SLOCKNOG_1
text:
"Hello dear Empressss! Tisss a good day for monarchy, to have two sssuch prominent and powerful leadersss united on thisss vesssel!" Slocknog nods to Dianesh and pulls his special lighter out from his pocket and lights a cigarette, then offers one to the empress. Dianesh considers the roll for a few moments before turning it down reluctantly.

"I... appreciate the sentiment, yellow Slug."

Slocknog stops her. "Sssslocknog." He extends his tentacle, which Dianesh shakes without much force.

"Right, Slocknog. As I was saying. I appreciate the sentiment, but... well I'm quite confused. The Kleptocracy does not have monarchs. You talk so much about bloodlines and legacy... but Slugs don't have that anymore. I vaguely remember the ancient days of the Clairvoyant Empire, but that empire vanished by the time my kind reemerged into the galaxy."
	
Slocknog is speechless. "Uhm... well... uh... It'sss a bit of an unconventional approach to monarchy, yessss. But we have to make due sssometimesss with what the left handssss usss sssometimesss, yesss?"

"The... left? I don't understand what you mean."

"Yessss, the left. You know, the liberal essstablissshment. Any good leader knowssss compromissse isss necessssary, but ssssometimesss thessse liberalssss really get on my nervesss. They're trying to change too much at once, too much reform will dessstabilize the nation! It'ssss clear if you follow hissstory, the passst wasss alwaysss better."

"I... what are you talking about? It sounds like if people are trying to constantly reform the Kleptocracy, you clearly have issues that need reform. If so many people want change for the better, why not give it to them? I don't know much about Kleptocracy politics, but I do know there seems to be a lot of turmoil over there right now."
	
"Nevermind. Sssshould have known better not to get into politicssss again. Pfft, a leftisssst monarch? Never thought I'd ssssee the day..."

name: SOCIALIZE_DIANESH_MISSILE_1
text: You find Dianesh in the cargo bay, staring at one of the missile launchers that's currently under calibration. It takes a few moments before you realize it's the Dianesh Missiles. "It disgusts me to see my name used in such a way."

choice.text: Having a weapon named after you?

event.text: "What? No. That, I couldn't mind in the slightest. I mean being an entity of such high worship. I don't want to be a goddess. 			Nights chuckles, lost in some deep irony only he understands. "Mr. Invincible thought it'd be fun. Thought politicssss would be asss much an adventure as being a pirate. And who could blame him? The god damn 'election' cycle involvessss a bunch of moronssss racing to sssteal sssome sssstupid ssshitty crown. It'sss a mockery, but it'sss a sssacred tradition. text:

	As you walk closer, Sylvan addresses you without even looking up. "A sssstrange game, thisss issss. Carle Hektar, founder of... well, Hektar Indusssstriesss, obvioussssly, brought thisss game back with him from hissss tripsss to the Union. It'sss an exercise in total market domination. Monopoly."
	
	Sylvan takes out one of the player pieces and puts it on a colorful square on the gameboard. "It's rather sssimple. You take your piece and move it down the board with each dice roll. You use your money to buy property on the ssspace you land on, and if another player landsss on your property you charge them rent!"

event.text: "Oh yesss, very! It'sss a race to win it all, sssstranger! But run out of money, and you're bankrupt! All out of luck, but you sssstill gotta ssssit and watch assss everyone elssse getsss to play! But, my favorite part of the game issss what happensss after that!"

Sylvan suddenly leaps up, grabbing his blaster, and fires 7 rounds right at the game board. "You annihilate everything! Thosssse rat basssstardssss with their bourgeoissss bullsssshit and their fancy ssssuitssss, their ssssmug grinsss as they rob you blind and then force you to sit and watch in bleak missssery! OFF WITH THEIR HEADSSSS, I SSSAY! YOU WITH ME, SSSSTRANGER? DEATH TO THE MARKETSSS! DEATH TO THE ELITE! WE'LL MAKE THE CORPORATE FLOORSSS RUN READ WITH THEIR BLOOD ASSSSS OUR REVOLUTION BURNSSSS THE SSSSTATUSSSS QUO AT THE SSSTAKE!"

choice.text: Yeah! I'm all for a revolution!

event.text: "Oh I wasssn't being literal, ssstranger! It'sss all but a game. I love me a free market! I love me a ssstatusss quo. And I esssspecially love me a man in a ssssuit. Mmmm." Sylvan suddenly bows to you. "But sssshould the headsss be rolling, give me a call, yeah? I might have a vessssted interesssst, but I'd rather it not be my head that rollsss..."

"Oh, don't think I wassss being ssserioussss, sssstranger! I wassss jusssst describing the game, isss all. End of the day, you pack the game up and everyone goesss back to being friendssss. No heads roll. Everyone gets along and agreesss. Nothing ever changessss. And who would want it anything different, huh? Glad we agree!"

name: SOCIALIZE_SYLVAN_GENERIC_8
text: "How's it going, huh stranger? Seeing you always brightens my day. And not just because it usually means more money for me!"

choice.text: Awww, thanks - wait, why aren't you slurring your s's?

event.text:
"Hm? Oh! Haha. My bad. Ssssorry, I forgot that wasss a thing we still pretend we do. You really thought every Ssslug hasss thisss sssspeech impediment? No, of courssse not! We just agreed asss a sssspeciesss at one point that it would be a hilarioussss way to messs with everyone elsssse!"
			
			You genuinely can't tell if Sylvan is being serious or not, but before you can inquire further he suddenly vanishes behind a corner.

name: SOCIALIZE_SYLVAN_GENERIC_9
text: "I have to sssay Sssstranger, thisss isss one tight sssship and crew you run! Remindssss me of my old pirate dayssss. Don't get me wrong, my little transssport crew is great, but... well they're sssso expendable. It feelssss ssssometimesss asss if the universsse only caresss about a select few of ussss, yeah? That some divine hand ordainssss who mattersss. I wassss never a sssspiritual one myssself, but I've sssseen ssssome sssstuff Sssstranger. Be kind to your crew. Every life matterssss, even in a universsse like thisss."

name: SOCIALIZE_SYLVAN_SLOCKNOG_1
text:
Both Sylvan and Slocknog are having a smoke together in the corner of the lounge. "Ssso, I heard you like to go by the title of 'wandering hero'. Bit of a... ssshowy title, but I can't really judge." Sylvan chuckles at his little jab at Slocknog.
	
Slocknog doesn't seem too bothered, but he's eager to correct Sylvan. "Oh, well no, not really. I'm not wanderer and certainly no hero. Unlike you, I might add. You're the real deal... a true myssstery. It'sss an honor to meet sssuch a famousss name, not jussst in the Kleptocracy but in the whole Multiverssse!" Slocknog extends his tentacle. "It'sss always... good to have connectionssss, you know?"

Sylvan shakes Slocknog's hand, but only after a brief pause. "Not sssure 'hero' really dessscribesss me, ssstranger. I'm a merchant. I'd gladly trade all the pressstige I've earned over the yearsss for a bit of ssscrap and sssome sssafety. Unfortunately, with the legacy I've left, it sssseemsss ssome foolssss can't help themselvessss but throw every damn thing they've got at me trying to prove ssssomething. Asss you can tell by me ssstanding here, they... don't often sssucceed." Sylvan shrugs. "But I am certainly honored to meet a former king. I don't ssstick around the Kleptocracy much... but yessss, a few connectionssss certainly help, don't they?"

name: SOCIALIZE_SYLVAN_DYLAN_1
text: "Sssstranger, what is this thing?" You walk over and find Sylvan staring at Dylan, who is currently trying to touch his nonexistent nose with his tongue.

choice.text: He's part of the CEL like you, isn't he?

event.text:
"I mean yesss, sssstranger, but do you even realize how big the CEL issss? I couldn't posssssibly memorize every member." Sylvan faces Dylan and tries to get his attention. "Hello? What are you, sssstranger?"
			
			"M A DYLON!" Dylan suddenly manifests a nose, which he successfully licks, then begins to spin in circles very slowly.
			
			"What clussssster are you from? I'm from the Prime clusssster. Assss in, well... you know the one."
			
			"UH OH."
			
			Both you and Sylvan look at each other, but are suddenly thrown back as Dylan violently explodes. "Did he jusssst die?" Sylvan seems in utter shock.

Moments later, Dylan suddenly manifests back into being, good as new. He says a few incoherent words and then floats away. Sylvan is still utterly speechless. For once it seems you've gotten used to something weird before him. Feels kind of nice.

name: SOCIALIZE_SYLVAN_TRIO_1
text:
You find Sylvan, Obyn, and Anurak all seated around a big pot in the cafeteria. Anurak is rubbing his hands together and seemingly saying some kind of very long winded prayer. Sylvan and Obyn are both trying to hold in their giggles, when Anurak suddenly opens his eyes.
	
	"Shellskenbry! How wonderful of a time for you to arrive! We were just about to dig into this wonderful pot of soup! Would you care to join us?"

event.text:
Anurak claps with joy and procures a throw cushion, setting it next to Sylvan. A little uneasy sitting next to the Slug, you do so anyways so as not to be rude. Sylvan smiles, but doesn't say anything. Anurak clasps his hands together to resume the prayer.
			
			"And may the Eye, shining ever brightly, manifest the highest blessings upon this meal. And may, with the powers invested in by my monkhood, serve as authority over its divine providence here today to wish the sincerest blessings upon my dearest friends."
			"Obyn, great warrior and talented poet. May your guiding light reveal the path to his people, so that he may be reunited with those of his kin." Anurak gestures to Obyn, laying his palm upon his head briefly.
			"Sylvan, benefactor of all who come his way. May your ethereal power cure my good friend of his smoking addiction, before his lungs give out." While his eyes are still closed, Anurak smirks a bit. Sylvan playfully swats his hand away at first but finally lets him rest his palm over his cloak.
			"And last, but certainly not least. Shellskensbry, fearless Renegade and kind Captain. May you, oh great eye, bestow upon them all the success that they are due, so that they may see victory and vanquish their most dreadful foes."

You bow slightly, allowing Anurak to lay his palm upon your head. It's warm and feels glassy, but only for a moment before he pulls it away. He finishes with a chant, and then finally opens his eyes. "Soup time! Oh I do love me some soup!"

"Oh, well that's quite a bummer Shellskenbry! But-but why? I made such a delicious pot of soup, and I assure you it's really quite delicious, I used all my favorite ing-"
			Sylvan puts a tentacle to Anurak's lips to shush him. "Quiet now, Anurak. The Captain issss a busssy persssson. Let ussss not disssturb them, eh?" Sylvan smiles at you, but you can't help but feel there's a bit of malice behind it...

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_NOTHING
text: Alkali sounds annoyed as you approach him, despite seemingly not being involved in anything at the moment. "Do you mind? Thhhere is limited oxygen supply in any given room and my biology happens to require a lot of it. Unless you have somethhhhing life changing to tell me, you're doing nothhhing but hogging my air supply. I request thhhat you leave."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_GENERIC_1
text:
You spot Alkali fiddling with the water purification system and demand to know what he's doing. "Why are you bothhhering me? Can't you see I'm busy?"

You fold your arms and demand Alkali explain what he's doing with the purification system once again. He lets out an exaggerated sigh to demonstrate how much he finds your unintelligence frustrating. "I'm experimenting thhhhe effects of various species ingesting sulfuric acid. I can assure you thhhhe results will be enlightening."

choice.text: Demand to know what "results" Alkali is looking for.

event.text: Alkali pauses and you could swear he attempts to roll his eye, though you can't see it through his shell. "You wouldn't understand thhhe complexity of thhhe process, so I'll make it simple. Sulfuric acid goes down thhhe hatch, and makes thhhe tummy feel bad. I want to know to what extent thhhe bad tummy feeling impacts different species. Now, I ask that you stop interrupting my experiments. Please, let me know immediately once the crew start vomiting blood. Thhhat's how I'll know thhhe control test is working."

You pat Alkali on the head and give him a thumbs-up, congratulating him on embracing the scientific method. Entirely missing the point, he only seems more encouraged. "Finally, someone understands my genius. Now, I ask thhhat you stop interrupting my experiments. Please, let me know immediately once the crew start vomiting blood. Thhhat's how I'll know thhhe control test is working."

choice.text: Give up and leave him alone.

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_GENERIC_2
text: Alkali rolls up to you, seeming rather nervous. After a few moments of awkward silence, you finally ask him what's wrong. You expect him to explain he's accidentally poisoned the water supply again or killed someone while experimenting on them, but instead he catches you off-guard. "Captain, important question. Testing a hypothhhesis. Am I... racist?"

event.text:
"Uhm. Wait, what? Hahah... no, no I'm not... I'm not racist! What a stupid thhhing to say! Eugenics and racism are very different thhhings! One is scientific, and thhhe other is unfounded tribal nonsense! Look how well it has worked for thhhhe Shells! We all get along, thhhere's zero conflict, everyone serves thhheir purpose faithfully!"
			
Alkali continues, the irony completely lost on him. "A few genetically unviable people have to die, but thhhe rest are just never born! Thhhat's why Shells are so efficient and smart, unlike othhher species! Er... sorry, I didn't mean to imply YOU weren't genetically viable. You are. Almost. Kind of. Wait. Shit, I'm being an 'asshole' again, aren't I? Ugh. Remind me later to ask if I'm an asshole when I have thhhe mental energy again." Alkali seems a bit hurt, but rolls away to go drown himself in his experiments again.

"What? A little? A LITTLE? Are you out of your god damn mind? I am not racist, asshole! Idiot. God damn it, why would you even suggest such a thhhing. Are you just trying to warn me you're mentally insufficient? Yikes." Alkali rolls away.
"Not really? Why thhhhe uncertainty? Of course I'm not racist, idiot. Hmph. Man, sometimes it's painful being thhhhe only one with thhhe confidence to say thhhe obvious." Alkali rolls away.

"Oh phew, what a relief! So many people were telling me thhhat I was thhhat I was starting to get worried! Well, glad to know I'm still thhhe only one who's right about anythhhing." Alkali rolls away.

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_GENERIC_3
text: "An important... dare I say, philosophhhical question for you." Alkali stares intently at you. "Do you hate anyone? Like, a burning, seering hatred. Someone you want dead. Like, a special, painful, very gruesome kind of dead."

event.name: ALKALI_GENERIC_3_PART2
event.text: "Mhm. And I also have a second, follow up question for you. One of equal importance. If you hate someone like thhhat, in thhhat special, burning, gruesome hate kind of way, does it make you a bad person? Please do not bring any spiritual bullshit into thhhis, I am asking objectively."

"Uhuh. Well, it's a good thhhing I don't hate anyone thhhen! Hate is an irrational impulse, driven by primitive brain chemicals. I am not bound by pointless emotions, only scientific truthhh. Thhhat bitch Nerva is such an asshole, it's a fact thhhat she's simply unworthy of love. I'm glad to see we are on thhhe same page, Renegade."

"Uhuh. Of course, to label such a basic and innate impulse as 'evil' is the kind of nonsense spoken in churches and inscribed in spiritual text. Hate is, in thhhhe mind of a sane individual such as myself, born out of nothing but reason. And thhhere are many reasons to hate Nerva, that cowardly bitch! I'm glad to see we are on thhhe same page, Renegade."

"And neithhher am I, dipshit. If I thhhought you were a philosopher, I might use vocabulary above an elementary level with you. Fine, I see your brain is useless for picking. I will go elsewhere to find answers."

"Uhm... I was not looking for humor in your response, shitface. I know you don't hate me, because I doubt you'd even have thhhe self control to not punch me to deathhh. Fine, I will find answers elsewhere."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_GENERIC_4
text:
You notice some odd drawings of creatures and evolutionary trees hung up in Alkali's room as if they were part of an evidence board. Alkali catches you staring at them and answers your unspoken questions. "I am renowned for my scientific genius in thhhe galactic community for my work in genetic studies and thhhe engineering of several advanced lifeforms, with thhhe Morphhhs of course being my latest project. However, thhhhat pales in comparison to my TRUE mission. A breakthhhrough so major... so huge it would shake thhhe very foundations of our existence."
	
Alkali pauses for dramatic effect, clearly proud of just how important whatever he's about to say next is. "I first gained prominence in thhhe Science District for my study into thhhhe history of the Shell and Slug species, specifically trying to find our common ancestor.

Thhhe problem is... I couldn't. No one could. Thhhere's no fossil records. No artifacts, not even cave paintings. Zero evidence of any transitional period. With such distinct biology you would thhink thhhere would be... somethhhing. Thhhis lead to my greatest hypothhhesis. Thhhere seems to be evidence suggesting thhhhere was TAMPERING in thhhe evolution of thhhe Slug species. As if thhhey were just... spliced togethhher from Shell and alien DNA. This is corroborated by thhhe fact thhhe telepathhhhic abilities of thhhe Slugs is unlike anythhhing seen in any othhhher species in the Multiverse. Thhhey contain biochemistry found on our homeworlds, but also thhhat of something unlike anythhhing we've ever seen elsewhere in thhhe Multiverse. Thhhere HAS to be more, and I'm going to find out what. And when I do, thhhere won't be a single person alive able to refute my genius!"

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_GENERIC_5
text: You spot Alkali leafing through a stack of old letters, and briefly catch the name "Kordet Kip'y" before Alkali stashes them away again.

event.text: Alkali seems a bit startled, and his voice is wavering. You can tell he's sad, but he's trying to hide it underneath his usual tone of annoyed indifference. "Mistakes from thhhe past. Love is a pointless thhhing. A chemical reaction thhhhat makes you do stupid, rash thhhings in pursuit of a happiness you'll never find. It's an easy trap to fall for. Luckily, my work helps keep me distracted from such pointless and dangerous pursuits."

choice.text: That's a bad way of looking at it.

event.text: Alkali scoffs. "Well, Renegades are known for thhhheir promiscuous flaunting of sexual favors. I doubt someone like you would have enough control over your cognitive functions to inhibit lust and love. I'm a scientist and a genius, I'm more qualified about thhhis thhhan you are, asshole. Just... get out of my room."

Alkali doesn't seem comforted at all by your agreeance. "You're only agreeing because you were probably hurt real bad by some whore in a brothhhel somewhere. I've reached thhhis conclusion through years of careful analysis and scientific thhheory. I don't just THHHINK love is bad, I have PROVEN it. Now, get out of my room."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_OOJ_1
text: You catch Alkali eyeing OOJ, who is wiggling pointlessly in the middle of the hallway. "Look at it. Biological perfection, thhhe ultimate weapon, thhhe ultimate utility. It was created to phase out an entire generation of worthhhless nothhhings. You're very lucky, Renegade, you have bothhh thhhe greatest biological marvel aboard your ship AND its creator."

choice.text: OOJ isn't an 'it', or a weapon. He's a person too.

event.text: "AHAHAHAHAHAH! HAHAHAHAH! Oh. You're not joking. God what are you, some kind of humanitarian? Some pro-life bullshit propagandist? IT was born in a lab, made in a test tube. Thhhhings born in labs are not PEOPLE. Unless thhhey're Shells. Or uh... the vitro-fertilized. Okay - maybe you have a point. But only maybe. I will conduct a greater hypothhhesis on thhhhis later, if only just to prove you wrong."

"Good, I was getting afraid you weren't going to respond. It's not often people outside of my laboratory staff get to interact with me, so take in thhhe view and stunning genius of my commentary while you can. It won't last forever!" Alkali rolls away.
Awkwardly, Alkali laughs to himself. "Yep... real lucky..." Alkali rolls away, not sure what to make of your silence.

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_OOJ_2
text: You catch OOJ and Alkali deep in a conversation, speaking gibberish back and forth. You're fairly surprised to see this, because as far as you knew no one could understand what they're saying. Though, if anyone could, it makes sense to be Alkali.

choice.text: You know what the Morphs are saying, Alkali?

event.text: Alkali turns to you, annoyed by your interuption. "What? No. I never finished pathhhing thhhe right neurons for thhhem to communicate properly. It's baffling thhhey can 'speak' at all. I'm probing for patterns, some kind of indication it's a real language thhhey're speaking and not nonsense. Thhhe results are inconclusive... but not discouraging. If I can't crack thhhis damn code, thhhere's no one else in thhhe Multiverse thhhhat can! So go away and let me concentrate. Thhhhis isn't an easy or quick process."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_FREDDY_1
text:
Alkali rolls up to Freddy and begins observing him silently as he drinks his tea. Freddy stares back for a few moments before he puts down his saucer. "Pardon my intrusion, but might I inquire what it is you're uhm... Doing?

"Observing. You're quite thhhhe strange specimen. All prior Mantis I have observed are incredibly unintelligent, to a comedically distressing degree. You, however, appear to be at least of an average intelligence. Would you mind if I dissected your brain later to discover what genetic mutation occurred thhhat lifted your IQ from thhhhat of a potato?"

"Well that's quite rude. Are you always like this, or do you just have something against my species?"

"Oh nonsense, I view all barbarian species equally. Thhhey all serve places in thhhe galaxy, but I hardly thhhink you should mind my gentle prodding. I find Mantis often admire my vast intellect!"

Freddy says nothing more to Alkali but turns to you. "Where did we find this asshole again? And may I vent him?"

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_ARIADNE_1
text:
You hear a high pitched scream come from the other end of the ship and rush to find the source. When you arrive, you find Ariadne has grabbed Alkali by the arm and is holding him in the air. As he squirms and squirms to be let free, Ariadne glowers at him. When Alkali notices you've arrived he pleads for you to help. "Please, thhhhe vicious brute has gone mad and is trying to kill me! Tell it to let go at once! Thhhe Multiverse cannot afford to lose my genius!"

You glance up at Ariadne who grunts. "This little mold spore just thought it funny to call me a man because I was ugly. I thought I should smash his face open with my fist, but maybe he'd rather I throw him out the window instead."

Alkali speaks up, as if insulted Ariadne should insinuate such a thing. "Oh nonsense, I made no such claim! I requested thhhe knowledge as to if your species were hermaphhhrodites. I know very well you are a woman, but as thhhe Slugs go, gender is but a social construct inherited from thhhe Union! I was merely wondering since you do take on thhhe appearance of a male and-"

Ariadne smacks Alkali against the ground and kicks him against a wall, where he lays in a daze. Though tempted to allow Ariadne to continue beating him up, you can't afford to let her kill him and reluctantly ask her to calm down.

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKALI_ELLIE_1
text:
Ellie and Alkali are sat next to each other in the break room, with a diagram in front of them. Alkali seems to be trying to explain something about inheritance and alleles to Ellie using the diagram, but instead she's doodling a horse on the paper with a pink crayon. Unlike his typical behavior however, Alkali doesn't seem annoyed, if not perhaps a bit exasperated by his lack of understanding of her behavior. 

"You are... remarkably unconventional, professor Ellie. N-not thhhat thhhat's a bad thing! We need unconventional science to build the future, and you've done marvelous work with your Quarp Juice! It's just... I was wondering if you had your own thhhoughts to add on my research. There are few scientists whose opinions I respect enough to review my work, but yours I most certainly do!"

"Ssshh... Ellie's drawing a horsie!"

"Yes, yes... but after you're done drawing the Equinoid, could you look over my paper?"

"Sure thing! Ellie'll do anything for a fan!"

Alkali seems relieved. "Good, good! Well I won't disturb you in the meantime..." Alkali rolls away, taking one last long look at Ellie as he goes.

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_NOTHING
text: "Oh heavens! You startled me Captain! Sorry, I was about to start meditating. It helps calm my anxiety. Maybe we can talk later, then?"

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_GENERIC_1
text: Tyrdeo slithers past, humming a song in his native language that doesn't pass well through your translator. Curious about it, you ask him what the song is. "Oh, this little tune? It's just one from my childhood! We used to sing it on the playground as kids! So much nostalgia..."

event.text: "Oh, it's the song the revolutionaries sang when they murdered Oertiss! It's about passing around the embalmed segments of his organs. The third and fourth melody are about the story of an argument about who got his liver!" Tyrdeo doesn't seem to think this sort of song is inappropriate for children, and goes back to singing as he carries on his way.

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_GENERIC_2
text: Strangely, several portraits of Tyrdeo have been mysteriously appearing around the ship, decorating various hallways and rooms. It's frankly obvious who's hanging them up, but you aren't sure what you want to do about it.

event.text: "Oh... I uh... heh... uhm..." Tyrdeo seems caught off-guard, unsure how to justify his narcissism. "Sorry, I've been practicing my painting. It's hard to do gardening aboard a spaceship so I wanted to find other venues of artistic expression. I'll uh... I'll take the paintings down. I'm sorry." Tyrdeo seems genuinely apologetic and slithers away to go take care of the situation.

You pull the paintings off the wall and start stacking them in a pile. While the technique seems a bit amateur, you can tell painstaking effort went into each of them. Tyrdeo eventually notices you taking them down and stares woefully at the pile, not having enough courage to do anything about it.

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_GENERIC_3
text: "I think some species are quite strange in the characteristics they look for in a leader!" Tyrdeo shakes his head. "The Republic has been down on its luck - I swear, I was trying! - But I find the leaders of more functional nations to still be quite silly! What do people see in Lumei or Wentworth or..." Tyrdeo hesitates his next words. "Well... Nights, I guess. I don't want to slander my ally but... he's a bit gruff, you know? It sure was nice to have another leader in that room who was gay, but god did he drink like the world was about to end!" You can tell if you don't stop him now, Tyrdeo's about to open the floodgates to ranting.

event.text: "And god did he smell! He smelled terrible, awful, truly miserable. I heard he was once quite attractive and cunning back in the day. I got to see that Gregory at least a little bit, but things sure went downhill fast! The excesses of the Kleptocracy, it's ridiculous how much they waste! Spending billions funding government-run pleasure cruises and casinos and bars, and... and they drink and they gamble and by god! How do they manage to stay afloat? The Kleptocracy should be in ruins like the Republic if they've really been running themselves this way all this time! It's a shame Slocknog thought it wise to invade us, because I had heard great things about him before that!"

"And Nights wasn't even the worst of them! When he wasn't absolutely wasted I actually appreciated his wit sometimes, he could be quite funny and charming! But god, Toarde? The Rockman? By the sweet heavens was he ever a snooze! Always talking about the next move, the next plan, the next battle, bla bla bla. Business, business, business. No rapport, and I swear by golly did I try to have some! Nights and Leik and I would go off on outings sometimes, spend time in each other's nations, get to know each other - but Toarde never came! He's just an unbearable asshole, and the atrocities he comits in his homeland?! It's despicable! I thought the Coalition was supposed to be about a new and better future for the galaxy, but if Toarde was in charge, there sure wouldn't be anything better in his galaxy! Leik was nice though. I could always tell she had more underneath her charisma, trying to weasel what she wanted out of everything, but who can blame her? She never trusted Nights and Nights never trusted her, but she was always gushing with me! Maybe it was because the Republic sided with the Hive during the Federation-Mantis war? Not many did, besides the Confederacy."

"It's funny, now that I think about it. How casual our meetings were whenever Toarde was out on some other business. Nights was such a party-goer, Leik was always so forthcoming and kind, and I'm certainly not against a bit of fun every now and then... you'd almost think we were friends! And... maybe in another life we could have been? I don't have many friends! It was so nice. I was always aware I was only there by circumstance... just a stroke of luck. I know they were pulling my strings, getting me to do what they wanted. But if that's what it takes to save the Republic then I'll do what I must! I'll do anything to save the Republic, to save my people! I was a good President, god damn it! I did everything I could! I may not be the brightest but I'm no Oertiss, Aerkae, or Kaero!" Tyrdeo starts to break down, but collects himself enough to not cry in front of you. "Oh heavens, I'm very sorry Captain! I've been talking for quite a while... I'll go now."

choice.text: Tell him you have to go.

event.text: "Oh! Of course, Captain. Well, I'll see you around sometime then! Bye bye!"

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_GENERIC_4
text: "Do you think maybe we could hire some servants, Captain? To assist with preparing food and making our beds and you know, pointless manual labor? I can't imagine they're too costly, maybe only a salary of a couple hundred scrap for a cheap one. We'd need at least 4 or 5, of course, but it would be manageable, right? Right?" You say nothing, instead staring at Tyrdeo to determine if he's joking or not. "Right... well, I'll take this uncomfortable silence as a no then. Sorry for the trouble. Heheh..."

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_GENERIC_5
text: "I've heard the Confederacy has a little movement going on, trying to rally support to join the Coalition. I did always wonder if that was going to happen, since the Confederates did support the Hive during the war. What a strange and volatile place we live in. Do you ever think of other galaxies, and what they're like? We have all this fancy Multiverse travel and yet no one's ever been to another galaxy. I'm no spaceologist or astronomologist or whatever they're called but I do think about it quite often. What if we're living in the bad galaxy? Hmmm..."

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_TURZIL_1
text: Tyrdeo slithers up to you in the break room and takes a seat across from you. "I don't mean to sound gossipy here but I'm simply quite curious... about that Engi we have aboard. Turzil, yes? He's so very... peculiar? I'm familiar with all shades of peculiar of course, but it's... well, hmm, how do I say this. He's not very social, is he?"

event.text: "Well, I heard he was aspiring in some form of art. I happen to be rather partial to a portrait or two of myself, and I asked if he might paint me! He said yes, although somewhat reluctantly, and he just kept apologizing the whole time that he wouldn't do a good job! The poor boy, heavens, I wasn't trying to intimidate him. Then when he was finished and gave me the painting I told him it was beautiful, which was certainly no lie, and he just shut down! Dear... I don't believe I said anything wrong to him." Tyrdeo shakes his head. "Hmmm, Engi. Such strange creatures. Never met one quite like him though."

name: SOCIALIZE_TYRDEO_OOJ_WEALSEY_1
text: A ruckus of screaming from the other room leads you to Tyrdeo with his tongue plunged deep into OOJ's squishy and slimy body, fishing around and tugging. "HELP! HELP! OH GOD OH HEAVENS THE MONSTER HAS EATEN MY DEAR WEALSEY! MY PRECIOUS BIRD! Please Captain, help me! Heeeeelp!" Tyrdeo begins to sob, still struggling to fish the bird from out of OOJ.

event.text: You stand next to Tyrdeo and reach your arm into OOJ, fishing around in the suspiciously spacious cavern within. You feel all sorts of sharp metal, or maybe glass, what might be part of a Mantis exoskeleton, and many more things you can't even begin to guess at. Finally, you feel a plump and squishy, bird-like object and grab it, pulling Wealsey out from the gelatinous Morph. For having just been eaten, Wealsey looks surprising okay, and flutters to the top of Tyrdeo's head and tweets. "Oh sweet grace be this day. I thought I had lost him forever! Thank you Captain. Why- why do we let this thing roam the hallways? It's dangerous!" OOJ jiggles again, as if insulted. "Parra para tik spikle mika pallajoo! Piss."

choice.text: Tell OOJ to spit Wealsey out.

event.text: "Pakook malahoo kooj kooj!" OOJ vibrates and wiggles, and moments later spits out a yellow blob onto the floor. For having just been eaten, Wealsey looks surprising okay, and flutters to the top of Tyrdeo's head and tweets. "Oh sweet grace be this day. I thought I had lost him forever! Thank you Captain. Why- why do we let this thing roam the hallways? It's dangerous!" OOJ jiggles again, as if insulted. "Parra para tik spikle mika pallajoo! Piss."

Admist your cruel teasing Tyrdeo continues to pull. Somehow, whether it's OOJ reaching an understanding of the situation or just random chance, the grey blob decides to finally release the bird from his grasp. Wealsey seems surprisingly okay and tweets in greatings to his Leech father, who lifts the bird cautiously and places him between his crown and slithers away without glancing back at either of you.

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_NOTHING
text: Alkram is laying in shock in his room. At first, he doesn't respond to you, but eventually you get his attention. "Why are you snapping at me? Can't you see I'm having a moment... When you get to be my age, and have seen the things I've seen, sometimes you need to just... stop for a while and think. And that thinking means not being disturbed."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_GENERIC_1
text: Alkram seems particularly bothered by some thought of his, and angrily vents in your general direction but not necessarily to you specifically. "Bah, the purity and will of the public conscience is a myth. What this galaxy needs is a set of strong leaders who aren't tainted by democratic notions and have the strength and intelligence to lead us! And I don't mean some bourgeoisie monarchist flakes like Leiiikonpliiinakra or the Elders. I mean someone capable and competent! Those Shells seem to have the right idea. I can't say I'm a fan of their eugenics, but their leadership selection portrays an immense wisdom..."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_GENERIC_2
text: "There are days when I regret the side I took in the Federation-Mantis War. There are days I regret my history as a war-hero. There are many days I mourn the lives of all I took. There are countless days I think of the soldiers that I couldn't save. But there is never a day I regret being a part of the Eargen Republic. We are a divided and downtrodden people, but beneath our endless depression there is a great culture and spirit that is all but lost. We must fight to reclaim it. My ideal Republic is no Federation member, this is true. But it is not of the Coalition either. I think our people simply need some isolation, to ponder our national identity and the values we used to stand for so long ago. And when we have, only then shall we emerge from this darkness as a new, vigorous nation full of life and wellbeing for the galaxy. It is a shame I could not be the one to bring us this future."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_GENERIC_3
text: "In my observations of your behavior I have noticed you lack a great deal of the discipline one would look to find in a good soldier. You lack the uniform and, I think, the nationalist spirit I would expect to see too. Yet, I see the heart and the spirit of one. Tell me Captain, do you see yourself as a soldier?"

choice.text: Yes, I am a soldier of the Federation.

event.text: "I see. I suppose this bears true in both a metaphorical and litteral sense. You do fight for the Federation, although you are a part of no platoon or squadron. Still, I have a great respect for any man or woman who serves a great debt to their nation. Even in my enemies, I can hold no ill will if they fight with true valor for a value they believe in. Such is what a soldier must be."

choice.text: Yes, but a soldier of no allegiance.

event.text: "Hm. Then not a good soldier are you? A soldier is one who fights for a cause, whatever that cause might be. I suppose it's in the name, yes? 'Renegade'. One without an allegiance. But are you then, I wonder, really a soldier at all? Or are you just another soul wandering this cosmos with no true purpose? Fighting for anything that seems right in the moment, but never finding a true ground to believe in. Not to say I know the answer, because I don't. And I doubt you do either. But this is the kind of reflection one must make to really find themself."

"And so scornfully you speak of it! At least, I must assume so for such a strong willed opinion. Yes, I know the type. I am, really, in no position to argue. I am proud to be a soldier, but I would not be proud to bring shame on someone else for not preferring the label."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_GENERIC_4
text:
"There was a dark time in my life when I fell into much the same pit as my Leech brethren. This was shortly after we lost the war, when it felt like the Republic had done the impossible and fallen from grace when it hadn't even had any to begin with. I felt so much shame for who I was and my actions, and so I turned to dark avenues. It never reached, perhaps, the same lengths as many of my kind. But alcohol has a certain allure that seems to draw in and unite all the lost and poor souls in this galaxy. And so I became a drinker. I quit the military and subsided into history, to be forgotten as just another foolish man who thought he had a place in this galaxy. That was, until the Kleptocracy invaded. I could stand the Chrysolic practioners and their invasive monasteries. It was slanderous to our culture, sure, but we Leeches were never a spiritual folk before anyways. But such a brazen attack from an alien foe? I was drawn back into the fray."
	
Alkram blinks, realizing he's been rambling a bit longer than he had anticipated. "What I mean to say, if you are to take the advice of this old general, is what we think we want and what reality shows us we need to be often lacks symmetry. Every man and woman has a purpose, but that purpose ought to be realized only when we're willing to see it."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_GENERIC_5
text: "I could have been a poet. Or an author. I studied literature a bit, and it fascinated me. The way people commanded words was facsimile to troops on a battlefield. In the command of a strategic and skilled author, language can be deployed with as much deadly precision and destructive - or constructive - power as the greatest militaries in the Multiverse. But it was not to be my calling. War had other ideas. And so I put down my pen and traded it for sword, and the rest is history."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_GENERIC_6
text: "During the Mantis War I had gained little respect and lost plenty for the Confederacy. At that time the Vampweeds seemed disorganized and weak willed. I foresaw their hasty and shameful surrender long before it happened, signing some document of false peace with the Gathering to bail on the war and leave us all to burn. But I can see under the reforms of this new Premier, Ivar, they have become as proud and strong a nation as the Eargen Republic once was in its glory days. Perhaps their ideals are not for me, but that is irrelevant as long as they stay true to them. If this was the Confederacy I had fought alongside in the war, I think just maybe victory would have been our glory to reap."

name: SOCIALIZE_ALKRAM_ARIADNE_1
text:
Alkram approaches Ariadne, flaring his muscles with electric currents in an effort to appear even tougher and more grissled than usual. "So you are the Rockwoman I have heard so much about! How proud I am to serve aboard this vessel with another with such great revolutionary spirit!"
	
Ariadne slowly turns away from her work to look at the Leech. "You and I are about as similar as fire is to coffee. I turned away from the life of a princess in the house of one of the most powerful men in the entire known Multiverse to fight in mud and trenches to free people who don't even know they're enslaved from a brutal dictatorship led by 5 of the most cunning and murderous monsters in all of history. YOU are an aging veteran who fought on the side of a tyranical Hive mind in some long-gone war and got bored of eating batteries in a retirement home, so you incited the latest of some dozen revolutions in a fractured Republic against a ditzy and eccentric gardener whose greatest crimes were being culturally insensitive to a flower and using political gain as a cover to making friends."

With each word Ariadne makes a violent jab towards Alkram, who reels back in shock from the sudden hostility. There's a few moments of awkward silence before Alkram hurries away in shame.

name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_NOTHING
text: You attempt to walk up to Tony to talk, but he just doesn't bother. Instead he sits there staring at you, sadness in his eyes. You begin to feel miserable as well, and can't bear to be around any longer. Hopefully, this will fade soon.

name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_1
text: While divying up tasks to the rest of the crew for typical ship maintenance, you notice Tony isn't around. You send someone out to look for him, but they report they can't find him anywhere. He's not in the restrooms, the cargo bay, his room, or the dining area where he normally is. Worried, you have just one other idea where he might be. You head to the ship's fuel tank, where Tony is busy emptying it into barrels. "Uhm... hello. Look, I understand what this looks like, but fuel is about to spike in price due to this war - if we sell it off at the peak and wait a few months, we could triple our fuel reserves!"

choice.text: And lose the war in this universe?

event.text: "Yes, yes, THIS universe. What's one of an infinite number of them being lost, when you could make a profit? I swear, you let me on your ship, but you never want my help."

name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_2
text: "In the corporate world, you don't make very many friends. Well, unless you consider fusing two species together "making" friends. So I got to thinking, what better way to make my store stand out than to pretend to be Tony Sr., your friendly neighborhood galactic marketplace owner? Now, the veneer has long since fallen off, but Tony's has locations in every free market nation in the Multiverse. But had I known how it'd all end, cornered by an Angel... I think I'd have hired more body doubles."

name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_3
text: "Ah, there you are. I was just going over my plans for the newest branch of the company - Tony Senior's Senior Helpline. I've noticed that the bulk of our support calls are from senior citizens, and so I've come up with a way to cut costs on them. We train a small team to make callers think they're smarter than the employee they're talking to, and offer to hire them after they've paid a training fee. The trick is, the fee is more than they'll make before they die of old age, and they get all the calls from seniors that take up our time! Don't you get it? They'll be paying us to give bad advice to each other, AND we don't have to spend time on the elderly!"

event.text: "What's so evil about it? They aren't taking that money into whatever afterlife they're stupid enough to believe in, they may as well give it to someone who already has the money to afford anti-aging treatments. If they didn't want to fall into a pyramid scheme in their golden years, they should've tried being rich enough to stay young and beautiful, like me."

event.name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_3_ACCEPT
event.text: "Oh no. If a poor person thinks this is a good idea, maybe I'm in the wrong here? What if they call ME to thank me for their job? I don't want to talk to the elderly, that's why I had my grandmother put away. Eugh, thanks for letting me talk about this idea with you."

event.name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_3_DECLINE
event.text: "Now, you see? That's your conscience talking. It tells you that the ideas that will make you rich are bad, so you don't realize how good it feels to not care about people." Tony slithers away, clearly under the impression he has given you excellent advice. You just hope he doesn't send you a bill for it.

name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_4
text: You find a stack of recordings underneath one of the cabinets in Tony's room, all clearly marked as blackmail on his business associates. One in particular is marked as 'The Good One'.

event.text: "Oh god, ahahahahahah! This guy tried to steal baby food from one of our stores when his business went south, then tripped and broke the jars inside his jacket while he was walking out. So he staggers back in to clean the blood, glass, and baby food off of himself in the bathroom, and bumps right into me! Next thing I know, he's crying for mercy, begging me to not let his kid starve, the whole nine yards - long story short, he didn't have to go to prison, and I got my body double! I guess the moral of the story is, you never know when a great opportunity will knock on your door, so seize it when you can!"

choice.text: Put the tape back and don't ask.

name: SOCIALIZE_TONY_GENERIC_5
